Toheed said the impact could become dangerous even before an official heatwave declaration, as residents face rising temperatures alongside inadequate access to water and electricity. Heat stress also carries an economic cost. Workers exposed to high temperatures may experience lower productivity, while households and businesses face higher cooling requirements and increased pressure on already strained power supplies. Water, power shortages compound heat stress Karachi's expanding population has not been matched by adequate infrastructure and green spaces, Toheed said, adding that water scarcity was compounding the effects of rising temperatures. The problem becomes more acute when electricity outages prevent households from operating fans, pumps and other cooling equipment. Toheed cited areas including North Karachi, Ajmer Nagri, Pahar Ganj and Lyari, where he said prolonged load-shedding was common. He also cited Baba Bhit Island, where outages could last as long as 18 hours. Even the distribution company shuts down electricity supply to Ajmer Nagri on alternative days. In some neighbourhoods, he said, residents experienced 10 to 14 hours of daily outages, while certain areas faced interruptions lasting an entire day. These accounts highlight the interaction between heat exposure and infrastructure deficiencies. Without reliable electricity and water, households have fewer options to reduce heat stress, while businesses may face disruptions to working hours and operations. SUPARCO also highlighted the implications of reduced natural infiltration and drainage capacity, noting that rapid urbanisation could increase flood risk during intense monsoon events. It cited the severe Karachi floods of 2020, when record rainfall and inadequate drainage contributed to widespread flooding. Over 60% informal settlements The effects of rising temperatures are not distributed equally across the city. Toheed estimated that between 62% and 70% of Karachi's population lived in informal settlements, where high population density, limited ventilation and inadequate housing could increase exposure to extreme heat. He said many households had eight or more members and lived in houses with galvanised iron or steel-sheet roofs, which can become oven-like under direct sunlight. Women and children face particular risks, he added. While some men can leave their homes to sit in open spaces during hot periods, women, children and the elderly may have fewer opportunities to escape overheated indoor environments because of household responsibilities and social restrictions. The economic consequences extend beyond immediate health risks. Heat-related illness can increase healthcare costs, disrupt education and reduce the ability of workers to earn income, particularly among households that cannot afford cooling equipment or alternative accommodation. Heat governance and planning gaps Toheed said heat management remained an underdeveloped area of urban governance in Pakistan, contrasting the country's approach with cities elsewhere that have appointed dedicated heat officers to coordinate public awareness, preparedness and responses to extreme temperatures. He also argued that Karachi had lagged in household solar adoption despite Pakistan's wider growth in solar energy, citing affordability, rental housing and limited rooftop space as barriers. He estimated that only around 10% of households had solar panels. The availability of rooftop solar alone would not resolve the city's heat vulnerability, but reliable and affordable electricity could help households maintain cooling during extreme temperatures. Toheed further alleged that electricity supply obligations under the Heat Wave Management Plan 2017 were not being adequately observed by Karachi's electricity distribution company during heatwave conditions.

title: LHC summons Punjab home secretary, Kot Lakhpat Jail chief over Imran's sisters' detention
description: Court seeks explanation for continued detention of Aleema, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi after their 30-day orders expire
content: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Thursday summoned the Punjab home secretary and the superintendent of Kot Lakhpat Jail over the continued detention of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan’s three sisters despite the expiry of their 30-day detention orders. Justice Abher Gul Khan adjourned further proceedings until October 28 and directed the two officials to appear before the court and explain why Aleema Khan, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi remained in custody after the expiry of their detention period. The three sisters were detained in September under Section 3 of the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, 1960, ahead of PTI’s planned September 27 protest march towards Islamabad. Aleema was detained on September 20, while Uzma and Noreen were taken into custody a day later. The Lahore deputy commissioner issued the 30-day detention orders. The orders cited police reports alleging that the women’s activities posed a threat to public safety and the maintenance of public order. The sisters subsequently challenged their detention in the Lahore High Court, seeking the annulment of the orders and their immediate release. On September 25, the court declined to suspend the detention notifications against Uzma and Noreen at that stage and sought responses from the relevant authorities. Also Read: LHC moved for Imran's sisters release The petition, filed a day earlier by Shahrez Khan, Aleema’s son, sought the recovery of the three sisters, arguing that their continued detention was unlawful. They had been detained for 30 days under orders issued by the Lahore deputy commissioner but remained at Kot Lakhpat Jail after the detention period expired. During Thursday’s hearing, the judge asked the petitioner’s counsel, Rana Mudassar Umar, why the Lahore deputy commissioner had not been impleaded as a respondent. The counsel said the deputy commissioner had not been made a party to the petition because the detention notification issued by the official had expired. Uzma’s husband, Ahed Khan, then approached the rostrum and requested that the court summon the deputy commissioner as well. Justice Abher Gul observed that the deputy commissioner had not even been named as a respondent in the petition and directed the petitioner’s counsel to satisfy Ahed on the matter. Fresh plea Shahrez filed a fresh petition in the LHC on Wednesday, seeking the production and release of his mother and her sisters, filed through Advocate Rana Mudassar Umar, named the Punjab Home Secretary, the inspector general of police, the capital city police officer and the superintendent of Kot Lakhpat Jail as respondents. The petition stated that the sisters’ 30-day detention orders, issued on September 20, had expired on October 19, but they remained in custody despite requests for their release. It argued that their continued detention violated the law and their fundamental rights, adding that they were not wanted in any criminal case and could be implicated in what the petitioner called false cases if they were not released. The plea further contended that the detentions stemmed from the sisters’ efforts to secure their brother’s release and that preventive detention could not be used as a substitute for ordinary criminal law. It challenged the orders under Article 10 of the Constitution and Section 3 of the Punjab MPO Ordinance, 1960, and asked the court to declare the orders void and direct the jail superintendent to produce the women before the court and release them.

title: Pakistan to host UN conference on space technology for disaster warnings, climate action: SUPARCO
description: Conference to bring together 250 participants to strengthen preparedness and climate resilience from Oct 27-31
content: Pakistan will host a five-day United Nations–Pakistan international conference in Islamabad from October 27 to 31 to explore how space technology can strengthen early warning systems, improve disaster risk assessment and support climate action, the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO) said on Thursday. The United Nations–Pakistan International Conference on Leveraging Space Technology for Early Warning for All (EW4All), Climate Action and Disaster Risk Assessment will be held at the Serena Hotel. It is expected to bring together 200 to 250 participants, including 60 to 70 international delegates and around 150 national participants. “The conference aims to advance the use of space-based technologies, satellite observations and geospatial data to strengthen early warning systems, improve disaster risk assessment, and support climate action,” according to an official release. The conference is being co-sponsored by the United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs (UNOOSA), through its UN-SPIDER programme, the Asia-Pacific Space Cooperation Organisation (APSCO) and the Inter-Islamic Network on Space Sciences and Technology (ISNET), it said. It will bring together experts, policymakers, diplomats, educators, researchers, United Nations agencies, development organisations and representatives of the space industry to promote international cooperation, knowledge exchange and technical dialogue, it added. A key focus will be the United Nations’ Early Warnings for All (EW4All) initiative, which seeks to protect communities and critical infrastructure from climate-related disasters through effective early warning systems, according to the handout, the statement further said. Discussions will also cover the use of space technology in disaster risk reduction, climate-resilient development and the monitoring of water resources, agriculture, forests and environmental change. The programme will feature leadership dialogues, technical sessions, expert panels and presentations on disaster risk assessment, climate intelligence, geospatial technologies and emerging tools such as GeoAI, it added. “Participants will examine practical approaches to shifting disaster management from reactive responses towards proactive risk assessment, preparedness and early action,” the statement said. The conference will also highlight the contributions of young researchers and youth-led initiatives to climate research and innovation. Discussions will align with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, the Paris Agreement and Sustainable Development Goal 13 on climate action, with the aim of translating international commitments into practical outcomes at the national and regional levels. For Pakistan, the conference is expected to strengthen national capacity to use satellite-based and geospatial information for early warning, climate resilience and disaster risk reduction, the handout stated. “Enhanced technical capabilities in assessing flood, drought and heatwave risks can contribute to more informed decision-making, improved preparedness and better protection of vulnerable communities,” it added. The event also aims to promote institutional cooperation, technical capacity-building and the practical use of satellite-derived information in disaster management and climate-related planning. The conference will conclude on October 31 with a closing ceremony and a technical visit to the National Disaster Management Authority, where participants will have an opportunity to examine Pakistan’s disaster management systems and the operational use of geospatial data, satellite monitoring and early warning tools. “Through this international gathering, Pakistan aims to strengthen partnerships and advance the effective use of space technology to build a safer, more climate-resilient and disaster-prepared future,” the statement concluded.

title: Govt, JI negotiating committees to meet over petroleum levy tomorrow
description: JI's Baloch says protests will begin again tomorrow, and that negotiations and protests will continue 'side by side'
content: The government and Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) negotiating committees are set to meet in Islamabad on Friday to discuss the abolition of the petroleum levy, as the party prepares to resume nationwide protests over fuel prices, JI Deputy Emir Liaquat Baloch said on Thursday. Baloch said the meeting, scheduled for October 23, was arranged following a telephone conversation between Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and himself. He added that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif was also expected to meet JI Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman during the negotiations. Baloch said the party would also hold nationwide protests on Friday to demand the abolition of the petroleum levy. “Negotiations and protests will continue side by side. The people must receive relief and economic activity must continue,” he said. The party has maintained that it will continue its protest campaign until the government agrees to withdraw the levy. Protests and negotiations JI first launched sit-ins on August 16 in Karachi, Lahore, Peshawar and Quetta against the petroleum levy, rising fuel prices and inflation. The party accused the government of shifting the burden of its economic policies onto ordinary citizens and demanded the abolition of the levy and a reduction in petrol prices. The party held a nationwide shutdown strike on September 3, after which the government and JI agreed to form technical committees to examine proposals for reducing the levy and fuel prices. JI subsequently submitted six proposals to the government during the first round of negotiations in Islamabad on September 7. However, successive rounds of talks failed to produce an agreement, with the government citing economic constraints and pressure under the International Monetary Fund programme, while JI insisted that the levy should be abolished. On September 20, the party launched a long march towards Islamabad, beginning with a train journey from Karachi. The caravan travelled to Sukkur before continuing towards Multan, where JI chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman addressed supporters. Read: Minister defends daily fuel pricing formula Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif subsequently telephoned Rehman and asked him to postpone the march, offering to meet the party leadership after returning from abroad to discuss relief for the public. Rehman said the party had agreed to give the prime minister an opportunity to hold talks but would not abandon its demands. JI suspended the train march at the prime minister’s request, with its workers remaining in Multan pending further negotiations. The government and JI continued discussions in the following weeks, but the dispute over the levy remained unresolved. The party has since maintained that any meeting between its chief and the prime minister must focus on the complete abolition of the charge. What is the petroleum levy? The petroleum levy is a federal charge imposed on petroleum products and forms part of the taxes collected by the government through fuel sales. It is separate from the underlying price of the fuel and contributes to the cost paid by consumers at petrol pumps. JI argues that the levy adds to the financial burden on households already facing inflation and higher transport costs. The party has linked its demand for the levy’s abolition to its wider campaign for lower fuel prices and relief from the rising cost of living. The government, meanwhile, has said it is working to provide relief to consumers while managing economic constraints under the IMF programme. The disagreement has persisted despite several rounds of negotiations, with JI demanding the complete withdrawal of the levy rather than a limited relief package.

title: HSY to design new PIA cabin crew uniforms, set to debut on Oct 31
description: Design to blend local craftsmanship with contemporary fashion and debut on PIA's inaugural London to Islamabad flight
content: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) has selected celebrated Pakistani couturier Hassan Sheheryar Yasin, popularly known as HSY, to design new uniforms for its cabin crew, with the collection set to debut on October 31, the national flag carrier announced on Thursday. According to a statement issued by PIA, the collection aims to combine Pakistan’s cultural heritage with contemporary fashion while reflecting the airline’s emphasis on hospitality, passenger comfort and crew confidence. The collection will make its official debut aboard PIA’s inaugural Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner flight from London to Islamabad on October 31, marking another step in the airline’s efforts to refresh its onboard identity under its consortium-led new management. “The collection marks a stylish leap forward in PIA’s ongoing transformation,” PIA spokesperson Abdullah Hafeez Khan said, adding that the designs would introduce a contemporary aesthetic while keeping passenger comfort and crew pride at the forefront. In a post on X, PIA described the initiative as “bringing runway glamour back to the skies” and said HSY had been chosen to create the new look for its crew. The airline also highlighted its longstanding association with international fashion, recalling that French designer Pierre Cardin created its pioneering A-line tunic and hood in 1966, helping establish PIA as a prominent name in aviation fashion. According to the statement, the legacy continued in the 1970s when Sir Hardy Amies, the royal couturier to Queen Elizabeth II, brought his tailoring expertise to the airline’s uniforms. More recently, designer Nomi Ansari’s uniform inspiration had remained part of PIA’s identity for 12 years, the airline said. HSY, one of Pakistan’s best-known fashion designers, has built an international profile through his couture work, celebrity styling and appearances on global fashion platforms. “Designing for our national flag carrier is about capturing our collective pride and the genuine warmth of Pakistani hospitality,” HSY said. He added that the aim was to create uniforms that would allow crew members to feel confident and comfortable while representing Pakistan internationally. “We wanted uniforms that our crew feels extraordinarily confident and comfortable in — apparel that respects our heritage, reflects modern fashion, and tells our story beautifully in every airport across the globe,” he said. The statement further read that the collection had been developed with a focus on functionality and comfort, taking into account the demands of long-haul operations and the physical movement required of cabin crew members. The designs feature breathable fabrics, ergonomic construction and structured tailoring intended to balance durability with a refined appearance. The colour palette and detailing also draw on Pakistan’s cultural craftsmanship while retaining the practical features required of airline uniforms, according to the statement. The final design was selected following a competitive showcase in Karachi, where 10 leading Pakistani fashion designers presented their concepts to a jury comprising fashion figures and industry representatives, the statement added. The spokesperson said the launch would introduce the airline’s refreshed visual identity to passengers, signalling what PIA described as a new chapter centred on comfort, sophistication and national pride. The appointment brings a prominent name in Pakistani couture into the national carrier’s latest efforts to reshape its image while drawing on a fashion legacy that has linked PIA with internationally recognised designers for decades.

title: PSX plunges over 1,400 points as selling pressure mounts
description: Trading volume stands at 60.55 million shares, with a traded value of Rs5.11 billion so far
content: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) came under selling pressure in Thursday’s session, with the KSE-100 Index falling 1,421.85 points, or 0.86 per cent, to 164,509.13 by midday. The market remained open, and the decline erased gains from the previous day. The benchmark had closed Wednesday at 165,930.98 after rising 779 points. Today, it opened near its intraday high of 166,180.32 before sliding to a low of 164,186.90. Trading volume stood at 60.55 million shares, with a traded value of Rs5.11 billion so far. Selling was visible across several heavyweight sectors, including oil and gas exploration, oil marketing companies, power generation, cement, automobile assemblers and refineries. Read: PSX gains 779 points amid partial recovery Index-heavy names such as OGDC, PPL, MARI, HUBCO, PSO, HBL and UBL traded lower. The move came after Wednesday’s rebound, which had been supported by selective institutional buying and optimism around diplomatic efforts on the US-Iran front along with the draft Auto Policy. By early afternoon, the Index was trading near its session low, with the broader market reflecting cautious sentiment. Volumes remained moderate for a midday session, and further direction will depend on how the remaining trading hours unfold.

title: IMF forecasts 1.3% contraction in Pakistan, 6.6% growth in 2027
description: Says outlook remains ​clouded by 'exceptionally high uncertainty'
content: The IMF on Thursday forecast a sharp drop in economic output in the Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan this year due to the ​US-Israeli-led war against Iran, followed by a rebound to 6.6% growth in ‌2027, while warning that further energy production disruptions could worsen the outlook. The International Monetary Fund said the region's output was expected to contract by 1.3% as a result of the war's ​impact on energy production, shipping, tourism, trade and confidence. Economic output would ​increase sharply in 2027, but output in those economies would generally ⁠stay below pre-war projections. The war's impact had been substantial, but uneven, with oil-exporting ​economies directly affected by disruptions to energy production and shipping hit harder, and oil ​importers proving to be more resilient, the IMF said in its regional outlook released Thursday in Dubai. The IMF said its baseline assumed that the conflict would abate in early 2027 and that ​trade would gradually normalize during the year, but it said the outlook remained ​clouded by "exceptionally high uncertainty." "The main risks derive from further disruption to energy production and trade routes ‌that ⁠could drive energy prices higher," the IMF said in a statement outlining its key messages, noting external financial conditions could also tighten. External financial conditions could also tighten if investors reassess AI-driven productivity gains and interest rates rise further amid heightened concerns about ​inflation and fiscal ​positions, it said. Oil ⁠importers had proven more resilient, with domestic demand supported by remittances and tourism flows, favorable financial conditions, and prompt policy responses ​that safeguard consumers from higher commodity prices, the IMF said. Growth ​in the ⁠Caucasus and Central Asia was moderating toward a more sustainable pace, the IMF said, forecasting a 5.2% rise in economic output in 2026 and 5% in 2027. The IMF underscored ⁠the ​mantra it delivered during last week's annual meetings, ​urging policymakers to prioritize maintaining price stability, while preserving fiscal sustainability, maintaining central bank independence and enacting structural ​reforms to boost productivity and create jobs.

title: Russia, Ukraine exchange strikes as US envoy leaves after talks
description: Both sides continue to launch a barrage of attacks despite latest US mediation attempts to end war
content: Missiles struck Kyiv in the early hours of Thursday, a Reuters witness said, and Ukraine sent hundreds of ​drones towards Moscow overnight, as the two sides kept up a barrage of ‌attacks despite the latest US mediation attempts to end the war. The Russian strikes wounded 15 people and damaged subway infrastructure on the Southern Bridge over the Dnipro River in the Ukrainian capital while also restricting traffic there, ​Kyiv authorities said. The strikes followed another attack on the city a day earlier that ​wounded six people. A Russian strike killed a woman and injured another four people ⁠in the Kharkiv region in Ukraine's northeast, Regional Governor Oleh Syniehubov said on Telegram. A drone ​also hit energy infrastructure in the Kremenchuk area in the Poltava region, a local official said on ​Telegram, without giving details. Read: Trump holds off on new measures against Russia to avoid undermining Ukraine peace talks Located on the Dnipro River, Kremenchuk is a major industrial hub and home to one of Ukraine's biggest oil refineries. The area has been repeatedly hit by Russian strikes, including a 2022 attack ​on a crowded shopping mall that killed at least 21 people. In Russia, two people were wounded ​near Moscow after 630 drones were sent towards the capital during the night, Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said on Telegram. ‌Most ⁠of the drones were downed at long range, he added. In the city of Lipetsk - home to a major steel plant some 400 km (250 miles) south of Moscow - a man was injured as drones hit apartment buildings and a medical facility, Governor Igor Artamonov said on the Telegram app. Russia ​invaded Ukraine in 2022 ​after annexing the ⁠Crimea peninsula from its southern neighbour eight years earlier, locking the two nations into the deadliest conflict on the European continent since World War ​Two. Read more: Putin agrees to resume US-mediated Ukraine talks The latest strikes come after US presidential envoy Steve Witkoff held talks this ​week with ⁠Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and Russia's President Vladimir Putin to mediate an end to the conflict. Zelenskiy said yesterday that Ukraine supported a US proposal for three-way talks with Russia and the United States ⁠at the ​level of negotiators to be held as soon as ​possible, and the Kremlin said Putin has agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Kyiv as soon as next month.

title: China's natural disaster losses hit $30b in first nine months of 2026
description: Southwestern, southern China account for majority of affected populations and ​fatalities
content: China recorded 199.36 billion yuan ($29.9 billion) in direct losses from natural disasters in the first ​nine months of 2026, mainly driven by severe typhoons, flooding ‌and landslides, its Ministry of Emergency Management said on Thursday. The losses were down 8 per cent from 217.65 billion yuan over the same period last year. Southwestern ​and southern China accounted for the majority of affected populations and ​fatalities. "Several sudden extreme disasters in southern regions led to a significant increase in deaths and missing persons compared to the five-year average," the ministry said. Read: Xi calls for improving disaster prevention as floods, landslides batter China Overall, 1,162 ​people have died or have been classified as missing from ​China's natural disasters in the first nine months of the year, up from 742 ‌a ⁠year earlier. Eastern coastal provinces suffered the heaviest property destruction and economic losses due to repeated typhoon landfalls. Geological hazards, which include rain-triggered landslides and mudslides, caused the highest proportion of fatalities and ​made up 60% ​of all disaster ⁠types, while typhoons caused the largest amount of direct financial damage, the ministry added.

title: North Korea threatens South with 'most horrible' consequences, announces border countermeasures
description: Pyongyang to raise military alert levels along southern border, deploy anti-South Korean loudspeakers within days
content: North Korea warned South Korea of the "most horrible and distressing situation" if Seoul continues what Pyongyang described as interference, announcing new countermeasures along their heavily militarised border. Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, said the country would raise its alert status along the entire southern border, according to the state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). She said anti-South Korean loudspeakers would be ready for deployment along the border within days, signalling a further escalation in tensions between the two neighbours. Read: South Korea orders stern response to any North Korean provocations amid border tensions Kim warned that continued interference by Seoul would trigger severe consequences, although the specific actions that prompted her latest warning were not immediately clear. The announcement marks another deterioration in relations between the two Koreas, which remain technically at war because the 1950-53 Korean War ended in an armistice rather than a peace treaty. The latest warning comes amid tensions over a September 21 land mine explosion in the Demilitarised Zone that wounded three South Korean soldiers, two seriously. Read More: South Korea shifts focus to ‘peaceful coexistence' with North Korea instead of 'confrontation' Seoul accused Pyongyang of deliberately planting the mines and sought an apology, while North Korea rejected the allegations as "blame-shifting" and accused the South of attempting to tarnish its international image.

title: Government websites in Europe, elsewhere go dark as software flaw sparks security scramble
description: PHP programming language developers urge users to update their sites after a fix was released
content: Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent ‌website operators scrambling to protect their systems. Developers of the PHP programming language said Tuesday they had identified two critical vulnerabilities, and urged users to update their sites as soon as a fix was released. They said around 1345 GMT on Wednesday that a new version fixing the vulnerabilities was live. But with reports that hackers were exploiting the flaws to break into websites, government agencies in the Netherlands and Finland were among those that took sites offline ahead of ​the fix as a precaution. PHP underpins large parts of the internet, raising concerns that a significant number of websites could be vulnerable to attack. "PHP is everywhere. It quietly powers WordPress, ​Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under ⁠the hood," cybersecurity company Huntress said in a blog post. Read: US judge orders Saudi engineer held in OpenAI case Dane Knecht, the chief technology officer of Web and cloud security firm Cloudflare, said that attacks were emerging and Cloudflare was updating its ​firewall rules as a stopgap measure. "We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up. This is a STOPGAP only. Patch as soon as PHP releases the update," he ​said on X. Wordfence, a security plugin that protects WordPress websites, said all WordPress sites run on a PHP-installed server. It warned that automatic updates would not apply the fix and advised site owners to find out who is responsible for updating PHP on their sites. Cybersecurity agencies in Europe, Australia, Japan and Britain have urged PHP users to update immediately or take websites offline until patches can be applied. The Dutch cybersecurity agency itself went offline, saying ​it had done so as a precaution because of the vulnerabilities. Officials have said that all PHP versions from PHP 5 onward could be affected, although PHP has not yet disclosed which versions are ​vulnerable. Critical software PHP is a programming language used to run websites. When a visitor loads a page, a server running PHP assembles the content and sends it to the browser. It is free, open-source software maintained by ‌volunteers. It is also ⁠among the most widely used software on the internet. PHP runs roughly 75% of websites whose programming language can be identified, according to web technology tracker W3Techs. It is the engine behind WordPress, which powers about 43% of all websites, from blogs and small business pages to government portals, online stores and news sites. Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com, said: "We don't comment on the details of security issues, but our team is prepared and has been working with the PHP security team to ensure a smooth update." Security experts said the vulnerabilities could potentially open the door to millions of servers because so ​many websites rely on the same underlying software. ​Rather than target victims individually, attackers could scan ⁠the internet for systems running vulnerable versions of PHP. Read more: Israeli firm used online ads to run vast spy operation, researchers say AI-assisted hacking campaigns, which have proliferated in recent weeks, could magnify the threat, said Lukasz Olejnik, a visiting senior research fellow at King's College London. "The scale is huge," Olejnik said. "And with AI, exploitation may happen instantly, on a large scale." The risk is particularly ​acute for small websites run by individuals or organisations with limited technical resources, often on shared hosting services where customers do not directly ​manage the underlying servers. Security ⁠experts said such sites could take longer to patch and remain exposed well after fixes become available. Mass outages In the Netherlands, several organisations followed the example of the National Cyber Security Centre and took public-facing websites offline, including the Port of Rotterdam, government portal Overheid.nl, the national soccer association KNVB, the websites of the country's five largest political parties and several hospital websites. Danish municipal IT company Kombit said it had shut down several ⁠services, including ​the national school communication platform, a spokesperson told Reuters. Disruption was even more widespread in Finland, where state IT services provider ​Valtori said government public network services had been taken offline "as a precautionary measure." France's Interior Ministry said it had temporarily taken local government administrative websites offline while awaiting a security fix. The US cybersecurity agency CISA did not respond to emails seeking comment.

title: Electronic Arts to cut 400 jobs, shut down BioWare, cancel next 'Mass Effect' game
description: US video game publisher plans to cut 3% of workforce as part of restructuring following $55 billion Saudi-led buyout
content: Electronic Arts (EA) plans to lay off 400 employees, close its BioWare studio and cancel the next "Mass Effect" game, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday. The layoffs will affect 3% of the US video game publisher’s workforce, including 50 employees at BioWare, the studio behind the popular "Mass Effect" and "Dragon Age" franchises. In an internal letter, EA executives said the company reviewed its operations and decided to cancel several projects to reduce costs. Read: Saudi-led consortium finalises $55b acquisition of gaming giant EA “Across our portfolio, we’re making deliberate choices to align talent and investments where we see the greatest opportunities for players and long-term growth,” they wrote. EA will also cancel a planned game in "The Sims" franchise, code-named "Project Lotus", while reducing the team developing the skateboarding game “skate”. The company said it would continue investing in its sports games, “Apex Legends”, “Battlefield” and upcoming “Star Wars” and Marvel titles. Founded in 1995 and acquired by EA in 2007, BioWare struggled in recent years with disappointing game releases and declining sales. The restructuring follows EA’s $55 billion Saudi-led buyout in August, which took the company private and added $18 billion in debt.

title: OpenAI expands ChatGPT ads to Pakistan and 25 more countries in bid to boost revenue
description: Advertisers can access ChatGPT ads in the new markets through technology partners or use a self-service option
content: OpenAI said on Wednesday it was expanding advertising on ChatGPT to Pakistan and 25 additional countries, bringing the total number of markets where ads are available to 89, as the artificial intelligence company seeks to grow revenue ahead of a potential initial public offering. The company said in August that its advertising business had reached an annualised revenue run rate of $1 billion. OpenAI began testing ads on ChatGPT's Free and Go plans in the United States earlier this year. More than 100,000 advertisers have since run campaigns on the platform, the company said. Read: Israeli firm used online ads to run vast spy operation, researchers say The latest expansion includes 14 additional Latin American countries, including Argentina, Chile, Colombia and Peru, following earlier launches in Mexico and Brazil, it outlined, adding that advertising was also launching in markets across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia, including Nigeria, South Africa, Serbia, Ukraine, Cambodia, Bangladesh and Pakistan. Advertisers can access ChatGPT ads in the new markets through technology partners or use a self-service option through the company's Ads Manager platform. The company said ads will appear only on ChatGPT's Free and Go subscription plans, while Plus, Pro and Enterprise subscriptions will remain ad-free. In September, OpenAI introduced artificial intelligence-powered tools for advertisers and began testing business-sponsored agents with select US advertisers, as it expands its advertising capabilities on the platform.

title: Tesla-SpaceX deal: Wall St says inevitable but Musk says it's not certain
description: Shares of SpaceX were up 8.4%, while Tesla gained 1.5% in premarket trading
content: Elon Musk sees "a lot of merit" in combining Tesla and SpaceX, but the decision is ​not his to make: two special committees he cannot join and a Tesla shareholder vote he calls a high hurdle ‌stand in the way. That tension runs through a deal that many analysts call inevitable. Musk, a self-described 'conflicted party', said the committees are yet to agree on the terms and a merger is not certain, even though Wall Street expects a deal by the end of next year. Shares of SpaceX were up 8.4%, while Tesla gained 1.5% in premarket trading. SpaceX ​and Tesla are jointly developing the Terafab chip plant, and AI now makes up more than half of SpaceX's revenue, with ​another $35 billion to $40 billion in spending likely in the fourth quarter to fund further expansion. Read: Trump says companies should pay 'dividend' to communities to make data centres popular "I think a Tesla-SpaceX merger makes sense. ⁠It's very strategic because both companies are rapidly transitioning into artificial intelligence and autonomous systems, and both have huge infrastructure projects underway," said Justus ​Parmar, CEO of Fortuna Investments and an investor in both companies. "It would also avoid redundancy and the time he spends going back and forth between ​two entities, and there would be a reduction in public company overhead, legal costs and administrative burdens." Analysts have said that burgeoning capital spending for expensive AI and space infrastructure would weigh on SpaceX's free cash flow, a strain a combined company could ease by sharing services and borrowing jointly with Tesla. They also point to last week's Roadster ​unveiling, where a Tesla car built with SpaceX rocket thrusters flipped and leapt over a truck, as a teaser for what a combined company ​could produce. Tesla's vote is the hurdle Control may also be part of Musk's appeal for a merger. Musk holds about 85% of SpaceX's voting power through super-voting shares. ‌But ⁠at Tesla he has roughly 20%. Bill Birmingham, head of research at REX Financial, estimates a merger would give the billionaire about 57% of voting rights. Read more: Japan launches world's first mission to collect samples from Martian moon Ryan Zurrer, founder of Dialectic, puts it at 58% at an exchange ratio of 0.7 of one SpaceX share, the illustrative level Barclays has floated. No ratio has been negotiated. Zurrer said a ratio near 0.6 would be needed for Musk to keep control if he sold more equity, and that "the ​biggest hurdle will be the Tesla ​shareholders vote vs Elon's own incentives". Musk ⁠said Tesla side needs a majority of all shares, not just those voted, so every uncast ballot counts against a deal. Analysts have flagged turnout as a risk, citing uncast broker votes at last year's meeting ​as a potential factor that could affect chances of a deal going through. Governance and regulatory questions would follow. ​When Tesla bought ⁠SolarCity in 2016, a Delaware court cleared it after years of litigation but said it should have formed an independent committee. "A deal where one man runs both sides will draw tough questions on governance," said Josh Gilbert, lead analyst for APAC at eToro. The business case, not just the process, could also decide ⁠it. Ipek ​Ozkardeskaya, senior analyst at Swissquote, said if Tesla is better off exploring AI synergies ​with other companies, the deal "could be rejected by investors". Tesla is set to report third-quarter results after markets close. Analysts said they were also watching out for disclosures of merger talks ​in regulatory filings ahead of the automaker's December 3 annual shareholder meeting.

title: Trump says companies should pay 'dividend' to communities to make data centres popular
description: Highlights data centres that were once highly unpopular became extremely popular after a ​financial deal was reached
content: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that companies ​building data centres should pay a "dividend" to the communities ‌where they are sited if they want to make the developments popular. "I have watched the process closely, and data centres that were highly unpopular in ​a certain area have become extremely popular when a ​financial deal is struck," Trump said in a Truth Social ⁠post. Data centres fueling the rise of AI have become a ​political flashpoint in communities across the country given the high quantities of ​water and power they require, with opposition uniting voters across ideological lines. The Trump administration, which has prioritised rapid AI development to compete with China, has ​also noted the shifting voter sentiment. Read: 'Apartheid automation': How Israel uses AI to monitor Palestinian land, movement and lives "New and large, in some cases ​gigantic, Data (centers) are mandated by me to make their own electricity, and give ‌or ⁠sell any excess back to the local community, or grid," Trump said in his post. Trump said in February that major technology companies must build their own power plants for their data centres in ​order to protect ​consumers from rising ⁠bills. AI giant Anthropic and Elon Musk have laid out blueprints in recent days for sharing some of ​the spoils of the AI boom. The creator of Claude ​models ⁠said over the weekend it is committing 5% of its shares to a new fund for the "public good", while Musk pledged on Monday ⁠to ​give one SpaceX share to "every kid in ​America", arguing for such direct distributions as the burgeoning sector faces public scrutiny.

title: England reach 85-2 against Sri Lanka in tri-series
description: Dunith Wellalage removes both openers Tom Banton (50) and Ben Duckett (29) after they give a solid start to England
content: Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis won the toss and elected to bowl first against England in their ODI tri-series match at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Thursday. Sri Lanka brought in left-arm spinner Dunith Wellalage for Sachindu Colombage, while opener Avishka Fernando also featured. England made two changes following their defeat to Pakistan, with Josh Tongue and Liam Dawson replacing Sonny Baker and Adil Rashid. title: Pakistan climb to fourth in ODI rankings as India hold top spot
description: New Zealand second and South Africa third in latest ICC standings; Pakistan sit just one point behind South Africa
content: Pakistan have moved into fourth place in the latest ICC men's ODI team rankings, with India retaining the top spot. Recent back-to-back victories against Sri Lanka and England have benefitted Pakistan. Pakistan have 103 rating points from 34 matches, one point behind third-placed South Africa, who have a rating of 104. New Zealand are second on 109 points, while Australia sit fifth on 102. Pakistan recently downed Sri Lanka by 37 runs and then inflicted a crushing 87-run defeat on England in the ODI tri-series at Rawalpindi. India lead the standings with a rating of 115 from 36 matches, underlining their position at the top of the one-day international rankings. England, Sri Lanka and Afghanistan occupy sixth, seventh and eighth places respectively, all with 94 rating points. Bangladesh are ninth on 81, followed by West Indies on 79. Zimbabwe are 11th with 64 rating points, ahead of Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands. The United States are 15th, while Namibia, Nepal, Oman, the United Arab Emirates and Canada complete the 20-team table.

title: Mahnoor snares Sindh's first gold
description: Promising girl lifts 5000m race walk title as National Athletics Championship explodes into action
content: Sindh's Mahnoor Fatima on Thursday was crowned champion of the women's 5,000 metres race walk event of the 54th National Athletics Championship which exploded into action at the NED University of Engineering and Technology on Thursday. Mahnoor clocked 32 minutes and 32.40 seconds time to take the women’s 5000m race walk crown. WAPDA’s Ammara Manawwar claimed silver, while Punjab’s Sawera secured bronze. “It is the first day of the National Athletics Championship, and I won a gold medal for Sindh in the 5000m race walk,” Mahnoor said. “I would like to thank organisers for holding this event. I would also like to thank my coach Nadia, Shahbaz and Abdullah for their support and guidance,” she added. In the men’s 20km race walk, Waqas secured gold for WAPDA, with Navy’s Muhammad Younis Khan taking silver. WAPDA’s Muhammad Gulfam claimed bronze. Sindh Home Minister Zia Hussain Lanjar will inaugurate the championship on Thursday (today) at 5pm. The event is being held under the supervision of the Athletics Federation of Pakistan (AFP) and is being organised by the Sindh Athletics Association (SAA), with the support of Lok Sahaeta. A total of Rs9 million has been allocated as prize money for medal winners. Teams from Higher Education Commission (HEC), Pakistan Air Force, Navy, Railways, Police, four provinces Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Islamabad and Gilgit-Baltistan are taking part in the event. Olympic gold medallist Arshad Nadeem, national 100 metre record holder Shajar Abbas and Sindh's international sprinter Moeed Baloch are among the athletes expected to attract attention during the competition.

title: St.Louis down Columbus to win US Open Cup
description: Edelman’s decisive kick gives his side a 5-3 shoot-out victory
content: St. Louis City won the first trophy in the club's history on Wednesday, defeating Major League Soccer rivals Columbus Crew on penalties to lift the US Open Cup. Daniel Edelman stroked in the decisive spot-kick to secure a 5-3 shoot-out win for St. Louis after the two teams finished locked at 0-0 after extra-time in Columbus. Substitute goalkeeper Ben Lundt was another hero for St. Louis, saving Columbus's opening penalty from Santiago Rodriguez in the shoot-out. It was a case of history repeating itself for St. Louis's Edelman, who scored the winning penalty in a shoot-out to eliminate Columbus during the 2024 MLS postseason. "Thankfully I've been there before and it's all about the process when you step up," Edelman said afterwards. "You just have to believe, have a good mindset and focus on how you strike the ball, which is exactly what I did." Edelman marked his winning penalty by sprinting the length of the pitch to celebrate with St. Louis supporters at Crew's ScottsMiracle-Gro Field. The US Open Cup – the oldest annual team tournament in the United States which was first played in 1913-1914 – marks the first silverware won by St. Louis, who joined MLS as an expansion team in 2019. "It's the first trophy for me and a lot of guys and for the city," Edelman said. "For us as a team it's phenomenal to have this night and have this trophy."

title: MotoGP bids farewell to Phillip Island
description: Riders prepare for an emotional final weekend at the iconic circuit
content: Seven-time world champion Marc Marquez admits it will be "emotional" this weekend as one of MotoGP's most iconic circuits at Phillip Island hosts its last race after nearly three decades. The picturesque and often windswept track, some two hours outside of Melbourne, has been a staple on the calendar since 1997 and a favourite among the riders given its waterfront location and demanding layout. But its contract expires this year. Promoter MotoGP Sports Entertainment wanted to broaden its appeal and shift it to Melbourne's Albert Park, which hosts the Australian Formula One. The Victorian state government was adamant it should remain at Phillip Island. With negotiations breaking down, South Australia stepped in and secured the race for six years from 2027 in Adelaide -- the first MotoGP to be held in a city‑centre location. "Phillip Island is an extraordinary circuit. Racing here for the last time will be emotional," said Ducati's Marquez, who heads into the weekend two points behind Aprilia's Jorge Martin in the championship standings. "It is a track with a unique, breathtaking layout. Here I won one of my first races with Ducati and we are motivated to do well, ready to fight right away for the positions that matter." The venue has seen some of the Spaniard's most impressive rides -- he is a four-time winner -- and also some of his worst moments including a huge high-speed crash with Johann Zarco in 2018. Teammate Francesco Bagnaia has never stood on the top step of the Phillip Island podium. But the 2022 and 2023 races, where he finished third and second respectively, were vitally important to his title-winning exploits and he too is sad to see it go. "It will be the last time on this track, a circuit where I haven't managed to win yet, but which holds an incredible charm, an extraordinary layout, and pure adrenaline," he said. With five rounds to go, the title fight has effectively become a three-way battle between Martin, reigning champion Marquez and Marco Bezzecchi, who won the last race in Indonesia to stay in touch. Aprilia's Bezzecchi is 44 points behind Marquez and 50 clear of fourth-placed Ai Ogura. "We arrive in Australia with the gaps in the riders' standings even tighter, so we have to keep working and keep faith in what everyone at Aprilia and the team is doing," said Martin. "I'm confident that my team and I will do an excellent job and give this circuit the send-off it deserves." Marquez and Martin both missed last year's Australian race with injuries, and Spain's Raul Fernandez grabbed his chance to surge to a maiden MotoGP victory. Currently seventh in the standings, Fernandez is equally dismayed at the race leaving Phillip Island. "I will cry a little bit," he said. "Not because I got my first MotoGP victory here but also because I always enjoy it a lot coming to Phillip Island -- it is super nice. "There were so many interesting races in the past here, not just in MotoGP, also in Moto2 and Moto3, so it's a track that everybody will miss a little bit."

title: No to strategic imbalance
description: World community must take a deeper interest in these shifting security doctrines
content: India's unilateral move to rewrite its strategic doctrine towards Pakistan is a cause for alarm and a direct outcome of its hegemonic designs. New Delhi's reported deployment of nuclear weapons aboard a submarine, alongside its missile modernisation programmes, heavily risks escalation. The plot thickens as the reputable SIPRI also cautioned that India has deployed around 12 nuclear warheads on a submarine for deterrence patrols. This shift has cast doubt on India's declared 'No-First-Use' policy. This transformation follows a pattern of power-maximising behaviour that does not bode well for a region sitting on tenterhooks of suspicion and instability. Ultimately, the induction of ballistic missiles, hypersonic weapon systems and AI-based strike capabilities are clear attempts to shift the deterrence dynamics in the region. The concern expressed by two NCA advisers at a seminar in Islamabad yesterday was on the mark. They rightly suspected that India was moving towards a more "prepared, potentially first-use capable nuclear posture". Their contention that Pakistan "will review and reconsider all options for appropriate deployments in order to restore the strategic balance and strategic stability while retaining the policy of strategic ambiguity" is the new plausibility in terms of re-assuring a deterrent. It is worth-mentioning that Pakistan rejects a No-First-Use policy and officially maintains a first-use capability, as part of its nuclear deterrence strategy against India. That means Islamabad relies on a doctrine of "Full Spectrum Deterrence" to offset India's conventional military superiority. The world community must take a deeper interest in these shifting security doctrines and ensure that the nuclear dyad maintains the status quo. Adding to the suspicion, India failed to inform Pakistan of its submarine ballistic missile tests, bypassing established protocols like the annual exchange of nuclear asset lists and military flag-meetings. New Delhi must remember how the May 2025 confrontation brought both nations to the brink of a nuclear exchange, and refrain from using dangerous jingoism for political gain.

title: Failure beyond negligence
description: Consider the circumstances surrounding Ali's death
content: Few failures of law enforcement are more damaging than an investigation in which the pursuit of truth becomes secondary to the defence of institutional incompetence. In Mir Raza Ali's murder case, precisely such a breakdown appears to have occurred, with investigators disregarding elementary procedures, defending questionable conclusions and compromising the very evidence needed to establish culpability. This is what the judicial commission has uncovered. Consider the circumstances surrounding Ali's death. His body was discovered in bushes in Karachi's Gulistan-e-Jauhar, yet police hastily pursued a suicide theory, citing financial difficulties and an initial post-mortem examination that was subsequently contradicted. A second autopsy established that he had been shot from behind, while the commission identified acid burns, traces of anesthesia in his blood and a bullet trajectory incompatible with suicide. The pistol he was seen carrying in CCTV footage remains missing. Despite these glaring inconsistencies, crucial evidence was mishandled and investigative procedures disregarded. Particularly damning is the commission's finding of criminal negligence by the SHO and the first investigating officer. Such serious lapses demand an explanation of how a suspected murder was allowed to become a deeply compromised investigation. Accountability must now take precedence over institutional damage control. The Sindh government should immediately constitute the JIT recommended by the commission, ensuring that it operates independently of officers implicated in the original inquiry. Criminal negligence identified on the part of the SHO and investigating officers must be followed by disciplinary proceedings, while an independent inquiry should determine whether evidence was deliberately destroyed or concealed. With much of the physical evidence already compromised, investigators must prioritise available digital and forensic evidence. Public disclosure of the inquiry's progress and regular communication with the family are essential to restoring confidence in the investigation.

title: Minor's brutal killing
description: The short life of Waseem Abbas, the victim, was a catalog of institutional neglect
content: The horrific incident in Multan - where a 15-year-old boy was chased and crushed to death by a car - has once again highlighted the plight of children in Pakistan. It also raises questions about the state of orphanages, the depth to which humanity has stooped, and the shameful conduct of lawyers. The short life of Waseem Abbas, the victim, was a catalog of institutional neglect. Abandoned at a private shelter after his parents separated, the minor boy was sent to learn electrical work under a contractor who oversaw dozens of boys - a clear violation of child labour laws. When Waseem tried to flee this abusive arrangement after a workplace dispute, his employer, Tauqeer Nazir, chased him down in a car, deliberately crushing him against a gate. He died at the scene, alone and terrified, while the state's only contribution was to record his murder after the fact. This tragedy exposes the dark side of our society that tends to ignore the exploitation of its most vulnerable. Here, children are not viewed as innocent lives to be nurtured, but as cheap, expendable commodities. The way Waseem ran for his life suggests a child running away from systemic physical or emotional abuse - yet there was no safety net to catch him, only the cold cruelty of an entitled master. That a man could look at a fleeing, terrified teenager and weaponise a vehicle to crush him shows how deeply the moral fabric of our society has rotted. Compounding this moral decay was the disgraceful spectacle at the local courts. When the accused was produced for his hearing, a group of lawyers assaulted him outside the courtroom, slapping and punching him despite the presence of police. It was a mob in black coats acting as self-appointed judges – making a mockery of the rule of law. Ironically, those sworn to uphold the law instead mirrored the very lawlessness that killed Waseem, exposing a broken system where raw emotion and brute force override the pursuit of actual institutional justice.

title: Ballot and money
description: People like Elon Musk need enormous government welfare in the form of subsidies for his companies
content: In non-democratic societies, it is usually the one with the most amount of money that gains the most political power or vice versa. They join politics because they have money and then they acquire more money because they have joined politics. For a very long time, I genuinely believed that corruption in politics and political systems being compromised due to the role of money are the kinds of things that happened in underdeveloped and poor nations. I wasn't entirely wrong. However, it took many years for me to realise that the proudest democracy in the world, namely the United States of America, is home to some of the most corruption-laden politics mankind has ever seen. The 14th amendment to the US constitution was meant to free slaves but somehow the wording of the amendment was twisted around to make it to mean US corporations' freedom. And especially after the Citizens United of 2010, there is practically no limit to how much money can be spent in elections to influence, corrupt, and actually throw American democracy out the window. Elon Musk and a bunch of other rich and morally bankrupt individuals have been busy spending millions of dollars in order to influence the outcome of the Midterm elections in the US. They call Musk a genius. I think his only intelligence is to understand early on the role of money in American elections and how he can use that to his advantage. And he is doing exactly that right now. In non-democratic societies, since public opinion doesn't matter, nobody is spending any energy or money to steer or influence public opinion because the leader with political power can do whatever he or she needs to do in order to advance his or her financial interests and those of their cronies. Things are a bit interesting, however, in the proudest democracy. Since people have the power to vote and I guess that is all the power that is left in the hands of the people, it is important to influence their minds. Propaganda becomes very essential. That money that people with questionable morals such as Elon Musk spend in elections is exactly for that; to reach a massive audience with a message dripping with propaganda. The goal is to create a misinformed citizenry. People like Elon Musk need enormous government welfare in the form of subsidies for his companies and also to block Chinese EV makers from entering the US market because Tesla cannot compete with them. The power to write those cheques resides with people's elected representatives. This is where the relationship between the candidate running for office and people like Elon Musk becomes very sinister. Elon lays down a simple bargain for the candidate running for office: I help you confuse the electorate with propaganda by paying for slick ads and you help me get these subsidies for my otherwise dying companies. In other words, I help you steal their vote, you help me steal their money. I help you convince them to vote against their interests and you help me take steps to work against the people who elect you. I help you create a misinformed electorate and you help me make sure that investment becomes profitable to an unheard of enormity. This is no exaggeration. Elon Musk had spent about $290 million in US presidential elections in 2024 helping elect Trump and his net worth after that went from about $300 billion to over a trillion dollars. Do the math. He turns public servants into his private slaves doing his bidding. Even in the absence of proof of all this, and there is proof available though, what possibly could be the reason behind large corporations or billionaires spending millions of dollars to help a certain candidate running for office to reach the voters. Could it be that these billionaires care about the health of American democracy and they are only acting so in a fatherly manner to help the people and the nation? The last sentence above is as fictional as Israeli claims of victimhood.

title: Modi's playbook: deceive, distract, lie and justify
description: Modi government needs distractions from high unemployment rates in India, corruption, rapes
content: When Congress leader Jairam Ramesh mentioned Narendra Modi following DDLJ, Indians wondered if the Indian prime minister also had to do something with Shah Rukh Khan and Kajol's iconic movie, Dil Wale Dulhaniya Le Jayein Ge. So Ramesh had to clarify to remove confusion. There is no Bollywood romance or a happy ending, but a deep crisis of governance, lack of accountability or transparency, cutting democratic dissent, intimidation, and manufactured outrage against those who dare to question. So if you are thinking that, maybe, Pakistan has attacked India, or China has stopped its trade, or the plague that is spreading in Russia has entered India, this article is not about that. It is about the complete collapse of a system and chaos that the country is facing under 'Lashkar-e-Modi'. Rather than resolving the grievances of its citizens, the government accused opposition and the protesting students of embarrassing India and creating anarchy, and alleged it is a regime change operation. So the message is clear: dissent is not simply a democratic right but is a threat to national stability. When did raising voice against the ills of the country become equivalent to conspiring against the country? But the Modi government needs distractions from high unemployment rates in India, corruption, rapes, SIR, Manipur, farmers and falling GDP numbers. For months they said that all these protests were foreign-funded and one name was highlighted in media, George Soros, who they alleged was behind it and trying to detabilise India. When things got out of the hand, and the Indians demanded Home Minister Amit Shah's resignation, godi media started taking the name of familiar targets – ISI and Pakistan – because this is never out of fashion in Modi's Bharat today. But blaming Islamabad will not resolve India's internal problems. It just shows BJP's own political insecurity. The greatest irony: BJP has forgotten that the party itself owes much of its political history to agitation, sit-ins and protests as an opposition party in India. The party was built upon raising voices and challenging the status quo, all used as legitimate instruments of political oppositions. Dr Shyama Prasad Mukherjee, considered to be the ideological founder of BJP, struggled against the British, and then Nehru, before starting a political agitation over IIOJ&K. So imagine if Dr Mukherjee or former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee were alive today, would they also be called 'urban Naxals', or accused of spreading anarchy in the country? Vajpayee reached the parliament in a bullock cart to protest against rising petrol prices in Indira Gandhi government but no one called him a CIA-funded agent. In 1976, Modi, during India's first emergency, used to send messages to the students, urging them to take to streets 'to save democracy'. If public protest was a patriotic duty, then why is it portrayed as dangerous disorder under Modi? The Modi government should be working on these troubling indicators, as they deserve a greater scrutiny: Per India's National Crime Records Bureau, the national rape rate is 4.4 per 100,000 women, and 31,500 rape cases are registered annually. The Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao campaign is just a slogan. India's jobless rate is closer to 10% but official figures say it is 3.2%. According to experts, 62.3% of workers are underemployed and stuck in low-paying work. Another lie: India's GDP growth rate is 7.7%-7.8%. But economists like Professor Arun Kumar and former finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg question whether the numbers reflect ground realities. In fact, alternative calculations put the actual growth rate closer to 2.6%. The total crime rate in India stands at 418.9 per 100,000, and the country ranks 21st in Asia on the Global Organized Crime Index with a 5.9 criminality score, driven primarily by human trafficking, drug transit and cybercrime. So if after 12 years of rule, Modi still has to blame Pakistan, or Soros, it is irrelevant who is protesting against him, because he still needs someone else to blame.

title: The irony of non-serious politics
description: Agitational politics, whipping up youth sentiment, has its obvious pitfalls
content: It was ANP's government in K-P (2008-2013). The savvy Chief Minister along with the Governor and the Corps Commander would visit GHQ, for what was later known as the 'Apex Committee' meetings, and take the Army Chief into confidence on myriad issues, with terrorism and the province's chronic financial woes topping the agenda. The COAS would, consequently, intercede with the PPP-led Federal Government, and K-P would get handsome handouts. The result: one district where I belong today has two universities (including one for women), a medical college and a state of the art medical centre, in addition to infrastructure development. Fast forward. Islamabad. During a meeting with another former Chief Minister, from PTI, who despite the military background, was unnecessarily gung-ho. Once reminded of the ANP modus operandi with the Centre, as witnessed by me, he laughed and said K-P had no dearth of funds. To this, my stark reminder was the province's inability to pay teachers. Agitational politics, whipping up youth sentiment, has its obvious pitfalls. Any politician and any political party, worth its name, must hold supreme the welfare of its people…the electorate –always and every time. There is no going around this cardinal principle, and there is no other sure bet to win elections without it. Leaders do not abandon their cadres, and do not run away once the chips are down, and they do not hide as guests with some political 'untouchables' in tribal fiefs, leaving their political rank and file directionless, dispirited and feeling betrayed and abandoned. Political flexibility is the name of the game. Any politician, who does not understand the 'constants' of Pakistan's 'enduring political culture', has no right to represent people, on whatever pretext. Emotional sloganeering and social media activism, without service delivery is political suicide. In a Federation, where the big brother Punjab has numbers; smaller federating units have to meander carefully, to be able to pick up larger than their due share. This is Pakistan's undeniable, hard and democratic reality. The Government of K-P must be of the K-P, by the KP and for the KP. With no interest in running the affairs of the terror-ridden province, chasing distant ideals, for obscure reasons, under insurmountable odds is no sensible politics. It is childish and nonsensical. Remaining within the Constitution, without foul-mouthing this or that institution, and remaining on good working relationship with the Centre, despite political differences, is pragmatic politics. Sulking and brooding thereafter in palatial CM House that people did not rise (thankfully), once shown the door, and feeling abandoned and complaining betrayal is vengeful and of no consequence. Our primary school headmaster would say, 'time has a tail that is in front, not behind.' Cannot catch it once it passes and slips. Comparatively, with no love lost for PML(N)-led dispensation in Punjab, I think Lahore gets a hell of a good advice, except for the cheap gimmicks of personality projection. Two issues surface. Long march and terrorism. As stated by the Interior Minister, the 'Long March' was no issue, as the thinking at the Centre was: a) it will not gain momentum; b) it will fizzle out on motorway within K-P; and c) the Centre would deal effectively with the remaining marchers, if and when in the Federal Capital. The last episode being a case in point. In any case, conquering Islamabad, making a laughingstock of the country when foreign dignitaries were visiting, forcing the fickle-headed security establishment to barricade 'Fortress Islamabad' by commandeering privately-owned containers and creating immense hardships for the general public is no smart politics, and this trend needs to come to an end for good, sooner than later. Civility and maturity in politics is what Pakistan needs. No wonder politicos command no respect. Second, terrorism. Yes, situation in parts of K-P – especially the southern districts – needs immediate attention. As mentioned in this space, in addition to the Afghan swamp, terrorism also has an internal dimension. And this lies squarely within the provincial government domain, yes with Federal assistance. Police needs reform, reorganisation, relief, resolute leadership and recoupment, in direction, manpower, weapons and equipment. The abandoned US weapons and military hardware in the hands of terrorists outgun and outsmart police. Pashtun sociology respects success, so local success by terrorists et al gives their recruitment a boost. Police leadership needs to be resolute, and on the same page. Police martyrs must get the respect, support and recognition they deserve. These are administrative matters squarely within the provincial purview. But when the provincial leadership, during such critical times, is busy sloganeering atop containers – abdicating its immediate and urgent functions – this is criminal neglect. When the provincial leadership emphasises non-military means against terrorists, then it needs to demonstrate its will; put its intentions into action; and show the needed spine to stand up with the LEAs. Meek statements, weak and late denunciations, belated visits to the scenes of terrorism and affected families, and 'running with the hare and hunting with the hounds' is not a strategy that would have gotten the PTI-led provincial government very far. And it surely did not, putting an end to PTI's 13-year stint in government, with no spectacular achievements to be shown, on a par with ANP's single stint, except for the eyesore of Peshawar Metro bus (jangla bus) that has ruined whatever remains of an idyllic Peshawar. Third, the Federal Government. Without any tilt towards any political dispensation, except for Pakistan, it is fair to say that the Federal Hybridism, this time around, played more mature, savvy, tolerant and patient. They ran the full course of political process with negotiations continually making no headway with the PTI-led provincial apex. The childish obduracy repeatedly obstructed compromise, leaving recourse to hard options thinkable. Centre commendably showed the spine. Administration, in its true sense, is always about spine, protecting national interests and serving the public. There was no dithering once the decision was made. Keeping the PPP on board, and dangling carrot to JUI (F) astute politics of accommodation. If present is any guide, PTI has lost Punjab to Maryam's delivery; Sindh and Balochistan were never for it to take; even K-P would be 'doubtful', if not outright impossible, during next elections. PTI-led corruption is still to surface. I am keeping my fingers crossed!

title: Israeli clearance of Gaza rubble could destroy 'evidence'
description: Albanese says Palestinians should take charge of clearance
content: A UN expert said on Monday that Israeli clearance of rubble in Gaza could destroy valuable evidence of "atrocity crimes" and prevent the recovery of human remains. Israel's assault on Gaza - started after the deadly raid into Israel by Hamas in October 2023 - has generated around 61 million tons of wreckage and debris that could take seven years to clear, according to the United Nations. Francesca Albanese, the UN expert on the Palestinian territories, said evidence should be gathered and human remains identified before full clearance started. She issued a statement headlined: "UN expert warns Israeli rubble-clearing could erase traces of atrocity crimes" and said Palestinians should be behind any plans to remove waste. "In devastated Gaza, rubble is not just construction waste. It is part of a crime scene, a graveyard, and the material record of what happened during a brutal and senseless bombing campaign that lasted two years," she said. She said that multiple sources had confirmed Israeli companies were involved in the clearance, without naming those sources. Her office did not immediately respond to questions on where that information had come from. Israel's Foreign Ministry, its Prime Minister's Office and military did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In the past, all have fiercely disagreed with Albanese, who has emerged as one of the most vocal critics of Israel's military actions in Gaza. In February, Germany, France and Italy all condemned what they said were her overly negative statements about Israel, though she denied making the remarks they cited. In July last year, the U.S. imposed sanctions on Albanese over what it said were her efforts to prompt the International Criminal Court to take action against U.S. and Israeli officials, companies, and executives. UN experts are commissioned by the Geneva-based Human Rights Council to monitor and document specific human rights crises but are independent of the organisation itself. The 2023 Hamas-led attacks killed 1,200 people in Israel while another 251 were taken hostage, according to Israeli tallies. More than 73,000 Palestinians have been killed in Israel's military campaign, according to Gaza health authorities. Israel says it has gone to great lengths to avoid civilian casualties and that Hamas uses Gaza's civilians as human shields in densely populated areas - a claim Hamas denies. Palestinian authorities estimate more than 8,000 people remain buried in the wreckage. A Palestinian recovery team that combed through the wreckage in Gaza City last month said it found the remains of 112 people from the same clan.

title: Rahul Gandhi, Indian opposition lawmakers detained over election chief protest for second day
description: Visuals show security personnel hauling Gandhi and Priyanka Vadra into separate vehicles and taking them away
content: Indian ​police detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and several lawmakers for the third time in two ‌days on Wednesday as they launched an unannounced protest demanding the resignation of the election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists. Opposition parties, their student units, and the "cockroach" youth movement have been staging almost daily demonstrations seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, ​after the Indian Express newspaper last month reported disagreements within the poll panel over updating voter ​lists, stoking concerns over its neutrality. Opposition lawmakers led by the Congress party leader protested ⁠on Tuesday as well, seeking a meeting with Kumar and his deputies, before police broke up their gathering ​and briefly detained them. Read: Police detain Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi at poll chief protest Wednesday's protest began after a lunch meeting of lawmakers that Congress organised at a restaurant ​in central Delhi, close to the Jantar Mantar site where authorities permit demonstrations. Indian police detain opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and several lawmakers for the third time in two days as they demand the resignation of the election chief over revision of voter lists, which disenfranchises 130M citizens, mostly Muslims https://t.co/mg3WB8uuHh — TRT World (@trtworld) October 7, 2026 "Yesterday ... Delhi Police stopped us and said you cannot protest here ... so today ... we will go to the designated protest site, sit there, and tell the country that, for us, Gyanesh Kumar is ​not the legitimate commissioner," Gandhi told reporters, referring to Jantar Mantar. "The people who have done this [vote theft] ​are traitors ... Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign," he said, before boarding a bus that was to take the lawmakers to Jantar ‌Mantar. New ⁠political challenge to Modi Lawmakers in the bus held posters against the windows that said, "no vote theft, no democracy theft", and "election commission, not BJP commission", referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Hundreds of Congress members accompanied the bus on foot amid heavy deployment of police and paramilitary personnel in riot gear. Police also closed ​the road leading to ​Jantar Mantar, forcing the ⁠bus to take a detour. Gandhi later stepped out of the bus, with a live feed on his party's YouTube channel showing him standing at the centre of a crowd ​of protesters and security personnel, while his sister Priyanka Vadra and other lawmakers ​sprawled out ⁠on the road. Visuals showed security personnel hauling Gandhi and Priyanka into separate vehicles and taking them away. लोकतंत्र के गद्दारो को बचाने के लिए बचे-खुचे लोकतंत्र को घसीटा गया है। हिसाब होगा - एक भी देशद्रोही बख्शा नहीं जाएगा। pic.twitter.com/QbngN1p9y6 — Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) October 6, 2026 There was no immediate comment from the police on the detentions.
