The report also pointed to more than 50 provincially controlled companies and authorities performing urban functions, including water supply, waste management, transport and development. {{pdf}} In Sindh, it identified provincial appointees’ effective veto over development plans proposed by elected councillors. In Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, it cited the reversal of an earlier commitment to channel development spending through local governments. Balochistan faced additional challenges from geographic dispersion, limited administrative capacity and a narrow revenue base. Direct elections, control over services The task force recommended directly elected mayors and chairpersons, alongside clear rules and judicial review for suspending or superseding elected councils. It proposed metropolitan corporations in major cities, headed by directly elected mayors with authority over development agencies, water and sanitation bodies, mass transit and industrial estate development institutions. Rural districts would have elected chairpersons responsible for services including rural roads and coordination of agricultural extension. Local governments should primarily oversee education up to matriculation, primary and secondary healthcare, water supply, sewerage, solid waste management, local roads and community welfare. Provinces would retain responsibility for tertiary healthcare, higher education, inter-district infrastructure and policy coordination. Read more: HIV outbreak at Karachi hospital The report stressed that transferring functions without staff and budgets would render devolution ineffective. It proposed placing civil servants in Grade 16 and below in devolved departments under local government control, along with their salaries and allowances. District accounts officers should report administratively to elected local chief executives while remaining under the professional supervision of provincial accountant generals. Performance monitoring and Auditor General audits would strengthen accountability. Constitutional safeguards The report proposed expanding Article 140-A through a constitutional schedule defining local government responsibilities, including education, healthcare and municipal services. It also recommended amending Article 160 to establish a timetable and methodology for PFCs comparable to the National Finance Commission, giving local governments predictable funding. Articles 7 and 226 should be reviewed to strengthen the constitutional standing and enforceability of local government elections. A model legislative framework developed through the Council of Common Interests should establish minimum standards while clarifying the responsibilities of union, tehsil or town, and district bodies. The task force called for merit-based recruitment, professional training for officials and elected representatives, and the online publication of budgets, development plans and performance indicators. It proposed immediate constitutional, fiscal and electoral changes, followed by legislative and institutional reforms within one to two years and revenue and civil service measures over two to four years. Local reform before new provinces On demands for new provinces, the report argued that smaller administrative units and stronger local governments were compatible, but local reform should take precedence while broader political consensus remained elusive. Also Read: MQM-P calls for new administrative units to address urban Sindh’s woes Its comparison of the United States, Germany, India, Brazil and China identified predictable financing, control over local revenue and sustained accountability as essential to effective governance. The task force was chaired by BNU Vice Chancellor Dr Moeed Wasim Yusuf, with Sanober Institute Chairman Aizaz Ahmad Chaudhry as co-chair and BCPR Director Mansoor Ahmad Khan as convener. Members included former federal ministers Khurram Dastagir Khan and Shafqat Mehmood, alongside legal experts, researchers and civil society representatives. The report concluded that meaningful devolution required municipal institutions capable of delivering everyday services, from functioning schools and staffed hospitals to timely road repairs.

title: Mir Raza’s final hours: A trail of calls, a Rs30m plea and a vanishing act
description: Phone records and CCTV footage trace the victim’s movements through Karachi before he disappeared from view at 4:38am
content: A flurry of late-night phone calls, a WhatsApp message seeking Rs30 million, the sudden disappearance of social media accounts and a trail of CCTV footage that eventually runs cold — the final five hours and 14 minutes of Mir Raza Ali’s life are marked by a series of unexplained developments. A forensic examination of his mobile phone has pieced together a timeline of his movements and communications in the hours before he vanished on July 28, offering a minute-by-minute account of his final known activities. The sequence began late on July 27, with a series of calls between Mir Raza and his friends. At 11:24pm, his friend Raziq called him for 30 seconds. Six minutes later, Mir Raza called Ahmed Bhardey. The two spoke again at 11:39pm, a minute after Raziq had called Mir Raza for the second time. Another call from Raziq followed at 11:43pm, but it lasted just two seconds. At 11:49pm, Mir Raza made a much longer call to his friend Sarim bin Tahir, speaking for 168 seconds. Three minutes later, he sent Sarim a WhatsApp message asking for Rs30 million, adding that something was going to happen in the morning that he was not prepared for. What he meant by the message remains unclear from the available timeline. At around 1:30am, Mir Raza and Raziq had a meal at Ghaffar Kabab House, before the trail of calls resumed. Read: In damning report, judicial commission seeks JIT for Mir Raza probe, FIA-led inquiry into police conduct At 2:13am, Mir Raza called Ali Jimani, who returned the call three minutes later. Their conversations lasted 42 and 75 seconds, respectively. At 2:23am, Mir received a call from his business partner, Abdullah Bhardey. They spoke for 201 seconds. Then, around 3am, another development emerged: Mir Raza’s social media accounts began to be deactivated. His fiancée, Salwa Khan, noticed the disappearing accounts and tried to reach him through WhatsApp calls and messages. She received no response until 3:58am, according to the timeline. By then, Mir Raza was making arrangements to travel. At 3:57am, Bykea driver Ehsanullah received a ride request from Mir’s number. The ride was booked at 4am. Until 4:02am, Mir continued exchanging WhatsApp messages with Ahmed Bhardey, even as he remained unresponsive to his fiancée. At 4:07am, the Bykea ride reached Cheese Valley in PECHS. Two minutes later, at 4:09am, Salwa informed Mir Raza’s friend Haitham that all his social media accounts had been deleted. Around the same time, his WhatsApp account was also deleted, adding another unexplained turn to the sequence of events. At 4:11am, CCTV footage from Cheese Valley showed Mir Raza sitting in the front seat of a vehicle. The next recorded attempts to contact him went unanswered. Between 4:20am and 4:22am, Salwa made eight calls to his SIM number. Shahryar, an employee of Wafflix, also tried to reach him during the same period. Neither received a response. Read more: Judicial commission visits Mir Raza murder site, summons key witness At 4:28am, CCTV footage captured Mir Raza getting out of a vehicle outside United Charter School in Gulistan-e-Jauhar’s Block 3. He was subsequently seen walking along Qila-e-Street towards University Road. The trail continued for another 10 minutes. At 4:38:27am on July 28, Mir Raza was last seen on CCTV footage from a rent-a-car office on Hill View Road. After that, the available footage offered no further sighting of him. His body was recovered on July 29, at a location some distance from where he was last seen. The timeline leaves several questions unanswered: what prompted Mir Raza’s request for Rs30 million, why his social media accounts disappeared within hours, and what happened after he was last captured on CCTV. The phone records and camera footage establish a sequence of calls, messages and movements. But the circumstances surrounding his disappearance — and the events that led to the recovery of his body the following day — remain the central mystery.

title: Twin cities brace for smog
description: Smog season begins across Punjab; air pollution levels rise in Islamabad, Pindi
content: The smog season has begun and will continue until January 15, with the air quality index deteriorating across the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad and other parts of Punjab, raising concerns about the spread of diseases. The season runs from October 15 to January 15. Claims that smog would be controlled before the onset of the season have failed to materialise. Authorities in Rawalpindi Division have decided to monitor smog and smoke emissions through drones and CCTV cameras. The air quality index has reached hazardous levels in Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Murree, Lahore and other major cities of Punjab. Islamabad recorded an index of 131, while Lahore registered 251, described as extremely hazardous. Gujranwala recorded 213, Faisalabad 155 and Multan 126. Rawalpindi's air pollution index reached 176, while Murree recorded 105. The index stood at 103 in Chakwal, 120 in Talagang, 122 in Jhelum and 178 in Attock. Efforts to improve air quality have so far failed to produce the desired results, while measures taken by the Environmental Protection and Climate Change Department have faced setbacks. Smog is a form of toxic air pollution caused by a combination of smoke and fog. The term was first used by British doctor Henry Antoine des Voeux in a paper in London. The severe smog that enveloped London in December 1952 is considered one of the worst such events in history. The combination of coal smoke and cold-weather fog caused thousands of deaths within a few days, prompting Britain to pass the Clean Air Act in 1956. Since the late 20th century, industrialisation and the growing number of vehicles have turned smog into a recurring winter crisis in countries including the United States, China, particularly Beijing, and South Asia, especially Punjab and Lahore. Smog forms when smoke, dust and harmful gases released by factories, vehicles and other sources - including sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and carbon monoxide - mix with natural winter fog and moisture. During winter, temperature inversion can trap this toxic layer close to the ground, preventing it from dispersing easily under sunlight. There are two main types of smog. Sulphurous smog, also known as London smog, is primarily caused by coal burning and industrial emissions. Photochemical smog, also known as Los Angeles smog, forms through chemical reactions between vehicle emissions and sunlight. The Environmental Protection Department, the secretary of the Regional Transport Authority (RTA) and traffic police said that, since October 1, authorities had shut down 20 stone-crushing machines, demolished 14 brick kilns and sealed 119 others to curb smog. They also issued notices to 1,403 farmers for burning crop residues and challaned 11,953 vehicles, collecting fines totalling Rs35,859,000. The RTA inspected 811 vehicles, issued 201 challans and collected fines amounting to Rs502,500. Meanwhile, officials of the relevant departments have reportedly started praying for heavy rainfall to help reduce air pollution.

title: Karachi polio case takes Pakistan’s tally to seven this year
description: Of the total cases, five are from K-P and the remaining two are from Sindh
content: The National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) for Polio Eradication on Monday confirmed Pakistan’s seventh polio case of the year in Karachi East, Sindh, underscoring the urgent need for consistent vaccination to protect children against the paralytic disease, which has no cure but can be prevented through vaccination. Polio is a highly infectious disease caused by the poliovirus that primarily affects children under the age of five. It invades the nervous system and can cause paralysis or death. While there is no cure for the disease, vaccination remains the most effective means of prevention. Pakistan and Afghanistan remain the only countries where wild poliovirus is endemic. According to a press release issued by the NEOC, the affected child is a six-month-old boy from Union Council Jamali Colony in Karachi East. The case was detected through the polio surveillance network and confirmed by the Regional Reference Laboratory for Polio Eradication at the National Institute of Health in Islamabad. Read: 2.2m kids vaccinated against polio The NEOC said a comprehensive investigation into the case had been launched. “The Polio Eradication Initiative (PEI) is already analysing the best science-based response to tackle and prevent further transmission, including targeted vaccination activities and support to strengthen routine immunisation,” the press release stated. The statement noted that Karachi’s last reported polio case was in December 2024, almost two years ago. Despite an overall decline in wild poliovirus transmission, Karachi has continued to report environmental detections of the virus throughout the year, indicating that transmission remains a threat to children. Pakistan has reduced polio cases by 99.8%, according to the NEOC. The estimated number of cases fell from around 20,000 in the early 1990s to 31 in 2025. Seven cases have been reported so far this year. Read more: K-P's Bannu reports fifth poliovirus case of the year Of the seven cases reported this year, five are from Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, including four from the province’s southern districts, while the remaining two are from Sindh. According to the NEOC, Pakistan has conducted four large-scale polio vaccination campaigns this year, targeting more than 45 million children. These efforts have been complemented by smaller, targeted oral and injectable vaccination campaigns in high-risk areas. A subnational campaign in September vaccinated more than 29.3 million children across the country, the NEOC said. The next vaccination campaign is scheduled to run from November 2 to 8, targeting nearly 24 million children in 97 districts, including all districts of Karachi. The PEI urged parents and communities to ensure that all children under the age of five receive polio vaccines during every campaign.

title: SHC rejects state appeal challenging Mahrang's acquittal in terrorism, sedition case
description: Observes that original complainant in the case is private individual, declares appeal not maintainable
content: The Sindh High Court (SHC) on Monday dismissed a provincial government appeal challenging the acquittal of Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC) leader Mahrang Baloch in an incitement case, declaring the appeal not maintainable. The case against Mahrang and others was registered in Karachi on Oct 11, 2024, on the complaint of a citizen, Asad Ali, under the country's terror law. The complainant stated that Mahrang was a facilitator of terrorist organisations that were enticing educated youth from Balochistan and arranging a movement of terrorists under the guise of processions and rallies. A year later, an anti-terrorism court (ATC) acquitted Mahrang, ruling that the prosecution had failed to present credible evidence. Subsequently, the acting prosecutor general Sindh challenged the acquittal before the SHC in December 2025. During today's hearing, the high court questioned the prosecution's authority to challenge the acquittal, observing that the original complainant in the case was a private individual. The bench questioned how the prosecution could independently file an appeal against the acquittal when the case had been lodged by a private complainant. The prosecution argued that the ATC had overlooked material facts while allowing Mahrang's application for acquittal. The state counsel maintained that clear evidence existed against her and argued that the prosecution should have been allowed to present its evidence during the trial. The prosecutor further contended that acquitting her before the formal framing of charges was inappropriate, as the prosecution had not yet presented its case before the trial court. However, the high court declared the appeal not maintainable and dismissed it, leaving the ATC's acquittal decision undisturbed. The BYC, known for its activism against enforced disappearances in Balochistan since 2018, has been under increasing scrutiny by law enforcement agencies. Mahrang has been in custody since March 22, 2025, following her arrest during protests in Quetta over alleged enforced disappearances and other human rights violations in Balochistan. Her lawyer, Imaan Mazari, is also facing different charges, including those of terrorism and is also currently detained along with her husband. On June 22, 2026, an ATC in Quetta sentenced her to life imprisonment in a separate case involving the killing of a security officer during a protest in Gwadar in July 2024. The conviction drew criticism from human rights organisations, including Amnesty International, which raised concerns over due process and the fairness of the trial. With additional input from Reuters.

title: SC sets up legal aid cell for deserving litigants
description: New facility at Public Facilitation Centre to guide people seeking legal assistance; court services online
content: The Supreme Court on Monday established a Legal Aid Cell at its Public Facilitation Centre (PFC) to assist deserving litigants seeking guidance in pursuing or defending their legal rights. According to Shumaila Naz of the Judicial Reforms Initiative, a dedicated legal assistant has been appointed at the cell to guide eligible individuals towards appropriate legal assistance. Naz said the facility was aimed at making access to justice simpler and more responsive, and would complement the administrative and facilitation services already being provided through the PFC. The centre functions as a one-window facility for litigants and visitors to the Supreme Court, allowing them to seek assistance at a single point instead of approaching different branches of the court separately. Naz said the PFC coordinates internally with the relevant branches to help citizens access the service they require. Also read: SC restores female heirs’ inheritance in ancestral property after 71 years, lays burden of oral gift's proof on beneficiaries The initiative is also part of the apex court's broader effort to expand technology-based public services. Nearly 20 services are currently accessible online through the PFC portal on the Supreme Court's website, allowing citizens to avail themselves of several facilities without visiting the court premises, she said. The court has also introduced the 1818 helpline through which members of the public can obtain information about their cases, seek assistance in using online services and raise administrative queries. Naz said the Legal Aid Cell would now provide an additional channel through the same facilitation framework for people requiring legal assistance. She said access to justice was not limited to entering a courtroom, but also required citizens to be able to understand procedures, identify the relevant offices and obtain information about their cases without unnecessary difficulty. The PFC, its online portal, the 1818 helpline and the newly established Legal Aid Cell were interconnected initiatives aimed at making the Supreme Court more accessible and responsive to litigants, she added. “The idea is to ensure that a citizen does not have to know which branch to approach, whom to contact, or where to go merely to obtain an answer,” Naz said. She said the broader objective was to organise administrative, technological and legal assistance around the needs of citizens rather than requiring litigants to navigate the court system on their own.

title: Fact check: Viral video does not show Peshawar BRT buses being moved to Punjab after governor's rule in K-P
description: The visuals date back to August 2026 and relate to the arrival of newly purchased buses for Peshawar's BRT system
content: Several social media users, many of whom appear to be supporters of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) and pro-Afghan accounts, based on their profiles and posts, have been sharing visuals across multiple social media platforms since Wednesday, claiming that they show buses being transferred from Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa to Punjab following the imposition of governor's rule in the province. However, the visuals date back to August and are unrelated to the situation in K-P. The federal government imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in K-P on Sunday following the president’s approval of the recommendations by the federal cabinet. The measures have been approved under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution. The decision to impose the emergency provisions came during an emergency meeting of the federal cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, where he was briefed on the security situation in K-P. Cabinet members reviewed the situation and took note of the “provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”, according to the Prime Minister’s Office. A couple of hours after the imposition of emergency was announced, K-P Information Minister Shafi Jan, who had been accompanying now-dysfunctional K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on the PTI’s long march, claimed the latter had been taken into custody. Later, the PTI issued a statement, condemning the “arrest” of Afridi and others and describing it as an act of “political victimisation and an attempt to weaken the province’s elected leadership and democratic institutions”. Communication and internet services have also been disrupted in the province. How it started On Wednesday, an X account that appeared to be pro-Afghanistan, based on its previous posts, shared a video with the following caption: "Following the imposition of governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, 200 Peshawar BRT buses have been transferred to Punjab under the cover of darkness. Analysts say Punjab is attempting to take advantage of the governor's rule to seize Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's mineral resources and other assets." The post gained 92,500 views. The video was also shared by another pro-PTI account on the same day, repeating the same claim. The post gained 82,000 views. Subsequently, the same claim was shared by several other users on X, as seen here, here, here, here, here, here, here, here and here. The claim was also shared on Facebook. Methodology A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its high virality and keen public interest in K-P’s situation after the changes to its governance and the information gap amid the connectivity and internet issues. A reverse image search was conducted to trace the source of the video, which yielded the same visual shared by several social media accounts in August 2026. A TikTok user shared the same video on August 28, 2026, with a caption referring to a BRT bus in the Gulmuhmad area of Peshawar. The post described the footage as an update regarding the local BRT service. A day later, on August 29, 2026, a TikTok user shared the same video, stating that a new fleet of Chinese-manufactured BRT buses had arrived in Peshawar after being shipped through Karachi port, marking a major upgrade to the city's public transport system. Following the reverse image search, a keyword search was conducted, which led to a ProPakistani report published on August 27, 2026, titled "Peshawar BRT to Get 52 New Buses." The report stated that the K-P government had purchased 52 new buses to expand Peshawar's BRT fleet. Of these, 25 had arrived at Karachi port from China, while the remaining 27 had been dispatched. The addition of these buses was expected to increase the fleet from 244 to 296 vehicles. Another report by ARY News, published on August 30, 2026, titled "Peshawar BRT holds largest bus fleet in Pakistan, says Muzamil Aslam," quoted K-P Chief Minister's Adviser on Finance Muzzammil Aslam as saying that the province had received 25 new BRT buses, with another 27 expected to arrive from China. He stated that the fleet expansion would bring the total number of buses to 296, making Peshawar's BRT fleet the largest in Pakistan. The Peshawar BRT administration also refuted claims circulating on social media that its buses were being relocated from Peshawar, stating: “It should be clear that this news is completely baseless and misleading.” It clarified that the video being shared was from the time “when the BRT buses were being brought to Peshawar”. Fact-check status: False The claim that viral visuals show 200 Peshawar BRT buses being transferred to Punjab following the imposition of governor's rule in K-P is misleading. The visuals date back to August 2026 and relate to the arrival of newly purchased buses for Peshawar's BRT system.

title: Former G-B CM sent on judicial remand
description: Case has been registered against Khurshid at Islamabad's Aabpara police station
content: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Saturday rejected the police's request for physical remand of former Gilgit-Baltistan chief minister and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) leader Khalid Khurshid and sent him to jail on a 14-day judicial remand. Khurshid, who was arrested by the federal police, was produced before ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain. The police had sought a 30-day physical remand, but the court rejected the request and ordered that he be sent to jail on judicial remand. A case has been registered against Khurshid at Islamabad's Aabpara police station.

title: Over 300,000 put under 1,291 smart lockdowns
description: Punjab, Sindh cross grim mark of 50,000 cases
content: The National Command and Operation Centre (NCOC) was informed on Saturday that smart lockdowns had been enforced in 1,292 localities across the country during the last 24 hours to prevent the further spread of Covid-19. The forum, which serves as the nerve centre of the country’s unified efforts to contain the spread of novel coronavirus, heard that a total of 308,600 people now remain under the restrictions in various parts of the country. A total of 10 localities in the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT), having a population of 60,000, were put under smart lockdown, the forum was told. The smart lockdowns had been enforced in 844 localities of Punjab, confining 15,200 people. Similarly, the lockdown had been imposed in 414 localities of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, with a population of 11,000, seven localities in Sindh with a population of 7,000, 12 in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) and five areas in Gilgit-Baltistan. It was also informed that the federal and provincial authorities were ensuring compliance with the health guidelines and instructions, particularly regarding workplaces, industrial sector, transport, markets and shops, besides pursuing the track, trace and quarantine (TTQ) strategy. The NCOC meeting, chaired by Planning Minister Asad Umar, was also informed that over 13,116 violations of health guidelines were observed across the country in the last 24 hours and punitive actions were taken against 1,541 markets and shops, 33 industrial units and 1,429 vehicles. Later, the NCOC released details of ventilators and beds’ availability for Covid-19 patients across the country. According to a statement, 379 beds, 68 oxygenated beds and 43 ventilators were available in AJK. Though there was no patient on the ventilator there. In Balochistan, 2,148 beds, 262 oxygenated beds and 36 ventilators were available for the virus patients. It said that no Covid-19 patient in the province was on ventilator. There were 151 beds, 43 oxygenated beds, 28 ventilators available in Gilgit, where one patient was on ventilator. Islamabad had 514 beds, 262 oxygenated beds, 90 ventilators, while 18 patients were on ventilators, the NCOC said, adding that 4,856 beds, 1,081 oxygenated beds and 340 ventilators were available in K-P, where 85 patients were on ventilators. In the most-affected provinces, 9,276 beds, 3,500 oxygen beds and 387 ventilators were available in Punjab, where 233 patients were on ventilators, while 8,274 beds, 739 oxygenated beds and 368 ventilators were available in Sindh, where 83 patients were on ventilators. 50,000 cases Punjab and Sindh, two of the most populous provinces of the country, each crossed the grim mark of 50,000 coronavirus cases on Saturday, as the country endured another day of over 6,000 new infections amid a record-breaking surge in the pandemic. In the last 24 hours, each of the two provinces recorded more than 2,000 new cases. According to the official data released on Saturday morning, the number of recoveries also crossed 50,000. However, as the day progressed, more Covid-19 positive cases were confirmed. By midnight, the nationwide tally of Covid-19 patients stood at 135,943 with 50,087 cases in Punjab, 51,518 in Sindh, 17,450 in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, 8,028 in Balochistan, 1,093 in Gilgit-Baltistan, 7,163 in Islamabad and 604 in Azad Jammu and Kashmir. The virus has so far, claimed at least 2,597 lives. The NCOC said that some 839,019 people had so far been tested, with nearly 30,000 tests conducted over the past 24 hours. The data showed that death ratio in confirmed cases also rose to 2%, from 1.7% earlier, while recoveries also climbed from 20% to 32%. Spread among medical staff According to the data, 3,858 health workers, treating the virus coronavirus patients, have also fallen victims to this pandemic. The disease has so far, claimed the lives of 36 health workers – 14 in Sindh, 7 in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, 5 in Balochistan, 6 in Punjab, 2 in Gilgit-Baltistan and 2 in Islamabad. According to the report, the health workers affected by coronavirus included 2,327 doctors, 476 nurses and 1,055 other staff. Among them, 266 health workers are being treated in various hospitals, including 3 on ventilators due to their critical condition. Over 1,450 have recovered so far. (WITH INPUT FROM APP)

title: Tales of survivors: ‘Isolation, not coronavirus, was my worst nightmare’
description: I was convinced that if my time is not up, this virus can never kill me
content: I’ve lived my worst nightmare. It wasn’t the coronavirus, but the prolonged treatment [read: observation] in isolation that made it a hellish experience. Imagine being confined to a tiny room with no social interaction whatsoever for almost a month. Doctors and nurses were the only visitors, who, too, would check on me once or twice a day. If you’re sick, you need your loved-ones around you. The sense of having someone who cares about you gives you strength to fight illness. Conversely, social isolation makes you more vulnerable to sickness. Your immune system doesn’t respond properly in isolation and it takes you longer to heal. In my case, it wasn’t me alone; my wife also shared the isolation ordeal at Mohammadabad Hospital, in Danyore, Gilgit-Baltistan. Interestingly, she didn’t have any symptoms, but tested positive for the virus. We both were in the isolation ward, while our five kids were at home – alone and worried. The ordeal started after a trip to Iran. My wife and I went in a group of 22 pilgrims to visit the holy shrines in Iran. We mostly stayed in Qom, though our pilgrimage also took us to Mashhad, and to neighbouring Iraq. Tales of survivors: ‘Never before had I seen doctors dressed up like aliens’ On Feb 22, we were preparing to return to Pakistan when we heard about the outbreak of some contagious disease in Qom. Until then, I didn’t know much about the coronavirus. On Feb 25, we took a flight for Lahore. At Tehran airport, they didn’t allow anyone to board the flight without screening. Neither of us was sick. At Lahore airport, we were screened again. We drove to Rawalpindi where we stayed for two days. While fellow pilgrims dispersed, we took a bus for Gilgit on Feb 28 and reached our village Nomal, some 15km from Gilgit city, in the evening. In the night I felt feverish. I took it for travel fatigue, took over-the-counter fever reducers from my neighbour and tried to sleep. It didn’t help. I started having chills. Next morning, I called up the District Headquarters Hospital Gilgit and told medics about my travel and fever. A team of doctors immediately came to see me and my wife. We were then driven to the DHQ hospital in an ambulance. They took samples to test us for the novel coronavirus, while we were shifted to the Civil Hospital Basin. The samples were sent to National Institute of Health (NIH) in Islamabad for PCR test because the facility wasn’t available in Gilgit-Baltistan. I lost my appetite but I tried to force-feed myself so that I could gather some energy to fight off my illness. After a couple of days, our test reports were received from NIH: both of us were positive for COVID-19. After the diagnosis, they shifted us to the Mohammadabad Hospital, where we were to stay for the next 25 days. Interestingly, by now my fever was gone, while I had no cough, no muscle soreness, no sore throat, and no shortness of breath. My appetite returned to normal [I started eating more than I normally do]. My wife remained asymptomatic throughout all this time. Tales of survivors: How I became Pakistan's first COVID-19 patient I’m a 51-year-old ex-serviceman and my wife is 45. I had heard that the coronavirus could be fatal for people of my age and older. Doctors sought to reassure me. But honestly, I wasn’t scared one bit. It is part of our faith that every living being has to die one day. I knew if I was destined to die, I’d die no matter what. But if my time is not up, this virus can never kill me. We were tested several times during our 25-day nightmarish sojourn. We had no symptoms, but would still test positive. I’ve heard that my wife’s reports were mixed up with another patient’s at the NIH. Luckily, the PCR testing facility was made available in Gilgit in the meantime and we were tested locally for the first time. The results were negative and a repeat test a day later confirmed the virus was out of our bodies. It was a huge relief. We were discharged from the hospital on March 28, but doctors said we should avoid socialising for 14 days. We’ve rented a house in Gilgit city to spend these two weeks here. It’s been five days now and we are counting the days till we are completely in the clear. My advice to the sick: Don’t dread this virus. Keep your faith in God and power up your will, Inshallah you will defeat it. To everyone else, I say take all precautions possible. If not out of concern for the virus, then think of the ordeal isolation can create. (Narrated to Naveed Hussain)

title: 'We honour his sacrifice': Dr Usama's fight against COVID-19
description: It is a national tragedy and we will award him the status of national hero, says G-B CM
content: “We will again see what the issue is, and if they [quarantined pilgrims] need further treatment, they will be shifted to DHQ or city hospital, but if they can be treated here, we will provide treatment to them here.” These were the last words of young doctor Usama Riaz, heard in a video recorded at a quarantine centre at Sakwar, Gilgit – where he ultimately ended up contracting the novel coronavirus while checking pilgrims returning from Iran and Iraq. “Usama was continuously on duty and unfortunately was without proper protective gear necessary to handle coronavirus patient,” said a doctor referring to his video in which Riaz is seen wearing an ordinary mask. The video went viral on social media attracting sympathies for the young doctor. Pakistani volunteers 3D-print ventilators, join war against COVID-19 According to relatives, Riaz returned home on Friday night from duty and went to bed. “But he couldn’t wake up next morning,” said the relative, adding he was rushed to combined military hospital (CMH) and then the district headquarter (DHQ) hospital where a CT scan machine was found to be out of order. The relatives appealed for airlifting him to Islamabad for treatment but that did not materialize either. The 26-years-old Riaz, who was a resident of Chilas town, was then put on a ventilator at DHQ Gilgit, where he remained for the next three days before passing away on Sunday. “It’s a national tragedy and we will award him the status of national hero,” Chief Minister Hafeezur Rehman told The Express Tribune. “He was our frontline defence and we honour his sacrifice.” Riaz’s death brings the tally of fatalities to five in Pakistan. The country has so far above 800 known cases of the virus. Sindh has reported the highest number of cases. Mehtabur Rehman, a local journalist, who visited the quarantine centre said, “I visited the centre where Usama was deputed and found the situation deplorable”. “As far as protective gear, there was no such thing on the ground,” said the journalist who was later put on quarantine on ‘suspicion’ of visiting the centre without following the standard operating procedures. Rehman termed the quarantine as a vendetta for exposing the government’s false claims. Young doctor screening coronavirus patients dies of COVID-19 in Gilgit The Pakistan Medical Association of Gilgit-Baltistan (PMA G-B) reacted to Riaz’s death and accused the government of showing negligence towards genuine issues of the doctors. “Dr Riaz had contracted COVID-19 due to the negligence of government and its health department,” said President PMA G-B Dr Zulfiqar Ali while addressing a press conference in Gilgit.

title: New coronavirus case emerges in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan's tally rises to 20
description: The 14-year-old boy, a resident of Skardu, was held at an isolation centre where he tested positive for COVID-19
content: The second coronavirus case of Gilgit-Baltistan emerged on Wednesday, raising Pakistan’s tally of total confirmed cases to 20. The 14-year-old boy, a resident of Skardu, was held at an isolation centre where he tested positive for the mysterious viral pneumonia-like disease caused by the novel coronavirus. So far 20 Pakistanis have been tested positive for COVID-19 with 15 of them belonging to Sindh, four in Gilgit-Baltistan now and one in Balochistan. First coronavirus case surfaces in Quetta, raising Pakistan’s tally to 19 On Tuesday, the first coronavirus case emerged in the Balochistan capital. The 12-year-old patient had arrived in Quetta along with his parents from Iran via Taftan border, head of a government hospital said. The family belongs to Dadu district in Sindh, said the medical superintendent (MS) of Fatima Jinnah Hospital, adding that parents, three siblings and paternal aunt of the child are tested negative. One patient has already fully recovered and was discharged from the hospital in Karachi last week. Meanwhile, Dr Zafar Mirza, the de facto health minister, has said the federal government is looking closely at the changing situation and new cases are being provided with the best medical care. “No need to worry… the situation is completely under control. The federal and provincial governments are jointly making all-out efforts to protect the masses from coronavirus on war footing,” he wrote using his official Twitter handle. Dr Mirza admitted that the coronavirus cases in Pakistan had doubled in the last 24 hours. “This is not surprising. Disease has spread in 106 countries. All 19 cases have brought this from abroad. All are stable. There is no evidence of local spread as yet. If we act responsibly we can avoid spread,” he wrote. He also advised the public to observe hygiene by washing hands properly, avoid touching face and keeping distance with sick people. “The government is working hard to contain the spread, but we all need to take our part in this fight,” he added. All educational institutions in Sindh and Balochistan have been closed till March 13 over fear of the contagious disease’s outbreak. The mysterious COVID-19 virus, which originated in a vet market of the central Chinese city of Wuhan late last year, has since then spread to more than 110 countries of the world, killing over 4,000 and infecting over 115,000 people, mostly in China thus far. But new outbreaks in Europe, the Middle East and in Asia have fanned fears of the contagion taking hold in poor nations that lack the healthcare infrastructure to cope. There are growing fears in Pakistan — sandwiched between China and Iran, both hotspots for the disease — over how the country would deal with the outbreak.

title: Turkiye plans mandate to send military personnel to Saudi Arabia, ruling party official says
description: AKP ​lawmaker says no Turkish troops deployed to other countries under ‌⁠pact would take part in offensive operations
content: Turkiye will submit to parliament ​a mandate allowing for military personnel to be ‌deployed to Saudi Arabia under its joint defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a lawmaker from the ruling AK Party ​told Reuters on Wednesday. The lawmaker, speaking on condition ​of anonymity, said the mandate would be sent ⁠to parliament once a bill ratifying the accord ​has been approved. Turkiye submitted the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement — signed by ​the three countries in August — to parliament for ratification on Tuesday, moving NATO's second-largest army closer to a formal mutual defence pledge ​with Riyadh as it faces Houthi attacks. The AKP ​lawmaker said that no Turkish troops deployed to other countries under ‌the ⁠pact would take part in offensive operations, adding that technical personnel and experts would be sent initially to help with air defences, electronic warfare technologies, and other ​defensive support. Read: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted, destroyed drones in Madinah, eastern province Earlier, two ​officials had ⁠told Reuters that Turkiye's contribution was expected to be limited to military equipment, intelligence sharing ​and weapons systems, adding that no other ​form ⁠of deployment had taken place under the alliance so far. Turkiye, which has condemned the Houthi attacks, has also agreed ⁠to ​join a Saudi-led coalition to ensure ​navigational safety in the Red Sea. A day earlier, Reuters reported that Turkiye submitted a defence ‌pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to parliament for ratification, according to three parliamentary sources. The trilateral Makkah Joint Defence Agreement outlines that an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all. The ​agreement's first article says the parties shall use "all necessary means" to eliminate threats to one another's territorial integrity, sovereignty or internationally recognised ​borders, according to a text seen by Reuters. "In the event one of the parties is subjected to an armed ⁠attack or military aggression by another country or group of countries, the parties shall immediately provide assistance to the party under attack, utilising the ​full range of mutual assistance measures available to them," Article 2 of the agreement says. The provision, similar to NATO's Article 5, refers to Article ​51 of the UN Charter, which covers the individual or collective right of states to self-defence against armed attack. Also Read: US must maintain ties with Pakistan from 'geographic standpoint', says Rubio The three countries "will decide on the scope and nature of the support to be provided following an objective assessment of the assistance required" and will cooperate within their available resources, including military capabilities and resources, the same article says. At ​an emergency meeting of the alliance in Riyadh earlier this month, the three countries agreed to ensure the "rapid deployment" of military forces and capabilities in Saudi ​Arabia. Turkiye, which has a robust defence industry, has condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, expressed willingness to help meet Riyadh's military technology needs and agreed to join ‌a Saudi-led ⁠coalition to ensure navigational safety in the Red Sea. The agreement also envisages close cooperation on defence industry, intelligence sharing, logistical support and the fight against "all means of terrorism," including at the operational level.

title: Egypt's Sisi says Saudi defence role would not include attack on Yemen
description: Says Egypt's military support for Saudi Arabia would be limited to defending the kingdom's territory
content: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said Egypt's military effort to ​defend Saudi Arabia would not include ‌an attack on Yemen and would be limited to defending the kingdom's ​territory and borders, according to ​a statement by the Egyptian presidency ⁠spokesperson on Wednesday. On Monday, Egypt's parliament ​delayed until October 26 a vote ​on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia if requested, lawmakers said, extending ​deliberations over a potentially deeper ​Egyptian role following recent attacks by Yemen's ‌Houthis. Egypt ⁠would also defend the territory of any other Arab country if asked, while its military effort would not ​extend ​beyond Egypt ⁠or a fellow Arab state whose security and stability ​Cairo sought to protect, ​the ⁠statement said. Read: Egypt's Sisi seeks parliament's backing to help defend Saudi Arabia if asked Sisi added that Egypt's support for Gulf states was an ⁠extension ​of shared Arab national ​security. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis have in recent days attacked Riyadh's international airport and the ​state oil giant Saudi Aramco, amid renewed fighting with the Saudi-backed forces of ​the internationally recognised government following the collapse of a truce. The statement came days after the Egyptian president said last week that Cairo would take all necessary measures to defend Saudi Arabia if requested, amid escalating Houthi attacks on the kingdom. Sisi said Egypt would act in accordance with the directives of Saudi King Salman bin Abdulaziz and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The crown prince visited Sisi on September 15, following a renewed outbreak of fighting in Yemen, to discuss several issues, including security and navigation in the Red Sea. Egypt and ​Saudi Arabia are close strategic and economic partners. Saudi ​Arabia and ⁠other oil-rich Gulf states provided Egypt with billions of dollars in aid, central-bank deposits and investments after the military ouster of Islamist president Mohamed ⁠Morsi ​in 2013. Egypt also joined the Saudi-led coalition ​that intervened in 2015 to support the Yemeni government against the Houthis.

title: 2 killed after Saudi air defenses intercept drone targeting Aramco oil field
description: Pakistani injured among two after falling debris sparks fire in vehicle at oil field, says Energy Ministry
content: Two foreign nationals were killed and two others injured Wednesday after Saudi air defenses intercepted a drone attempting to target a facility at Saudi Aramco’s Shaybah oil field in the country’s Eastern Province, the Energy Ministry said. A ministry official said Saudi air defenses intercepted the drone as it attempted to strike one of the facilities at the oil field, according to the Saudi Press Agency (SPA). Debris from the interception sparked a fire in a vehicle belonging to a contractor working at the field, outside the facility’s perimeter, the official said. The incident did not affect operations at the oil field, the ministry added. The official identified the two fatalities as Philippine and Nepalese nationals, while the injured were Pakistani and Indian nationals. Relevant authorities responded to the incident and took the necessary measures, according to the statement. Earlier in the day, the Saudi-led coalition said that it intercepted and destroyed four drones launched toward Saudi Arabia. Coalition spokesman Brigadier General Turki al-Maliki said on the US social media platform X that the interception and destruction operation was carried out in the regions of Madinah and the eastern province. In a separate statement, al-Maliki said coalition forces had intercepted and destroyed a drone heading toward the eastern region. After report of the interception, the Houthis' military spokesperson said in a statement, "We did not launch any drones towards Saudi Madinah on Wednesday." However, the Houthi spokesperson, Yahya Saree said later that the group had targeted the Saudi-led coalition's “military operation room at the Badr Camp in Aden with a ballistic missile,” Al Jazeera reported. The confirmation came after, according to Al Jazeera, a loud blast was heard in Aden. Separately, warplanes carried out airstrikes targeting Houthi positions east of the coastal city of Mokha in southwestern Yemen, Yemen TV reported. The broadcaster reported the strikes but did not provide further details on the targets or any casualties. There was also no immediate information on the extent of the damage or comment from the Houthis. The airstrikes came amid an ongoing military offensive against the Houthis in southwestern Yemen. On Tuesday, the Yemeni army said it had carried out 744 attacks against the group over 24 hours, neutralising around 200 of its members and destroying or damaging 90 vehicles and other military assets. Further, Al Jazeera cited the Saudi-led coalition saying its forces were "engaged in heavy fighting against the Houthis in Kahboub, southwestern Yemen and were trying to repel a large-scale attack" by the group. Yemen’s central bank orders freezing assets of 135 Houthi-linked individuals, entities On Tuesday, Yemen’s central bank ordered banks and exchange companies to freeze the accounts and assets of 135 Houthi-linked individuals, entities and vessels placed on terrorism lists, the government-run SABA news agency reported. The Aden-based bank issued the directive under an October 19 order by the country’s public prosecutor to designate those listed and freeze their assets over their alleged ties to the Houthi group. The measures also ban financial and commercial dealings with those listed, including opening new bank accounts or carrying out transactions on their behalf. Financial institutions were instructed to identify and report the accounts, assets and money transfers of those listed to the country’s financial intelligence and anti-money laundering authorities. Read: Death toll from Houthi attack on Yemen training camp rises to 73 According to SABA, the list includes Houthi political, military and security officials, businessmen, a company and five oil tankers identified by Yemeni authorities as smuggling vessels. The agency did not disclose the names of those listed. On October 11, Yemen’s internationally recognised government approved a draft law designating the Houthis a “terrorist organisation” and criminalising the group’s activities and financing. The government also called for completing the legal and constitutional procedures needed to enact the legislation. EU exploring ways to increase support for Yemeni government: Kallas On the same day, the European Union announced it was exploring ways to increase its support for Yemen's government and stood ready to back mediation efforts aimed at resuming meaningful political negotiations, EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said. Addressing a plenary session of the European Parliament in Strasbourg, France, Kallas said the EU was examining options to step up its assistance to Yemen amid escalating Houthi attacks and worsening regional security. Emphasising the need for a diplomatic solution, she said the EU was ready to support efforts to revive political negotiations. "We also stand ready to support all mediation efforts to resume meaningful political negotiations. Escalation will leave everyone worse off," Kallas said. She urged all parties concerned to help bring "the Houthi aggression" to an end and called on the group to re-engage with the United Nations-led mediation process. Read More: Saudi Arabia intercepts, destroys Houthi ballistic missile, coalition's spokesperson says On maritime security, Kallas said the EU's Operation Aspides had escorted hundreds of commercial vessels to safety since its launch in response to Houthi attacks on shipping in the Red Sea. "We have a huge list of companies requesting our support and not enough ships to help all who request it," she said, adding that the EU lacked sufficient naval assets to meet all requests for protection. She stressed that the operation was not intended to engage in the war but to protect commercial shipping and European trade interests. The bloc will also continue supporting the Yemeni Coast Guard and other maritime actors in the region, including Djibouti, to combat arms smuggling, Kallas added. On calls to designate the Houthis as a terrorist organisation, she noted that such a move would require the support of all member states. Yemen has been engulfed in conflict since the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and several other provinces in September 2014, prompting a Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government. The Houthis control much of northern and western Yemen, while government forces and their allies hold Aden and large parts of the country’s southern and eastern provinces.

title: Fact check: Viral visuals do not show Bangladeshi man, woman executed in Saudi Arabia
description: Visuals are old from unrelated incidents, while others have been doctored
content: Several people, including Indian propaganda accounts based on their past posts, have been sharing visuals on multiple social media platforms since October 16, 2026, allegedly showing a Bangladeshi man and woman executed over an indecent act in a mosque in Makkah. However, some of the visuals are old, while others have been doctored. A Bangladeshi man and woman were executed on October 14, 2026, after being convicted of committing an “indecent act” inside a mosque, according to the Saudi interior ministry. The ministry did not specify the nature of the offending act. Bangladesh has reached out to the Saudi government about the offences involved and legal proceedings in the case, said state minister for foreign affairs, Shama Obaed Islam. The Daily Star reported that the two have been in detention since August 2023 in connection with separate allegations — cybercrime and adultery. On October 18, a local Indian news outlet, UPUK News, shared a video on X, showing a woman kissing the black stone (Hajar al-Aswad) at Makkah’s Holy Mosque while being surrounded by men. The caption of the post reads: “Saudi Arabia executes two Bangladeshi nationals over ‘having sex’ inside Makkah mosque. Saudi Arabia has announced the execution of two Bangladeshi nationals convicted of committing what authorities described as a “sexual act” inside a mosque in the holy city of Makkah. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the Saudi Ministry of Interior identified the individuals as Nazrul Islam Abdul Basir and Siti Akhtar. According to the ministry, security authorities arrested the two following the incident. They were subsequently charged after an investigation and later executed, the statement said.” The post racked up 26.8 million views. Another user shared the same clip with the following caption: “The Saudi Ministry announced the implementation of the death penalty ta’zir against Bangladeshi citizens Nuzrul Islam Abdul Basir and Seti Akhtar, for committing an indecent act inside a mosque in Makkah Al-Mukarramah, on October 14, 2026.” The post accumulated 7.5m views. Another Indian user, based on its past posts, shared the same clip with the following caption: “Saudi Arabia executes two Bangladeshi nationals over ‘having sex’ inside Makkah Mosque. Saudi Arabia has announced the execution of two Bangladeshi nationals convicted of committing what authorities described as a ‘sexual act’ inside a mosque in the holy city of Makkah.” The post gained 6.3m views. Another Indian user shared the same clip with the following caption: “A couple from Bangladesh has been reported executed on charges of engaging in sexual activity inside a mosque in Makkah. They were identified as Nazrul Islam Abdul Basir and Siti Akhtar. Saudi authorities described their offence as an ‘immoral act’ (definitely sexual) inside a mosque.” The post gained 1.5m views. Another Indian user shared the same video with a similar caption, accumulating 276,500 views. Other users also shared the same video in a similar context on X, as can be seen here, here, here, here, and here; collectively gaining 240,200 views. Methodology A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its virality and keen public interest in the incident. A keyword search was conducted to verify whether any credible international, Saudi or Bangladeshi news outlets had reported the recent incident featuring the viral video, but it yielded nothing. A reverse image search conducted to trace the source of the video yielded the same clip shared on Instagram, dated February 27, 2026, with the following caption: “This footage, recorded during the circumambulation (tawaf) of the Kaaba in Makkah, has drawn backlash. Allegations of harassment against women in this context are on the rise.” A Turkish media outlet, Daktilock, also posted the same clip on X, dated February 28, 2026, with the following caption: “This footage, recorded during the circumambulation of the Kaaba in Makkah, has sparked widespread reaction.” Later on, the same video was also shared on YouTube, dated August 2, 2026. Therefore, the viral video of a woman kissing a black stone is old and unrelated to the current Bangladeshi couple incident. Other visuals Viral video of daughter of couple executed in Saudi Arabia An Indian X account that appears to support the Bharatiya Janata Party, based on its past posts, shared a video on Oct 19 showing a little girl crying and throwing soil onto what appears to be a grave. The caption in Hindi reads: “At the age of six or seven, this little girl is filling soil into the graves of both her mother and father. The crime of her mother and father was that they had kissed each other while making a reel in a mosque in Saudi Arabia.“ The post received 436,900 views. A minute later, the account shared the same video again, with a similar caption. The second post received 2.5m views. Another X account shared the same footage with a Turkish caption that translates to: “A Bangladeshi couple went to Umrah for their honeymoon. A man of Pakistani nationality filmed the couple kissing in a mosque courtyard and sent the video to Saudi Arabian authorities. The couple was then arrested and sentenced to death. Saudi Arabian authorities executed Abdulbasir and Siti by beheading. Their young daughter, while throwing soil on her parents’ graves, is trying to make sense of the event.” The post received 2.4m views. An Indian account shared the same video, on the same day, with the caption: “A little Bangladeshi girl places soil on the graves of her mother and father following their execution in Saudi Arabia over an alleged act inside a mosque in Makkah.” The post received 681,700 views. A third Indian account shared the same video with the caption: “The only mistake this little girl’s parents made was creating a video at a sacred site. Yet, she is the one bearing the ultimate punishment.” The post received 672,500 views. A Thai account also shared the same footage with a caption in Thai that reads: “A Bangladeshi couple were on their honeymoon trip for Umrah when a Pakistani man secretly filmed them kissing in a mosque courtyard and sent the video to Saudi Arabian authorities. Both were arrested, sentenced to death, and beheaded. Their young daughter stood scattering soil on her parents’ graves, trying to understand what had happened.” The post received 643,400 views. The same video was also shared by multiple accounts on X and Facebook, as seen here, here, here, here, here, and here. However, the video predates the claim and is unrelated to the incident in Makkah. The same footage was shared on Facebook on May 26, 2026, with a Bangla caption that translates to: “Seeing the daughter’s tears, everyone started crying.” Furthermore, in a recent interview published by Bangladeshi news outlet Jagonews24, Abdul Bachir, the father of the man reportedly executed in Saudi Arabia, said his son was unmarried and that the woman executed alongside him was not his wife. The iVerify Pakistan team also identified the man’s Facebook account, which showed no mention of a marriage or photographs indicating that he was married. Therefore, the claim that a viral video shows the daughter of the couple executed in Saudi Arabia over an indecent act in a mosque is false. Viral video of Bangladeshi woman being beheaded over indecent acts in Makkah mosque On Oct 16, a US-based Bengali content creator shared a video on X allegedly showing a woman in a burqa being beheaded at a public square with the following caption: “Two Bangladeshis were executed by beheading yesterday inside a mosque in the holy city of Makkah, Saudi Arabia, for sexual offences.” The post attracted 3m views. An Indian journalist shared the same video in a similar context on Oct 20, gaining 895,000 views. Another Indian account shared the same video in a similar context with the following caption: “For giving a kiss, a husband and wife have had their heads cut off and been killed. Is this the religion that emphasises love and peace?” The video garnered 324,000 views. A Nigerian digital media outlet shared the same video in a similar claim with the details of the execution that happened on Oct 14, 2026. The post gained 205,000 views A reverse image search was conducted to trace the old visuals, which yielded the same visual shared by Dawn on January 27, 2015, in a news article titled: “A Saudi beheading, an IS beheading”. According to the news article, the visuals show Laila Bint Abdul Muttalib Basim, a Burmese woman living in Saudi Arabia, being publicly beheaded in Makkah after being accused of murdering and sexually abusing a seven-year-old girl. The child was reportedly her husband’s daughter from a previous marriage, making her Laila’s stepdaughter. The same visual with the same context was shared by several other mainstream international media outlets, such as Middle East Eye, Faras News, Time of Israel, and Europa Press. Therefore, the claim that a viral video shows a woman being beheaded over her indecent act in a mosque in Makkah is false. Images related to the two Bangladeshis Since October 18, a collage carrying six visuals has been shared by several users, including Bangladeshi users. The collage carries six images, with three questionable visuals. First, a man mourning over the alleged coffin of the executed couple. Second, faces of the executed man and woman. Third, the man and woman detained with faces blurred. A Bangladeshi user, based on its cover photo and past posts, shared the collage with the following caption: “A Pakistani Kulaungar citizen residing in Saudi Arabia conspired to secretly take a photo of two Bangladeshi citizens from behind and supplied the information to the 1st Saudi government, thereby assisting in the implementation of the death penalty. That Pakistan is Bangladesh’s sworn enemy from birth has once again been proven in this Saudi incident. I express my utter contempt.” The post gained 1.4m views. Another account shared the same collage with a caption: “Saudi Arabia enforced its laws after a man and woman committed indecent acts inside a mosque in Makkah; Islamic jurisprudence applied, sentences upheld, royal order carried out. If you don’t like Islamic jurisprudence, leave Saudi Arabia.” The post gained 27,632 views. The same image collage can also be seen here, here, and here. Other users also shared the same image in a similar context on Facebook, as can be seen here and here. For the first visual, a reverse image search yielded the same image shared by Bangladeshi news outlet Jagonews24 in an article dated June 16, 2019, titled: “He went abroad in a healthy body, but returned as a corpse before fulfilling his dreams”, which said expatriate deaths were rising, with statistics showing a 12% increase in 2018 compared to the previous year. According to the news article, the visual accompanied a report about Bangladeshi migrant workers who died abroad and whose bodies were repatriated to Bangladesh. The report specifically highlighted the case of a 35-year-old worker, Ratan, who died in Malaysia on June 11, 2019, following health complications. As for the second visual from the collage, a reverse image search yielded no credible news outlets that ran the images as being of the man and woman executed. Examining the visual using the SynthID detector, which identifies a digital watermark, showed that it had been generated using OpenAI. A forensic analysis of the third image was also conducted using the SynthID detector, which showed the image was edited or generated using Google AI. Fact-check status: false The claim that viral visuals show the Bangladeshi man and woman who were executed by Saudi authorities is false. Some of the visuals are old from unrelated incidents, while others have been doctored. This fact check was originally published by iVerify Pakistan— a project of CEJ-IBA and UNDP.

title: 'Apartheid automation': How Israel uses AI to monitor Palestinian land, movement and lives
description: From detecting changes to Palestinian homes to tracking people, systems expand Israel's surveillance in West Bank
content: From detecting changes to Palestinian homes through satellite imagery to scanning faces at military checkpoints and identifying people for deadly strikes, Israel's expanding use of artificial intelligence is raising concerns about how automated technology is being used to control Palestinian lives. In the occupied West Bank, AI-powered systems are helping Israeli authorities monitor land, buildings and movement, raising fears that the technology could facilitate demolitions and accelerate displacement. In Gaza, investigations have documented accounts of AI-generated lists of suspected targets being used to inform military strikes, with Israeli intelligence officers describing approval processes that sometimes took just seconds. Read: US Senate blocks measure demanding report on rights violations in West Bank "It's all apartheid automation," Mustafa Jarrar, professor of AI at Hamad Bin Khalifa University, and director of SinaLab, told Anadolu. "What is new now is that the AI is not only collecting and analysing, but also can make orders," he said. Palestinian researcher Jalal Abukhater warned that the expanding surveillance systems were helping reinforce Israeli control. "The pattern of behaviour, the movement, the people you speak to, it's all monitored and going to one purpose: to aid the Israeli occupation in dominating and controlling this population," Abukhater, the policy manager for Palestinian digital rights organisation 7amleh, told Anadolu. AI tool identifies changes to Palestinian land A September 17 report by Al Jazeera highlighted ImiSight, an AI-powered tool reportedly used to identify changes to buildings and land, helping Israeli authorities detect structures they consider unauthorised and target them for enforcement. Initially used in the Naqab desert, where Palestinian Bedouin citizens of Israel face restrictive building policies and demolitions, the technology has reportedly been introduced in the occupied West Bank, raising concerns about the use of automated surveillance to expand Israeli control over Palestinian land. Israeli media reported in January 2025, citing Israel Land Authority figures, that ImiSight helped survey about 10,735 square kilometres (4,145 square miles) in 2024. The authority said it opened about 495 enforcement proceedings following detections by the system and inspections on the ground. Enforcement operations contributed to the eviction of thousands of Palestinian Bedouin citizens of Israel. Jarrar explained that AI systems can compare satellite images taken at different times to detect changes to structures and flag them for further inspection, allowing authorities to identify buildings for potential enforcement action. Researcher Abukhater said that before such systems were deployed, the process required officials to inspect sites in person before authorities sent forces and bulldozers to demolish structures. “It would require, you know, human individuals going in to check and verifying,” Abukhater warned, adding that such technologies could accelerate demolitions and deepen Israeli control over Palestinian communities. Demolitions accelerate amid restrictions The technology's reported expansion comes amid rising demolitions of Palestinian structures in the occupied West Bank. Across the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, more than 1,100 structures had been demolished in 2026 by the time of United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)'s September reporting, displacing more than 1,500 Palestinians. According to OCHA data, the annual average number of structures demolished by Israel in Area C over lack of building permits rose about 80%, from 537 in 2010-2022 to 966 in 2023-2025. Area C accounts for roughly 60% of the West Bank and remains under full Israeli administrative and security control. Palestinians face severe restrictions on obtaining construction permits, leaving many structures vulnerable to demolition. Read More: UN official sounds alarm about Gaza, West Bank year after ceasefire In April 2025, an Israel Land Authority enforcement unit was established to operate in the West Bank, according to the UN. Israeli rights group Peace Now described the move as a step toward annexation, while the UN warned it would intensify discriminatory building-permit enforcement and deepen Palestinian displacement. In March 2025, ImiSight said its technology helped the authority identify unauthorised land use through satellite imagery, drones and aerial photography, reducing delays in enforcement. “Years of AI-driven insights have transformed enforcement operations, reducing delays and enabling rapid, effective action in the field!” the company said in a blog post. Abukhater estimated that the number of demolitions carried out since the introduction of these AI-supported systems has doubled. "These entire systems are designed in a way to entrench the occupation, to empower the occupation with tools that could accelerate its actions against Palestinian communities," he added. Facial recognition tracks Palestinians Surveillance extends beyond land and buildings to the people living in the occupied territory. In a May 2023 report, Amnesty International documented Israel's use of Red Wolf, a facial recognition system deployed at military checkpoints in Hebron. Red Wolf scans Palestinians' faces without their consent and compares them with biometric databases to help determine whether they can pass through checkpoints. Amnesty also documented the Blue Wolf smartphone application and Wolf Pack database, which Israeli forces use to collect and access information about Palestinians. The organisation said the systems reinforced restrictions on freedom of movement, particularly in Hebron's H2 area, which remains under Israeli control. It also documented extensive camera surveillance in occupied East Jerusalem, warning that facial recognition technology undermined privacy and discouraged political activity. Abukhater said Palestinians were being photographed at both checkpoints and during military raids on homes. "They just take a phone and take a photo of the person's face," he said, describing instances in which soldiers photographed Palestinians at checkpoints even when they did not present identification. He also described nighttime raids in which soldiers photographed residents, including children. "The soldiers have targets, and they are told that you should photograph 100 Palestinians a day," he added. Abukhater said the information gathered could be used to build extensive profiles of Palestinians, including their movements, relationships and personal histories. He described the wider system as "a big prison" and said Palestinians were subjected to surveillance that restricted their fundamental rights. Jarrar said information from cameras, smartphones and vehicle identification systems could be combined to build detailed profiles of individuals. He also said that Israeli forces hack Palestinians' private cameras. "You identify human, you identify car … different kinds of objects," he said. "You monitor them all the time and so you identify targets." He explained that AI could also detect unusual travel patterns, such as someone taking a different route between Ramallah and Nablus. “AI will detect a new pattern and will quickly, basically click alarms,” he said. From surveillance to military targeting Along with the system documented in the occupied West Bank primarily that involve monitoring and surveillance, investigations into Israel's operations in Gaza have raised separate concerns about AI-assisted military targeting. An April 2024 investigation by +972 Magazine and Local Call, based on interviews with six Israeli intelligence officers, reported that an AI system known as Lavender identified suspects as potential bombing targets, and marked as many as 37,000 Palestinians during the early stages of the war. One intelligence source described personnel acting as a "rubber stamp" for the system's recommendations, sometimes spending only about "20 seconds" reviewing a target before approving an attack. Also Read: Over 800 Palestinian teachers killed by Israel since Gaza war: education ministry Jarrar warned that such rapid approval processes could leave little room for meaningful scrutiny. "It's all fully automated," he said of the process he described, calling it "machine killing, basically." The investigation also identified a system known as Where's Daddy?, reportedly used to track suspected targets and determine when they entered their family homes. With the system, according to the award-winning NAZA documentary, a phrase as simple as “daddy’s home,” can trigger a bombing. Jarrar said the wider use of such technologies should concern governments and researchers beyond the region. "Israel is actually pushing and encouraging other countries to do the same," he said. "It's being a model." Abukhater warned that the spread of such technologies could accelerate violations against Palestinians in the West Bank as well. "My concern is that these tools are accelerating the plans of ethnic cleansing, of entrenching the occupation, of solidifying the annexation of Palestinian territory in the occupied West Bank," he said. Technology companies face scrutiny The expanding use of surveillance technology has also raised questions about international companies providing digital services to Israeli security agencies. Microsoft came under scrutiny in 2025 after The Guardian reported that an Israeli military intelligence unit used its Azure cloud platform to store recordings of Palestinian phone calls collected through surveillance in Gaza and the West Bank. On September 25, 2025, Microsoft said a review had found evidence supporting elements of the reporting, including the use of Azure storage in the Netherlands and AI services. The company disabled specified cloud-storage and AI services used by a unit within Israel's Defence Ministry, saying its terms prohibited mass surveillance of civilians. "This is a direct complicity by private company actors with Israeli state actors who are directly violating rights," Abukhater said. "It's something that these companies should be held accountable for." Jarrar also urged stronger international rules governing the use of AI in military operations. "We need really a new international law regarding the use of AI in automated killing," he said.

title: US VP Vance says staying out of Israel vote as Trump backs Netanyahu
description: 'I am not anti-endorsing him. I'm not pro-endorsing him. I'm not getting involved in Israeli elections'
content: United States Vice President JD Vance said he would not be following Donald Trump in endorsing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and wanted to stay on the sidelines. "I'm not anti-endorsing him. I'm not pro-endorsing him. I'm not getting involved in Israeli elections," Vance said of Netanyahu, in an interview Monday with journalist Mark Halperin. "I endorse American candidates, and that's where I'm focused on is the (US) midterms," he added. Trump on Sunday issued a public endorsement of his right-wing ally Netanyahu, who is seeking a new term as premier in Israel's October 27 parliamentary election. Vance's reticence to weigh in on the Israeli vote contrasts with his approach to European elections. Read: Vance acknowledges 'failures' in US handling of Iran war Days before Hungary's parliamentary election in April, he flew to Budapest to support then-prime minister Viktor Orban, another right-wing figure. He has also voiced support for Germany's far-right AfD party, whose leader, Alice Weidel, he met last year. Vance, who is widely viewed as aiming to succeed Trump in 2029, reportedly expressed opposition to launching the US-Israeli war with Iran, but has since defended the campaign. The vice president also had notably strong words for Israeli officials who criticised a short-lived US-Iran ceasefire agreement in June. "Trump is the only head of state in the entire world who is sympathetic to the nation of Israel at this moment," he said at the time. "If I was in the cabinet of the Israeli government, I might not be attacking the only powerful ally that I have anywhere left in the entire world," he added.

title: Trump's approval falls to record low of 31% as midterms near, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
description: Democrats lead Republicans 47% to 35% on congressional generic ballot, 68% disapprove of Trump's handling of economy
content: President Donald ‌Trump's approval rating fell to a record low as Americans worried about high gasoline prices and appeared ready to punish his Republican Party in the November 3 congressional elections, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that closed on Monday. Some 31% of Americans approve of Trump's ​performance in office, down a percentage point from two weeks earlier and the lowest level in ​either of his presidential terms, the four-day poll showed. Trump approval at record low Reuters/Ipsos polls gather responses from adults nationwide Asked which party they would vote ⁠for if the congressional elections were held today in what is known as a "generic ballot" question, some ​47% of registered voters in the nationwide poll picked Democrats and 35% chose Republicans. The 12-point Democratic advantage ​was the widest over the current election cycle and could bolster Democratic hopes of seizing control of the US House of Representatives and the US Senate. For Republicans, losing control of either chamber could complicate Trump's agenda in the last two years ​of his term. Generic ballot polls are national polls that provide an overall view of which party poll respondents ​want to see in charge in Congress. While these polls provide a view of national public sentiment, they do not ‌capture ⁠all the nuances of the state-by-state and district-by-district contests that determine control of the Senate and House, contests in which Republicans hold some structural advantages. A Reuters/Ipsos poll two weeks earlier showed Democrats leading Republicans by 7 points, 44% to 37%. Which party do Americans want to run Congress?
