Reuters/Ipsos poll of registered US voters nationwide Much of the drop in support for Republican congressional candidates was due to a larger ​share of women saying they ​would pick Democrats. Some ⁠50% of female voters said they would vote Democratic, compared to 32% eyeing Republican candidates. Men also favored Democrats, but by a smaller margin. Trump's popularity has suffered ​since he ordered military strikes on Iran in February alongside US ally Israel. ​The war ⁠triggered a surge in gasoline prices, hitting household finances. Some 68% of Americans disapprove of Trump's handling of the economy, including 37% of self-identified Republicans. Voters in the poll picked Democrats over Republicans as the better stewards of the ⁠economy, by ​40% to 33%. The survey, which was conducted online, gathered responses ​from 1,679 US adults, including 1,279 registered voters. The poll's results had a margin of error of 2 percentage points for all respondents ​and 3 points for registered voters.

title: Declared dead: Indian voters fight to get back on electoral rolls
description: Around 130 million names removal from India's electoral rolls under a revision has ‌sparked mass protests
content: Kamta Prasad has been shuttling between government offices in Delhi, trying to prove he ​is not dead. The 53-year-old tailor is among 130 million names removed from India's electoral rolls under a voter roll revision that has ‌sparked mass protests and posed the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has led to removals for reasons ranging from "logical discrepancies" to people being recorded as dead, leaving many such as Prasad struggling to get more than just their voting status restored. He has had to forgo his daily wage of 250 rupees ($2.63) that supports his family of four ​to scurry around the city to reverse the error. "I panicked when I heard about it," said Prasad, who is among 4.2m Delhi voters ​struck off the list, according to the draft rolls published by the poll body on August 31. "Since then I've been ⁠going everywhere to prove that I'm alive." Read: India's 'cockroach' movement founder released a day after detention The deletions have triggered a political storm, with opposition parties and youth groups staging near-daily protests in New Delhi and elsewhere, ​which have been met with force by the police. They allege Election Commission chief Gyanesh Kumar manipulated the revision to benefit Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), a charge denied by ​both the commission and the BJP. 'Nobody listens' According to Rajendra Kumar, a volunteer with non-profit Jan Sarokar, about 2,000 of the roughly 9,000 voters in Prasad's block were struck off after the revision, classified as absent, shifted, deceased or registered elsewhere. Prasad is the only person in this block who has been declared dead, but several similar cases have been reported by local media ​across the country. The Election Commission has said it was removing duplicate, deceased, shifted and otherwise ineligible voters and that anyone excluded in error can file claims, ​submit supporting documents and pursue appeals before the rolls are finalised. For voters such as Prasad, however, exclusion leads to a bureaucratic maze, and depending on the circumstances they may have ‌to provide ⁠proof of life, establish residency, correct alleged discrepancies or submit fresh documentation. That involves repeated visits to election offices, hearings before electoral officials and multiple rounds of appeals, with some spending weeks or months trying to restore their names. Read more: Imran Khan challenges 'unconstitutional' exit notice in Bombay High Court "I told them I voted in the last assembly and general elections and have been voting for 35 years, but nobody listens," Prasad said. India's Election Commission did not reply to a request for comment for this story. Register as a new voter Following weeks of protests, ​the Election Commission ordered fresh verification in ​some states, including Delhi, and Prasad ⁠said officials had assured him his name would be restored. Kamal Lal, a 38-year-old private school teacher in Delhi, was marked as "shifted" even though he still lives in a settlement beneath a flyover with dozens of other families. "It is very disappointing ​that we have been voting in this country and now our names have been cut because we do not ​have land papers or ⁠a water bill," he said. Lal said he first learned of his exclusion in September and has since approached election officials, attended hearings and filed multiple reinstatement applications. For some excluded voters, the remedy offered by officials has brought little comfort: rather than restoring their previous registrations, they were advised to apply afresh as new voters. For poorer voters, ⁠fears run even ​deeper. "Now local election officials are asking us to register as new voters, and my husband is ​strongly opposed to that because he has voted in the last few elections," said 39-year-old Mamta, who does not use a surname. "I am worried that if our names are not restored to the ​list, I could lose access to subsidised ration and other government welfare schemes."

title: Meet the heat storm: 7 takeaways from Reuters investigation that gave supersized heat waves a new name
description: A data-driven examination of global temperatures shows heat waves have surged in size and frequency since the 1960s
content: Heat waves have evolved from sporadic, isolated episodes to massive, cascading weather events that can blanket vast swaths of the planet for months or even years at a time. To continue calling such sprawling phenomena “heat waves” would be like calling a monsoon a rain shower. To understand the new reality of these immense expanses of heat, Reuters consulted with two dozen climate researchers and analysed temperatures around the globe for every hour of every day since 1960. From those results, we developed a new concept: the “heat storm.” Scientists and researchers often discuss global warming in the context of risks that will arise if the planet’s average global temperature rises more than 2°C (3.6°F) above pre-industrial levels. What is an ordinary person to make of that? Not much. Heat waves are the connective tissue between the science of global warming and our everyday experience. But supersized heat waves used to be rare. No longer. Now they swarm the planet. 2020s: The 10 largest heat storms mark a new era, with massive, cascading heat events touching virtually every person on the planet. Illustration: Reuters Naming events is “a powerful way for people to understand that something is happening”, Anthony Leiserowitz, director of the Yale Programme on Climate Change Communication, told Reuters. Yet “we don't currently do that with heat waves”, he said, even though heat has been estimated to kill almost half a million people a year. These are the key findings of the Reuters investigation, The Age of Heat Storms: What is a heat storm? There is no universal definition of a heat wave. So, in consultation with climate scientists, we have defined an ordinary heat wave as five or more consecutive days of abnormally high temperatures. We call the largest heat waves — those that at their peak cover at least 1% of the globe, roughly half the size of Canada — heat storms. More and bigger Heat storms were rare in the 1960s, when they averaged about five active storms per year. This decade, heat storms have averaged about 102 a year. One of them caused this summer’s deadly heat in Europe. Read: Heatwave in Karachi leaves eight dead, rescue confirms Biography of a 367-day heat storm The largest heat storm on record, named Heat Storm Vera, lasted for 367 days over 2023-2024 and swept over nearly 85% of the globe. Reuters tells the story of how Vera impacted every corner of the world, from a football player going to the hospital in Texas, to Amazonian river dolphins dying in a “circus of death", to a cocoa farmer whose livelihood was destroyed in Ivory Coast. After heat storms battered Bolivia in October 2023, Lake Titicaca, one of South America’s largest lakes, edged towards record low levels. Photo: REUTERS Greenhouse gas emissions As greenhouse gas emissions have increased, so too have heat storms and ordinary heat waves. From the 1960s to this decade, the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere has increased by more than 30%. Over that time, the average portion of the planet likely to be covered by heat storms and heat waves has risen more than 12-fold. 18 years without a break Another new phenomenon we identified: heat storms that run consecutively, simultaneously, or both — heat storm cascades. The duration of these cascades swelled from an average of roughly two months in the 1960s to nine months in the early 2000s. Then, on July 6, 2008, a cascade started — and still has not stopped. For more than 18 years straight, at least one heat storm has been roiling the planet, and often more than one. We are in a heat storm now The world is now in the grip of Heat Storm Raimundo, which broiled Europe and stoked massive wildfires in Spain and France this summer. Since its inception on February 28, 2026, Raimundo has touched almost three-quarters of the planet’s surface. Live tool to track heat storms As part of this series, Reuters has created an online Heat Storm Tracker that names and follows heat storms in real time. This is now a feature of the Reuters Climate Monitor, which offers several ways to understand major weather events and measure how the planet is warming.

title: Trump says military execution of Fort Hood shooter will not be livestreamed
description: Though the immediate families of the victims will be able to view it in person
content: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the ​execution of the Fort Hood gunman would not ‌be livestreamed, but that immediate families of the victims would be able to view it in person. "I think streaming the ​execution for all to see might have been ​a strong deterrent for the world to ⁠witness how America deals with terrorists and scum ​like Hasan but, many very good and well-meaning ​people would rather not watch him die, through streaming, or through any other visual device," Trump wrote. "He will die, ​as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event ​will not be streamed. That said, the execution may be viewed ‌in ⁠person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose. They deserve to witness justice!" pic.twitter.com/9J8IA5wPL1 — Rapid Response 47 (@RapidResponse47) October 15, 2026 Some of Trump's fellow Republicans, including Vice President JD ​Vance, as ​well as ⁠religious leaders and international observers, had expressed doubts about the Pentagon's plan to ​livestream the December 3 execution of ​Nidal Hasan. ⁠ Recent polls have also shown a majority of Americans opposed livestreaming it. Hasan, a former US Army psychiatrist, ⁠was ​found guilty in a military ​trial of fatally shooting 13 people at Fort Hood in Texas ​in 2009.

title: Pope Leo back on his feet after shock cancer diagnosis
description: Blood tests, chest X-ray show normal post-operative results after part of Pope Leo's right lung removed in operation
content: Pope Leo's recovery from surgery is progressing as expected, and ​he has begun walking in his hospital room and eating normally, the Vatican said on Wednesday, after doctors announced the 71-year-old pontiff was being ‌treated for lung cancer. World leaders, Catholics across the globe and senior cardinals at the Vatican have offered prayers for Leo after he had part of his right lung removed in an operation on Tuesday. Blood tests and a chest X-ray carried out on Wednesday showed normal post-operative results, the Vatican said, adding that the pontiff had undergone respiratory physiotherapy. JUST IN: Pope Leo is back on his feet after surgery as doctors confirm his recovery is progressing as expected. The Holy Father has begun walking around his room, resumed eating regular meals, and undergone respiratory physiotherapy following his lung procedure. Dr. Luigi… pic.twitter.com/a94O8Gvlo3 — Fox News (@FoxNews) October 14, 2026 Read: Pope Leo admitted to Rome hospital for lung surgery The cancer diagnosis for a pope known to be relatively young and energetic ​and who was elected only in May 2025 caused shock and raised questions about the future shape of his papacy as he deals with the illness. Leo normally ​follows a very busy schedule. He is due to make a tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17 ⁠, and the Vatican press office said on Wednesday that "nothing has changed" regarding the planned trip. However, Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori said on Wednesday that the dates could change because of the ​amount of time his recovery would take. The pope is the ultimate earthly authority for the world's 1.4 billion Catholics and does not have a deputy who steps in when ​he is sick. When a pope is incapacitated, the business of the Vatican's vast bureaucracy carries on as usual, holding off on any decisions that require papal approval. Prayers for Leo A prayer was recited for Leo to have a good convalescence and complete healing during an open-air Mass in St Peter's Square on Wednesday following the surgery. The pope has been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of ​lung cancer, and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung during Tuesday's operation in an effort to eliminate all cancerous tissue. Human lungs have five lobes — three ​in the right lung and two in the left. The operation lasted about 90 minutes and was completed without complications, the pope's lead surgeon, Professor Stefano Margaritora, and his personal physician, Dr Luigi Carbone, said ‌late on ⁠Tuesday. Pope Leo XIV underwent thoracic surgery at Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, as planned, according to a statement from Dr. Luigi Carbone and Professor Stefano Margaritora released by the Holy See Press Office. The surgeons removed the lower lobe of the Pope’s right lung,… pic.twitter.com/QAShHu1eG6 — Vatican News (@VaticanNews) October 13, 2026 The Vatican has not disclosed the size of the tumour or whether the disease had spread to nearby lymph nodes, key factors in determining prognosis. Read More: Pope Leo diagnosed with cancer Dr Serena Ricciardi, a lung cancer specialist at Rome's San Camillo Forlanini Hospital, said that if the cancer had not spread to Leo's lymph nodes, the surgery may have been sufficient for treatment. "If there are no further issues or lymph node involvement, we could consider the surgery curative," she told Reuters. "The disease has been completely removed." Leo is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys ​sports, including tennis, and is not known ​to be a smoker or to have ⁠had recent health issues. Engagements cancelled until next week The Vatican said this week that the pope was expected to remain in hospital for about a week and that all his public engagements had been cancelled until October 20. The Mass on Wednesday was the closing act ​of an assembly of bishops called by Leo to discuss the Church's family life teachings, the largest gathering of Church leaders ​so far during this ⁠papacy. Filipino Cardinal Luis Tagle led the service in place of Leo. The pope last week approved Tagle as the dean of the Church's College of Cardinals, in the first selection of an Asian cleric to the elite role. Pope Leo calls on us to take to heart the riches of ‘Amoris laetitia’ In a homily read by Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, Pope Leo XIV called on the Church to put the Apostolic Exhortation's pastoral guidance into practice in the heart of families. The homily was delivered at the… pic.twitter.com/XCa1Gsl97l — Vatican News (@VaticanNews) October 14, 2026 Political leaders offered messages of support. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he and his wife Jeanette were praying for the pope, an American who was born ⁠in Chicago. "May the ​Lord give him strength and the Holy Spirit guide the medical professionals taking care of the Holy ​Father," he said on X. Rubio met Leo at the Vatican in May. Jeanette and I are united in prayer for @PONTIFEX’s health following his recent diagnosis. May the Lord give him strength and the Holy Spirit guide the medical professionals taking care of the Holy Father. https://t.co/KPVoGrnKUW — Secretary Marco Rubio (@SecRubio) October 13, 2026 There was no immediate response on social media from US President Donald Trump, who has criticised the pope, or from Vice President JD Vance, who ​is a Catholic.

title: Greta Thunberg joins French teens on new day of school protests
description: Protest movement over teacher shortages, classroom overcrowding, crumbling school buildings enters its fourth week
content: Swedish activist Greta Thunberg joined protesters outside a high school in a working-class ‌suburb of Paris on Tuesday as French pupils took to the streets for another day of demonstrations over poor learning conditions. Now in its fourth week, the nationwide protest movement over teacher shortages, classroom overcrowding and crumbling school buildings has involved marches, blockades of hundreds of schools and, in some cases, clashes with police. Pupils clustered outside several schools in Paris and other cities on Tuesday morning, ​brandishing placards and megaphones. Read: France's high school students plan fresh protests "We are inspired by the young people who are demanding their basic rights," Greta told reporters outside Lycee Paul Eluard in ​Saint-Denis, north of Paris, one of the schools where the protest movement first gained traction. Climate and social justice activist Greta Thunberg joined students at a high school in the Paris suburb of Saint-Denis, as France faced a new day of nationwide marches and strikes on top of the blockades at schools. pic.twitter.com/gC3Zx4x3Cn — The Associated Press (@AP) October 13, 2026 "Whether it's not funding schools enough, or ⁠the climate crisis, or social injustice crises ... it's about time that young people are stepping up and reclaiming that future," she said. Mostly peaceful protests, with outbreaks of ​violence Large crowds marched peacefully through Nantes in the west, Strasbourg in the east and Marseille in the south, holding hand-made signs with slogans such as "Tear gas doesn't make ​us cry as much as the state of the national education system". Marchers were also mustering in Paris. Footage from BFM TV showed clashes between people dressed in black and riot police in Strasbourg and Nantes, with clouds of tear gas in some streets. In Lyon, the local authorities asked organisers to call off a march after a group of "hostile individuals" preceding the main procession ​vandalised shops and a petrol station and clashed with police. While there was no immediate information on who was involved, it is not uncommon in France for street ​protests to attract so-called "casseurs", a fringe of rioters who seek to confront police and destroy property. Read More: French policing under scrutiny as student protest injuries mount The scene was calmer in front of Paris city hall, where a youth orchestra played Antonin ‌Dvorak's "New World ⁠Symphony". Some musicians had protest stickers on their cellos and violins. The education ministry said 214 schools were closed, down from 800 on a similar protest day a week ago. It said 94.2% of high schools were open. The cash-strapped government has promised to act to address the pupils' concerns, but has little room for manoeuvre at a time when concerns over the national debt and the budget deficit are pushing up borrowing costs to the highest level in years. It has expressed sympathy with the students' grievances, but has ​deployed riot police to quell the protests, ​leading to confrontations in which hundreds ⁠of people have been injured and thousands arrested. Political polarisation ahead of election The government suspended the use of stun grenades last week after one teenager lost a hand. Six months ahead of a presidential election, the protest movement and the police response have elicited polarised ​responses from leading contenders to replace Emmanuel Macron. "The police are losing their breath running after young people to beat ​them up and injure ⁠them," said hard-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon, who has a chance of making the runoff according to opinion polls, in a post on X on Tuesday. La hargne médiatique s'essouffle dans son invisibilisation des violences policières. Le ministre s'essouffle à fermer les lycées. Les policiers s'essoufflent à courir derrière les jeunes pour les tabasser et les blesser. Seuls les jeunes ne s'essoufflent pas à protester… — Jean-Luc Mélenchon (@JLMelenchon) October 13, 2026 "The only ones not losing their breath are the young people bravely protesting," he added, accusing the media of failing to show the extent of police brutality and renewing his call for adults to stand ⁠with the ​students to protect them. Far-right leader Marine Le Pen, the frontrunner in the presidential race according to polls, ​has denounced violence by protesters and called for those who have damaged schools — or their parents if they are minors — to pay for repairs. The government has already introduced a bill that would allow precisely ​that. It is going through parliament.

title: Trump says ‘it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president’ who can ‘make a deal’ with Russia
description: Criticises Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, warning they could worsen fuel shortages and hurt US farmers
content: US President Donald Trump on Saturday called for Ukraine to “get a new president,” accusing Volodymyr Zelenskyy of repeatedly failing to reach a deal to end the war with Russia. “I suggest they get a new leader who can make a deal, because he could have made many deals that, for some reason, he never does,” Trump said, criticising the Ukrainian leader. “I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president,” he added. Trump argued that the Russia-Ukraine war could have been avoided. Read More: 11 killed, including three children, in overnight Russia-Ukraine strikes “If I were president, you wouldn't have ever had that war. That war would have never started,” he said. The US president also accused Zelenskyy of missing multiple opportunities to end the conflict. “Zelenskyy could have settled this war many times, many, many times, and he chooses not to,” Trump said, describing the situation as “very difficult”. Trump also criticised Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure, arguing that attacks on refineries could worsen global fuel shortages and affect American farmers and ranchers. “We told them, do whatever you want, but don't hit the diesel fuel because there's a big problem. Big shortage,” he said.

title: UAE says Omani flydubai co-pilot planned suicide attack on Tel Aviv flight
description: UAE prosecutors says flydubai co-pilot drew inspiration from 9/11 and studied the Tel Aviv route
content: An Omani flydubai co-pilot had intended to seize a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight and crash it into a terminal at Israel's Ben Gurion airport on September 30 in a suicide attack before he was thwarted by his fellow pilot, the UAE attorney general said on Friday, according to the state news agency. The statement by Attorney General Hamad Saif al Shamsi did not appear to implicate flydubai in any wrongdoing, and contained the most detailed account yet from prosecutors about what happened. Flydubai was not immediately available for comment. The UAE attorney general said the Omani co-pilot of the Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv planned to hijack the aircraft and carry out a suicide attack on a terminal at Ben Gurion Airport. The suspect confessed to acting alone, but authorities are investigating possible… pic.twitter.com/llMwjKMPGH — Clash Report (@clashreport) October 9, 2026 The suspect "had begun carrying out a premeditated terrorist plot to seize control of the aircraft and use it to launch a suicide attack targeting the passenger terminal at Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv, with the aim of causing the greatest possible loss of life", Al Shamsi said. Read More: Flydubai co-pilot attacked pilot with axe, attempted 'terrorist attack', UAE says The plan was inspired by the September 11, 2001, attacks on the US, UAE public prosecutors think, as a result of their criminal investigation launched on October 1. It found the suspect had used two previous flights to Tel Aviv to "familiarise himself with the flight route and the airport", the state news agency WAM reported. It is the first public confirmation of the co-pilot's 9/11 inspiration. The incident caused the jet to plunge 4,900 metres in 30 seconds. Al Shamsi said the suspect had previously worked for several airlines in different countries, including Oman Air and Royal Air Maroc, before joining flydubai in January 2026. Saudi Arabia has launched a separate safety investigation into flight FZ1073's incident, sources told Reuters. The aircraft was in Saudi airspace when the Omani co-pilot attacked the aircraft's captain with a crash axe, typically kept in the cockpit for use during emergencies.

title: Navi Pillay: Nobel laureate who led UN inquiry that found genocide in Gaza
description: She chaired a UN commission probing violations by all sides in the Occupied Palestinian Territory and Israel
content: Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, the South African jurist who led a UN inquiry that concluded Israel had committed genocide against Palestinians in Gaza, was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize on Friday. The Norwegian Nobel Committee honoured the 85-year-old “for her efforts to promote peace and international law”, placing particular emphasis on her career holding states and political leaders accountable. Pillay’s work on Gaza became one of the most consequential and controversial chapters of that career. From 2021 until November 2025, she chaired the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel. Established by the UN Human Rights Council, the commission investigated violations committed by all sides and collected evidence that could be used in future legal proceedings. Its first major report following October 7, 2023, found in June 2024 that Israeli authorities were responsible for war crimes and crimes against humanity during military operations in Gaza. It also concluded that Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups committed war crimes during their attacks in Israel, including deliberately killing civilians and taking hostages. Read More: South Africa's Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize “It is imperative that all those who have committed crimes be held accountable,” Pillay said at the time, arguing that adherence to international law was the only way to end recurring cycles of violence and retaliation. The commission’s investigation later focused on Israel’s attacks on hospitals and the broader destruction of Gaza’s healthcare system. In October 2024, it accused Israeli forces of deliberately attacking medical facilities and personnel, as well as mistreating Palestinian detainees. “By targeting healthcare facilities, Israel is targeting the right to health itself,” Pillay said, warning that the destruction would have lasting consequences for Gaza’s civilian population. “Children in particular have borne the brunt of these attacks, suffering both directly and indirectly from the collapse of the health system,” she added. ‘Absence of action amounts to complicity’ In September 2025, the commission issued its most far-reaching conclusion: that Israeli authorities and security forces had committed four of the five acts defined as genocide under the 1948 Genocide Convention. These included killing members of a protected group, causing serious bodily or mental harm, deliberately imposing conditions calculated to bring about the group’s physical destruction and taking measures intended to prevent births. The commission also concluded that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, President Isaac Herzog and former defence minister Yoav Gallant had incited genocide and that Israeli authorities had failed to punish them for it. Pillay said the evidence showed “an intent to destroy the Palestinians in Gaza” and placed responsibility with Israeli authorities at the highest levels. She also directed criticism at governments continuing to arm or politically support Israel. “When clear signs and evidence of genocide emerge, the absence of action to stop it amounts to complicity,” she said. The commission called on states to halt transfers of weapons and equipment that could be used to commit genocidal acts, prevent companies and individuals under their jurisdiction from contributing to them and support accountability proceedings. Israel rejected the findings, accused the commission of bias and maintained that its military campaign targeted Hamas rather than the Palestinian population. The commission’s determination was not a binding judicial ruling and it did not speak for the UN as a whole. The International Court of Justice is separately considering South Africa’s genocide case against Israel. Pillay stepped down from the commission in November 2025, citing her age, medical issues and other commitments. From apartheid to international justice Born in Durban in 1941 into a South African family of Indian origin, Pillay began her legal career under apartheid, when racial and gender discrimination restricted both her professional opportunities and the rights of her clients. In 1967, she became the first woman to establish a law practice in the province of Natal. She represented anti-apartheid activists and trade unionists, exposed allegations of torture and helped secure rights for political prisoners held on Robben Island. Her work attracted the attention of apartheid-era security authorities, and she was denied a passport for years. After apartheid ended, President Nelson Mandela appointed Pillay as an acting judge on the South African High Court in 1995, making her its first non-white woman judge. That same year, she joined the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, later serving as its president. Pillay sat on the panel that decided the landmark case against Jean-Paul Akayesu, the first conviction for genocide by an international tribunal. The judgment also established that rape and sexual violence could constitute acts of genocide when committed with the intention of destroying a protected group, an enduring contribution to international criminal law. Pillay subsequently served as a judge at the International Criminal Court from 2003 to 2008 and as UN high commissioner for human rights from 2008 to 2014. She currently serves as an ad hoc judge at the International Court of Justice in The Gambia’s genocide case against Myanmar. Announcing the award, the Nobel Committee said Pillay’s career demonstrated how international law could provide accountability for victims and offer an alternative to violence at a time when courts and legal institutions were facing growing political attacks. The Nobel Peace Prize, carrying an award of 12 million Swedish kronor ($1.2 million), will be presented in Oslo on December 10.

title: US F-16 crashes at Spangdahlem air base in Germany
description: Fire and disaster units sent to the scene, one person injured
content: A US F-16 fighter jet crashed on Tuesday near Spangdahlem Air Base in western Germany, military authorities said in a statement. The jet, assigned to the 52nd Fighter Wing, went down at about 2:30pm local time (1230GMT), according to the military base's press office. “The pilot ejected safely and is receiving medical care,” it said. “The cause of the incident is under investigation. Additional information will be released as it becomes available.” Earlier today, the Eifelkreis Bitburg-Pruem district said fire and disaster protection units had been sent to the scene. “According to current knowledge, one person was injured,” the district administration said, adding that it could not provide additional details. Several residents told reporters they saw a large black column of smoke after the jet went down. Regional outlets also published pictures of the plume. Read More: All Iranian airlines to shut down worldwide by Sept 23, US Treasury chief says A spokesperson for Germany’s air traffic control agency told public broadcaster SWR that the crash happened after a training exercise involving four aircraft. Two were returning Spangdahlem when the first crashed. The other three diverted to Ramstein Air Base. Spangdahlem Air Base lies about 30 kilometres north of Trier in the state of Rhineland-Palatinate in West Germany. It is home to an F-16 squadron of the US 52nd Fighter Wing. The base has seen previous F-16 crashes. In October 2019, an F-16 crashed during a training flight after a power failure shortly after takeoff; the pilot ejected and was lightly injured. In September 2006, another F-16 crashed in the Bitburg-Pruem district. No one was injured.

title: Nobel prize sum raised to $1.27m for 2026
description: Nobel prize hike adds $106,000, with the sum shared if more than one laureate wins in a category
content: This year's Nobel Prize winners, to be announced from October 5-12, will receive 12 million kroner ($1.27m) per discipline, up from 11m in 2025, the Nobel Foundation said on Friday. The hike is equivalent to around $106,000 or 9 per cent more and the sum is shared if there is more than one laureate in any of the six prize categories. "This year, we are celebrating the 125th anniversary of the Nobel Prize, and in connection with this, we are pleased to be able to increase the prize amount by one million (kroner)," the director of the Nobel Foundation, Hanna Stjarne, said in a statement. "By increasing the prize amount, we uphold the long-term significance of the Nobel Prize and ensure that the financial part of the prize retains its value over time," she said. Read More: Sweden's centre-left wins election The first Nobel prizes were awarded in 1901, when the prize sum was 150,782 kroner per discipline. The medicine prize will kick off this year's Nobel week on October 5, followed each day by the prizes for physics, chemistry, literature and peace. The economics prize will wrap up the announcements on October 12. Winners of this year's prizes in physics, chemistry, peacemaking, literature, economics and medicine or physiology will be announced between October 5 and October 12, marking the 125th anniversary of the first awards. Established by the will of Swedish 19th-century businessman Alfred Nobel, the inventor of dynamite, the first awards in 1901 were for 150,782 crowns per category, according to the foundation.

title: PSX gains 779 points amid partial recovery
description: Draft auto policy, US-Iran de-escalation hopes bolster confidence
content: Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) rebounded on Wednesday as institutional investors returned to buy select stocks following recent weakness, while expectations of progress in diplomatic efforts to ease US-Iran tensions helped improve sentiment. The session commenced on a relatively healthy note and the KSE-100 index hit 165,845.69, up 694 points by 9.33 am. Adding to the positive tone, a committee reviewing Pakistan's Automotive and Auto Parts Manufacturing Policy 2026-31 proposed a broad set of reforms to boost exports, including preferential sales tax rates for new energy vehicles (NEVs), covering both locally assembled and imported cars. The bourse touched the intra-day high of 166,242.43 and low of 164,731.91 while mostly trading in the green. At close, the benchmark KSE-100 index posted gains of 779.34 points, or 0.47%, and settled at 165,930.99. According to KTrade Securities, the KSE-100 rose 779 points (+0.5%), a partial recovery with subdued trading volumes of 130 million shares. Activity remained concentrated in refinery, investment companies and securities, and technology and communication sectors, while selective buying in power generation, commercial banks and oil and gas exploration stocks provided support. Sector-specific performance was positive, where commercial banks, power, cement and autos contributed to the index's gains. However, weakness in Attock Refinery, Fatima Fertiliser, Engro Holdings, Fauji Cement and Millat Tractors partially offset the advance. Meanwhile, Brent crude remained elevated at $110/barrel, causing macroeconomic uncertainty and tempering the risk appetite. "We expect the market to remain range bound amid cautious investor sentiment, with near-term direction driven by oil-price movements, geopolitical developments and corporate earnings," KTrade wrote. "The market gained momentum amid renewed institutional buying, driven by optimism over intensified diplomatic efforts to resolve the US-Iran conflict and expectations of easing geopolitical tensions. Additionally, the prime minister's approval of the draft auto policy for 2026-31 brought auto stocks back into investors' focus," Arif Habib Limited Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib wrote. The proposed auto policy aims to boost automotive exports to $6 billion through tariff rationalisation, localisation and EV incentives. The draft also envisages export-linked incentives and stricter safety standards, subject to requisite approvals. Hub Power, Habib Bank, UBL, OGDC, Mari Energies, PPL, Fauji Fertiliser, Sazgar Engineering, Lucky Cement and NCPL were the major contributors, adding 711 points to the index. Overall trading volumes decreased to 379.9 million shares from 446.8 million a day ago. The value of traded shares stood at Rs21.3 billion.

title: Cash flow data could unlock SME financing
description: Digital banking service targets small and medium businesses
content: Verifiable sales records and digital cash flows could help Pakistani small businesses overcome a major barrier to bank financing: their inability to demonstrate reliable financial performance, as digital banking platforms seek to bring undocumented businesses into the formal financial system. A large number of Pakistan's micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) operate without formal registration or digitised accounts, making it difficult for banks to assess their creditworthiness. Consequently, lenders often demand collateral, which many small businesses cannot provide. Speaking at the launch of NEO BIZ, a digital banking service for SMEs, Mashreq Bank Pakistan CEO Muhammad Hamayun Sajjad said businesses often maintained bookkeeping records that banks did not consider reliable enough for lending decisions. Pakistan has approximately 7.14 million MSMEs, contributing nearly 40% to gross domestic product (GDP), 30% to exports and employing more than 80% of the non-agricultural workforce. However, outstanding SME financing stood at around Rs882 billion as of December 2025, according to figures cited at the event. Digital-first banking models could help bridge this gap by creating verifiable records of business transactions, including sales, payments and collections. Banks could use these records to assess turnover, analyse cash-flow patterns and evaluate repayment capacity, potentially enabling creditworthy businesses without conventional financial statements to access loans. However, digital records alone would not guarantee financing, as lenders would still need to assess profitability, liabilities and business risks. NEO BIZ like services offer digital business account opening and management, payments and collections. Its broader roadmap includes transaction analytics, invoicing, bookkeeping, payroll solutions and business debit and virtual cards. The planned development also includes cash-flow-based financing, tax facilitation and supply-chain services. Whether these features translate into increased lending will depend on their implementation and banks' credit policies. "Pakistan's SME sector is both dynamic and under-served, with significant gaps in access, awareness and digital capability," Sajjad said, adding that the platform was intended to simplify banking and reduce reliance on physical channels. The initiative comes amid a longstanding debate over whether banks' substantial exposure to government borrowing crowds out private-sector lending. Banks have argued that the relationship is not straightforward, maintaining that they can obtain liquidity through the State Bank of Pakistan open market operations (OMOs) while holding government securities and extending credit to businesses.

title: Oil-driven inflation fears keep gold subdued
description: Safe-haven asset falls Rs900/tola despite global uptick; rupee edges up
content: Gold prices in Pakistan fell by Rs900 per tola on Wednesday to Rs434,536, despite a slight recovery in international markets, as oil-driven inflation concerns and tensions in the Middle East weighed on investor sentiment. According to the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association, the price of 24-karat gold per 10 grams declined by Rs772 to Rs372,544. Similarly, 22-karat gold per 10 grams dropped by Rs707 to Rs341,511. The domestic market's decline came even as spot gold in the US edged up 0.1% to $4,127.31 per ounce by 1510 GMT, recovering slightly after touching its lowest level since October 15 earlier in the session, as per Reuters. US gold futures for December delivery also rose 0.1% to $4,145.20 per ounce. International bullion prices remained near a one-week low as a rally in oil prices fuelled concerns about inflation amid escalating Middle East tensions. Investors were also assessing the outlook for US monetary policy ahead of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting. A Reuters' poll indicated that the Fed was likely to refrain from raising rates at its upcoming meeting. However, uncertainty over inflation and the future path of monetary policy continued to cloud the outlook for gold. Higher rates generally weigh on non-yielding assets such as gold by increasing the opportunity cost of holding bullion. Persistent inflationary pressures, meanwhile, could complicate expectations for future rate cuts. Analysts said risks for gold prices remained skewed to the downside, reflecting uncertainty over rates and broader economic conditions. In the domestic market, silver prices also declined. The rate of silver fell by Rs27 per tola to Rs6,207, while 24-karat silver per 10 grams dropped by Rs23 to Rs5,321. Meanwhile, the Pakistani rupee appreciated by Rs0.01 against the US dollar in the inter-bank market, closing at Rs276.86, according to the State Bank of Pakistan. The local currency had settled at Rs276.87 against the greenback on Tuesday.

title: Apparel sector takes its case to COP31
description: PRGMEA holds Permanent Observer Organisation status under the UNFCCC
content: The Pakistan Readymade Garments Manufacturers & Exporters Association (PRGMEA) will represent the value-added apparel sector at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20, 2026, pressing for textile decarbonisation, climate finance and support for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). PRGMEA holds Permanent Observer Organisation status under the UNFCCC. Despite contributing less than 1% of global greenhouse gas emissions, Pakistan remains vulnerable to climate change.

title: PSX sheds 814 points in topsy-turvy trading
description: Rising oil prices, regional tensions undermine investor sentiment
content: Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) closed lower on Tuesday after a topsy-turvy session with the benchmark KSE-100 index swinging between gains and losses before extensive selling dragged it down by 814 points. In the morning, trading opened in positive territory as investors bought stocks of automobile assemblers, cement firms, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration companies and oil marketing companies. However, sentiment remained fragile as repeated swings failed to establish a sustained upward move. The index was marginally higher at midday, but selling pressure subsequently intensified, pulling it close to the session's low by the close. The bourse touched the intra-day high of 166,425.56 and low of 165,111.14 and eventually settled at 165,151.64 points, down 0.49%. Internationally, oil prices advanced, with Brent crude hovering around a five-month high as traders priced in a geopolitical risk premium following Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. The developments kept geopolitical risks in focus amid concerns over potential disruptions to regional energy supplies. KTrade Securities wrote in its market wrap that the KSE-100 index dropped 814.44 points (-0.5%) amid cautious investor sentiment and subdued trading volumes of 144 million shares. Weakness was broad-based, led by commercial banks, technology, refinery and power sectors, where Attock Refinery, Systems Ltd, Habib Bank, Hub Power and Fauji Fertiliser were the largest drags. Meanwhile, Brent crude remained elevated at $109 per barrel, reinforcing macroeconomic uncertainty and weighing on risk appetite. "We expect the market to remain range bound, with near-term direction contingent on global oil prices, geopolitical developments and corporate earnings. A sustained recovery in trading volumes remains critical to supporting a durable market recovery," KTrade said. Arif Habib Limited Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib commented that the PSX witnessed a negative trading session, where the benchmark KSE-100 index declined 814 points (-0.49%) to close at 165,152. The market opened on a positive note, reaching the intra-day high of 166,426 (+460 points), before reversing course and touching the low of 165,111. Rising oil prices weighed on investor sentiment, prompting cautious trading and driving the index lower. Among corporate results, Pakistan Oilfields reported earnings of Rs8.2 billion (EPS: Rs28.86), up 51% year-on-year, while Attock Petroleum's earnings increased 74% YoY to Rs6.64 billion (EPS: Rs53.36), supported by higher petroleum prices, inventory gains and improved other income. Attock Refinery posted a sharp 13x YoY increase in net profit to Rs18.6 billion. "Going forward, the market may remain volatile amid rising oil prices and cautious sentiment. Selective buying could support recovery, while investors should prioritise fundamentally strong stocks and monitor geopolitical developments," Najib said. Cumulatively, trading volumes increased to 446.8 million shares versus 370.9 million a day ago. The value of traded shares stood at Rs19.4 million. Of the 499 companies traded, 128 rose, 324 declined and 47 remained unchanged. Cnergyico Pk was the volume leader with trading in 46.5 million shares, falling Rs0.47 to close at Rs12.41. Foreign investors bought shares worth Rs206 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

title: Gold falls as market awaits breakout
description: Slips Rs3,600/tola over US rate outlook; rupee inches up
content: Gold prices in Pakistan fell Rs3,600 per tola to Rs435,436 on Tuesday, while 10-gram gold dropped Rs3,086 to Rs373,316, according to the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association, as international bullion remained range bound amid uncertainty over the US rate outlook. Silver prices remained unchanged at Rs6,234 per tola. In the international market, spot gold was largely steady at $4,138.54 per ounce by 1519 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery declined 0.1% to $4,157.90 per ounce. Investors remained cautious ahead of next week's Federal Reserve meeting and the release of personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation data, which could provide fresh direction about monetary policy. "Inflation and the Fed rates are the big stories that gold is fighting at the moment," said Bob Haberkorn, Senior Market Strategist at StoneX. Adnan Agar, Director at Interactive Commodities, said international gold had touched the intra-day high of $4,155 per ounce and low of $4,111. Later, it was trading around $4,127. He said the market was moving within a tight range, with resistance on the upside and support limiting the advance and decline, making a breakout likely over the coming days. According to Agar, gold's broader trading range was from $4,060 to $4,220 per ounce. A sustained decline below $4,000 could push prices towards $3,700-$3,800, while a breakout above the $4,250-$4,280 zone could open the way towards $4,400 and potentially $4,600. He said the market's next move would depend on whether inflation data and Federal Reserve signals strengthened demand for gold or made interest-bearing assets more attractive. Meanwhile, the Pakistani rupee closed at 276.87 against the US dollar, gaining Rs0.03 from Monday's close at 276.90.

title: 'Urdu AI model Buraq to keep data at home'
description: Minister says identity, Raast & WASL exchange must come before AI can scale
content: Pakistan is building Buraq, its own large language model trained on Urdu and regional languages, and procuring sovereign compute capacity so that Pakistani data is processed within Pakistan, Federal Minister for IT and Telecom said at the Global AI and Digital Summit 2026 in Seoul. The minister told a World Bank panel on digital government service delivery that the model, and the public compute capacity behind it, form the AI layer of a programme built on four foundations, according to a statement issued by the Ministry of IT on Wednesday. On digital identity, the National Database and Registration Authority provides verified identity to more than 100 million Pakistanis, now extended into a digital identity that authenticates citizens online and records and enforces consent. On payments, the State Bank's Raast instant payment rail turns an AI model's identification of a qualifying household into delivery. On data, WASL, the national exchange layer of the Digital Public Infrastructure stack built under the World Bank-supported Digital Economy Enhancement Project, lets institutions share data with every transaction authenticated, encrypted and logged. A citizen Super App and the National Open Data Ecosystem sit on top. On safeguards, the National Data Governance Policy sets a single rulebook for classifying, sharing, protecting and publishing public data. Governments that skip the foundations get pilots that never scale and systems citizens do not trust, she said. AI is the last layer, not the first.

title: Pakistan, US near trade deal
description: Commerce secretary says substantial progress made, technical issues remain with USTR
content: Pakistan and the United States have achieved substantial progress on several important provisions of their proposed bilateral reciprocal trade agreement, with only a few technical points left to be discussed with the United States Trade Representative (USTR), Commerce Secretary Jawad Paul told a meeting chaired by Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan. The review of the negotiations came during a meeting between the commerce minister and US Chargé d'Affaires Natalie A Baker to discuss bilateral economic relations, market access and cooperation in agriculture, minerals, technology and investment, according to a statement issued on Tuesday. Both sides expressed commitment to advancing discussions towards a mutually beneficial outcome. The meeting also discussed market access for Pakistani agricultural products, particularly mangoes and dates. Paul highlighted the need to expedite the visit of relevant US inspection teams for mango export arrangements and sought progress on the pending market access process for Pakistani dates, saying greater access would create export opportunities for growers, particularly in Balochistan. The US delegation indicated willingness to follow up with relevant American authorities. Both sides also explored enhanced agricultural trade, including US exports of cotton and soybeans to Pakistan. Paul highlighted the importance of competitive pricing and trade financing in facilitating greater imports from the United States, with discussions covering possible financing arrangements and closer coordination with trade institutions and industry associations. Kamal Khan underlined Pakistan's potential in agriculture, food processing, livestock and value-added production, and encouraged American companies to explore investment in modern agricultural machinery, food processing technologies, cold-chain infrastructure and improved farming practices. He invited US businesses and agricultural organisations to participate in FoodAg 2026, scheduled in Karachi from November 23 to 26. The US chargé d'affaires appreciated Pakistan's efforts to promote agricultural trade and expressed interest in facilitating engagement between American agricultural technology companies and Pakistani businesses. Kamal Khan identified dates, olive oil and other agricultural products as promising areas for value addition and export development in Balochistan. Minerals and mining also featured in the discussions, with both sides exploring investment, technical cooperation, skills development and responsible resource development.

title: Development hinges on tech innovation
description: Minister says EV charging facilities reflect private sector's efforts to promote clean energy
content: Federal Minister for National Food Security and Research Rana Tanveer Hussain has emphasised that the future of Pakistan depends on sustainable development, technological innovation and responsible investment. "Initiatives such as EV charging facilities demonstrate how the private sector can contribute to national efforts to promote clean energy, reduce environmental pollution and build a greener Pakistan," he said. He welcomed the cooperation agreement between StarCharge, a leading global provider of electric vehicle (EV) charging and smart energy solutions, and McDonald's Pakistan, aimed at expanding access to EV charging facilities and promoting environmentally sustainable transportation across Pakistan. Speaking at a ceremony, the federal minister appreciated the initiative, describing it as an encouraging step towards developing modern, environmentally friendly infrastructure and accelerating Pakistan's transition towards cleaner energy solutions. Under the agreement, StarCharge and McDonald's Pakistan will explore opportunities to establish EV charging facilities at suitable McDonald's locations across the country. The proposed collaboration will combine StarCharge's expertise in EV charging technology with McDonald's extensive customer network. The two organisations will jointly assess potential locations based on technical feasibility, infrastructure requirements and commercial viability. The food security minister stressed that the expansion of electric mobility infrastructure would help reduce dependence on conventional fuels, encourage the adoption of environmentally friendly transportation and support Pakistan's broader objectives of energy efficiency and environmental sustainability. He highlighted the importance of public-private collaboration in introducing modern technologies and attracting investment into emerging sectors of the economy. "Pakistan needs innovative partnerships that translate technological advancement into practical benefits for citizens. The expansion of EV charging infrastructure will not only facilitate electric vehicle users but also encourage greater private-sector participation in sustainable development," he remarked. The minister said that environmental sustainability and economic development must advance together, adding that initiatives promoting cleaner transportation could contribute to improved air quality, reduced carbon emissions and a more resilient national economy. He appreciated the commitment of StarCharge and McDonald's Pakistan to exploring investment in green infrastructure and expressed hope that their cooperation would encourage other businesses to adopt similar environmentally responsible initiatives. The agreement reflects the growing role of private-sector partnerships in supporting the government's efforts to encourage electric mobility, strengthen charging infrastructure and promote a cleaner, greener and more sustainable future.

title: FinMin seeks BB rating, $1.5b financing
description: Minister eyes Sukuk, Panda bonds and Eurobond tokenisation to diversify funding
content: Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb has sought Fitch Ratings' assessment of the requirements for Pakistan to progress towards the BB sovereign rating category, as the government explored a potential structure combining a World Bank policy-based guarantee with MIGA coverage to mobilise approximately $1.5 billion in financing at competitive rates. The discussions took place during a series of meetings with international financial institutions, global investors, credit rating agencies and development partners on the sidelines of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, according to a statement issued on Friday. In talks with Fitch Ratings, the finance minister, accompanied by State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) Governor Jameel Ahmad, highlighted progress in macroeconomic stabilisation, fiscal consolidation and sustained primary surpluses, alongside restored access to international capital markets. The delegation outlined improvements in foreign exchange reserves, exchange-rate stability, inflation management and debt sustainability, reaffirming commitment to the IMF programme, structural reforms and export-led growth. With Alvarez & Marsal, discussions examined a structure combining a World Bank policy-based guarantee with Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) coverage, subject to the available guarantee envelope and transaction structure. The minister emphasised leveraging existing World Bank resources and a Development Policy Operation to avoid delays. With Deutsche Bank, discussions covered diversification through Sukuk, Panda bonds, rupee-denominated dollar-settled bonds and potential Eurobond tokenisation, as well as debt management and currency diversification.

title: FinMin presses lenders to cut costs
description: ITFC to renegotiate terms as credit profile improves; M6 loan pending signature
content: Pakistan has secured agreement from the International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation (ITFC) to renegotiate the pricing and volume of its remaining financing tranche, with technical teams set to explore adjustments that align borrowing costs with the country's improved market conditions, according to statements issued by the Ministry of Finance on Thursday. The understanding was reached at a meeting between Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb and ITFC Chief Executive Officer Adeeb Y Al Aama on the sidelines of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok. Both sides agreed to find a mutually acceptable solution, as Pakistan seeks to replace costly short-term borrowing with longer-maturity financing without increasing external debt. Separately, discussions with the OPEC Fund for International Development covered M6 motorway financing, including the approved first tranche, the pending loan agreement and subsequent tranches. Fund President Dr Abdulhamid Alkhalifa invited the minister to visit and sign the project agreement, with ML-1 railway modernisation and power transmission infrastructure identified as priorities. With Chinese Finance Minister Lan Fo'an, the minister reviewed Pakistan's inaugural Panda Bond issuance, including regulatory support, credit enhancement from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), a 2.5% coupon and strong investor demand. He reiterated Pakistan's intention to be a repeat sovereign issuer in the Chinese capital market, and discussions covered Pakistan's return to the Eurobond market after four years and further Panda Bond issuances under the approved RMB 7.2 billion programme. Both discussed Pakistan's Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) chairmanship, including the forthcoming summit and the preceding SCO Finance Ministers' Meeting in Islamabad, which Lan said he would attend. They exchanged views on the proposed SCO Development Bank, with China seeking Pakistan's active participation in consultations and support for consensus. Infrastructure cooperation covered progress towards consensus on proposed changes to the route of a China-Pakistan highway project. In an interview with Channel News Asia, the minister said Pakistan is shifting from aid to trade and investment across bilateral partnerships, acknowledging support from longstanding partners, particularly Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. Remittances reached $41.6 billion last year and are expected to rise to $44 billion this year. He said CPEC Phase II focuses on monetising existing infrastructure through business-to-business collaboration, joint ventures and export-oriented production. Pakistan seeks stronger ties with both China and the United States under an "and-and" approach, while expanding engagement with GCC countries, Central Asian republics and ASEAN to unlock regional trade. In a meeting with Moody's, the minister welcomed the recent rating upgrade and improved fiscal and external indicators, highlighting renewed access to international capital markets, rising foreign exchange reserves and reduced State Bank forward liabilities. He sought the rating agency's views on achieving a stronger rating and striking the right balance between political risk and economic performance. At the JP Morgan Investment Seminar, titled "Pakistan: The Road to Resilience in a Turbulent Global Economy Landscape", the minister highlighted fiscal consolidation, revenue mobilisation and sustained primary surpluses, alongside strong remittances and a contained current account deficit. Discussions also covered federal-provincial fiscal coordination. At the Bank of America Small Talks Symposium, he outlined tax administration reforms, broadening the tax base and privatisation, alongside tariff reforms, competitive inputs and targeted financing to promote export-led growth. Discussions covered managing regional conflict, energy-price pressures and climate-related shocks. With United Nations (UN) Deputy Secretary-General Amina J Mohammed, the minister discussed development financing, debt sustainability and climate resilience. He emphasised a stronger Global South voice, simpler access to climate finance, local currency financing and strengthening the Borrowers' Forum through peer learning and an effective virtual Secretariat. He thanked her for appreciating Pakistan's mediation in the recent US-Iran crisis. With Alibaba International Digital Commerce (AIDC) leadership, discussions covered digital payments, a cashless economy and social protection payments. Both sides discussed rationalising e-commerce taxation, accelerating the Pakistan Single Window platform, tracking cross-border payments, and cooperation on cloud infrastructure, artificial intelligence (AI) and tax administration. They explored modernising Pakistan Post's sorting systems and expanding agricultural exports to China through Alibaba's retail network. With International Organization for Migration (IOM) Deputy Director-General SungAh Lee, discussions covered climate mobility, early warning systems, skills training aligned with labour-market demand and safe migration pathways. With Thai Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas, the two discussed increasing bilateral trade, cultural ties, two-way tourism and resuming high-level exchanges. In the Atlantic Council conversation, the minister said tax revenues rose 40% over two fiscal years, with the tax-to-GDP ratio at approximately 10.3%, supported by digitalisation and structural reforms. Privatisation of power distribution companies and airport outsourcing are advancing, alongside growing private-sector and foreign investor interest. Rs838 billion has been allocated to the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP). He said Pakistan is moving towards investment- and export-led growth rather than consumption-driven expansion, and will assume the G-24 chairmanship on November 1 while chairing the Borrowers' Platform Governing Council.

title: Pakistan showcases AI innovations at UAE fair
description: Pakistani pavilion was inaugurated by Ambassador Shafqat Ali Khan
content: Pakistan is showcasing its growing capabilities in artificial intelligence and emerging technologies at the AI Everything Global 2026, one of the region's leading public-private gatherings on artificial intelligence, bringing together more than 500 exhibitors and 150 investors from 70 countries. Pakistan has established a strong presence at the Abu Dhabi event, featuring five leading Pakistani technology companies presenting innovative AI-driven solutions and services including Al data intelligence, Al surveillance, Al sales solutions and sovereign Al. The pavilion has been established under PSEB. The Pakistani pavilion was inaugurated by Ambassador Shafqat Ali Khan. He interacted with participating Pakistani companies and highlighted the importance of enabling Pakistan's technology sector to play a proactive role in the rapidly evolving global AI landscape.

title: Farmers to get access to AI in daily lives
description: Parliamentary Secretary says they will be able to forecast their yields and productivity
content: The government of Punjab is working towards incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) into the daily lives of farmers as the provincial leadership believes in data and technological revolution. This was stated by Parliamentary Secretary Osama Leghari while speaking at the Pakistan Agricultural Coalition's Agri Connections Conference and Expo on Thursday. "I hope that during the remaining two and a half years of our tenure, we will successfully lay the foundation through which our farmers will have access to AI and will be able to forecast their yields and productivity," said Leghari. He added "a farmer is someone who buys wholesale, sells retail and pays carriage both ways so, we, as a government, have declared this the Year of the Value Chain". "We are encouraging our partners".

title: AI risk warnings rattle global markets
description: Wall Street's elite tech index, the Nasdaq 100, slid 1.2% to a six-week low in early trading as chip stocks
content: AI-linked stocks plunged worldwide on Monday after leaders of the biggest artificial intelligence companies warned of risks from rapid development, the starkest threat yet to the billions of dollars being poured into the industry that have driven world markets to record highs. The selloff rippled through the industry, where companies are increasingly relying on debt and circular financing to fund ambitious AI spending plans even as global borrowing costs, reflected in multi-year-high bond yields, continue to rise. Wall Street's elite tech index, the Nasdaq 100, slid 1.2% to a six-week low in early trading as chip stocks, which have led the AI sugar rush, fell the most.

title: Minister reaffirms BRI commitment at Hong Kong summit
description: CPEC was transforming country's economic landscape through cooperation in infrastructure, energy, industrialisation
content: Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan has reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), saying the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) is positioning the country as a regional hub for trade, investment and connectivity, according to a statement issued on Thursday. Addressing the 11th Belt and Road Summit in Hong Kong, he said CPEC was transforming the country's economic landscape through cooperation in infrastructure, energy and industrialisation. "Pakistan is emerging as a vital bridge between West, Central and East Asia," he said, citing expanding rail and road links with China and transit-trade arrangements with Central Asian states.

title: UK fund eyes expansion of investment footprint
description: BII expresses interest in climate finance, renewable energy and power transmission
content: British International Investment (BII) plans to invest at least $2 billion across Asia and Africa under its 2026-31 strategy, with a significant focus on South Asia, and has identified Pakistan as an important investment destination. BII Managing Director and Head of Asia Srini Nagarajan shared the plans with Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb at a meeting to discuss expanding BII's investment footprint and mobilising private capital, according to a statement issued on Thursday. Nagarajan expressed BII's interest in significantly expanding its investment in the country over the coming years, and outlined its focus on mobilising private capital alongside its own investments in infrastructure, climate finance, financial services, technology and private markets. Aurangzeb welcomed BII's commitment, highlighting improved macroeconomic stability and investor confidence, alongside the government's focus on structural reforms, privatisation and private-sector-led growth. The delegation highlighted the potential of private equity, fund-of-funds structures and private credit to deepen financial intermediation. Nagarajan welcomed capital-market reforms and efforts to improve the investment and exit environment.

title: Americans hit with record gasoline prices
description: National average gasoline price will probably hit $4.03 on Labour Day
content: With the war in the Middle East still raising energy costs, Americans face record-high gasoline prices for Labour Day weekend, just as political campaigns kick off for midterm Congressional elections. The national average gasoline price will probably hit $4.03 on Labour Day, far surpassing the previous record of $3.83 per gallon set in 2012, said GasBuddy analyst Patrick De Haan. "Gasoline, while not at all-time records, is at its highest level ever recorded this late in the calendar year, meaning Americans could for the first time ever see a national average price of gasoline above $4 per gallon on Labour Day," De Haan wrote in a blog post.

title: China donates livestock vaccines for CPEC 2.0
description: Minister urges scientists to develop focused projects for modernisation
content: Minister for National Food Security Rana Tanveer Hussain has called upon agricultural scientists and researchers to develop focused and innovative projects under the second phase of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC 2.0), saying agriculture will be a key component of the mega initiative aimed at enhancing productivity and modernising the sector. Speaking at a vaccine handover ceremony at the National Agricultural Research Center (NARC), Hussain said the livestock sector constitutes 60% of Pakistan's agricultural economy and remains vital for rural livelihoods and food security. The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs of China donated veterinary vaccines against lumpy skin disease and brucellosis. Hussain expressed gratitude to the Chinese government and its ministry for the donation. Highlighting the sector's economic weight, Hussain noted that livestock contributes significantly to agricultural GDP, provides employment to millions of rural households and supplies essential commodities including milk, meat, hides and skins. He warned that lumpy skin disease and brucellosis pose serious threats to animal health, reproduction and milk production, resulting in heavy economic burdens for smallholder farmers. Under the prime minister's directives, the government is placing paramount focus on boosting agricultural productivity. The Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences has been engaged to provide recommendations for modernising research institutions like PARC, with implementation slated to begin within two to three months. Hussain noted that 1,000 Pakistani students have already returned after acquiring practical knowledge in China and are being integrated into various agricultural sectors. The process to send an additional 1,000 students to China is underway and will be completed by March.

title: Govt taps HK expertise for virtual assets
description: Finance minister appreciated efforts to engage with international policymakers
content: Pakistan is exploring emerging opportunities in the virtual assets and digital finance ecosystem, including the potential application of blockchain and tokenisation technologies in financial markets, following constructive engagement between the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA) and Hong Kong policymakers, according to a statement issued on Tuesday. PVARA Chairman Bilal Bin Saqib briefed Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb on his recent visit to Hong Kong, where he held discussions with the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau, Hong Kong Monetary Authority, and Securities and Futures Commission. The meetings covered international practices relating to digital assets, stablecoins, compliance frameworks and digital financial infrastructure. Saqib shared perspectives on digital financial products, tokenisation and potential areas for institutional cooperation. Aurangzeb emphasised the importance of developing a responsible, transparent and well-structured digital assets ecosystem that supports innovation while maintaining appropriate safeguards. The finance minister appreciated efforts to engage with international policymakers and stressed the importance of building on these engagements to identify practical use cases that can contribute to the development of Pakistan's digital financial ecosystem.

title: Oil slips ahead of US announcement
description: Treasury Department announced new sanctions on 60 individuals
content: Oil prices fell more than $2 a barrel on Monday as investors took profits after recent gains and awaited details of expected new US sanctions on Iran, which could further disrupt supplies. Brent crude futures were down $1.71, or 1.81%, to $92.69 at 1648 GMT, while US WTI crude was at $85.34 a barrel, down $1.72, or 1.98%. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US was launching an "economic onslaught" against Iran's financial connections around the globe. The Treasury Department announced new sanctions on 60 individuals, entities and vessels but that list did not include any of the Chinese financial institutions suspected of facilitating Iran's oil trade.

title: SNL  veteran Kenan Thompson discusses Shane Gillis  controversial monologue
description: He lamented that the controversy had diverted attention from other performers  new cast members and the musical guest
content:
He lamented that the controversy had diverted attention from other performers, new cast members and the musical guest
Kenan Thompson has said the backlash over Shane Gillis’ controversial Saturday Night Live (SNL) monologue overshadowed the rest of the episode, adding that Gillis would need to have a serious conversation with the cast if he returned as host.
Speaking at the Axios Media Trends Live summit, Thompson discussed the reaction to Gillis’ joke about women dressing like “wh*res” at the gym.
The SNL veteran said he did not consider Gillis a mean person but suggested they would discuss the monologue if he hosted again.
“I know Shane, and I don’t know him to be a mean person, necessarily,” Thompson said.
Thompson also stressed the need to balance creative freedom with responsibility, describing the challenge as “finding the balance of both things — allowing creative liberties but also watching your step as far as harmful words are concerned.”
Shane Gillis’ 'SNL' monologue falls flat as jokes about Hitler and women draw few laughs
'Saturday Night Live UK' takes brutal dig at Shane Gillis over messy 'SNL' hosting gig
Travis Kelce comes under fire for allegedly liking Shane Gillis’ problematic 'SNL' joke about women
Dan Levy blasts 'misogynist' Shane Gillis over 'SNL' joke about women’s gym clothing
He lamented that the controversy had diverted attention from other performers, including new cast member Grace Reiter and musical guest Rosalía.
“Grace [Reiter], one of our newest cast members, had a phenomenal show, and it’s sad because nobody’s even talking about it,” Thompson said.
He clarified that the decision to invite Gillis back was not his to make, but added, “if he were to come back, then I think we would have to have some sort of real chat where people’s actions don’t wave-pool the rest of us.”
Reactions to the monologue have divided the entertainment industry. Some performers criticised the joke, while comedian Dana Carvey defended Gillis.
Peter Micelli, CEO of Range Media Partners, which represents Gillis, also defended comedians’ freedom to test boundaries, arguing that comedy requires room for creative expression.

title: Clayface    confirms Batman exists in DCU as Peter Safran teases live action Gotham
description: Batman previously appeared as a silhouette in    Creature Commandos    season 1
content:
Batman previously appeared as a silhouette in ‘Creature Commandos’ season 1
Batman is active in Gotham during the events of Clayface , DC Studios co-CEO Peter Safran has confirmed, offering a fresh clue about the superhero’s place in the developing DC Universe.
Speaking to Collider , Safran explained that the upcoming horror film will introduce audiences to the DCU’s live-action version of Gotham City, even though Batman’s specific activities during the story have not been revealed.
“We haven’t really talked about what he’s doing during the actual events of Clayface ,” Safran said. “But Batman is there. This is the introduction to the live-action Gotham.”
He also pointed to the animated series Creature Commandos , which previously featured a brief silhouette of Batman. The moment appeared in the sixth episode of its first season, showing the character standing on a rooftop overlooking the Penguin’s nightclub.
The confirmation adds to the references establishing Batman’s presence in the DCU. The character was also mentioned in the sixth episode of Lanterns , when Hal Jordan complained about Batman using the Bat-Signal in Gotham. The project also forms part of DC Studios’ wider plans to introduce characters associated with Gotham. Poison Ivy is reportedly set for a live-action debut in the DCU, although further details about that project remain limited.
