title: Dune  Part Three    beats Christopher Nolan   s    The Odyssey    in first day ticket sales
description: Denis Villeneuve   s sci fi sequel generated   880 000 in advance ticket sales at the London venue
content:
Denis Villeneuve’s sci-fi sequel generated £880,000 in advance ticket sales at the London venue
Dune: Part Three has broken the first day advance ticket sales record at London’s BFI IMAX, surpassing Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey after selling 33,000 tickets in just 24 hours.
The highly anticipated science fiction sequel generated £880,000 in presales, equivalent to approximately $1.2m, at the United Kingdom’s largest cinema screen. The previous record was held by The Odyssey , which earned £750,000, or around $1m, in advance bookings.
The figures place Denis Villeneuve’s upcoming film ahead of several major releases at the venue. Dune: Part Two , released in 2024, recorded £366,000 in presales, while Oppenheimer reached £254,000. Avatar: Fire and Ash followed with £116,000, according to the reported figures.
The latest record comes after strong demand for earlier screenings of Dune: Part Three . Three opening weekend screenings sold out in less than an hour last April, while two additional previews also sold out earlier this month.
The British Film Institute is preparing to present Villeneuve’s latest instalment on an IMAX 70mm print, reflecting its commitment to preserving and showcasing film projection formats.
The film is expected to conclude Villeneuve’s current Dune saga. Set nearly two decades after the previous instalment, the story follows Paul Atreides, played by Timothée Chalamet, as he faces the consequences of his rule. Zendaya returns as Chani, alongside a cast that includes Robert Pattinson, Florence Pugh, Jason Momoa, Anya Taylor-Joy, Javier Bardem and Josh Brolin.
Dune: Part Three is scheduled to arrive in cinemas, including the BFI IMAX, on December 18.
The venue also achieved a major milestone with The Odyssey , recording its best ever opening weekend at the box office earlier this year. Its performance placed the single screen among the leading IMAX venues in the United Kingdom and international markets during the film’s opening weekend in July.
With its presale record already established, Dune: Part Three is heading towards its release amid considerable audience anticipation.

title: Cyberpunk 2077 to get eight player co op support  beta launching October 23
description: Cyberpunk 2077 s NightCoop mod introduces co op for up to eight players  with open beta launching on October 23
content:
Cyberpunk 2077's NightCoop mod introduces co-op for up to eight players, with open beta launching on October 23
Cyberpunk 2077 is getting multiplayer co-op support through NightCoop, a fan-made modification that allows up to eight players to explore Night City together.
The mod is set to enter open beta on October 23 at 11am EDT, following a period of closed testing.
The release comes as CD Projekt Red prepares the game's official 2.5 update, arriving on October 22 alongside the recent release of the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 anime.
The update includes new quests, a perk enabling dual wielding and console mod support, among other additions.
However, NightCoop introduces a different way to experience the role-playing game by allowing players to complete activities together.
According to the mod's recently released trailer , the modification synchronises the game world so that combat and stealth encounters work across all participating players.
The synchronisation also extends to special abilities. When a player activates Sandevistan to slow time, other participants can see the character moving with an afterimage effect.
Dialogue and story decisions are handled through a voting system, with the majority choice determining what happens for the group.
The trailer also demonstrates cooperative heists, showing players taking on different roles, including operating cameras and drones while another player leads an assault.
NightCoop will additionally support player-versus-player (PvP) combat, which the host can enable or disable. The system considers players' equipment and character statistics during shootouts, while adjusting damage to account for differences in character levels.
To install the modification, players must download NightCoop and the RED4ext library. The host can then load an existing save or create a new co-op game, allowing other players to join as their own versions of V.
CD Projekt Red has previously supported community modding, including introducing console mod support for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt.
Cyberpunk 2077's RED4ext library has accumulated 12.6 million downloads on Nexus Mods, highlighting the popularity of community-created modifications.

title: Former Mass Effect 5 writers speak out after EA closes BioWare
description: Former Mass Effect 5 writers shared experience after EA cancelled game  and closed BioWare s Edmonton studio
content:
Former Mass Effect 5 writers shared experience after EA cancelled game, and closed BioWare's Edmonton studio
Former writers on Mass Effect 5 have spoken out following Electronic Arts' (EA) decision to cancel the upcoming game and close BioWare's Edmonton studio, ending more than 30 years of the developer's history.
The announcement was included in an open letter published on October 21 2026. EA stated that it had decided not to continue early development on the next Mass Effect instalment and would close the studio and its Edmonton workspace.
The decision prompted reactions from former team members, including New York Times bestselling author Catherynne M. Valente, who responded to criticism of the industry's inability to deliver a successful sequel to the acclaimed series.
“We did figure it out. We were working on a great game. Just saying,” Valente wrote on X.
She also clarified that she had not worked on Dragon Age: The Veilguard, Mass Effect: Andromeda or Anthem, adding that she was “not, in fact, the personification of BioWare”.
Award-winning science fiction author Derek Künsken also shared his experience working on Mass Effect 5, revealing that he had contributed to the project intermittently over the past five years.
Künsken explained that he could now discuss his involvement following the studio's closure, although he expected to gain greater clarity about what he could disclose in the coming weeks.
“Over the coming weeks, I'll get more clarity on what I can say about what I did and saw and learned. I hope it's more than nothing — what we were cooking was really cool,” he wrote.
He also revealed that he had collaborated with Valente on developing storylines, characters, lore and science fiction concepts for the next chapter of the Mass Effect universe.
Describing their partnership, Künsken called it “the most energizing, in-the-zone collaboration I've ever had.”
Following the cancellation, fans have speculated about whether EA might sell BioWare's intellectual properties to another developer.
Former executive producer Mark Darrah suggested that possibility could become more likely as EA faces financial pressures.
Meanwhile, the planned Mass Effect television series for Prime Video remains in active development.

title: German Twitch streamer Skyline TV dies aged 36 from a brain haemorrhage

content:
The streamer, whose real name was Adam Wolke, died due to a ruptured cerebral aneurysm, his close friend revealed
German Twitch streamer Adam Wolke, widely known online as Skyline TV, has died aged 36 following a brain haemorrhage caused by a ruptured cerebral aneurysm, according to a statement shared by his close friend.
Fellow streamer Verena Ullrich announced his death on Instagram on October 20, expressing her sadness at the loss of the online personality.
“It is with deep sadness that we must inform you that our Adam has sadly passed away,” Ullrich wrote.
In her statement, she explained that Wolke had suffered a severe brain haemorrhage and that friends remained by his side until the end.
“We were by his side until the very end and accompanied him on his final journey. We are deeply shaken and still can hardly put into words what has happened,” she added.
Ullrich also asked the public to respect the privacy of Wolke’s family, relatives and close friends during their period of mourning.
Wolke began livestreaming in 2013 and built a substantial online following through his content.
He had more than 265,000 followers on Twitch and approximately 120,000 followers on Instagram, where he regularly shared travel-related posts.
Wolke appeared to have last streamed on Twitch in September, while his final Instagram post was dated September. 15
Following news of his death, fans and fellow creators shared tributes across social media, remembering him for his personality and contribution to the online streaming community.
YouTuber ollistuntbuddy wrote, “Rest in peace ❤️”.
German creator Johny Münster also paid tribute, describing Wolke as a kind person, while German Truck Driver remembered him as “an enrichment to the scene”.

title: Rose salutes Bournemouth s past heroes ahead of AC Milan clash

content:
The hosts hope to build on Sunday’s Premier League victory and maintain their strong continental form
Bournemouth manager Marco Rose paid tribute Wednesday to the team that helped preserve the club's English Football League status as they prepare to face Italian giants AC Milan in a landmark European fixture.
The Cherries opened their inaugural Europa League campaign with victory at Real Sociedad and then won 3-0 at home to Sturm Graz last week.
A match at home to AC Milan, one of Europe's leading clubs, was the last thing on Bournemouth fans' minds when the side were on the brink of dropping out of the Football League following a 17-point deduction ahead of the 2008/09 season as a result of failing to meet their terms for exiting administration.
But Steve Fletcher's memorable goal against Grimsby eventually secured survival in Bournemouth's final home game of the season at Dean Court, which was followed by a mass pitch invasion after the final whistle by joyous Cherries fans.
Rose only succeeded Andoni Iraola as Bournemouth boss before the start of this season but the German is well aware of a pivotal moment in the club's history as his side bid to maintain their perfect start to the Europa League.
"We are looking forward to playing it, but I think many years ago the club had a much bigger game after the points reduction," Rose told a pre-match press conference.
"They needed to win the last game at home and Fletch scored a goal –- but it is not about Fletch, it is about the whole team. This is a foundation to be here, to have these kind of games and we are looking forward to play this game.
"It is a huge club of Europe which is coming here, but we feel prepared. We love to play this kind of games and now we are going to go for it."
The Cherries beat Sunderland on Sunday for a first Premier League win under Rose.
Now he wants to use that result as a springboard for continued success against an AC Milan side coached by former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim.
"We feel in a good spot," added Rose. "As I said days ago, we had other topics, and now we won two games back to back and we are confident.
"But even before the two games we won, I always told you that I feel confidence in my team. Now we have created a good momentum for us and we should use it."

Anderson’s family announced his death through his official social media accounts. Their statement paid tribute to the singer as a husband, father, grandfather and best friend.
“It is with the heaviest of hearts that we share the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and best friend,” the family said.

The singer attended the Country Music Hall of Fame’s Medallion Ceremony in Nashville on October 18, just three days before his death.
Anderson’s estimated net worth was $7 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth, as cited by. This figure is an estimate rather than a confirmed valuation of his estate.
Anderson built his wealth through a music career spanning nearly five decades, earning income from album sales, songwriting royalties, music publishing and live performances.
His best-known songs included “Swingin’,” “Seminole Wind,” “Straight Tequila Night,” “Wild and Blue” and “Money in the Bank”. He achieved five number-one country singles and released 22 studio albums during his career.
Anderson was inducted into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2014 and the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2024.
He is survived by his wife, Jamie Anderson, whom he married in 1983, their two daughters and his grandchildren.

The 35-year-old adventurer is undertaking a 434-mile journey from Nola in the Central African Republic to Mossaka in the Republic of Congo, crossing remote waterways where reliable communication can be difficult.
Concern grew on Wednesday, October 21, when a team member named Matt announced on Instagram that they had not heard from Dykes or his team for more than 16 hours.
“ATTENTION. It’s been more than 16 hours since we last heard from Ash and the team which is concerning,” the message read.
The team later provided a reassuring update , confirming contact through Dykes’ Garmin satellite device after his Starlink connection and power bank ran out.

“There’s no way for them to send videos or updates, they can only send short messages whenever they get signal on the Garmin,” the team explained on Instagram.
Although communication has resumed, the equipment problems mean detailed updates and video footage may remain unavailable until the team can recharge its devices and restore a more reliable connection.
The expedition forms part of Dykes’ wider Project Six mission, comprising six expeditions.
His journey highlights the challenges of exploring isolated regions, where equipment failures and limited access to assistance can complicate even well-prepared adventures.
The latest satellite contact update offers reassurance, although supporters will be awaiting further news as Dykes continues his journey through the Congo Basin.

Both sides continue to launch a barrage of attacks despite latest US mediation attempts to end war
Missiles struck Kyiv in the early hours of Thursday, a Reuters witness said, and Ukraine sent hundreds of ​drones towards Moscow overnight, as the two sides kept up a barrage of ‌attacks despite the latest US mediation attempts to end the war.
The Russian strikes wounded 15 people and damaged subway infrastructure on the Southern Bridge over the Dnipro River in the Ukrainian capital while also restricting traffic there, ​Kyiv authorities said. The strikes followed another attack on the city a day earlier t hat ​wounded six people.
A Russian strike killed a woman and injured another four people ⁠in the Kharkiv region in Ukraine's northeast, Regional Governor Oleh Syniehubov said on Telegram.
A drone ​also hit energy infrastructure in the Kremenchuk area in the Poltava region, a local official said on ​Telegram, without giving details.

Located on the Dnipro River, Kremenchuk is a major industrial hub and home to one of Ukraine's biggest oil refineries. The area has been repeatedly hit by Russian strikes, including a 2022 attack ​on a crowded shopping mall that killed at least 21 people.
In Russia, two people were wounded ​near Moscow after 630 drones were sent towards the capital during the night, Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said on Telegram. ‌Most ⁠of the drones were downed at long range, he added.
In the city of Lipetsk - home to a major steel plant some 400 km (250 miles) south of Moscow - a man was injured as drones hit apartment buildings and a medical facility, Governor Igor Artamonov said on the Telegram app.
Russia ​invaded Ukraine in 2022 ​after annexing the ⁠Crimea peninsula from its southern neighbour eight years earlier, locking the two nations into the deadliest conflict on the European continent since World War ​Two.

The latest strikes come after US presidential envoy Steve Witkoff held talks this ​week with ⁠Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and Russia's President Vladimir Putin to mediate an end to the conflict.

title: Bangladesh crash out of tri series after Afghanistan defeat
description: Rahmat Shah   s unbeaten 67 guides Afghanistan into final against Zimbabwe
content:
Rahmat Shah’s unbeaten 67 guides Afghanistan into final against Zimbabwe
Bangladesh crashed out of the ODI tri-series after suffering a crushing seven-wicket defeat to Afghanistan, whose comfortable victory secured their place in Friday’s final against Zimbabwe.
Needing to win by more than 40 runs to qualify on net run-rate, Bangladesh were bowled out for 160 in 41.2 overs after electing to bat first at Sharjah Cricket Stadium.
Afghanistan chased down the target with 87 balls to spare, reaching 161-3 in 35.3 overs, as captain Rahmat Shah led the way with an unbeaten 67.
The Afghans will face Zimbabwe in the final after already thrashing them by 158 runs in the group stage. Bangladesh, meanwhile, had also suffered a 99-run defeat against Zimbabwe.
Parvez Hossain Emon offered the main resistance for Bangladesh, scoring a career-best 70 in his first one-day international in more than a year. But his fighting innings could not prevent another batting collapse.
Leg-spinner Rashid Khan claimed four wickets for 31 runs to dismantle the lower order, while fast bowler Yamin Ahmadzai struck twice in the second over to leave Bangladesh reeling.
Opener Tanzid Hasan Tamim fell for one before Soumya Sarkar was dismissed for a duck on consecutive deliveries, both undone by loose shots.
Azmatullah Omarzai then removed Najmul Hossain Shanto for 15 and captain Towhid Hridoy for a duck in the space of three deliveries, reducing Bangladesh to 28-4 in the seventh over.
Emon, recalled to the squad after Liton Das was injured, attempted to rebuild alongside Saif Hassan, who provided valuable resistance amid the early collapse.
The pair added 93 runs for the fifth wicket before Saif fell for 41 while attempting an attacking shot against Mohammad Nabi.
Emon reached his second half-century in just his fourth ODI, striking five fours and two sixes to give Bangladesh hope of posting a competitive total.
But Rashid triggered another collapse, with Bangladesh losing their final five wickets for just 39 runs.
Despite the modest target, Bangladesh had a slim mathematical chance of defending their total by dismissing Afghanistan for fewer than 119 runs.
Fast bowler Taskin Ahmed briefly raised hopes by removing Rahmanullah Gurbaz for six with a sharp inswinger before dismissing Sediqullah Atal for four, leaving Afghanistan at 39-2 in the seventh over.
However, Bangladesh failed to capitalise on the early breakthroughs as Mustafizur Rahman and Shoriful Islam struggled to contain the chase.
Debutant mystery spinner Aliss Al Islam also went wicketless, conceding 47 runs in 8.3 overs.
Rahmat steadied the innings with a 56-run partnership with Ibrahim Zadran, who scored 34, before adding an unbeaten 66 with Hashmatullah Shahidi, who finished on 36.
The partnerships ensured Afghanistan reached their target comfortably and ended Bangladesh’s hopes of reaching the final.
Taskin finished with two wickets for 36 runs, while Mustafizur claimed one for 32.

Manchester United were hammered 4-1 by Como in the Champions League on Wednesday as the pressure increased on beleaguered manager Michael Carrick, while a late Declan Rice equaliser earned Arsenal a 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich.
Elsewhere, Real Madrid thumped RB Leipzig 4-1 and there were also notable victories for Inter Milan, Aston Villa and Real Betis.
The most remarkable scoreline, though, came in driving rain on the banks of Lake Como, where United suffered their joint-heaviest loss in the Champions League in the last 30 years.
Nico Paz scored twice for Cesc Fabregas's Como, with Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramon getting their other goals. This was a second 4-1 home win in this season's competition for the tournament debutants.
Joshua Zirkzee pulled one back at the death for United, but they are now seven games without a win in all competitions.
The Red Devils have just one win in the Premier League this season and have now suffered back-to-back losses in Europe. Carrick's position risks becoming untenable.
"I have not given my own position any thought," Carrick said.
"For us to play in that way, it's not acceptable. It wasn't a good performance at all," he admitted.
Last season's beaten finalists Arsenal have seven points from a possible nine after Rice struck in the 82nd minute to earn a draw in Munich.
Bukayo Saka went off injured early on but his replacement Eberechi Eze fired Arsenal into the lead, only for Alphonso Davies to level before the interval.
Harry Kane set up that goal with a magnificent pass and then gave Bayern the lead from a second-half penalty, his 10th strike this season in all competitions.
But Arsenal hit back as Bayern registered a second straight Champions League stalemate.
"We looked dangerous, we got the goal and we had a moment there where we could have killed off the game," Kane told broadcaster DAZN.
"Probably a draw was a fair result overall... There's a lot of games and we've got players with injuries, players missing tonight, so we take the point and move on."
Jose Mourinho's Real are one of five teams with three wins from three in this season's Champions League, as goals either side of half-time from Bernardo Silva and Arda Guler set them on their way at the Bernabeu.
Kylian Mbappe made it 12 goals in 12 games this season for Real before Tidiam Gomis pulled one back, but Yan Diomande completed Real's victory with a spectacular volley against his former club.
"We know every point is important to get into the top eight, we know we have to win as many games as possible -- we've won three and there are five to go," Mbappe told Movistar.
Villa also have a perfect record after three games, as they won 3-1 at home to Viking Stavanger with Ross Barkley's opener being followed by Emiliano Buendia's penalty and Henrik Heggheim's own goal.
Peter Christiansen got one back for the Norwegian champions who are still looking for their first win.
Inter had Alessandro Bastoni sent off midway through the second half before Carlos Augusto's late goal secured a 1-0 win at home to Shakhtar Donetsk, as the Italian champions got their first points.
Betis have maximum points as an Isco penalty handed them a 1-0 win over Feyenoord in Seville.
Club Brugge defeated Lens 3-0 in Belgium as Hans Vanaken, Joaquin Seys and Carlos Forbs all found the net.
Victor Osimhen sealed a 4-2 victory for Galatasaray away to his old side Lille in France, after earlier efforts from Yunus Akgun and Aleksey Batrakov and a Nabil Bentaleb own goal.
Teenager Soriba Diaoune got both goals for Lille, who have lost three out of three.
LASK of Austria have their first points after a fine 3-2 victory over Sporting in Lisbon.
Luis Suarez scored twice for Sporting, including an early penalty, but Christoph Lang, Sasa Kalajdzic and Krystof Danek all netted in between for the visitors.
Reigning champions PSG are top of the 36-team standings after beating Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday, but the French side confirmed Wednesday that star winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in that game.
He will undergo surgery in the coming days amid doubts as to whether he will play again this season.

title: Dengue cases surge sharply across K P
description: Dengue cases surge sharply across K P
content:
Province reports 1,510 infections in October, with Kohat emerging as the worst-hit district
Dengue virus infections are rising sharply across Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, with 1,510 cases reported during October so far, including 99 new infections confirmed in the past 24 hours, according to the provincial health department.
The department's daily dengue situation report identified Kohat as the worst-affected district, reporting 975 cases during October, followed by Peshawar with 209 cases. The total number of confirmed dengue infections in the province has reached 4,091 this year, while one death has been reported in Dera Ismail Khan.
According to the district-wise report for 2026, Kohat and Peshawar remain the main hotspots, although infections have also been reported in Bannu, Charsadda, Haripur, Abbottabad, Hangu, Nowshera and several other districts.
The province currently has 144 active dengue cases, with Kohat accounting for 80. Bannu has 24 active cases, Peshawar 18, Hangu nine, Charsadda seven, DI Khan three, Nowshera two and Lakki Marwat one.
Kohat's situation remains particularly concerning, with 2,567 cases recorded since the beginning of the year. These include 42 cases in July, 387 in August, 1,116 in September and 975 in October, reflecting the continued spread of the virus in the district.
In Peshawar, the annual tally has reached 566, including 75 cases in August, 144 in September and 209 in October.
Other districts have also reported a significant number of infections. Bannu recorded 81 cases during October, followed by Charsadda with 37, Haripur with 34, Abbottabad with 21, and Hangu and Nowshera with 20 each.
The report showed 17 cases in Karak, 14 in DI Khan, 11 in Lakki Marwat, 10 in Bajaur, seven each in Swabi and Lower Chitral, three in Malakand and one in Mardan. Two cases were reported in Battagram, while no infections were recorded in Upper Chitral.
Several districts, including Shangla, Upper Dir, Upper Kohistan, Kolai-Palas, Lower and Upper South Waziristan, Lower and Upper Kurram and Torghar, reported no cases this year.
The monthly figures indicate a marked increase in infections since August. The province recorded 115 cases from January through May, 90 in June, 111 in July, 573 in August, 1,692 in September and 1,510 so far in October.
Health officials have urged residents to take preventive measures to curb the spread of dengue. People have been advised to prevent water from accumulating in homes, streets and neighbourhoods, keep water containers covered and eliminate potential mosquito breeding sites.
Residents experiencing fever, severe headaches, body aches, joint pain or other suspected symptoms have been advised to seek prompt medical attention.

title: PHC bars arrest of K P Assembly deputy speaker

content:
Suspends order sealing Suraiya Bibi's official residence
The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Wednesday restrained the police from arresting Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Assembly Deputy Speaker Suraiya Bibi under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance and suspended the administration's notification sealing her official residence.
A two-member bench comprising Justice Ijaz Anwar and Justice Muhammad Fahim Wali heard the writ petition filed by the deputy speaker through her counsel, Yasar Khattak Advocate. The court issued notices to the chief secretary, inspector general of police and other relevant authorities, directing them to submit their replies by the next date of hearing.
Counsel for the petitioner told the court that Suraiya Bibi was allotted the official residence in 2024 in her capacity as deputy speaker. Following the imposition of emergency and Governor's Rule in the province on October 11, police raided her residence on October 14 and sealed the premises, an action he described as illegal.
Khattak argued that even under emergency and Governor's Rule, the official residence of the deputy speaker could not be sealed without fulfilling legal requirements. He sought orders restraining her arrest under 3-MPO and directing the authorities to de-seal the residence, contending that the moves amounted to political victimisation.
The lawyer further submitted that both the speaker and deputy speaker continue to hold their constitutional offices under the law until a new assembly is formed, and any such action against them is ultra vires the Constitution and the law.
After hearing the arguments, the bench stayed Suraiya Bibi's arrest under 3-MPO and suspended the notification sealing her official residence pending further proceedings.

title: LHC quashes case over unproven allegation
description: LHC quashes case over unproven allegation
content:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has ruled that a person cannot be prosecuted under Section 182 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) merely because an allegation or information provided by them could not be substantiated.
Justice Ghulam Sarwar Nehung, in a written judgment, held that the prosecution must establish that the information was knowingly false and provided with mala fide intent.
The judge observed that failure to prove an allegation and proving it false were two distinct matters.
The court held that a person providing information in good faith could not be convicted under the provision merely because it subsequently proved incorrect.
It further ruled that a written complaint by the public servant concerned was mandatory for initiating proceedings under Section 182 of the PPC. Proceedings initiated without such a complaint did not fulfil the legal requirements, the court observed.
The judge also held that a show-cause notice must be issued to the person concerned, giving them an opportunity to explain their position before proceedings were initiated.
Allowing a petition filed by Muhammad Shahid, the high court set aside the subordinate courts' orders dated February 26 and March 24, 2025, and quashed the criminal proceedings against him under Section 182 of the PPC.
The proceedings had been initiated after an error in the identification card number recorded in the property tax record was corrected.

title: Minor domestic worker beaten to death by employer
description: Minor domestic worker beaten to death by employer
content:
12-year-old girl dies while nine-year-old sustains fractured arm
A 12-year-old girl died allegedly after being tortured by her employer, while a nine-year-old girl sustained injuries in a separate incident.
In the first incident, a 12-year-old girl, identified as Zainab, allegedly died after being assaulted by her employer at a house on Khalid Road in the jurisdiction of A Division police station.
According to her mother, Zainab had been working at the house of a woman named Farhanda for the past 18 months for a monthly salary of Rs4,000.
She said that after 10pm on the night of the incident, Farhanda called her and told her that the girl was unwell and asked her to come to the house immediately without bringing anyone along.
The mother said she was unable to afford even the Rs100 rickshaw fare and had to walk for nearly two hours to reach the house.
She alleged that the woman repeatedly refused to let her speak to her daughter over the phone.
Upon reaching the house, she found Zainab lying on the floor, with a wooden stick lying nearby. The woman and her son were reportedly not present at the house at the time.
The victim's mother said her brother called police. The police collected evidence and shifted the body to a hospital for a post-mortem examination.
Farhanda, her son Ali Haider and her husband, Riffaqat, have been nominated in the case.
Zainab's father had died six months ago, while her mother works at a brick kiln.
The family's financial difficulties had compelled the girl to work as a domestic helper, earning Rs4,000 a month, her mother said.
In a separate incident two days earlier, a nine-year-old girl, identified as Iman Fatima, allegedly suffered a fractured arm after being assaulted by a married couple in Gujjar Town, within the jurisdiction of Sadar police station.
In a video statement, the girl alleged that her employer repeatedly applied a heated metal rod to sensitive parts of her body. She said neighbours intervened after hearing her screams and helped rescue her.
According to sources, the woman, identified as Zunaira, and her husband, Waris, both work for the police department. Police have registered a case and initiated legal proceedings.
District Police Officer Bilal Zafar Sheikh has taken notice of the incident and constituted a team under the supervision of the SP Investigation.
Police said further action would be taken in light of the post-mortem report and available evidence. Advocate High Court Hamid Khan said the incident of violence against a domestic worker in Sheikhupura was the second such case reported in the city within a few days.
He said the failure to enforce the law and ensure justice, coupled with influential individuals escaping punishment, was contributing to an increase in such incidents.
He stressed that the state must take strict measures to prevent such crimes and ensure that perpetrators think twice before committing similar acts in the future.
Suspect Riffaqat has been arrested following strict notice taken by Sheikhupura District Police Officer (DPO) Bilal Sheikh.
The DPO said strict legal action would be taken against the suspects and that no leniency would be shown towards them.

title: People of Pakistan stand with Saudi Arabia
description: People of Pakistan stand with Saudi Arabia
content:
CM, envoy from Riyadh discuss potential of Punjab's resources
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif met newly-appointed Saudi Ambassador to Pakistan Dr Rajeh Albugamy and congratulated him on assuming his diplomatic responsibilities.
The chief minister appreciated the ambassador's diplomatic services and expressed gratitude to the Saudi leadership for its economic and financial assistance to Pakistan. She described the Makkah defence agreement as the beginning of a new chapter in bilateral relations and condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, expressing deep sorrow over the loss of lives.
She invited Saudi citizens to visit Punjab's prominent tourist destinations and conveyed her best wishes to the custodian of the Two Holy Mosques and the Saudi crown prince.
The leaders discussed opportunities to utilise Punjab's resources and potential to enhance exports of livestock, beef, poultry, fruits and vegetables to Saudi Arabia.
They also deliberated on organising a roadshow in Riyadh to attract investment in Punjab and agreed on a target of over Rs500 billion in export of livestock, beef, poultry, mangoes, potatoes and shrimp.
Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz said the Saudi leadership held a unique, revered place in the hearts of Pakistanis. She said the decades-long relationship of trust between the Saudi leadership and former prime minister Muhammad Nawaz Sharif was a shining example of enduring bilateral ties.
She noted that Saudi Arabia was Pakistan's largest source of remittances.
She said attacks on Saudi cities and civilian infrastructure, including attempts to target Makkah and Madinah, were condemnable.
The chief minister said the joint defence agreement signed in August reflected the shared resolve of Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to protect their sovereignty and security. She said Pakistan fully supported Saudi Arabia's right to defend its people, cities and critical infrastructure.
"The people of Pakistan and Punjab stand shoulder to shoulder with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," she said, adding that shared economic strength was a reliable guarantee of collective security.
CM Maryam Nawaz said Punjab had the potential to become a reliable supplier of halal-certified food products to Saudi Arabia. She also paid tribute to the services of the former Saudi ambassador for promoting and strengthening relations between the two countries.
Dr Albugamy appreciated the deep-rooted, fraternal and strategic relations between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia and their people, expressing a commitment to strengthen the cooperation in all fields.
The ambassador thanked the government, armed forces and people of Pakistan for their support to Saudi Arabia, particularly their backing for measures aimed at safeguarding the kingdom's security, stability and integrity.

title: Sugarcane under attack
description: Sugarcane under attack
content:
Brazilian experts identify multiple crop diseases in belt as yields slashed by up to 70%
A wave of crop diseases has dealt a severe blow to sugarcane cultivation in Shaheed Benazirabad and adjoining areas, with Brazilian agricultural experts warning that infestations could cut per-acre yields by as much as 70%, prompting urgent calls for modern farming practices to prevent further losses.
A team of Brazilian agricultural specialists has arrived in Nawabshah at the invitation of a private sugar mill to assess the damage and advise growers on protecting their crops. Led by agricultural expert Dr William Burnsquist, the team visited severely affected sugarcane fields in Qazi Ahmed, Daulatpur and Shahpur Jehania, as well as surrounding areas.
During field inspections, the experts examined diseased crops and provided farmers with on-site guidance on modern techniques and preventive measures to contain the spread of infections.
According to the Brazilian specialists, sugarcane crops in the region are being affected by several serious diseases, including red rot, grassy shoot disease, Echinochloa grass infestation and shoot borer damage.
The reported damage has raised alarm among local growers, who are already facing substantial financial losses as the diseases threaten one of the area's key cash crops.
The experts urged farmers to move away from traditional cultivation methods and adopt modern agricultural practices, improved crop management and timely preventive measures to minimise damage and restore productivity.
They stressed that early identification of crop diseases and the adoption of appropriate control measures would be crucial to preventing further deterioration and safeguarding sugarcane yields in the affected areas.

title: LPG prices hit Rs580 kg amid gas shortages
description: LPG prices hit Rs580 kg amid gas shortages
content:
Daily demand exceeds 50 tonnes as residents turn to LPG; women protest prolonged gas outages
Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) prices in Hyderabad have surged to Rs580 per kilogram amid persistent natural gas shortages, with consumers forced to pay nearly twice the official rate as rising demand and alleged profiteering fuel black marketing.
The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) has fixed the price of domestic LPG at Rs279.34 per kilogram for the current month. However, retailers across the city are charging between Rs550 and Rs580 per kilogram, adding to the financial burden on households already struggling with prolonged gas outages.
The city's daily LPG demand has exceeded 50 tonnes as residents increasingly turn to the alternative fuel for cooking amid an unreliable supply from Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC). The situation has also triggered frequent arguments between consumers and shopkeepers over prices.
Abdul Qadir, general secretary of the LPG Union Association Hyderabad, alleged that OGRA-registered producers were supplying LPG to retailers at Rs520 per kilogram or higher, leaving shopkeepers to add transportation and other expenses to the final price.
"OGRA has fixed the price after including all applicable taxes, but producers themselves are supplying LPG at rates far above the notified price," Qadir told The Express Tribune.
He said the association had repeatedly lodged complaints with OGRA and registered LPG companies, but the prices remained unchanged. He added that the divisional commissioner and deputy commissioner of Hyderabad had also been informed, while meetings with representatives of LPG plants had been held to discuss the issue.
Qadir said five LPG plants operated in the wider Hyderabad-Jamshoro area, including three in Hyderabad, one in Jamshoro and one in Kotri. He maintained that a reduction in government taxes could help bring prices down.
Around 250 shops across Hyderabad district sell LPG, which is increasingly being used not only by households but also by rickshaws, Qingqi rickshaws, mini-taxis, Suzuki vehicles, hotels, restaurants and tea stalls. The rising cost of the fuel has also contributed to higher prices of food items, according to the report.
SSGC's gas supply schedule has further compounded the crisis. Domestic consumers receive gas for three hours at a time, three times a day, while low pressure and delays in the restoration of supply continue to disrupt household routines. Residents say that during the morning, evening and night supply windows, air often flows through pipelines for the first 15 to 20 minutes before gas becomes available.
Separately, women residents of Amani Shah Colony in Latifabad, Unit 11, staged a protest at Khuda Hafiz Board Chari against prolonged gas shortages, suspending traffic and chanting slogans against SSGC management.

title: Sheesha caf  s face indefinite closure
description: Sheesha caf  s face indefinite closure
content:
CJ Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar criticises prolonged delay in framing the rules
The federal government's failure to finalise regulations governing sheesha cafés despite repeated revisions and extensions has prompted the Islamabad High Court (IHC) to intervene, directing officials to complete the regulatory framework without unnecessary delay.
In its detailed written judgment, Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar observed that the Sheesha Rules 2023 had not been finalised despite the passage of considerable time.
The draft regulations had repeatedly been returned to the relevant ministry for revision by the Cabinet Committee for Legislative Cases.
The court noted that proceedings had been initiated because the regulatory framework remained incomplete despite repeated extensions and assurances given to it.
Observing that no specific rules and regulations governing sheesha cafés were currently in place, the IHC directed the relevant authorities to finalise the framework without unnecessary delay.
The court ruled that all sheesha cafés in Islamabad would remain closed until the regulations were framed, including establishments holding existing no-objection certificates (NOCs).
It ordered that previously issued certificates be treated as withdrawn.
The chief commissioner, deputy commissioner and Islamabad inspector general of police were directed to ensure implementation of the order.
The court also noted that an IHC order issued in 2022 concerning sheesha cafés had not been implemented. The Supreme Court had also issued directions to all provinces regarding sheesha cafés in a suo motu case in 2016.
Incorporating World Health Organisation guidelines into its judgment, the court observed that sheesha smoking exposes users to nicotine, carbon monoxide and other toxic substances that can cause cancer.
It further noted that tobacco smoke poses serious health risks to children and other vulnerable people in surrounding areas. Citing WHO reports, the judgment said sheesha smoking should be prohibited in enclosed public places and shopping malls, adding that passing smoke through water does not eliminate its toxic substances.

title: Russia frees retired US schoolteacher
description: Russia frees retired US schoolteacher
content:
Witkoff called Putin 'humanitarian' in thanking him
Russia freed Stephen Hubbard, a retired US schoolteacher in custody since 2022, from prison on Wednesday and took him to St Petersburg to fly back to the United States, after talks that Washington said were a step toward ending the war in Ukraine.
Russian President Vladimir Putin made the announcement at a meeting in St Petersburg with US envoy Steve Witkoff, who later said the talks will continue toward planned technical-level discussions involving the US, Russia and Ukraine.
Witkoff called Putin a "humanitarian" in thanking him for the move, a remark that drew sharp rebuke from Republican and Democratic lawmakers given Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The prisoner release comes as President Donald Trump's recent gestures toward Moscow, including a deal to buy Russian diesel and a waiver of new sanctions, have already sparked bipartisan pushback in the US Congress and worry in European capitals.
Putin's spokesman, Dmitry Peskov, said Putin had freed Hubbard, 74, at Trump's request, and that he had also taken into account the American's poor health. Trump later confirmed he had asked Putin on a call in recent days, and Putin agreed.
"The president sends his thanks, our whole nation sends their thanks, because of Stephen Hubbard," Witkoff told Putin in the meeting shown on Russian state TV. "Because of you he's going home to his family."
In a video shared with Reuters, Hubbard, wearing a dark fleece and clean-shaven, is seen in an undisclosed location in Russia shaking Witkoff's hand and thanking him. Later, Trump posted a picture of Hubbard appearing inside a plane with others and holding an American flag.
Hubbard's son, Joseph Coleman, told Reuters in a voice message that he spoke briefly by phone with his father before he boarded the airplane in Russia.
"Today he seemed light in his step, a sense of happiness in his voice", Coleman said.
Witkoff called the talks with Putin "constructive" and said in a post on X that he had also met Ukrainian and European leaders in Oslo to advance Trump's mission to end the war.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he supported the US proposal for three-way talks with Russia and the United States at the level of negotiators to be held as soon as possible, preferably by early November.
Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere, who also met Witkoff, had earlier said the talks will likely happen in mid-November and focus on a potential post-conflict security structure.
On Wednesday evening, officials in Kyiv said Russian forces attacked the capital city with ballistic missiles that damaged homes and a petrol station and caused injuries.
Witkoff's praise for Putin over Hubbard's release was scorned by some in Washington. "Look up the definition of 'humanitarian.' What an embarrassing and outrageous thing to say," Republican US Senator Thom Tillis said in an X post directed at the US envoy.
Trump, asked about Witkoff's "humanitarian" comment, told reporters at the White House: "Well, I guess you have to say for that particular purpose, for the purpose of allowing a man, who was thinking he was going to be in prison for life, out. But I wouldn't say anything one way or the other."
The US "gave nothing in exchange" for the prisoner release, Trump said, adding "we're getting closer" to settling the war.
"He is the happiest man around," Trump said of Hubbard. "This was very surprising to him, but I did it, it really took place on a phone call at the end of last week with President Putin, so we appreciate it very much. And his family is extremely happy."
Hubbard, a native of Michigan, had been serving a prison sentence of six years and 10 months in Russia following a conviction for mercenary activity in a closed-door trial.

title: Macron rebukes foreign leaders over unrest rhetoric

content:
Far-right politicians blame immigrants for French protests
Far-right politicians around the world have blamed immigration for France's recent riots, exploiting the unrest ahead of crucial elections despite there being no established link between the violence and immigration.
The riots, which erupted from protests over the cost of living, have become a talking point for politicians in the United States, Spain and Israel, where populist leaders face electoral tests. French President Emmanuel Macron, however, appeared to criticise the foreign leaders.
US President Donald Trump claimed France had been "conquered, looted and burned to the ground by migrants, jihadists and communists". Spain's far-right Vox leader Santiago Abascal warned of "Islamo-leftism", while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described France as facing an "invasion".
Marine Le Pen, France's far-right presidential candidate who is leading polls for next year's election, has blaming "decades of anarchic immigration" for the country's problems. Macron condemned "people who campaign at France's expense" and the "stupid comments by many, including foreign leaders".
Political scientist Pascal Perrineau said people from immigrant backgrounds were among those involved in the unrest, but represented only one section of a diverse crowd that also included students, revolutionary activists and radical "black bloc" protesters.
The demonstrations initially involved students complaining about poor conditions at school before widening into broader anger over inflation and the cost of living. Perrineau warned that France's presidential election campaign could become "extremely agitated" amid years of recurring protests and deep social divisions.

Meta said it had removed 720 posts containing AI-generated material that lacked proper labelling. It also restricted political advertising on its platforms to candidates and parties registered with the electoral court.
The dispute comes as the candidates prepare for a closely contested second round. Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, secured 47% of the vote in the first round earlier this month, compared with Lula's 45%. Opinion polls indicate a technical tie ahead of Sunday's vote.

title: Putin agrees to resume US mediated Ukraine talks
description: Putin agrees to resume US mediated Ukraine talks
content:
Trilateral negotiations could begin in Abu Dhabi after US midterms
Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to resume US-mediated peace negotiations with Ukraine as early as next month, the Kremlin said on Wednesday, following a nearly three-hour meeting with US envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg.
The proposed trilateral talks, to be held at a technical level, could take place in Abu Dhabi on or after November 10, with discussions focusing on guarantees for Russia's and Ukraine's security after the war ends, Kremlin officials said.
The meeting marked Witkoff's ninth in-person encounter with Putin and came amid growing concerns in Kyiv and among its allies over Washington's commitment to Ukraine. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February, before the United States and Israel launched their war against Iran.
The Kremlin said the discussions were less encouraging about the outcome of Witkoff's earlier meeting in Oslo with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, Nordic leaders and European and NATO representatives. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the proposals presented by Ukraine did not satisfy Moscow.
Putin used the meeting to offer assistance to Washington in dealing with Iran, saying a nuclear agreement with Tehran was both possible and necessary. He also offered to supply large quantities of fertiliser to help American farmers.
The Kremlin said the possibility of a meeting in China next month involving Putin, Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping was also discussed, with Beijing reportedly preparing for the proposed encounter.
Despite the renewed diplomatic push, Moscow and Kyiv remain far apart on the terms of a settlement. Putin has maintained demands for full Russian control of Ukraine's Donetsk region, Kyiv's exclusion from NATO and a comprehensive peace agreement rather than a temporary ceasefire.
Witkoff said he had brought documents containing ideas for a potential settlement for Putin to review. Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, also conveyed proposals during the meeting remotely.
Meanwhile, tensions between Washington and Kyiv have persisted over intelligence sharing and Ukraine's access to the Starlink satellite system. Zelenskiy said discussions in Oslo had produced an agreement to resolve those concerns, while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied that Washington had withdrawn Ukraine's access to Starlink.

Govt websites across Europe taken offline as precaution
Government websites across Europe and elsewhere went offline on Wednesday after critical vulnerabilities in the widely used PHP programming language prompted cybersecurity agencies to issue urgent warnings, with experts fearing a wave of attacks as hackers race to exploit the flaws.
PHP developers released emergency fixes for vulnerabilities that had remained undetected for years and urged users to update immediately. With hackers reportedly already exploiting the weaknesses and patches now publicly available, experts warned that attackers could use artificial intelligence (AI) to identify and exploit vulnerable systems on a massive scale.
"AI was powering a 'race to exploit'," said Costin Raiu, co-founder of cybersecurity research and incident response firm TLP, warning that the next stage could involve the mass compromise of vulnerable web servers worldwide.
PHP underpins a substantial portion of the internet and is used by platforms including WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento. Web technology tracker W3Techs estimates that PHP runs roughly 75% of websites whose programming language can be identified.
"This issue impacts the majority of the Internet," said Tiffany Farriss, interim chief executive of the Drupal Association, adding that servers running PHP versions released over the past 20 years were vulnerable.
Cybersecurity agencies in Europe, Australia, Japan and Britain urged website operators to apply the fixes immediately or take their sites offline until they could be secured. The Dutch National Cyber Security Centre itself temporarily went offline, while the operator of Wikipedia said it had taken an unspecified number of systems down for patching.
In the Netherlands, the Port of Rotterdam, government portal Overheid.nl, the national football association KNVB, websites of the country's five largest political parties and several hospital websites were also taken offline. Finland's state IT services provider suspended government public network services as a precaution, while France's Interior Ministry placed all its websites under preventive maintenance.
In Denmark, municipal IT company Kombit shut down several services, including the national school communication platform. Japanese cloud provider Sakura Internet also suspended a database appliance function.
The vulnerability was discovered using AI tools, cybersecurity company Wiz said. Its researchers used the company's autonomous research tool alongside Google's Gemini 4 Argon and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, coordinating with PHP developers and other cybersecurity firms to verify the fixes.
Wiz said the flaws had remained hidden in the codebase for more than a decade and would have been difficult for human researchers to exploit at scale. The White House, which said it had been informed on Friday, described the discovery as an example of American innovation strengthening national security.
Experts warned that smaller websites, particularly those hosted on shared servers and managed by operators with limited technical resources, could remain exposed after patches became available. Lukasz Olejnik, a visiting senior research fellow at King's College London, said AI could enable exploitation "instantly, on a large scale".

title: Meta hit with  25b penalty over user deception
description: Meta hit with  25b penalty over user deception
content:
Ruling follows verdict over Facebook data scandal
A New Mexico judge ruled on Wednesday that tech giant Meta must pay $25 billion to the state after a jury found last month that the social media giant had deceived users in a case related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal, according to media reports.
The penalty comes a couple of months after Meta agreed to pay $18 billion to settle claims brought by 48 other states, including allegations tied to Cambridge Analytica – a political consulting firm found to have improperly harvested personal data from millions of Facebook users during the 2016 US elections.
Revelations at the time showed that the firm had obtained data gathered through a personality quiz app called "thisisyourdigitallife," which was installed by about 270,000 users but also collected information on their friends. In total, the app reached roughly 87 million Facebook users worldwide.
Facebook learned in December 2015 that Cambridge Analytica had acquired the data but did not disclose it publicly until 2018, after a whistleblower came forward, sparking a major political scandal. Jurors in the New Mexico trial found that the misconduct affected all of the state's more than 2.1 million residents.
Earlier this year, New Mexico won nearly $1 billion in combined penalties against Meta in a separate case over harms to children. In March, a jury in that case ordered Meta to pay $375 million after finding the company liable for endangering children by making them vulnerable to predators on its platforms.
In August, a judge ordered Meta to implement product changes and pay an additional $567 million to the state to fund the treatment and prevention of harms caused by Facebook and Instagram.

Egypt, Turkey plan military support as Macron makes surprise visit to Riyadh
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Wednesday that Egypt would defend Saudi Arabia and other Arab countries if requested, but ruled out military action against Yemen, as intensifying Houthi attacks prompted fresh diplomatic and defence moves by Riyadh's partners.
Sisi's comments came as Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and intelligence chief Hassan Rashad met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Riyadh. This was followed by French President Emmanuel Macron's surprise visit to Riyadh to demonstrate solidarity with Saudi Arabia.
According to Saudi state news agency SPA, Abdelatty delivered a written message from Sisi to King Salman. Sisi said Egypt's military support would be confined to protecting Saudi territory and borders, or those of another Arab country whose security and stability Cairo sought to defend.
Meanwhile, Turkiye plans to seek parliamentary authorisation to deploy military personnel to Saudi Arabia under its joint defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan. A ruling party lawmaker said the mandate would be submitted after parliament ratified the accord, signed by the three countries in August.
The initial Turkish deployment would involve technical personnel and experts providing air-defence assistance, electronic warfare technology and other defensive support, the lawmaker told Reuters, adding that the Turkish personnel deployed under the pact would not participate in offensive operations.
French President Macron also arrived in Riyadh on a surprise visit intended to demonstrate solidarity with Saudi Arabia following weeks of Houthi attacks. His Gulf tour also aims to secure diesel and petrol supplies and diversify hydrocarbon sources amid rising energy prices and domestic unrest in France.
The attacks, meanwhile, continued on Wednesday, with the Houthis claiming to have targeted a Saudi operations room at Badr camp in Aden with a ballistic missile. Security sources said the attack hit a site near the airport belonging to forces from the Saudi-led coalition.
The group also targeted a military base at Al Rayyan airport in Al Mukalla with missiles and drones, according to military officials. The Saudi-led coalition separately said it had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi-launched drone over Saudi Arabia's southern region.
The escalation has opened another front in the wider Middle East conflict, which began with US and Israeli attacks on Iran in February and has threatened global energy supplies. Saudi Arabia and the internationally recognised Yemeni government have faced sustained Houthi attacks.

title: Pakistan  Maldives sign 20 MoUs  target  200m trade
description: Pakistan  Maldives sign 20 MoUs  target  200m trade
content:
Move coincides with 60th anniversary of bilateral relations
Pakistan and the Maldives agreed to increase bilateral trade from $13.9 million to $200 million within the next two years, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced on Wednesday, as the two countries signed 20 agreements and memorandums of understanding (MoUs) to expand cooperation across several sectors.
The pacts were signed during the three-day state visit of the President of the Maldives, Dr Mohamed Muizzu, which is the first visit by the country's president in 11 years, coinciding with the 60th anniversary of the bilateral diplomatic relations.
Speaking at a ceremony following the signing, PM Shehbaz said the trade target had been agreed with the "complete endorsement" of Maldivian President Muizzu.
"We will do our best jointly to raise this bilateral trade quantum from 13 million dollars to 200 million dollars in the next two years," he said.
Shehbaz said existing trade, valued at $13.9 million, represented only a fraction of the countries' economic potential.
He said the two sides had held "very productive and very fruitful discussions" on economic and trade relations, strategic defence cooperation and training in policing, defence, education and health.
Highlighting existing cooperation in healthcare and education, he said a large number of Maldivian students had studied at Pakistani universities and colleges, particularly in healthcare.
"About 250 Pakistani doctors are serving the cause of suffering humanity along with Pakistani paramedics in Maldives and other places in your great country," he said, adding that Pakistan was willing to provide more professionals to meet the Maldives' needs.
Shehbaz announced that Pakistan would support the Maldives' plan to plant five million trees by providing 100,000 olive cuttings and 100,000 seeds of different plant species.
The material would be provided "in due course of time with mutual understanding", he said.
Pakistan was also ready to provide technical expertise under the agreements. The prime minister welcomed the Maldives' efforts to establish data centres, saying Pakistan had developed its own technical capabilities and would be willing to share its experience.
"We have already set up various data centres in various parts of Pakistan starting from half megawatt to eight and a half megawatt," he said.
The prime minister also welcomed the Maldives' support for Palestine, "Maldives fully supports the cause of Palestine steadfastly and in an unwavering fashion," he said. "Pakistan stands fully committed to the cause of Palestine and their right to self-determination and the establishment of an independent, sovereign and contiguous state of Palestine in accordance with relevant UN resolutions," he added.
The prime minister said he had also briefed President Muizzu on Pakistan's position on Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir, reiterating Islamabad's support for a peaceful resolution in accordance with relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people.
He also raised Pakistan's concerns over India's decision to place the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, stressing that international agreements must be respected.
"Legally binding treaties must be respected, and shared water resources must never be weaponised or used as an instrument of political pressure or blackmail," he said.
Referring to his remarks at the United Nations General Assembly, PM Shehbaz repeated, "Water is a red line for Pakistan." He added that any violation concerning shared water resources would be regarded by Pakistan as "an act of war".
Welcoming President Muizzu, PM Shehbaz said the visit was significant as it was the first by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in 11 years and coincided with the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries, established in 1966.
"We extend a very warm welcome to you on behalf of the people of Pakistan, my government and myself," he said.
The premier also expressed confidence that the visit would give bilateral relations fresh momentum and take them to a "stronger, broader and more substantive level".
He also congratulated President Muizzu on the honorary doctorate he was due to receive from the International Islamic University Islamabad in recognition of his leadership and public service.
The prime minister pledged to work personally with President Muizzu to ensure the agreements were implemented promptly.
"I will be very happy to personally work with you to translate these written MOUs into action with prompt decision-making and speedy implementation," he said.
President Muizzu, in his address, said the agreements marked an opportunity to move the relationship between the two countries into "a new era" of partnership, building on six decades of diplomatic ties.
"My visit is particularly significant because of the timing," he said. "It is 60 years since Pakistan opened diplomatic relations with the Maldives and those have been 60 years of warm friendship between us."
He said the visit, the first by a Maldivian president in a decade, offered "important opportunity not simply to celebrate the friendship of the past but to define the partnership of the future."
He thanked PM Shehbaz, the government and the people of Pakistan for the "exceptional warmth and gracious hospitality" extended to him, his wife and his delegation.

title: NAB fine remains payable despite jail
description: NAB fine remains payable despite jail
content:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has ruled that a person convicted in a National Accountability Bureau (NAB) case remains liable to pay a fine even 20 years later, holding that serving a prison term for non-payment does not extinguish the outstanding financial obligation.
A division bench comprising LHC Chief Justice Aalia Neelum and Justice Muhammad Amjad Pervaiz issued a 15-page judgment while dismissing an application filed by Mehr Muhammad Baqar seeking to stop the recovery of a Rs2 million fine.
The bench held that the six-year limitation period for recovery of fines did not apply to NAB cases, as the special law governing accountability proceedings took precedence in recovering penalties.
It observed that even after serving one year in prison for failing to pay the fine, a convict could not claim exemption from the financial liability. Under the National Accountability Ordinance (NAO), 1999 the amount could be recovered as arrears of land revenue, the judgment said.
The court further held that recovering the fine could not be treated as double punishment, adding that the legal obligation to recover fines in corruption cases remained enforceable despite the passage of time.
The bench directed the relevant authorities to complete proceedings for recovery of the Rs2 million fine within three months.
In a separate case, the Islamabad High Court (IHC) disposed of a constitutional petition challenging the National Accountability Bureau (Amendment) Ordinance 2024, which extended the period of physical remand in NAB custody from 14 days to 40 days.
Justice Inaam Ameen Minhas issued the written judgment, holding that the ordinance had lapsed by operation of law and that no live controversy remained before the court regarding the expired legislation.
The ordinance was promulgated by the acting president on May 27, 2024, but was neither extended by parliament nor converted into an Act of Parliament.
The court observed that once the ordinance had expired, it was unnecessary to express an opinion on its constitutional validity. It also noted that the petitioner had failed to establish that any proceedings or punishment had been imposed against him under the ordinance.
The judgment stated that courts could not issue anticipatory rulings to prevent the enactment of possible future laws. Consequently, the IHC disposed of the constitutional petition as having become ineffective following the ordinance's expiry.
The LHC has also previously disposed of a similar petition after the expiry of the NAB ordinance, according to the information provided.

title: Pakistan expands strategic defence footprint in Gulf
description: Pakistan expands strategic defence footprint in Gulf
content:
Signs 'Badr' MoU with Turkey, Qatar & Indonesia New framework seeks joint defence production Arrangement leave
Pakistan on Wednesday joined Qatar, Turkiye and Indonesia in signing a new multilateral defence cooperation framework, marking another step in Islamabad's growing strategic engagement with key Muslim countries at a time of rapidly shifting regional security alignments.
The "Badr" Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), signed in Doha, seeks to deepen cooperation in defence manufacturing, joint research and development, technical training and industrial capacity building among the four countries.
A joint statement issued by the Foreign Office said the agreement reflected the four countries' commitment to strengthening cooperation and developing strategic partnerships in the defence sector.
The agreement brings together the defence ministries of Pakistan, Qatar, Turkiye and Indonesia, along with Pakistan's Defence Industrial Production and Regulatory Authority and Turkiye's Presidency of Defence Industries.
Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif attended the signing alongside Qatar's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of State for Defence Affairs Sheikh Saud bin Abdulrahman bin Hassan Al Thani, Turkish Defence Minister Yasar Guler and Indonesian Deputy Defence Minister for Logistics, Defence Industries and Technology Yusuf Jauhari.
Pakistan's Minister for Defence Production Raza Hayat Harraj and Haluk Gorgun, head of Turkiye's Presidency of Defence Industries, were also present.
According to the joint statement, the MoU is aimed at promoting cooperation in defence manufacturing, strengthening the defence capabilities of the four countries and expanding collaboration in technical training and research and development.
The arrangement is also designed to combine the respective strengths of the participating countries' defence industries, potentially opening the way for greater integration, joint production and technological collaboration.
The statement attached considerable economic significance to the initiative, saying the four countries would seek to leverage their respective defence manufacturing capabilities to build industrial capacity and meet the requirements of allied and friendly countries.
Asif said the agreement reflected a shared commitment to regional peace and stability and would advance cooperation in joint research and development, training exchanges and industrial capability building.
"Pakistan places great importance on strengthening defence cooperation with trusted partners," the defence minister said.
He said Islamabad looked forward to exploring opportunities for greater self-reliance, industrial collaboration, joint production and technology transfer by drawing on the complementary strengths of the participating countries' defence industries.
The agreement, however, is different in character from the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in August.
Unlike the Makkah pact, which contains an explicit collective-defence commitment under which an armed attack against one member is considered an attack against all three, the Badr MoU is primarily focused on defence industry cooperation, technology, training and research.
Nevertheless, the overlap is significant. Pakistan and Turkiye are members of both arrangements, while Qatar has close strategic and defence ties with Ankara. Indonesia, meanwhile, adds a major Southeast Asian Muslim country to an emerging network of defence partnerships stretching from the Gulf and Middle East to South and Southeast Asia.
The Badr framework also leaves room for expansion. According to Qatar's official news agency, other friendly countries could join the arrangement in the future subject to criteria agreed upon by the four founding participants.
The latest development comes just over two months after Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on August 7.
That agreement represented a more consequential security commitment, stipulating that an armed attack against any one of the three countries would be treated as an attack against all.
The three countries have since moved quickly to institutionalise the Makkah arrangement. Their foreign and defence ministers and military chiefs met in Istanbul on August 31 and agreed to establish a permanent secretariat in Saudi Arabia, initially headed by a Pakistani secretary general for three years.
They also agreed to deepen defence industry cooperation, joint technology development and production, areas that now overlap with some of the objectives outlined under the Badr initiative.
The two arrangements point to a broader trend in which Pakistan is increasingly positioning itself as a defence and security partner beyond its immediate South Asian neighbourhood.
Pakistan has long maintained close military ties with Gulf countries, particularly Saudi Arabia, while its defence relationship with Turkiye has expanded considerably in recent years through training, exercises and defence production.
The inclusion of Qatar and Indonesia in the Badr framework potentially widens that network and creates new avenues for Pakistan's defence industry, including joint ventures, technology sharing and exports.
The development also comes against the backdrop of heightened security concerns across the Middle East and growing debate among regional countries over reducing dependence on traditional external security providers.
The Makkah pact gave that trend a collective-defence dimension. The Badr initiative now adds a wider defence-industrial component by bringing together four countries with different capabilities, markets and technological strengths.
The emerging arrangements have also raised Pakistan's geostrategic profile, with Islamabad increasingly involved in security consultations and defence partnerships linking the Gulf, Turkiye and the wider Muslim world.
Pakistani officials have maintained that such arrangements are defensive and are not directed against any particular country.
The Badr MoU, too, has been presented not as a military alliance but as a framework for pooling industrial and technological capabilities.
Its significance will ultimately depend on whether Wednesday's memorandum translates into concrete projects, including joint production, technology transfer and collaborative weapons and defence systems.
But coming soon after the Makkah defence pact, the agreement underscores Pakistan's expanding role in a new set of security and defence-industrial relationships taking shape across the Muslim world.

title: Eleven killed in Rajanpur bus accident
description: Eleven killed in Rajanpur bus accident
content:
An inter-city bus on Wednesday met with a tragic accident on the Indus Highway near the Rajanpur district of Punjab a mishap that resulted in the death of at least eleven passengers. Thirty-four passengers of the bus also suffered injuries.
According to officials, the passenger bus was travelling from Karachi to DI Khan when it hit the concrete divider between two under-construction roads near Bangla Hidayat a locality in the Rojhan tehsil of Rajanpur located along the Indus Highway.
Eyewitnesses said the impact of the collision was so intense that the bus overturned. They said Rescue 1122 officials, along with some local people reached the site and started shifting the dead and the injured to Rajanpur's DHQ hospital. Fourteen people received first aid at the accident site.
The hospital sources later told The Express Tribune that eleven people succumbed to their injuries soon after the accident while 34 others sustained injuries. Seven of the injured were in critical condition. Five of these people were later referred to DI Khan while two were referred to Rahim Yar Khan hospitals.
According to officials, most of the dead and injured passengers belonged to DI Khan, Tunsa and various areas of Balochistan. They said the bodies were later shifted to their native areas after completing legal formalities.
Officials said the police in Umarkot registered a case against the bus driver. They said the apparent cause of the accident was over-speeding.

title: Rubio defends ties with Pakistan
description: Rubio defends ties with Pakistan
content:
US defense secretary admits challenges of balancing such ties
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said the United States needed to maintain a relationship with Pakistan, citing its geographical importance and nuclear capabilities.
"It's a country that we have to have a relationship with. It's a country that possesses nuclear weapons. It's a country that, from a geographic standpoint, we need to be able to interact with it in much the same way as the government of India has to have and has a relationship and meets with leaders from Iran," Rubio said in an interview with India's Network18.
His remarks came during a visit to India, where Washington and New Delhi have been discussing bilateral trade, defence cooperation and regional security.
The US secretary of state acknowledged the challenges of balancing such relationships, saying they remained an essential part of Washington's foreign policy.
He further suggested that maintaining communication with Islamabad could help Washington address India's security concerns.
"And I think in a way it could be a positive thing, because if we have a relationship and we can speak to them, it could perhaps put us in a position to help discourage the kinds of things that India is worried about," he added.
Referring to his current role, Rubio said his responsibilities as secretary of state required him to engage with countries with which Washington might have differences.
"In my new role, I'm no longer a senator. I'm the secretary of state. I have to manage the foreign policy of the US, and that does require us to have relationships with countries, including those that we may have some disagreements with," he said.
Diplomatic engagement between the United States and Pakistan reached new heights after Trump helped broker a ceasefire between Pakistan and India during their brief war.
