title: Suspect remanded in Rs35b US stamp fraud
description: Suspect remanded in Rs35b US stamp fraud
content:
Five-day NCCIA custody ordered in alleged US postage scam
A district court on Wednesday remanded Faheem Akram, the alleged mastermind of a Rs35 billion fraud involving the online sale of counterfeit US postage stamps, in five-day custody to the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA).
The suspect, identified as a 33-year-old resident of Khanewal, had been charged by a Florida jury with defrauding the United States Postal Service (USPS) of $126 million, the US Attorney's Office of the Southern District of Florida said on Sept 28.
The NCCIA produced the suspect before the court and sought his physical remand for investigating into the alleged scam.
According to the investigating officer, the suspect had been operating a website under the name "Labels Bank" since August 2023 and allegedly sold more than five million counterfeit US postage stamps.
The investigation officer further alleged that 16 bank accounts belonging to members of the suspect's family had been used to operate the fraud network. The court granted the NCCIA five days of physical remand to interrogate the suspect and investigate the alleged financial fraud.
According to the US Department of Justice, the website run by the Pakistani national was not authorised to sell USPS products and services.
The counterfeit labels allegedly allowed customers to ship packages at rates "far below legitimate USPS prices", it said, adding that it caused losses exceeding $126m to the postal service.
US prosecutors alleged that the website sold the labels for around $2 each, regardless of a package's weight, size or destination. A US court order authorised the seizure and shutdown of the website.
On Tuesday, NCCIA's Lahore Zone Additional Director Atif Ameer said eight special teams had been formed in Punjab, Islamabad and Sindh to trace the suspect and investigate the network.
He said 16 bank accounts had been used in the scam, including some allegedly operated by his close relatives.
US prosecutors alleged that he sold counterfeit US postage at a fixed rate regardless of a package's weight, size or destination.

title: Senate polls put K P direct rule to test
description: Senate polls put K P direct rule to test
content:
Restoration of provincial assembly could open way for change in government
The Senate elections scheduled for March 2027 have raised the question of whether governor's rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa will have to be ended before the completion of its six-month period, as the provincial assembly is required to elect 12 senators.
In March next year, 48 senators are due to complete their six-year terms. Elections to fill the vacant seats are scheduled for the first week of March, with the National Assembly and the four provincial assemblies electing their respective representatives to the upper house.
The K-P Assembly has been suspended and rendered non-functional following the imposition of governor's rule and an emergency in the province on October 11, 2026. The chief minister and provincial cabinet have also ceased to function.
Under the Constitution, an assembly can remain suspended and non-functional for six months after the imposition of governor's rule. In the case of K-P, this period extends until April 10, 2027, overlapping with the Senate elections scheduled for early March.
The situation has raised the question of how the province's 12 senators will be elected if the assembly remains suspended. The federal government would therefore have to consider restoring the K-P Assembly in late February or early March 2027, before the completion of the six-month period.
If the assembly is not restored in time, the election of the province's 12 senators could not take place, leaving the Senate incomplete for its next six-year term, from March 12, 2027, to March 11, 2033.
The restoration of the provincial assembly would also reactivate the offices of the chief minister and provincial cabinet, creating the possibility of a change in the provincial government through the assembly.
In such a situation, a new provincial government could be formed from within the assembly and work alongside the federal government on counterterrorism operations, adopting a common approach to the campaign against terrorism.

title: ATC names state counsel for Imaan  Hadi

content:
Turns down adjournment plea in security breach case
An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Wednesday assigned a state counsel to cross-examine prosecution witnesses on behalf of lawyers Imaan Zainab Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha in a security breach case.
On Oct 7, the ATC had framed charges against Imaan and Hadi in the case related to the alleged violation of a designated route and incitement during the arrival of an international cricket team, despite defence objections that legal requirements had not been fulfilled.
On Wednesday, the ATC directed Advocate Taimur Janjua to appear at the next hearing after defence lawyers failed to cross-examine witnesses during the day's proceedings.
Advocate Aimal Khan Mandokhail appeared before the judge on behalf of Imaan and Hadi and requested an adjournment.
The court turned down the request, observing that the prosecution witnesses were present at the hearing and the defence could cross-examine them.
"The witnesses are present; you may proceed with the cross-examination," judge Tahir Abbas Sipra said.
Advocate Mandokhail replied that senior counsel Riasat Ali Azad was not present and that he would cross-examine the witnesses.
The judge observed that the accused were lawyers themselves and could conduct the cross-examination in their own case if they wished.
The court order stated that it was "made crystal clear" at the last hearing that the accused should ensure the presence of their lawyers for cross-examination.

title: LHC moved for Imran s sisters release
description: LHC moved for Imran s sisters release
content:
The son of Aleema Khan, detained sister of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, moved the Lahore High Court (LHC) on Wednesday, seeking the production and release of his mother, as well as two aunts.
All three of Imran's sisters - Aleema, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan - were detained by authorities in September, under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960, as the PTI geared up of for a planned protest march towards Islamabad. Their detention was ordered for 30 days.
Aleema's son, Shahrez Khan, filed a fresh plea challenging their detention in the LHC on Wednesday.
The petition stated that Imran's sisters remained at Lahore's Kot Lakhpat jail despite the lapse of the 30-day period of their detention.
The Punjab home secretary (grievance redressal commissioner), the inspector general of police, the Lahore capital city police officer and the Kot Lakhpat jail superintendent have been named as respondents.
The petition, filed through Advocate Rana Mudassar Umar, said the sisters' detention orders were issued on Sept 20 and expired on Oct 19, yet the jail authorities had not released them despite requests.
"Therefore, detention of the detenues is against the law and fundamental rights of the individuals," it contended.
The plea further said that the three sisters were not wanted in any case, and raised concerns that they may be implicated in "false criminal cases" if not released.
The petition argued that their detention was a consequence of their efforts for their brother's release. It further contended that the preventive detention could not replace ordinary criminal law, and that the order violated Article 10 as well as the safeguards of Section 3 of the MPO.
The petitioner requested the court to direct the jail superintendent to produce the detainees before the court and "set them at liberty, in the interest of justice, equity and fair play". He asked the court to declare the detention orders void and issue directives for the detainees' release, while suspending the operation of the orders.
The petition has been fixed for Thursday before Justice Abher Gul Khan.

content:
Four UK-trained Pakistani stylists display techniques at 'The Art of Hair' show
Hairstyling took centre stage as international salon brand TONI&GUY South Pakistan hosted a fashion show titled The Art of Hair in Karachi, showcasing the creative skills of four Pakistani stylists trained in the United Kingdom.
Held at the brand's flagship salon, the event featured 20 models sporting contemporary hairstyles created using advanced cutting, colouring, highlighting and balayage techniques. The models walked the ramp in outfits by Pakistani designers Zareeh and Deepak Perwani, combining fashion with professional hairstyling.
The event was attended by TONI&GUY Global Technical Artistic Director Francesco Fontana and Global Artistic Director Efi Davies, who travelled from London, along with British Deputy High Commissioner Alison Blackburne.
The show highlighted hairstyling as a discipline that combines science, artistic expression, technical expertise and continuous professional learning.
TONI&GUY South Pakistan Chief Executive Officer Saeeda Mandviwalla said education was fundamental to professional growth, particularly in hairstyling, where scientific knowledge and creativity went hand in hand.
She said the organisation aimed to bring hairstyling education in Pakistan up to international standards by equipping young professionals with skills that would enable them to work globally.
The four stylists' UK training, she added, reflected the potential of Pakistani talent. The organisation invested in staff development so that professionals could acquire modern techniques abroad and apply their expertise to improve industry standards at home.
Mandviwalla said human creativity, technical skills and professional experience would remain important even in the age of artificial intelligence. She also announced plans to establish an academy in Pakistan to provide advanced training to local hairstylists.
She stressed the importance of creating opportunities for young people from underprivileged backgrounds and minority communities, enabling them to develop professional skills and become economically empowered.
British Deputy High Commissioner Alison Blackburne praised the salon's training programme, saying Pakistan-UK partnerships could open new career opportunities for young people.
The event also highlighted the professional journeys of four stylists - Khawar Javed, Muhammad Waseem, Waeem Waris and Parvez Boota - who completed a six-week advanced technical training programme at the TONI&GUY academy in London.
According to the organisation, the training combined practical experience with modern hairstyling techniques, qualifying the four professionals to work at TONI&GUY salons worldwide.
A cut-and-colour technician said the achievement reflected years of hard work, experience and continuous learning.
The audience applauded the stylists' work as the models showcased their creations on the ramp.

title: 10  inflation splits rate call predictions
description: 10  inflation splits rate call predictions
content:
Growth Securities expects 50-100bps hike, AKD sees a hold as reserves, remittances strengthen
Pakistan's headline inflation is expected to rise to 10% in October 2026, driven by higher electricity charges, petrol prices and food costs, while persistent inflationary pressures could prompt the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) to raise its policy rate by 50-100 basis points at its October 26 meeting, according to a Growth Securities report authored by Nasheed Malik, which projects the National Consumer Price Index (NCPI) increasing by 1.5% month-on-month (MoM), compared with 6.2% year-on-year (YoY) and 1.7% MoM in October 2025.
Average inflation during the first four months of FY27 is expected to reach 10.2%, compared with 4.8% in the corresponding period of FY26, and the October projection is above the government's expected average of 8.9% for FY27, the report said.
The transport index is expected to rise by 0.15% to 0.20% MoM following a 5.5% monthly increase in the average petrol price to Rs396.06 per litre, up 48.3% YoY, while the housing index is also expected to increase on a monthly basis due to higher electricity charges and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices, which are projected to rise by 6.2% MoM.
The food index is forecast to increase by around 0.25% to 0.30% MoM, mainly due to price increases of 10% in wheat, 14% in chicken, 11% in pulse gram and 5% in garlic, according to the report.
Malik said real interest rates returned to positive territory in June 2026 and are projected to reach 1.5% in October, compared with 1.2% in September, and he expects inflation to remain in the 9% to 10% range until March 2027 if average fuel prices stay between Rs390 and Rs400 per litre, with average inflation for FY27 projected at 9% to 9.5%. He expects the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) to raise the policy rate by 50-100 basis points at its October 26, 2026 meeting if fuel prices remain elevated.
A separate assessment by AKD Securities Director Research Mohammed Awais Ashraf holds that Pakistan's improved external and fiscal position is strengthening the case for holding rates steady, with robust remittances, improving exports, record-high foreign exchange reserves and a contained current account position improving macroeconomic buffers and giving the SBP room to hold at its upcoming MPC meeting.
The successful issuance of a $3 billion Eurobond at record-low spreads had further supported external stability, and Ashraf wrote that a slowdown in large-scale manufacturing (LSM), coupled with a decline in fuel prices since the previous MPC meeting, was also expected to support a status quo decision.
He raised his FY27 inflation forecast to 9.1% from an earlier projection, reflecting a higher oil-price assumption of $96.3 per barrel compared with $72.5 previously, maintained the FY28 forecast at 6%, and pushed back the assumed start of monetary easing to April 2027 from October 2026, citing prolonged higher oil prices and a larger-than-expected rise in wheat prices.
Dubai crude declined 15.5% since the previous MPC meeting, from $127 to $107 per barrel, reflecting improved flows through the Strait of Hormuz and the end of seasonal refinery maintenance, though renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, Red Sea disruption and declining US oil inventories continue to underpin prices.
Real interest rates are expected to average 3.4% over the next 12 months, assuming normal rupee depreciation and gradual normalisation of oil prices through February 2028, with fiscal discipline improving further.

title: GSP  hinges on meeting EU standards
description: GSP  hinges on meeting EU standards
content:
In meeting with textile council, ambassador stresses need for improvement in areas of concern
European Union Ambassador Raimundas Karoblis, while referring to the Generalised Scheme of Preferences Plus (GSP+) assessment of Pakistan covering the period 2023-2025, published on July 16, has emphasised that improvements in areas relating to human rights and rule of law commitments are essential for securing benefits under the new GSP+.
He met with the Pakistan Textile Council (PTC) leadership to discuss Pakistan's position under the EU's GSP+ facility, the process ahead for the next phase of arrangement and the strategic importance of textile and apparel exports in Pakistan's trade relationship with the EU.
According to the EU's assessment, the European Union remains Pakistan's largest export destination, with textiles and clothing making up roughly 70-76% of Pakistan's exports to the EU. The current GSP+ arrangement has been in place for over a decade.
The ambassador clarified that the EU was not introducing new standards. Rather, the expectation was effective implementation at an acceptable level of commitments Pakistan had already made under the relevant United Nations conventions.
He emphasised that the European Commission would enhance engagement with the government of Pakistan, adding that the immediate priority would be demonstrable short-term improvements in areas of major concern, followed by a credible action plan with concrete measures, timelines and measurable performance indicators. "The new framework places greater emphasis on effective implementation rather than ratification of conventions or adoption of legislation." The ambassador acknowledged Pakistan's readiness to cooperate at the highest level and stressed that sustained coordination and implementation would also be required at ministerial and working levels.
PTC Chairman Fawad Anwar said that member companies of the council were predominantly value-added exporters with significant dependence on the EU market. He stressed that the continuation of GSP+ was critical not only for Pakistan's textile and apparel exports but also for employment, tax contribution and the broader ecosystem of businesses and livelihoods associated with the sector. He observed that the EU-India Free Trade Agreement would put significant additional competitive pressure on Pakistani exporters, even if Pakistan's GSP+ status remained in place.
Council Vice Chairman Anees Khawaja noted that the report acknowledged progress across all four clusters covering human rights, labour, environment and governance. He invited the ambassador to visit Multan to witness firsthand how GSP+ had contributed to improving livelihoods and economic opportunities in Pakistan's smaller cities.
Gul Ahmed CEO Zaki Bashir requested that conditions within Pakistan's textile and apparel export sector be assessed separately from national-level findings. He pointed out that the concerns presented were national findings rather than sector-specific assessments.

title: Malaysia edge Pakistan in Sultan of Johor Cup

content:
The hosts remain undefeated in the competition
Malaysia edged Pakistan 3-2 to maintain their unbeaten record at the Sultan of Johor Cup and move closer to securing a place in the final.
The hosts secured a measure of revenge after losing twice to Pakistan at last month's Junior Asia Cup in Inner Mongolia, China.
Malaysia, coached by Nor Saiful Zaini, have won all three of their matches at the Taman Daya Hockey Stadium in Johor and lead the standings. They are virtually assured of a place in the final, with only a match against Canada remaining on Friday.
Pakistan had an opportunity to take an early lead in the 12th minute when they were awarded a penalty stroke, but goalkeeper Abid Amsyar Hanif saved Rana Waleed's flick.
Malaysia broke the deadlock in the 28th minute through forward T. Naaveennash Panicker, before Adeel equalised for Pakistan from close range in the 36th minute.
The contest took a decisive turn in the 51st minute when Pakistan were reduced to 10 players. Waleed received a red card for striking a Malaysian player on the forehead with his stick.
Pakistan's disciplinary problems continued three minutes later when Mustafa Ghulam was shown a yellow card, leaving his side further disadvantaged.
Malaysia capitalised on their numerical advantage, with Safwan Salihe restoring their lead in the 55th minute. Naaveennash then scored his second goal of the match two minutes later to put the hosts 3-1 ahead.
Pakistan's difficulties deepened when Haider Asam received a yellow card in the 58th minute, leaving them with only eight players on the field.
Despite their numerical advantage, Malaysia were unable to convert any of their eight penalty corners.

title: How mega infrastructure is rewriting politics
description: Beijing s model has also lately changed
content:
Almost a decade ago, the main argument about mega-infrastructure was mainly about economics. Would the port pay for itself? Would the motorway move enough freight and boost commercial activity? Would the power-generating plant alleviate the energy woes of a country? However, today across three continents, the mega-infrastructure projects have become a reason for governments to win, lose or constrain.
In the context, China emerges at the top of the list. Its engagement across the 150 countries of BRI reached around $126 billion in the first half of 2016, and this is the highest since the BRI's inception in 2013. Here, more than the volume of concrete, what is more intriguing is how it affects the politics on the ground in host countries.
Beijing's model has also lately changed. Open-handed sovereign lending gradually tailed off around 2019. Since then, China has shifted from being a financier to a creditor collecting repayments, with more money going into further equity, mining, energy and data centres rather than concessional loans to finance ministries. Nevertheless, the political consequences for the host countries have only started to arrive.
Kenya is an excellent example to start with. China's flagship project in Kenya, the Standard Gauge Railway (SGR), was stopped well short of the Ugandan border because Beijing decided to halt funding. Kenya had built the SGR using a loan of $5.08 billion from China ExIm Bank to be paid back from 2029 to 2035. Since another sovereign loan, that too in dollars, was politically unsellable, President William Ruto's government restructured what it already owned. The three dollar-denominated loans of China were converted into yuan, and their maturity was extended to 2040. In March 2026, construction resumed, but the seed money was sourced from a domestic cargo levy worth about $270 million. Consequently, SGR survived, but the financing model did not.
In Peru's case, the argument is more about the jurisdiction than money. COSCO, a Chinese shipping company, built the deepwater port in Chancay with an investment of $1.3 billion. Because the port was built purely from private capital, the regulatory body for ports in Peru, Ositrán, was ordered by the Constitutional Court of Lima to stand back from any kind of supervision or intervention. After five months, a Lima appeals court reversed the decision and posited that Chancay port is a public-use infrastructure regardless of the ownership. COSCO has again taken the case to the Constitutional Court. As of now, a port built to move copper has become a test of who governs it.
The pattern follows in South Asia too. Sri Lanka and Bangladesh are cases in point.
Then there is Pakistan, which is the laboratory. CPEC brought nearly $25.4 billion in investment, around 510 km of highway, 886 km of transmission line and 8,000 megawatts into a grid that used to fail daily. Load-shedding is no longer the national grievance as it was before 2013; however, the bill arrives through the electricity meter. While ensuring the production capacity, Pakistan signed take-or-pay contracts obliging it to pay the producers regardless the power was used or not. Resultantly, the system-wide capacity payments have jumped up from Rs384 billion to Rs2.1 trillion; power-sector circular debt reached Rs1.9 trillion by February 2026. When Islamabad asked the Chinese producers to waive Rs170 billion in the late-payment charges following the domestic producers, they showed reluctance on the grounds that it would set a wrong precedent for other BRI projects. Here, while China is defending its contracts, Pakistanis are paying the tariffs.
The second bill is constitutional in nature. Where Balochistan holds the crown jewel of the corridor, it gains the least from CPEC. Since 2021, at least 20 Chinese nationals have been killed in various attacks by BLA and allied groups, in addition to numerous attacks on civilians and armed forces of Pakistan. Islamabad's response was to dedicate a police force to protecting Chinese nationals. No matter what the logic is, a separate protective apparatus for foreigners in a single province indicates who the corridor is for; the grievance is left where the asset is placed, with benefits centralised in Islamabad. The second phase isn't as robust as the first one. Three out of nine SEZs have started operating; China pulled back from financing the ML-1 railway, which is the biggest project of the corridor, in 2025, and in the first six months of 2026, no new Chinese engagement was recorded in Pakistan. Pakistan is yet to recover from the first phase and is still fighting to protect it.
So far, Washington, Brussels and Delhi have been responding by drawing rival lines. The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), announced at the G20 in 2023 as an explicit alternative to the BRI, still has not materialised. By May 2026, it was yet to secure any firm funding commitments, and has no construction timeline either; its route through the Strait of Hormuz seems considerably less promising after this year's disruption to Gulf shipping.
That does not mean that IMEC is politically inactive. Governments will be called upon to decide on maps, but not yet on assets. On the other hand, the real money continues to flow: Africa hosted the most Chinese investments and construction, with $46.99 billion in the first half of 2026.
Here, the common thread is not Chinese investments or the West's response. Mega-infrastructure projects are signed on political timescales and repaid on geological ones: a port takes five years to build, thirty to pay for, and outlives every government which championed it.
Three things determine whether a project leads towards more stability or otherwise. The first is whether the contract can withstand disclosure: Kenya renegotiated in public and kept its railway, while Peru's regulatory carve-out became a sovereignty crisis precisely because it was settled quietly in court. The second is whether the people closest to the asset can see a return; Balochistan's insurgency is an economic grievance, and it has a security expression; no protective police force can solve it. The third is whether the state keeps the fiscal room to say no later; the lesson Pakistan is learning one tariff notification at a time.
The most consequential fact about mega-infrastructure is not that it moves goods. It is that it converts a discretionary political choice into a fixed obligation that the next government, and the one after that, must defend. The concrete does not vote. It simply narrows, year by year, the range of things a country can plausibly decide.

title: Punjab govt rejects allegations of CM ordered CCD encounters after Multan incident suspect s death
description: Azma Bokhari defends CCD  says cases involving organised crime are referred to CCD for better investigation
content:
Azma Bokhari defends CCD, says cases involving organised crime are referred to CCD for better investigation
Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari on Wednesday rejected the criticism surrounding the alleged police encounter in which a man accused of killing a 15-year-old boy was himself killed, categorically denying that Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz had ordered the Punjab Crime Control Department (CCD) to carry out encounters and asserting that the provincial government stood with the oppressed, not the oppressors.
The suspect, Tauqeer Nazir, had allegedly chased Waseem Abbas in his car after a dispute over work and run him over in a private housing society in Multan on Monday. He was arrested and handed over to police on a four-day physical remand by a judicial magistrate the following day. Earlier today, police said the suspect fled custody and was then killed by his accomplices when a police party tried to re-arrest him.
Hours before the incident, the prime suspect in the case involving the death by suicide of former International Islamic University Islamabad student Laiba Ejaz also died after being wounded by gunfire allegedly by his accomplices during an attack on a police team in Islamabad. The developments were met with criticism, with calls for justice through the legal route and the courts.
Read : HRCP calls for independent probe into Waseem Abbas case, expresses concern over alleged extrajudicial killing of prime suspect
In an interview on local television programme Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Sath about the killing of Multan incident's primary suspect, the minister was asked about hundreds of alleged extrajudicial killings by the CCD, in which the main suspect was reportedly killed while accomplices escaped, rejecting the suggestion that this pattern occurred in every case.
She said that even when a suspect was killed, the remaining suspects were subsequently traced, arrested and brought before the police.
“When a suspect is killed, the investigation slows down a little. When suspects flee, it takes some time to trace them. But this does not mean that this happens in every incident,” she said.
Asked whether the chief minister had directly ordered the CCD to carry out encounters against such suspects, the minister categorically denied it.
“Why would the chief minister order an encounter? It is not as if she has foreknowledge of such incidents,” she said.
“The state has a responsibility to stand with the oppressed. You may consider this a mistake on the part of the state or an allegation against it; you may call it whatever you like, but the Punjab government does not stand with the oppressor. It stands with the oppressed,” she said.
She added that there was no backdoor for the powerful in the province to evade the law or avoid facing legal proceedings.
Also Read : Man accused of running over Multan teenager killed in CCD encounter
Bokhari said an investigation had revealed that the Multan incident suspect was short-tempered and ill-mannered and had treated Abbas harshly. She said the boy had tried to flee three times but was caught each time.
She said the suspect’s actions demonstrated his mindset, alleging that he chased the teenager and killed him while the latter was attempting to escape through a gate. The minister added that the brutality was such that the victim’s face had become unrecognisable.
Bokhari further alleged that Nazir was a violent person who did not treat his own children properly and subjected them to violence as well.
The minister acknowledged that he had no previous criminal record and that, given the evidence against him, including CCTV footage, a court could have sentenced him. However, she said, he chose to flee rather than face trial.
“These are criminal-minded people. He could have been punished by a court, but if someone tries to escape from the court, or his accomplices help him flee, what can the police do?” she said.
Read : Primary suspect in Laiba Ejaz suicide case dies after being shot by accomplices: police
When asked about a post on X by PML-N MPA and Punjab government official Hina Pervez Butt that was later deleted, Bokhari questioned the seriousness of the former’s statements.
“I do not want to talk about her, but she has posted such things before, perhaps out of a lack of seriousness. She has also made statements that created problems for her and caused embarrassment for the government,” she said.
Earlier in the day, Hina had shared screenshots of a television report about the Multan encounter on X, drawing criticism for her supportive remarks.
“This is Maryam Nawaz sahiba’s government; justice is served immediately here,” she wrote in a post that was later deleted amid criticism over its perceived endorsement of an extrajudicial killing under the provincial government’s watch.
Bokhari said cases involving organised crime were referred to the CCD rather than the regular police to ensure more effective investigation and prosecution and to meet all legal requirements for delivering justice.
She said the CCD had arrested hundreds, possibly thousands, of criminals, adding that public discussion should also focus on those who had been prosecuted and punished rather than only on the few hundred suspects who had allegedly tried to flee.
The minister reiterated that the chief minister had not ordered any encounter, adding that the government stood with the oppressed rather than the oppressors.
On judicial reforms, Bokhari said Pakistan was among the few countries with a large number of judicial laws, but the key issue was their implementation.
She added that the chief minister was also working to revamp the prosecution system and that considerable progress had been made in this regard.
Allegations of extrajudicial killings and increasingly unlawful conduct by Punjab’s CCD have long been a source of concern for human rights organisations, which have repeatedly raised the issue.
According to figures released by the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan in June, the organisation had documented 808 police ‘encounters’ since the CCD was established in April 2025, in which at least 1,100 suspects were killed.
Earlier today, it expressed concern over Abbas's killing and the subsequent death of the primary suspect in an alleged police encounter , calling for an independent and transparent investigation into the case.
The commission said extrajudicial killings violated the right to due process and deprived victims and their families of the opportunity to establish the truth and seek justice.
It added that the perception that such killings were an acceptable means of controlling crime suggested that vengeance without accountability was being prioritised over justice.
The HRCP called for an independent and transparent investigation into the case and urged the authorities to bring an end to extrajudicial killings in all forms.

title: Lea Michele to reprise Rachel Berry role in    Glee    reboot
description: Lea Michele will reprise her role as Rachel Berry in the upcoming    Glee    reboot for Disney  and Hulu this time
content:
Lea Michele will reprise her role as Rachel Berry in the upcoming ‘Glee’ reboot for Disney+ and Hulu this time
Lea Michele is set to reprise her role as Rachel Berry in the upcoming Glee reboot for Disney+ and Hulu, according to Variety , which confirmed the news through multiple sources.
The actress starred as Rachel throughout the musical comedy-drama’s six-season run on Fox from 2009 to 2015. The character was an ambitious and talented member of McKinley High School’s glee club who dreamed of becoming a Broadway star.
Michele’s return follows recent developments surrounding the reboot, with creator Ryan Murphy confirming that he had completed a script alongside collaborators Brad Falchuk and Ian Brennan.
Murphy also revealed that he had been in contact with around 10 original cast members, who responded enthusiastically to the possibility of returning to the series.
Two other original cast members, Heather Morris, who played Brittany Pierce, and Chord Overstreet, who portrayed Sam Evans, have also shared social media posts suggesting their involvement in the reboot. Overstreet posted, “Reunited and it feels so good!” on October 21.
Michele had previously expressed interest in returning to Glee , telling E! News that the series would always hold a special place in her heart. She also spoke warmly about her relationship with Murphy and said she would follow him wherever he went.
Before joining the series, Michele had established herself as a Broadway performer, appearing in productions including Les Misérables , Ragtime , Fiddler on the Roof and Spring Awakening .
Following Glee , she appeared in Murphy’s Fox series Scream Queens before returning to Broadway in the revival of Funny Girl in 2022. Her performance as Fanny Brice drew attention partly because Rachel Berry had also dreamed of playing the role on Glee .
Michele received an Emmy nomination and two Golden Globe nominations for her work on the original series.
The Glee finale aired on March 20, 2015, ending Rachel’s story with a Tony Award win, her marriage to Jesse St. James and her future as a surrogate mother for Kurt Hummel and Blaine Anderson.
Further details about the reboot, including its release date and complete cast, have yet to be announced.

title: Interior minister returns Rs5 million to Laiba Ejaz s family  updates on case progress
description: Laiba s father expresses gratitude to  PM Shehbaz  interior minister  for their support and efforts in the case
content:
Laiba's father expresses gratitude to PM Shehbaz, interior minister for their support and efforts in the case
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Wednesday handed Rs5 million to the family of late student Laiba Ejaz during a visit to her residence to offer condolences and brief the family on progress in the case.
Laiba, who had aspired to study at a top US university, was found hanging from a tree near a road in Islamabad on October 9, after her family allegedly lost around Rs7 million to a consultant who had promised to secure her admission and a scholarship.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice of the incident and directed the inspector general of Islamabad police and the chief commissioner to take immediate action against the suspect. Naqvi also vowed to look into the case personally. The primary suspect in the case died after being wounded by gunfire from his own accomplices during an exchange of fire with police in Islamabad a day ago.
Laiba's father told The Express Tribune that the interior minister handed him Rs5 million recovered by the police from the primary suspect.
Naqvi was accompanied by Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry during the visit to Laiba's residence in G-10, Islamabad.
Read : PM takes notice of gold medallist's suicide
Naqvi expressed his condolences to the bereaved family and offered prayers.
The interior minister informed Laiba's family about the progress made in the investigation of her case/
“The entire team worked day and night on the Laiba Ejaz case. Fulfilling the promise made to you was our duty,” Naqvi said.
Read More : Primary suspect in Laiba Ejaz suicide case dies after being shot by accomplices: police
Laiba's father expressed his gratitude to PM Shehbaz and the interior minister for their support and efforts in the case.
“We had heard that the state is like a mother. Today, we have come to believe it,” he said.
According to a police spokesperson, the primary suspect, identified as Muhammad Nauman, was in custody and was being taken to a location for recovery on the basis of information provided by him when the incident occurred.
The spokesperson said four of Nauman’s accomplices, travelling on two motorcycles, had been lying in wait along the route. They opened indiscriminate fire on the police team in an attempt to secure his release.
Nauman was wounded by gunfire from his own accomplices, the spokesperson said, adding that police personnel remained unharmed due to their bulletproof jackets and other precautionary measures.
The injured suspect was taken to a hospital for medical treatment but later succumbed to his injuries, the spokesperson confirmed.
Search operations were under way to arrest the remaining suspects, according to the police.
The Federal Investigation Agency’s (FIA) Anti-Human Trafficking Circle in Islamabad had registered a case against Nauman and Fatima Sarwar under Sections 419 (cheating), 420 (cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property) and 109 (abetment) of the Pakistan Penal Code, read with Sections 18 and 22 of the Emigration Ordinance, 1979.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspects allegedly acted in connivance to deceive Laiba with promises of a US visa and scholarship. They allegedly received a total of Rs9.3 million from the family.
The FIA said the suspects allegedly prepared fake scholarship award letters, university admission offer letters and fee payment receipts to keep the family under the impression that the process was genuine. Of the total amount, Rs2.9m was transferred through Laiba’s personal bank account, while the remaining sum was received in cash, according to the agency.
Also Read : Islamabad court grants five-day remand of suspect in Laiba suicide case
Laiba's family stated that she had aspired to enrol at Harvard University for further studies and that they had made significant financial sacrifices to secure Laiba’s academic future and fulfil her dream. Laiba’s father sold his plot and pitched in Rs2.1 million from the sale’s proceeds, while her mother sold her gold jewellery.
According to the family, the suspect who reportedly defrauded them claimed to be an accounts officer at the Islamabad High Court and at other times presented himself as an employee of the superior judiciary or an officer of a sensitive institution. The family claimed that despite the substantial payment, the promises regarding admission and the scholarship given to Laiba were never fulfilled.
Laiba’s maternal uncle, Rana Amjad, stated that the Harvard University admission letter, scholarship letter and other documents provided by the suspect turned out to be fake upon verification.
He said that Laiba suffered severe distress and mental anguish after the alleged fraud came to light. Her family demanded a thorough investigation into the matter, the arrest of all individuals involved in the alleged fraud, and the recovery of the money.

title: Novo Pakistan steps up to support insulin access

content:
Novo Pakistan works towards long-term solutions to address diabetes care needs and support insulin access
Novo Pakistan is stepping up to support people living with diabetes amid concerns about access to insulin.
The company is working closely with its partners to play its part in supporting continuity of treatment, recognising how much dependable access to insulin means to people living with diabetes and their families.
Pakistan has an estimated 33 million people living with diabetes and more than one million relying on insulin. Novo Pakistan understands the challenge and strives to address the need for practical, long-term solutions to confront the diabetes burden in the country.
Mehtaz Sultan Khan, General Manager, Novo Pakistan, said:
Diabetes care has been at the heart of Novo for more than 100 years and delivering on that commitment remains our priority today. For people who depend on insulin, reliable access to treatment is essential. We recognise the concerns being raised and are stepping up to play our part in supporting patients in Pakistan.
As Pakistan continues to confront the growing burden of diabetes, Novo Pakistan remains committed to working alongside healthcare professionals, policymakers and patient communities to improve care.
People concerned about their prescribed insulin should speak to a healthcare professional about appropriate next steps. They can also access educational resources, guidance and connections to healthcare professionals through NovoCare.
For information and support, visit NovoCare.pk or call 021-1111-46686.
Novo Nordisk is a leading global healthcare company founded in 1923 and headquartered in Denmark. The brands purpose is to drive change to defeat serious chronic diseases built upon our heritage in diabetes.
They do so by pioneering scientific breakthroughs, expanding access to their medicines, and working to prevent and ultimately cure disease. Novo Nordisk employs about 68,800 people in 80 countries and markets its products in around 170 countries.

title: Iran open to diplomacy if US shows  sincerity   says Araghchi
description: IRGC deputy commander says Iran   s armed forces control Strait of Hormuz battlefield for as long as Tehran desires
content:
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards say preparing to unveil ‘father of all bombs’
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday stated that Tehran was prepared to give diplomacy another chance if it saw "strong evidence" of a sincere desire by the United States to "build trust and reach a just solution".
In a post on X, while sharing his opinion piece published earlier in The Financial Times, Araghchi warned that if the US "chooses war over diplomacy, it'll certainly result in an even greater strategic failure".
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards say preparing to unveil ‘father of all bombs’
Iran is preparing to unveil a new weapon described as the “father of all bombs,” a spokesman for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Wednesday.
“We are in the stage of preparing to unveil the ‘father of all bombs.’ This is something new for the enemy,” Hossein Mohebi said in statements carried by Iran’s Young Journalists Club news agency.
He did not provide further details about the weapon.
On Friday, US President Donald Trump had hinted at the possible use of the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast Bomb, also known as the “mother of all bombs,” to target Iranian nuclear facilities.
Weighing around 9,800 kilograms (21,600 pounds), the GBU-43/B is one of the largest non-nuclear conventional bombs in the US arsenal.
It was first used in April 2017, during Trump’s first presidential term, against a tunnel complex belonging to the ISIS (Daesh) terrorist organisation in Afghanistan.
Mohebi also said Iran’s missile stockpile has increased by 1.5 times following the 12-day war between Iran and Israel in June 2025, without providing specific figures.
“The quality of the missiles has improved significantly, and their range, destructive power and accuracy in hitting targets have increased,” he added.
Pezeshkian says Washington cannot expect dialogue with Tehran while issuing threats
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Wednesday that the US could not expect dialogue with Iran while at the same time issuing threats.
Washington “must recognise the rights of our nation and stop their bullying and aggression; then we can sit together and talk,” Pezeshkian said in remarks carried by the state-run IRNA news agency.
“You cannot block all the roads and threaten and at the same time want to talk,” he added.
Accusing the US of “reneging” on its commitments, Pezeshkian said: “I believe that one should not enter into a pact lightly, but once a pact is made, one must remain committed to it until the end – even if it proves disadvantageous.”
Tensions in the Middle East have remained high since the US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28.
Tehran responded with missile and drone attacks across the region and effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, while Washington later imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports.
The US and Iran subsequently signed a memorandum of understanding in June concerning freedom of navigation in the strait, but implementation stalled over disagreements related to security in the strategic waterway
US-Iran talks continue through Pakistan, Qatar: Iranian FM
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said negotiations with the United States were continuing without interruption through mediators, including Pakistan and Qatar, IRNA reported on Wednesday.
According to the post on X , Iranian media stated, "Speaking to Iraqi media, FM Araghchi stated that negotiations with the United States, conducted via mediators such as Pakistan and Qatar, remain ongoing without interruption."
Iranian media further added that Major General Mostafa Izadi, deputy commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), said that Iran's Armed Forces control the battlefield in the Strait of Hormuz and would continue to do so for as long as the Islamic Republic desires.
Addressing a gathering in the central Iranian city of Khomain on Tuesday, Izadi claimed that the IRGC Navy and Aerospace Forces maintained operational and intelligence superiority over the strategic waterway.
He said that Iran's enemies sought to push the people away from the scene, adding that the people’s presence and support for the country were key to safeguarding achievements and thwarting the enemies’ plots.
Referring to Iran's missile capabilities, Izadi claimed that American forces were “dawdling at sea” and had moved approximately 700 kilometres away to avoid being targeted by IRGC missiles.
Read: Pakistan, Turkiye, Qatar, and Indonesia to ink defence industry pact
The IRGC deputy commander also referred to the 12-day and 40-day wars, claiming that Iran had emerged victorious despite its adversaries deploying their full military capabilities.
He said Iran's armed forces, supported by the country's people, had delivered a firm response during both conflicts.
Izadi maintained that neither psychological warfare nor propaganda could change the outcome on the battlefield, arguing that Iran's victories were the result of the steadfastness of its people.
Iran's FM says his country is ready for diplomacy, but will 'defend ourselves'
Iran is ready for diplomacy but will defend itself, FM Araghchi wrote in an article published in the Financial Times on Wednesday. "While Iran is firmly committed to seeking a dignified peaceful resolution to the conflict, we are also fully prepared to defend ourselves," he wrote.
He said the White House had shown no willingness to reach an understanding and that there was little reason to expect progress now.
US engaging multiple countries over possible Iran talks: Rubio
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was engaging with multiple countries over possible negotiations with Iran, but insisted that any agreement must prevent Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon, Al Jazeera reported on Wednesday.
Iraq closes Sheeb border crossing with Iran to review security, sources say
Iraq has closed the busy Sheeb border crossing with Iran to review security and install detection equipment to stop the smuggling of prohibited materials, an Iraqi border official said on Wednesday.
Sheeb would be closed to passengers, vehicles and commercial trucks until further notice, two other sources at the crossing said.
A security official from Iran's southwestern Khuzestan province also said that the Sheeb crossing, known in Iran as Chazabeh, will be closed until further notice, adding that the decision was taken by the Iraqi government, the Iranian labour news agency reported on Wednesday.
The Iranian official, Valiollah Hayati, said consultations to resume operations at the border crossing were ongoing between Iran's Interior Ministry and Iraqi provincial authorities.
Hayati advised passengers and trucks to use Shalamcheh crossing, also in Khuzestan province, which Iraq closed temporarily in September as a precaution after drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, two security sources said at the time. Riyadh said the drones had been launched from Iraq, which did not comment on the matter.
The current security measures at Sheeb are weak and inadequate, the Iraqi border crossing official told Reuters.
Iran says Saudi Arabia, Houthis have not answered mediation offer
Iran has not received a response from Saudi Arabia or Yemen's Houthis to its offer to help broker talks to end the fighting between them, Iranian foreign minister said in a television interview aired on Tuesday. He offered to help facilitate dialogue as the Houthis intensified strikes on Saudi Arabia earlier this month.
In the interview with Iraq's Al Ekhbariya TV, Araghchi also responded to the possibility of Egypt joining Saudi Arabia in the war against the Houthis.
"Any foreign intervention would complicate matters," he said, adding Cairo has previously told Tehran that it would "not directly" interfere in the Yemeni conflict. Egypt has said it is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security, potentially raising the stakes ​in the Middle East.
A vote in the Egyptian parliament on a possible move against the Houthi fighters by the country's military, one of the Arab world's largest, was delayed until October 26.
Pak-Iran border reopens as CDF visits Tehran
The Pakistan-Iran border was reopened on Tuesday as Chief of Defence Forces and Army Chief Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir held a series of high-level talks in Tehran at the time when Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia added a new and potentially difficult dimension to Islamabad's regional balancing act.
Field Marshal Asim Munir, accompanied by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and General Mohsen Rezaei, representative of Iran's Supreme Leader and Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, during his fifth visit to Iran in recent months.
Read more: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted, destroyed drones in Madinah, eastern province
Unlike his previous trips, which were largely driven by Pakistan's efforts to defuse tensions between Iran and the United States, the latest visit came against the backdrop of repeated attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Saudi energy, airport and other infrastructure.
The development presents a delicate challenge for Islamabad. Pakistan has pledged to defend Saudi Arabia under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, while at the same time maintaining close engagement with Tehran and attempting to revive stalled Iran-US diplomacy.
There was no official statement from the Pakistani side until the filing of this report. However, an official familiar with the visit told The Express Tribune that the talks went "very well", without sharing specifics. The official also confirmed that the Pakistan-Iran border had reopened.
Iranian readouts also quoted Field Marshal Asim Munir as saying that issues concerning the border had been resolved. "The issues concerning the Iran-Pakistan border have been resolved, and the border has been reopened as of this morning," the CDF was quoted as saying during a meeting with General Rezaei.

title: Pakistan, Maldives sign 20 MoUs, target $200m in trade in two years | The Express Tribune
description: PM Shehbaz hopes visit will strengthen bilateral ties, President Muizzu calls agreements 'new era' of partnership
content:
PM Shehbaz hopes visit will strengthen bilateral ties, President Muizzu calls agreements 'new era' of partnership
Pakistan and the Maldives agreed to increase bilateral trade from $13.9 million to $200 million within the next two years, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced on Wednesday, as the two countries signed 20 agreements and memorandums of understanding (MoUs) to expand cooperation across several sectors.
The pacts were signed during the three-day state visit of the President of the Maldives, Dr Mohamed Muizzu, which is the first visit by the country’s president in 11 years, coinciding with the 60th anniversary of the bilateral diplomatic relations.
Speaking at a ceremony following the signing, PM Shehbaz said the trade target had been agreed with the “complete endorsement” of Maldivian President Muizzu, who was on a three-day state visit to Pakistan.
"We will do our best jointly to raise this bilateral trade quantum from 13 million dollars to 200 million dollars in the next two years,” he said.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif presents an honorary PhD degree to Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu during a special convocation at the Prime Minister’s House in Islamabad on Wednesday. Photo: PID
PM Shehbaz said existing trade, valued at $13.9 million, represented only a fraction of the countries’ economic potential.
He said the two sides had held “very productive and very fruitful discussions” on economic and trade relations, strategic defence cooperation and training in policing, defence, education and health.
Highlighting existing cooperation in healthcare and education, he said a large number of Maldivian students had studied at Pakistani universities and colleges, particularly in healthcare.
“About 250 Pakistani doctors are serving the cause of suffering humanity along with Pakistani paramedics in Maldives and other places in your great country,” he said, adding that Pakistan was willing to provide more professionals to meet the Maldives’ needs.
PM Shehbaz announced that Pakistan would support the Maldives’ plan to plant five million trees by providing 100,000 olive cuttings and 100,000 seeds of different plant species.
The material would be provided “in due course of time with mutual understanding”, he said.
Pakistan was also ready to provide technical expertise under the agreements. The prime minister welcomed the Maldives’ efforts to establish data centres, saying Pakistan had developed its own technical capabilities and would be willing to share its experience.
“We have already set up various data centres in various parts of Pakistan, starting from half megawatt to eight and a half megawatt,” he said.
The prime minister also welcomed the Maldives’ support for Palestine, “Maldives fully supports the cause of Palestine steadfastly and unwaveringly,” he said. “Pakistan stands fully committed to the cause of Palestine and their right to self-determination and the establishment of an independent, sovereign and contiguous state of Palestine in accordance with relevant UN resolutions,” he added.
The prime minister said he had also briefed President Muizzu on Pakistan’s position on Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir, reiterating Islamabad’s support for a peaceful resolution in accordance with relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people.
He also raised Pakistan’s concerns over India’s decision to place the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, stressing that international agreements must be respected.
“Legally binding treaties must be respected, and shared water resources must never be weaponised or used as an instrument of political pressure or blackmail,” he said.
Referring to his remarks at the United Nations General Assembly, PM Shehbaz repeated, “Water is a red line for Pakistan.” He added that any violation concerning shared water resources would be regarded by Pakistan as “an act of war”.
Welcoming President Muizzu, PM Shehbaz said the visit was significant as it was the first by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in 11 years and coincided with the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries, established in 1966.
“We extend a very warm welcome to you on behalf of the people of Pakistan, my government and myself,” he said.
The premier also expressed confidence that the visit would give bilateral relations fresh momentum and take them to a “stronger, broader and more substantive level”.
He also congratulated President Muizzu on the honorary doctorate he was due to receive from the International Islamic University Islamabad in recognition of his leadership and public service.
The prime minister pledged to work personally with President Muizzu to ensure the agreements were implemented promptly.
“I will be very happy to personally work with you to translate these written MOUs into action with prompt decision-making and speedy implementation,” he said.
President Muizzu, in his address, said the agreements marked an opportunity to move the relationship between the two countries into “a new era” of partnership, building on six decades of diplomatic ties.
“My visit is particularly significant because of the timing,” he said. “It is 60 years since Pakistan opened diplomatic relations with the Maldives and those have been 60 years of warm friendship between us.”
He said the visit, the first by a Maldivian president in a decade, offered “an important opportunity not simply to celebrate the friendship of the past but to define the partnership of the future.”
He thanked PM Shehbaz, the government and the people of Pakistan for the “exceptional warmth and gracious hospitality” extended to him, his wife and his delegation.
President Muizzu said his discussions with the prime minister had reflected a shared ambition to make bilateral relations “broader, more dynamic and more directly beneficial to our peoples”.
President Muizzu said the exchange of 20 MoUs in areas including health, education, fisheries and agriculture, youth, arts, Islamic affairs, tourism, information technology, police and defence would open new avenues for cooperation.
“Agreements are meaningful only when they produce results,” he said, adding that the next step was to turn the understandings into “tangible opportunities and meaningful benefits for the people of both nations”.
“I fully endorse and agree to take our bilateral trade between our two countries from 13 million to 200 million dollars within the next two years,” he said.
He said the two sides had agreed to expand trade, encourage investment, deepen tourism cooperation and improve connectivity.
The Maldives-Pakistan Business Forum, scheduled for Thursday, would bring together business leaders, investors and innovators from both countries to develop partnerships, he said.
President Muizzu also welcomed ongoing discussions on establishing direct flights between the two countries, saying air links would create new opportunities for tourism.
“We also see considerable potential in halal and Muslim-friendly tourism, where our shared values and experiences provide a strong foundation for partnership,” he said.
President Muizzu said the two leaders had placed particular emphasis on young people and agreed to broaden opportunities for Maldivian students, athletes, coaches and young professionals in Pakistan.
“Pakistan has long provided valuable scholarships, training opportunities and placements for Maldivian students, athletes, coaches and young professionals,” he said. “We deeply appreciate this support.”
Maldivian president said that the two countries would strengthen their youth exchange programme and expand cooperation in skills development, entrepreneurship, innovation and leadership. They had also discussed opportunities for young people in emerging fields, including artificial intelligence, digitalisation and future technologies.
“We want our next generation to be prepared for the future and be prepared to shape that future,” President Muizzu said.
He said that in healthcare, the talks focused on expanding opportunities for Maldivian students and medical professionals, including increasing MBBS placements under Pakistan’s Technical Assistance Programme and exploring internships in Pakistan for Maldivian medical graduates.
“These are investments not merely in institutions, but in people, in knowledge and skills and in the future capacity of our nation,” he said.
Speaking on climate change, President Muizzu said that for the Maldives, climate change was not an “abstract environmental concern.”
“It is a direct challenge to our security, our development and our future,” he said.
He welcomed stronger cooperation with Pakistan on conservation, sustainable waste management, renewable energy and climate resilience.
The Maldivian president also thanked the prime minister for announcing donations to support the Maldives’ target of planting five million trees during the five-year term of his government.
President Muizzu highlighted the shared commitment between Pakistan and the to advancing common interests through engagement at the United Nations, the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation and other multilateral and regional forums.
He also stressed the importance of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), saying the regional body had significant potential to address shared challenges through collective action.
“The Maldives remains firmly committed to playing a constructive and proactive role in revitalising SAARC,” he said. Rebuilding trust, promoting meaningful dialogue and strengthening mutual understanding were essential to regional cooperation, he added.
“The Maldives stands ready to work closely with all SAARC member states towards creating the necessary conditions for convening the next SAARC Summit at the earliest possible opportunity,” President Muizzu said.
On Palestine, he reiterated the Maldives’ support for the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination and an independent, sovereign state based on the pre-1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.
He also commended Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts amid the ongoing crisis in the Middle East, including its efforts to promote dialogue, de-escalation, humanitarian assistance and a lasting peace.
“The prime minister and I agreed that it is the friendship between our people, the bonds of faith, the exchange of knowledge and the spirit of mutual respect that gives us a relationship with strength and permanence,” he said.
President Muizzu said Pakistan had been a trusted friend of the Maldives for 60 years and that, “Today, the prime minister and I have agreed to turn a new leaf, to build a new era of partnership on the foundations of our six decades of friendship.”
He said the partnership would deliver “greater opportunity, greater prosperity and greater benefits” to the people of both countries.
President Muizzu expressed confidence that the understandings reached during the talks would deepen bilateral ties and create further opportunities for cooperation.
“May the friendship between the Maldives and Pakistan continue to flourish for generations to come,” he said, adding that the two countries could look towards a bright future.
20 MoUs signed between Maldives and Pakistan
The agreements covered information technology, cyber security, artificial intelligence, digital skills, narcotics control, social protection, health, recruitment of health professionals, defence, maritime security, agriculture, fisheries, technical and vocational training, higher education, youth and sports development, air connectivity and environmental cooperation. They also included cooperation between Pakistan’s Drug Regulatory Authority and the Maldives Food and Drug Authority.
PM Shehbaz and President Muizzu witnessed the ceremony as the representatives from both sides exchanged the pre-signed documents.
Meanwhile, Chief of Defence Forces and Army Chief Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir called on President Muizzu in Islamabad, according to the military's media wing.
The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that during the meeting, the two sides discussed matters of mutual interest, the prevailing regional security environment, and avenues for enhancing bilateral cooperation, further adding that both sides underscored the importance of strengthening defence cooperation, institutional linkages, and professional exchanges.
"The COAS & CDF highlighted the longstanding and cordial relations between Pakistan and the Maldives and reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further strengthening bilateral cooperation and promoting regional peace, stability and security through constructive engagement," ISPR added.
The media wing added that President Muizzu commended the professionalism of Pakistan’s armed forces and appreciated Pakistan’s continued efforts to promote peace and stability in the region.
Maldives president presented guard of honour
Earlier, the Maldivian president was presented with a guard of honour at the Prime Minister’s House as he arrived to meet PM Shehbaz for high-level delegation talks.
He is accompanied by First Lady Sajidha Mohamed and a high-level delegation comprising cabinet members and senior officials.
PM Shehbaz welcomed President Muizzu at the formal reception ceremony, during which the national anthems of Pakistan and the Maldives were played as the two leaders stood at the salute dais.
A smartly turned-out contingent of the Pakistan Armed Forces presented the guard of honour to the visiting president, who reviewed the contingent.
Following the ceremony, the two leaders introduced their respective delegations before proceeding to one-on-one and delegation-level talks. He also planted a sapling on the lawns of the Prime Minister’s House.
The visit marked the first by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in 11 years and coincided with the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries, established in 1966.
Earlier, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met President Muizzu, reaffirming Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening bilateral relations and expanding cooperation in trade, investment, education, climate change and tourism, the Foreign Office (FO) said.
In a post on X, the FO said FM Dar “conveyed warm greetings and best wishes from President Asif Ali Zardari and PM Shehbaz to President Muizzu”.
“He warmly welcomed the President and his delegation to Pakistan,” the ministry added.
Reaffirming Pakistan’s commitment to its longstanding fraternal relations with Maldives, FM Dar underscored the importance of expanding "bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade, investment, education, climate change and tourism."

title: Matthew Perry   s sister reveals what fans never knew about his  Friends  wedding scene
description: Matthew Perry   s sister Mia reflects on his addiction and bittersweet memories behind the iconic Friends wedding scene
content:
Matthew Perry’s sister Mia reflects on his addiction and bittersweet memories behind the iconic Friends wedding scene
Matthew Perry’s sister, Mia Perry Bowick, has opened up about the late actor’s struggles with addiction and the emotional memories surrounding one of his most memorable moments on Friends .
In an interview with People published on October 21, Mia reflected on the filming of the season seven episode in which Perry’s character, Chandler Bing, married Monica Geller, played by Courteney Cox.
While the wedding remains a fan-favourite moment from the popular sitcom, Mia recalled that the experience carried a deeper emotional significance for their family. According to her, Perry had recently left rehabilitation when the episode was filmed, following an escalation in his alcohol and drug use between seasons five and seven.
Mia said the family understood the seriousness of his addiction, leaving them uncertain about what the future might hold.
She also reflected on how the fictional wedding represented something Perry wanted in his personal life. Beyond his success as an actor, he hoped to find a life partner and have children, she explained in the interview.
Perry became widely known for portraying Chandler Bing throughout the NBC sitcom’s 10-season run from 1994 to 2004. His character’s relationship with Monica became one of the show’s central storylines, culminating in their wedding during the seventh season.
The interview marks one of Mia’s first public conversations about her brother since his death in October 2023 at the age of 54.
Her reflections feature in discussions surrounding The One About Matthew Perry , a Netflix documentary examining the actor’s life, career and prolonged struggle with addiction. The project includes personal accounts from people who knew him and offers insight into experiences beyond his television fame.
Perry’s portrayal of Chandler remains a defining part of his legacy, while his openness about addiction helped bring greater attention to the challenges of substance use and recovery.
Through her recollections, Mia offers a personal perspective on the contrast between her brother’s beloved on-screen moments and the difficulties he faced away from the cameras.

title: Martin Garrix announces debut album    MARTY    featuring Madonna  U2 and Ed Sheeran
description: The 14 track project  the first album of the artist  will arrive on March 5  2027
content:
The 14-track project, the first album of the artist, will arrive on March 5, 2027
Martin Garrix has announced the release date for his long-awaited album MARTY, featuring collaborations with Madonna, U2, Ed Sheeran and Spanish singer AITANA. The 14-track project will arrive on March 5, 2027, marking a new chapter in the Dutch DJ and producer's career.
Announced on October 21, the album will be released through Darkroom Records and Garrix's own label, STMPD RCRDS. Named after his first DJ alias, MARTY explores different chapters of his life, tracing his journey from childhood through his rise to international stardom.
Although Garrix previously released Sentio in 2022, he describes that project as a club album, positioning MARTY as his first pop-dance record. The new release also sees him step beyond his established role as a DJ and producer, singing solo on four tracks for the first time.
The album features several high-profile collaborations, including Madonna on Bizarre, U2 on Fireflies and Ed Sheeran on Rewind Repeat It. The latter track was created more than a decade ago before its eventual release, while Garrix's collaboration with U2 brings together the producer and all four members of the legendary Irish rock band.
AITANA will also appear on Garrix's first Spanish-language song, with its title yet to be officially announced. Additional collaborators are expected to be revealed ahead of the album's release.
Garrix has already shared several tracks connected to the project. Catharina, released in March 2026, is a personal song dedicated to his mother, while Bizarre, featuring Madonna, arrived in July. His latest single, This Dream of You, was released on October 2.
Speaking to Rolling Stone, Garrix reflected on working with some of the music industry's most celebrated artists, describing the experience as surreal. He also explained that he had remained comfortable behind the DJ booth for much of his career, but had increasingly become interested in exploring his identity beyond producing electronic dance music.
The album's release comes more than a decade after Garrix rose to global fame with Animals in 2013. Since then, he has collaborated with artists including Dua Lipa, Usher, Macklemore and Fall Out Boy's Patrick Stump, establishing himself as one of electronic dance music's most recognisable names.
With MARTY, Garrix is set to combine his signature dance production with a more personal, pop-focused sound, offering listeners a closer look at the artist behind the DJ decks.

title: Govt cuts petrol by Rs2 71  increases diesel by 31 paisas for Oct 22
description: Petrol price decreases to Rs379 31 per litre  while HSD will cost Rs390 11
content:
Petrol price decreases to Rs379.31 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs390.11
The federal government on Wednesday decreased the price of petrol by Rs2.71 per litre while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by 31 paisas per litre for October 22.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs379.31 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs390.11 per litre for Thursday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol and HSD by 88 paisas and 53 paisas per litre, respectively, for October 21.
Read : Govt increases petrol by 88 paisas, diesel by 53 paisas per litre for Oct 21
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices were little changed on Wednesday ‌as investors weighed possible progress toward Russia-Ukraine talks against declining US oil stocks and a lack of US-Iran dialogue.
Brent crude futures gained 27 cents, or 0.2%, to $109.04 a barrel by 10:50 am ET (1450 GMT). US West Texas Intermediate crude was down 11 cents, or 0.1%, to $97.72.
"Crude futures are trading both sides of unchanged this morning but well below the overnight highs as attacks in the ​Strait of Hormuz look to be continuing with at least two more ships being struck overnight," said Dennis Kissler, senior vice president of ​trading at BOK Financial, in a note to clients.
