title: England  Sri Lanka seek revival
description: Both sides target first win to keep tri series hopes alive
content:
Both sides target first win to keep tri-series hopes alive
England will be desperate to get their campaign back on track when they face Sri Lanka in the second match of the ODI tri-series at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Thursday.
Both teams have lost their opening matches against Pakistan, who have emerged as a formidable side despite some shortcomings in their batting. England and Sri Lanka will therefore be under pressure to improve their performances and keep their hopes of reaching the final alive.
Harry Brook-led England, who recently defeated Sri Lanka in an ODI series at the latter's backyard, will need to address several weaknesses exposed in Tuesday's 87-run defeat by Pakistan.
Despite showing some resistance in the top order, England's batsmen failed to build on their starts and lost wickets in clusters. They also struggled against short-pitched and back-of-a-length deliveries on a double-paced surface, with Pakistan's seamers exploiting conditions effectively..
Sam Curran, Ben Duckett and Joe Root fell to Pakistan's pace attack, while left-arm spinner Arafat Minhas proved even more damaging, claiming 6-40 to dismantle the visitors.
Chasing 303, England appeared well placed at 165-3 before a dramatic collapse saw them dismissed for 215, handing Pakistan a convincing victory.
Pakistan also benefited from missed chances in the field. Gus Atkinson dropped Hasan Nawaz at backward square leg when he was on 28, while Minhas was also dropped three times. The most costly miss came when Minhas edged Curran behind on 12, but wicket-keeper Jordan Coxh failed to hold the catch after diving to his left.
Minhas later bowled England captain Harry Brook for five with a delivery that dipped and straightened, showcasing the accuracy and variation that made him the standout performer of the match.
Brook acknowledged England's failure to build partnerships after an encouraging start from Tom Banton and Duckett.
“We thought Banton, Duckett set the tone to get a 100 partnership and then it was a case of losing too many wickets in clumps, we couldn’t string the partnerships together and we ended up on the wrong side,” Brook said.
“We’ve spoken a lot about rotation of strike through the middle but I think we were a little too careful against the spinners especially, so we can probably put them under a little bit more pressure in stages and we’ve got to tonight to talk about it.”
England must also improve with the ball. Although they reduced Pakistan to 81-4, they failed to maintain the pressure and allowed the hosts to recover and pass 300.
Pakistan's batsmen capitalised on loose deliveries.
England will hope that their first outing in Pakistan has provided valuable lessons and that greater familiarity with the conditions will help them produce a more disciplined performance against Sri Lanka.
Sri Lanka, meanwhile, will also be looking to recover after letting a promising position slip against Pakistan. They recently played a T20I series against the hosts and finished that campaign with an emphatic eight-wicket victory in the final match.
In the ODI opener, however, Sri Lanka's lack of composure at a crucial stage proved costly. Chasing 306, they were well placed at 253-5 before losing their final five wickets for just 15 runs.
Pakistan's pace attack deserves credit for the turnaround. Faheem Ashraf broke a threatening partnership by dismissing Pavan Rathnayake for 79, while Haris Rauf removed Janith Liyanage for 60 to swing the match in Pakistan's favour.
Both England and Sri Lanka need to raise their game if they are to remain in contention for the final.
Pakistan moved to Lahore on Wednesday, with the remaining four matches of the tri-series scheduled to be played at the Gaddafi Stadium. The top two teams will qualify for the final on October 31.

title: Fact check  Viral video does not show Palestinian flag atop Eiffel Tower amid France riots  is AI generated
description: France has been experiencing widespread protests over rising living costs  demands for better resourced schools
content:
France has been experiencing widespread protests over rising living costs, demands for better-resourced schools
Several people, including right-wing American accounts, have been sharing a video on social media platform X since October 19, claiming it shows a Palestinian flag hoisted at the top of the Eiffel Tower during protests in Paris. However, the video is AI-generated.
France has been experiencing widespread protests over rising living costs, concerns about public services and demands for better-resourced schools. Demonstrations that began among high school students in the Paris region spread across the country, with students protesting deteriorating school facilities and staff shortages.
The movement has also drawn support from trade unions and other demonstrators, while some protests have escalated into violent demonstrations in Paris, including clashes with the police, burning cars and looted shops, while police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse protesters.
On October 19, an X account shared a video of flags being hoisted atop the Eiffel Tower, with the following caption: “Congratulations, Emmanuel Macron, you destroyed Paris.”
Read: Fact check: Viral K-P Home Department notification ordering arrests of PTI workers is fake
A pro-Trump account on X, based on its past posts and profile picture, also shared the same video on the same day with the same caption. The post gained 2.7m views.
Another account on X shared the same video on the same day with the following caption: “Paris has fallen. There is a Palestinian flag at the top of the Eiffel Tower. America, wake up. This could easily happen to us.”
The same video was shared by other right-wing American accounts on X and Instagram, as can be seen here , here , here , here , here and here , collectively gaining 304,995 views.
A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its high virality and keen public interest in visuals from the protests.
A keyword search was conducted to verify whether any credible French or international media outlets had reported that protesters had hoisted a Palestinian flag atop the Eiffel Tower. However, no credible reports confirming the incident or the viral visuals were found.
Another visual inconsistency was identified by comparing the viral video with authentic images of the Eiffel Tower. The people appearing in the video are disproportionately large in relation to the tower compared with those seen in real photographs.
Analysing the video using AI-detection tools showed that Deepfake Detector flagged the footage as 57 per cent AI-generated.
Similarly, another AI detection tool, UncovAI, also flagged the video as 54% AI-generated.
Hive Moderation also flagged the video as 49.7% AI-generated.
The claim that a viral video shows a Palestinian flag hoisted at the top of the Eiffel Tower in Paris is false .
The viral video is AI-generated and contains inconsistencies in the flags and the structure of the tower.
This fact check was originally published by iVerify Pakistan — a project of CEJ-IBA and UNDP.

title: 10 killed  35 injured as bus overturns on Rajanpur s Indus Highway
description: Bus was travelling from Karachi to Dera Ghazi Khan  overturned after hitting a divider on an under construction road
content:
Bus was travelling from Karachi to Dera Ghazi Khan, overturned after hitting a divider on an under-construction road
At least 10 passengers were killed and 35 injured on Wednesday when a passenger bus travelling from Karachi to Dera Ghazi Khan overturned after hitting a divider on an under-construction road near Bangla Hidayat on the Indus Highway in Rajanpur, Rescue 1122 said.
Women and children were among the dead and injured, according to rescue officials. Rescue teams reached the site after receiving information about the accident and shifted the injured to hospitals for treatment.
Rescue officials said 20 injured passengers were taken to Rajanpur District Headquarters Hospital, while 12 people with minor injuries were provided medical assistance at the scene.
Seven of the injured were initially reported to be in critical condition. Five were referred to a hospital in Dera Ghazi Khan and two to a hospital in Rahim Yar Khan for further treatment.
The deceased and injured belonged to Dera Ghazi Khan, Taunsa and Balochistan, rescue officials said.
The death toll rose to 10 after a woman and a child succumbed to their injuries, according to successive updates from Rescue 1122. The deceased included at least seven men and two women.
Read: Five young men killed as speeding car overturns, catches fire in Multan
October has seen a series of fatal road accidents across the country, including several involving passenger vehicles and heavy transport. On October 19, five young men were killed when a speeding car overturned and caught fire on Bosan Road in Multan. The car reportedly went out of control near Sabzazar Metro Station, hit a road divider, overturned, and crashed into a wall.
In a separate accident reported the same day, four people , including women and children, were killed when a Mazda truck collided with an Alto car near Darbi in Balochistan’s Bolan district.
Earlier, on October 16, eight people were killed and eight injured in two separate accidents in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. Six people died when a passenger van overturned in Buner, while two children were killed after being run over by a truck near Tarnab Road in Charsadda.

The same day, three members of a family , including a 15-year-old boy, were killed when a 22-wheeler trailer carrying cement crushed their car at a traffic signal on Allama Iqbal Road in Lahore’s Garhi Shahu area. The impact trapped the occupants inside the wreckage. While witnesses blamed brake failure, the first information report alleged that the trailer driver had been driving recklessly.
On October 13, four people, including a woman, were killed and five others injured when a van travelling from Quetta to Kalat collided with a truck on the Quetta-Karachi National Highway near Badrang in Mastung district. Police said the deceased and injured belonged to Kalat district.

Under the leadership of Shaheen Shah Afridi, Pakistan have won back-to-back matches against Sri Lanka and England in the ODI tri-series being played on home soil.
Pakistan defeated Sri Lanka by 37 runs before crushing England by 87 runs at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium, strengthening their position in the three-team competition. The series is also providing an opportunity to assess players and develop a combination capable of adapting to the varied pitches and conditions expected in southern Africa.
Despite the encouraging results, Pakistan's batting remains a concern, particularly at the top of the order.
The opening pair of Fakhar Zaman and Saim Ayub have struggled to make a consistent impact, while Babar Azam has yet to convert promising starts into substantial scores during the series.
There have, however, been encouraging performances from the middle order. Salman Ali Agha scored a century against Sri Lanka, while Hasan Nawaz and young all-rounder Arafat Minhas impressed against England.
The 21-year-old Minhas produced a particularly outstanding performance, scoring 59 runs to help Pakistan cross the 300-run mark before dismantling England's batting with figures of 6-40 in a commanding victory.
Pakistan captain Shaheen Afridi also acknowledged on Tuesday that some batsmen were short of form, highlighting an area the team management must address as it works towards a settled combination for the World Cup.
With time still available before the tournament, former Pakistan Test opener Sadiq Mohammad believes the selectors must prioritise technically sound batsmen who can adapt to the conditions expected in Africa.
“I think technically correct batsmen will be needed if Pakistan are to cope with the conditions in Africa,” Sadiq told The Express Tribune in an interview.
He recommended that Abdullah Shafique, Sahibzada Farhan and Maaz Sadaqat be considered for the World Cup plans, arguing that Pakistan would need technically proficient players to cope with challenging conditions.
“Shafiq, Farhan and Maaz also should be part of the World Cup plans as you will need such batsmen who are technically sound,” Sadiq said.
He also suggested that Fakhar and Saim return to domestic cricket to regain their confidence and develop the ability to play longer innings before being considered for the national side again.
“Saim has been a total failure with the bat where we need him most as opener and he has been given ample chances but did not perform,” Sadiq said.
Sadiq said Salman Ali Agha proved effective, pointing to his century against Sri Lanka. He also praised the team's decision to field five specialist bowlers.
“My suggestion to play Salman Ali Agha paid off with a century. Playing five bowlers also made a big difference,” Sadiq said.
He stressed that Pakistan needed to make changes at the top of the order and establish a dependable opening partnership well before the World Cup.
“It’s about time that Pakistan make some changes in top order and make sure that we have a solid opening pair,” he said.
Sadiq also backed Hasan Nawaz, suggesting that the young batsman could provide the middle order with the power-hitting ability required to finish innings strongly.
“Hasan can be an ideal batsman in the middle order. He can use long handle, the way Iftikhar Ahmed used to do,” Sadiq pointed out.
The former opener also called for Pakistan to develop greater depth in the all-round department, identifying Minhas as a promising option after his impressive performance against England. He suggested that off-spinner Sajid Khan could also be considered for an opportunity in ODI cricket.
“There is a need of a good all-rounder. Arafat has shown his guts both with the bat and ball and Sajid Khan could be another option as he can also prove to be handy if given chance in ODI cricket,” Sadiq said.
“He is a real fighter and should be tested,” he said, referring to Sajid.
Sadiq added that Pakistan needed to identify at least two more fast bowlers to strengthen their options alongside established pacers Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf and Naseem Shah.
“Pakistan also need two more pacers to be settled in the combination besides the regular bowlers Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf and Naseem Shah,” Sadiq said.

title: Christopher Nolan   s    The Prestige    returns to cinemas for 20th anniversary with first ever IMAX and 70mm theatrical screenings
description: Christian Bale and Hugh Jackman lead thriller about rival magicians  which earned two Oscar nominations
content:
Christian Bale and Hugh Jackman lead thriller about rival magicians, which earned two Oscar nominations
Christopher Nolan’s acclaimed thriller The Prestige is returning to cinemas in January 2027 to mark the 20th anniversary of its original release, giving audiences their first opportunity to experience the film on IMAX and 70mm screens.
Disney will re-release the 2006 film on January 29, 2027. The anniversary screenings will offer a new theatrical experience for the mystery thriller, which stars Christian Bale and Hugh Jackman as rival stage magicians whose professional competition develops into an increasingly dangerous personal feud.
Nolan expressed his excitement about bringing the film back to cinemas, particularly through the premium formats.
“I’m very excited to bring ‘The Prestige’ back to the big screen, and particularly thrilled to offer audiences the chance to see it on 70mm film, and on IMAX for the first time,” the director said in a statement.
Originally released on October 20, 2006, The Prestige explores obsession, sacrifice and deception as its two central characters attempt to outdo one another through increasingly elaborate illusions. The cast also includes Michael Caine, Scarlett Johansson, Rebecca Hall, Andy Serkis and David Bowie.
The film earned approximately $100 million worldwide and received two Academy Award nominations, further establishing its reputation as one of Nolan’s distinctive works. He co-wrote the screenplay with his brother, Jonathan Nolan, and produced the film alongside Emma Thomas and Aaron Ryder.
The anniversary release also highlights Nolan’s longstanding association with large format cinema. In subsequent years, he directed major productions including The Dark Knight trilogy, Inception , Interstellar and Oppenheimer , helping expand audience interest in IMAX presentations.
His later projects have continued to demonstrate the commercial potential of theatrical releases, particularly when presented in premium formats.
For fans revisiting The Prestige , the January screenings will provide an opportunity to experience the film’s intricate visual storytelling on a larger scale.

title: Sooryavanshi told to be patient
description: Consistent performances from Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma leave the teenager competing for an opening spot
content:
Consistent performances from Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma leave the teenager competing for an opening spot
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi "can't just walk straight into the team", India captain Shreyas Iyer said Wednesday, after calls for the teenage sensation to be unleashed for the T20 series against New Zealand starting in Christchurch this week.
The 15-year-old Sooryavanshi made his international debut for India in July but has been used sparingly against top opponents despite his glittering Indian Premier League form.
India landed in New Zealand on Tuesday, two days before they begin their 40-day tour including five T20s, five one-day internationals and two Test matches.
It marks 100 years of sporting ties between the two nations.
"He has many more years ahead to get opportunities," Iyer said when asked about the teenager's role in the squad.
"It's not as if he can just walk straight into the team right now because our openers have been scoring consistently and also won us the World Cup."
Sooryavanshi has taken the cricketing world by storm after making his IPL debut aged 14 years and 23 days in 2025.
Nine days later he scored his first IPL century.
In eight T20 internationals Sooryavanshi is averaging just over 30 at a strike rate of 186, below his IPL average of 44 and strike rate of nearly 229.
Since July Sooryavanshi's rivals for India's opening spot, Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma, have averaged 25 and 30 respectively, at strike rates of 172 and 200.
Iyer said Sooryavanshi would learn plenty from the tour, with or without game time.
"Look at it this way: coming overseas like this will give him a fair idea of how the game plays on these particular wickets, so next time when he comes he will be very well prepared for these conditions."
New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner said he was aware of Sooryavanshi's talents from playing in the IPL but pointed to the power of India's whole lineup.
"I think he has a huge part to play for India, whether it's in this series or in the future," Santner said.
"If he does get a crack guys have found it quite hard to stop him, but we've got some plans for him."
Santner said conditions would be seam friendly in the opening match at Hagley Oval.
India would have to get used to some unfamiliar conditions as they start the series, he said.
"Temperature-wise, you know, we've always when we've gone to India, it's hot, it's humid," Santner said.
"Here tomorrow night could be the flip side for India, could be a little bit cold, maybe windy, some cold hands."
New Zealand are without Will O'Rourke, Mark Chapman and Zak Foulkes for the T20 series but will be able to lean on the power hitting of Finn Allen and Tim Seifert at the top of the order.
India recalled seamer Bhuvneshwar Kumar after a four-year absence while Jasprit Bumrah was rested as part of workload management after he played a key part in the team's recent Asian Games gold medal in Japan.

title: UEFA demands answers from FIFA over Infantino presidency
description: The letter raises 42 questions across 12 topics and demands a response before FIFA   s December council meeting
content:
The letter raises 42 questions across 12 topics and demands a response before FIFA’s December council meeting
UEFA has sent a letter to FIFA seeking answers by November 2 about Gianni Infantino's presidency, including questions over the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) project and the FIFA Peace Prize.
European soccer's governing body UEFA has led calls ‌for Infantino to resign since he proposed the now-abandoned FFE project, which involved creating a company to run the commercial interests of FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, and selling a minority stake to private investors.
The 56-year-old, who is up for reelection next year, apologised to the FIFA Council last week and told attendees to ⁠submit any questions they had about his governance in writing so he could answer them at the next meeting on December 16.
However, UEFA General Secretary Theodore Theodoridis wrote to his FIFA counterpart Mattias Grafstrom on Monday seeking a swift response to 42 questions covering 12 topics.
"These questions require answers now," Theodoridis wrote.
"They cannot be deferred until the next meeting of the FIFA Council - nor can future governance reforms substitute for scrutiny of decisions already taken and accountability for them...
"We expect FIFA to provide the transparency required by its own governing body and to ‌respond ⁠fully within the above deadline."
"The FIFA Governance Regulations state that Council meetings and their associated documentation are confidential," a spokesperson for world soccer's governing body FIFA said on Tuesday.
"While FIFA intends to reply to questions submitted by its Council members it has ⁠no intention of breaching confidentiality by commenting on internal communication and/or documentation to media.
"FIFA considers respect for these Regulations to be a function of respect for the Council itself and for its individual ⁠members. FIFA will always maintain this respect and will not be drawn into any exchange with any third parties that undermines this."
UEFA did not immediately respond to a request ⁠for comment.
Infantino will stand for reelection in March 2027, with a November 18 deadline looming for potential candidates to submit their nominations.

title: Time to move on from LIV  says Oosthuizen
description: The 2010 British Open champion prioritises a more manageable tournament schedule
content:
The 2010 British Open champion prioritises a more manageable tournament schedule
Former British Open champion Louis Oosthuizen is set to become the latest player to leave LIV Golf with the South African saying it was time to move on from ‌the breakaway circuit as it grapples with an uncertain future.
Former world number one Jon Rahm is among those quitting the rebel circuit, which is fighting to emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) said in April it was ⁠cutting funding.
LIV has secured investment from BC Partners Credit and is set to make a decision this month on whether it winds down or moves forward with a 2.0 model.
Oosthuizen, who was among the first golfers to join LIV and played in its inaugural event in June 2022, told the South China Morning Post that the proposed stripped-back schedule would require a lot of international travel for single events.
"I need ‌to ⁠arrange my own schedule and look after my body," said the 44-year-old ahead of this week's Hong Kong Open.
"I want to play near one spot for three weeks at a time, not have all the big travelling ⁠for one tournament.
"I loved LIV and the team aspect, but it's time to move on," added the 2010 British Open champion.
Oosthuizen is still listed as captain ⁠of the Southern Guards GC team on the LIV website. Reuters has contacted LIV for confirmation on his departure.
According to reports in ⁠U.S. media, players have a soft deadline of October 25 to make an official decision on whether they will stick with the circuit.

title: Shami not giving up hope of India return
description: The 36 year old last represented India in March 2025
content:
The 36-year-old last represented India in March 2025
Mohammed Shami said he was determined to work his way back into the India team after the injury-plagued fast bowler was again left out of the squad for their multi-format tour ‌of New Zealand.
Shami has taken 462 international wickets in 197 matches across all three formats but last featured for India in March 2025 during their successful Champions Trophy campaign, in which he was the team's joint-highest wicket-taker.
The 36-year-old, whose career has been disrupted by ⁠leg issues, told reporters on Tuesday he would never lose hope of returning to the international arena.
"In any profession, you shouldn't leave hope. You should always have a goal," he said. "If we are playing in the Ranji Trophy, it is to win the title for the state, right? Goals should always be there. I don't deny that I have that goal."
Shami was dropped by Bengal for their Ranji Trophy match against Services ‌last ⁠week but he said that decision was based on the pitch being better for spin and that his fitness was not the issue.
"I am still at my peak," he added. "You all can see it for yourselves, I trained ⁠today and yesterday as well."
Shami was the leading wicket-taker when India won the 2023 ODI World Cup on home soil but looks unlikely to feature in their ⁠title defence next year.
"I don't think that far ahead. You never know what will happen in life," he said. "You don't know who will ⁠score runs or take wickets."
India begin their five-match T20 series against New Zealand on Thursday, with five more ODIs and a two-test series to follow.

Pakistan all-rounder Arafat Minhas described his performance against England as a memorable day after scoring 59 runs and taking six wickets for 40 runs in an outstanding display with bat and ball.

The left-arm spinner said bowling in the right areas had been key to his success, while Pakistan captain Shaheen Shah Afridi’s instructions helped him execute his plans.
“The captain’s plan was for me to bowl in the right areas,” he said. “Bowling in the right areas worked to my advantage.”

Minhas said Pakistan needed a partnership when he came out to bat. "We put England under pressure while batting," he said.

title: Pooh Shiesty reportedly held in cell for 23 hours a day as feds push back against jail conditions request
description: The rapper s trial over alleged robbery and kidnapping involving Gucci Mane is scheduled to begin in February 2027
content:
The rapper's trial over alleged robbery and kidnapping involving Gucci Mane is scheduled to begin in February 2027
Rapper Pooh Shiesty is reportedly being confined to his cell for 23 hours a day at a Texas jail, as federal prosecutors push back against his legal team’s request for improved conditions ahead of his February 2027 trial.
The rapper, whose real name is Lontrell Williams Jr., is being held at Rolling Plains Regional Jail in Haskell, Texas.
His lawyers filed an emergency motion seeking court intervention, claiming his monthly in-person visitation allowance had been reduced from four hours to two.
The defence argues that Williams has not engaged in violent or threatening behaviour warranting the restrictions and says the jail has offered only a vague explanation that his isolation is necessary for his protection.
His attorney, Kent Schaffer, told Complex , “He is locked down 23 hours per day and has no contact with anyone other than staff.”
Schaffer also argued that pre-trial detention should not be punitive and said the restrictions were affecting his client’s mental and emotional well-being.
Williams’ aunt has similarly expressed concerns about his anxiety and apparent decline.
However, federal prosecutors are urging the judge to reject the request, arguing that the restrictions are necessary to maintain security and order.
According to court documents reviewed by Complex , they cited alleged safety concerns, including an incident involving inmates attempting to reach Williams and claims about his conduct at a previous halfway house.
Prosecutors also pointed to his access to a tablet for video calls, emails, games and streaming content, stating that he had made 231 video calls totalling more than 45 hours.
Williams’ trial over alleged robbery and kidnapping involving Gucci Mane is scheduled to begin in February 2027. The allegations have not been established in court.

title: US must maintain ties with Pakistan from  geographic standpoint   says Rubio
description: Says US needs relationship with Pakistan  just as India engages Iran
content:
Says US needs relationship with Pakistan, just as India engages Iran
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the United States needed to maintain a relationship with Pakistan, citing its geographical importance and nuclear capabilities.
"It's a country that we have to have a relationship with. It's a country that possesses nuclear weapons. It's a country that, from a geographic standpoint, we need to be able to interact with it in much the same way as the government of India has to have and has a relationship and meets with leaders from Iran," Rubio said in an interview with India's Network18 .
His remarks came during a visit to India, where Washington and New Delhi have been discussing bilateral trade, defence cooperation and regional security.
The US secretary of state acknowledged the challenges of balancing such relationships, saying they remained an essential part of Washington's foreign policy.
He further suggested that maintaining communication with Islamabad could help Washington address India's security concerns.
"And I think in a way it could be a positive thing, because if we have a relationship and we can speak to them, it could perhaps put us in a position to help discourage the kinds of things that India is worried about," he added.
Referring to his current role, Rubio said his responsibilities as secretary of state required him to engage with countries with which Washington might have differences.
"In my new role, I'm no longer a senator. I'm the secretary of state. I have to manage the foreign policy of the US, and that does require us to have relationships with countries, including those that we may have some disagreements with," he said.
Read: America has 'true friendship' with PM Shehbaz and CDF Munir, says US War Secretary Pete Hegseth
Diplomatic engagement between the United States and Pakistan reached new heights after Trump helped broker a ceasefire between Pakistan and India during their brief war.
Since then, leaders from both countries have exchanged cordial gestures and praised each other’s leadership on international platforms. PM Shehbaz even nominated President Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize in recognition of his mediation efforts.
Trump, in turn, has frequently praised PM Shehbaz and Pakistan’s military leadership, notably describing CDF Munir as his “favourite field marshal”.
Building on this positive momentum, Islamabad now seeks to translate the goodwill into tangible economic benefits by pursuing a more favourable trade agreement with Washington, including tariff concessions and expanded market access for Pakistani exports.
Most recently, after a war broke out between the US and Iran in February this year, Pakistan emerged on the international stage as a peace broker. Islamabad brokered a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran on April 8, followed by critical talks in Islamabad attended by senior delegations from both countries on April 11 and 12

title: Israel   s Katz vows to strike Beirut   s southern suburbs over any rocket or drone fire
description: Defence minister threatens to expand southern occupation  acknowledges demolition of over 60 villages  23 000 homes
content:
Defence minister threatens to expand southern occupation, acknowledges demolition of over 60 villages, 23,000 homes
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz warned Tuesday that any rocket or drone fire targeting Israel would prompt strikes on Beirut’s southern suburbs.
In a post on the US social media platform X, Katz said Israel could expand its occupation toward the Nabatieh and Litani areas if Lebanon’s Hezbollah group joined an Iranian attack. He warned that residents of any newly seized territory would be evacuated and the areas permanently incorporated into what Israel calls its security zone in Lebanon.
Katz also ruled out an Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon until Hezbollah was disarmed throughout the country.
In an acknowledgment of the scale of destruction, Katz said Israeli forces had demolished more than 60 Lebanese villages containing 23,000 homes, claiming they had been used by Hezbollah for military purposes. He further claimed that Israel had established a 700-square-kilometre security zone inside Lebanon and displaced around 200,000 residents.
Read: Peace in southern Lebanon remains ‘elusive’: UN mission
His remarks came as Lebanese and Israeli military delegations held United States-mediated talks at the US Central Command headquarters in Tampa, Florida on Tuesday.
Israel has carried out attacks on Lebanon since March 2, killing and injuring thousands of people and displacing over 1.5 million residents.
On June 26, Lebanon and Israel signed a US-sponsored framework agreement providing for a gradual Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory, the deployment of the Lebanese army and the disarmament of Hezbollah.
Despite the agreement, Israel has continued its attacks on southern Lebanon. Israeli forces also continue to occupy Lebanese territory , including areas held for decades and others seized during more recent wars and military operations.

content:
'KPop Demon Hunters 2' to reportedly receive theatrical release following first film’s record-breaking Netflix success
KPop Demon Hunters 2 has reportedly secured a theatrical release following the first film’s success on Netflix.
The sequel’s cinema plans were mentioned in a report by The Hollywood Reporter on October 20, although an official announcement has not yet been made.
According to the report, former Netflix film chief Dan Lin helped secure a theatrical release for the upcoming animated film before his departure from the company.
The move follows the popularity of limited theatrical screenings for the original KPop Demon Hunters, which became Netflix’s most-watched offering.
Netflix and Sony reportedly agreed to develop a second animated film in November 2025, with a release planned for 2029.
Further projects connected to the franchise have also been discussed, including a live-action adaptation, a stage production, a spin-off series and a short film. However, these additional projects have not been officially confirmed by Netflix.
The original film follows Huntrix as the group balances its musical careers with protecting the Honmoon. Co-director Maggie Kang has previously indicated that there are more stories to explore within the franchise.
“We’ve set up so much for potential backstory,” she told Variety in July. “Obviously, there’s a lot of questions that are left unanswered and areas that are not explored. We had to do that because there’s only so much movie you could tell in 85 minutes.”
The first film’s success has extended beyond streaming, generating merchandise, sing-along screenings and collaborations with brands including McDonald’s, Fortnite and LEGO.
Its singers, EJAE, Rei Ami and Audrey Nuna, have also performed the film’s music at major events, including the Oscars.
The reported theatrical plans reflect a broader discussion at Netflix about releasing films in cinemas. The Hollywood Reporter noted that Lin supported theatrical releases, recognising demand for cinema experiences among younger audiences, while co-chief executive Ted Sarandos favoured a strategy centred on streaming.

title: We re children of incest   Dylan Sprouse s comment about family tree prompts reaction from twin Cole

content:
Dylan spoke about discovering unexpected connections between their families through genealogy programme Ancestry
Dylan Sprouse has joked that he and his twin brother, Cole Sprouse, are “children of incest” after discovering unexpected connections between their families through genealogy programme Ancestry. Cole subsequently reacted to the headline on Instagram.
Speaking on Tuesday’s episode of the Wildmen Podcast , the 34-year-old actor explained that he had connected with relatives he had never met because of divisions within his father’s side of the family.
Dylan said both sides of his family had been in California during the Gold Rush, with their family lines eventually connecting through marriage in the 1800s.
He also revealed that his family tree included seven sets of twins across four generations.
“The reason we have a lot of twins is because it’s the same family!” he said, before concluding, “Long story short, Cole and I are children of incest.”
Dylan also shared other unusual family stories, including an account of an aunt whose cyst reportedly contained teeth and hair. He added jokingly that he did not “have webbed toes”.
Cole, 34, responded to the coverage in an Instagram Story on October 20.
Sharing a screenshot of the headline, the Riverdale actor wrote, “No media training on earth can prep you to read this clickbait headline at 10am.”
The brothers rose to fame playing Zack and Cody Martin in the Disney Channel sitcom The Suite Life of Zack & Cody.
Dylan recently welcomed his first child, a daughter named Sylvie, with his wife, model Barbara Palvin. The couple announced the arrival of their daughter last month.

title: UN experts urge Indian authorities to cease  use of excessive force  to curb protests
description: Seek independent investigation into crackdown that injured demonstrators  some reporting ill treatment
content:
Seek independent investigation into crackdown that injured demonstrators, some reporting ill-treatment
United Nations experts called on Tuesday for an independent investigation into Indian authorities' conduct in a recent crackdown on protests , where they said demonstrators had sustained injuries and some reported being subjected to ill-treatment.
Opposition political parties and student organisations have held protests in recent weeks in India demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter ​lists that they say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party .
Mass protests also took place in the summer over exam-paper leaks and led to the resignation of India's education minister .
"Despite the non-violent nature of the assemblies, law enforcement agencies have reportedly deployed force against unarmed students, including lathi charges, and have prevented thousands from joining the protests," the two dozen independent experts said in a statement, referring to batons used to break up crowds.
Read: India's 'cockroach' movement founder released a day after detention
"We call on the authorities to immediately cease the use of excessive force, rescind blanket assembly bans, and refrain from the misuse of digital surveillance , including through biometrics, and internet disruptions," they said.
India has repeatedly dismissed such criticism and cast it as interference in the country's internal affairs, including when the UN human rights office earlier this month expressed concerns over mass detentions in relation to the latest protests.
The Indian embassy in Washington did not respond to a request for comment. India's government said this month the country's law enforcement acted "strictly in accordance with the law."
Read More: What is fuelling India's protests over changes to voter lists?
Protesting groups say the removal of 130 million names from voter lists led to eligible voters being disenfranchised, which disproportionately affected poor and homeless people as well as ethnic minorities including Muslims, who are unlikely to vote for the Hindu nationalist BJP. The BJP ​and India's Election Commission deny this.
The Election Commission says it was removing duplicate, deceased , shifted and otherwise ineligible voters and that anyone excluded in error can pursue appeals.
The protest crackdown has been condemned by human rights groups like Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch. UN ​experts are appointed by the UN Human Rights Council to monitor and document specific human rights crises ​but are independent of the organisation itself.

title: Trump administration says it has revoked over 300 000 visas
description: Trump administration says it has revoked over 300 000 visas
content:
Trump administration has enforced tightened social media screening of immigrants and ​visa applicants
President Donald Trump's administration has revoked over 300,000 US visas during his second term, the State Department said on ​Tuesday as the federal government continues its sweeping immigration crackdown.
The ‌number showed an acceleration in the pace of visa revocations in recent weeks.
In an update issued on August 10, the State Department had put the number of ​visa revocations since Trump's current term began in January 2025 at ​over 175,000 .
Trump says his immigration crackdown and deportation drive aim to ⁠improve domestic security. Rights advocates say the crackdown has violated ​due process and free speech rights and has created an unsafe environment, ​particularly for ethnic minorities, who have raised concerns about racial profiling.
Read More: US to revoke visas of up to 200,000 asylum seekers
In announcing the latest number on X, State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said the Trump administration "has revoked ​more visas at a faster pace than any administration in history."
Pigott ​said the administration had "zero tolerance for foreigners here on visas who break the law, ‌commit ⁠fraud, or undermine our national security."
Among visa revocations particularly condemned by rights advocates are those of pro-Palestinian foreign protesters demonstrating against US ally Israel's attacks on Gaza and of foreigners over their social media comments about ​conservative commentator Charlie ​Kirk's assassination.
In addition ⁠to attempts to deport foreign protesters, the Trump administration has enforced tightened social media screening of immigrants and ​visa applicants.
Also Read: US launches online portal to report suspected visa fraud
Rights advocates say the government has deployed ​national security ⁠reasons to target critics and used isolated cases of fraud to broadly target immigrant communities such as the Somali American community in Minnesota.
While Trump ⁠campaigned ​in 2024 on stopping illegal immigration, his ​administration has also made legal immigration more difficult — for example, by imposing expensive fees for ​certain work visas.

title: Putin agrees to resume three way peace talks with Ukraine and US
description: Kremlin says Putin Zelenskiy meeting will need to be painstakingly prepared in advance by aides to make it worthwhile
content:
Kremlin says Putin-Zelenskiy meeting will need to be painstakingly prepared in advance by aides to make it worthwhile
Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month, ​the Kremlin said on Wednesday, after Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in Washington's latest push to stop Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two.
The negotiations in a grand imperial palace in ‌St Petersburg, the ninth time that Witkoff has met Putin in person, began with a goodwill gesture from Russia - the release of Stephen Hubbard, a retired US school teacher held in Russia whom US President Trump had asked the Kremlin chief to release.
Wednesday's encounter unfolded amid concerns in Kyiv and among its allies that the United States is backing away from Ukraine, at times holding back real-time intelligence on Russian attacks and hobbling Ukraine's military communications.
The latest talks also came more than ​two years after Trump promised in his successful election campaign to end the Ukraine war within 24 hours.
Read : Trump holds off on new measures against Russia to avoid undermining Ukraine peace talks
The Kremlin said the new three-way peace talks, which would be at a technical level, could take ​place in Abu Dhabi and would be focused on how to guarantee the security of Ukraine and Russia once the war ended. They could begin sometime on or ⁠after November 10, it said. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February before the United States and Israel launched a war against Iran .
The Kremlin was less upbeat, however, about the outcome of talks ​Witkoff had held a day earlier in Oslo with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, the leaders of Finland and Norway, and European and NATO representatives. Witkoff told Putin the talks had been characterised by "some degree of ​momentum" and a US official said Ukraine had brought new ideas and proposals .
"These nuances, so to speak, do not entirely satisfy us," Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters after the St Petersburg meeting - which lasted nearly three hours.
Possible meeting between Trump, Putin and Xi
Ukraine and Russia remain far apart when it comes to the terms of any possible peace deal, though Trump has recently intensified pressure on Ukraine to strike some kind of a deal. He said on Tuesday it was ​time for Ukraine to end the war or face "a very bad thing".
Putin also used Wednesday's talks to offer to help Trump deal with Iran, saying Russia had a decades-long relationship with Tehran which it ​has repeatedly offered to leverage to address US concerns about Iran's nuclear programme. Putin told Witkoff it was possible and necessary to get a deal with Tehran, the Kremlin said.
Russia could also supply vast quantities of fertiliser to ‌the United ⁠States to help US farmers, the Russian president told Witkoff.
A potential meeting in China next month with Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping was also discussed. The Kremlin said Beijing was already preparing what it said would be the first meeting of its kind in history.
Putin has shown few signs of compromising on his central war aims, which include full Russian control of the Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine, no NATO membership for Kyiv, and an overall peace deal rather than a temporary ceasefire.
Kirill Dmitriev, Putin's special investment envoy, was also present at the talks with Witkoff, and the Kremlin said that major joint economic projects had been discussed, ​including some that were close to being realised.
Witkoff said ​he had brought some documents with him containing ⁠various ideas for a potential peace deal for Putin to review, and that Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, also wanted to convey some ideas to Putin. Kushner later joined the meeting remotely by phone.
Zelenskiy said he hoped to discuss key issues on how to end the war during a trilateral meeting with Putin and ​Trump.
The Kremlin has repeatedly said that any Putin-Zelenskiy meeting would need to be painstakingly prepared in advance by aides to make it worthwhile.
US-Ukraine ties have deteriorated sharply ⁠since Trump announced a diesel export deal with Russia earlier this month to help lower prices in the United States. High fuel costs since he launched strikes on Iran have hurt his Republicans ahead of November legislative elections.
Read More : Russia says it will send first diesel cargo to US on Thursday
Since the diesel deal, Ukraine has complained of disruption to some intelligence sharing and to its use of the Starshield military satellite system, though Zelenskiy said that Tuesday's Oslo meeting had reached an agreement to resolve those ⁠issues.
Citing US officials ​and people familiar with the matter, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that billionaire Elon Musk had last week ordered ​the slowdown of a military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite service that Ukraine relies on to track Russian ballistic missile strikes.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
Musk has said any such decision is taken by the US military or the president. Trump has ​said he was not responsible, and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio reiterated on Wednesday that Washington had not pulled back Kyiv's ability to access Starlink.

Fans argue Barbara Palvin deserved Fantasy Bra more than Kylie Jenner after VS runway comeback six weeks postpartum
Barbara Palvin has received support from fans following her return to the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show just six weeks after giving birth, with some questioning why Kylie Jenner was chosen to wear the brand’s $22 million Fantasy Bra instead.
Palvin walked in the 2026 show in Los Angeles on October 19, marking her sixth appearance at the annual event. The Hungarian model welcomed her first child, a baby girl, with husband Dylan Sprouse last month.
Social media users praised Palvin’s return to the runway as she was named "the #1 MOST mentioned celebrity at the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show on social media". Prompting fans saying she deserved greater recognition from the lingerie brand.
A fan suggested that Palvin should have received the Fantasy Bra, writing , “Maybe next year they should give the fantasy bra to Barbara Palvin. She could pull the engagement VS wants”.
Others highlighted Palvin’s modelling career and the labels she has faced regarding her body. One post recalled that she had been considered Victoria’s Secret’s first plus-size Angel, while another questioned the contrast between her experience compared to Jenner’s prominent role at the show.
Palvin, who made her Victoria’s Secret debut in 2012 at the age of 19, discussed her return with Page Six Style before the event.
“I tell everyone: This is normal. Maternity leave is six to eight weeks; I’m six weeks tomorrow, so I’m just doing what everyone [else] is doing. And I only need to walk down a runway!” she joked.
“Funny enough, my body bounced back — luckily — really quickly. And I think it’s because I’ve never been healthier,” Palvin explained , describing how she prioritised nutrition during pregnancy and while breastfeeding.
She also credited her family and friends for helping her adjust to motherhood, encouraging others not to be afraid to ask for support.

title: League of Legends fans criticise upcoming Mel rework for removing her unique W
description: League of Legends fans have criticised Mel   s planned Patch 26 22 rework  which removes her spell reflection
content:
League of Legends fans have criticised Mel’s planned Patch 26.22 rework, which removes her spell reflection
League of Legends fans have criticised Riot Games’ planned rework of Mel, arguing that removing her ability to reflect enemy spells will take away one of the champion’s defining features.
The changes are currently targeted for Patch 26.22 and would replace her W’s reflection mechanic with team-focused defensive effects.
Under the proposed changes, Mel’s W would continue destroying incoming projectiles but would no longer send their ability effects back to their casters.
Instead, the ability would generate a nova that shields nearby allies, grants movement speed and deals a small amount of retaliatory damage.
Riot also plans to reduce Mel’s early durability and passive damage while increasing her health and armour growth.
Her Q would become slightly slower, with more damage distributed across subsequent hits rather than the initial explosion. Her ultimate would receive greater cooldown reductions at higher ranks.
However, many players have objected to the proposed changes, arguing that spell reflection is central to Mel’s identity and that the rework risks pushing her towards a support role.
One player criticised the direction, writing, “Yet another unique midlaner having their entire power fantasy gutted and being pushed to a support - and just because a loud minority don't understand counterplay beyond mindlessly spamming important projectiles at her”.
Another fan questioned the decision to remove the mechanic, saying, “Once again riot is removing any trace of uniqueness within a character's kit before addressing what's actually making him an issue”.
Other players argued that opponents could counter Mel’s W by waiting for the ability to enter cooldown before attacking. One commenter described reflection as the main reason the champion was enjoyable, adding that it created “fun and exciting interactions”.
Riot’s stated aim is to make Mel less frustrating to face while shifting some of her power towards later stages of the game. The revised W would provide more direct protection for teammates, rather than relying on reflecting enemy attacks.

title: Coastal flood damages in Asia Pacific could reach  199b annually by 2050  ADB
description: Region s coastlines generate  7 trillion in annual economic output but face intensifying threats
content:
Region's coastlines generate $7 trillion in annual economic output but face intensifying threats
Annual coastal flood damages in Asia and the Pacific could rise more than sixfold by 2050 and nearly twentyfold by 2100 without adaptation measures, according to a new report released by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Wednesday.
The Asia–Pacific Climate Report 2026: Coastal Risks on the Rise—Actions for a Resilient Future warned that annual flood damages across 30 coastal economies could reach $172 billion to $199 billion by 2050 and $520 billion to $739 billion by 2100, compared with approximately $27 billion today.
According to the ADB press release , the region's coastlines generate $7 trillion in annual economic output but face intensifying threats from rising sea levels and coastal hazards.
The report noted that investments in coastal resilience could generate benefits up to 20 times greater than the required investment.
It estimated that keeping flood damages near current levels would require annual investment of $9 billion to $19 billion in coastal protection, potentially avoiding $178 billion to $360 billion in flood damages each year.
“Coasts are the overlooked engine-room of Asia and the Pacific’s growth but are retreating in the face of rising seas and escalating hazards,” said Yevgeniy Zhukov, Director General of ADB’s Climate Change and Sustainable Development Department.
Read: ADB to help boost tertiary healthcare
“We are at a turning point and must act now with long-term, adaptive, and risk-informed solutions to create resilient coasts that keep people safe and economies running,” he added.
The report highlighted that more than 400 million people in the region, representing over one in 10 residents of ADB's developing members with coastlines, live within 10 kilometres of the sea.
It noted that coastal areas serve as major centres for ports and trade, as well as tourism and heritage sites, making them critical to the region's economic future.
According to the report, larger economies could face some of the highest economic losses in absolute terms without adequate adaptation measures.
However, the relative impact could be particularly severe for atoll nations, where annual flood damages could reach 30% to 60% of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2100 under a high-emissions scenario.
The report warned that coastal floods historically occurring once every 100 years could become annual events by the end of the century in major cities such as Bangkok, Jakarta, Kolkata and Mumbai.
Read more: ADB cuts growth forecast to 3.7%
It also estimated that approximately $40 billion to $45 billion was at risk annually from disruptions to ports across the region.
To strengthen coastal resilience, the ADB called for adaptive planning that connects immediate measures with long-term development objectives while allowing policies to evolve.
The report recommended four steps: integrating adaptive planning into development decisions, strengthening institutions and governance, mobilising financing, and sustaining implementation and ownership.
According to the ADB, international adaptation finance to coastal economies in Asia and the Pacific roughly doubled from approximately $5 billion in 2015 to an annual average of $11.4 billion in 2022–2023.
Despite the increase, the report noted that a substantial financing gap remained.
It stressed that public finance formed the foundation of coastal resilience investment, but closing the gap would require expanding fiscal space and mobilising additional public, private and concessional financing for long-term resilience projects.
The ADB, founded in 1966, is a multilateral development bank supporting sustainable, inclusive and resilient growth across Asia and the Pacific.
The bank works with its members and partners through financial tools and strategic partnerships to address development challenges, build infrastructure and protect the environment.
ADB is owned by 69 members, including 50 from the region.

title: ECP orders Islamabad local government elections under 2015 law
description: Election commissioner says holding elections under existing law will not affect delimitation of constituencies
content:
Election commissioner says holding elections under existing law will not affect delimitation of constituencies
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Wednesday ordered local government elections in Islamabad to be held under the Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Act, 2015, and directed officials to issue the election schedule.
A five-member commission, headed by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja, issued the order after hearing a case concerning the prolonged delay in holding local government elections in the federal capital. Interior Secretary and ECP officials appeared before the commission.
During the hearing, the ECP’s Special Secretary Zafar Iqbal Malik told the commission that delimitation in Islamabad had been carried out six times and that election schedules had been issued on four occasions.
He said the last election programme had been issued on October 9, while the final delimitation of constituencies had been published on October 14.
The commission was informed that the presidential ordinance issued by the government had expired on September 6, while the federal government had yet to introduce a new local government law. The interior ministry had also been sent two reminder letters regarding the expiry of the ordinance, officials said.
The special secretary said the rules governing Islamabad’s local government had not been provided and that the ministry of law had refused to approve them. He argued that the 2015 law remained in force and that elections should therefore be held under the existing legislation.
Read: ECP issues notices over delay in Islamabad local govt elections
The interior secretary acknowledged that the facts presented by the ECP were correct, but said proceeding under the 2015 law would mean that the work completed so far would have to be scrapped.
The chief election commissioner, however, said holding elections under the existing law would not affect the delimitation of constituencies.
Raja said the interior minister, interior secretary, Islamabad chief commissioner and a committee of ministers had previously given assurances regarding the conduct of the elections.
“It appears that the government does not want to hold local government elections in Islamabad,” the chief election commissioner said.
He said the Constitution required local government elections to be held under the law and that the commission was being compelled to order the polls.
The chief election commissioner also read out the commission’s short order, directing that the election schedule be issued on Wednesday.
Last week, the ECP summoned the interior secretary and Islamabad chief commissioner for a hearing on October 21 over the continued delay in holding local government elections in the capital. The notices followed the expiry of the Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, on September 6 without replacement legislation being enacted.
In a statement on October 14, the commission said it had completed the delimitation process and intended to issue the election schedule under the 2015 law if the legal framework remained unresolved. The federal government had pursued new legislation, but the ordinance expired before the process was completed.
Article 140-A of the Constitution requires provinces to establish local government systems by law and devolve political, administrative and financial authority to elected representatives. The ECP is responsible for holding local government elections under Article 140-A and Article 219 of the Constitution.
Islamabad’s last local government elections were held in 2015 , and the elected local government’s term expired in February 2021. Fresh polls have since been delayed amid repeated changes to the legal framework.
The ECP had scheduled local government elections in Islamabad, but the process was disrupted in January 2026 when President Asif Ali Zardari promulgated the Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, amending the 2015 law and replacing the Metropolitan Corporation structure with three town corporations.
The changes required fresh delimitation and effectively reset the election process, prompting the ECP to cancel the scheduled polls.
The federal government subsequently pursued amendments to the local government law, while a separate committee led by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal worked on proposals for a new Islamabad government structure. The National Assembly’s Standing Committee on Interior approved the ICT Local Government Bill 2026 on September 3, but the ordinance expired on September 6 before the replacement legislation was enacted.

title: Pakistan  Turkiye  Qatar  Indonesia sign defence cooperation accord
description: Turkiye  Qatar  Pakistan  Indonesia sign defence cooperation accord
content:
'Badr MoU' reflects countries' desire to further deepen cooperation, develop partnerships, says Turk Defence Ministry
Pakistan, Turkiye, Qatar, and Indonesia signed an agreement on Wednesday to boost defence cooperation and strengthen defensive capabilities, the Turkish Defence Ministry said.
In a statement, the ministry said the countries signed the "Badr Memorandum of Understanding" in Doha as a sign of their desire to further deepen cooperation and develop partnerships.
"The agreement holds substantial economic importance," it said, adding the accord sought to foster cooperation in military production, boost military capabilities, and help collaboration in technical military training, research and development.
"By leveraging the unique military production capabilities of each country, the initiative will facilitate cooperation and integration, enhance defence industrial capacities, and enable the fulfilment of the needs of allied and friendly nations," it added.
The agreement was signed Wednesday in Doha, the capital of Qatar, by the defense ministers of the four countries.
The signatories were Turkish National Defense Minister Yasar Guler, Qatar’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of State for Defense Affairs Sheikh Saud bin Abdulrahman bin Hasan Al Thani, Indonesian Deputy Defense Minister Yusuf Jauhari and Pakistani Defense Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif.
The ceremony was also attended by Haluk Gorgun, head of Turkiye’s Presidency of Defense Industries.
Turkiye, which has NATO's second-largest army and a robust defence industry, has been helping Gulf nations, including Qatar, where it has a military base, bolster their defences amid the Iran war .
In August, it signed a mutual defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, under which an attack on one party constitutes an attack on all. Ankara also has close ties with Indonesia, notably in the defence industry.
The ministry said the Badr accord would strengthen ties between the countries' defence industries and bolster collaboration to promote security and achieve shared objectives
The memorandum will build on existing defence projects among the four countries, marking a new step in Turkiye's approach to multilateral cooperation.
Efforts coordinated by the secretariat focus on moving beyond the supply of military platforms to joint production, technology transfer, interoperability, and the integration of supply chains.
In a statement, the secretariat said defence industry partnerships pursued with the support of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan are among the strategic elements supporting Turkiye's foreign policy. It added that efforts focused on mass production and exports have gained momentum under Haluk Gorgun, the secretariat’s head.
"Technology sharing, joint development and strengthening domestic production capabilities lie at the heart of a sustainable defence industry. As Turkiye, we ⁠value partnerships that go beyond off-the-shelf procurement models, ​that foster the development of a nation's own human capital and industrial infrastructure," Gorgun said in a statement.
"We believe that the Badr Memorandum of Understanding will contribute to transforming the complementary capabilities ​of Qatar, Pakistan, Indonesia, and Turkiye into concrete ‌projects," he added.
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said that Pakistan places great importance on strengthening defence cooperation with trusted partners, reaffirming the country’s commitment to promoting regional peace and stability through enhanced defence collaboration.
In his statement, Asif said the memorandum reflects a shared commitment to regional peace and stability while opening avenues for greater cooperation between the respective defence industries.
He emphasised that the partnership would provide opportunities to strengthen self-reliance, promote industrial collaboration, expand joint production and facilitate technology transfer, drawing on the complementary strengths of both countries’ defence industries in accordance with relevant international and domestic laws and regulations.
The defence minister further highlighted the importance of expanding cooperation in joint research and development, training exchanges and industrial capability building.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
That agreement stated that “any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both” and committed the two sides to strengthening defence cooperation and joint deterrence.
The three countries already had extensive military links. Pakistan had provided training and technical assistance to Saudi forces for decades, while Islamabad and Ankara had maintained close defence ties through military training, naval cooperation and defence equipment. In 2023, Saudi Arabia agreed to purchase Turkish drones in what Ankara described as its largest defence export contract.
Pakistan had also expanded its military and security cooperation with the kingdom, deploying about 8,000 troops, fighter jets, drones and an air-defence system to Saudi Arabia, according to Reuters . Pakistan deploys troops to Saudi air base under defence pact. Islamabad had also been pursuing wider security and economic ties in the Gulf, including negotiations with Kuwait on an expanded cooperation pact linked to energy and investment. Pakistan-Kuwait agree to boost cooperation across key sectors
More than 55% of defence exports since 2012 took place in the last 4 years
According to the Turkiye Defence and Aerospace Industry Exporters' Association, the defence and aerospace sector saw approximately $54 billion in exports from 2012 through the first nine months of 2026.
More than $30 billion of that total took place in 2023-2026, meaning the last four years accounted for more than 55% of the sector's exports over the period.
Read: Pakistan, Qatar review security cooperation, explore new areas of collaboration as Naqvi visits Doha
Defence and aerospace exports rose 48% year-on-year in 2025 to top $10 billion, while exports over the latest 12-month period surpassed $11 billion for the first time.
According to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI), Turkiye boosted its arms exports 122% over the last five years, becoming the world's 11th-largest arms supplier. NATO allies account for 56% of Turkiye's defence and aerospace exports.
Joint production and technology transfer with Qatar
Qatar, one of the parties to the planned memorandum, has a longstanding defence industry partnership with Turkiye.
Bayraktar TB2 armed drones, armoured vehicles, and fast attack craft supplied to the Qatari Armed Forces are among the prominent examples of bilateral cooperation.
Read more: Pakistan, Qatar agree to expand security partnership, strengthen internal security cooperation
Barzan Holdings, a subsidiary of Qatar's Defence Ministry, has also signed cooperation agreements in previous years with Turkish defence companies including Aselsan, STM, and MKE.
BARQ, a joint venture established in Qatar by Aselsan and Barzan Holdings, has begun local assembly, production, and calibration activities for SARP remote-controlled weapon systems and electro-optical equipment.
Projects carried out by Turkish companies in Qatar also enable the provision of defence industry solutions to third countries.
Corvette partnership with Pakistan, joint tank production with Indonesia
The PN MILGEM Babur-class corvette project is a leading example of defence industry cooperation between Turkiye and Pakistan.
Under the four-corvette project, led by main contractor Asfat, the first two vessels were built in Istanbul and the other two at Karachi Shipyard.
The project modernised Karachi Shipyard's production infrastructure and transferred shipbuilding and outfitting engineering capabilities to the local workforce. It thus contributed to Pakistan's domestic production capacity alongside the supply of naval platforms.
The KAPLAN MT medium-weight tank development project is a prominent example of Turkiye's defence industry cooperation with Indonesia.

Launched under an intergovernmental agreement between the secretariat and Indonesia's Defence Ministry, the KAPLAN MT was jointly designed and developed by Turkish defence company FNSS and Indonesia's PT Pindad.

title: Oil rises on Middle East supply fears  US inventory drawdowns
description: Brent crude futures rise  1 59  or 1 5   to  110 38 per barrel
content:
Brent crude futures rise $1.59, or 1.5%, to $110.38 per barrel
Oil prices gained over $1 on Wednesday as escalating Middle East tensions fuelled fears of supply disruptions, while falling US crude and product inventories lent support to the market.
Brent crude futures rose $1.59, or 1.5%, to $110.38 per barrel. US West ​Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained $1.36, or 1.4%, to $99.18 per barrel.
Prices fell in the previous trading session after ​Iran's president discussed mediation efforts in a meeting with Chief of Defence Forces and Army Chief Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir in Tehran, though ⁠Brent hit a five-month high before easing.
"Oil prices have been having a bit of a wild ride in ​the last couple of sessions," said Suvro Sarkar, head of energy research at DBS.
"We believe this is a mix ​of profit taking and optimistic hopes of a Qatar- or Pakistan-brokered deal, countered by the realisation that any deal is still very distant and compounded further by inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), which shows drawdowns continuing in the US ​for both crude and products."
Iran told CDF Munir there would be no talks with Washington until its ​demands were met, Iranian media outlet Nournews reported on Tuesday, adding that a Qatari delegation had arrived in Tehran. There was ‌no official ⁠confirmation of the reports.
Maritime security risks are also escalating. Shiptracker Kpler said on Monday that at least 18 vessel attacks were recorded over the past two weeks, while LSEG analysts warned Iran was targeting tankers well beyond the Strait of Hormuz, reaching into the Gulf of Oman and jeopardising Gulf crude loadings and the ​ship-to-ship transfers supporting regional loadings.
Read: Pak-Iran border reopens as CDF visits Tehran
In Saudi ​Arabia, the Houthis on Monday ⁠claimed responsibility for attacks on a Saudi Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield and Saudi Arabia's Riyadh and Abha airports.
The death toll from a Houthi attack on ​Yemeni government forces on Monday rose to 73 as fighting intensified.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas ​Araghchi said in ⁠a television interview aired on Tuesday that Iran has not received a response from Saudi Arabia or Yemen's Houthis to its offer to help broker peace talks.
In the US, two Energy Department officials said on Tuesday they ⁠were working ​with refiners around the world to boost fuel output as a diesel ​shortage has raised prices.
According to market sources citing API data, US crude stocks fell by 4.9 million barrels in the week ended October ​16.

Lawmaker to be detained at Haripur jail; order cites anti-state activities, instigating locals
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) MNA Maulana Syed Naseem Ali Shah was ordered detained for 30 days under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance by Bannu Deputy Commissioner Ziaur-Rehman over allegations of inciting illegal protests, blocking public roads and obstructing official duties, according to an order that emerged on Wednesday.
According to a detention order issued on October 19, the deputy commissioner exercised his powers under Section 3(1) of the MPO and directed that the lawmaker be detained at Central Jail Haripur for 30 days, unless the order was withdrawn earlier.
“The activities of the following individual involved in anti-state activities and actively instigating local residents to participate in illegal protests,” the order stated, adding that the activities included blocking public roads and obstructing the smooth functioning of official duties.
The deputy commissioner said the material presented before him had led him to conclude that the lawmaker’s presence could pose a serious threat to public safety and result in a breach of public peace and order.
The detention period, according to the order, would begin from the time of his arrest and detention.
The order was also forwarded to senior provincial officials, including the additional chief secretary of the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Home and Tribal Affairs Department, the commissioner of Bannu Division, the regional police officers of Bannu and Hazara divisions, and the DPOs of Bannu and Haripur. The superintendent of Central Jail Haripur was directed to keep the lawmaker in custody in accordance with the order.

title: LeBron leads Sixers past champion Knicks
description: Detroit erase a 22 point deficit to beat Boston 121 113
content:
Detroit erase a 22-point deficit to beat Boston 121-113
LeBron James and his new Philadelphia 76ers teammates crashed the New York Knicks' season-opening celebrations on Tuesday, beating the defending NBA champions 106-100 on the night they raised their title banner at Madison Square Garden.
James, 41 and entering a record-extending 24th NBA season with his fourth team, scored 14 points and handed out seven of the 76ers' 28 assists in a tantalizing glimpse of how he will be a facilitator for younger teammates like Tyrese Maxey -- who led all scorers with 28 points.
"I could be a lot better," James told broadcaster NBC. "Still getting my rhythm, obviously just a little bit over two weeks with the new squad.
"But I like the way we played. I think we played exceptionally well, especially defensively."
Jaylen Brown, the former Boston Celtics star who arrived in Philly in a stunning trade for Paul George in July, scored 19 points with eight rebounds and six assists and center Joel Embiid added 13 points and 11 rebounds for the 76ers.
Jalen Brunson led the Knicks with 21 points and Karl-Anthony Towns scored 19 points with 12 rebounds, but after regaining the lead in the third quarter the 76ers repelled every Knicks charge.
The Knicks ended a 53-year title drought with their victory over the San Antonio Spurs in last season's NBA Finals.
Knicks legends including Bill Bradley, Earl Monroe and Walt Frazier handed out the Knicks' championship rings in an emotional pre-game ceremony at the Garden, where the crowd featured diehard celebrity Knicks fans like Ben Stiller and Spike Lee along with other famous faces including rocker Jon Bon Jovi and NFL commissioner Roger Goodell.
Before the club's third championship banner was raised to the rafters, NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Brunson told fans the Knicks were "ready to turn the page as a team.
"But one thing I would like to say -- the joy that this city had this summer we'd love to replicate that again," Brunson said of a Knicks team aiming to be the first repeat champions since 2018.
James, a four-time NBA champion and the league's all-time leading scorer, admitted that winning on another team's ring ceremony night was especially satisfying.
Both teams were slow to fire offensively. James scored his first points for his new team with a layup that cut the deficit to 19-18 late in the first quarter.
The Knicks pushed their lead to 10 three times in the second quarter but the Sixers chipped away and trailed by four at halftime.
A 76ers steal culminated in Brown's alley-oop pass to James for a basket that pulled the Sixers within one early in the third quarter and James's running layup put Philadelphia back in front, 64-63.
They would trade the lead before the 76ers pulled away for good, hanging on after New York cut the deficit to one late in the final period.
In the nightcap of the opening day triple-header, Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs took on two-time defending MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the Oklahoma City Thunder in a rematch of last season's Western Conference finals.
The NBA'S 81st season tipped off in Detroit, where the Pistons used a fierce second-half fightback to spoil George's sparkling Celtics debut in a duel of last season's top two regular-season teams.
Cade Cunningham and Jalen Duren scored 22 points each and Duncan Robinson scored 15 of his 21 in the fourth quarter as the Pistons rallied for a 121-113 victory.
Trailing by as many as 22 in the third period, the Pistons unleashed a 23-0 scoring run in the fourth to seize the lead.
"We just didn't do our brand of basketball good enough in the first half and we had to turn it up," Cunningham said. "We had a good talk at halftime and lit that fire a little bit better."
Nine-time All-Star George scored 38 points, the most by any player in his Celtics debut, and added five rebounds, five steals and three assists.
"Felt great competing with these guys," George said. "But I'm not a moral victory guy so, means nothing. We lost. We've just got to get ready for the next one."
