title: Man accused of running over Multan teenager killed in CCD encounter
description: Tauqeer escaped custody on Tuesday night  was killed in an exchange of fire with CCD in Bahawalpur
content:
Tauqeer escaped custody on Tuesday night; was killed in an exchange of fire with CCD in Bahawalpur
The suspect accused of chasing and running over a 15-year-old boy in Multan two days ago was killed in an encounter with the Crime Control Department (CCD) in Bahawalpur on Wednesday, police said.
The suspect, Tauqeer Nazir, had allegedly chased Waseem Abbas in his car after a dispute over work and run him over in a private housing society in Multan on Monday. He was arrested and handed over to police on a four-day physical remand by a judicial magistrate on Tuesday.
According to a statement issued by the CCD, Tauqeer escaped from police custody on Tuesday night.
CCD Bahawalpur personnel attempted to stop two men riding a motorcycle near the Northern Bypass in Bahawalpur on Wednesday morning. The suspects opened fire on the police team instead of stopping, prompting an exchange of fire.
Tauqeer was killed during the exchange, while his accomplice fled the scene while firing at the police, the CCD said. Special teams were pursuing the fleeing suspect.
Read: Suspect sent on 4-day physical remand after running over 15-year-old employee in Multan
A day earlier, Police arrested the suspect, who was later granted four days of physical remand by a court.
Waseem had been living at an orphanage for five years and wanted to learn electrical work, according to Shoaib Haider, the orphanage’s general secretary. The orphanage had sent him to contractor Tauqeer six days earlier to learn the trade.
The incident took place within the jurisdiction of the DHA Police Station. Rescue officials said Abbas suffered a severe head injury and died at the scene.
His body was shifted to Nishtar Hospital under police supervision before being transported to his native Muzaffargarh district, where he was buried.
Police arrested suspect Tauqeer and registered a case. He was presented before Judicial Magistrate Saadia Aslam, who granted him four days of physical remand.
When Tauqeer was brought before the court, lawyers assaulted him outside the courtroom despite the presence of police.
The first information report (FIR), registered on Monday, names Tauqeer Nazir and Amjad Ali as suspects and invoked Sections 302 and 34 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), relating to murder and acts done by several persons in furtherance of their common intention. It alleged that the two men pursued Abbas in a car and deliberately ran him over, causing fatal head injuries.
According to the FIR, Sub-Inspector Liaquat Ali Bhatti was on patrol with police personnel in Royal Orchard when a man identified as Mukhtiar Ahmed approached them at around 4:35pm. Mukhtiar told police that his cousin, Abbas, had been working as an electrician for the suspects and that they had allegedly subjected him to violence and threatened to kill him.
The report stated that Abbas had fled to a neighbouring street to escape the alleged abuse, while the two suspects pursued him in a vehicle. Police said they saw Abbas running in fear, followed by a Honda vehicle bearing registration number BVE-474.
The FIR alleged that the suspects ran the vehicle over Abbas with the intention of killing him. His head struck a pillar at the gate of house 3-A, crushing his skull and causing severe injuries. He died at the scene.
Two residents, Saqlain Raza and Syed Naseem Abbas, were named in the FIR as witnesses to the incident. According to the report, they told police that Abbas had passed by shortly before the incident, saying that the suspects wanted to kill him and that he was running to save his life.
The FIR further stated that the vehicle stopped after the incident and the suspects attempted to flee. Tauqeer was apprehended at the scene, while Amjad escaped. Police took the vehicle into custody as evidence.
Mukhtiar told police that Abbas wanted to leave the job because of the alleged violence and feared for his safety. The FIR alleged that the suspects pursued him over his decision to leave and acted in concert to kill him.
Abbas’s funeral prayers were held at around 2am in Mouza Daulatpur, and he was buried in his ancestral graveyard. The prayers were held promptly because of the condition of the body. Only close relatives and orphanage officials attended.
Haider said the orphanage had sent Abbas to Tauqeer after making inquiries about the contractor, who had a team of around 40 to 45 boys.
According to Haider, Tauqeer claimed he had followed Abbas in his car after the boy became tired while running away on foot. The suspect maintained that his car had slipped, but Haider said the video footage did not appear to support that explanation.
“It looks as though he was hit with the car,” Haider said, adding that Tauqeer would have to explain during the investigation why the boy had run away from him.
Haider said the orphanage had received no previous complaints against Tauqeer. Another boy from the facility had also been working for the contractor, but the orphanage had brought him back following the incident.
Abbas’s cousin Nadeem, who had been living at the orphanage for six years, said the boy had often expressed reluctance to go to the electrician to learn the trade, saying he wanted to return home. Nadeem said he did not know Tauqeer and had never met him. He added that Abbas had not returned to the orphanage since leaving to learn electrical work.
Abbas's uncle, Jafar Hussain, told the media that the boy’s father had died nine years ago. His maternal grandfather initially supported him, after which Hussain looked after him for two to three years. Abbas was later admitted to the orphanage by his grandfather and uncle, he said.
“Tauqeer deliberately killed my nephew. I know what condition Abbas was in and how I saw him,” Hussain said, demanding justice.
Abbas’s maternal grandfather said he had taken the boy to the orphanage because he wanted him to receive an education rather than struggle on the streets. He also demanded that the suspect be punished.
Residents said Abbas and his brother had been admitted to the orphanage after their mother remarried following their father’s death.
Bureau rejects Multan orphanage’s registration
Meanwhile, the Child Protection and Welfare Bureau (CPWB) refused to register a Multan-based orphanage over its failure to ensure the safety and supervision of a child placed with a contractor for work, its chairperson Sarah Ahmad said.
In a statement on X, Sarah urged the Punjab police to take legal action against the orphanage owner and hold those responsible accountable for the death of the 15-year-old boy.
She said the bureau had issued minimum care standards for all orphanages housing children in Punjab, adding that no institution could be allowed to neglect its duty of care.
Sarah also called on the Punjab Charities Commission to review the orphanage’s registration and licence and cancel it, where warranted under the law, besides initiating action against those responsible.
“Every child deserves protection, dignity and safety. No orphan should be left at the mercy of those entrusted with their care,” she said.

title: Rabies costs Punjab 3rd life in October | The Express Tribune
description:
Elderly dog-bite
victim from
Jaranwala dies in
Mayo Hospital
content:
Elderly dog-bite victim from Jaranwala dies in Mayo Hospital
A 70-year-old man from Jaranwala has died of rabies at Mayo Hospital. The deceased, Anwar, had been bitten by a dog about two months ago.
He initially sought treatment at the Nankana Sahib District Headquarters Hospital before being transferred to Mayo Hospital on October 17 after his condition deteriorated. He was admitted to the isolation ward, where he remained under treatment until his death.
Doctors diagnosed him with rabies and recorded cardiopulmonary arrest as the immediate cause of death. This was the third fatality caused by rabies in Punjab this month. Rabies is preventable through timely medical intervention after exposure but once clinical symptoms develop, it is almost invariably fatal.
According to figures attributed to the Punjab health authorities, the province has recorded 70,586 dogbite cases during the ongoing year, including 30,514 in Lahore.
However, a confirmed provincial tally of confirmed rabies cases is not available. A report submitted by the health and population welfare department to the Lahore High Court had shown that Punjab had recorded 232,704 dog-bite incidents in 2024, 243,299 in 2025 and 38,586 in the first three months of 2026.
The figures indicate that dog bites have remained a persistent public health problem. Provincial authorities had directed the local governments and district health authorities earlier this year to address stray dog populations, ensure the safe disposal of animal carcasses and coordinate efforts to reduce attacks.
The health services directorate general had also underscored the need for uninterrupted supply of rabies vaccine, prompt treatment and the recording of dog-bite cases on the District Health Information System dashboard.
The government also took measures based on the Capture, Neuter, Vaccinate and Release (CNVR) approach alongside municipal campaigns in high-risk areas, public awareness initiatives and improvements in waste management.

title: PSG stun Barcelona in Champions League
description: Late strikes from Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz secure a 4 2 win for the holders
content:
Late strikes from Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz secure a 4-2 win for the holders
Holders Paris Saint-Germain made it three wins from three in this season's Champions League, beating Barcelona 4-2 thanks to late goals from Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz on Tuesday, while Liverpool clinched a dramatic comeback victory over Villarreal.
Phil Foden scored a hat-trick as Manchester City thrashed AEK Athens 5-1, while there were also much-needed wins for Roma and Napoli.
PSG kept their place at the top of the league-phase table, but could yet count the cost of injuries suffered by Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at the Parc des Princes.
"We don't feel superior to any team but we trust in ourselves, in everyone who starts and who comes off the bench," Paris midfielder Ruiz told Movistar. "There's still a long way to go."
Barcelona twice levelled against the two-time defending champions, but were ultimately well beaten as they slipped to their first defeat of the season.
"We tried to play how we want to play, we pressed them very high. There were a lot of fantastic things on show today," said Flick, whose team had won their previous 11 games in all competitions this term.
Kvaratskhelia hit the post, Dembele hobbled off and Ferran Torres was denied by Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia in a fast-paced opening.
PSG took a deserved lead in the 38th minute as Desire Doue collected the ball outside the area and thumped a shot into the bottom corner.
Garcia made another excellent save shortly after the break from Achraf Hakimi, before Xavi Espart burst through to level for Barca against the run of play.
Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos both pulled up injured within seconds of each other and had to leave the field.
The home team continued to press, though, and Lucas Hernandez restored their advantage 18 minutes from time with a brilliant header.
Lamine Yamal powered past Warren Zaire-Emery to equalise again seven minutes later.
But Vitinha hammered home from outside the box in the 81st minute and Ruiz's tap-in gave Luis Enrique's team a second straight 4-2 Champions League win after seeing off Man City by the same scoreline last week.
Liverpool battled back from two goals down to also maintain their 100-percent record by edging out Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield.
Liverpool fell behind in the fourth minute when Georges Mikautadze pounced on a terrible error from Virgil van Dijk, before Villarreal defender Sergi Cardona strolled through their defence to make it two.
Alexis Mac Allister pulled one back for the hosts nine minutes before half-time by heading in Kostas Tsimikas's corner.
Andoni Iraola's men were level in first-half added time through Ronald Araujo's back-post header after Cardona inexplicably left Rio Ngumoha's cross.
Mac Allister completed the turnaround by firing in from Ngumoha's square pass, and half-time substitute Florian Wirtz's first goal of the season gave the Reds some breathing space.
Tani Oluwaseyi set up a nervy finish for Iraola, but Liverpool held on.
"We are facing very good teams. It's good to come back but we've started losing too many goals this season," Iraola told Amazon Prime.
At the Etihad, Elliot Anderson put Manchester City in front with his first goal for the club, before Phil Foden made it two goals in as many games after scoring against Ipswich at the weekend.
AEK halved the deficit early in the second half through Stavros Pilios, only for Rayan Cherki to sweep in City's third in the 57th minute.
Foden later fired in his second and third goals in a comprehensive victory, despite Erling Haaland being rested after picking up a knock at the weekend.
"Slowly, but surely. Still got a long way to go, but I am going in the right direction," Foden told TNT Sports of his gradual return to form.
Roma eased to their first Champions League win since 2019 as the capital club brushed aside pointless Slovan Bratislava 4-0 at the Stadio Olimpico.
All four Serie A clubs in the competition lost last week, but Napoli made it two wins from two on Tuesday for the Italian sides.
Massimiliano Allegri's men were twice pegged back by Bodo/Glimt but eventually got the better of the Norwegians in a 4-3 thriller, as Scott McTominay scored a brace.
Atletico Madrid played out a 1-1 draw with Stuttgart in Germany, despite playing much of the second half with 10 men.
Borussia Dortmund ended a run of four straight away defeats in the Champions League with a 2-1 win over Sabah in Baku.

Festival to be held over three days from 12th-14th
The Punjab government has rescheduled Basant 2027 in Lahore for a second time, with the provincial cabinet approving March 12, 13 and 14 as the new dates for the festival.
The decision reverses the schedule Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif had announced earlier, under which Basant was to be celebrated over 10 days from January 29 to February 7, with a break on February 5 to observe Kashmir Day.
According to sources, Lahore Deputy Commissioner Captain (retd) Muhammad Ali Ijaz sent a summary proposing a change in the festival dates to the Punjab Home Department, which forwarded it to the provincial cabinet for approval.
The cabinet has now approved the March dates.
Maryam had announced the January dates as part of an extended celebration aimed at promoting Punjab’s cultural heritage and Lahore’s traditional identity.
She had directed the relevant departments to prepare in advance and strengthen public safety and facilitation arrangements. The latest rescheduling means the festival will now be held over three days in March, replacing the previously announced 10-day programme.
Meanwhile, preparations for Basant 2027 are underway under a regulatory framework governing kite flying, kite manufacturing and sales, and the transport and use of kite string.
The Lahore district administration has said kite flying will be permitted only on the designated festival dates. Chemical-coated, metallic, and sharp kite strings, commonly known as ‘manjha’, are prohibited under the announced restrictions, while only approved kite sizes and cotton string are permitted

content:
Suspect allegedly sold 5.1m counterfeit postage labels through online platform
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) Lahore Zone has arrested Faheem Akram, a Pakistani national indicted by United States authorities over an alleged online scheme involving the sale of more than 5.1 million counterfeit US postage labels, causing losses exceeding $126 million to the country’s postal service. According to the NCCIA, Akram allegedly operated the scheme from August 2023 till last month, selling counterfeit shipping labels for around $2 each. The agency cited transactions worth approximately Rs35 billion, while clarifying that the $126 million figure represented alleged losses to the US Postal Service. A case has been registered and the investigation is under way. The US Department of Justice had announced on September 28 that a federal grand jury in the Southern District of Florida had indicted Akram, 33, a resident of Khanewal, on charges including conspiracy to defraud the US government, counterfeit postage and wire fraud. According to US prosecutors, a website, LabelsBank. com was not authorised to sell US Postal Service products and services. It allegedly offered counterfeit postage at a fixed price, irrespective of a parcel’s weight, size or destination, allowing customers to ship packages at rates substantially below legitimate postal charges. US court record showed that more than 5,200 people had used the website to purchase over 5.1 million counterfeit shipping labels. A court order authorised the seizure and shutdown of the website. The investigation identified 16 bank accounts allegedly linked to the case of which seven belong to the suspect, five to his brother, two to his wife, and one each to a sister and maternal aunt

title: Gymkhana lease record sought
description: Punjab Assembly committee asks BoR to share legal grounds for low rent
content:
Punjab Assembly committee asks BoR to share legal grounds for low rent
A special committee of Punjab Assembly on Tuesday sought complete record of the renewal in 1996 of the Lahore Gymkhana Club’s lease after officials failed to explain the legal basis for leasing around 117 acres of prime state land along The Mall Road for Rs5,000 a year despite its estimated value of up to Rs218 billion.
The committee directed the Board of Revenue Colonies Wing to present the lease deed, official summaries, file notings, approval orders and valuation criteria, along with a written explanation identifying the competent authority and the legal grounds for fixing the rent.
It raised the question why the lease had been renewed for 50 years, from 2000 to 2050, in 1996, four years before it was due to expire. According to sources, the board failed to provide satisfactory answers regarding the decision and stated that it had no record of government approval for buildings constructed on the land between 1972 and 2012.
The Special Committee No. 6, convened by MPA Sami Ullah Khan, took up an adjournment motion and a privilege motion concerning the club’s use of government land, its lease terms and public accountability. According to documents placed before the committee, the land in the club’s possession is valued at between Rs76 billion and Rs218 billion.
A district price and rent assessment committee headed by the Lahore deputy commissioner had assessed comparable land along The Mall, Jail Road and Zafar Ali Road in January last year at Rs70 million to Rs200 million per kanal, with market rents ranging from Rs15,000 to Rs200,000 per marla per month.
Even at residential rental rates, the approximately 1,090 kanal could generate Rs3.9 billion to Rs5.2 billion annually. The club has occupied the land since 1913, initially under a licence for a golf course. Its annual rent was fixed at Rs1,600 in 1921 and remained unchanged for 79 years.
The lease was renewed in 1996 for 50 years at the annual rent of Rs5,000. The club also occupies a six-acre cricket ground in Bagh-e-Jinnah at an annual rent of Rs900 under a lease extending until 2069. Committee members questioned the substantial concession granted to the club, contrasting it with the eviction of shopkeepers from government land and anti-encroachment operations against street vendors.
MPA Amjad Ali Javed described the arrangement as “elite capture” and questioned whether the state had adequately protected its assets. MPA Ahmad Iqbal Chaudhry termed the club a “colonial relic” and called for a review of privileges that, he said, were inconsistent with equitable governance.
MPA Chaudhry Iftikhar Hussain Chachar demanded accountability of officials whose alleged inaction had allowed the arrangement to continue. He also asked whether the permanent structures erected on the land had the requisite approvals.
The members also highlighted the disparity between the club’s existing lease and the government’s 2023 gymkhana policy, under which clubs are required to pay 10 per cent of market rent, with an annual increase of 5%.
Under that policy, 13 gymkhanas in nine districts have been allotted land at annual rates ranging from Rs200,000 to Rs1.4 million per acre.
Applying the policy to the Lahore Gymkhana at residential rental rates would generate approximately Rs390 million to Rs520 million annually. However, the Board of Revenue maintains that the policy does not apply to the club’s existing lease.

title: Ten Hag says Ronaldo let Manchester United down
description: The Dutchman also accuses United   s hierarchy of breaking promises and undermining his authority before his 2024 sacking
content:
The Dutchman also accuses United’s hierarchy of breaking promises and undermining his authority before his sacking
Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has accused Cristiano Ronaldo of letting the team down during his time in charge.
Portugal star Ronaldo was in his second spell at United when Ten Hag was hired in 2022.
Ten Hag's relationship with Ronaldo quickly became tense and the striker refused to come on as a substitute in a win over Tottenham in the October 2022.
Ronaldo was dropped for a subsequent match against Chelsea, prompting him to give an explosive television interview in which he said he felt betrayed by United and did not respect Ten Hag.
The former Real Madrid forward's contract at United was mutually terminated the following month.
"He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him," Ten Hag said in an interview with The Athletic.
"Obviously, he's one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire in."
Ten Hag said Ronaldo pulled out of training sessions and did not complete the full run that players were set after they were beaten 4-0 by Brentford early in his reign.
"I confronted him with this. Many times I say, 'Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can't bring yourself in the box, you can't score'. He was not capable to do this," Ten Hag said.
"It's the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he's exhausted. But he couldn't.
"He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn't prepare himself."
Ten Hag also claimed promises made by United's owners went unfulfilled before he was sacked in 2024, shortly after signing a new contract.
Although United won the FA Cup just months earlier with a surprise final victory against Manchester City, Ten Hag was axed with the team languishing in 14th place in the Premier League.
The Dutchman blamed the United hierarchy of some of his problems, saying he was left humiliated when Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay was sold to Napoli without his consent.
Ten Hag also said he wanted to sign Harry Kane, Declan Rice and Frenkie de Jong during his spell at United.
"They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned. We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn't keep," he said.
"I said, 'No selling Scott McTominay'. And in the end they sold him. I got, of course, very embarrassed and disappointed."

title: Regulator has  power  to force Manchester City sale
description: Club denies wrongdoing and have appealed against findings over alleged financial rule breaches
content:
Club denies wrongdoing and have appealed against findings over alleged financial rule breaches
English football's Independent Regulator (IFR) will have "absolute power" to force Manchester City’s owners to sell if they are ultimately found to have run the club improperly, the watchdog’s chair has said.
Premier League leaders City have been found guilty on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules by an independent commission between 2009 and 2018.
The club have appealed and deny any wrongdoing, but face a severe sanction unless they overturn the verdict.
Owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan, vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, City have blossomed into the dominant force in English football since a 2008 takeover.
“We have the power to ask an owner to step away from a club if we believe that they run a club in a way that is neither fit, fair or done with propriety," the IFR's chair David Kogan told "The Rest is Football" podcast.
Asked if an owner could refuse to divest, Kogan added: “No. We’ve got absolute power to do so."
Kogan also said last week he would resign if there is any political interference in any investigation the IFR may undertake into City.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has come under criticism for his initial comments on City's guilty verdict, saying he would be "really concerned" if the club's Abu Dhabi owners left the club following the verdict.
Downing Street subsequently had to backtrack, insisting no one was "above the rules".
Burnham, who was mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to June 2026, has since published all of his dealings with the City hierarchy.
But the case poses a delicate balancing act for the UK government in preserving its longstanding ties with the Emirates without interfering in the independence of the disciplinary action against City.

title: Teenager allegedly run over by employer after work dispute
description: Teenager allegedly run over by employer after work dispute
content:
Police secure four-day remand of main suspect
A 15-year-old orphan was allegedly run over and killed by a car following a dispute over work at a private housing society in Multan. Police said the incident occurred in Royal Orchard, within the jurisdiction of the Defence Housing Authority (DHA) police station. Rescue officials said Muhammad Waseem Abbas, the teenager boy, sustained a severe head injury and died at the scene. His body was shifted to Nishtar Hospital under police supervision before being taken to his native area in Muzaffargarh, where he was buried. According to police, Waseem was learning electrical work under contractor Tauqeer Nazir, who was carrying out work at a house in the housing society. Following an argument over work, the teenager allegedly tried to leave, prompting Tauqeer to chase him in a car and run him over. Police said another suspect, Amjad Ali, was also in the vehicle at the time of the incident. Investigators said Waseem had been staying at Tauqeer’s house in Zakariya Town for around a week and a half. He was sent to the housing society on October 11 to learn electrical work and returned to the orphanage on October 15, where he met his friends. He went back to work with Tauqeer on the morning of October 17, police said. The contractor reportedly took him to work and brought him back each day. Other children were also working under him. Waseem’s maternal grandfather had enrolled him in an orphanage to enable him to receive an education. Police arrested Tauqeer after the incident and registered a case against him and the other suspect. On Monday, DHA police produced Tauqeer before Judicial Magistrate Saadia Aslam at the district courts under tight security. The police sought physical remand to complete the investigation and arrest Amjad Ali. The court granted the request and handed Tauqeer over to police on a four-day physical remand, directing investigators to produce him again after its completion. As police escorted the suspect out of the court after the hearing, a group of lawyers surrounded him and assaulted him with slaps and punches. Despite a heavy police presence, the lawyers reached the suspect and continued beating him as he was taken from the court premises towards the outside of the district courts. Police eventually placed him in a rickshaw and took him to the DHA police station. Lawyers, including Shahbaz Khan Baloch, said they would pursue legal action to secure justice for the deceased teenager and ensure that those responsible were punished in accordance with the law. Meanwhile, Multan City Police Officer Akhtar Farooq told the Express News that the investigation was under way and that police had collected important evidence. The vehicle allegedly used in the incident was in police custody, he said. A police team was in Faisalabad conducting raids to arrest Amjad, who remained at large, the CPO added, expressing confidence that the second suspect would be arrested soon.

title: Liverpool rally to beat Villarreal
description: Allister scores twice as the Reds recover from a two goal deficit to maintain their perfect Champions League record
content:
Allister scores twice as the Reds recover from a two-goal deficit to maintain their perfect Champions League record
Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said the Reds cannot afford to relax after storming back from a two-goal deficit to beat Villarreal 4-3 on Tuesday and maintain a perfect start to their Champions League campaign.
Villarreal coach Inigo Perez looked set to get one over on his old boss Iraola as the Spaniards deservedly took a 2-0 lead inside 30 minutes through Georges Mikautadze and Sergi Cardona.
But twice the visitors were undone by their failure to defend crosses into the box as Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo levelled before half-time.
Mac Allister fired in his second 25 minutes from time and substitute Florian Wirtz completed the comeback as Liverpool moved alongside Paris Saint-Germain at the top of the Champions League table with nine points from three games.
"In the first half, especially the first 30-35 minutes, they have been much better than us. In the second half, especially the first 30-35 minutes, we were much better," said Iraola.
"I think when we've been under pressure and we had to go and leave everything, I think we've answered well.
"When we've relaxed a little bit at the beginning of the game, or when you score the 4-2, you think, 'ok it's done', it has cost us. You cannot relax."
Iraola left out all three of his over £100 million ($133 million) forwards as Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola joined Wirtz on the bench with one eye on the visit of high-flying Brighton in the Premier League on Sunday.
Villarreal took full advantage of the much-changed Liverpool side early on and were gifted the opening goal after just four minutes.
Virgil van Dijk miscued his attempted header back to Alisson Becker and Mikautadze finished coolly from close range.
Perez's own managerial career got started by chance when he was denied a work permit to join Iraola as his assistant at Bournemouth.
Instead he ended up as boss at Rayo Vallecano, where he had previously worked under Iraola, and led the La Liga minnows to the Conference League final last season.
Perez's knowledge of Iraola's system was clear as Villarreal opened up Liverpool at will at times during the first half.
A fine team move finally led to a second goal when Nathan Saliba picked out the run of Cardona from left-back and he steered the ball past Alisson.
Liverpool's understudies in attack had barely threatened until Mac Allister's looping header from a Kostas Tsimikas corner kickstarted the fightback.
Rio Ngumoha then began to tease the Villarreal defence but the first of two assists for the 18-year-old owed a lot to poor defending.
Cardona let Ngumoha's cross go at the back post, unaware that Araujo was steaming in to head in the equaliser.
That was the Uruguayan's last act as he made way for Wirtz at half-time and Liverpool clicked through the gears after the break.
Ngumoha's searing pace down the right wing opened up the Villarreal defence and his low cross was smashed in off the underside of the bar by Mac Allister.
"He was amazing tonight," said Mac Allister on Ngumoha's impact. "He made the difference."
Just three minutes later Cody Gakpo picked out Wirtz to score his first goal of the season and hit back at his critics over a lack of end product.
Iraola's men remained suspect at the back, though, and Tani Oluwaseyi set up a nervy finish with a sweet connection to Ayoze Perez's cross.
But Liverpool held on to close in on the last 16 and leave Villarreal on just three points from their first three games.

content:
The six-time Grand Slam champion cites a persistent left thigh problem
Iga Swiatek has withdrawn injured from the Ningbo Open, where she had hoped to earn vital points towards qualifying for the year-end WTA Finals, tournament organisers announced on Tuesday.
The Polish player, ranked ninth in the race to the Finals ahead of this week's 500-level event in China, is battling it out with seventh-placed Karolina Muchova and 10th-placed Marta Kostyuk for the eighth and final berth at the tournament.
This season's Finals will take place at Indian Wells on November 8–15.
Czech Muchova is not competing this week, while Ukrainian Kostyuk is seeded third in Ningbo.
"After careful consideration, I've decided to withdraw from the tournament," six-time Grand Slam winner Swiatek said in a statement released by the tournament.
"I've been experiencing an ongoing problem with my left thigh over the past weeks and I feel that giving myself the time to rest and recover is the right decision."
The 25-year-old was hampered by the same thigh issue during her defeat last week in the semi-finals in Wuhan against her compatriot Maja Chwalinska, who went on to win the title.
Swiatek is replaced in the draw in Ningbo by Russia's Anastasia Zakharova.

title: Foden hat trick fuels Manchester City rout
description: Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki also score in a 5 1 victory over AEK Athens
content:
Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki also score in a 5-1 victory over AEK Athens
Phil Foden hit a hat-trick to underline his long-awaited return to form as Manchester City crushed AEK Athens 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday.
After a significant dip over the last two seasons, Foden provided hope of a renaissance for the England playmaker with a sublime display at the Etihad Stadium.
The 26-year-old, who has admitted struggling with mental health issues, hadn't scored for 10 months prior to his goal in Saturday's win against Ipswich.
Long heralded as one of England's brightest talents, Foden was left out of his country's World Cup squad earlier this year in a damning sign of his fall from grace.
Having ended his run without a goal in the Champions League since November 2025, Foden now has to produce nights like this on a regular basis to complete his revival.
Elliot Anderson put City ahead early in the first half with his first goal for the club since his close-season move from Nottingham Forest.
Foden doubled City's lead before the break and although Stavros Pilios pulled one back for the Greek side after the interval, the Premier League leaders finished with a flourish.
Rayan Cherki bagged City's third goal in typically flamboyant fashion and Foden struck twice more to complete his treble.
It was City's second win in the league phase after beating Porto in their opening game and losing to holders Paris Saint-Germain last week.
City's future remains in limbo as they wait the result of their appeal against an independent commission's verdict that they were guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.
With reports emerging that City are set to be hit with a massive points deduction that will almost certainly condemn them to relegation, this season's Champions League campaign could be the club's last for some time.
Enzo Maresca and his players have shown little sign of being affected by the scandal, while City's fans defiantly show their backing for the Abu Dhabi-owned club.
They have won 10 of their 11 games in all competitions this season and even the absence of Erling Haaland couldn't derail them.
City started with Haaland on the bench after the Norway striker limped down the tunnel at the final whistle with a foot injury following his double against Ipswich.
Maresca made eight changes from the Ipswich game, with 17-year-old academy graduate Floyd Samba showing flashes of his talent on the flanks.
City's understudies took just 12 minutes to seize the lead.
Enzo Fernadez's free-kick cannoned down off the bar and Anderson reacted quicker than the flat-footed AEK defence as the midfielder slotted into the empty net from 10 yards.
Foden doubled City's lead at the climax of an eye-catching move in the 34th minute.
Exchanging passes in a blur of movement and precision, Foden and Rico Lewis cut through AEK with ease before Foden fired high into the roof of the net from an acute angle.
Perhaps overconfident after such a one-sided half, City lost their focus, allowing Pilios to reduce the deficit with their first shot on target in the 52nd minute.
City quickly regained their two-goal lead in the 57th minute.
Picked out by Foden on the edge of the area, Cherki unfurled a balletic turn that took him into space for a fine finish in keeping with his graceful first touch.
In the 65th minute, Cherki's long ball was knocked down by Lewis and Foden arrived to caress his shot into the top corner from 18 yards.
Foden made a perfectly-timed run to tap home Ryan McAidoo's cross in the 76th minute, sealing his first hat-trick for over two years.

title: School inquiry flags construction plan
description: School inquiry flags construction plan
content:
Report says Peshawar school building not designed for educational use
A government inquiry into a school roof collapse in Peshawar's Dir Colony has found that the building was originally designed for residential use and its makeshift upper-floor roof could not bear the weight of pupils and classroom furniture.
The report by the Capital Metropolitan Government's Eastern Zone, sent to the provincial government and governor, said the building's approved plan was missing from official records and the relevant planning inspector had not reported it as unsafe.
The building was constructed in 2011, when the area fell under Town-IV Tehsil Municipal Administration, and was later converted into a private school, despite being unsuitable for educational use.
The two-storey structure had cement-brick walls and an iron-girder-and-tile roof on the ground floor. The first floor had unplastered walls and a makeshift roof of wooden planks topped with bricks, the report said.
The roof could not withstand the combined weight of pupils and furniture, causing the rear section of a classroom to collapse on Oct. 15, it added.
The report said the planning inspector had not flagged the building because it did not appear dangerous from the outside.
It placed responsibility for regulating and monitoring private schools with the Private Schools Regulatory Authority.
The findings raise questions about building safety checks, regulatory oversight and how the school was allowed to operate in a residential building unsuitable for educational use.

title: K P raises daily wheat release to 4 000 tonnes
description: K P raises daily wheat release to 4 000 tonnes
content:
Additional 1,000 metric tonnes will be supplied to operational flour mills
The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Food Department has increased the daily wheat release quota from 3,000 to 4,000 metric tonnes following a Peshawar High Court decision and directions from the Cabinet Oversight Committee.
The additional 1,000 metric tonnes will be supplied to operational flour mills from the National Reserve Centre (NRC) warehouses in Azakhel to ensure timely utilisation of stored wheat and prevent further losses.
According to a notification issued by the Food Department, the additional wheat quota will be distributed among all districts in proportion to the province's population of 43.84 million.
The Director Food has issued necessary instructions to all district food controllers and rationing controllers to implement the revised allocation.
Under the revised arrangement, Peshawar will receive an additional 116 metric tonnes daily, followed by Mardan with 67 tonnes, Swabi with 46 tonnes, Charsadda with 45 tonnes, Nowshera with 43 tonnes and Lower Dir with 40 tonnes.
Other allocations include 39 tonnes for Lower Swat, 35 tonnes for Abbottabad, 44 tonnes for Mansehra, 45 tonnes for Dera Ismail Khan, 33 tonnes for Bannu, 32 tonnes for Bajaur and 30 tonnes for Kohat. The remaining quota has been distributed among other districts according to their respective allocations.
The department decided to release the additional wheat after a report by the Storage and Enforcement Officer at NRC Azakhel highlighted damage to stored stocks caused by recent flash flooding.
According to the report, floodwater entered the warehouses and affected the lower layers of wheat bags. Six of the centre's 11 warehouses sustained damage, while the remaining five stayed safe.
The report recommended the immediate release of stocks to prevent further damage, particularly in view of forecast rainfall.
To ensure transparency, the Director Food has directed district food controllers and rationing controllers to submit verified lists of operational flour mills to the release committee before lifting wheat stocks. The move aims to maintain a proper record of wheat release and distribution.
The notification also makes it mandatory to update all records relating to wheat allocations, transportation and release on the ICT application without delay.
Relevant officials will ensure that government flour produced from the additional wheat reaches consumers through authorised dealers at officially notified prices.
The department has directed all concerned officials to strictly monitor district allocations, verify operational flour mills and ensure the sale of government flour at prescribed rates so that the benefit of the additional wheat supply reaches the public.

title: Quetta s Hanna Lake   a fading beauty
description: Quetta s Hanna Lake   a fading beauty
content:
Water shortage dries up lake, hitting tourism and livelihoods
Hanna Lake, a popular tourist attraction near Quetta, is drying up because of a prolonged water shortage, leaving stretches of cracked earth where boats once sailed and threatening local businesses dependent on tourism.
Located about 18 kilometres from the Balochistan provincial capital, the lake was once known for its scenic surroundings, boating, water sports and migratory birds. But falling water levels have diminished its appeal, disappointing visitors and raising concerns among boat operators and other tourism-related businesses.
Tourists travelling from other cities said they were dismayed by the lake's deteriorating condition, having expected to see one of Balochistan's best-known natural attractions.
Hanna Lake covers about 1,818 acres and has a reported depth of 43 feet and a storage capacity of around 322 million gallons. A prolonged lack of rainfall and declining water levels have affected its recreational value and natural environment.
The drying lake has also hit people who depend on boating and water sports for their livelihoods. With water-based activities curtailed, operators face declining business and income, adding to concerns about the future of tourism in the area.
The water shortage could also affect the lake's ecosystem, including the arrival and habitat of migratory birds, as well as orchards in nearby areas. Experts warn that sustained declines in natural water reserves can disrupt ecosystems and threaten wildlife and communities that depend on them.
The lake's deterioration highlights the need for better management of available water resources and a viable restoration plan. Measures to address the causes of the shortage and replenish the lake could help protect its ecological value, support local livelihoods and revive tourism.
Hanna Lake is an important part of Quetta's natural heritage. Without timely intervention, its continued decline could deepen the economic and environmental consequences for the surrounding area.

title: PPP steps up local govt poll preparations across Punjab
description: PPP steps up local govt poll preparations across Punjab
content:
Party directs Central Punjab units to shortlist candidates
Following the Election Commission of Pakistan's refusal to postpone the local government elections until April, the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) has directed its organisational units across Central Punjab to accelerate preparations and submit candidate lists within a stipulated deadline.
Meanwhile, the party's Lahore chapter has invited applications for local government positions until October 27, with nomination papers tentatively scheduled to be filed from October 27 to 30.
The directives were issued at a meeting of the PPP Central Punjab's Local Bodies Monitoring Committee, chaired by its convener, Rana Farooq Saeed, at the Peoples Secretariat in Model Town.
The meeting discussed candidate selection, election monitoring, organisational mobilisation and the possibility of political alliances.
The committee directed district presidents of all 31 organisational units in Central Punjab, comprising 26 districts and five major cities, to become active immediately and identify and shortlist suitable candidates at the union council level.
Candidate lists must be submitted within the stipulated deadline, while the monitoring committee will visit each division to assess the state of preparations.
Rana Farooq Saeed said elections at the union council level could provide the foundation for success in the next general elections. He stressed that candidates should be selected on the basis of their influence in their respective constituencies, public outreach and political standing.
He said candidates should be finalised at the divisional level in consultation with district presidents, while organisational decisions should be coordinated with the party's designated ticket holders.
He added that the party's organisational structure would be extended to the union council level, with divisional and district leadership kept informed.
The committee also called for greater participation by young candidates and loyal party workers, alongside efforts to strengthen district organisations and launch membership drives.
Provincial Information Secretary Shahzad Saeed Cheema said the committee would formulate terms of reference for the elections and involve the party's main wing, the Peoples Students Federation, the women's wing and other affiliated organisations.
Rana Farooq Saeed maintained that the PPP did not accept the existing Local Government Act but would participate in the elections regardless. Participants also discussed challenging the legislation in court and preparing a white paper on the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz's performance during its 23-year tenure in Punjab.
In Lahore, PPP city president Faisal Mir announced that applications had been invited for the positions of mayor, deputy mayor, union council chairman, vice chairman and councillor across all towns of the city.
The deadline for submitting applications is October 27, while nomination papers are tentatively scheduled to be filed between October 27 and 30, subject to the Election Commission's final notification.
Applications are available at the PPP Lahore office at 16-J/2, Johar Town. Mir said people seeking to join the party or contest the elections through an electoral alliance could also apply.

title: Mir Raza s final hours  A trail of calls  Rs30m plea
description: Mir Raza s final hours  A trail of calls  Rs30m plea
content:
Sequence began late on July 27, with a series of calls between Mir Raza and his friends
A flurry of late-night phone calls, a WhatsApp message seeking Rs30 million, the sudden disappearance of social media accounts and a trail of CCTV footage that eventually runs cold - the final five hours and 14 minutes of Mir Raza Ali's life are marked by a series of unexplained developments.
A forensic examination of his mobile phone has pieced together a timeline of his movements and communications in the hours before he vanished on July 28, offering a minute-by-minute account of his final known activities. The sequence began late on July 27, with a series of calls between Mir Raza and his friends.
At 11:24pm, his friend Raziq called him for 30 seconds. Six minutes later, Mir Raza called Ahmed Bhardeh. The two spoke again at 11:39pm, a minute after Raziq had called Mir Raza for the second time. Another call from Raziq followed at 11:43pm, but it lasted just two seconds.
At 11:49pm, Mir Raza made a much longer call to his friend Sarim bin Tahir, speaking for 168 seconds. Three minutes later, he sent Sarim a WhatsApp message asking for Rs30 million, adding that something was going to happen in the morning that he was not prepared for.
At around 1:30am, Mir Raza and Raziq had a meal at Ghaffar Kabab House, before the trail of calls resumed. At 2:13am, Mir Raza called Ali Jimani, who returned the call three minutes later. Their conversations lasted 42 and 75 seconds, respectively.
At 2:23am, Mir received a call from his business partner, Abdullah Bhardeh. They spoke for 201 seconds.
Then, around 3am, another development emerged: Mir Raza's social media accounts began to be deactivated.
His fiancée, Salwa Khan, noticed the disappearing accounts and tried to reach him through WhatsApp calls and messages. She received no response until 3:58am, according to the timeline.
At 3:57am, Bykea driver Ehsanullah received a ride request from Mir's number. The ride was booked at 4am. Until 4:02am, Mir continued exchanging WhatsApp messages with Ahmed Bhardeh, even as he remained unresponsive to his fiancée. At 4:07am, the Bykea ride reached Cheese Valley in PECHS.
Two minutes later, at 4:09am, Salwa informed Mir Raza's friend Haitham that all his social media accounts had been deleted. Around the same time, his WhatsApp account was also deleted, adding another unexplained turn to the sequence of events.
At 4:11am, CCTV footage showed Mir Raza sitting in the front seat of a vehicle.
At 4:28am, CCTV footage captured Mir Raza getting out of a vehicle outside United Charter School in Gulistan-e-Jauhar's Block 3. He was subsequently seen walking along Qila-e-Street towards University Road.
The trail continued for another 10 minutes.
At 4:38:27am on July 28, Mir Raza was last seen on CCTV footage from a rent-a-car office on Hill View Road. After that, the available footage offered no further sighting of him.
His body was recovered on July 29, at a location some distance from where he was last seen.

title: KU entrance test results reveal a tale of two scores
description: Admissions committee lower passing marks from 50 to as low as 25 in some disciplines after low scores in six depts
content:
Admissions committee lower passing marks from 50 to as low as 25 in some disciplines after low scores in six depts
At the University of Karachi, securing admission this year has turned out to be a tale of two scores: while a relatively small proportion of candidates managed to cross the 50-mark threshold in the entrance test, thousands were offered a place after the university relaxed passing criteria in six disciplines.
The admission lists for around 20 degree programmes, based on the entrance test held on September 11, have thrown up some striking numbers. Of the 6,669 candidates who appeared, only 2,832 secured at least 50 marks, translating into a pass rate of around 40%.
The turnout itself was lower than last year, when more than 7,000 candidates took the entrance test for the 2026 academic session.
But the more revealing figures emerged from an analysis of the results published on KU's website. Faced with relatively low scores in six departments, the admissions committee, headed by Dr Saima Akhtar, lowered the passing threshold from 50 marks to as little as 25 in selected disciplines.
The move paved the way for 3,255 candidates to be offered admission against approximately 1,400 seats, with the revised criteria allowing candidates with considerably lower scores to qualify in some programmes.
Applied Chemistry recorded the lowest qualifying threshold at 25 marks. In Applied Physics and Environmental Studies, the minimum was reduced to 35, while candidates scoring 40 marks were also offered admission in Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT), Education and International Relations.
The score distribution offers another glimpse into how candidates fared.
The largest group among those offered admission comprised 1,073 candidates who scored between 50 and 59 marks, accounting for nearly a third of the total. Another 865 candidates, or 26.57%, fell in the 40-49 bracket, while 661 candidates (20.31%) secured between 60 and 69 marks.
Higher scores were considerably less common. Only 244 candidates managed between 70 and 79 marks, representing 7.50% of those offered admission. The number dropped sharply at the next level, with just 35 candidates scoring between 80 and 89 marks.
At the top end, only seven candidates secured between 90 and 97 marks, accounting for 0.22% of those offered admission.
Meanwhile, the university's decision to lower the qualifying threshold brought candidates with scores below 40 into the admission pool. Of those offered admission with fewer than 50 marks, 34 had scored between 25 and 29, while another 336 obtained between 30 and 39.
The figures underline the wide spread of scores among candidates offered admission and the role of department-specific passing criteria in determining who makes the final list.

title: 27 Dow University employees found with fake degrees
description: Of the university s 5 350 employees  only 1 945 verified  leaving more than 3 400 cases pending
content:
Of the university's 5,350 employees, only 1,945 verified, leaving more than 3,400 cases pending
Thousands of employees, millions in salaries and a verification exercise that remains incomplete - an audit of Dow University of Health Sciences has exposed serious gaps in the scrutiny of academic credentials, with 27 employees found to have fake degrees.
The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of the Sindh Assembly on Tuesday ordered the recovery of all salaries paid to the employees, who have since been dismissed, and sought reports from all public universities on the verification of degrees held by their faculty and staff.
The scale of the problem extends beyond the 27 cases. Of the university's 5,350 employees, only 1,945 had undergone degree verification, leaving more than 3,400 cases pending, the committee was told during a meeting chaired by Nisar Khuhro.
The PAC was reviewing audit paras relating to the university for 2024 and 2025 when the issue came to light. The audit had questioned the administration's failure to verify employees' degrees and its lack of a satisfactory response to the matter.
Dow University Director Finance Zainul Abideen Shah told the committee that the institution had outsourced the verification process to HRSG under a contract worth Rs7.36 million. Of the degrees verified so far, 27 were found to be fake, he said.
The employees identified in the audit held positions ranging from receptionists and clerical staff to computer operators, administrative officers, billing personnel, technicians and nursing staff. Their allegedly fake qualifications included BCom, BA, BSc and MCom degrees, matriculation certificates, nursing diplomas and a master's degree in computer science.
Shah said all 27 employees whose degrees were found to be fake had been dismissed from service. Vice Chancellor Dr Nazli Hussain told the committee that more than 70 per cent of the degrees held by academic doctors had been verified, while the remaining cases were still being processed.
Khuhro directed the university to recover the entire amount paid in salaries to the employees found to have secured employment on the basis of fake degrees. The committee also sought reports from all public universities in Sindh on the verification of academic and non-academic staff credentials.
The committee also examined Dow University's finances, with Khuhro asking about its annual budget and revenue generation.
Shah told the PAC that the university had an annual budget of Rs26 billion and generated around Rs25 billion a year through academic services, radiology, laboratory services and other sources. Student fees accounted for an additional Rs4.5 billion in annual income, he said.
Hussain told the committee that the university offered more than 300 open-merit seats. Annual fees stood at Rs500,000 for self-finance students and Rs60,000 for those admitted on open merit. International students paid between $10,000 and $18,000 annually, in line with the fee structure prescribed by the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council, she said.

title: K E meter reader shot four times in broad daylight
description: K E meter reader shot four times in broad daylight
content:
Armed men open fire in Mehmoodabad; assistant escapes unhurt
A routine round of electricity meter readings turned violent in Mehmoodabad on Tuesday when two armed men on a motorcycle opened fire on a K-Electric employee, shooting him four times before fleeing the scene.
The 33-year-old meter reader, Muhammad Shehbaz, was taking readings with his assistant when the suspects approached and asked what they were doing.
Upon being told that they were recording meter readings, the men allegedly opened indiscriminate fire, leaving Shehbaz seriously wounded while his colleague escaped unhurt.
The attack took place near the laboratory of a private hospital in Mehmoodabad No 1, within the jurisdiction of PS Mehmoodabad. The assailants fled without taking anything from the victims, leaving investigators to probe what prompted the shooting.
Shehbaz, son of Zafar Iqbal, was shifted to Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre after sustaining four bullet wounds to his leg and abdomen.
PS Mehmoodabad SHO Anees Abro said the meter reader and his assistant, Umair, were performing their duties when two unidentified armed men arrived on a motorcycle. The suspects asked them about their activities before opening fire, he added.
The SHO said no robbery had taken place and both employees retained their belongings. He added that there was no electricity in the area at the time of the incident.
Police called in the crime scene unit to collect evidence and recovered four to five spent 30-bore pistol casings from the scene. Investigators are examining footage from nearby CCTV cameras and attempting to trace the suspects' escape route.
Police said the incident was being investigated from all angles.
Meanwhile, K-Electric spokesperson Imran Rana described the firing on the utility's staff while on duty as extremely distressing and strongly condemned the attack.
He said the injured employee was receiving medical treatment and that the company's management remained in contact with his family, offering all possible assistance.
The incident had been reported to law enforcement agencies, while K-Electric was extending full cooperation to establish the motive and other circumstances surrounding the attack, Rana said.
The company reiterated that the safety of its field staff was a priority and called for strong legal action against those responsible.

title: Judicial Commission recommends JIT in Mir Raza case
description: Report describes police investigation as  epic failure   urges FIA probe into police conduct
content:
Report describes police investigation as 'epic failure', urges FIA probe into police conduct
A case that began with a missing young man and a police theory of suicide has exposed what a judicial commission has described as a deeply flawed investigation, compromised evidence and a breakdown of public trust so severe that even the identification of the actual killer may not convince the public.
The single-member Judicial Commission probing the death of 25-year-old Mir Raza Ali has recommended a joint investigation team (JIT), led by DIG Irfan Baloch and comprising senior representatives of the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Intelligence Bureau (IB), Pakistan Rangers (Sindh) and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), to establish the truth.
In a scathing assessment, the commission termed the police investigation an "epic failure", warning that the trust deficit between the Sindh police and society had become "nearly unrectifiable" in this case.
Headed by Sindh High Court Judge Justice Omar Sial, the commission submitted its report to the provincial chief minister on October 15, 2026.
The commission concluded that the available medical and physical evidence was incompatible with suicide. "The bullet trajectory, the unusual location of the wound for a self-inflicted injury, the absence of blood, the state of the body, the principles of medical jurisprudence, acid burns and the anesthesia detected in the blood, all clearly excluded suicide as the cause of death. It was a murder," the report stated.
The commission found that the police had failed in their most basic responsibility: establishing the truth. It said the suicide hypothesis rested on a handful of unconfirmed text messages, selectively obtained video footage and a preliminary post-mortem report that did not itself conclude that the death was a suicide.
The report also pointed to contradictions between the first and second reports prepared by Dr Osama Shaikh, further weakening the police position.
Describing the investigation as "a rudderless ship, not aware of its destination", the commission said the possibility of an active cover-up in the initial stages "cannot be conclusively ruled out".
The commission described the change in medical board as a "highly irregular, inexplicable, legally flawed overreach", attributing it to officials at the upper levels of the Sindh Health Secretariat, particularly the secretary and special secretary.
It further observed that the director-general of health services had "looked the other way", despite being aware that he lacked the legal authority to constitute such a board. "The two gentlemen who directed the change in the Board could not give a cogent reason for the abrupt change," the report stated.
With a significant portion of the physical evidence compromised, the commission said the case had reached a critical juncture at which a conventional police investigation was unlikely to restore public confidence.
It warned that even an accurate conclusion or the apprehension of the actual culprit might not be accepted by the public because of the severe breakdown in trust.
To address this, the commission recommended a JIT led by DIG Irfan Baloch, incorporating representatives of the ISI, IB, Pakistan Rangers (Sindh) and NCCIA, in line with the family's request. "This extreme step is necessary to restore public trust and end speculation," the report stated.
The commission also called on the police to acknowledge their operational failures, apologise transparently and initiate formal inquiries against the officers responsible.
Separately, it recommended that a high-level committee, preferably headed by the FIA, investigate whether police officials involved in the first ten days of the probe had violated Sections 201, 166(2) and 218 of the PPC, concerning evidence-related offences and misconduct by public servants.

title: High voltage shock claims two lives in Chakwal
description: High voltage shock claims two lives in Chakwal
content:
Homeowner, domestic worker electrocuted as iron railing touches wires on rooftop
A homeowner and her domestic worker died after suffering electric shocks from high-voltage wires in the Yasirabad neighbourhood of Chakwal.
The tragic incident occurred within the limits of Chakwal City police station when the two women came into contact with high-voltage wires while moving a metal railing on the roof of a house.
According to sources, the women were washing clothes on the second floor of the house when they attempted to move an iron railing to another location. During the process, the railing touched high-voltage wires passing overhead, electrocuting both women. They died on the spot.
The deceased homeowner originally belonged to Dowalmial village but had been living permanently with her family in Yasirabad, Chakwal. The domestic worker was reportedly a resident of Sargodha district.
Rescue 1122 teams rushed to the scene after receiving information about the incident and shifted the bodies to the District Headquarters Hospital, Chakwal, for medico-legal formalities and post-mortem examinations.
News of the deaths plunged the families and relatives of the victims into grief.
The incident has also raised concerns about safety arrangements around high-voltage power lines passing close to residential rooftops. Moving metal objects near such wires can pose a serious risk, as direct contact may result in fatal electrocution.
The tragedy serves as a reminder to exercise extreme caution when handling metal objects or carrying out construction work near high-voltage power lines. Residents should seek assistance from the relevant electricity distribution company to ensure appropriate safety measures are in place.

As wedding bells begin to echo and streets glow beneath strings of colourful lights, a season of celebration sweeps across the cities. From grand wedding ceremonies to glittering bridal showers, lively birthdays and intimate farewells, the desire to celebrate in style is creating a new race among young entrepreneurs to turn every occasion into a memorable event.

Event management, once largely associated with a few established and expensive companies is increasingly attracting young men and women who are entering the field with creative ideas, flexible packages and services designed for different budgets.
Event managers say the growing appetite for professionally organised gatherings has changed the way people approach celebrations. Customers are no longer interested only in booking a hall; many now want complete arrangements covering décor, lighting, catering, photography, seating and entertainment.
"People want their events to look different and memorable. Even a small gathering is now planned with attention to decoration, theme and presentation," said an event manager.
The wedding season remains one of the busiest periods for the industry. Banquets, marquees, hotels and restaurants witness increased activity as families prepare for wedding ceremonies, receptions, mehndi functions and related gatherings.
Fozia Danial, a woman client, said even the choice of venue had become part of the celebration planning, with halls offering flexible options from half-hall to full-hall bookings. She said some venues allowed children under five to attend free of charge, but a separate charge was applied when a child occupied a designated seat, giving families more flexibility in managing their celebration budgets.
Hotel owners say the demand, however, is no longer confined to weddings. "Bookings now come for birthdays, bridal showers, baby showers, farewell parties, corporate dinners and other family gatherings as well," said a hotel manager Bilal Abbasi.

title: Unsafe school buildings face sealing  demolition
description: Unsafe school buildings face sealing  demolition
content:
District teams to identify dilapidated structures across Rawalpindi
The district administration has launched a survey of private school buildings across Rawalpindi district following the deaths of children in a school building collapse in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).
Buildings found to be dilapidated and structurally unsafe will be sealed and barred from use until reconstruction, while authorities will initiate action to demolish such premises, official sources said.
The district administration has constituted survey teams comprising personnel from the Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA), Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA), Municipal Corporation, education department, Rawalpindi Waste Management Company (RWMC), Revenue Department and District Council.
The teams have been directed to identify unsafe buildings through photographs and video footage and prepare detailed reports, including the names of building owners and the dates of construction.
According to sources, the exercise aims to identify private schools operating in hazardous buildings and ensure that they are relocated before the premises are sealed. The administration will subsequently initiate the process of demolishing buildings deemed unsafe.
Survey teams from the respective departments will submit their findings to the district administration, enabling it to take action against buildings posing a threat to the lives of students and staff.
On the other hand, authorities have imposed a ban on educational activities within hazardous buildings and dilapidated classrooms across all public and private schools in the province, including those in the six districts of the Rawalpindi Division.
The Director of Public Instruction (Education), Punjab, Qaiser Rasheed has issued a stern warning to all school heads, private school associations and education officials: should any untoward incident occur at a school, the head of the respective institution will be held responsible.
Orders have been issued to immediately seal all classrooms that leak during rain. He added that the safety of children is the top priority, and no violations will be tolerated.
The circular strictly directs the Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) of all District Education Authorities to ensure the immediate and complete implementation of the following mandates across all public and private schools in Punjab.

title: Pindi cracks down on Leh dumping

content:
Task force to monitor illegal waste; offenders to face arrest, vehicle seizures
The Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA) has constituted a task force, with help from the Punjab Enforcement and Regulatory Authority (PERA) Force, to prevent dumping of construction materials and solid waste into Nullah Leh.
The agency has also launched action to remove encroachments, goods-transport parking areas, and building-material depots along both banks of the stormwater drain.
WASA Managing Director Azizullah Khan said the task force would continuously monitor Nullah Leh and take action against those found dumping waste or construction materials into it. Offenders would face arrest and the registration of first information reports (FIRs), while tractor-trolleys used for dumping would be seized. Action would also be taken against the owners of buildings whose construction materials were dumped in the drain.
He said a goods transport depot behind Ganj Mandi Police Station had already been removed and that encroachments, material depots and transport stands along the drain would no longer be tolerated.
The water body has also decided to plant six-to-seven-foot-tall trees along the banks of Nullah Leh through the Parks and Horticulture Authority (PHA) to help reduce environmental pollution. The initiative aims to prevent further obstruction of the drain, whose depth has reportedly been diminishing rapidly because of the continued dumping of construction debris and solid waste despite an existing ban.
The Rawalpindi Cantonment Board (RCB) has launched a cleanliness and public awareness campaign, scheduled to run from October 20 to November 5, covering all 10 wards.
An awareness walk was held from the RCB office, led by Additional Cantonment Executive Officer Tayyaba Naseer, Assistant Secretary Imran Habib and Horticulture Officer Atiqa Nadeem.
Under the campaign, special sanitation operations are being conducted to clean streets and drains, remove rubbish and raise public awareness about maintaining a clean environment. Residents, students, traders and social organisations have been urged to support the initiative.
During the first phase, on October 20 and 21, a cleanliness operation is under way in Ward No 1, covering Habib Colony, Rahim Town, Allahabad, Zahid Baig Road, Hafizabad and Sultanabad. The work includes street sweeping, drain clearance, rubbish collection and the removal of grass and weeds. Trolleys, excavators and other machinery have been deployed to transport collected waste to designated dumping points.
The campaign involves the sanitation, horticulture, enforcement, building control, water supply, engineering, food and dengue control branches. Measures are also being taken to prevent the illegal dumping of waste and construction debris, maintain green spaces, enforce hygiene standards at food outlets and eliminate potential mosquito breeding sites.
A complaints cell has been established at the Cantonment Board office to address residents' grievances. Citizens can register sanitation-related complaints by calling 051-9274422.
Cantonment Executive Officer Aamir Rashid has directed the relevant departments to ensure the effective continuation of cleanliness measures and called for public cooperation to make Rawalpindi Cantonment cleaner and greener.

title: Indian voters fight to get back on electoral rolls
description: Indian voters fight to get back on electoral rolls
content:
About 130 million names removed under voter roll revision
Kamta Prasad has been shuttling between government offices in Delhi trying to prove he is not dead.
The 53-year-old tailor is among 130 million names removed from India's electoral rolls under a voter roll revision that has sparked mass protests and posed the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.
The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has led to removals for reasons ranging from "logical discrepancies" to people being recorded as dead, leaving many such as Prasad struggling to get more than just their voting status restored.
He has had to forgo his daily wage of 250 rupees ($2.63) that supports his family of four to scurry around the city to reverse the error.
"I panicked when I heard about it," said Prasad, who is among 4.2 million Delhi voters struck off the list, according to the draft rolls published by the poll body on August 31. "Since then I've been going everywhere to prove that I'm alive."
The deletions have triggered a political storm, with opposition parties and youth groups staging near-daily protests in New Delhi and elsewhere, which have been met with force by the police.
They allege Election Commission chief Gyanesh Kumar manipulated the revision to benefit Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party, a charge denied by both the commission and the BJP.
According to Rajendra Kumar, a volunteer with non-profit Jan Sarokar, about 2,000 of the roughly 9,000 voters in Prasad's block were struck off after the revision, classified as absent, shifted, deceased or registered elsewhere.
Prasad is the only person in this block who has been declared dead but several similar cases have been reported by local media across the country.

title: CNN s Christiane Amanpour to leave network after 43 years
description: CNN s Christiane Amanpour to leave network after 43 years
content:
Famed journalist Christiane Amanpour announced on Monday that after 43 years at CNN, she would leave the network next June.
"After many months of thought and a few sleepless nights, I have decided to separate from CNN, my partner of 43 fantastic years!" Amanpour, CNN's chief international anchor, said in a statement.
The 68-year-old journalist said she looks forward to new projects and will continue reporting and travelling worldwide for CNN through June 2027.
Her international interview program will transition to a weekly format in January 2027 before ending in May, according to CNN.
Amanpour covered major global conflicts, including the Gulf War, the Bosnian War, Rwanda, Afghanistan, Ukraine, and Iran.
"Remember: always be truthful, not neutral," she said in her statement.
She said she will continue her podcast, The Ex Files, which she co-hosts with her former husband Jamie Rubin. Her program with public broadcaster PBS, Amanpour & Company, is scheduled to end in December.
CNN Chairman Mark Thompson praised Amanpour as "one of the most trusted and beloved journalists anywhere" and thanked her for decades of journalism.
Under a recently finalised merger deal, CNN is moving into new ownership under a media giant called Skydance, which will also include CBS and its news division, and the streamers HBO Max and Paramount.

title: 150 killed in South Sudan drone attack
description: 150 killed in South Sudan drone attack
content:
South Sudanese officials said Sudan's military had carried out drone strikes that hit a market in the disputed Abyei region, killing over 150 people, one of the deadliest attacks in a war that has spilled across Sudan's borders.
The strike showed the lethality of airstrikes in Sudan's war, which erupted in April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), triggering a major humanitarian crisis and drawing in local militias and foreign powers.
According to local authorities, the attack that hit the market in Abyei took place around midday on Monday. Yohana Akol Ngor, the caretaker minister of information in Abyei, told Reuters on Tuesday that the death toll had jumped to 153 from 73.
He said Sudan's army was responsible for the attack, without providing evidence. A spokesperson for Sudan's armed forces did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Three diplomatic sources, an aid worker and an expert on the conflict told Reuters the strike hit a fuel depot in the market. The diplomatic sources said the depot had been used in the past by the RSF to supply its forces.
