title: Turkiye sends Makkah pact to parliament
description: Turkiye sends Makkah pact to parliament
content:
Ratification required for formal approval
Turkiye has submitted a defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to parliament for ratification, three parliamentary sources said on Tuesday, moving NATO's second-largest army closer to a formal mutual defence pledge with Riyadh as it faces Houthi attacks.
The three countries signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in August, under which an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all.
The agreement's first article says the parties shall use "all necessary means" to eliminate threats to one another's territorial integrity, sovereignty or internationally recognised borders, according to a text seen by Reuters.
"In the event one of the parties is subjected to an armed attack or military aggression by another country or group of countries, the parties shall immediately provide assistance to the party under attack, utilising the full range of mutual assistance measures available to them," Article 2 of the agreement says.
The provision, similar to NATO's Article 5, refers to Article 51 of the UN Charter, which covers the individual or collective right of states to self-defence against armed attack.
The three countries "will decide on the scope and nature of the support to be provided following an objective assessment of the assistance required" and will cooperate within their available resources, including military capabilities and resources, the same article says.
At an emergency meeting of the alliance in Riyadh earlier this month, the three countries agreed to ensure the "rapid deployment" of military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia.
Turkiye, which has a robust defence industry, has condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, expressed willingness to help meet Riyadh's military technology needs and agreed to join a Saudi-led coalition to ensure navigational safety in the Red Sea.
The agreement also envisages close cooperation on defence industry, intelligence sharing, logistical support and the fight against "all means of terrorism," including at the operational level.
Parliamentary ratification is required for Turkiye to formally approve the agreement.
Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmus, currently visiting Kyrgyzstan, will refer the agreement to parliament's foreign affairs commission upon his return, two of the sources said. The contents and details of the agreement are expected to become public once it is submitted to the commission.
The commission could debate the agreement as early as Friday, another source said.
President Tayyip Erdogan's communications director, Burhanettin Duran, said that Turkiye's recent step marked an important milestone towards the institutionalisation of strategic cooperation between the three nations.
"This strategic partnership developed between our countries aims to strengthen collective deterrence, enhance joint capabilities in the defence sector, and safeguard security and stability in our region," Duran said in a post on X.
A Turkish official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said Turkiye's own contribution was expected to be limited to military equipment, intelligence sharing and weapons systems, adding that no other form of deployment had taken place under the alliance so far.
Asked how Turkiye could help Saudi Arabia defend against attacks by Yemen's Houthis, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said that the Makkah agreement was not an "offensive agreement", adding that Turkiye would not send troops to another country to carry out attacks on its territory.

title: France mobilises troops ahead of fresh protests
description: fresh protests
content:
France will reinforce police with troops and mount a huge security operation for more protests planned on Saturday, the government said on Tuesday, acknowledging failures in its response to last weekend's violence.
"The deployment next Saturday will be massive," Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, adding that the immediate priority was to restore order after rioting and looting swept Paris, Marseille, Lyon and other cities on October 17.
In a sometimes rowdy debate, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the military would be deployed alongside police, while the government pledged to overhaul tactics after widespread criticism that city centres had been left vulnerable.
Framing the crisis as a choice "between violence and the Republic", Lecornu blamed the unrest on far-left groups, who in turn have accused the government of underestimating public anger over high living costs and declining public services.
The unrest shocked France because of both its scale and the apparent inability of police to contain it, inflaming tensions ahead of presidential elections next year with candidates from the far right and hard left performing strongly in polls.
Protests in other European countries, including Italy and Albania, have added to concerns that anger over living standards risks spreading around the continent at a time when many nations, including France, are struggling with budget woes.
A night of relative calm in France followed targeted curfews imposed in several areas affected by the turmoil, which the government said had helped reassert control.
In central Paris, police emptied and guarded the Place de la Republique overnight, with a helicopter overhead. In Lille, in the north, where the curfew only applied to minors, officers patrolled the city centre, checking bypassers' identities.
Marseille mayor Benoit Payan said there would be curfews for minors around the commercial areas hardest hit by the weekend's riots, starting Tuesday night.

title: Maldives president arrives for three day visit
description: Maldives president arrives for three day visit
content:
Maldives president arrives for three-day visit
Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday for a three-day state visit to Pakistan from Oct 20 to 22, at the invitation of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, according to state media.
According to a statement issued from the Office of the President of the Maldives, the visit coincides with the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the Maldives and Pakistan, which were formally established on July 26, 1966, and also "marks the first high-level bilateral engagement between the Maldives and Pakistan in over a decade".
The statement further added that upon arrival at Islamabad International Airport, the president and first lady were accorded a 21-gun salute.
"The president will be accorded an official welcome tomorrow at Prime Minister House."
A delegation from the Maldives arrived earlier in the day led by Foreign Minister Iruthisham Adam and comprised cabinet ministers and senior officials, according to a statement from the Foreign Office (FO).
The FO previously said that President Muizzu would meet President Asif Ali Zardari, who would also host a state banquet in his honour, further adding that the visiting dignitary would also hold restricted and delegation-level talks with PM Shehbaz.
"The two leaders will review the entire spectrum of bilateral relations and explore avenues for further strengthening cooperation in trade, investment, health, education, tourism, agriculture, defence, maritime security, climate change and people-to-people exchanges," the statement noted.
The statement added that the state visit was the first by a president of the Maldives to Pakistan in 11 years and assumed special significance as the two countries commemorate the 60th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations in 1966.
The FO further added that Pakistan and Maldives enjoyed warm and fraternal relations rooted in shared faith, mutual respect, longstanding goodwill and close cooperation at regional and international forums.
"The forthcoming visit reflects the shared commitment of both countries to further strengthening their bilateral partnership and opening new avenues of mutually beneficial cooperation," the statement concluded.

title: Fazl rejects rationale for K P governor s rule
description: Fazl rejects rationale for K P governor s rule
content:
Fazl rejects rationale for K-P governor's rule
Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Tuesday rejected the government's justification for imposing governor's rule and an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), alleging that the measures were aimed at gaining control of the province's mineral resources rather than addressing terrorism.
Addressing a press conference after a meeting of the party's central shura, Fazl called for an in-camera session of parliament to brief lawmakers on the security situation and discuss the government's actions.
He announced that no JUI-F member would join the interim council being formed in K-P, arguing that political power should change hands through constitutional means rather than the use of force at the behest of powerful quarters.
Fazl said his party believed in political dialogue and that grievances over government policies should be addressed through discussion rather than allegations and accusations.
He urged the government to convene an in-camera parliamentary session to hear the concerns of political parties and deliberate on the way forward.
Rejecting governor's rule in K-P, the JUI-F chief said the federal government's justification for the move was baseless and questioned the results of repeated military operations against terrorism. He alleged that the measures were intended to bring the province's mineral resources under control.
He pointed out that the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) government had merged the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (Fata) with K-P but was now placing the former tribal areas under federal control. In his view, he said, the developments were driven by an interest in controlling the province's mineral wealth.
Fazl questioned the constitutional basis for the measures, arguing that governments should be installed or removed in accordance with the Constitution rather than through coercion.
He asked whether governor's rule imposed by former prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and former president Asif Ali Zardari had been accepted at the time.
He also accused President Asif Ali Zardari of failing to fulfil his constitutional obligations by signing the relevant measure without being satisfied that the requirements had been met.
The JUI-F chief said no single power could claim to represent the interests of the entire nation. He urged policymakers to formulate a strategy keeping future challenges in view, observing that Asia was once again emerging as a global economic hub.
Fazl also called for the Muslim world to form a united and effective bloc. He regretted that the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) was ineffective. He said Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia were an attempt to thwart Muslim unity.
Regarding the fight against terrorism, Fazl said his party had also suffered heavily, with more than 150 people killed in terrorist violence. He said the JUI-F had rejected the politics of the gun.
He criticised the system introduced by former military ruler Pervez Musharraf, saying it had failed. He recalled that the police had been separated from the administration under that system, adding that there had subsequently been calls to reverse the arrangement.
He questioned why, 25 years later, the same system was again being considered for restoration.
Fazl said his party had called for extensive consultation before the merger of Fata with K-P, but the decision had been imposed wholesale on the people of the former tribal areas. He noted that the emergency had now also been imposed in those districts.
He said tribal elders from the former Fata had been invited to meetings and asked about the merger, during which there had been agreement that the process had failed.
Fazl said he had maintained a relationship of respect with former prime minister Nawaz Sharif, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and former president Asif Ali Zardari in the past, and that the relationship continued to this day.
Referring to former US secretary of state Colin Powell, he said Powell had acknowledged that the proposal to send troops into Fata had originated with the United States.
Fazl said his party had no objection to investment but questioned why the United States alone was showing interest, insisting that such matters should be placed before the nation.
Announcing the party's future plans, Fazl said a jirga of tribal representatives from the former Fata would be convened, while a student convention would be organised in Islamabad. The party would also hold a public gathering in Sargodha on November 26.
He said the central shura had called for fresh elections, adding that the JUI-F did not accept the results of the 2018 and 2024 general elections.
Fazl said his party was not seeking a certificate of patriotism from anyone, stressing that its members had taken an oath in parliament and remained committed to honouring it.

title: PM ready for talks with political parties  Sana
description: PM ready for talks with political parties  Sana
content:
Says Balochistan govt cooperating on counterterrorism but PTI-led K-P govt didn't
Prime Minister's Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said on Tuesday that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif remained ready to hold talks with all political parties on counterterrorism, but stressed that the fight against terrorism required a united national response.
Speaking in the Senate, he said the Balochistan government was extending full cooperation to the armed forces and the federal government in counterterrorism efforts, whereas Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had repeatedly refused to allow military operations in the province.
Sanaullah said the government had sought political engagement with the opposition.
He said the prime minister was still willing to sit with political leaders if they were prepared to discuss the issue collectively. He said the challenge of terrorism could not be ignored.
Sanaullah criticised the opposition's reluctance to engage with the government, saying National Assembly Leader of Opposition Mahmood Khan Achakzai had declined an invitation to meet the prime minister at the Speaker's Office.
Recalling previous negotiations with the PTI, he said an agreement had once been reached to hold elections in the first week of September 2022 after the party dissolved its assemblies and demanded fresh polls.
However, he said, the arrangement fell through after PTI Vice Chairman Shah Mahmood Qureshi sought to consult the PTI founder and subsequently conveyed his refusal.
The adviser accused the PTI of using meetings with its incarcerated founder to build a narrative against the government, warning that contemptuous statements could lead to restrictions on meetings under applicable rules and law.
He said the draft of recent negotiations that were held ahead of the imposition of emergency in K-P showed that the parties had settled several matters but the opposition refused to agree to one point concerning support for the war against terrorism.
The adviser also accused the PTI of repeatedly seeking external intervention and said its proposed long march had involved talk of bringing two million people to Islamabad to launch an assault.
Sanaullah argued that the PTI did not represent the entire electorate in K-P, saying it had received 3.1 million votes out of 8.2 million, while other parties had secured the remaining votes.
He maintained that all political parties must support the armed forces in the fight against terrorism, adding that victory was the country's only option.
Senator Mishal Yousafzai said emergency measures had been imposed in K-P districts rich in minerals, while governor's rule had been introduced elsewhere in the province.
The PTI lawmaker questioned whether the K-P assembly had passed a resolution seeking the imposition of an emergency and asked what counterterrorism measures the authorities had taken during the first week of governor's rule.
She also alleged that the governor had invited international organisations to extract minerals just three days after the emergency was imposed, raising concerns about the government's motives.
JUI-F's Maulana Abdul Wasay said people in Balochistan were suffering from violence by both terrorists and the state. He cited the abduction of a commissioner and alleged that local residents had to pool money to pay ransom. He added that employment and economic activity in the province was disrupted.
Senator Dr Afnanullah Khan rejected the opposition's allegation that the emergency measures were motivated by mineral resources, arguing that the deposits had not been discovered recently.
He accused the PTI of conspiring against the country and the government, citing 3,000 terrorist incidents in K-P over the preceding year. Afnanullah also compared socioeconomic indicators, saying un-employment in K-P had risen from 8% in 2013 to 12%, while literacy remained at 50%.
PTI Senator Falak Naz Chitrali said her party neither feared an emergency nor governor's rule, arguing that K-P had been in a state of conflict for four years.
She said the party's voters had supported it despite the imprisonment of its leadership and the loss of its electoral symbol. She alleged that the province's mandate had been stolen on October 11 and asked whether the right to claim Pakistani identity belonged exclusively to the PML-N.
The Senate session was subsequently adjourned until 10:30am on Friday.

title: At SCO  Dar proposes trade in local currency
description: At SCO  Dar proposes trade in local currency
content:
DPM urges regional bloc to build financial safeguards
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday urged member states of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) to accelerate the use of national currencies in mutual settlements and establish regional financial institutions to finance development projects and shield their economies from international financial shocks.
Addressing the 25th meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of Government in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, Dar called for establishing an SCO Development Bank, Development Fund and Investment Fund, saying these mechanisms could strengthen economic cooperation and help member states withstand external financial pressures.
He also stressed the need to strengthen the SCO Interbank Consortium, harmonise cross-border payment systems and facilitate trade financing. Pending the establishment of the proposed development bank, he said, the consortium could play a greater role in financing infrastructure upgrades.
Dar said Pakistan remained committed to the SCO's founding principles of mutual trust, sovereign equality, respect for cultural diversity and shared prosperity, collectively described as the "Shanghai Spirit". He called for translating regional cooperation into practical initiatives that deliver economic benefits.
Emphasising the importance of connectivity, Dar said targeted investment in energy and transport infrastructure was essential for linking regional economies and advancing economic integration. He also called for greater investment in agriculture, mining, minerals and information technology to strengthen economic resilience.
Dar described the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) as an opportunity for all SCO partners to participate in regional economic integration. He said artificial intelligence, digital transformation, technological innovation, energy cooperation and international information security should become key pillars of future cooperation among member states.
He urged the SCO to strengthen its business institutions by establishing direct business-to-business links, organising joint trade exhibitions and streamlining customs procedures, particularly to support small and medium-sized enterprises. Such measures, he said, could expand intra-regional commerce and deepen economic partnerships.
Criticising protectionist policies and unilateral coercive measures, Dar said they undermined international law, restricted technological progress and increased inequality. He called for reforming global financial and trade systems to promote more equitable development and strengthen the resilience of regional economies.
The foreign minister also proposed expanding structured partnerships with international organisations, including the United Nations, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and the Economic Cooperation Organisation, alongside regional and international financial institutions.
He said the SCO should adopt a forward-looking strategy focused on climate resilience, sustainable energy, secure supply chains and joint technological innovation. Operationalising Eurasian energy and transport corridors, alongside stronger cultural, educational and people-to-people exchanges, would further advance regional integration.
Turning to regional security, Dar said sustainable economic development depended on lasting peace and stability, particularly in Afghanistan. He reiterated Pakistan's desire for a peaceful, stable, prosperous and regionally integrated Afghanistan that maintained peaceful relations with its neighbours.
He said Pakistan expected the Afghan Taliban authorities to ensure that Afghan territory was not used for terrorist activities against Pakistan or other countries. Regional stability, he stressed, remained essential for economic development and shared prosperity.
Dar also reiterated Pakistan's commitment to dialogue and diplomacy as the most effective means of resolving regional tensions, highlighting Islamabad's efforts to facilitate de-escalation in West Asia and the Gulf. He said Pakistan remained engaged in mediation efforts between the United States and Iran and would continue supporting peaceful dispute resolution.
Dar also highlighted Pakistan's role in the organisation, including its chairmanship of the SCO Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure and leadership of the working group on poverty alleviation. He said Islamabad intended to emphasise the contribution of small and medium-sized enterprises to reducing poverty.
He said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's vision for Pakistan's SCO chairmanship centred on "Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation and Shared Prosperity". Its priorities include peace and security, regional trade, artificial intelligence, climate resilience, sustainable energy and people-to-people exchanges.
Dar reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to strengthening regional partnerships and said Islamabad looked forward to hosting the SCO Council of Heads of State summit in August 2027. He called for collective efforts to build a peaceful, interconnected and prosperous regional community.
During his visit to Dushanbe, Dar also met Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Muhriddin, with both sides reaffirming longstanding ties and calling for expanded trade, economic cooperation, regional connectivity and collaboration in energy and security.

title: Britain deploys Typhoons to defend Saudi Arabia
description: Britain deploys Typhoons to defend Saudi Arabia
content:
RAF jets bolster Saudi air defences as Yemen crisis worsens
Britain will deploy Royal Air Force Typhoon fighter jets on defensive missions over Saudi Arabia, the British Ministry of Defence announced on Tuesday, as intensifying Houthi missile and drone attacks threaten the kingdom's cities, critical infrastructure and energy supplies.
The United Nations said that renewed fighting in Yemen has displaced more than 250,000 people, so far, and pushed the besieged city of Taiz towards a humanitarian catastrophe, warning that the closure of the city's only supply route to Aden was placing civilians at grave risk.
The Defence Ministry in London said that the fighter jets would help protect Saudi airspace against aerial attacks, following a request from Riyadh, adding that Britain will also provide an Atlas A400M transport aircraft and military advisers, expanding assistance announced in September.
The minister stressed that the aircraft would not conduct offensive strikes against the Houthi movement. Defence Minister Wes Streeting said the additional military support was intended to protect Saudi cities and infrastructure from missiles and drones.
The British deployment comes as Saudi forces reported intercepting a ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh on Tuesday, followed by the interception of a drone in the capital's vicinity. Authorities issued a brief danger warning, while two blasts were heard in the city, according to AFP journalists.
The latest incidents underscore the growing pressure on Saudi Arabia as the conflict spreads beyond Yemen's battlefields, threatening transport links, oil facilities and the kingdom's efforts to attract foreign investment.
The conflict has also intensified inside Yemen, where authorities said a Houthi strike on Monday against a training camp for security forces backed by Saudi Arabia killed 73 people. The renewed fighting has deepened the regional crisis.
As fighting escalated, the United Nations said that more than 250,000 people had been internally displaced in Yemen between August 1 and October 17. Matthew Saltmarsh, spokesman for the UN refugee agency, said the number of displaced people was continuing to rise sharply.
Around half of the newly displaced people are being hosted in Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, where Houthi fighters have encircled the urban centre since early October. The blockade has cut the road connecting Taiz to Aden, the interim capital of the Saudi-backed government.
UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk called for humanitarian assistance to enter Taiz immediately. He said restrictions on essential goods and access to safe water had sent commodity prices soaring, leaving many residents without food and other basic necessities.
The UN human rights office has verified that 32 civilians, including nine women and 14 children, were killed across Taiz governorate between August 1 and October 19. Another 115 civilians, including 34 women and 36 children, were injured during the same period.
Turk warned that fighting moving closer to densely populated areas could further increase civilian casualties. He urged the warring parties to refrain from using explosive weapons with wide-area effects in populated areas and to take all feasible precautions to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure.
Tarik Jasarevic, spokesperson for the World Health Organisation (WHO) warned that Taiz's health system was at "critical risk", with fighting and road closures threatening supplies of fuel, oxygen, medicines and other essentials needed to keep hospitals operating.

title: Pak Iran border reopens as CDF visits Tehran
description: Field Marshal Asim holds talks with Iran s leadership  says border issues resolved after discussions
content:
Field Marshal Asim holds talks with Iran's leadership; says border issues resolved after discussions
The Pakistan-Iran border was reopened on Tuesday as Chief of Defence Forces and Army Chief Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir held a series of high-level talks in Tehran at the time when Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia added a new and potentially difficult dimension to Islamabad's regional balancing act.
Field Marshal Asim Munir, accompanied by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and General Mohsen Rezaei, representative of Iran's Supreme Leader and Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, during his fifth visit to Iran in recent months.
Unlike his previous trips, which were largely driven by Pakistan's efforts to defuse tensions between Iran and the United States, the latest visit came against the backdrop of repeated attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Saudi energy, airport and other infrastructure.
The development presents a delicate challenge for Islamabad. Pakistan has pledged to defend Saudi Arabia under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, while at the same time maintaining close engagement with Tehran and attempting to revive stalled Iran-US diplomacy.
There was no official statement from the Pakistani side until the filing of this report. However, an official familiar with the visit told The Express Tribune that the talks went "very well", without sharing specifics. The official also confirmed that the Pakistan-Iran border had reopened.
Iranian readouts also quoted Field Marshal Asim Munir as saying that issues concerning the border had been resolved. "The issues concerning the Iran-Pakistan border have been resolved, and the border has been reopened as of this morning," the CDF was quoted as saying during a meeting with General Rezaei.
In a separate meeting with Ghalibaf, the army chief described the recent border problems as "temporary and technical" and said crossings between the two countries had reopened.
The reopening is significant for bilateral trade and movement of people, particularly for communities living along the lengthy Pakistan-Iran frontier. But the wider focus of the field marshal's visit appeared to be the continuing diplomatic effort to find a way out of the Iran-US confrontation.
The Iranian readouts suggested that Tehran used the visit to communicate its position on any future engagement with Washington. Rezaei told the army chief that Iran would not allow its enriched nuclear material to be taken out of the country.
"Not even a single particle of enriched nuclear material will leave the country," he was quoted as saying, describing the material as a national asset intended for domestic use. He also maintained that Tehran would not enter negotiations until Washington took steps to restore trust by meeting Iran's conditions.
Ghalibaf also delivered a similar message, saying that Tehran had "nothing new to say" to Washington and that the US could not regain Iran's trust without fulfilling the seven conditions previously presented by Iran in New York.
Ghalibaf also accused the Trump administration of violating what Tehran calls the "Islamabad understanding" and said subsequent US threats had further deepened Iranian distrust. "I explicitly told the US vice president that the long history of negative actions by the United States against Iran... has left us in a state of profound distrust," Ghalibaf was quoted as saying.
The Iranian parliament speaker insisted that military pressure would not force Tehran to change course. "Threats and military manoeuvres cannot influence the strategic decisions of the Islamic Republic of Iran," he said.
Pezeshkian, meanwhile, thanked Field Marshal Asim Munir and the Pakistani government for the efforts to reduce tensions and seek a diplomatic solution. According to an Iranian readout, Pezeshkian told the army chief that pressure, threats and sanctions would have to be removed before negotiations could resume.
The Iranian president blamed Washington for the latest regional tensions, including disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, and accused the US of undermining diplomacy through its previous actions against Iran.
The meetings indicated that Islamabad remains engaged in efforts to bridge differences between Tehran and Washington despite the hardened positions on both sides.
The Pakistani Army Chief's visit also came at a sensitive moment for Pakistan-Iran ties, with Islamabad seeking to preserve cooperation with Tehran while managing the fallout of wider regional tensions.
The Iranian accounts suggested the field marshal also carried messages between the two sides. According to the readouts, he received what was described as a "clear, serious and explicit" Iranian response to a message from the Americans. No details of the US message or Tehran's response were officially disclosed.
The Army Chief also conveyed greetings from Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq and stressed continued cooperation between Pakistan and Iran.
The visit underlined Pakistan's attempt to keep diplomatic channels open at a time when Tehran continues to insist that any renewed engagement with Washington must begin with concrete US steps rather than fresh Iranian concessions.

title: FCC reinstates Karachi ATC judge  voids de notification
description: FCC reinstates Karachi ATC judge  voids de notification
content:
Rules 65-year age limit cannot curtail tenure of judges appointed before amendment
The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has reinstated a judge of the Anti-Terrorism Court-IV, Karachi, who was de-notified by the Sindh government following an amendment to the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA), 1997.
The constitutional court ruled that the newly prescribed upper age limit could not be applied retrospectively to curtail an existing fixed-term appointment.
In a 15-page judgement authored by Justice K K Agha, a division bench led by Justice Syed Hasan Azhar Rizvi set aside a Sindh High Court's (SHC) decision and declared the petitioner's de-notification unlawful and without legal effect.
The court held that the Anti-Terrorism (Sindh Amendment) Act, 2025, contained neither an express provision nor any necessary implication making the newly introduced age limit applicable to appointments made for a fixed tenure before the amendment came into force.
The petitioner, a retired district and sessions judge, was appointed as judge/presiding officer of ATC-IV, Karachi, by the Sindh government on September 19, 2024, under Section 14(2) of the ATA, 1997, for a term of two and a half years under Section 14(3). His tenure was due to expire in March 2027.
At the time of his appointment, he was approximately 70 years old. The law then in force prescribed no upper age limit for appointment as an ATC judge.
However, following the 2025 amendment, which introduced an upper age limit of 65 years, the Sindh government de-notified four ATC judges above that age on October 22, 2025.
The FCC observed that the central question was not whether the legislature was competent to prescribe an upper age limit, but whether the amended provision was intended to apply to appointments already made for a fixed tenure and thereby curtail their subsisting tenure.
"The petitioner, having been appointed for a specified tenure under the law then in force, had acquired a vested right to hold office for that period, subject to the conditions governing its lawful continuation or premature termination," the judgement stated.
It added that where an amended provision admitted of two reasonably possible interpretations, the interpretation preserving the existing right should be preferred.
The court noted that the expression "appointed under this section" in the amended provision could be construed as covering persons already appointed under Section 14.
However, it could equally refer to appointments made after the amendment came into force.
The mere fact that the cessation of office would take effect after the amendment's commencement did not, by itself, establish that the legislature intended to affect rights already accrued under earlier appointments, it observed.
The bench further emphasised the importance of certainty in law, saying citizens must be able to know what the law is at a particular time. Without such certainty, compliance with the law could become problematic and its application potentially unfair.
It noted that retrospective legislation was generally an exception rather than the rule and that an intention to give a law retrospective effect was ordinarily expressly stated in the relevant legislation.
The court held that the SHC failed to appreciate that applying the newly prescribed age limit to existing fixed-term appointments would impair vested rights arising from appointments made under the previous law. "The interpretation adopted by the High Court, therefore, cannot be sustained," it said.
Allowing the petition, the FCC declared the petitioner's de-notification, along with those of two other ATC judges, to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect.
The court directed that the petitioner be deemed to have continued in office notwithstanding the issuance of the de-notification and remain entitled to serve as judge of ATC-IV, Karachi, until completion of his two-and-a-half-year tenure, subject to the conditions governing his appointment under the law.
The Anti-Terrorism (Sindh Amendment) Act, 2025 (Sindh Act No. XXIII of 2025) was passed by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh on August 8, 2025, assented to by the Governor of Sindh on August 20, 2025 and came into force immediately.
It transferred powers exercisable by the Federal Government concerning Anti-Terrorism Courts (ATCs) in Sindh to the Provincial Government.
The law empowered the Provincial Department, with the approval of the provincial government, to increase, decrease, or abolish the number of Anti-Terrorism Courts in the province.

title: Achakzai warns opposition may take to streets

Opposition Leader in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai on Tuesday warned that the opposition would take to the streets if its concerns were not addressed through the courts, saying the final phase of its struggle against the government had begun.
"We want decisions to be made in courts. If that does not happen, matters will move to the streets," Achakzai said, calling for peaceful protests against the government.

Achakzai said the 1973 Constitution had been drafted with great difficulty and recalled that Article 58(2) had led to the dissolution of four assemblies. He said the opposition had no enmity with either Nawaz Sharif or Asif Ali Zardari.
The K-P CM represented 40 million people and had been ridiculed, he said.
Referring to protests against inflation in France, Achakzai said millions of people had taken to the streets and set things on fire, but the French police had not fired a single bullet.
"We will also have to stage peaceful protests against this government," he said, adding that the final phase of the struggle had begun.
Speaking on the occasion, PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan said the PTI had challenged both emergency and governor's rule, alleging that the measures were undemocratic and unconstitutional.
He said the mistreatment of party workers was continuing, adding that the party had always described terrorism as a menace and consistently supported the federal government in the fight against it.
"We had our own government, and our mandate was snatched away," Gohar said.
He alleged that 12 PTI members of the National Assembly and 14 members of the provincial assembly had been picked up, claiming that raids were being conducted at party members' homes and that they were being harassed.
Gohar said the office of a District Development Advisory Committee chairman had been demolished and plaques had been removed.

title: PHC seeks govt s reply on K P emergency
description: PHC seeks govt s reply on K P emergency
content:
Gohar says PTI's mandate was snatched away on Oct 11
The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Tuesday issued notices to the federal government, the attorney general, the advocate general and other relevant authorities on petitions challenging the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), after petitioners' counsel argued that the measures were unconstitutional and had been imposed without fulfilling the legal requirements.
A division bench comprising Justice Ijaz Anwar and Justice Muhammad Faheem Wali heard the petitions filed by PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and National Democratic Movement (NDM) leaders, including Mohsin Dawar.
During the hearing, the petitioners' counsel argued that the provincial government had not lost control of the province and that the imposition of emergency and governor's rule amounted to an attack on provincial autonomy and democracy.
Barrister Sameer Khosa, representing the petitioners, argued that no circumstances indicated the provincial government was unable to maintain control of the province. He said non-functional K-P chief minister Sohail Afridi and provincial assembly speaker Babar Saleem Swati were missing and their whereabouts were unknown.
Justice Anwar asked whether the petition sought their production before the court or their recovery. "Yes, we have made that request in the petition," Khosa replied.
Citing the Supreme Court's judgment in the Pir Sabir Shah case, Khosa argued that even if an emergency was imposed, the chief minister and cabinet would continue to function. In the present case, however, the chief minister, cabinet and advocate had been prevented from performing their duties and rendered inactive, he said.
Khosa urged the court to restore the provincial assembly and secure the release of Afridi and Swati.
Petitioners' counsel PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja argued that governor's rule and emergency had been imposed without fulfilling the legal requirements, urging the court to declare the measures illegal and restore the provincial assembly.
Raja maintained that Afridi remained the chief minister and that the provincial cabinet was still in place. He said that imposing an emergency required a resolution to be passed by the provincial assembly, adding that governor's rule could only be justified if the provincial government was unable to function.
Raja also alleged that the sanctity of homes and the privacy of their occupants were being violated in the province.
Another petitioner's counsel, Advocate Muazzam Butt, challenged the legality of both measures, arguing that the constitutional provisions invoked to impose emergency and governor's rule had not been followed. He said provincial assembly approval had not been obtained for the imposition of emergency.
"If they claim that terrorism has increased, there is an Apex Committee for that," Butt said, adding that the committee included representatives of the provincial and federal governments.
After hearing the petitioners, Justice Anwar said the court was issuing notices to the federal government, the attorney general, the advocate general and other relevant parties.
Raja then requested the court to also issue an order on the interim relief sought by the petitioners. "We will examine it and pass an order," the court said.
The hearing was adjourned until November 10.

An additional station house officer (SHO) of Miranshah Police Station was martyred when unidentified armed men opened fire on him near Miranshah Bypass in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's North Waziristan on Tuesday evening, police officials confirmed.

He said the police were determined to track down the militants and would not allow them to operate in the area.
Police launched a search operation in the area to trace the attackers and determine their escape route. Security personnel were also investigating the circumstances surrounding the attack, while the identities and motives of the assailants remained unknown.
The attack comes amid continuing security challenges faced by police personnel in the district. Police officials have repeatedly been targeted in gun attacks in different parts of the region.
Despite such threats, police personnel continue to perform their duties to maintain law and order and protect the lives and property of local residents.

title: Pakistan expands digital infrastructure for AI push
description: Pakistan expands digital infrastructure for AI push
content:
Information Technology Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja said on Tuesday that Pakistan had significantly expanded its digital infrastructure through a major spectrum auction, 5G deployment and nationwide fibre-optic connectivity to meet rising demand for digital services.
Addressing a high-level panel at the Global Digital and AI Summit in Seoul, South Korea, she said Pakistan viewed artificial intelligence (AI) primarily as a network challenge under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's Digital Nation Pakistan vision.
Khawaja said Pakistan conducted its largest-ever spectrum auction in March 2026, acquiring 480 MHz of spectrum for $509 million and increasing telecom operators' combined holdings from 274 MHz to 754 MHz. Within six months, 5G services had been launched at more than 1,700 sites across 24 major cities, delivering average speeds of 130 Mbps.
She added that download speeds had risen by 68.1% over two years, while more than 234,000 kilometres of optical fibre cable had been deployed nationwide. The government had abolished right-of-way charges to reduce costs and accelerate fibre expansion.
Pakistan was connected to international networks through six submarine cables with combined capacity exceeding 17 terabits per second, she said, adding that the country was developing the Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) Digital Corridor to connect Central Asia with the wider world.
Highlighting connectivity in remote areas, Khawaja said regulators were finalising a framework for satellite communications and licensing to facilitate direct-to-device services. Satellite technology would complement, rather than replace, terrestrial networks. New frameworks for mobile virtual network operators and infrastructure sharing had also been introduced to attract investment.
On digital inclusion, she said the Universal Service Fund had provided connectivity to more than 38 million people across 22,100 settlements in over 110 districts. Pakistan had assembled 17.6 million smartphones locally in 2025, while instalment plans were being introduced. The gender gap in mobile connectivity had narrowed from 25% to 8%, she added, citing World Bank reports.
Khawaja also said Pakistan's ranking in the International Telecommunication Union's ICT Development Index 2026 had improved by 27 places. She described universal connectivity as an unfinished promise, urging stakeholders to share investment risks and make connectivity the foundation for AI-driven growth.

title: Pakistan committed to fiscal sustainability
description: Pakistan committed to fiscal sustainability
content:
Zardari tells IMF delegation stakeholders, provincial govts back reform agenda
President Asif Ali Zardari has reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to economic reforms, fiscal sustainability, energy sector reforms, privatisation and social protection, while ensuring inclusive and green growth, as he met a visiting International Monetary Fund (IMF) delegation at Aiwan-e-Sadr on Tuesday.
During the meeting, President Zardari and Jihad Azour, director of the IMF's Middle East and Central Asia Department, discussed Pakistan's economic reform agenda, progress under the IMF-supported programmes and prospects for continued economic recovery and stability.
The president appreciated the Fund's continued engagement with Pakistan and expressed confidence in the country's progress following the successful conclusion of the latest programme reviews and a staff-level agreement.
The IMF delegation also included Iva Petrova, IMF Mission Chief for Pakistan, and Mahir Binici, IMF Resident Representative for Pakistan (country head).
The president appreciated the IMF's continued engagement in supporting Pakistan's home-grown reform agenda.
He also acknowledged the IMF leadership's confidence in Pakistan's efforts to implement reforms under the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).
Referring to the successful conclusion of the fourth review of the EFF and the third review of the RSF, along with the staff-level agreement, Zardari expressed confidence in Pakistan's continued progress towards economic recovery and stability.
President Zardari noted that Pakistan had moved from economic stabilisation towards recovery, with the economy reaching $452.1 billion in FY2026 and real GDP growth accelerating to 3.7 per cent, up from 3.2 per cent in FY2025.
He also highlighted improvements in fiscal management, noting that the fiscal deficit had declined to 2.6 per cent of GDP in FY2025-26, while a primary surplus had been recorded for the third consecutive year in FY2026.
The president reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to strengthening revenue mobilisation, improving tax administration and reforming public sector institutions as part of its broader economic reform agenda. He highlighted the government's efforts to expand tax documentation, digitise revenue collection and curb tax evasion.
He emphasised that the reform programme had the support of all political stakeholders and that provincial governments were contributing to meeting reform commitments and targets.
The president also underscored Pakistan's efforts to promote peace amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
Jihad Azour acknowledged Pakistan's continued engagement with the IMF under the ongoing reform programme and emphasised the importance of sustaining reform efforts to strengthen macroeconomic stability, maintain fiscal discipline and support sustainable economic growth.
Minister for Finance and Revenue Muhammad Aurangzeb, Senator Sherry Rehman, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla, former federal minister Syed Naveed Qamar, MNA, and the secretary of finance were also present at the meeting.

title: New Delhi warned against shifting nuclear balance
description: New Delhi warned against shifting nuclear balance
content:
Adviser to the National Command Authority (NCA) Lt Gen (Retd) Khalid Kidwai has asserted that Pakistan will not allow India to create a strategic imbalance in South Asia.
He has warned that New Delhi is shifting toward a more ready, potentially first-use capable nuclear force able to launch a strike with virtually no warning.
"Pakistan never has and never will accept strategic imbalances to be induced in South Asia," Kidwai said at the second edition of the Islamabad Non-Proliferation Conference held on Tuesday.
Gen Kidwai and Lt Gen (Retd) Sarfraz Sattar, also an NCA adviser and a former head of the Strategic Plans Division, said India's reported deployment of nuclear weapons aboard a submarine, combined with missile modernisation and recent military confrontations between the two countries, raised serious concerns about regional strategic stability.
Citing the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute's (Sipri) Yearbook 2026 and other publicly available information, the two NCA advisers pointed to reports that India had deployed about 12 nuclear warheads on a submarine for deterrence patrols.
They highlighted India's moves toward missile canisterization and broader nuclear and conventional modernisation, arguing that these developments cast doubt on the credibility of its declared No First Use policy.
Gen Kidwai said the submarine deployment suggested India had mated some nuclear warheads with submarine-launched ballistic missiles and conducted sea-based deterrence patrols. "I do not see any reason why a Sipri report might be inaccurate or speculative," he said.
"This irresponsible escalatory transition towards creating asymmetry in nuclear posture will have profound destabilising effects on South Asian strategic stability," Gen Kidwai added.
He argued that India's ability to maintain a continuous at sea deterrent would further undermine the credibility of its declared No First Use policy and indicate a shift toward a more offensive nuclear posture.
"The operational reality that emerges is that India can undertake a first strike against Pakistan at zero notice," Gen Kidwai said. "Strategic balance and strategic stability in South Asia have apparently been dangerously disturbed by India once again."
He also expressed concern over the absence of advance notification for Indian submarine-launched ballistic missile tests.

He noted that Pakistan imported all its oil requirements, while volatility in international markets made it necessary for the government to ensure an uninterrupted supply chain and prevent profiteering and hoarding.
The minister maintained that keeping domestic petroleum prices close to international market rates helped ensure that changes in global prices were reflected in local prices.
This approach also helped maintain the security of the supply chain, he added.
He said the trend in international oil prices became clearer after three to four days, indicating whether prices were rising or falling. The existing pricing mechanism helped improve fuel availability at petrol pumps and reduce difficulties faced by consumers, he added.
Malik stated that the government had adopted the seven-day average mechanism to address supply-related problems and ensure the availability of petroleum products.
The minister also informed the House that, at the prime minister's request, refineries had once again reduced their gross refining margins.

title: Panel seeks curbs on counterfeit cosmetics
description: Panel seeks curbs on counterfeit cosmetics
content:
Senate committee reviews amendments to proposed law
The Senate Standing Committee on Science and Technology Tuesday reviewed proposed amendments to the Pakistan General Cosmetics Bill, 2026, stressing the need for an effective regulatory framework to curb counterfeit cosmetic products, protect consumers and safeguard legitimate businesses.
The committee, which met under the chairmanship of Senator Kamil Ali Agha, considered the bill referred back by the House during its sitting on October 14, 2026, along with amendments moved by Senator Saleem Mandviwalla for reconsideration and report.
The meeting was attended by Senators Nadeem Ahmed Bhutto, Husna Bano, Dr Afnanullah Khan and Mandviwalla, Minister for Science and Technology Khalid Hussain Magsi, Minister for Defence Production Muhammad Raza Hayat Harraj, and senior officials of the Ministry of Science and Technology.
During the deliberations, Mandviwalla highlighted the importance of incorporating appropriate amendments to address the growing problem of counterfeit cosmetic products and strengthen regulatory oversight.
He stressed that the proposed legislation should also take into account the concerns of importers and relevant industry associations.
Representatives of the concerned association informed the committee that the sector had been operating for approximately 15 years but continued to face challenges due to counterfeit products.
They said several fake products were being marketed under the names of established brands, making effective regulation and enforcement essential to protect consumers and legitimate businesses.
Harraj briefed the committee on efforts to regulate cosmetic products and address public health concerns associated with unsafe and substandard items. He emphasized the need for an effective legal framework to ensure consumer safety and improve regulatory oversight.
Magsi stressed that legislation should be thoroughly examined before enactment, cautioning that inadequate or impractical provisions could create serious difficulties during implementation.
He stressed the need for a balanced law that protects consumers while supporting the growth and competitiveness of the domestic industry.
The committee also deliberated on the proposed composition of the Board under Section 4 of the bill, including the representation of relevant stakeholders and government organizations.
The members discussed the nomination of the Board's chairperson by the federal government and reviewed its proposed composition of eight members.
Mandviwalla proposed adding two members to the Board, including a senator and a representative of importers, to ensure broader representation of relevant stakeholders.
The committee further examined provisions relating to overlapping requirements under Section 10, the formulation of rules and safeguards against the possible misuse of regulatory powers.
The members stressed the need for clear implementation procedures and an effective mechanism to regulate the sector.

title: 'You Can See Everything' is the talk of Tinseltown | The Express Tribune
description:
'You Can See Everything' 
is the talk of Tinseltown
content:
After record-breaking opening weekend and rave reviews, film could become first documentary in history to win 'Best P
With a record-breaking opening weekend at the box office under its belt, Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes film "You Can See Everything" is reportedly pursuing an awards campaign that could make it the first-ever documentary nominated for Best Picture at the Academy Awards.
No documentary in history has ever been nominated for Best Picture, the Oscars' top honor, but film distributor A24 is reportedly pushing forward with an awards campaign seeking to recognize "You Can See Everything" in the coveted category.
The distributor is launching an Oscars campaign for consideration across most major categories, including Best Director for Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, another honor no documentary has ever notched.
Aside from the top honors, A24 is also pushing for Oscars consideration for categories including editing, cinematography, costume design, production design, sound, original score and makeup and hairstyling, Variety reported.
Recognition for documentaries in other categories is not impossible, but still rare: "Hoop Dreams," a 1994 basketball documentary, landed a Best Editing nomination, while a handful of documentaries in recent years have been nominated for Best International Feature Film.
Possibly even more surprising than a Best Picture nomination would be "You Can See Everything" landing an acting nomination for the film's surprise star, who was revealed in the second half of the documentary to be Amanda Seyfried, years after she won an Emmy Award for playing Holmes in the Hulu series "The Dropout." No documentary has ever landed a nomination in any acting category. Variety confirmed that Seyfried, who appears as herself and also plays Holmes in reenacted scenes, will be eligible at the Academy Awards, but current rules at the Golden Globe Awards would exclude her from consideration. A24 is pushing ahead with a supporting actress campaign for Seyfried, Variety reported. Also eligible in the acting categories is Christopher Abbott, who plays Holmes' partner Billy Evans in the reenactments, and Fielder may be eligible to submit himself as an actor, but Variety reported he will not.
Are Oscar Odds For "You Can See Everything" Rising?
Variety has already predicted "You Can See Everything" will earn a Best Picture nomination, but it currently has "The Odyssey" pegged as the winner. It also predicts a nomination for best editing. The Hollywood Reporter went a step further, predicting nominations for best picture, director, supporting actress and editing.
The awards campaign for "You Can See Everything" will likely be helped by the film's stellar reviews and impressive box office performance. The movie has a near-perfect 98% score on Rotten Tomatoes, and the social media site Letterboxd announced earlier this week the film has an average 4.7-star rating out of a possible 5 based on user reviews, making it the site's highest-rated film. "You Can See Everything" earned the biggest opening weekend for a documentary in two decades, grossing $15 million from a limited opening of 855 theaters and selling out more than 2,000 screenings.
"You Can See Everything" could face off against several other movies about tech billionaires at the Oscars. Also seeking a Best Documentary nomination is "Musk," a four-hour film about the world's wealthiest person, which has also garnered rave reviews from critics. "Artificial," a forthcoming movie about OpenAI CEO Sam Altman's brief 2023 ouster, has also garnered strong reviews and is considered by some awards pundits to be a contender.
On review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes, the film holds an approval rating of 98% based on 135 reviews, with an average rating of 9.3/10. The website's consensus reads: "Nathan Fielder's ironclad commitment to the bit is pushed to its limit in You Can See Everything, an inscrutable Rorschach test of Elizabeth Holmes's psyche that's as absorbing as it is haunting." Metacritic, which uses a weighted average, assigned the film a score of 97 out of 100, based on 40 critics, indicating "universal acclaim". PostTrak audiences gave the film a 98% positive score, while 91% rating it a "definite recommend". The film's Telluride premiere drew positive early reviews, highlighting the filmmakers' close access to Holmes and Fielder's deadpan role as an on-camera interviewer.

title: Mobile industry stagnant at 10%-15% localisation | The Express Tribune
description:
Mobile industry stagnant at
10%-15% localisation
content:
Prime says imported kits face zero duty while local components face 20% to 30%
Pakistan's mobile phone manufacturing industry has failed to achieve meaningful localisation despite attracting international brands and establishing dozens of assembly plants, with domestic value addition remaining at just 10% to 15%, industry sources say. An unfavourable tariff structure has made imported components cheaper than locally manufactured parts, limiting investment in the domestic supply chain.
The Policy Research Institute of Market Economy (PRIME), in a brief titled "Protecting Assembly, Distorting Markets," said the Mobile Device Manufacturing Policy 2020 succeeded in attracting assemblers but fell short of its broader objective of developing a competitive manufacturing ecosystem.
Tecno Pack Electronics CEO Aamir Allawala said the policy was designed to bring mobile phone assembly to Pakistan initially, followed by the localisation of components such as motherboards and displays to support exports. The policy attracted global manufacturers, including Samsung, Xiaomi, OPPO, Vivo, Transsion and Nokia. According to the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA), more than 35 manufacturers established plants in the country, generating approximately 40,000 jobs.
However, the localisation drive has remained constrained by the government's failure to implement the policy's roadmap and a tariff regime that penalises domestic component production.
Under the existing structure, importing chargers, batteries, cables and motherboards as part of completely knocked-down (CKD) kits attracts zero customs duty. Meanwhile, raw materials and intermediate inputs used to manufacture these components locally face duties ranging from 20% to 30%.
This inverted tariff structure weakens the business case for local manufacturing, discouraging investment in components despite the industry's interest in expanding domestic production. PRIME Research Economist Maryam Ayub said tariff protection should translate into technology transfer and the development of local suppliers rather than perpetuating dependence on imported kits.
The brief said 31 companies had obtained manufacturing authorisations by February 2023, bringing in approximately $300 million in investment. Local plants produced 21.94 million handsets in 2022, compared with 1.53 million commercially imported phones.
Yet localisation reached only 10% against a target of 49% by June 2023. Customs data cited in the brief showed that Pakistan spent around Rs520 billion on mobile phone imports in FY26, including Rs420 billion on kits used for local assembly.
India, meanwhile, has developed a broader component manufacturing base through a more supportive tariff regime and incentives for manufacturers. Its mobile phone industry has achieved approximately 20% local value addition, with more than 400 companies producing various components.
Incentives under India's Production Linked Incentive scheme and export rebates have helped expand manufacturing capacity and exports. Mobile phone exports exceeded $30 billion last year, according to industry figures cited in the material. PRIME also highlighted the tax burden on imported handsets, arguing that high taxes widen the price gap between formally imported and smuggled devices. According to the brief, taxes account for 23.6% of the cost of a $30 phone and 50.26% of a $700 handset, adding Rs98,500 to a phone costing Rs196,000.
The PTA blocked approximately 100 million illegal devices in FY25, including nearly 72 million counterfeit phones and 27 million devices with cloned International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) numbers, the brief said. To address these challenges, PRIME recommended replacing the 25% sales tax on imported phones priced above $500 with a uniform 18% rate. It also called for linking concessions to verifiable plant-level value addition, production and export performance, while monitoring formal imports, tax collection and registration violations.
The proposed Mobile and Electronic Devices Manufacturing Policy 2026-33 aims to place greater emphasis on component production, technology transfer and exports, with penalties for companies that miss localisation targets.
The policy's success, however, will depend on whether the government aligns tariffs with its localisation objectives and ensures that incentives produce measurable gains in domestic manufacturing rather than merely expanding assembly operations.

title: PM okays 1  sales tax on battery Evs
description: PM okays 1  sales tax on battery Evs
content:
Conventional cars face up to 10% levy; penalty on missing export target
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday approved a reduction in the sales tax rate to 1% only for local and imported Battery Electric Vehicles and agreed to substantially cut import taxes under a new five-year auto policy, which would substantially reduce prices of both conventional and new energy vehicles.
After months-long discussions, the premier approved the final policy draft that would now be presented to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for approval before the federal cabinet gives its nod. Following the IMF and cabinet approval, the government will present a new bill in parliament to give effect to these tax rates.
The final draft was presented to the prime minister after it was endorsed by a committee led by Law Minister Azam Nazir. However, PM Sharif also approved a 2% to 10% Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) levy to raise an estimated Rs232 billion over five years to incentivise the billionaire-club of car assemblers to increase exports.
According to the new automotive and auto parts policy 2026-31 draft, the PM decided to divide new energy vehicles (NEVs) into three categories of Range Extended Electric Vehicles (REEVs), Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEVs) and Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs). Hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) and ICE conventional vehicles will be treated equally in terms of duties and taxes.
Subject to the IMF's approval, the PM agreed to reduce the rate of sales tax to 1% on BEVs, 6% on REEVs and 9% on PHEVs for both locally assembled and imported vehicles. Likewise, for NEVS, there will be reduced tariff of 5% for the first two years of policy on import of small electric vehicles of less than $15,000 value (Rs4.2 million) and reduced tariff of just 1% on EV-specific non-localised parts' import in CKD form.
The premier once again endorsed enhancing the credit limit for NEV financing from Rs3 million to Rs10 million with tenor increased from three years to five years. It was decided that ICE vehicles above 2,000cc and NEVs exceeding the value of $75,000 would be charged higher rates of federal excise duty to discourage their use.
According to the approved policy draft, for all types of ICE cars and SUVs, the customs duty will be 15% in the year 2031 with no additional or regulatory duty. But in the case of NEVs, the customs duty will be 1% for prime movers, trucks, dumpers and passenger vehicles. For 4W and other NEV categories, the rate will be 15% for completely built units.
As a result of the new policy, the local Suzuki Alto price of Rs3.2 million would come down to Rs2.845 million in this fiscal year because of 15% tax on CKD and 18% sales tax. But the reduction for NEV is substantial in the same category, where the price will come down from Rs4 million to Rs2.7 million for Wuling Bingo BEV.
The policy will also result in a reduction in the Suzuki Cultus price from Rs4.3 million to Rs3.8 million in the first year, but the comparable BEV will see a reduction from Rs5.3 million to just Rs3.6 million within a year. These prices will go down further as the reduction in customs duty takes effect during the five-year period.
According to the policy draft, the Yaris 1496cc price will go down from Rs6 million to Rs5.3 million and the comparable BEV Baojun Yep Pulse price will come down from Rs6.3 million to Rs5 million.
Likewise, the price of Kia Sportage will decrease from Rs12.2 million to Rs11.1 million and the price of comparable Haval AWD PHEV will fall from Rs12.9 million to Rs11.1 million in the first year.
According to the policy draft, the MG HS ICE price will go down from Rs9.5 million to Rs9.2 million in the first year and the price of comparable PHEV will drop from Rs10.3 million to Rs9 million.
The Toyota Fortuner price is projected to go up from Rs20.5 million to Rs21.7 million due to the imposition of new 5% FED and 10% ICE levy. But the price of a comparable RAV PHEV will go down from Rs23.3 million to Rs18.3 million.
The policy sets a $6 billion export target, but the cost of export will be paid by those ordinary citizens who buy new ICE vehicles. The government will recover an estimated Rs232 billion from consumers in five years and distribute it among car assemblers.
An exporter will get 5% compensation of the net B value of exports on the base value of exports and the incentive will increase to 10% on incremental exports.
The government has decided that failure to meet minimum export targets by the manufacturers will result in a penalty equal to an amount which will be a percentage of the annual production value, ranging from 1% to 3%.
Failure to meet export targets for two consecutive years will result in cancellation of the manufacturing certificate, according to the draft policy. To fund export incentives (a revenue-neutral DLTL scheme), an automotive development levy on all ICE vehicles above 1,000cc has been proposed.

title: Power firm draws flak for seeking tariff hike
description: Power firm draws flak for seeking tariff hike
content:
Other companies oppose petition seeking increase of over Rs3 per unit for hydropower
The Punjab Power Development Company Limited (PPDCL) on Tuesday came under fire from other power firms and faced questions from the regulator for seeking an increase in electricity rates by more than Rs3 per unit.
Power-sector regulator, the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra), held a public hearing to review the motion filed by PPDCL for Chianwali, Marala and Pakpattan hydroelectric power projects. During the proceedings, the petitioner pointed out that the total fixed charge was Rs7.4316 per kilowatt-hour (kWh), amounting to Rs371.54 million, and sought an upward revision to Rs10.9133.
Officials of Gujranwala Electric Power Company (Gepco), Multan Electric Power Company (Mepco) and Central Power Purchasing Agency-Guarantee (CPPA-G) strongly opposed any tariff revision for hydropower plants, saying it would increase the cost of electricity for consumers and would pave the way for other hydroelectric power companies to seek a tariff review.
PPDCL officials asked for a reduction in plant factor and revision in canal closure factor from 20 to 34 days. They said Punjab had initially intimated that canals would be closed for 20 days but it did not include the unscheduled closure of canals. PPDCL sought a reduction in the annual energy benchmark from 49.995 gigawatt hours to 34.045 GWh.
Based on the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractor's design, PPDCL in its petition requested for adoption of an estimated annual generation of 43.067 GWh at a 65.5% plant factor, but the regulatory authority in its determination foresaw a remodelling of the 49.995GWh benchmark at a capacity factor of 75.5%.
It said actual water flows/discharges reflected reductions around 26% from the historical water flows/discharges adopted in the feasibility study of Marala hydroelectric power plant.
While calculating the estimated generation, in the feasibility study and EPC contract, no scheduled and forced outage factor was accounted for. As against the actual 34-day annual canal closure, 15 days and 20 days were adopted in the feasibility study and EPC contract design, respectively.
After accounting for scheduled and forced outage, extended canal closures and low water flows, the annual energy benchmark was estimated at 34.045 GWh, at 51.4% capacity factor, which was much higher versus run-of-canal hydropower stations operated by Wapda.
The Punjab power firm also sought permission for pass-through of insurance capped at 0.8% of EPC cost and requested a reduction in the operation insurance cap from 1.35% to 0.8%, or actual cost, whichever was lower.
PPDCL has agreed with the power purchaser to reduce the insurance cap from 1.35% to 0.8% of the EPC cost. To compare the actual insurance cost, the company said the cost cap of $0.2772 million may be translated into Pakistani rupees at the US dollar conversion rate as at the valuation date of insurance cover for the related year.
The petitioner said it had agreed with the power purchaser to change the tariff structure from take-or-pay to take-and-pay with the most-run and hydrological risk to be shifted from the buyer to the seller.
All fixed and variable operation and maintenance (O&M) components, irrespective of foreign or local origin, will be indexed annually with respect to the National Consumer Price Index (NCPI).
The upward US dollar indexation of the return on equity (RoE) will be discontinued from January 1, 2026 and exchange rate will be fixed at Rs280.55/US dollar. Rupee appreciation will be passed on annually.

title: Refinery margins slashed further
description: Refinery margins slashed further
content:
Revision, following consultations with industry, leads to reduction in diesel prices
Oil refineries have agreed to slash their margins on high-speed diesel (HSD) by another $3.9 per barrel at the government's request, helping reduce diesel prices by Rs7.69 per litre on October 19.
The decision came following consultations held by Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik with the management of five refineries – Attock Refinery, National Refinery, Cnergyico Pk, Pakistan Refinery and Pak-Arab Refinery. The minister chaired a meeting with refinery executives on Monday, where the industry agreed to make further concessions to provide relief to consumers despite financial pressures arising from international crude oil prices.
Following consultations, the federal cabinet approved a revised HSD pricing formula, fixing the maximum allowable refinery crack at $38 per barrel while maintaining the minimum floor at $11.33 per barrel. The latest concession of $3.9 per barrel is in addition to the earlier reductions in refinery margins.
Responding to a query from The Express Tribune, Cnergyico Pk vice chairman said "the refining sector has made unprecedented contributions during the ongoing crisis, despite facing significant financial challenges".
"The refining sector has played an unprecedented role throughout this crisis, something no other industry has done in the past. Whether it is providing price relief to consumers, supplying discounted fuel for Hajj flights or supporting our defence forces through fuel supplies at reduced prices, the refineries have stepped forward in the national interest," he said.
He pointed out that the industry had continued to absorb substantial financial pressure as the existing pricing mechanism did not fully account for the actual cost of crude oil procurement. "The realised crack on diesel remains low because the pricing mechanism does not fully account for the cost of crude oil purchased at international market prices," he added.
The vice chairman also called on the government to examine other sectors that had increased prices of goods and services on the pretext of higher fuel costs. "These sectors should now pass on the benefit of lower diesel prices to consumers instead of keeping the additional margins resulting from earlier price increases."
He underscored that the refining industry's contribution should be viewed in the broader context of national energy security, particularly when refineries were ensuring fuel supplies to essential sectors despite financial constraints.
According to an official communication issued by the Petroleum Division to the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) on October 19, the federal cabinet approved a revised diesel pricing mechanism following consultations. Under the new formula, the maximum diesel crack will be determined on the basis of the average crack spread over the preceding seven working days, subject to a ceiling of $38 per barrel. The minimum floor of $11.33 per barrel will remain unchanged.
The cabinet also approved the continuation of the revised crude-based pricing mechanism for another three months. However, the arrangement may be reviewed earlier if geopolitical conditions improve and international petroleum prices drop sharply. All other parameters of petroleum product pricing will remain unchanged.
