title: Timoth  e Chalamet and Hans Zimmer release    Desert Chant    from    Dune  Part Three
description: Chalamet  who reprises his role as Paul Atreides  has already contributed his voice to the film   s music
content:
Chalamet, who reprises his role as Paul Atreides, has already contributed his voice to the film’s music
Timothée Chalamet and composer Hans Zimmer have released Desert Chant , the first single from the soundtrack of Dune: Part Three , ahead of the highly anticipated film’s theatrical debut in December.
Released by WaterTower Music on October 20, the track features Chalamet’s vocals alongside Zimmer’s score for director Denis Villeneuve’s upcoming science-fiction epic. The song begins with Chalamet humming before building into an intense, cinematic war chant that reflects the scale and atmosphere of the world of Arrakis.
Chalamet, who reprises his role as Paul Atreides in the third instalment, has already contributed his voice to the film’s music. Zimmer previously confirmed that the Fremen chant featured in the film’s first trailer was performed by the actor, who developed the vocal element in collaboration with the composer and Villeneuve.
Zimmer has described his work on the Dune films as a deeply personal creative experience, connecting his longstanding admiration for Frank Herbert’s science-fiction novel with his collaboration with Villeneuve. The composer returns for the third film after creating the scores for Dune (2021) and Dune: Part Two (2024).
The upcoming film will conclude Villeneuve’s planned trilogy, adapting the next chapter of Herbert’s saga following the events of Dune: Part Two . Set nearly two decades after Paul takes control of the Imperium, the story follows him as emperor while he confronts the consequences of his rule, political conspiracies and threats to his power. Chani, played by Zendaya, remains central to the unfolding conflict.
Alongside Chalamet and Zendaya, the cast includes Jason Momoa, Florence Pugh, Rebecca Ferguson, Anya Taylor-Joy, Javier Bardem, Charlotte Rampling, Isaach de Bankolé and Robert Pattinson, who joins the franchise as Scytale.
Villeneuve directs from a screenplay co-written with Brian K. Vaughan, based on Herbert’s Dune Messiah . The film is produced by Legendary Pictures in association with Warner Bros. Pictures, with Zimmer returning to provide the music.
Dune: Part Three is scheduled to arrive in cinemas and IMAX in December 2026, with international releases beginning on December 16 and a North American release set for December 18.
With Desert Chant , Chalamet’s vocal performance becomes a prominent part of the film’s musical identity, offering fans an early taste of the sound accompanying the next chapter of Paul Atreides’ story.

Keira Knightley and Luke Thompson star in 'The Lives of Others', a spy thriller play set in 1984 East Germany
Keira Knightley and Luke Thompson are joining forces for The Lives of Others , a new theatre production set in 1984 East Germany that explores surveillance, espionage and the lives of people living under an oppressive regime.
The actors discussed the upcoming spy thriller during an appearance on ITV's This Morning on October 20. The production centres on a Stasi officer who secretly monitors a writer and an actor from an attic above their apartment.
The Stasi was East Germany's secret police, known for its extensive surveillance of citizens. The play's setting provides the backdrop for a tense story involving observation, privacy and the consequences of state control.
Knightley, known for her work in films including Pride & Prejudice and Atonement , brings her experience in film and theatre to the production. Thompson, who gained widespread recognition for playing Benedict Bridgerton in Netflix's Bridgerton , joins her in the stage thriller.
During the interview, Knightley also spoke about the return of her Netflix spy thriller series Black Doves . The series follows Helen Webb, a spy whose work becomes complicated when her secret life intersects with personal relationships and political intrigue.
Her involvement in both projects continues her association with espionage-themed stories, with The Lives of Others exploring surveillance in a historical setting and Black Doves focusing on contemporary intelligence operations.
The new stage production brings together two actors recognised for their work across different genres and platforms. While the play is rooted in the political atmosphere of 1980s East Germany, its themes of surveillance and personal freedom remain relevant to modern audiences.
Further details about the production, including its full performance schedule and additional casting information, were not included in the ITV This Morning report.

title: Nicole Kidman and Keith Urban   s daughter Sunday Rose opens up about modelling with famous parents
description: I   m very aware that I   m given opportunities that not everyone can have   Sunday Rose Kidman Urban said
content:
“I’m very aware that I’m given opportunities that not everyone can have," Sunday Rose Kidman Urban said
Sunday Rose Kidman Urban is opening up about building her modelling career while navigating life as the daughter of Hollywood actress Nicole Kidman and country music star Keith Urban. The 18-year-old model discussed the opportunities that come with having famous parents in a new interview with Vogue Germany , explaining how she approaches her work and balances it with her education.
“I’m very aware that I’m given opportunities that not everyone can have, and I’m truly grateful to be able to take advantage of them,” Sunday Rose said, acknowledging the advantages her family background has afforded her.
The rising model added that she takes her professional responsibilities seriously, regardless of how tired she might feel while travelling for work. “When I’m at work, I make sure to always give my best, never come to work with a negative attitude, no matter how tired or jet-lagged I may be, and treat everyone with respect,” she explained.
Sunday Rose also discussed whether she has ever deliberately kept her parents’ identities a secret from people she meets. “Not really. I mean, I haven’t intentionally told anyone, but not that many people live in our area, so I think most people just knew when I started school,” she said.
Despite her growing presence in the fashion industry, the model credited school with helping her maintain a sense of normality. She admitted that balancing the two worlds initially felt challenging but said she has gradually learned to appreciate both modelling and the routine of returning home to her studies.
“Funnily enough, I think school is what keeps me grounded the most when I’m modelling,” she said. “But now I’ve found a way to enjoy modelling, travelling and experiencing all these amazing things with these amazing people, and then coming back here and enjoying the comforting feeling of routine and going to school.”
Sunday Rose added that she has become more organised as a result, making sure she completes and submits assignments on time despite her professional commitments. “I need to make sure I hand in my assignments on time, because that’s no excuse,” she said.
The teenager made her runway debut in October 2024, walking for Miu Miu during Paris Fashion Week. Her mother had previously explained that Sunday Rose was eager to enter the modelling world but would have to wait until she turned 16 before pursuing it professionally.
Since her debut, Sunday Rose has continued to build her fashion portfolio, appearing for major designers and participating in events in international fashion capitals. She also attended the 2026 Met Gala alongside Kidman, wearing a pink Dior couture gown for the occasion.
Kidman, an Academy Award-winning actress known for films including Moulin Rouge! , The Hours and Babygirl , has occasionally discussed her approach to raising her daughters away from the pressures of celebrity life. Urban, a Grammy-winning country musician known for songs such as Somebody Like You and Blue Ain’t Your Color , has likewise maintained a prominent career in music.
Sunday Rose’s latest interview offers insight into how she is approaching a career in fashion while recognising the privileges that accompany her family name. Rather than dismissing those advantages, she emphasised gratitude, professionalism and the importance of maintaining a routine outside the industry.

title: Dirty Dancing    sequel will honour Patrick Swayze without using AI  producer confirms
description: Jennifer Grey is set to reprise her role as Frances  Baby  Houseman in the follow up to the beloved romantic drama
content:
Jennifer Grey is set to reprise her role as Frances 'Baby' Houseman in the follow-up to the beloved romantic drama
The upcoming Dirty Dancing sequel will honour the legacy of late actor Patrick Swayze without recreating him using artificial intelligence, producer Nina Jacobson has confirmed. Jennifer Grey is set to reprise her role as Frances “Baby” Houseman in the follow-up to the beloved 1987 romantic drama, which originally starred Swayze as dance instructor Johnny Castle.
Speaking at IndieWire’s Future of Filmmaking 2026 Summit on October 17, Jacobson discussed the challenge of continuing the story without one of its most recognisable stars. She emphasised that the filmmakers want to acknowledge Swayze’s absence while allowing audiences to remember his contribution to the original film.
“That’s one of the things that you really have to focus on: how to let people mourn him in a movie,” Jacobson said. “And don’t worry, we won’t be bringing him back with AI.”
Swayze died from pancreatic cancer in 2009 at the age of 57. His performance as Johnny, whose romance with Baby unfolds through dance lessons at a summer resort, helped make Dirty Dancing a cultural phenomenon. The film’s enduring popularity has placed considerable attention on how a sequel can move the story forward without attempting to replicate the chemistry between its original leads.
Grey, who is returning as Baby, has previously acknowledged that Swayze cannot be replaced. In a 2020 interview with PEOPLE, the actress said that she did not believe the sequel should try to recreate the magic of the original.
“There is no replacing anyone who’s passed,” Grey said. “You never try to repeat anything that’s magic like that. You just go for something different.”
The sequel is expected to be set in the 1990s, with Grey returning to the world of Dirty Dancing alongside a new generation of young actors. The storyline remains under wraps, but the film is intended to introduce a new romance while exploring where Baby’s life has taken her since the events of the original movie.
Jacobson, who is producing the film alongside Brad Simpson, said the creative team wants to capture the emotional impact of the original rather than simply reproduce its plot. She also praised Grey’s understanding of why Baby continues to resonate with audiences decades after the film’s release.
The producer reflected on how her perception of Dirty Dancing has changed over the years. While she initially viewed it as glossy entertainment, she now sees a film that took significant creative risks and addressed subjects that were not commonly explored in mainstream romantic dramas.
Jacobson specifically pointed to the original film’s abortion storyline, which follows Baby’s efforts to help Penny Johnson, another dancer at the resort. She suggested that the film’s willingness to tackle difficult subjects contributed to its lasting impact.
The sequel’s screenplay is being written by Kim Rosenstock, known for Dying for Sex , with Jacobson and Simpson producing through their company, Color Force. The project is being developed by Lionsgate, although a director and release date have not yet been announced.
First released in 1987, Dirty Dancing became a defining romantic drama, celebrated for the performances of Grey and Swayze, its dance sequences and its soundtrack. The film won the Academy Award for Best Original Song for “(I've Had) The Time of My Life”.
With Grey returning and the creative team committed to preserving the original film’s emotional legacy, the sequel will aim to introduce a new chapter in Baby’s story while acknowledging the absence of the actor who helped make the original unforgettable.

Prince Harry wants to reconcile with King Charles and Prince William despite ongoing royal family tensions worldwide
Prince Harry has expressed his desire to repair his strained relationships with King Charles III and Prince William, saying reconciliation is important despite continued tensions within the British royal family.
The Duke of Sussex discussed his family relationships in an interview with GQ , published on October 20, after being asked whether he was grieving the complicated relationships he shares with his father and elder brother.
“Some people don't want it to work out. I want it to work out. With everything else that's going on in the world, the most important thing is to reconcile -- that's the key point,” Harry said.
The prince also reflected on how family disagreements affect people beyond the royal household. He suggested that sharing his experiences could encourage others dealing with similar difficulties to work towards resolving their own family conflicts.
“People maybe look at us and go, 'How are you gonna work it out? Maybe that will help me work my stuff out,'” he added.
Harry emphasised that there was already enough conflict in the world and in people's personal lives, making it important to address family disputes whenever possible.
His relationship with the royal family has faced significant challenges since he stepped back from royal duties and moved to California with his wife, Meghan Markle, and their two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet.
According to TMZ, Harry and his family have recently spent time with King Charles and Queen Consort Camilla. However, his relationship with Prince William, Kate Middleton and other members of the royal family reportedly remains strained.
Harry's latest comments indicate that he remains open to reconciliation, although it is unclear whether his remarks will lead to renewed efforts to resolve the longstanding disagreements.
His willingness to speak publicly about repairing these relationships also highlights the importance he places on family reconciliation despite their ongoing differences.

title: France to deploy troops  admits to failures over weekend unrest
description: Interior Minister Laurent Nunez says the military would be deployed alongside police
content:
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez says the military would be deployed alongside police
France will reinforce police with troops and mount a huge security operation for ​more protests planned on Saturday, the government said on Tuesday, acknowledging failures in its response to last weekend's violence.
"The deployment next Saturday will be massive," Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu ‌said, adding that the immediate priority was to restore order after rioting and looting swept Paris, Marseille, Lyon and other cities on October 17.
In a sometimes rowdy debate, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the military would be deployed alongside police, while the government pledged to overhaul tactics after widespread criticism that city centres had been left vulnerable.
Framing the crisis as a choice "between violence and the Republic", Lecornu blamed the unrest on far-left groups, who ​in turn have accused the government of underestimating public anger over high living costs and declining public services.
The turmoil shocked France because of both its scale and the apparent inability of ​police to contain it, inflaming tensions ahead of presidential elections next year with candidates from the far right and hard left performing strongly in polls.
Read: Trump warns Kansans that US will 'burn' like France if Democrats win
Protests ⁠in other European countries, including Italy and Albania, have added to concerns that anger over living standards risks spreading around the continent at a time when many nations, including France, are struggling with budget woes.
A ​night of relative calm in France followed targeted curfews imposed in several areas affected by the chaos, which the government said had helped reassert control. The localised curfews, some directed at children and teenagers under ​age 18, were extended to Tuesday night, police said.
Lecornu acknowledged shortcomings in the state's response at the weekend, saying there had been intelligence failures, while police deployments had been too static and authorities had erred by not cancelling planned police leave.
Nunez apologised for the mistakes. "I deeply regret what happened. I accept my share of responsibility," he said.
Suspect arrested for Limoges town hall destruction
Parliament is setting up a commission of inquiry to establish the causes of the unrest, ​while authorities have assigned 200 investigators to identify and track down those involved in the street violence.
Police arrested on Tuesday a man suspected of starting a blaze that destroyed a historic town hall ​in the central city of Limoges during the rioting. Officials said he had been on a security watch list and belonged to an ultra-left group.
Sylvain Maillard, a Renaissance deputy for Paris, told Reuters some apps had become "a ‌walkie-talkie system ⁠for rioters and looters".
Read more: France places Paris, Nice under partial curfews
Underscoring the broad impact of the crisis, French borrowing costs rose further on Tuesday as investors fretted about the prospect of more unrest, with the yield on benchmark 10-year government bonds touching its highest level in 24 years.
Supermarket chain Carrefour said it had lost tens of millions of euros through theft and damage, warning that it faced an "unprecedented situation" because of the disorder.
France's main student union UNEF has called for further protests on Saturday, pledging to maintain pressure on Macron's government over what it says is a deteriorating and underfunded education system. "We carry on," it said on social media.
Separately, groups identifying ​themselves as "Gilets Jaunes" (Yellow Vests) called for protest actions ​over rising fuel costs.
The yellow vest movement, ⁠largely inactive in recent years, sprang up in 2018 during Macron's first term over plans to raise petrol taxes. Traffic blockades continued for months until the government made costly concessions it can ill afford now.
Italy faces new form of unrest, minister says
Northern Italian cities, including the financial capital Milan, were also ​hit by riots last weekend.
Though not on the scale seen in France, the unrest nonetheless jolted Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government, which was ​expected to introduce new security ⁠measures at a cabinet meeting on Tuesday.
Also Read: French police clash with protesters as tens of thousands rally over cost of living
Defence Minister Guido Crosetto described the disturbances as a form of "hybrid warfare" conducted through social media platforms such as TikTok, YouTube and other online networks.
"The events in Milan and elsewhere in Italy are fundamentally different from those seen in other eras," Crosetto wrote on X. "The West has yet to realise this or take any meaningful action in response."
In Milan's central Corso Vittorio Emanuele II, sportswear retailer ⁠On and a ​Levi's store that were targeted during the unrest had reopened on Tuesday but remained boarded up. Luxury stores had ​restored merchandise to window displays after temporarily removing it for security reasons.
In Albania, protesters were expected to take to the streets of Tirana for a seventh consecutive day against the government of Prime Minister Edi Rama.

title: Bavuma leads South Africa fightback
description: Hosts declare at 425 9 after captain s brilliant 179
content:
Hosts declare at 425-9 after captain's brilliant 179
South Africa captain Temba Bavuma struck a career-best 179 to lead a determined recovery before the hosts declared their first innings at 425-9 on the third day of the second Test against Australia at Saint George's Park on Tuesday.
Bavuma recorded his fifth Test century in a patient 226-ball knock, while Marco Jansen scored 85 from 100 deliveries and Simon Harmer added 82 to frustrate Australia's bowlers.
South Africa had resumed on 97-5 after rain restricted play to just 43 overs across the first two days, but Bavuma and Jansen turned the contest around with a 132-run partnership for the seventh wicket.
The stand surpassed South Africa's previous record for the seventh wicket at St George's Park, an 89-run partnership against England in 1896.
Jansen attacked Australia's bowlers before falling to Scott Boland in the first over with the second new ball. Boland finished with 5-63, his third five-wicket haul in Test cricket and first outside Australia.
Bavuma continued to anchor the innings alongside Harmer, extending South Africa's resistance before he was dismissed for 179.
Australia had made an early breakthrough on Tuesday when Mitchell Starc removed Wiaan Mulder for 13. Mulder gloved a short-pitched delivery to slip fielder Matt Renshaw while attempting to evade it, with the dismissal confirmed after a review.
The wicket was Starc's 450th in Test cricket.
South Africa's recovery gave them a substantial total after Australia dominated the opening Test in Durban, winning by 214 runs to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.
Bavuma's innings, supported by Jansen's aggressive batting and Harmer's determined contribution, helped the hosts recover from a precarious position and put pressure back on the visitors in the second Test.
The series continues as South Africa seek to level the contest, while Australia aim to strengthen their position with another victory.

content:
Sarah Rafferty reflects on family Alzheimer’s diagnoses and urges early discussion of symptoms and treatment options
Sarah Rafferty has opened up about her family’s experience with Alzheimer’s disease, describing the emotional toll of watching her father and grandmother live with the condition.
The Suits alum, 53, discussed their diagnoses in an interview with PEOPLE published on October 20, explaining how the experience has influenced her approach to brain health and raising awareness about early symptoms.
“It was really hard to watch my beloved grandmother and my father struggle through this,” Rafferty said. “It’s scary.”
According to the actress, her father was his mother’s primary caregiver after her Alzheimer’s diagnosis. He received his own diagnosis shortly after his mother died.
Rafferty also recalled an incident when her father lost his way while driving home from a familiar neighbourhood location. The experience alarmed the family and highlighted the challenges of recognising changes in memory and thinking.
Her father, now 90, is still alive. Reflecting on his journey, Rafferty described the experience as “a very long goodbye” and said it remained difficult to think about.
The actress said stigma surrounding Alzheimer’s disease and memory problems had previously made conversations about brain health challenging. She added that families sometimes mistake early symptoms for normal signs of ageing.
Rafferty is now partnering with Eli Lilly and Company to raise awareness of early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease and encourage people to speak with healthcare professionals about symptoms and available treatment options. The campaign highlights Kisunla, a treatment designed to slow disease progression in eligible patients.
The actress also said her family’s experience had encouraged her to prioritise her own brain health. She focuses on exercise, healthy eating, stress reduction and adequate sleep.
Rafferty urged families to discuss cognitive changes with doctors sooner rather than later, noting that early action can help people explore available options.
Her message highlights the importance of recognising potential Alzheimer’s symptoms and seeking medical guidance rather than dismissing changes in memory as part of ageing.

title: Guillermo del Toro gets emotional at Morelia Film Festival  says  we   re handing down a world in ruins
description: His remarks came as he received the festival   s Artistic Excellence Award in recognition of his contributions to cinema
content:
His remarks came as he received the festival’s Artistic Excellence Award in recognition of his contributions to cinema
Guillermo del Toro became emotional while reflecting on the state of the world during his appearance at the 24th Morelia International Film Festival in Mexico, where he celebrated the 20th anniversary of his acclaimed dark fantasy film Pan’s Labyrinth . The Oscar-winning filmmaker lamented the world younger generations are inheriting, saying it pained him to see older generations fail those who would come after them.
“We’re handing down a world in ruins,” del Toro said, describing a world he believes has become morally, spiritually and socially fragmented. The director was visibly moved as he spoke about the responsibility of previous generations and the challenges facing young people today.
Del Toro attended the festival to present a restored 3D version of Pan’s Labyrinth , his 2006 Spanish-language fantasy film that explores the brutality of fascism through the perspective of a young girl. The film follows Ofelia, played by Ivana Baquero, who escapes into a fantastical world while navigating the horrors of post-Civil War Spain under the authoritarian rule of Francisco Franco.
The anniversary screening offered an opportunity to revisit the film’s themes of authoritarianism, resistance and the power of imagination. Del Toro drew parallels between the political climate depicted in the film and the resurgence of fascist ideas in contemporary society, arguing that the mechanisms used to maintain power, including division, hatred and antagonism, remain relevant.
The filmmaker also reflected on how difficult it can be to maintain hope in a world increasingly shaped by cynicism and hostility. He argued that solidarity and the belief that people can come together are sometimes dismissed as naïve, while pessimism can be mistaken for intelligence.
Despite his concerns, del Toro emphasised the importance of continuing to believe in the possibility of a better future. He suggested that acknowledging the failures of previous generations and expressing genuine regret to younger people could be a meaningful starting point for rebuilding trust.
The director’s appearance at Morelia also extended beyond cinema. During his visit, he voiced support for people protesting the water crisis in Guadalajara, his hometown, where residents have raised concerns about the quality of their water supply. Del Toro defended the use of cultural events as spaces for public discussion, arguing that access to clean water should be treated as a basic human right rather than something people must fight to obtain.
His remarks came as he received the festival’s Artistic Excellence Award in recognition of his contributions to Mexican and international cinema. The event brought together several collaborators associated with Pan’s Labyrinth , including actress Ivana Baquero, cinematographer Guillermo Navarro and producer Bertha Navarro.
Released in 2006, Pan’s Labyrinth became one of del Toro’s most celebrated films, earning six Academy Award nominations and winning three Oscars for cinematography, art direction and makeup. Its blend of historical drama, dark fantasy and political allegory has helped establish it as a landmark of contemporary cinema.
Two decades after the film’s release, del Toro’s reflections demonstrated why its themes continue to resonate. By connecting the story’s portrayal of authoritarianism and resistance with present-day concerns, the filmmaker used the anniversary to highlight not only the enduring power of storytelling but also the responsibility of older generations to the people who will inherit the world they leave behind.

title: Kyle Kennedy  granddaughter of Bobby and Ethel Kennedy  dies at 42
description: Kyle Kennedy  granddaughter of Robert F  Kennedy and Ethel Kennedy  has died at 42 after years of disability advocacy
content:
Kyle Kennedy, granddaughter of Robert F. Kennedy and Ethel Kennedy, has died at 42 after years of disability advocacy
Kyle Kennedy, the granddaughter of Robert F. Kennedy and Ethel Kennedy, has died at the age of 42. The educator and disability rights advocate died at her home in Westwood, Massachusetts, on September 21, according to her obituary.
Her cause of death remains pending, the Westwood Town Clerk told PEOPLE .
Born on July 6, 1984, in Washington, D.C., Kyle was the daughter of Michael Kennedy, who died in 1997, and Victoria Denise Gifford. She was one of 34 grandchildren of the former US attorney general and his wife, Ethel.
Kennedy built a career in education, focusing on early childhood learning and educational reform for disadvantaged children and people with disabilities. After earning a history degree from Georgetown University, she completed a master's degree in early education at Pace University and a Master of Education in education policy and management at Harvard University's Graduate School of Education.
She began her professional career in New York City as a teacher with Teach For America.
In August 2012, Kennedy married Liam Kerr in Boston. They welcomed twins, Conor and Josie, although their daughter died days after birth. The couple later had a second son, Declan. Her obituary identifies Kerr as her former husband.
Kennedy sustained a severe spinal cord injury in 2020 that resulted in long-term paralysis. Following the injury, she became an advocate for people with disabilities, speaking out about discrimination and barriers to healthcare access.
Her activism included testifying at a hearing at the Massachusetts State House concerning healthcare discrimination against people with disabilities.
Kennedy is survived by her sons, Conor and Declan, her mother, Victoria, her brother, Michael, and her sister, Rory. She also leaves behind several nieces and nephews.
Her work in education and disability advocacy formed a significant part of her legacy, alongside her connection to the prominent Kennedy family.

title: Turkiye submits Makkah defence pact to parliament for ratification  sources say
description: Parliament commission could debate pact    as early as Friday  another source says
content:
Parliament commission could debate pact ​as early as Friday, another source says
Turkiye has submitted a defence ‌pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to parliament for ratification, three parliamentary sources said on Tuesday, moving NATO's second-largest army closer to a formal mutual defence pledge with Riyadh as it faces Houthi attacks.
The three countries signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in August, under which an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all.
The ​agreement's first article says the parties shall use "all necessary means" to eliminate threats to one another's territorial integrity, sovereignty or internationally recognised ​borders, according to a text seen by Reuters .
Read : PM reaffirms Pakistan’s support for Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks in meeting with newly appointed envoy
"In the event one of the parties is subjected to an armed ⁠attack or military aggression by another country or group of countries, the parties shall immediately provide assistance to the party under attack, utilising the ​full range of mutual assistance measures available to them," Article 2 of the agreement says.
The provision, similar to NATO's Article 5, refers to Article ​51 of the UN Charter, which covers the individual or collective right of states to self-defence against armed attack.
The three countries "will decide on the scope and nature of the support to be provided following an objective assessment of the assistance required" and will cooperate within their available resources, including military capabilities and resources, the same article says.
At ​an emergency meeting of the alliance in Riyadh earlier this month, the three countries agreed to ensure the "rapid deployment" of military forces and capabilities in Saudi ​Arabia.
Turkiye, which has a robust defence industry, has condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, expressed willingness to help meet Riyadh's military technology needs and agreed to join ‌a Saudi-led ⁠coalition to ensure navigational safety in the Red Sea.
The agreement also envisages close cooperation on defence industry, intelligence sharing, logistical support and the fight against "all means of terrorism," including at the operational level.
Parliamentary ratification is required for Turkiye to formally approve the agreement.
Aim to “strengthen collective deterrence”
Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmus, currently visiting Kyrgyzstan, will refer the agreement to parliament's foreign affairs commission upon his return, two of the sources said. The contents and details of the agreement are ​expected to become public once it ​is submitted to the commission.
The commission ⁠could debate the agreement as early as Friday, another source said.
President Tayyip Erdogan's communications director, Burhanettin Duran, said that Turkiye's recent step marked an important milestone towards the institutionalisation of strategic cooperation between the three nations.
Also Read : FO says Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye move to implement Makkah defence pact
"This ​strategic partnership developed between our countries aims to strengthen collective deterrence, enhance joint capabilities in the defence sector, ​and safeguard security and ⁠stability in our region," Duran said in a post on X.
A Turkish official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said Turkiye's own contribution was expected to be limited to military equipment , intelligence sharing and weapons systems, adding that no other form of deployment had taken place under the alliance so far.
Asked ⁠how Turkiye ​could help Saudi Arabia defend against attacks by Yemen's Houthis, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan ​Fidan said that the Makkah agreement was not an "offensive agreement", adding that Turkiye would not send troops to another country to carry out attacks on its territory.
Turkiye's constitution requires separate permission from ​parliament to deploy troops abroad regardless of any international agreement.

title: Punjab govt reschedules Basant 2027 in Lahore for second time  sets March dates
description: Provincial cabinet approves March 12   14 for festival  reversing the January 29   February 7 schedule announced earlier
content:
Provincial cabinet approves March 12–14 for festival, reversing the January 29–February 7 schedule announced earlier
The Punjab government has rescheduled Basant 2027 in Lahore for a second time, with the provincial cabinet approving March 12, 13 and 14 as the new dates for the festival.
The latest decision reverses the schedule announced earlier by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, under which Basant was to be celebrated over 10 days from January 29 to February 7, with a break on February 5 to observe Kashmir Day.
According to sources, Lahore Deputy Commissioner Captain (retd) Muhammad Ali Ijaz sent a summary proposing a change in the festival dates to the Punjab Home Department, which forwarded it to the provincial cabinet for approval. The cabinet has now approved the March schedule.
Maryam had announced the January dates as an extended celebration intended to promote Punjab’s cultural heritage and Lahore’s traditional identity. She had directed the relevant departments to prepare in advance and strengthen public safety and facilitation arrangements.
The latest rescheduling means the festival will now take place over three days in March, replacing the previously announced 10-day programme.
Meanwhile, preparations for Basant 2027 have been underway under a regulatory framework governing kite flying, the manufacture and sale of kites, and the transportation and use of kite string.
The Lahore district administration has said kite flying will be permitted only on designated festival dates. Chemical-coated, metallic and sharp kite strings, commonly known as manjha , are prohibited under the announced restrictions, while only approved kite sizes and cotton string are permitted.
Registration of kite manufacturers began on September 5. Manufacturers must complete the prescribed registration and approval process, with licences issued only to those meeting the legal requirements. Assistant commissioners have been directed to verify applicants’ credentials and inspect their premises.
Read More : Basant comes back, but not as before
The district administration has also introduced a dedicated registration portal for Basant 2027, requiring manufacturers and other stakeholders to complete the applicable formalities. Authorities have warned of penalties for violations of regulations governing the manufacture, transportation and use of prohibited kite string.
The government had also been preparing cultural and beautification activities, including decorations along major roads, parks and green belts, as well as events showcasing Lahore’s heritage.
The Walled City was being considered for cultural activities featuring traditional Basant colours, food stalls offering local cuisine and live performances by musicians and artists.
The festival was revived in Lahore from February 6 to 8, 2026, after a prolonged ban, under restrictions intended to prevent accidents and protect public safety. Authorities have been directed to strengthen safety arrangements for the 2027 celebrations.

title: Nasir begins Venus ABC Open title quest
description: Pakistan fields seven men and three women squash players at Karachi event
content:
Pakistan fields seven men and three women squash players at Karachi event
Pakistan’s experienced squash player Nasir Iqbal will begin his title quest against Canada’s Salah Eltorgman in the men’s singles preliminary round of the Venus ABC Open 2026, which begins at the DHA Creek Club on Wednesday (today).
The event is being held under the auspices of the Sindh Squash Association (SSA).
The 11th-seeded Nasir, who was part of Pakistan’s silver-medal-winning campaign at the recent Asian Games, is expected to make a strong start in the tournament, which features 24 men, including seven players from Pakistan.
Experienced campaigner Asim Khan is also among the participants. He has received a bye in the first round and will advance directly to the pre-quarter-finals on Thursday.
Meanwhile, wild-card entrant Azan Ali Khan will face Egypt’s Ziad Ibrahim, while Anas Shah will take on Malaysia’s Yee Xian Siow in the preliminary round on Wednesday.
Another wild-card entrant, Abdullah Nawaz, will meet Malaysia’s Ameeshenraj Chandaran.
Top seed Curtis Malik of England has also received a bye in the first round.
The 24-player men’s draw features seven players from Pakistan, four each from Egypt and Malaysia, and two each from England and Hong Kong. Japan, Bahrain, Canada, Sri Lanka and the Netherlands are each represented by one player.
The women’s event will also feature 24 players, with Sana Bahadar, Anam Aziz and Rushna Mahboob representing Pakistan.
Egypt has six players in the women’s draw, while Pakistan and Germany have three each. Switzerland, Hong Kong, Japan, the Czech Republic, England, Singapore and the Netherlands are each represented by one player.
Event director and SSA president Adnan Asad said the tournament’s primary objective was to provide players with opportunities to gain international exposure.
“Our key focus is to provide a platform for players to gain exposure,” Adnan told a news conference at the DHA Creek Club.
Speaking alongside squash legend Jahangir Khan, Adnan said Pakistan’s top player, Noor Zaman, would not participate because he was competing in a tournament in Canada.
Jahangir said the aim was to help revive squash in Pakistan and restore the sport’s prominence.
“We want to help revive squash. We have established academies so that players can receive proper training,” Jahangir said.
He added that he had also proposed to the prime minister that departmental teams be revived.
“Most of our players come from humble backgrounds. If the departmental system is restored, it will help them secure jobs and focus on their game,” he said.
According to the tournament’s information sheet, the organisers have announced a total prize package of $41,000, comprising $30,000 in on-site prize money, along with accommodation and court bonuses.
The player prize pool amounts to $28,500, with the winner set to receive $5,415 and the runner-up $3,420.
Players finishing third and fourth will each earn $2,137.50, while those placed fifth to eighth will receive $1,282.50 each. Players finishing ninth to 16th will collect $783.75 each, while those placed 17th to 24th will receive $498.75 each.
The prize structure also includes a 5 per cent player contribution of $1,500, bringing the on-site prize fund to $30,000. An additional $6,000 has been allocated for accommodation bonuses and $5,000 for court bonuses, taking the total package to $41,000.
The tournament will continue until October 25. First-round matches are scheduled for October 21, followed by the second round on October 22, the quarter-finals on October 23, the semi-finals on October 24, and the finals and closing ceremony on October 25.

title: Josh Duhamel reacts to    Ransom Canyon    cancellation despite Netflix show   s No  1 success
description: The actor says he would prefer another cowboy role over playing a defence attorney in his next project
content:
The actor says he would prefer another cowboy role over playing a defence attorney in his next project
Josh Duhamel has opened up about Netflix cancelling Ransom Canyon , admitting he was surprised the Western romantic drama would not return for a third season despite its strong performance.
Speaking to Us Weekly , Duhamel said the decision caught him off guard because the series had reportedly topped Netflix’s rankings for almost two weeks. He believed the audience response suggested the story had connected with viewers.
“I was pretty surprised, if I’m being honest,” the actor said. He also expressed disappointment that the streaming service decided against continuing the show, adding that he felt sorry for fans who had become invested in its characters.
Netflix reportedly made the cancellation decision in September 2026, less than two months after the second season premiered in July. Although the series attracted viewers, its performance was not enough to secure another instalment.
Based on Jodi Thomas’ book series, Ransom Canyon follows residents of a small Texas town, including Duhamel’s rancher character, Staten Kirkland, and Minka Kelly’s Quinn O’Grady. Their romance formed a central part of the drama, with the second season finale leaving room for their relationship to develop further.
Showrunner April Blair had indicated that a potential third season would explore the couple’s life together and the difficulties they might face as they built a future. The cancellation therefore left viewers without the continuation that had been planned for the characters.
Duhamel acknowledged that decisions about television renewals are part of the streaming business, even when audiences respond positively to a programme. His comments reflect the disappointment surrounding the series ending before its central relationship could receive further attention.
The actor has not ruled out returning to similar roles in future projects. He told that a couple of possibilities were in development, although he was not ready to reveal details.
For now, Duhamel appears keen to remain connected to the Western genre. “But I’d much rather play a cowboy than a defense attorney,” he said, offering a glimpse of the kinds of roles he hopes to pursue next.

title: Death toll from Houthi attack on Yemen training camp rises to 73
description: More than 200 people are injured  14 remain missing after ballistic missiles hit security forces during training
content:
More than 200 people are injured; 14 remain missing after ballistic missiles hit security forces during training
An attack by Yemen's Houthi movement on a government security forces training camp in Shabwa province killed 73 people, the provincial media ​office said, raising the toll from Monday's strike as fighting ‌intensifies.
Fourteen people remained missing, it added.
The Iran-aligned Houthis and Yemen's internationally recognised government, backed by a Saudi-led coalition, have traded attacks since September when the group ​advanced towards territory near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a shipping ​chokepoint at the Red Sea's mouth.
Read : Houthi attack kills 53 at Yemen government training camp, officials say
Local authorities said three ⁠ballistic missiles hit security forces on Monday during training. Reuters -verified video ​showed injured people and bloodied bodies scattered on the ground.
More than ​200 people were injured, according to provincial governor Awad al-Wazir.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the camp was run by Saudi forces. Saudi authorities did not immediately ​respond to a request for comment.
Yemeni government forces began a ​campaign this month to retake Houthi-held areas, recovering ground near the strait. The Houthis ‌are ⁠besieging Taiz, the last major urban stronghold of anti-Houthi forces in Yemen's southern highlands.
The conflict has become another front in the wider US-Israeli war on Iran , with Houthi attacks targeting Riyadh's international airport and Saudi ​Aramco in Saudi ​Arabia, the ⁠world's largest crude exporter.
Shabwa, an energy-rich coastal province overlooking the Gulf of Aden, hosts the Balhaf liquefied ​natural gas facility, Yemen's largest industrial investment.
Yemen's war began ​with ⁠the Houthi seizure of Sanaa in 2014, which drove the government south. A Saudi-led intervention in 2015 produced a bloody stalemate before a 2022 ⁠truce ​that held until this year.
Aid agencies warn ​of rapidly deteriorating conditions in what is already one of the world's worst humanitarian ​crises.

title: Hunter Schafer reveals she had gender affirming surgery  says she feels  amazing
description: I just had bottom surgery in December  which was amazing  and I love it so much     Schafer said
content:
“I just had bottom surgery in December, which was amazing, and I love it so much,” Schafer said
Euphoria star Hunter Schafer has revealed that she underwent gender-affirming surgery in December 2025, describing the experience as “amazing” in a new interview with Elle . The 27-year-old actor opened up about her decision to undergo the procedure, explaining how her understanding of her gender identity evolved over time.
“I just had bottom surgery in December, which was amazing, and I love it so much,” Schafer said in the interview published on October 19. She reflected on her journey towards the decision, explaining that she had spent years trying to embrace her body before deciding that medical transition was the right choice for her.
“For a long time I've embraced the gender-expansive part of myself, and I really wanted to try to make that previous body work, because I thought there was something really cool and badass about it,” she explained.
Schafer said her experience eventually led her to reconsider the relationship between her ideas about gender and how she wanted to live in everyday life. Reflecting on where she stands today, the actor said, “I'm a woman. I'm a girl.”
The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes star also discussed her recovery following the procedure. She rented a large apartment where friends and family could visit while she rested, with her movement initially restricted to a very limited number of steps each day.
“I think my limit was 150 steps per day, which is nothing,” Schafer recalled, describing the restrictions she faced during recovery.
The actor, who began transitioning at the age of 14, has spoken publicly about her experiences as a transgender woman throughout her career. However, she has also expressed frustration with being defined primarily by her transgender identity, explaining in a 2024 interview with GQ that she wanted to move beyond repeatedly discussing her transition and focus on her work.
Schafer first gained widespread recognition for playing Jules Vaughn in HBO's Euphoria , opposite Zendaya. The role established her as a prominent young actor, while her work in fashion and films such as The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes has expanded her career beyond television.
In her latest interview, Schafer also reflected on how much she has changed since Euphoria premiered in 2019. She described herself as an introverted teenager when she first joined the series, adding that she has since become more comfortable performing and expressing herself publicly.
Beyond discussing her own journey, Schafer revealed that she would like to star in a romantic comedy centred on a transgender woman. “I would just love to see a trans girl rom-com,” she said, explaining that she had been thinking about the idea for some time and would like to help make it happen.
Schafer's latest comments offer a personal account of her decision to undergo surgery and the way her understanding of herself has developed. She also emphasised that her experience is individual, reflecting the different paths transgender people may take in deciding what is right for them.

Cardi B made her NPR Tiny Desk debut with eight songs, a live band and a set mixing hits with personal tracks onstage
Cardi B made her NPR Tiny Desk Concert debut on October 19, performing eight songs with a live band in an intimate office setting that attracted one of the largest crowds the venue’s producers had seen.
The Grammy-winning rapper delivered a set spanning her biggest hits and more personal tracks, showcasing her versatility through stripped-down arrangements and playful audience interactions.
The performance opened with “Hello”, followed by “ErrTime”, before Cardi shifted to more emotional material with “Man of Your Word” and “Be Careful”. The change in mood highlighted a more vulnerable side of the artist, whose music is often associated with bold lyrics and energetic production.
Cardi later brought the energy back with “Up” and “AH HA”, joking, “Change the vibes, change the vibes,” before moving into the upbeat tracks.
She also performed “Bodak Yellow”, the breakthrough hit that established her as a major force in hip-hop, and closed the set with “I Like It”, her Latin-influenced hit featuring elements of the boogaloo tradition.
Musical director Adam Blackstone led the accompanying band, playing bass and keyboards. The ensemble also featured guitarist Clayton Sears, drummer Cedric Thompson, keyboardist Eugene Roberts, saxophonist Kenneth Whalum and trumpeter Melvin Jones. DJ Ray G handled the turntables, while background vocalists Tiffany Stevens and Ebony Franklin supported the arrangements.
NPR producer Alanté Serene described the gathering as one of the largest crowds she had seen at the office, reflecting the interest surrounding Cardi’s appearance.
The NPR Tiny Desk series is known for bringing established and emerging artists into a compact performance space, allowing musicians to reinterpret their work through live arrangements.
Cardi’s eight-song set demonstrated how the format can offer a fresh perspective on familiar tracks while highlighting an artist’s personality and musical range.

title: Selma Blair is trying to manage her Multiple Sclerosis after plane arrest
description: The actress pleaded not guilty to two counts of second degree assault after her October 11 arrest
content:
The actress pleaded not guilty to two counts of second degree assault after her October 11 arrest
Selma Blair is working to manage her multiple sclerosis while dealing with the aftermath of her recent arrest following an incident aboard a Delta flight, according to a source close to the actress who spoke to PEOPLE .
In an article published on October 19, 2026, the source said the 54 year old actress felt embarrassed and upset about the situation. They also described the challenges of balancing her health, professional responsibilities and personal commitments.
“Managing her MS is complicated and it can be a lot to handle,” the source told PEOPLE , adding that Blair was making an effort to manage her health while continuing to work.
Blair was arrested at New York’s John F. Kennedy International Airport on October 11 after allegedly assaulting flight crew members during a Delta flight. Reports also alleged that a nurse and a Port Authority police officer were assaulted. These remain allegations, not findings of guilt.
The actress appeared in court the following day and pleaded not guilty to two counts of second degree assault. She was released on bail.
Blair’s representative said she had experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct. The statement added that she received medical attention after landing and was in stable condition.
Her attorney, Shawn Barnes, also told media outlets that Blair had missed several doses of medication and had been maintaining a demanding work schedule before the flight. He said the incident was not an intentional assault.
Blair publicly disclosed her multiple sclerosis diagnosis in 2018. The condition affects the central nervous system and can cause symptoms including muscle weakness, numbness, vision problems and difficulties with memory. Its effects can vary considerably between individuals.
On October 16, Blair’s representative issued a further statement highlighting the physical challenges she has faced since her diagnosis, including daily pain. The statement also disclosed that she has pseudobulbar affect, a neurological condition associated with her MS that can affect emotional expression.
The representative urged the public to consider all the facts before reaching conclusions. Blair’s case remains subject to the legal process, and the allegations have not been proven in court.

title: Aiman Khan questions flying car obsession as climate crisis worsens
description: Actor shares story on contrast between futuristic ambitions  environmental disasters affecting vulnerable communities
content:
Actor shares story on contrast between futuristic ambitions, environmental disasters affecting vulnerable communities
Actor Aiman Khan has questioned the world's fascination with flying cars amid the worsening climate crisis, sharing an Instagram story that highlighted the contrast between futuristic technological ambitions and the environmental disasters affecting communities around the world.
In the story , Khan shared footage of severe flooding, showing vehicles partially submerged in muddy water, alongside the caption: “I cannot tell you how uninterested I am in flying cars when the planet is collapsing.”
Although she did not explicitly mention Elon Musk, her post came amid renewed attention surrounding the billionaire entrepreneur's ambitions for flying-car technology.
On October 15, Tesla showcased its next-generation Roadster at a SpaceX facility in Texas. The demonstration featured a vehicle equipped with thrusters that performed a brief airborne manoeuvre. Musk presented the development as a glimpse of a future in which flying cars could become a reality.
Khan's post offered a contrasting perspective, drawing attention to the environmental challenges that continue to affect people's everyday lives. For communities hit by flooding, immediate concerns include safe housing, accessible roads, reliable electricity, clean drinking water and effective emergency response systems.
Pakistan's experience illustrates how climate-related disasters can have consequences long after floodwaters recede.
In 2022 , catastrophic monsoon flooding affected millions of people across Pakistan, destroying homes and agricultural land and causing extensive economic damage. The disaster drew international attention to the country's vulnerability to climate-related hazards.
More recently, an August 2026 report highlighted findings from WWF-Pakistan on rising temperatures, erratic rainfall, floods, droughts and glacial lake outburst floods. The report also examined extensive agricultural and infrastructure damage associated with the 2025 monsoon season.
These challenges underline why climate change is not merely an abstract environmental issue but one that affects public safety, economic stability, food security and human wellbeing.
Khan is among Pakistan's well-known television actors and social media personalities. She rose to prominence through dramas such as Meri Beti , Mann Mayal and Ishq Tamasha , building a substantial following during her acting career.
Her personal life and professional decisions have also attracted public interest, particularly after she stepped back from regular television appearances following her marriage to actor Muneeb Butt in 2018.

Imam-ul-Haq struck an unbeaten century for Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) while Mohammad Rizwan scored a half-century for Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited (SNGPL) on Tuesday as both batsmen made notable contributions on the second day of the seventh round of the President’s Trophy Grade-I.

Imam’s unbeaten 118 helped OGDCL take control against Ghani at the LCCA Ground in Lahore, while Rizwan’s 64 gave SNGPL a first-innings lead over Khan Research Laboratories (KRL) at the Shoaib Akhtar Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi.
OGDCL reached 277-3 in 63.2 overs after dismissing Ghani for 232, establishing a 45-run lead at stumps. Saad Khan contributed 88, while Ali Zaryab scored 42 to support Imam’s innings.
Ghani, resuming at 232-8, failed to add to their overnight total. Mohammad Hasnain took four wickets for 53 runs, while Aftab Ahmad and Mohammad Amir Khan claimed three wickets each.
Ubaid Shah took two wickets for 79 runs for Ghani.
At the Shoaib Akhtar Cricket Stadium, Rizwan scored 64 as SNGPL were dismissed for 195 in reply to KRL’s first-innings total of 151. SNGPL secured a 44-run lead, with Sameer Minhas contributing 49.
Daniyal Ali Khan led KRL’s bowling attack with four wickets for 48 runs.
KRL recovered in their second innings to reach 111-2 in 29 overs at stumps. Mohammad Faiq remained unbeaten on 64, helping KRL establish a 67-run overall lead with eight wickets in hand.
Elsewhere, MIT Solutions strengthened their position against Pakistan Television (PTV) at the Diamond Cricket Ground in Islamabad after enforcing the follow-on.
MIT Solutions, who resumed at 370-6, were bowled out for 412 in 88.4 overs. Kashif Ali and Khalil Ahmed took three wickets each for PTV.
Salman Aslam then claimed four wickets for six runs as PTV collapsed for 64 in 19.5 overs, conceding a first-innings deficit of 348 runs. Aamer Jamal took two wickets for 13 runs.
PTV responded more strongly in their second innings, reaching 177-2 in 43.1 overs at stumps. Waqar Hussain remained unbeaten on 102, while Taimur Khan was not out on 63. PTV still trailed by 171 runs, with eight wickets remaining.
At the National Ground in Islamabad, Kingsmen Academy resumed at 328-8 and were dismissed for 371 in 97 overs.
State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) reached 209-4 in 51.5 overs in reply, with Kamran Ghulam scoring 88 and Faham-ul-Haq adding 49. Mohammad Ilyas took two wickets for 55 runs as SBP ended the day 162 runs behind.
Imam’s century and Rizwan’s half-century were among the day's leading batting performances, while MIT Solutions moved into a commanding position against PTV after enforcing the follow-on.

North Waziristan District Police Officer (DPO) Sajjad Hussain confirmed the incident, saying that the police officer was on duty when he was targeted by the assailants, further adding that he sustained multiple bullet wounds and succumbed to his injuries.

DPO Hussain said further details regarding the investigation and the identification of the attackers were awaited. He said that the morale of the police force remained high and that the police would continue to pursue the attackers.
He said the police were determined to track down the militants and would not allow them to operate in the area.
Police launched a search operation in the area to trace the attackers and determine their escape route. Security personnel were also investigating the circumstances surrounding the attack, while the identities and motives of the assailants remained unknown.

The attack comes amid continuing security challenges faced by police personnel in the district. Police officials have repeatedly been targeted in gun attacks in different parts of the region.
Despite such threats, police personnel continue to perform their duties to maintain law and order and protect the lives and property of local residents. The incident has once again highlighted the risks faced by law enforcement personnel serving in the area.

title: Elizabeth Holmes contacts Nathan Fielder from prison after documentary that explores her life released
description: Fielder had not heard from Holmes for more than six months before their prison phone call
content:
Fielder had not heard from Holmes for more than six months before their prison phone call
Elizabeth Holmes gave filmmaker Nathan Fielder a puzzling response after speaking with him by phone about You Can See Everything , a documentary examining the disgraced Theranos founder and her family.
In an interview with Wired published on October 19, Fielder recalled speaking to Holmes after the film made its surprise world premiere at the Telluride Film Festival in September. He said they had not spoken for more than six months while she continued serving her prison sentence.
When Fielder asked how she felt about the documentary and the attention surrounding its release, Holmes said she had heard about some coverage but had not read much of it.
At the end of the conversation, she told him, “I trust you.”
Fielder responded, “OK, thanks.” Holmes repeated the same statement later in the call, leaving the filmmaker uncertain about what she intended to convey. He said their conversation also covered other matters, including her children, but declined to share personal updates he considered private.
Directed by Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, You Can See Everything follows Holmes, her fiancé Billy Evans and their two children during the 34 days before she reported to prison in 2023. The nearly three hour documentary examines the former technology executive’s public image, family life and the consequences of the Theranos scandal.
Holmes and Evans had initially approached production company and distributor A24 about making a documentary that would present what they described as the real Elizabeth. Fielder became interested in the story after reading John Carreyrou’s 2018 investigative book Bad Blood and sought an opportunity to film with Holmes and her family.
Holmes was convicted in 2022 of conspiracy and wire fraud offences connected to Theranos, the blood testing company she founded. She was subsequently sentenced to more than 11 years in federal prison.
Fielder’s account offers a glimpse into the complicated relationship between the filmmaker and his subject, although Holmes’ repeated statement does not establish how she ultimately feels about the finished documentary.

Britain will fly Royal Air Force ​Typhoon fighter jets on defensive missions to help protect ‌Saudi cities and critical national infrastructure from Houthi aerial attacks, the Ministry of Defence said on Tuesday.
The ministry said the aircraft would operate ​only in a defensive role and would not conduct ​offensive strikes against the Iran-aligned Houthis, whose attacks ⁠Britain says threaten regional stability and risk disrupting energy supplies ​and trade routes.
"The continuing attacks from the Houthis on our ​ally Saudi Arabia are absolutely despicable. The targeting of the airport in Riyadh in particular shows the lengths the Houthis are going to escalate ​the situation in the region," defence minister Wes Streeting ​said in a statement.

"That’s why today I have approved further UK military ‌support. ⁠RAF Typhoons will fly defensive air missions to help protect Saudi airspace from drones and missiles."
The additional support follows a request from Saudi Arabia's government, which Prime Minister Andy Burnham said earlier ​this month ​Britain was prepared ⁠to consider.
Britain will also deploy an Atlas A400M transport aircraft and military advisers, expanding assistance announced ​in September , which included an RAF Voyager air-to-air ​refuelling ⁠aircraft but not fighter jets.
Houthi attacks against Saudi oil facilities and other infrastructure have intensified in recent weeks as the conflict in ⁠Yemen ​has escalated.

title: Alberta votes by large majority to remain part of Canada in boost for Carney
description: 76  of Albertans back the  remain  side versus 24  in favour of a binding vote on separation
content:
76% of Albertans back the 'remain' side versus 24% in favour of a binding vote on separation
Alberta residents voted by a large majority to remain part ‌of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on separation, handing Prime Minister Mark Carney a much-needed win as he attempts to unify the country amid a trade war with the US.
At 5:45am (1145 GMT) on Tuesday, with three-quarters of the votes counted, 76% of Albertans had backed the "remain" side versus 24% in favour of a binding vote on separation. The referendum ​was nonbinding.
"Albertans made a clear choice," Carney said in a statement. "They chose unity, to build together, and to take care of each other."
"Canada ​is greater than the sum of its parts," he said.
Pollsters and analysts had dismissed the possibility of a separatist ⁠victory in Monday's vote, citing data that showed only about one-third of residents in the western energy-producing province supported a future referendum on leaving.
Read: Carney campaigns against Alberta secession vote
Alberta ​Premier Danielle Smith, who announced the referendum in May, issued a statement saying she was "very pleased" that early results showed widespread support for remaining in Canada.
Smith ​said she would address Albertans at 6:45pm on Tuesday to discuss "where our province goes from here."
A small but vocal group of separatists has campaigned for months for an independent Alberta, arguing that the province's energy wealth was subsidising poorer parts of Canada and that it would be far richer freed from Ottawa bureaucracy.
Last week, Carney told a ​rally in Calgary that voting to leave Canada would be "a dangerous bluff that will lead to years of deep division".
Carney seeks to reduce Canada's ​dependence on us
There was no immediate reaction to the vote's outcome from President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly talked about the United States annexing Canada. US Treasury Secretary Scott ‌Bessent, ⁠discussing Alberta in January, said: "I think we should let them come down into the US."
Monday's vote was the second time in two weeks that Carney has had to face a separatist challenge. An independence-minded party won power in the predominantly French-speaking province of Quebec on October 5 but fell short of the majority needed to fulfil a vow to hold a vote on breaking with Canada.
Quebec held independence referendums in 1980 and 1995, both of which failed.
Read more: Four killed in fire at Canadian military base
Carney, who ​grew up mostly in Alberta, acknowledges ​Albertans have often felt slighted by ⁠Ottawa. He has noted his government fast-tracked a proposed new pipeline, with Alberta and the federal government as majority owners. And he has pointed to Alberta's critical role in helping Canada reduce its dependence on the US.
First Nations groups ​have also objected to the idea of an independent Alberta, as their land treaties with Ottawa predate the province's ​creation within Canada.
Alberta independence ⁠movement set to carry on
The result is unlikely to end the independence movement. Before the referendum, some separatist leaders said they would continue to pursue another vote even if most Albertans said they wanted to remain.
According to data released on October 16 by the pollster Angus Reid, 62% of Albertans believe "there will never ⁠be an ​end to the separatist movement".
The vote on Monday also included nine other nonbinding questions on proposed ​measures to strengthen the province's hand when dealing with Ottawa. These covered immigration, access to provincial services — such as education, social care and healthcare — and voter identification requirements.
Provisional results showed voters ​backed eight of the nine measures, but some with only small majorities.

title: Young Sheldon    director recalls    worst run in    with Iain Armitage on set
description: Alex Reid has revealed how a comment about the young actor   s performance led to a tense exchange on set
content:
Alex Reid has revealed how a comment about the young actor’s performance led to a tense exchange on set
Young Sheldon director Alex Reid has recalled his “worst run-in” with star Iain Armitage while working on the hit CBS sitcom, revealing how a comment about the young actor’s performance led to a tense exchange on set. The incident is detailed in entertainment journalist Jessica Radloff’s new book, Young Sheldon: The (Juicier-Than-Meemaw’s-Brisket) Inside Story of the Hit Comedy .
Reid, who directed 36 episodes of the The Big Bang Theory prequel, explained that the disagreement happened while they were filming a scene in which he believed Armitage might not have realised the camera was on him. The director approached the young actor and encouraged him to give the scene his full effort.
“Iain, you’re on camera, so you got to give it your all,” Reid recalled telling him.
However, Armitage interpreted the comment as criticism of his acting. According to Reid, the actor became upset because he believed the director was suggesting he had not been trying hard enough.
“He took that as ‘I’m not giving it my all?’” Reid recalled. He said Armitage was “pissed” and repeatedly insisted they do the scene again so he could demonstrate that he was giving it his all.
The disagreement did not last long. Once filming was over, Reid approached Armitage and apologised, acknowledging that he had chosen his words poorly. He explained that he had been trying to protect the young actor because he was unsure whether Armitage realised the camera was capturing his performance at that moment.
“That was a terrible choice of words on my part, and I apologize,” Reid recalled saying. “I was just trying to protect you because you were on camera, and I wasn’t sure if you knew it or not.”
Reid said the exchange ended on a positive note, with the pair making up before he asked Armitage to take a photograph with him beside the Young Sheldon plaque on the set.
The director also reflected on how Armitage sometimes struggled to communicate his feelings directly. He suggested that the actor would sometimes respond with a stream of words, impressions, accents and jokes rather than openly discussing what was bothering him.
The anecdote appears in Radloff’s oral history of Young Sheldon , which explores the cast’s relationships and the challenges of making the sitcom over seven seasons. The series ran from 2017 to 2024, following Sheldon Cooper’s childhood in Texas before the events of The Big Bang Theory .
Armitage began playing the younger version of Sheldon, originally portrayed by Jim Parsons, when he was eight years old. The role made him the central figure in a production that required him to balance demanding filming schedules with school and the challenges of growing up in the public eye.
The book also includes reflections from other cast members about the pressures Armitage faced as the show’s young lead. Annie Potts, who played his grandmother Connie Tucker, acknowledged that there were times when the actor could be difficult but emphasised the burden of carrying a television series at such a young age.
“Yes, sometimes he was difficult. But I’ve worked with grown-ups who were a lot worse,” Potts said, adding that she believed exhaustion and the expectations placed on him could contribute to his behaviour.
Armitage has also addressed claims about his conduct on set, describing the role as a major undertaking for an eight-year-old. He said he always did his best and was grateful to those who understood that children could make mistakes.
“It was a complete privilege to be on this show and play this character, but yes, it was a big undertaking for an 8-year-old,” he said.
Despite the occasional disagreements, the book presents a picture of a cast whose relationships often resembled those of a real family, with moments of tension alongside genuine affection. Reid’s recollection offers a more specific look at one of those moments and how a misunderstanding between a director and a young actor was resolved through an apology.

title: Urwa Hocane questions why Pakistani projects are compared with Netflix
description: Says local productions should be recognised for storytelling  creative identity rather than glamour  commercial appeal
content:
Says local productions should be recognised for storytelling, creative identity rather than glamour, commercial appeal
Actor Urwa Hocane has criticised the entertainment industry's tendency to measure local productions against Netflix, arguing that Pakistani projects should be recognised for their storytelling and creative identity rather than their resemblance to international streaming content.
Speaking in an interview , Hocane questioned the use of the phrase “Netflix quality” as a benchmark for success, saying local productions had their own strengths and did not need to be validated through comparisons with the global streaming platform. “When someone says a project is ‘Netflix quality’, I find it so lame. I think we are doing better than that,” she said.
The actor also questioned whether Netflix should continue to be treated as the industry's gold standard, arguing that the platform's reputation should not overshadow the work being produced locally. “It is just an app or a portal that came along and worked for a couple of years. I don't think they know what they are doing anymore,” she said.
For Hocane, the defining strength of Pakistani productions lies in their stories and the creative processes behind them, rather than their technical polish or glamorous presentation. She argued that the industry already had quality work to offer and should focus on developing its own creative identity.
“There is quality in what we are making and showing. Why do we need more Netflix, and why are we comparing ourselves to it anyway?” she said.
She added that storytelling should remain central to the way projects were developed, with commercial appeal and visual presentation serving to complement the narrative rather than overshadow it.
“The soul of our projects lies in the stories and in how we prioritise our work process. We are not all about the glamour,” Hocane said. “Later, we commercialise it and make it beautiful,” she added.
Ultimately, the actor returned to what she considered the most important element of any production: the story itself. “I think the simple thing is our stories,” she said.
Hocane began her career as a video jockey before establishing herself as an actor in Pakistani television and cinema. Her acting credits include Udaari , Mushk , Punjab Nahi Jaungi , Na Maloom Afraad and Rangreza .
She has also ventured into film production, producing Tich Button , a romantic comedy featuring Farhan Saeed, Iman Ali, Sonya Hussyn and Feroze Khan, which was released in 2022.
Her interest in the creative process has also surfaced in earlier interviews , in which she discussed the importance of scripts and her desire to contribute to storytelling both in front of and behind the camera.

title: Pamela Anderson says she    will not be told what beautiful is    as makeup free journey continues
description: The actress says she still enjoys occasional glamour  pairing mascara with Sonsie Basic Balm for everyday wear
content:
The actress says she still enjoys occasional glamour, pairing mascara with Sonsie Basic Balm for everyday wear
Pamela Anderson is standing by her personal definition of beauty, explaining that she refuses to let other people dictate how she should look as she continues her largely makeup free lifestyle.
In an interview with PEOPLE published on October 19, 2026, the The Last Showgirl actress described beauty as “so subjective” while discussing the latest launch from her beauty brand, Sonsie.
“When I think about beauty, I think of ancient beauty,” Anderson said, adding that modern perceptions are heavily influenced by what people are repeatedly shown. For her, beauty is not simply about looking attractive but about having an inner radiance.
“I will not be told what beautiful is,” she said. “I have my own version of beauty, and it’s ageless. And it’s not comparative to other people.”
Anderson’s approach to makeup gained widespread attention in 2023, when she appeared barefaced during Paris Fashion Week. The decision marked a personal shift after the death of her longtime makeup artist, Alexis Vogel, in 2019.
The actress previously explained that wearing makeup no longer felt right without Vogel, whom she described as the best. She also said that appearing without makeup brought a sense of freedom, allowing her outfits to take centre stage without feeling compelled to compete for attention.
Anderson has since spoken about how people have connected with her decision, saying the experience reinforces the idea that people should feel good enough as they are.
She also considers stepping away from conventional beauty expectations somewhat rebellious, particularly in an industry where stylists and glamour teams often shape public appearances.
However, her approach does not mean she has abandoned makeup entirely. Anderson still enjoys experimenting with different looks and occasionally adds glamour for public appearances. For everyday wear, she says mascara works well with Sonsie Basic Balm.
Her philosophy centres on personal choice rather than following trends, allowing her to decide when makeup feels right and when she prefers to go without it.
