title: Matthew McConaughey fuels 2028 presidential speculation with call for independent candidates
description: The Oscar winner previously considered running for Texas governor but decided he was not ready to enter politics
content:
The Oscar winner previously considered running for Texas governor but decided he was not ready to enter politics
Matthew McConaughey has reignited speculation about his political future after releasing a six minute video urging independent candidates to take a more prominent role in American elections.
In the video, published on Sunday ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, the Oscar winning actor argued that political independents should be taken seriously rather than dismissed as protest candidates or spoilers. He did not announce a campaign or endorse any candidate or party.
“Independent does not mean you’re middle of the road. Independent is the original road,” McConaughey said, presenting political independence as an alternative to the traditional Republican and Democratic divide.
According to The Telegraph , the actor also argued that independently elected representatives could influence a closely divided Congress by encouraging compromise and acting as a check on both major parties. He urged voters to examine candidates’ positions and decide whether they represented their beliefs.
The statement has prompted renewed discussion about a possible presidential run in 2028. Political commentators have interpreted the video as a potential indication of future ambitions, although McConaughey has neither confirmed nor ruled out such a move.
McConaughey previously considered running for governor of Texas in 2021 but ultimately decided against entering the race. In July 2024, he described himself as being on a “learning tour” while weighing a possible future in public office. He later said that a political campaign was a path he was choosing not to take at that moment.
The actor’s latest message has also drawn criticism. Some commentators and online users questioned whether independent candidates could divide votes and affect the balance of power in closely contested elections.
The debate comes amid growing identification with political independence in the United States. A Gallup poll found that 45% of Americans identified as independents in 2025, a record at the time.

content:
'Michael' became the first biographical film to surpass $1 billion at the worldwide box office
Jaafar Jackson has reflected on playing his late uncle Michael Jackson in the biopic Michael , which became the first biographical film to surpass $1 billion at the worldwide box office, according to Variety .
Speaking on the Awards Circuit podcast, the 30-year-old actor revealed that he had set the ambitious financial target two years before filming began.
“I was pretty emotional,” he said. “I know how proud Michael would be of that, because he was someone who wanted to break many records.”
Jackson spent around two years preparing for the role, studying his uncle’s songs, recordings, journals, rehearsals and performances. He also worked with acting coach Angela Gibbs and studied established acting techniques to develop his performance.
He explained that capturing Michael’s distinctive voice came before mastering his movements, while recreating the choreography for “Bad” proved particularly challenging.
The actor also discussed the film’s original third act, which reportedly included sensitive subject matter but was ultimately removed. He said the experience of filming unused scenes still helped him develop as an actor.
Regarding a possible sequel, Jackson said he had not received a confirmed production date, despite reports that filming could begin in late 2026 or early 2027.
“I haven’t been told anything concrete, but whatever decision is made, I’m more than ready to get back into it and excited for where that goes,” he said.
Jackson also recalled his family’s emotional response to the film, revealing that his father, Jermaine Jackson, watched it at the Berlin premiere before praising his portrayal of his late brother.
Reflecting on his responsibility to represent Michael, Jaafar added: “My job is to come prepared and deliver the best performance I can.”

title: China   s economic resilience offers lessons for turbulent world
description: Innovation  industrial upgrading  and expanding trade are sustaining growth  according to Q3 data
content:
Innovation, industrial upgrading and expanding trade are sustaining growth, according to Q3 data
China’s economy gathered pace in the third quarter of 2026, offering reassurance to a global economy grappling with geopolitical tensions, volatile energy markets and uncertainty over international trade.
Growth of 4.5% year-on-year between July and September, up from 4.3% in the preceding quarter, highlights the resilience of the world’s second-largest economy.
Gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 4.6% in the first nine months, generating economic output worth approximately 107.11 trillion yuan, or $15.94 trillion, according to data released by China’s National Bureau of Statistics on October 19.
The performance has kept China on track to meet its annual growth target, although sustaining momentum will depend on whether industrial expansion translates into stronger domestic consumption.
An important structural shift is underway as advanced manufacturing, robotics, artificial intelligence-related industries, digital services and green technologies increasingly supplement traditional sources of growth. These emerging sectors contributed more than 40% of economic growth during the first three quarters, according to the supplied data.
China’s economic performance came amid heightened international uncertainty, including geopolitical conflicts affecting energy markets and disruptions to global trade.
Industrial production increased by 5.3% in the first three quarters, while high-tech manufacturing grew by 14.3% and equipment manufacturing by 10.2%.
In September, industrial output rose by 5.5% year-on-year, while the services production index increased by 4.8%. Retail sales grew by 1.1%, and the surveyed urban unemployment rate edged down to 5.2%.
The expansion of emerging industries is particularly significant. Industrial robot output increased by 29.1% year-on-year in the first three quarters, lithium-ion battery production rose by 39.5%, and 3D printing equipment output surged by 62.5%.
Information transmission, software and information technology services expanded by 10.4%, while leasing and business services grew by 12.3%. Manufacturing accounted for 25.7% of GDP, up 0.6 percentage points from a year earlier.
Technological upgrading can improve productivity, reduce costs through automation, and strengthen industrial competitiveness. It can also modernise established industries, with ceramics manufacturers adopting 3D printing and coal mines deploying intelligent monitoring systems.
However, rising production does not automatically guarantee commercial success. Sustainable gains will depend on profitability, demand, continued innovation and businesses’ ability to compete without excessive reliance on state support or price competition.
Beijing’s fiscal and financial support measures will also need to encourage sustainable private-sector investment, employment and household spending.
China’s industrial expansion has considerable implications for international supply chains. Its factories produce machinery, batteries, electronic equipment and components used by manufacturers worldwide.
Goods trade reached 39.94 trillion yuan in the first three quarters, an increase of 18.8% year-on-year. Exports of mechanical and electrical products rose by 23.7%, accounting for 64.3% of total exports. Intermediate goods represented more than half of exports, underscoring China’s role as both a supplier of finished products and a source of industrial inputs.
Reliable Chinese production can help businesses maintain supplies and avoid delays. However, China’s manufacturing strength has also raised concerns among trading partners about industrial overcapacity, import competition and excessive dependence on a concentrated manufacturing base.
Supply-chain diversification is consequently becoming a strategic priority. Rather than ending commercial ties with China, businesses may seek additional production centres and alternative sources of critical components.
China is likely to remain influential in global manufacturing, but preserving its position will require technological advancement, predictable commercial conditions and deeper integration with international markets.
Trade by foreign-invested enterprises rose by 19% to 11.69 trillion yuan in the first nine months, according to the supplied data. Their intermediate-goods trade increased by 27.4%, while exports of high-tech products rose by 42.1%.
International companies are using China not only to reach its domestic consumers but also to access its suppliers, engineering capabilities and manufacturing networks for products intended for other markets.
German automobile manufacturer Volkswagen’s reported shift from an “in China, for China” approach towards “in China, beyond China” illustrates this trend. Meanwhile, Chinese robotics manufacturer EFORT Intelligent Robot reportedly recorded an increase of more than 50% in overseas revenue during the first half of the year.
Nevertheless, foreign investment decisions also depend on market access, regulatory transparency, intellectual property protection and geopolitical risks. China’s ability to attract sustained foreign capital will depend on whether the advantages of its industrial ecosystem outweigh these concerns.
Despite strong industrial production and external trade, domestic consumption remains central to China’s economic outlook. September retail sales growth of 1.1% was modest compared with industrial expansion.
Real per capita disposable income increased by 4.4% in the first three quarters, while rural household income rose by 5.6%. Total retail sales of consumer goods and services reportedly increased by 2.6% year-on-year.
Higher incomes do not necessarily translate into equivalent spending. Consumer confidence, employment prospects, housing-market conditions and precautionary saving all influence household decisions.
Stronger consumption would help China reduce its dependence on external demand while creating opportunities for foreign businesses seeking access to Chinese consumers.
Policymakers must therefore ensure that industrial upgrading translates into higher household incomes, employment and living standards. Without a more durable recovery in consumption, industrial expansion alone may not resolve underlying economic imbalances.
China’s economic transformation is closely linked to its energy transition. The penetration rate of new-energy vehicles reportedly remained above 60% for six consecutive months, while energy consumption per unit of GDP fell by 3.1% in the first three quarters.
China’s scale in battery manufacturing, electric vehicles and related technologies gives it considerable potential to influence the global transition towards lower-carbon production. For emerging economies, affordable clean-energy technologies could help reduce fuel-import bills and diversify energy supplies.
However, declining energy intensity does not necessarily mean total energy consumption or emissions have fallen. The environmental impact must also be assessed against China’s energy mix and overall emissions trajectory.
China’s imports reportedly grew by 22.3% in the first three quarters, outpacing export growth. The upcoming China International Import Expo is expected to attract more than 4,100 overseas companies, offering foreign businesses a platform to showcase products and services.
Sustained import growth could benefit agricultural producers, industrial suppliers and consumer-goods manufacturers abroad. Greater openness, transparent regulations and predictable market-access conditions would help convert the scale of China’s economy into broader gains for international trade.
China’s economic trajectory carries particular significance for Pakistan because of their close economic relationship, established trade links and cooperation under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).
China’s expansion in advanced manufacturing, robotics, batteries and digital services offers Pakistan opportunities to move beyond a relationship centred primarily on infrastructure development and imports. Cooperation could increasingly cover industrial technology, skills development, agricultural processing, renewable energy, logistics and export-oriented manufacturing.
Pakistan’s long-term interests would be better served by attracting productive investment, developing domestic supplier networks and enabling local businesses to participate in regional and international value chains.
Chinese companies seeking to diversify production could consider Pakistan as a manufacturing and export platform, provided commercial conditions are suitable. Realising this potential would require reliable energy supplies, competitive logistics, predictable regulation, access to finance and a skilled workforce.
Pakistan must also strengthen its industrial competitiveness as Chinese manufacturers move towards more sophisticated and automated production. Cooperation in renewable energy, electric mobility and digital technologies could address development needs, provided projects are commercially viable and supported by appropriate financing and technical capacity.
The central lesson is that China’s economic resilience can create opportunities for Pakistan, but these are not automatic. Pakistan must develop the domestic capabilities needed to turn trade and investment into employment, exports, technological advancement and sustainable growth.
China’s third-quarter performance highlights the importance of industrial depth, technological upgrading and policy flexibility in navigating an uncertain international environment. Advanced manufacturing, services and trade have helped sustain growth despite external pressures.
Yet the durability of this performance will depend on stronger household consumption, productive investment and a predictable environment for private and foreign businesses. Beijing must reconcile expanding productive capacity with the need for more balanced domestic demand.
For the wider world, China presents both opportunities and challenges. Its manufacturing capabilities can sustain supply chains and accelerate technological change, even as other economies diversify suppliers and protect domestic industries.
The central question is whether China can convert its industrial and technological advantages into a more balanced, productive, and sustainable economic model. The answer will shape not only its future development but also the opportunities and pressures confronting the global economy.

Oppenheim has previously directed documentaries including Some Kind of Heaven and Spermworld . Pattinson, meanwhile, has built a varied career following the Twilight franchise, working with filmmakers including David Cronenberg and Robert Eggers.

title: In damning report  judicial commission seeks JIT for Mir Raza probe  FIA led inquiry into police conduct
description: Report recommends formation of joint investigation team
content:
Finds police investigation an 'epic failure'; says trust deficit between police, society now 'nearly unrectifiable'
A single-member judicial commission of inquiry, constituted to probe the death of 25-year-old Mir Raza Ali, has recommended the formation of a Joint Investigation Team (JIT) led by Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) Irfan Baloch and comprising senior representatives of the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Intelligence Bureau (IB), Pakistan Rangers (Sindh) and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), as the only viable path to a credible resolution of a case it described as compromised by police failure.
The commission, headed by Sindh High Court Judge Justice Omar Sial, submitted its report to the Sindh chief minister on October 15. The Express Tribune has reviewed the executive summary of the findings.
Mir Raza Ali, an Institute of Business Administration graduate who ran a waffle-making business under the banner Wafflix, went missing from his PECHS residence in the early hours of July 28. His family registered FIR No 795/2026 at Ferozabad Police Station the same day under Section 365 (Kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine person) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) — kidnapping. His body was found the next morning within the jurisdiction of Gulistan-e-Johar Police Station. A post-mortem was conducted at Jinnah hospital, and the body was buried the same day.
Police initially opined the death to be a suicide. The family contested this, claiming the body bore visible torture marks. The commission records that the police surgeon, in early August, pointed out anomalies in the first post-mortem report — the very document police had relied upon for their suicide theory. The body was exhumed on August 8, initial findings were shared on August 8–9, and the final official report, issued around August 31, confirmed the cause of death as "a perforating firearm injury from the back, ruling out suicide".
Charges under Sections 302 PPC (murder) and 201 PPC (destruction of evidence) were subsequently added to the FIR.
Read: Judicial commission grills doctor over errors in Mir Raza's first post-mortem report, calls it 'criminal negligence'
The Sindh Home Department uploaded the report to its website.
Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Memon said the provincial government was "committed to transparency, accountability and ensuring that due process of law is upheld" as it released the report .
The commission 's findings are unambiguous: "The bullet trajectory, the unusual location of the wound for a self-inflicted injury, the absence of blood, the state of the body, the principles of medical jurisprudence, acid burns and the anaesthesia detected in the blood, all clearly excluded suicide as the cause of death. It was a murder."
In a scathing assessment, the commission found that the police investigation "failed in its most basic duty: to establish the truth," noting that the police hypothesis rested on "a few unconfirmed and unsubstantiated text messages, selective video footage obtained by SHO Adeel Afzaal," and a first post-mortem report by Dr Osama Shaikh that "did not itself conclude suicide".
The commission observed that even Dr Shaikh's second report contradicted his first.
The report describes the handling of the case as "a rudderless ship, not aware of its destination" and states that "an active cover-up in the initial stages of the investigation cannot be conclusively ruled out."
Among its observations: senior officers demonstrated "tunnel vision"; the police "doubled down on their initial suicide ruling rather than investigating further", driven by ego ; "dozens of police officers – authorised and unauthorised" handled evidence without documenting it; and the force ignored the commission's own recommendation to appoint a focal person for public briefings, allowing speculation to embarrass the government.
The summary details "overnight bureaucratic manoeuvring" around the special medical board. On August 6, following a court order under Section 176(2) of the CrPC, an eight-member board headed by Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed was notified. In the early hours of August 7, the Sindh Health Directorate unilaterally replaced it with a trimmed five-member board heavily featuring doctors from Hyderabad and Jamshoro.
Mir Raza's family formally rejected the modified board at the graveyard, postponing the exhumation. Following public pressure and a legal notice, the government restored the original board on August 8, and the exhumation was completed at 11am the same day.
The commission termed the manoeuvring "a highly irregular, inexplicable, legally flawed overreach dictated entirely from the upper echelons of the Sindh Health Secretariat, more specifically by the secretary and special secretary, health," adding that the DG health services "looked the other way" despite being aware he was not legally competent to form such a board.
"The two gentlemen who directed the change in the board could not give a cogent reason for the abrupt change," the report states.
Regarding the controversial August 9 meeting at the CM's House, attended by Dr Osama at the request of the Karachi Additional IG Police, the commission found "no evidence has emerged" that it was convened to pressure the doctor, and that "no adverse inference can be drawn from the briefing itself".
However, it noted it "would have been prudent to invite the police surgeon to the meeting as well, which was not done". It further observed that Dr Osama "continued attempting to make the CM House controversial," as part of efforts to "defame and malign the police surgeon".
Read more: Mir Raza case: Commission says Dr Usama targeted Dr Summaiya with smear campaign
Pegged on its findings, the commission's key recommendations are:
First, acknowledging that the case has reached "a critical juncture," the commission warned that due to "a severe breakdown in trust, even an accurate conclusion or the apprehension of the true culprit is unlikely to be accepted by the public," a divide that "now appears nearly unrectifiable".
Because "a significant portion of physical evidence has been compromised", the case "can now only be resolved through a rigorous, intelligence-based investigation".
The police, it said, "must transparently acknowledge and apologise for past operational lapses , while immediately initiating formal inquiries against the responsible officers".
To accommodate the family's request, a joint investigation team under DIG Irfan Baloch should strategically integrate ISI, IB, Rangers (Sindh), and NCCIA representatives — "This extreme step is necessary to restore public trust and end speculation."
Second, noting the commission lacks investigative powers and therefore cannot conclusively determine whether an active cover-up occurred — though "certain inexplicable actions are difficult to justify and raise the possibility that one may have occurred at some stage" — a high-level committee, preferably led by the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), should inquire whether police officials involved in the first ten days of the probe breached Sections 201 (Causing disappearance of evidence of offence, or giving false information to screen offender), 166 (Public servant disobeying law, with intent to cause injury to any person) clause (2) and 218 (Public servant framing incorrect record or writing with intent to save person from punishment or property from forfeiture) of the PPC .
"The committee should initiate criminal action, in addition to disciplinary proceedings, against those it finds culpable."
The commission began work on August 27, recording statements through October 7 across 20 open sessions, including testimony from 50 witnesses, and conducted a comprehensive site inspection of the crime scene and adjoining areas on October 5. All sessions were held in public "to ensure transparency and reduce public speculation". Detailed observations on accountability are contained in the response to TOR 3 (page 52) and recommendations in the response to TOR 4 (page 58) of the main report.
The report was earlier presented to the cabinet in seven separate envelopes at a meeting chaired by Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah at the CM House in Karachi, according to a spokesperson.
The chief minister constituted a subcommittee comprising Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar, Nasir Hussain Shah, Saeed Ghani and the advocate general to oversee the implementation of the report’s recommendations.
Also Read: Mir Raza commission submits report to govt
The cabinet also approved a $150 million World Bank-supported programme to reform Sindh’s property tax system, aimed at improving revenue collection and strengthening the financial management of local government institutions.
Under the Sindh Property Revenue Enhancement Programme, the government has set a target of increasing property tax collection across Karachi’s 25 town municipal corporations (TMCs) from Rs2.3 billion to Rs25.5b.
According to a briefing to the cabinet, the World Bank will provide $110m for the Programme-for-Results component and $40m for investment projects. The Sindh government will contribute an additional 20% of the amount linked to the Programme-for-Results component as its share.
The programme also envisages modernising property tax collection in other urban local councils and strengthening the institutional capacity of 45 selected local councils.
Read More: Govt contests World Bank poverty report
Parallelly, the cabinet approved the introduction of an Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS) in local government institutions to improve financial management and administrative performance.
The package includes agreements on financing and implementation, a framework for assessing results, verification procedures, and environmental and social safeguards. It was submitted to the cabinet for post-facto approval, according to the CM’s spokesperson.
The World Bank’s board is expected to consider the programme package on October 30.

title: Rapper Blueface reportedly detained during California police response to gunman report
description: The incident reportedly took place at a Yard House restaurant  where deputies encountered a chaotic scene
content:
The incident reportedly took place at a Yard House restaurant, where deputies encountered a chaotic scene
Rapper Blueface was reportedly detained during a police response to reports of an armed man at a restaurant in Santa Clarita, California, on Monday night, October 19.
Los Angeles County sheriff’s deputies attended the 24200 block of Magic Mountain Parkway after receiving an emergency call about a person allegedly carrying a gun at a local business.
The incident reportedly took place at a Yard House restaurant, where deputies encountered a chaotic scene.
The Santa Clarita Valley Sheriff’s Station said one person refused to follow officers’ commands as they attempted to secure the area.
A sheriff’s watch commander told KTLA that an individual was detained on suspicion of misdemeanor delaying or obstructing officers in the performance of their duties.
Following an investigation, deputies determined there was no armed man at the location.
Blueface, whose real name is Johnathan Porter, was reportedly livestreaming on Kick when the police response unfolded.
Local entertainment outlet What’s Up SCV identified the rapper as someone allegedly detained during the incident.
The outlet also claimed on Instagram that a weapon had reportedly been brandished and several people had been arrested.
However, authorities have not confirmed those claims, and the sheriff’s watch commander could not verify whether Blueface was the person detained.
It remains unclear what prompted the initial gunman report or whether the individual detained will face criminal charges. Authorities have not released further details.
Blueface rose to prominence in 2018 with his distinctive rapping style. His hit single “Thotiana” reached No. 8 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2019, followed by his debut studio album, Find the Beat , in 2020.

title: Elizabeth Holmes expos      Bad Blood    returns to bestseller lists after Nathan Fielder documentary
description: John Carreyrou   s 2018 book spent more than 100 weeks across The New York Times bestseller lists
content:
John Carreyrou’s 2018 book spent more than 100 weeks across The New York Times bestseller lists
John Carreyrou’s Bad Blood: Secrets and Lies in a Silicon Valley Startup has returned to Amazon’s bestseller charts following the release of You Can See Everything , a documentary about disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes.
The 2018 book ranked No. 1 in three Amazon categories, biomedical engineering, business infrastructure and venture capital, according to Variety . It also reached No. 3,048 among all books listed by the retailer, reflecting renewed interest in the story behind one of Silicon Valley’s most notorious corporate scandals.
Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, You Can See Everything opened in cinemas nationwide on October 16, according to the report. The nearly three hour A24 documentary follows Holmes, her partner Billy Evans and their two children during the final weeks before she reported to federal prison in May 2023.
Carreyrou, a former The Wall Street Journal reporter, helped expose serious problems with Theranos’ blood testing technology through his reporting in 2015. His book examines how Holmes presented the company as a medical technology breakthrough, claiming its devices could conduct hundreds of tests using only a few drops of blood.
The technology failed to deliver as promised, and Theranos dissolved in 2018. The company had once been valued at approximately $9 billion, but its collapse became a defining cautionary tale about Silicon Valley investment and corporate accountability.
Bad Blood became a No. 1 bestseller after publication and spent more than 100 weeks on The New York Times bestseller lists. Carreyrou has also praised Fielder and Oppenheim’s documentary, with the report noting his view that their approach deserves Oscar recognition.
Holmes was convicted in 2022 of four counts of wire fraud and conspiracy connected to Theranos. She was sentenced to more than 11 years in prison and has continued to maintain her innocence.
The renewed attention highlights how the Theranos story continues to attract audiences through investigative journalism and documentary filmmaking, years after the company’s collapse.

title: Xbox manager deletes X account after saying developers who reject AI should leave industry
description: Xbox manager Brandon Stirrup deactivated his X account after defending AI use in game development
content:
Xbox manager Brandon Stirrup deactivated his X account after defending AI use in game development
Xbox senior business strategy manager Brandon Stirrup has deleted his X account less than 24 hours after defending the use of artificial intelligence in game development and saying developers who reject the technology should not be in the business.
Stirrup posted a series of messages on October 18, claiming that AI could make game development accessible to anyone.
According to PC Gamer, an Xbox source said he deactivated his account because of the volume of replies he was receiving.
Stirrup began his thread by explaining that he had used AI to create what he described as a “bad but improvable game” over two days, although he had actively worked on it for around three hours.
“I'm telling you I tried it and it's true…anyone can build a game,” he wrote.
He subsequently criticised developers and studios that were not incorporating AI into their strategies, describing their approach as “planning for a fake future”.
Stirrup also acknowledged the potential consequences of speaking publicly about the issue, writing, “Look if I'm fired tomorrow it will be because I told you the truth that nobody wants you to know.”
He added that Xbox was already using AI and argued that the company should be open about its adoption of the technology.
“I'm happy to take the hit if it means hundreds at Xbox can stop pretending that they're not using AI. It's time to accept and move forward,” he wrote.
In another post, Stirrup stated, “If you're a game designer refusing to believe that AI has a place in your future, you should not be in the business of being a business.”
AI adoption has become an increasingly prominent topic across the gaming industry. Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney recently discussed reorganising developers to accelerate AI use, while Xbox has introduced its Xbox Labs programme to explore emerging technologies.
Stirrup has also previously encouraged employees affected by Xbox layoffs to use Microsoft's Copilot to organise their performance reviews into structured records of their skills and accomplishments.
His X account deactivation followed the reaction to his comments, although available information does not indicate that his employment status has changed.

K/DA’s new song Firestarter surpasses 3m YouTube views within six hours of release, as fans celebrate comeback
K/DA has returned with its new song ‘Firestarter’, with fans celebrating the virtual League of Legends girl group’s comeback after a six-year wait. The music video surpassed three million YouTube views within six hours of its release on October 19.
The virtual K-pop group features League of Legends characters voiced by real-world singers. K/DA originally teamed up with I-dle members Miyeon and Soyeon, Madison Beer and Jaira Burns for its debut single, ‘Pop/Stars’, which has accumulated more than 668 million YouTube views.

Miyeon and Soyeon reprise their roles as the voices of Ahri and Akali, respectively, while Sophie Powers and Mimi Webb join the group as the voices of Evelynn and Kai’Sa.
The ‘Firestarter’ music video was produced in collaboration with Fortiche, the animation studio known for its work on the League of Legends series Arcane and K/DA’s original ‘Pop/Stars’ video.
Fans have praised the comeback, highlighting the animation and vocal performances. “They really said, ‘here’s the company card, impress them’. K/DA, you are worth ALL THE waiting,” one commenter wrote.

title: Disney reportedly in talks with Bungie and DICE for new Star Wars  Battlefront game
description: Disney is reportedly discussing new Star Wars  Battlefront game with DICE and Bungie  according to Jeff Grubb
content:
Disney is reportedly discussing new Star Wars: Battlefront game with DICE and Bungie, according to Jeff Grubb
Disney is reportedly in talks with DICE and Bungie about developing a new Star Wars: Battlefront game, potentially paving the way for a third instalment in the modern series.
Gaming insider Jeff Grubb shared the information in a recent Giant Bomb YouTube video , reporting that both studios have shown interest in working on the project. However, the game has not entered development, and no developer has been confirmed.
DICE developed the two games in the rebooted Battlefront series, released in 2015 and 2017. Although the studio subsequently moved on to other projects, it could return to the franchise nearly a decade after the release of Star Wars: Battlefront 2.
Disney and Lucasfilm have reportedly been searching for a development partner for some time, with few studios willing to take on the project.
According to Grubb, DICE appears to have the first opportunity to accept the work, with Bungie potentially stepping in if the EA-owned studio declines.
Bungie is known for developing science-fiction shooters, including Halo and Destiny. The studio has also worked on Marathon, an extraction shooter that has struggled commercially. Bungie has faced internal challenges in recent years, including staff layoffs and complaints about toxicity within its leadership.
Despite its recent difficulties, Bungie's experience with first-person shooters could make it a potential candidate for the franchise. However, its established approach to weapons and combat would need to accommodate the Star Wars setting.
A third modern Battlefront game has remained elusive since the release of Battlefront 2. An earlier project intended to continue the original series was cancelled, while DICE eventually moved on from the franchise.
With discussions reportedly ongoing, a new Battlefront game remains a possibility rather than a confirmed project. If development moves forward, the next instalment could still be several years away.

title: Vaneeza Ahmed urges women to read Nikahnamas  know their rights before marriage
description: Former model recalls overlooking her own Nikahnama until her divorce  warns provisions can be removed from document
content:
Former model recalls overlooking her own Nikahnama until her divorce, warns provisions can be removed from document
Former model Vaneeza Ahmed has urged women to read their Nikahnamas carefully before marriage, warning that many remain unaware of the rights and provisions included in the Islamic marriage contract until problems arise.
Speaking on Vasay Chaudhry’s show, Ahmed admitted that despite considering herself well-educated, she had not read her own Nikahnama until she was going through a divorce. “We don't read our marriage papers, even including myself, who I consider very educated. Even I did not read them until it was time for my divorce,” she said.
The actor stressed that women should not feel embarrassed about asking questions or discussing the terms of their marriage contracts. She urged parents, particularly mothers and fathers, to encourage their daughters to understand the document and the provisions that could help protect their rights if difficulties arose during the marriage.
“Every woman, mom, and father should not be embarrassed. Those clauses should be read by the daughter because they are in her benefit and rights, in the case that if some problem occurs, she gets her rights,” she said.
She also raised concerns about provisions being removed from Nikahnamas, urging families to examine the documents carefully rather than treating them as a formality. “There are many instances where men cut things out of the marriage papers,” she added.
Ahmed further highlighted financial provisions that people might overlook, including what she described as an entitlement to pocket money under the marriage contract. She encouraged both women and men to familiarise themselves with the clauses.
“Do you guys know that it is written in the marriage papers that we get pocket money? Nobody does. I say to every woman and sister, even every male: dad, or brother to check this out,” she said.
Acknowledging that marriage was often regarded as a matter of destiny in South Asian households, Ahmed argued that this belief should not discourage families from taking practical steps to safeguard women's interests.
“Yes mom’s are right that where you will get married is written in your destiny but we can also prepare for one’s benefit. I tell everyone, do not be ashamed to ask,” she said.
Her latest remarks echoed concerns she had previously raised about women's rights and marriage customs in Pakistan.
In 2023 , Ahmed spoke about the importance of understanding the terms of the nikkahnama in connection with the drama Kuch Ankahi , which featured a storyline encouraging women to reconsider the clauses in their marriage contracts.
She also discussed how women were often discouraged from asserting their rights and recalled her own experience with haq mehr , the dower agreed upon in an Islamic marriage contract. Her comments highlighted how social expectations could prevent women from questioning terms that directly affected their interests.
Ahmed rose to prominence as one of Pakistan's leading supermodels before establishing herself in television and film.
Her acting credits include the film Jinnah (1998), in which she played Dina Jinnah, and television dramas such as Ehd-e-Wafa (2019) and Kuch Ankahi (2023). In the latter, she played Sofia Agha, whose storyline touched on women's rights and social expectations.
In 2026, Ahmed has also featured in coverage of the drama Tum Larkay Bhi Na , in which she plays Nazish.

title: Louvre s  100m crown jewels still missing one year after daring heist
description: Thieves disguised as workmen sliced their way into the museum with industrial disc cutters on October 19 last year
content:
Thieves disguised as workmen sliced their way into the museum with industrial disc-cutters on October 19 last year
One year after a stunning break-in at the Louvre Museum, the four main suspects are in jail awaiting trial, but police appear to have run out of leads to locate the stolen crown jewels.
Thieves disguised as workmen sliced their way into the museum with industrial disc-cutters on October 19 last year before making off with eight irreplaceable items worth an estimated $100 million.
They include a brooch and crown from Napoleon III's wife Eugenie. President Emmanuel Macron referred to the robbery as an attack on France's history.
Experts from law enforcement and private art theft agencies who spoke to AFP believe the best chance of recovering the treasures is if the thieves acted alone and stashed their loot somewhere in the Paris region.
"There was a short period of time where they may have hidden them in a wall or buried them," Christopher Marinello from Art Recovery International, a private agency, told AFP .
All four men were arrested within 10 days of the heist.
The last known sighting of the glittering 19th-century gems was on CCTV footage recorded in an underground lock-up in the gritty Aubervilliers suburb of northern Paris, where all the suspects live.
Extensive searches directed by the 100-strong investigation team have been carried out at their homes and families' homes, in cellars, garages and attics – all to no avail.
If the jewels have been hidden or handed to a "fence" for safekeeping, there is still a chance that one of the suspects confesses in exchange for a more lenient sentence, said renowned Dutch private art detective Arthur Brand.
"The French police are very professional, they know how to interrogate, they know how to put pressure on (someone)," he told AFP . "You only need one to talk, and in many cases, one talks."
The more worrying scenario is that the gang was acting on orders from a ringleader or middleman with links to organised crime – to whom they handed the jewels once they had finished their smash-and-grab.
"The power of organised crime is not only to bring the experience to commit a crime, but also to have people to take the objects and sell them," said Corrado Catesi, head of the stolen art unit at international police body Interpol.
In custody, two of the suspects have claimed a ringleader was part of their team, which is being treated with scepticism by investigators, a source close to the case told AFP recently.
The worst-case scenario is that the jewels were transported either out of France or to a local contact in the underground precious stones business.
"It's mainly diamonds, so they have to dismantle them, recut them and sell them. If they would go to one place, it would be Antwerp," said Brand, referring to the Belgian diamond hub.
Marinello lists Tel Aviv and India as other possible destinations.
Tobias Kormind, managing director of 77 Diamonds, Europe's largest online diamond jeweller, told AFP that "once recut, re-entering the legitimate supply chain to be bought by wholesalers or retailers is fairly straightforward".
"Unless a stone possessed ultra-distinctive internal inclusions, even top diamond laboratories like the GIA would struggle to flag a freshly polished diamond as stolen property," he said.
The Louvre heist: Security flaws and deeper cracks at France’s top museum
But if the jewels fell into the hands of an organised crime group, there appears to be still some grounds for hope.
Brand referred to several cases where stolen jewels were recovered, notably after a raid on the TEFAF art fair in the Netherlands in 2022 or the break-in at the Gruenes Gewoelbe museum in Dresden, Germany, in 2019.
"Although we all think that most of the gold, silver and diamonds that get stolen, we never see them back, in some cases, we do," he explained.
"There is still a chance that we will see the Louvre jewels again and it might be that somebody talks before the court case."
The jewels remain listed as missing in Interpol's database of stolen artworks.
Analysis of investigations around the world reveals that objects "can take from three months to 40 years to be recovered", Catesi told AFP .

title: Pakistan has one expectation from Taliban regime  no use of Afghan soil for terrorism  says FM Dar at SCO
description: Says sustainable economic development can not be guaranteed without durable peace  security in region
content:
Says sustainable economic development can not be guaranteed without durable peace, security in region
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister (FM) Ishaq Dar on Tuesday said that Pakistan had "only one expectation from the Afghan Taliban regime: that Afghan territory must not be used for terrorism against Pakistan or any other country."
"Pakistan continues to be desirous of a peaceful, stable, regionally-integrated and prosperous Afghanistan which is at peace with itself and all its neighbours. We have made sincere efforts to support Afghanistan's development and the well-being of its people. In return, Pakistan has only one expectation from the Afghan Taliban regime: that the Afghan territory must not be used for terrorism against Pakistan or any other country," FM Dar said during the narrow-format session of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Council of Heads of Government (CHG) meeting in Dushanbe, Tajikistan.
The foreign minister stated that sustainable economic development could not be guaranteed without durable peace and security in the region, noting that "ensuring stability in Afghanistan is imperative for safeguarding peace and stability of our region."
"Pakistan remains committed to a peaceful and stable neighbourhood," he said, describing this as "an essential foundation for regional development and prosperity."
Regarding the SCO, FM Dar stated that over the past 25 years, the organisation had "remained anchored in the SCO Spirit of mutual trust and respect for diversity." He added that the SCO had also "expanded its mandate to encompass trade, infrastructure, culture and innovation."
"Pakistan's journey within the SCO highlights its commitment to the Shanghai Spirit," he stated.
FM Dar recalled that Pakistan hosted the Council of Heads of Government meeting in Islamabad in 2024, adding that Islamabad had also successfully concluded its chairmanship of the SCO Anti-Terrorism Structure this year and, as chair of the SCO Working Group on Poverty Alleviation, shared its experiences and learned from those of others.
"This year, we intend to highlight the role of small and medium enterprises in reducing poverty," he said.
Read: Dar warns Afghan Taliban of terrorism costs
He said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had unveiled Pakistan's vision for its SCO chairmanship under the theme "Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation and Shared Prosperity." He noted that the priority areas identified by Pakistan were peace, security and mutual trust; regional connectivity and trade; innovation, artificial intelligence and digital transformation; climate resilience and sustainable energy; and people-to-people exchanges.
FM Dar highlights targeted investments for 'seamless economic integration'
"For the region to achieve seamless economic integration, targeted investments in core sectors, most notably energy and transport, are vital," he added.
He also noted that in parallel, Pakistan "strongly advocates for expanding investments into high-potential industries including agriculture, mining, minerals and information technology to build a resilient and interconnected economic future for all our nations."
"We firmly believe that strategic investment in transport and energy infrastructure is not merely beneficial; it is absolutely imperative for true regional economic integration," he said.
He also noted that the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor offered "every SCO partner a compelling opportunity to participate in and accelerate our shared journey towards comprehensive economic integration."
FM Dar added that Pakistan also believed that "artificial intelligence, digital transformation, innovation, energy cooperation and international information security should become important pillars of future cooperation within the SCO."
The foreign minister reiterated the need to accelerate efforts to "promote the use of national currencies for mutual settlement," highlighting the establishment of an SCO Development Bank, an SCO Development Fund and an investment fund. "Such tools are measures which will advance developmental initiatives and help the SCO region offset international financial shocks," he said.
Read More: DPM Dar reiterates need to eliminate terrorist threat from Afghanistan at ECO meeting
Further, FM Dar stated, "Protections, policies and unilateral coercive measures contradict the principles of international law." He added that they "suppress economic growth, block technological progress and increase inequality," noting that therefore, "reform of the global financial architecture and trade regimes is essential for achieving equitable global development."
Concluding his address, the foreign minister congratulated the government of Tajikistan, the heads of the SCO's permanent bodies, the secretary general and the director of the SCO Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) "on the successful completion of this year's Council of Heads of Government meeting this year."
He also commended the national coordinators and experts working through various SCO mechanisms, who helped finalise the documents and decisions that "will hopefully be adopted today."
FM Dar added, "The joint communique and statements are reflective of our joint aspirations and commitments."
"The fundamental strength of SCO is anchored not only in our deeply intertwined histories, but more importantly, in the resilient, safe future that we collectively choose to forge," FM Dar said. He added that Pakistan stood "resolute in its commitment to serve as an active architect of this shared destiny and to shape the next decade of Eurasian connectivity and economic prosperity."
The foreign minister also extended heartfelt congratulations to the president of Uzbekistan on taking over the chair of the SCO Council of Heads of Government for 2026-27, saying "Pakistan looks forward to warmly welcoming in Islamabad the heads of state of the SCO family and their delegations for the Council of Heads of State summit in August next year."

title: Clannad  and  Angel Beats  creator Jun Maeda prioritises work over treatment after cancer diagnosis
description: Jun Maeda has chosen palliative care following throat cancer diagnosis to focus on completing his creative projects
content:
Jun Maeda has chosen palliative care following throat cancer diagnosis to focus on completing his creative projects
Jun Maeda, the creator behind Clannad and Angel Beats, has been diagnosed with throat cancer and chosen to focus on palliative care rather than active treatment, according to a statement from Visual Arts.
The company confirmed on October 19 that Maeda is hospitalised following his diagnosis. He began experiencing throat discomfort in early spring, with swelling and pain becoming more pronounced over the summer, prompting further medical examinations.
“After careful consideration of his condition and the outlook for treatment, Maeda has chosen not to pursue active treatment and instead to focus on palliative care, wishing to conserve his strength and devote himself to his creative work,” Visual Arts said.
Despite his condition, Maeda remains focused on completing projects for fans. He has finished his assigned writing for the main story of Heaven Burns Red through the first half of Chapter 6, as well as the major story elements leading to the chapter’s conclusion.
He has also completed the lyrics and composition for songs featured in the first half of the chapter. However, Visual Arts warned that the progression of his illness could prevent him from contributing to other story scenarios and songs.
Maeda, who also worked as a planner and writer on Angel Beats and composed music for the anime, had been developing an original music project intended to release new songs on YouTube over an extended period.
His diagnosis has prompted him to accelerate those plans so he can complete the music currently in development and share it with listeners.
“He felt that there was little time remaining in which he would be able to continue creating,” the company said.
Visual Arts added that Maeda remains determined to continue his creative work despite being hospitalised.
“Maeda is currently hospitalized, but even under these circumstances, he remains strongly determined to devote himself to creative work through to the very end,” the statement said.
Fans can send messages of encouragement using the email address provided in Visual Arts’ official English statement. The company has also supplied a postal address for letters, while asking supporters not to send gifts.

title: Christina Applegate returns to    MeSsy    podcast after hospitalisation  reveals MS misdiagnosis
description: Applegate was originally diagnosed with MS in 2021 and has since spoken openly about her health challenges
content:
Applegate was originally diagnosed with MS in 2021 and has since spoken openly about her health challenges
Christina Applegate has returned to her MeSsy podcast after a seven-month absence, revealing an emotional and unexpected update about her health. The Dead to Me actress, 54, disclosed that doctors recently told her she does not have multiple sclerosis (MS), despite having lived with the diagnosis since 2021.
Applegate shared the news during a new episode of the podcast, which she co-hosts with fellow actress Jamie-Lynn Sigler. The pair released back-to-back episodes on Tuesday, October 20, with Applegate opening up about the medical revelation and the emotional impact of discovering that her diagnosis may have been incorrect.
“She came into my room and said, ‘Congratulations, you don’t have MS,’” Applegate recalled through tears. She explained that she did not experience the relief others might have expected, as the news left her struggling to understand what had happened to her health over the past five years.
The actress stressed that the change in diagnosis has not improved her physical condition. Despite being told she does not have MS, she continues to experience debilitating symptoms and requires a wheelchair to attend medical appointments.
“You don’t get misdiagnosed and then all of a sudden I’m better,” Applegate told Sigler. “I haven’t gotten better, Jamie! If anything, I’ve gotten worse.” She added that she was back at square one as her doctors investigate what has been causing her symptoms since 2021.
In a subsequent episode, Applegate described the emotional toll of the news, revealing that she had experienced a deep depression while processing the revelation. She also expressed uncertainty about her identity within the multiple sclerosis community, where she had spent years sharing her experiences and supporting others living with the condition.
The actress said she felt as though she had let people down after becoming a prominent voice for those affected by MS. Her diagnosis had given her a framework for understanding her daily struggles, she explained, making the sudden change particularly difficult to process.
“I had a reason. I had a f---ing reason as to why my day sucked every day,” she said. “And now I don’t have a reason and it’s very unnerving and it’s very confusing for me.”
Applegate was originally diagnosed with MS in 2021 and has since spoken openly about her health challenges through interviews, social media and her podcast. She and Sigler created MeSsy to discuss their experiences navigating life with the condition, offering candid conversations about the physical and emotional difficulties associated with their diagnoses.
The pair announced a temporary break from the podcast on March 31, 2026. Applegate was subsequently reported to have been hospitalised in Los Angeles in late March, remaining under medical care for several months. Her representative declined to discuss the details of her treatment at the time, citing her long history of complicated medical conditions.
In April, Applegate thanked fans for their support, saying she was focusing on her health. She returned home in August following her lengthy hospital stay, according to reports.
Despite the new information about her diagnosis, Applegate's health difficulties remain unresolved. She described her situation as “the same game with a different name”, reflecting the uncertainty surrounding her symptoms and the further medical investigations ahead.
The actress, known for Married... with Children , Anchorman and Dead to Me , has continued to speak candidly about her health in recent years. Her latest podcast appearance marks a significant new chapter in that journey, as she and her doctors work to establish what has been happening since her original diagnosis.

title: Eman helps Strikers keep unbeaten run in T20
description: Muneeba hits 63 in Conquerors    victory over Challengers
content:
Muneeba hits 63 in Conquerors’ victory over Challengers
Eman Naseer and Muneeba Ali struck solid fifties to guide Strikers and Conquerors to three-wicket victories respectively in the National Women’s T20 Tournament 2026-27 in Faisalabad on Tuesday.
Eman’s unbeaten run of form helped Strikers maintain their unbeaten record as they chased down 133 against Stars with one ball to spare in the 16th fixture at Bohranwali Ground.
Batting first, Stars posted 132-6 in their allotted 20 overs, with Sadaf Shamas top-scoring with 50 runs. Tania Saeed, Fatima Sana and Syeda Masooma Zehra claimed two wickets apiece.
In reply, Strikers achieved the target a ball to spare after losing seven wickets in the process, thanks largely to Eman’s 51 off 49 balls. The right-hander struck eight fours and a six to anchor the chase under pressure.
Hafsa Khalid and Momina Riasat took two wickets each. Eman was named player of the match for her decisive contribution.
Earlier, Conquerors defeated Challengers by three wickets at Jawad Club, also in Faisalabad, after successfully chasing a target of 128.
Challengers made 127-6 in 20 overs, powered by Ayesha Zafar’s 75. Humna Bilal led the Conquerors attack with three wickets for 27 runs, while Mahnoor claimed two for nine.
Conquerors completed the chase in 19.2 overs as captain Muneeba Ali led from the front with 63 off 44 deliveries, including nine fours. Gull Rukh provided valuable support with 36 runs.
Quratulain and Fatima Khan took two wickets each for Challengers, but Muneeba’s innings proved decisive. The Conquerors captain was named player of the match.

title: Diomande starting to shine as Leipzig visit
description: Ivory Coast national scores his first goal for Los Blancos against Sevilla
content:
Ivory Coast national scores his first goal for Los Blancos against Sevilla
When Real Madrid splashed a club record 140 million euros ($157m) to sign Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig this summer, it was because of his clear potential to become one of the game's stars, as showcased at the 2026 World Cup.
That talent has begun to unveil itself in recent matches, with Diomande lashing in a spectacular strike against Sevilla on Sunday in La Liga ahead of a reencounter with his former side Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday.
Diomande's sheer potential was not, however, the only reason Madrid forked out.
President Florentino Perez pledged to fans during his campaign for reelection in June that he would pay a fee of that magnitude for a new star as Madrid tried to rebuild following two seasons without a major trophy.
Diomande had demonstrated exciting promise, shining with Leipzig during just one season in Germany after emerging at Spanish side Leganes.
The 19-year-old did not join Madrid to fill an obvious vacancy, with his arrival actually exacerbating an overbooking in attack.
On the same day Diomande's transfer was announced, Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior signed a new deal until 2032 with Los Blancos.
Madrid struggled last season to find a balance with Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius on the pitch together, let alone throwing a new attacking star carrying a record price tag into the mix.
For a combination of those factors, it should not come as a surprise that Diomande is still finding his footing in the Spanish capital.
The youngster has shown flashes of his great quality, without yet firmly establishing himself as an essential figure for coach Jose Mourinho, although he is improving.
Diomande scored his first goal for the club against Villarreal on October 10, securing Real Madrid a 1-0 win.
The winger's superb finish was not the main talking point though, after Vinicius was dismissed later in the game and subsequently banned for four matches.
That further opened the door for Diomande to settle in, with the winger starting on the left wing in Sunday's 4-1 rout of Sevilla, in which he lashed home from long range in the final stages.
Diomande also assisted the opener for Arda Guler, in his best performance for the club thus far. In total he has two goals and three assists in 11 appearances across all competitions.
"He has a lot to improve, he's young, he's still naive, he's still not the finished article," said Mourinho on Sunday.
"At Real Madrid, the demands are very high... but he had a great game, he's growing."
Diamonds form under pressure, and thus far in his career Diomande has handled it on and off the pitch.
He suffered rejection after leaving the Ivory Coast to go to school in Florida in the United States, unable to reach a deal with MLS sides Charlotte FC and Colorado Rapids.
Eventually the winger's senior debut came with Leganes against Real Madrid in March 2025, and in 10 games for the club he netted twice, earning himself a move to Germany.
Diomande helped Leipzig reach the Champions League with 12 goals and eight assists, and he was named "rookie of the year" in the Bundesliga, before his Madrid move.
The winger said he is spurred on by tragedy from his life. His sister Roxane died at age 15 in 2025 after her drink was spiked, Diomande explained in an open letter, published by The Player's Tribune in June.
"You were the one who always believed that I could be the next Cristiano (Ronaldo), when everybody else laughed," wrote Diomande to his late sister.
"You were telling everybody, 'My brother is going to be the greatest in the world'. I will prove that you were right, or I will die trying."
At the home of the record 15-time European champions, Diomande has the platform to do that.
"He has to improve his finishing... assist better... but that will come," added Mourinho.
"I remember when Vinicius arrived (and struggled), and in two or three years Vinicius was a top drawer player."
Vinicius is not suspended in Europe put Diomande will be hoping Mourinho gives him another chance to shine against his former side Leipzig on Wednesday, as Madrid aim for a third win from three Champions League games.

title: Govt calls on all political parties to unite  forge consensus against terrorism and set aside differences
description: Sanaullah says terrorism is a national issue  if all parties reach an agreement PM is ready to resolve it
content:
Sanaullah says terrorism is a national issue, if all parties reach an agreement PM is ready to resolve it
The government on Tuesday urged all political parties to set aside their differences and forge a consensus on a joint strategy to combat terrorism, saying it was a national issue that required collective efforts and a unified response.
“This is a national issue. We can sit together and formulate a policy. When everyone puts their heads together, a decision can be made, as happened when Zarb-e-Azb was launched. Even now, if all political parties [..] sit together and discuss this issue, I am making an offer today: if all parties come together and reach an agreement on this issue, the prime minister is still willing to invite them to resolve it. He is ready to proceed with these operations with everyone’s support," said Special Adviser to the Prime Minister Rana Sanaullah while speaking in the Senate.
This is not the first time the government has invited the opposition for talks . The government’s offer comes amid heightened tensions following the Centre’s imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), citing the deteriorating security situation and what it described as a lack of cooperation from the provincial administration in the fight against terrorism. Parliament has also endorsed the measures, with both houses approving the relevant proposals.
Sanaullah during today's Senate session said terrorism was a national issue that required all political parties to set aside their differences and agree on a joint strategy, adding that the government was prepared to engage with the opposition to resolve the matter.
He urged Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl leader Maulana Abdul Wasey to speak to party chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman.
Comparing the provincial governments’ approaches to counterterrorism, Sanaullah accused the K-P government of failing to provide the cooperation needed to eliminate terrorism, while saying the Balochistan government was fully cooperating with the armed forces and the federal government.
He said the now non-functional (K-P) chief minister Sohail Afridi had repeatedly stated that he would not allow operations in the province, adding that provincial apex committees provided a forum for discussing security matters, with the core commander attending meetings under the respective chief ministers’ leadership.
Sanaullah said he had attended apex committee meetings in Balochistan alongside the prime minister, where issues were discussed openly. In contrast, he said, only one meeting had taken place in K-P in 11 months, "and in that meeting the way that the CM was taken there Mohsin Naqvi described those circumstances."
“If you only raise the issue of terrorism to create headlines, I do not think that is national service or the right approach to resolving the problem,” he said.
Read: PHC seeks Centre’s response over imposition of emergency, governor’s rule in K-P
Sanaullah also criticised National Assembly opposition leader Raja Nasir Abbas for refusing to meet the prime minister or visit the speaker’s chamber, despite accepting the position of opposition leader.
Recalling an encounter with Abbas during a joint sitting of parliament, Sanaullah said, “I told him to leave this stubbornness aside and set a time to meet the prime minister,” adding that Abbas had refused, saying he did not recognise the National Assembly speaker.
Sanaullah questioned how Abbas could accept the position and its associated privileges while refusing to engage with the government through parliamentary channels.
The adviser also recalled negotiations with Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) over elections after the party dissolved its provincial assemblies. He said both sides had agreed to hold general elections in the first week of September, but the agreement subsequently fell through.
Sanaullah said PTI leader Shah Mahmood Qureshi had asked for time to inform the party’s founding chairman, Imran Khan, that the negotiating committees had reached an understanding. However, he said the party later rejected the agreement.
He added that a draft of the negotiations was available to the media and that committee members, including Sohail Afridi, had exchanged messages about the discussions.
Referring to recent negotiations, Sanaullah said several matters, including arrangements for meetings and other outstanding issues, had been settled. The parties had also discussed forming a political committee comprising representatives from both sides to address unresolved matters.
However, he said, the opposition had refused to sign the draft over one point: supporting counterterrorism operations and fulfilling its responsibilities in the fight against terrorism.
Sanaullah also responded to remarks by PTI leader Mashal Yousafzai about a helicopter and an alleged message conveyed during negotiations. He said the opposition had claimed it was asked to sign an agreement under which an emergency would be imposed within 72 hours and to call off its long march unconditionally.
Read more: 'No link between K-P emergency, minerals'
“If this was your preparation, as has now come to light, then I consider this another missed opportunity,” he said.
Sanaullah said security personnel continued to be killed in the fight against terrorism, paying tribute to an army major who was martyred yesterday in an IED attack. He criticised what he said was a narrative targeting an entire institution and its head, accusing some political actors of making derogatory remarks and amplifying them through social media.
Sanaullah said the government could restrict meetings with Imran under the law if party leaders continued to make derogatory remarks about the head of a state institution. “Then, under the rules and the law, restrictions can be imposed on meetings,” he said.
Sanaullah also questioned PTI’s repeated attempts to secure political gains through different channels, including the courts and US President Donald Trump, rather than resolving its disputes through negotiations.
He said the recent long march was PTI’s third such attempt and recalled earlier marches towards Islamabad, adding that it was PTI leaders, rather than the government, who had spoken about bringing two million people to the capital and launching an attack.
He urged the opposition to reconsider its approach and resolve its outstanding issues through dialogue, reiterating that the fight against terrorism required collective national support.
Later in the day, Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry urged opposition parties to engage with the government on a single-point agenda of building consensus against terrorism and formulating a joint policy to tackle the issue.
“Let us begin with this single issue and this single-point agenda — that we have to develop a consensus against terrorism. Two opposition leaders were with me at a programme yesterday, and they said that all political parties should develop a consensus against terrorism. I extended the invitation yesterday, and I am extending it again today to all opposition parties — and our allies are already with us — to come and sit together so that we can develop a consensus against terrorism," the minister said.
He urged all political parties to reach a consensus against terrorism, saying it was an issue on which “we should all be united” and that Pakistan’s peace and the future of its children were at stake.
Chaudhry said political differences should not come at the expense of national interests, asking why parties could not reach a consensus on issues concerning Pakistan’s development, prosperity and peace.
“Politics is not meant to compromise the national interest,” he said, reiterating his invitation to opposition parties to work together against terrorism.
Taking aim at the PTI’s performance in K-P, Chaudhry questioned why the party had failed to establish peace despite being in power in the province for 10 to 12 years, including its more recent two-and-a-half-year tenure.
“On one side, bombs are exploding, and the bodies of our martyred soldiers, officers, police personnel and Frontier Corps personnel are being sent to their homes. On the other, you have created a strange spectacle on the streets, as if it were an Under-19 tournament,” he said.
“Neither does the province function this way, nor does the country,” he added, urging the PTI to work with the federal government and contribute to ongoing intelligence-based operations.
“Even today, if you come to your senses and sit with the federal government, your own leaders are speaking. Develop a consensus on this issue,” he said, adding that the government remained committed to the fight against terrorism.
Chaudhry also defended the imposition of emergency in K-P, saying the federal government had taken the step in response to security challenges rather than out of a desire to assume control of the province.
He said an advisory council had been formed comprising technocrats with expertise in their respective fields, while a separate council included tribal elders to ensure local communities were consulted on intelligence-based operations.
“The federal government and the armed forces are committed to continuing operations against terrorists until terrorism is completely eliminated,” he said.
Distinguishing K-P and Balochistan, Chaudhry said the provincial administration and chief minister in Balochistan were cooperating with the federal government and law enforcement agencies in the fight against terrorism.
“The chief minister is standing shoulder to shoulder with our law enforcement agencies and is on the front line in confronting terrorists,” he said, adding that the Balochistan government was not refusing to cooperate with counterterrorism operations.
The minister also criticised those linking the imposition of emergency to the province’s mineral resources, arguing that Pakistan needed to utilise its natural wealth to generate resources for development and reduce its debt burden.
“If Allah has blessed Pakistan with these treasures, which have remained buried for 80 years, and you want to keep them buried for another 80 or 180 years, that is your choice,” he said.
He maintained that the people of the province where minerals were located would have the first right to those resources. He added that international companies involved in exploration would be expected to follow international standards and ensure their activities did not create difficulties for local communities.
Resources generated through minerals, oil and gas, he said, could help fund improvements in education and healthcare across the country.
He said the federal government’s two primary objectives were to establish lasting peace and completely eliminate terrorism, adding that emergency would remain in place until those targets were achieved.
“We can compromise on politics, but we cannot compromise on the state, the interests of the state or state institutions,” he said.
The government and opposition made several attempts to reach a political understanding before emergency and governor’s rule were imposed in K-P.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif made multiple offers of talks to PTI, saying the government was prepared to engage with the opposition if the party ended its long march and sit-ins.
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari also urged the federal government to pursue dialogue before resorting to constitutional measures, saying political parties needed to work together against terrorism. He later offered to approach PM Shehbaz to end the emergency if the opposition agreed to political dialogue.
Talks between the government and opposition subsequently broke down amid disagreements over access to PTI founder Imran Khan and the provincial government’s role in counterterrorism. The government said the parties had agreed on most points but could not reach consensus on support for counterterrorism operations. PTI, however, blamed the government’s refusal to meet its demands, particularly access to Khan, for the deadlock.
After negotiations failed, the federal government imposed emergency and governor’s rule in K-P on October 11, citing the deteriorating security situation and what it said was a lack of cooperation from the provincial administration in the fight against terrorism. PM Shehbaz said the government had been left with no option but to take the measures after efforts to reach an agreement failed. The move brought the PTI-led provincial administration to an end and prompted legal challenges.

title: Halle Berry   s daughter may testify after brother   s court appearance
description: Halle Berry   s daughter Nahla may testify in actress   s custody dispute with Olivier Martinez over their son Maceo
content:
Halle Berry’s daughter Nahla may testify in actress’s custody dispute with Olivier Martinez over their son Maceo
Halle Berry’s 18-year-old daughter, Nahla Aubry, has been listed as a potential witness in the actress’s ongoing custody dispute with ex-husband Olivier Martinez, following nearly four hours of testimony from their 13-year-old son, Maceo.
According to Page Six , Nahla could testify virtually because she is currently attending school. The hearing in Los Angeles County Superior Court concerns Martinez’s request for a domestic violence restraining order and sole custody of Maceo.
Nahla, whom Berry shares with former partner Gabriel Aubry, previously submitted a declaration supporting her mother.
She said she had never witnessed Berry “hit, slap, choke, grab, or physically abuse Maceo in any way”, according to Page Six .
Martinez’s legal team previously objected to Nahla testifying, arguing that her evidence would be biased and irrelevant.
Other potential witnesses include Berry, Martinez, Berry’s fiancé Van Hunt, school employees, therapists and medical professionals.
Maceo testified behind closed doors on Monday, with both parents ordered to leave the courtroom during his evidence. His testimony remains under seal, and the judge had previously limited it to issues related to the restraining order.
The dispute stems from an alleged confrontation on September 26 involving Maceo and a virtual-reality headset. Martinez alleged in court filings that Berry grabbed their son by the neck and choked him. Berry has denied the allegations, with her attorney describing them as “entirely meritless and deliberately misleading”.
Berry has challenged Martinez’s account, alleging that he “cherry-picked” messages and pointing to a photograph that she said showed no visible injuries.
She has described the encounter as playful roughhousing that became tense, while maintaining that she did not choke or attack her son.
Martinez is seeking sole custody, while Berry wants the restraining order dismissed and the previous 50/50 custody arrangement restored. She has also sought to regain decision-making authority over Maceo’s education and medical care.
