title: Mariah Carey wins dismissal of brother   s  20m memoir lawsuit
description: Mariah Carey has won dismissal of her brother   s  20m defamation lawsuit over her memoir  though appeal is planned
content:
Mariah Carey has won dismissal of her brother’s $20m defamation lawsuit over her memoir, though appeal is planned
Mariah Carey has won a legal victory in her five-year dispute with her brother Morgan Carey after a New York judge dismissed his $20 million defamation lawsuit over claims made in her memoir, The Meaning of Mariah Carey.
In a ruling issued on Monday, New York State Supreme Court Justice Leslie A. Stroth found that Morgan had failed to establish that the singer acted with “actual malice” when making statements about him in the 2020 book.
Morgan filed the lawsuit in May 2021, alleging that the memoir damaged his reputation by portraying him as a violent man and a “sometimes” drug dealer. He sought damages exceeding $20 million, according to the original filing.
“Plaintiff has not sufficiently pleaded actual malice on the part of [Mariah],” Justice Stroth wrote in the decision. “Plaintiff fails to provide any proof that [Mariah] made such statements with knowledge of their falsity or with reckless disregard for the truth.”
The judge added that Morgan’s allegations of ill will towards him were insufficient to satisfy the legal requirement for establishing actual malice.
Carey’s lawyer, John Rosenberg, welcomed the ruling in a statement to Rolling Stone, saying the court had recognised the public interest in the memoir and dismissed the claims in their entirety.
“[Mariah] believes the importance of the court’s decision goes well beyond her own interests in this particular litigation, as it confirms that authors must be afforded broad protection when they speak out on matters of public concern,” Rosenberg said.
However, the dispute may continue. Richard Altman, Morgan’s lawyer, said his client disagreed with the decision and intended to appeal.
“We respectfully disagree with today's decision as being completely inconsistent with prior rulings in the case. We intend to appeal it very soon,” Altman told the outlet.
The planned appeal could extend the legal dispute over the singer’s memoir and the statements her brother claims harmed his reputation.

She added, “So, I’ve got a little bit to say about that, the good and bad. I wanted the song to sound quite chaotic, it’s basically my story squished into three and a half minutes.”
The singer also described the emotional inspiration behind the music video, recalling her teenage years performing outside a local Sainsbury’s.
The renewed interest highlights how major fashion events can introduce established songs to new audiences, giving JADE’s solo career further visibility nearly two years after the single’s original release.

title: Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari wins defamation case against opposition leader Moeen Riaz Qureshi
description: Qureshi is liable to pay Rs3million in damages to Azma
content:
Qureshi is liable to pay Rs3million in damages to Azma
Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari on Tuesday won a defamation case against Punjab Assembly Opposition Leader Moeen Riaz Qureshi, with the court ruling that the latter pay Rs3 million in damages for accusing the minister in a television programme.
Azma had filed a case before the Punjab Defamation Tribunal under the Defamation Act, seeking Rs84 million in damages over Qureshi’s allegations concerning the visit of the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) chief minister to the Punjab Assembly.
In a short order issued today, seen by The Express Tribune , the Punjab Defamation Tribunal in Lahore acknowledged that the counsel for both parties had concluded their final arguments.
It further outlined that Azma had won the case, resulting in an award of general damages.
"The claim of the plaintiff is hereby decreed up to the extent of general damages amounting to rupees three million (3,000,000/-)."
However, the tribunal dismissed the claim of "special and punitive damages" in its order.
Speaking to the media after the decision, Azma's counsel, Ali Bukhari, said the opposition leader had levelled false allegations against the provincial information minister but failed to substantiate them during the trial.
Read: Punjab Police did not arrest journalist Iqrarul Hassan: Azma Bokhari
“Alhamdulillah, the court has delivered its verdict in our favour today,” the counsel said, adding that Qureshi had admitted during the trial that he did not have evidence to support his allegations.
Azma said Qureshi had alleged that the information minister brought more than 100 paid persons into the Punjab Assembly during the K-P chief minister’s visit . He added that the opposition leader had also accused journalists who questioned the K-P chief minister during the visit of being paid employees of the minister.
According to the counsel, Qureshi had maintained during the proceedings that he made the statement as his personal observation. However, he failed to prove the allegations, Bukhari said.
Qureshi refuses to back off, says fine will not silence him
Qureshi, in a post on X , strongly criticised the decision to impose a fine against him, saying that financial penalties would not deter him from raising his voice for public rights, constitutional supremacy, democracy, and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan.
"My voice cannot be suppressed by trying to impose fines, but the voice I raise in favour of the people's rights, the supremacy of the Constitution, and Imran Khan cannot be silenced," he said in the social media post.
He said his responsibility as opposition leader was not to appease those in power but to question their actions, defend the rights of the people, and resist what he described as undemocratic measures.
He raised concerns over the implications of the fine for freedom of expression and democratic values, arguing that demanding accountability and speaking up for citizens should not be treated as an offence warranting a financial penalty worth millions of rupees.
“This is not just an issue concerning one individual but the entire democracy and the right to dissent,” he opined.
Qureshi stressed that dissent was a fundamental strength of democracy rather than a weakness. He added that imposing fines in response to criticism could not invalidate an individual's position.
Reaffirming his resolve, the opposition leader said he would neither be intimidated by the decision nor abandon his principles under pressure.
“My stance is clear: no fear, no compromise, no silence,” Qureshi said.
Meanwhile, PTI's account on X also seconded Qureshi.
" Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf expresses profound reservations over the impending verdict in the defamation case against Moin Qureshi, the opposition leader in the Punjab Assembly. The government, propped up on a bogus mandate, is now unwilling to tolerate even political criticism and dissent," the party said in the social media post.
It further said the situation raises serious questions regarding the use of law against political opponents and freedom of expression.
The party also said the verdict should be viewed in the backdrop of an impending resolution in the Punjab assembly against the October 11 emergency and governor's rule in K-P.
"In such a sensitive political environment, the emergence of the defamation case verdict against him is not merely a judicial matter but also raises questions about its timing and political implications," the party hinted at a political vendetta against Qureshi for voicing dissent.
"Turning political differences into fear through legal actions is contrary to democratic values," PTI concluded, while highlighting that dissent against the interim K-P government should be responded to within constitutional and democratic bounds.

title: Jesse Eisenberg says Razzie win for  Batman v Superman  damaged his acting career
description: Jesse Eisenberg says his Razzie win for  Batman v Superman  hurt his career and prompted him to pursue directing
content:
Jesse Eisenberg says his Razzie win for 'Batman v Superman' hurt his career and prompted him to pursue directing
Jesse Eisenberg has said winning a Razzie Award for his performance in Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice damaged his acting career and influenced his decision to pursue directing.
The 43-year-old actor and filmmaker reflected on the experience during an appearance at the BFI London Film Festival on Sunday, October 18, while promoting his upcoming film The Debut.
Eisenberg played Lex Luthor opposite Ben Affleck’s Batman and Henry Cavill’s Superman in Zack Snyder’s 2016 superhero film.
His performance earned him the Golden Raspberry Award for Worst Supporting Actor, while the film also received awards for Worst Remake, Rip-off or Sequel, Worst Screen Combo and Worst Screenplay.
"Listen, a lot of it just came from fear," Eisenberg said, according to Variety. "I couldn't get into movie studio parts anymore because I had won a Raspberry Award from [being in the] 'Batman' movie … and I saw the trajectory."
The actor described the uncertainty of working in the film industry, saying performers often worry about whether their careers are progressing or declining.
"If you're an actor, you're constantly panicked about 'Am I on an upslope or a downslope?' Because there's no plateau. Acting is just this unstable, awful industry where you are either on the treadmill and you're doing okay and you're running up or you are yesterday's news and it's awful."
Eisenberg added that he began writing films because he believed directing could help sustain his career.
"So I was like, 'I've got to direct movies.' That's why I started writing them, just to kind of keep my career afloat, really."
He made his feature directorial debut with 2022’s When You Finish Saving the World, followed by 2024’s A Real Pain , which he also wrote.
"I genuinely think it actually hurt my career in a real way because I was poorly received in something so public," he said.

title: PSX sheds 814 points amid topsy turvy trading
description: Rising oil prices  regional tensions unsettle investor sentiment
content:
Rising oil prices, regional tensions unsettle investor sentiment
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) closed lower on Tuesday after a topsy-turvy session, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index swinging between gains and losses before broad-based selling dragged it down by 814.44 points.
The index touched an intraday high of 166,425.56 and a low of 165,111.14, eventually settling at 165,151.64 points, down 0.49% from the previous close of 165,966.08 points.
The session had opened in positive territory and saw buying in automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration companies and oil marketing companies. However, sentiment remained fragile, with repeated swings failing to establish a sustained upward direction. The benchmark was still marginally higher at midday, but selling pressure subsequently intensified, pulling it close to the session’s low by the close
Persistent jitters kept investors on edge as broad-based sell-off overshadowed intermittent buying in key sectors.
Internationally, oil prices advanced, with Brent crude hovering around a five-month high as traders priced in a geopolitical risk premium following Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. The developments kept geopolitical risks in focus amid concerns over potential disruptions to regional energy supplies.
Read: PSX slips 454 points as investors struggle to find direction
KTrade Securities wrote in its market wrap that the KSE-100 Index declined 814 points (-0.5%) to 165,152 on Tuesday, amid cautious investor sentiment and subdued trading volumes of 144 million shares. It added that it expected the market to remain range-bound amid cautious sentiment, with near-term direction contingent on global oil prices, geopolitical developments and corporate earnings.
A sustained recovery in trading volumes remains critical to broadening market participation and supporting a durable market recovery, KTrade said.
Weakness was broad-based, led by commercial banks, technology, refineries and power. Attock Refinery, Systems, Habib Bank, Hub Power and Fauji Fertiliser were the largest stock-specific drags. Meanwhile, Brent crude remained elevated at $109 per barrel, reinforcing macroeconomic uncertainty and weighing on risk appetite.
Cumulatively, trading volume increased to 446.8 million shares versus 370.9 million recorded a day ago, while the value of traded shares stood at Rs19.5 million. Of the 499 companies traded, 128 advanced, 324 declined and 47 remained unchanged.
Cnergyico PK was the volume leader with trading in 46.6 million shares, falling Rs0.47 to close at Rs12.41.

title: Anger at rising fuel prices bolsters Europe s far right as unrest sweeps France
description: Anger at rising fuel prices bolsters Europe s far right as unrest sweeps France
content:
Latest energy shock comes after years of economic strain following fallout from Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine
Rising fuel costs are piling pressure on households, businesses and governments across Europe, fuelling cost-of-living protests and bolstering the far right ahead of elections next year in countries including France, Italy and Poland. Some far-right parties are calling for a return to Russian energy.
The tractors rolling into the town of Gela on the southern tip of Europe are flying the Sicilian flag, emblazoned with Medusa, three bent legs and ears of wheat: a reminder of the island's role as a breadbasket since Roman times. But the farmers are not bringing in a harvest. They are protesting.
As soaring fuel prices squeeze household budgets and businesses across Europe, cost-of-living pressures are driving unrest and giving fresh momentum to far-right parties ahead of elections next year in countries including France, Italy and Poland.
Parties once considered fringe had already been gaining ground, with voters from motorists in rural France to young men in Germany's former Communist east looking for alternatives.
The US-Iran war – which erupted in February and sent energy prices sharply higher – has compounded the challenge for governments already struggling to contain inflation, support growth and rein in spending.
The discontent has spilt onto the streets.
In France, demonstrations that began over deteriorating school facilities in Paris' northern suburbs have morphed into some of the country's worst unrest in decades, with shops looted, buildings torched and a 19th-century town hall in Limoges set on fire.
Read More: France protests: demonstrators vow to shake government
Macron's 'sense of detachment' amid rising living costs and youth 'fears for future'
"Why am I here? Well, quite simply, I find the current cost of living truly terrifying," said Quentin Leviloux, a 21-year-old protester in Nantes.
"Just think of people who earn barely the minimum wage when you look at the cost of food, fuel, and everything else. It’s terrifying how incredibly expensive things have become."
The European Commission estimates the Iran conflict has cost Europe roughly €100 billion ($112 billion) through disrupted trade and energy markets. Gas prices have jumped about 140 per cent, and diesel prices have doubled.
In a weekend address, French President Emmanuel Macron acknowledged the "legitimate demands" of protesters angered by rising living and fuel costs, while condemning those responsible for violence and looting. "We must never confuse them with those who destroyed, vandalised and looted," he said.
Violence has also erupted elsewhere. In the wealthy northern Italian city of Milan, police clashed on Sunday with protesters hurling stones and looting stores during demonstrations over poor public services and rising living costs.
In Gela, on Sicily's southern coast, farmers say fuel costs have made operating machinery prohibitively expensive. "We cultivate the land, we harvest debts," said one banner.
"We are completely at a standstill," said Arcangelo Gambino, a farmers' representative in Caltanissetta province. "The (fuel) cost has more than doubled."
Roadblocks by truckers, farmers and steelworkers have disrupted transport across parts of southern Italy, contributing to local fuel shortages and concerns over supermarket supplies.
Tens of thousands marched through Lisbon on Saturday over low wages, housing costs and the rising cost of living, increasing pressure on Portugal's centre-right government.
In Spain, the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home sparked nationwide demonstrations over housing shortages and soaring rents, helping trigger a snap election next month.
Belgium has also seen demonstrations, while large rallies in Albania have been driven by anger over perceived government corruption, a lack of jobs and poor education standards.
The protests reflect broader economic anxieties that are increasingly shaping politics across the continent.
Concerns about purchasing power have become "a major driver of populist politics" across Europe, said Gilles Ivaldi, a political scientist at Sciences Po.
Politicians on both the hard right and hard left have increasingly argued that restoring energy ties with Russia would help lower costs, challenging Europe's mainstream consensus on support for Ukraine.
Read Also: Soaring fuel prices drive German far-right calls for a turn back to Russia
Le Pen puts fuel prices at heart of campaign
The latest energy shock comes after years of economic strain following the pandemic and the fallout from Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine .
In France, rising energy costs have provided an explosive backdrop to next April's presidential election. Macron's government is struggling with a ballooning budget deficit and pressure from bond markets.
Frontrunner Marine Le Pen of the far-right National Rally and hard-left veteran Jean-Luc Mélenchon have both made fuel prices central planks in their campaigns.
“Rising fuel prices are clearly an issue that boosts Marine Le Pen,” said Ivaldi. “I think this is an issue she has owned for quite some time."
Since the Iran war began, Le Pen's ratings have improved while Macron's have slipped, according to polling by Elabe.
Le Pen's proposal to sharply cut value-added tax on fuel has attracted broad public support. Analysts say the issue resonates strongly with her core voters in rural and semi-rural areas where car travel is often essential.
In neighbouring Germany, the Alternative for Germany (AfD) is leading national opinion polls after strong gains in local elections. The cost of living topped Germans' concerns for a fifth straight year in a survey published this month.
German inflation spiked to nearly a three-year high in September, with energy price inflation rising to 14pc, handing ammunition to the AfD to attack Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
The AfD is pushing to restore energy ties with Russia, arguing that Berlin’s support for Ukraine is needlessly self-sabotaging at a time when Europe’s largest economy and many of its energy-hungry companies are struggling.
AfD surges as Merz’s CDU suffers regional elections setback
Past experience indicates a link between high energy prices and voter turnout for the AfD, said Jan Steckel, professor for the political economy of climate change at the Technical University of Munich.
“Populist parties often frame energy costs as avoidable and attribute them to government policy choices rather than to the underlying geopolitical shocks that drive them," he said.
“These geopolitical shocks are ... much more difficult to explain. And I think this is why incumbent parties often struggle."
The argument is gaining traction elsewhere.
In Italy, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni faces growing competition from National Future, a new far-right party led by former army general Roberto Vannacci, that advocates restoring gas links with Russia.
In Poland – one of Ukraine's staunchest supporters – concern over energy bills is helping boost support for the far-right Confederation of the Polish Crown. Its leader, Grzegorz Braun, has called for a return to buying Russian oil and gas, making the case alongside AfD politicians in Lubmin, where the damaged Nord Stream pipelines land in Germany.
“I love the smell of Russian gas in the morning,” he said.

title: Minhas  Hasan help Pakistan demolish England
description: Fifties from them  followed by a late assault from Faheem lift hosts to a competitive total against England
content:
Rookie all-rounder hits 59 and grabs 6-40 as hosts romp to second straight win in tri-series
Arafat Minhas’ superb all-round performance catapulted Pakistan to an 87-run victory over England in their second game of the ODI-tri-series at the Pindi Stadium in Rawalpinid on Tuesday.
Arafat hit a superb 59, coupled with Hasan Nawaz’ 79, to enable Pakistan post 302-9.
Arafat then produced his career-best figures of 6-40 in 8.4 overs to fold England for 215 in the 39th over.
This is the second successive victory from Pakistan in the series after they downed Sri Lanka by 37 runs in their opener the other day.
Set to chase 303, Ben Duckett and Tom Banton gave England a strong start, putting on 91 for the opening wicket partnership before Duckett was caught by Fakhar Zaman off Haris Rauf for 45.
He hit eight fours in his 46-ball knock.
Banton continued to score freely, making 57 off 53 deliveries, including five fours and two sixes, before he was caught by Shaheen Afridi off Arafat Minhas in the 19th over.
Arafat Minhas then got rid of England’s captain Harry Brook to leave the visitors at 128-3.
Joe Root and Sam Curran attempted to steady the innings, but Root was bowled by Naseem Shah for 33 which featured two fours. Haris then dismissed Curran for 27, caught by substitute fielder Ghazi Ghori, to leave England at 177-5 after 31.3 overs.
Arafat Minhas then had Jordan Coz, trapped lbw for a 16-ball 18 and England were gasping at 197-6.
Arafat continued to destroy England as he picked up the wickets of Jamie Overton (1), Will Jacks (19) Asil Rashid (0) to leave Pakistan just one wicket away of victory. Gus Atkinson (7) then got run out as Pakistan completed well-deserved victory.
After being put into bat first, Hasan Nawaz and Arafat Minhas struck solid fifties before Faheem Ashraf provided late fireworks as Pakistan recovered from an early collapse to post 302-9.
Hasan top-scored with 79 off 74 balls, hitting five fours and four sixes while Arafat contributed 59 from 58 deliveries, including nine boundaries.
England, who elected to field, made an immediate impact when Gus Atkinson dismissed Fakhar Zaman for a first-ball duck. Sonny Baker then removed Saim Ayub for eight, leaving Pakistan under pressure at 31-2.
Babar Azam and Saad Baig attempted to steady the innings, but Babar fell for 34 from 52 balls, having struck four fours, when he was bowled by Will Jacks. Salman Agha managed 16 before becoming Adil Rashid's only victim, and Pakistan slipped to 81-4.
Baig scored 35 from 54 deliveries, hitting five fours, before Atkinson claimed his second wicket to leave Pakistan at 133-5 in the 28th over.
Hasan and Arafat then transformed the innings with a 78-run sixth-wicket stand, providing the platform for a strong finish. Hasan reached his fifty from 46 balls, combining five fours with four sixes, while Arafat brought up his fifty from 54 deliveries.
Hasan was bowled by Jamie Overton for 79, but Arafat continued to attack before falling to Baker for 59 in the 48th over.
Faheem added further momentum with an explosive 39 from just 26 balls, striking five fours and one six. His innings ended when he was caught by Jacks off Sam Curran, with Pakistan at 285-8.
As many as 52 runs came in the final five overs which boosted the total.
Baker took 3-65 while Atkinson got 2-35. Overton was economical, finishing with 1-38.
Earlier Pakistan went unchanged while England got Adil Rashid’s boost who had missed the previous ODI series.

title: Suspect sent on 4 day physical remand after running over 15 year old employee in Multan
description: Police arrest suspect  courts hands him four day physical remand
content:
After work dispute, teenager allegedly tried to leave, but Tauqeer chased him in car and ran him over
A 15-year-old boy was allegedly run over and killed by his employer after attempting to leave his workplace in a private housing society in Multan. Police arrested the suspect, who was later granted four days of physical remand by a court on Tuesday.
Waseem Abbas had been living at an orphanage for five years and wanted to learn electrical work, according to Shoaib Haider, the orphanage’s general secretary. The orphanage had sent him to contractor Tauqeer Nazir six days earlier to learn the trade.
The incident took place within the jurisdiction of the DHA Police Station. Rescue officials said Abbas suffered a severe head injury and died at the scene.
His body was shifted to Nishtar Hospital under police supervision before being transported to his native Muzaffargarh district, where he was buried.
According to police, Abbas was learning electrical work under contractor Tauqeer Nazir, who was carrying out work at a house in the housing society. Following an argument over work, the teenager allegedly tried to leave, prompting Tauqeer to chase him in a car and run him over.
Police said another suspect, Amjad Ali, was also in the vehicle at the time of the incident.
Investigators said Abbas had been staying at Tauqeer’s house in Zakariya Town for about a week and a half.
He was sent to the housing society on October 11 to learn electrical work and returned to the orphanage on October 15, where he met his friends. He went back to work with Tauqeer on the morning of October 17, police said.
According to police, the contractor took Abbas to work and brought him back each day. Other children were also working under him.
Abbas’s maternal grandfather had enrolled him at an orphanage so that he could receive an education.
Police arrested suspect Tauqeer and registered a case. Today, he was presented before Judicial Magistrate Saadia Aslam, who granted him four days of physical remand.
When Tauqeer was brought before the court, lawyers assaulted him outside the courtroom despite the presence of police.
The first information report (FIR), registered on Monday, names Tauqeer Nazir and Amjad Ali as suspects and invoked Sections 302 and 34 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), relating to murder and acts done by several persons in furtherance of their common intention. It alleged that the two men pursued Abbas in a car and deliberately ran him over, causing fatal head injuries.
According to the FIR, Sub-Inspector Liaquat Ali Bhatti was on patrol with police personnel in Royal Orchard when a man identified as Mukhtiar Ahmed approached them at around 4:35pm. Mukhtiar told police that his cousin, Abbas, had been working as an electrician for the suspects and that they had allegedly subjected him to violence and threatened to kill him.
The report stated that Abbas had fled to a neighbouring street to escape the alleged abuse, while the two suspects pursued him in a vehicle. Police said they saw Abbas running in fear, followed by a Honda vehicle bearing registration number BVE-474.
The FIR alleged that the suspects ran the vehicle over Abbas with the intention of killing him. His head struck a pillar at the gate of house 3-A, crushing his skull and causing severe injuries. He died at the scene.
Two residents, Saqlain Raza and Syed Naseem Abbas, were named in the FIR as witnesses to the incident. According to the report, they told police that Abbas had passed by shortly before the incident, saying that the suspects wanted to kill him and that he was running to save his life.
The FIR further stated that the vehicle stopped after the incident and the suspects attempted to flee. Tauqeer was apprehended at the scene, while Amjad escaped. Police took the vehicle into custody as evidence.
Mukhtiar told police that Abbas wanted to leave the job because of the alleged violence and feared for his safety. The FIR alleged that the suspects pursued him over his decision to leave and acted in concert to kill him.
Abbas’s funeral prayers were held at around 2am in Mouza Daulatpur, and he was buried in his ancestral graveyard. The prayers were held promptly because of the condition of the body. Only close relatives and orphanage officials attended.
Haider said the orphanage had sent Abbas to Tauqeer after making inquiries about the contractor, who had a team of around 40 to 45 boys.
According to Haider, Tauqeer claimed he had followed Abbas in his car after the boy became tired while running away on foot. The suspect maintained that his car had slipped, but Haider said the video footage did not appear to support that explanation.
“It looks as though he was hit with the car,” Haider said, adding that Tauqeer would have to explain during the investigation why the boy had run away from him.
Haider said the orphanage had received no previous complaints against Tauqeer. Another boy from the facility had also been working for the contractor, but the orphanage had brought him back following the incident.
Abbas’s cousin Nadeem, who had been living at the orphanage for six years, said the boy had often expressed reluctance to go to the electrician to learn the trade, saying he wanted to return home. Nadeem said he did not know Tauqeer and had never met him. He added that Abbas had not returned to the orphanage since leaving to learn electrical work.
Abbas's uncle, Jafar Hussain, told the media that the boy’s father had died nine years ago. His maternal grandfather initially supported him, after which Hussain looked after him for two to three years. Abbas was later admitted to the orphanage by his grandfather and uncle, he said.
“Tauqeer deliberately killed my nephew. I know what condition Abbas was in and how I saw him,” Hussain said, demanding justice.
Abbas’s maternal grandfather said he had taken the boy to the orphanage because he wanted him to receive an education rather than struggle on the streets. He also demanded that the suspect be punished.
Residents said Abbas and his brother had been admitted to the orphanage after their mother remarried following their father’s death.
Bureau rejects Multan orphanage’s registration
Meanwhile, the Child Protection and Welfare Bureau (CPWB) refused to register a Multan-based orphanage over its failure to ensure the safety and supervision of a child placed with a contractor for work, its chairperson Sarah Ahmad said.
In a statement on X, Sarah urged the Punjab police to take legal action against the orphanage owner and hold those responsible accountable for the death of the 15-year-old boy.
She said the bureau had issued minimum care standards for all orphanages housing children in Punjab, adding that no institution could be allowed to neglect its duty of care.
Sarah also called on the Punjab Charities Commission to review the orphanage’s registration and licence and cancel it, where warranted under the law, besides initiating action against those responsible.
“Every child deserves protection, dignity and safety. No orphan should be left at the mercy of those entrusted with their care,” she said.

description: Seam friendly conditions and careful planning to test Sooryavanshi in five match T20I series
content:
Seam-friendly conditions and careful planning to test Sooryavanshi in five-match T20I series
MELBOURNE: New Zealand ​have done their homework on India prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and expect their home conditions will challenge the 15-year-old sensation in the Twenty20 series starting on Thursday, paceman Jacob Duffy said.
Sooryavanshi has lit up world cricket with his power-hitting, ‌breaking a string of records in the Indian Premier League before becoming India's youngest international in the men's game with his debut in the T20 series in ‌England in July.
After a slow start ⁠against England, ​the teenage opener became the youngest player to score a half-century ​in men's international cricket when he ‌clobbered an 18-ball fifty against Zimbabwe. He ​recently won an Asian Games gold medal in Japan as India swept to the T20 cricket title in Aichi-Nagoya.
Duffy said New Zealand had been studying the left-hander in the buildup to the ⁠five-match series, which starts at Christchurch's Hagley Oval. "First of all, he's an incredible talent. Obviously, he's ‌taken the IPL by storm and what's amazing, he strikes it so hard but he does it so consistently," Duffy told reporters on Tuesday.
"He's striking at 250 (strike-rate) every game and he's not missing out very often. So ⁠that's incredible in itself. "I think he played in England, so conditions will ⁠be a little ​bit different for him, ‌so that's obviously one thing for him to be challenged with. "We've certainly had a good scouting session on him and got our plans as to what we want to do to him." India fans will be eager to see what Sooryavanshi can do in New Zealand, where the pitches tend to be seam-friendly.
Duffy said he had spoken to Hagley Oval's head groundsman about what to expect from the wicket, hoping that it will ⁠not be a batter's paradise like some subcontinent pitches. "He's from Invercargill, so he's promised me a little bit of bounce," said ⁠Duffy, who was born in Lumsden, a small town near the South Island city. "As long as it's not Hyderabad, I'm happy."
The T20 series is the first part of India's tour, with one-day matches and a two-test series to follow. Otago bowler Duffy has had a big year, claiming the Sir Richard Hadlee Medal as New Zealand's top player in 2025 and making the final of this year's T20 World Cup in India before winning the IPL with Royal Challengers Bengaluru.
He ⁠made his test debut last year at the age of 31 but ​missed the mid-year tour of England and the one-off test against Ireland to be home with his wife for the birth of their first child. The absence from the test setup has made him doubly keen to tear into India with the red ball ahead of a four-test ​tour of Australia. "I've played four tests in my life. I ‌get up for any test. There's something special about them," he said.

The couple exchanged vows on October 17, celebrating their Korean heritage with a garden ceremony and designer outfits
Grammy and Oscar-winning singer-songwriter Ejae, who also served as the singing voice of Rumi in the hit movie KPop Demon Hunters, married producer-turned-programmer Samuel Kim in Seoul, celebrating their relationship with a garden wedding at a venue closely connected to the bride’s childhood.
According to Vogue , the couple exchanged vows on October 17, 2026 at Stage 28, a former family home where Ejae spent much of her childhood exploring the garden and walking in the surrounding hills with her grandfather.
The couple first met in May 2017 through a songwriting session arranged by a mutual friend.
Their shared interests in anime and music helped establish their connection, and they began dating shortly afterwards.

Following Ejae’s growing international recognition for her work on KPop Demon Hunters , the couple moved their wedding plans from California to South Korea, giving them approximately four months to organise the celebration.
The festivities included a traditional Korean Paebaek ceremony and a welcome gathering at Congdu50 before the main wedding.
The garden setting featured green and earthy tones inspired by Ejae’s childhood memories, while the glasshouse reception incorporated soft fabrics and flowing drapes.
Ejae wore a custom Danielle Frankel gown for the ceremony, followed by a Zac Posen reception dress and a sparkling Milla Nova mini for dancing.
Kim chose a bespoke double-breasted tuxedo from Bhambi’s Custom Tailors before changing into a white Posen design.
The reception featured bilingual speeches, dinner, live music and Korean street food.
Reflecting on the celebration, Ejae told Vogue : “We are so thankful for each other and for our family and friends, especially given how many of our guests traveled across the world to celebrate with us!”

title: Rubio kicks off India visit with trade deal  Russian oil on agenda
description: Secretary of state to meet Jaishankar  Ambani as Washington  New Delhi seek to finalise trade deal
content:
Secretary of state to meet Jaishankar, Ambani as Washington, New Delhi seek to finalise trade deal
United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel to India on Tuesday, days after President Donald Trump delayed tariffs on US imports from the world's largest democracy as the two countries seek to finalise a trade deal .
During the two-day visit to Mumbai and Jamnagar in western India, Rubio is slated to meet government and business leaders, including Foreign Minister S Jaishankar and billionaire Mukesh Ambani, chairman of Reliance Industries, which operates the world's largest refining complex at Jamnagar.
Rubio and other officials have said in recent days that a comprehensive trade deal between the two nations is almost complete, raising the possibility that it could be signed during the secretary's visit.
Trump removed one potential stumbling block last Friday when he waived potential tariffs that would have punished New Delhi for the nation's extensive Russian crude oil purchases.
Read: Russian diesel deal puts Trump at odds with allies
Under legislation signed by Trump in September, the administration is authorised to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top five importers of Russian oil, which would include India, which is number two on that list after China. Trump's decision to waive all substantive provisions of that bill has upset both Democrats and Republicans who have pushed him to up economic pressure on Moscow for its war with Ukraine .
Rubio has said in recent days that the effort to finalise a trade deal was a factor in the decision to waive those tariffs . He also said that India has been diversifying its import mix away from Russian crude, even as it still buys millions of barrels of Russian oil every day.
He said the administration was entering a 60-day review period , during which it would consider which new tariffs, if any, to enact.
"You've got countries like India, for example, that have voluntarily diversified their energy portfolio, but are still getting a substantial amount of energy from Russia because it's hard to pivot from one day to the next," Rubio said on Sunday. "But they're also an important ally and partner of the United States."
Read More: Rubio says Russia and Ukraine have both voiced interest in 'limited ceasefire'
While the Trump administration has in the past pressed India to cut Russian oil imports, the US signed a deal with Russia last week to import diesel to bring down domestic fuel prices before the midterm elections , making it unclear to what extent that remains a foreign policy priority.
"Every country has a complex set of factors that they have to take into account," Rubio told reporters on Monday when asked about India's Russian oil purchases. "Geography is real. For some countries, it's very difficult to acquire energy from alternative sources." India imports more than 85% of its crude oil requirements to help power its fast-growing economy.
Rubio is slated to fly into Mumbai from Samarkand, Uzbekistan, where he was meeting with Central Asian political and business leaders.

Australian model and swimwear designer Sahara Ray, who gained international attention after being linked to pop star Justin Bieber, has died aged 34, according to reports published on October 19, 2026.
Ray’s family confirmed her death to TMZ , saying she passed away in hospital surrounded by loved ones.

Ray first attracted widespread attention in 2016, when she was photographed with Bieber during a holiday in Hawaii.

Born in Australia, Ray spent part of her childhood in California and Hawaii. Her father, professional surfer Tony Ray, influenced her connection to surfing and beach culture.
She later studied at the Fashion Institute of Design and Merchandising in Los Angeles before launching her swimwear brand, Sahara Ray Swim.
Ray also built a substantial social media following, sharing modelling photographs, fashion designs and updates about her personal life.
In 2024, she revealed that she had been diagnosed with Guillain-Barré syndrome following an accident in which she was reportedly struck by a vehicle.
The condition affected her mobility, leaving her temporarily dependent on a wheelchair as she documented her rehabilitation.
Ray’s mother, Gretchen Bach, also spoke about her daughter’s death in a statement to the Daily Mail , describing her as a passionate and kind young woman who loved her family, fashion, her daughter Snow and surfing.
Ray welcomed her daughter in January 2026. No confirmed information has established a link between her previous health condition and her death.

'Pakistan, Qatar working together for regional peace,' says Naqvi during meeting with Qatari counterpart
Pakistan and Qatar on Tuesday agreed to expand their security partnership and strengthen cooperation in internal security during a meeting between Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and his Qatari counterpart, Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, in Doha, according to a statement by the Ministry of Interior.
The meeting, also attended by the commander of Qatar’s Internal Security Force (Lekhwiya), focused on enhancing bilateral cooperation between the two interior ministries, as well as the prevailing regional situation and matters relating to regional peace and stability.
“Pakistan and Qatar are working together for regional peace and stability,” Naqvi said, while the Qatari interior minister said his country attached great importance to its relations with Pakistan.
Naqvi is in Doha attending the eighth Global Security Forum , where he highlighted Qatar’s role in diplomatic efforts to ease tensions between Iran and the United States. He said Pakistan and Qatar had worked to prevent further escalation and save lives, citing the involvement of Qatar’s Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani and Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir in efforts to keep negotiations on track.
He recalled the Lake Lucerne summit in Switzerland, where Qatar’s prime minister and CDF Munir worked for more than 16 hours to keep negotiations on track.
“The aim of both countries, Pakistan and Qatar, was never to take credit; the only aim was to stop further conflict and to save innocent lives,” he said.
Praising Qatar’s diplomatic efforts, Naqvi said, “In the diplomacy of our time, when others chose sides, Qatar chose to keep talking. Pakistan has seen this closely because we have worked beside you.” He said the experience had reinforced the importance of keeping diplomatic channels open, building trust and making sustained efforts for peace.
“We do not want credit for stopping wars. We want a future where wars do not start,” he added. Naqvi also called for stronger international cooperation, intelligence-sharing and joint efforts to combat terrorism, which he described as a common enemy.

title: Trump warns Kansans that US will  burn  like France if Democrats win
description: US president rallies in favour of Republican incumbent amid voter frustration over rising prices  Iran war
content:
US president rallies in favour of Republican incumbent amid voter frustration over rising prices, Iran war
United States President Donald Trump on Monday used violent unrest in France as an argument against Democrats in his battle to defend a Kansas Senate seat long held by Republicans but in danger of falling to his political opponents.
Trump's rally on behalf of Republican incumbent Roger Marshall was his latest foray into conservative states where Republican candidates are on defence due to voter frustrations over the Iran war and rising prices.
"I love you Kansas, but I'm here for a guy named Roger Marshall," Trump said.
In a new addition to his stump speech, Trump pointed to widespread protests in France as a scenario that could erupt in the US unless Republicans win. He provided no evidence.
Read: Trump threatens California officials with imprisonment over stance on mail ballots
France in recent days has seen some of the worst unrest in years as huge protests over the cost of living and underfunded public services descended into riots and looting. Trump himself has struggled to make goods and services more affordable in the US.
In his speech, Trump turned to anti-immigrant and anti-Muslim rhetoric, the type that he used to fuel his three presidential campaigns. "We're not going to let that happen to this country," he said. "When you see burning steeples and raging fires in France, just remember that is what the radical Dumocrats want to do to America."
Trump has been mocking Democrats by calling them Dumocrats. Rights advocates have repeatedly criticised Trump for his rhetoric over the years in which he has targeted and mocked immigrants and ethnic minority groups. Civil rights groups say such rhetoric normalises discriminatory attitudes towards those communities.
Kansas, a conservative Midwestern state Trump won by 16 points in 2024, has not elected a Democrat to the US Senate in 94 years. First-term Senator Marshall is in a close fight with Democratic candidate Adam Hamilton, pastor of a Methodist megachurch, who is running against Trump’s tariff agenda and what he calls the president's “erratic leadership.”
“He wants you to repent for being born White,” Trump said of Hamilton.
Marshall, in remarks to the rally, led his campaign argument on cultural issues like stopping "radical Islam." He called Hamilton "too woke" for Kansas because he supports gay pride parades, which the crowd loudly booed. "We need someone who can sort heifers and steers," he said.
In response, Hamilton's campaign spokesperson called Marshall's campaign "sinking."
"Nothing said at the rally can distract from the fact Kansans are being crushed by rising gas and diesel prices, struggling to access affordable healthcare, and are tired of Washington corruption," the spokesperson, Tyson Brody, said.
Read More: Trump administration reopened citizenship probe into Rep Ilhan Omar: report
In a Monday video, Hamilton welcomed Trump to the state and said his supporters have “a place” in his campaign. Hamilton said he will work with Trump when it makes sense and stand up for Kansans when Washington policies hurt farmers and rural hospitals.
The tightness of the race is emblematic of the challenges looming for Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections as they try to defy political headwinds and retain control of the Senate and the House of Representatives.
Trump is deep into a 32-day campaign blitz, frequently going to friendly areas that he won handily in previous elections.
One Republican familiar with Trump's midterm strategy said the president’s attention on rural parts of the country is in response to internal polling showing soft support from men 55 years and younger in rural areas nationwide, a voting bloc crucial to Trump’s 2024 presidential win.
The latest Reuters /Ipsos poll, published on Monday, found that 31% of Americans approve of Trump's ​performance in office, a record low for the president.
Democrats need a net gain of four seats in both the US House of Representatives and US Senate to overturn Republicans' narrow 218-214 and 53-47 majorities.
In Park City, near Wichita, many rallygoers walked more than a mile across Interstate 135 to reach the rural arena, as a red-and-green truck stop sign flashed its latest prices above their heads: $3.98 for gas and $5.78 for diesel. That is up about 45% compared to average gas prices in the state last year, according to motoring club AAA.
Economic concerns were palpable among Trump's most loyal supporters. “Being on disability, I don’t have much, but it seems like the prices are still going up and they need to come down. It feels like you’re having to search or hunt for food," said Monique Mullen, 59, a Republican voter from Hutchinson, Kansas, who takes care of her father.
Also Read: Vance suggests disagreement with Trump over Iran war
A small bloc of protesters gathered near the arena, including James Nightingale, a self-described independent from Halstead, Kansas. “I’m a farmer from Kansas and the Trump administration has decimated the farm economy in my area. Not only have his tariffs decimated our markets for grain sales, now he is bringing in imported beef from outside the country. What happened to ‘America First’?” he said.
Kansans have proven a willingness to cross parties, as voters have elected a Democratic governor, Laura Kelly, for the last two terms. "I don't think it's ever easy to get elected here," said Gina Seman, a Trump voter from Towanda, Kansas, noting that Republican candidates in the past have taken their popularity for granted.

title: US judge orders Saudi engineer held in OpenAI case
description: US judge orders Saudi engineer held in OpenAI case
content:
He was arrested on October 9 and faces up to five years in prison on charges of intercepting oral communications
A former OpenAI employee accused of planting a recording device at the company's San Francisco offices was ordered held without bail a day earlier, after a federal judge deemed him a flight risk.
US District Judge Alex Tse ruled that there was "significant" risk that Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, would fail to appear in court, rejecting his attorneys' request for release.
Prosecutors cited Alfozan's frequent contact with an unnamed member of the Saudi royal family in arguing against his release. Alfozan, 35, appeared in court a day earlier, dressed in orange prison clothing. He did not speak during the hour-long hearing.
He was arrested on October 9 and faces up to five years in prison on charges of intercepting oral communications.
Read More: OpenAI employee arrested over alleged recording device
In a document filed on Sunday, the US Attorney's Office alleged that Alfozan, who had worked at OpenAI since 2025, maintained frequent communications with a member of the Saudi royal family.
While the complaint against Alfozan does not allege spying activities, US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton implied in a statement last week that the case had national security implications.
"The government's investigation is ongoing and may result in additional serious charges," the new court filing said, adding that the matter is "a concern for the national security of the United States."
Also Read: OpenAI employee who left for Apple took files about unreleased device, OpenAI alleges
"Whether the defendant wanted to record OpenAI meetings to enrich himself by enhancing his own business prospects, or to provide aid (to) a foreign government, or both, his conduct is criminal," the document added.
The unnamed Saudi royal family member tried several times to recruit the engineer for an AI initiative in Saudi Arabia.
"Saudi (Arabia) needs you more than [sic] the US," the person wrote in one WhatsApp exchange, according to the filing. Alfozan responded with "100" -- a common way to indicate agreement.
Before his arrest, Alfozan bought a one-way ticket to Riyadh for October 12, with prosecutors arguing that such a move demonstrated he was a flight risk.
Alfozan's lawyer William Pernik disputes that, saying Alfozan had a US naturalisation interview scheduled on November 6.
Alfozan's wife and their baby left the United States on October 10, the day after his arrest.
They used tickets paid for by a Saudi military official, according to prosecutors, noting that the United States and Saudi Arabia do not have an extradition treaty.
Alfozan's attorneys argued in court that he was not a flight risk because he was working towards becoming a US citizen and was willing to put down $1 million worth of assets to secure his release on bail.
Prosecutors suggested it could be even more lucrative for him to return to Saudi Arabia.
Read: FBI arrests Saudi OpenAI engineer over covert recording device, DOJ says
"Once he leaves, there's no getting him back, the case goes away, and that is why this is a bigger case," Tse said in the courtroom.
The next hearing is scheduled for November 6.
Alfozan was caught on security footage from inside a restricted conference room where he appeared to look behind the television where a USB recording device, wrapped in toilet paper, had been placed, the Justice Department said last week.
The arrest and allegations come amid a fierce global race to dominate in artificial intelligence, which the Trump administration has pushed to be rebranded as "superintelligence."
Saudi Arabia's state-backed AI firm Humain invested $3 billion in Elon Musk's xAI shortly before the American billionaire's space company, SpaceX, acquired the AI division in February.
Now known as SpaceXAI, the division announced last year that it was teaming up with Humain to build a 500-megawatt data centre in Saudi Arabia.
In 2022, a former Twitter worker, Ahmad Abouammo, was found guilty of spying for Saudi officials keen to unmask critics on the platform.
A second former Twitter employee, Ali Alzabarah, was similarly accused of helping Saudi officials but left the United States before he could be charged -- which prosecutors in Alfozan's case cited in Sunday's filing.

title: Model Sahara Ray  Justin Bieber   s ex  dies at 34  months after welcoming daughter
description: Model Sahara Ray  briefly linked to Justin Bieber  has died aged 34  nine months after welcoming her daughter
content:
Model Sahara Ray, briefly linked to Justin Bieber, has died aged 34, nine months after welcoming her daughter
Australian model and swimwear designer Sahara Ray has died at the age of 34, months after welcoming her daughter, Snow.
Her family confirmed her death to TMZ , saying she passed away surrounded by relatives at hospital on Sunday, October 18. No official cause of death has been announced.
Ray was briefly romantically linked to singer Justin Bieber in 2016, when the pair appeared in an Instagram video showing them skinny-dipping in Hawaii.
She later developed her modelling career and launched her own swimwear brand, Sahara Ray Swim. She was the daughter of professional big-wave surfer Tony Ray.
Her death comes after years of health challenges. In April 2024, Ray revealed that she had developed Guillain-Barré syndrome following a car accident involving a drunk driver. The neurological disorder left her partially paralysed and unable to walk independently.
“So basically, right now I'm paralyzed from the tops of my upper thighs all the way down to my feet. I can't walk at all,” she said in a social media video at the time.
Ray subsequently documented her efforts to regain mobility, and videos shared in the months before her death showed her walking again. She welcomed Snow in January 2026 and described her daughter as her “whole heart” in a social media post in July.
The Daily Mail reported that Ray had allegedly suffered a fentanyl overdose and was placed on life support after being taken to hospital on Friday. However, these reports have not been confirmed as her official cause of death.
Ray's family described her as “an incredibly passionate and kind young woman who loved her family, fashion, her daughter, Snow, and surfing”, according to the report.
Ray is survived by her young daughter and leaves behind family, friends and followers who have shared tributes following news of her death.

title: Ronaldo handed 30 day suspension after walking out on Portugal
description: The 41 year old will also pay a 255 euro fine after apologising for his departure
content:
The 41-year-old will also pay a 255-euro fine after apologising for his departure
Cristiano Ronaldo has been handed a 30-day suspension for leaving the Portuguese national team camp, the country's football federation (FPF) announced on Monday.
The 41-year-old abruptly left the Portugal camp on September 30 during the UEFA Nations League, before accusing coach Jorge Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time.
Ronaldo apologised to supporters earlier in October, adding he would accept any punishment that was imposed.
The former Manchester United and Real Madrid star, who will also have to pay a fine of 255 euros ($286), has received the minimum penalty provided for in the federation's regulations, which stipulate suspensions of between one and six months for leaving the national team.
Ronaldo left Portugal's squad after first being made to warm up as a substitute against Norway on September 27 and not being brought on, and then finding out he would not start against Denmark in the match on October 1.
Ronaldo's suspension takes effect from the day of the Denmark match, meaning he has already served 19 days of his ban and will complete it by the end of October.
The FPF disciplinary committee said it took into account "the remorse shown in the statement" issued by Ronaldo on October 6, in which he admitted his mistake and expressed his willingness to accept a punishment.
The five-time Ballon d'Or winner is Portugal's all-time top goalscorer and record appearance-maker in men's international football.
But in his absence, Portugal won all four of their Nations League matches and qualified for the quarter-finals with two games to spare.
Portugal host Denmark on November 14 and then travel to face Wales on November 17 in their final two Nations League Group A4 matches -- by which time Ronaldo will have served his suspension.
In a social media post shortly after his walk-out, Ronaldo accused Portugal boss Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time in Nations League matches but insisted he was not retiring from international duty.
"I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team," Ronaldo posted.
He said Jesus had gone back on his word about bringing him on against Norway, and then in a press conference before the Denmark match had not said a series of points they had agreed upon during a conversation beforehand.
One of Ronaldo's pre-approved talking points was that Jesus had "made a mistake in asking someone of the stature of Pele or Maradona to warm up and then not sending him on in the match".
Jesus, speaking several days later, said he would select Ronaldo for international duty if the forward was playing for his club Al Nassr, and was interested in being called up.
Following the FPF's announcement, Ronaldo did not directly react to the news on Instagram but did post a picture of himself preparing to train with his Saudi club, accompanied with the caption, "Putting in the work".

title: Japan launches world s first mission to collect samples from Martian moon
description: Spacecraft to collect rocks  sand from Phobos before returning to Earth in July 2031
content:
Spacecraft to collect rocks, sand from Phobos before returning to Earth in July 2031
Japan successfully launched a spacecraft Tuesday on the world's first mission to collect rock and sand samples from a Martian moon, according to the country's space agency.
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) probe separated successfully from an H3 rocket and entered its planned orbit, the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) announced , according to Kyodo News Agency. The rocket lifted off from the Tanegashima Space Centre in southwestern Japan at 4.41am local time (1941GMT Monday).
JAXA project manager Makoto Arita said the spacecraft had reached its planned orbit with "exceptional precision."
Read: Astrophysics study suggests Venus may have swallowed its moon
The 4,480-kilogram spacecraft will travel to Phobos, the larger of Mars' two moons, and is scheduled to enter Martian orbit in August 2027. A French-German rover will first land on Phobos, followed by two planned landings by the Japanese spacecraft to collect samples.
The probe will subsequently observe Mars' second moon, Deimos, before departing Martian orbit in November 2030. It is expected to return samples to Earth in July 2031.
Read More: Space startups secure record $20.8 billion funding as infrastructure bets surge, report shows
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi welcomed the launch, expressing hope that the historic mission would succeed. The launch was originally scheduled for 2024 but was delayed following the failure of the H3 rocket's maiden flight in 2023.
The international MMX mission seeks to determine how Mars' moons formed and advance technologies for future planetary exploration.

title: Guehi praises Manchester City team spirit
description: The defender insists players have  trust and belief  in the club despite charges
content:
The defender insists players have 'trust and belief' in the club despite charges
Manchester City defender Marc Guehi said on Monday a "pretty calm" squad have "a lot of trust and belief in the football club" despite the English giants being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.
City have made an impressive start to the season under new manager Enzo Maresca, winning all of their seven opening league games to lead the Premier League table by three points from champions Arsenal.
But those results have been achieved against the backdrop of a mass of guilty verdicts, which have led to calls for City to be hit with huge points deductions, colossal fines and even the stripping of some of their Premier League titles.
Significantly, however, no punishments have yet been announced and City, who have repeatedly denied wrongdoing, are appealing against the verdicts.
The only blemish to City's on field form so far in the current campaign has been a 4-2 defeat in the Champions League by title-holders Paris Saint-Germain, with City eager to returning to winning ways in Europe at home to AEK Athens on Tuesday.
England defender Guehi, speaking at a pre-match press conference, said: "The team spirit has been really good, every single person, player, staff and fans are backing us and it has been great to see.
"We're pretty calm. There's a lot of relaxed faces because we have a lot of trust and belief in the football club and what's been going on here."
"It can be very easy to be affected by the noise that's going on. But I'm so happy to see the team spirit, the team bonding and everyone taking to what's happening and just focusing on the football," he added.
Guehi, who joined City from Premier League rivals Crystal Palace in a £20 million ($26.6 million) move in January last year, was asked how he had come to trust the club.
"Ever since I've got to the club, the club have been fantastic with me," the 26-year-old replied. "The support that I've had, tough times on the pitch and off the pitch.
"I'm aware already of the success the club has already had in the past and I want to be someone who's part of the future success."
Questioned on whether Enzo Maresca's players had been given any details about why the City hierarchy were so confident of mounting a successful appeal against the decision of an independent commission, Guehi answered: "No, nothing's been said. The only thing that's been said is to focus on the football, which is all we can do."

title: Saudi Arabia intercepts  destroys Houthi ballistic missile  coalition s spokesperson says
description: Houthi attack kills 58 at Yemen government training camp  governor says
content:
Explosions heard in Saudi capital following security warning as Yemeni army says 129 Houthis killed in Taiz
Saudi Arabia on Tuesday intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis towards Riyadh, the Saudi-led coalition’s spokesperson Colonel Turki al-Maliki said, according to Al Jazeera .
Earlier, explosions were heard in Riyadh, following a security warning issued by the country’s National Early Warning Platform amid escalating hostilities with Yemen’s Houthis.
Saudi Civil Defence announced on X that an alert had been issued in Riyadh over a potential danger. “A warning has been issued by the National Early Warning Platform in Riyadh City to alert of a potential danger,” it said, urging residents to follow safety instructions.
The warning was followed by reports of explosions in the capital. There was no immediate official information on the cause of the explosions or possible casualties and damage.
Yemeni army says 129 Houthis killed in clashes, airstrikes in Taiz
The Yemeni army said on late Monday that 129 Houthi fighters were killed and 176 others wounded in clashes and airstrikes over the past two days in the southwestern province of Taiz.
In a statement, the army’s Taiz Military Axis Command said government forces continued their offensive against Houthi positions in the al-Misrakh district, south of Taiz city, for a second consecutive day.
The operation was carried out with support from local fighters and residents, inflicting heavy losses on the group, it added. The command said army units also conducted a raid on a Houthi position in the al-Aqrud front, killing and wounding several fighters.
It added that warplanes carried out 13 airstrikes Monday evening, targeting Houthi positions, weapons, military equipment, ammunition depots and gatherings across Taiz province. “Some 129 Houthi fighters were killed and 176 others wounded by our forces and airstrikes over the past 48 hours,” the command said.
There was no immediate comment from the Houthis on the army’s claims.
Yemen’s Houthis fire four ballistic missiles at central city as army repels southern attack
Yemen’s Houthi group fired four ballistic missiles at the government-held city of Marib on late Monday, while the army reported repelling a separate Houthi assault in the country’s south, according to local authorities and military officials.
Marib’s local government said the missiles targeted the densely populated city, which hosts large numbers of displaced people. The authorities gave no immediate details on casualties or damage.
The latest attack came a day after local authorities reported that the Houthis had fired eight ballistic missiles at Marib, without providing information on possible losses.
On October 15, the governorate also reported a Houthi attack involving nine ballistic missiles and seven other projectiles targeting residential neighborhoods. Marib, a major government stronghold and oil and gas production hub, is home to more than 2.2 million displaced people, according to government figures.
Separately, Yemen’s army said on Monday that its forces had repelled a Houthi assault on the Kahbub front in the western part of Lahj governorate in southern Yemen. The army-affiliated Southern Giants Brigades said in a statement that Houthi fighters launched successive waves of attacks, triggering hours of clashes involving various weapons.
Read: Iran offers help to end Saudi-Houthi conflict through dialogue
Backed by the Saudi-led coalition, government forces forced the attackers to retreat, killing and wounding Houthi fighters and destroying military equipment, according to the statement.
The brigades did not provide casualty figures.
Saudi-led coalition warns Houthis against using traditional boats to smuggle arms
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen warned the Houthi group on Monday against using traditional boats to smuggle weapons, missiles and military equipment into the country, citing risks to civilians and regional security.
The coalition’s Joint Forces Command stressed in a statement that the practice threatened security in Yemen and beyond.
It urged boat owners not to cooperate with the Houthis in transporting weapons and military equipment to Yemen’s coast, warning that their lives and property could be put at risk.
The statement gave no details of specific smuggling operations or intercepted weapons shipments.
Houthi attack kills 58 at Yemen government training camp, governor says
Fifty-eight people were killed, and more than 200 were injured after an attack on Monday by the Houthis on a government security forces training ​camp in Yemen's Shabwa province, Governor Awad al-Wazir said, as fighting in the impoverished ‌country intensifies.
Video verified by Reuters from Shabwa province showed injured people and bloodied bodies scattered across the ground. Wazir also said that 14 other people remained missing after the Houthi bombardment of the Al-Alam camp.
The ​Houthis and the internationally recognised government, which is backed by a Saudi-led coalition, ​have been trading attacks since the group advanced in September towards territory ⁠near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a shipping chokepoint at the mouth of the Red Sea.
Read more: Six injured as Houthi projectile hits Najran, says Saudi Civil Defence
Local ​authority sources who spoke on condition of anonymity said the Houthis had launched three ballistic ​missiles at security forces during a training exercise.
Shabwa, an energy-rich province in south-central coastal Yemen overlooking the Gulf of Aden, is home to the Balhaf liquefied natural gas facility, Yemen's largest industrial investment.
Houthi military ​spokesperson Yahya Saree said on X that the group had targeted the training camp, which ​he said was run by Saudi forces. The Saudi authorities did not immediately respond to a request ‌for ⁠comment.

title: Spurs claim first league win
description: Tottenham beat Coventry 3 1 to climb to 16th in the Premier League
content:
Tottenham beat Coventry 3-1 to climb to 16th in the Premier League.
James Maddison made a sensational return to Tottenham's starting line-up on Monday as Roberto De Zerbi's men beat Coventry 3-1 to claim their first Premier League win of the season.
On a feel-good night in London, Maddison marked his first start in 17 months with a spectacular early goal while Dejan Kulusevski returned to the matchday squad after missing the whole of last season.
Jack Rudoni levelled early in the second half but the home side were back in front just before the hour mark when Omar Marmoush lashed home his first goal for the club and substitute Ben Davies made the points safe in added time.
"I just wanted to play well, I just wanted to show my qualities and show what I bring to the team and what the team's missed in the last 18 months or whatever it is from my last start," Maddison told Sky Sports.
"So the gaffer asked me to play and he wanted to enjoy watching me from the side, so hopefully I did that."
The Spurs playmaker said he believed he could help propel his team up the table as they seek to avoid the indignity of last season, when they narrowly escaped relegation.
"I'm 29, I've still got plenty of years left, and I have a lot of self-belief, and I know that I have quality that can really help us in this league," he added.
Spurs came into the match rock bottom of the Premier League and with the unwanted record of being the only team in England's top six divisions without a league win this season despite a huge summer outlay.
De Zerbi had taken his squad to Marbella in southern Spain for some warm-weather training in a bid to kickstart their season and it paid off against Frank Lampard's competitive Coventry side.
Maddison, who ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in August 2025, just three months after injuring the same knee, put his side ahead in the 14th minute after fine work from Mohammed Kudus on the right.
Lurking just outside the penalty area, he received the ball from Kudus and sent it curling past Coventry goalkeeper Carl Rushworth and into the top corner, sparking wild scenes of delight among the home fans.
Maddison came close to doubling Spurs' lead after half an hour but his half-cross, half-shot curled narrowly wide.
Newly promoted Coventry were level in the 49th minute, courtesy of a Rudoni strike from close range.
Spurs lost the ball in the Coventry half and the visitors swept forward. Rudoni's effort hit a teammate but the ball fell kindly for him again and he drove home.
Just nine minutes later Spurs were back in front when Manchester City loanee Marmoush held off Milan van Ewijk before unleashing a powerful shot from distance.
Kulusevski, whose career was interrupted by a knee injury in May 2025, was brought off the substitutes' bench in the final minutes to a huge ovation from the home fans.
Spurs veteran Davies made the three points safe in the dying minutes, poking home from the edge of the penalty area.
The win lifts Spurs up to 16th in the table, buying De Zerbi much-needed breathing space.

title: Boland shines as South Africa stumble in second Test
description: The Australian paceman takes 4 31 to leave the hosts reeling at 97 5 after two rain hit days
content:
The Australian paceman takes 4-31 to leave the hosts reeling at 97-5 after two rain-hit days
Scott Boland does not get many chances to bowl for Australia in Test matches, but he showed again on Monday that when he gets the call he is ready to step up.
Boland took four for 31 to have South Africa tottering at 97 for five after two rain-hit days of the second Test at St George's Park.
"I like to play every game I can," the 37-year-old said, but admitted it was not always possible with Australia having three world-class fast bowlers ahead of him in skipper Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood.
All four seamers are in the top ten of the world Test bowling rankings.
But Boland got his opportunity in Gqeberha when Australia opted for an all-seam attack.
Although he had not played in a first-class match since March and had not appeared in a Test match since January, Boland said he kept sharp by working hard before the tour and during net practices since the team arrived in South Africa.
"My mindset is to find my line and length quickly," he said.
Boland did that to devastating effect when he took both wickets as South Africa slipped to 20 for two on a rain-ruined first day.
Then he struck early on Monday -- after rain delayed the start of play by six hours -- and again shortly before the close.
Boland's relentless accuracy left world Test champions South Africa in a precarious position as they sought to play their way back into the three-match series after losing the first Test in Durban by 214 runs.
"He doesn't miss his spot very often," said South African batting coach Ashwell Prince in comparing Boland to former South African opening bowler Vernon Philander.
"His balls are always on or around the top of the stumps so there's always that uncertainty (for batters)."
But Prince said he expected the South African bowlers to be similarly threatening.
"The ball is moving around and the pitch is a bit soft so there are some divots around. I like to think we have a few bowlers that can present the same challenges," he explained.
Only five runs were added to the overnight 20 for two before Boland struck in his second over of the day.
Debutant Marques Ackerman was caught behind by wicketkeeper Alex Carey for six, with the left-hander edging a ball bowled from around the wicket which seamed away off the pitch.
Matthew Breetzke, who together with Ackerman was brought into the side to strengthen the batting, made only four before he provided Carey with a third catch when he played a loose shot against Starc.
South Africa seemed to be clawing their way back into the contest as Ryan Rickelton (31) added 52 for the fifth wicket with Bavuma but Rickelton fell to a sensational one-handed catch at first slip by Matt Renshaw when Boland was brought back into the attack shortly before the close.
