title: PHC seeks Centre   s response over imposition of emergency  governor   s rule in K P
description: Notices sent to Attorny General  Advocate General  relevant authorities  petition argues move was unconstitutional
content:
Gohar says their mandate was snatched away, claiming that 12 party MNAs and 14 MPAs has been picked up
The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Tuesday issued notices to the federal government, the attorney general, the advocate general and other relevant authorities on petitions challenging the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), after petitioners’ counsel argued that the measures were unconstitutional and had been imposed without fulfilling the legal requirements.
A division bench comprising Justice Ijaz Anwar and Justice Muhammad Faheem Wali heard the petitions filed by Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and National Democratic Movement (NDM) leaders, including Mohsin Dawar.
During the hearing, the petitioners’ counsel argued that the provincial government had not lost control of the province and that the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule amounted to an attack on provincial autonomy and democracy.
Barrister Sameer Khosa, representing the petitioners, argued that no circumstances indicated the provincial government was unable to maintain control of the province. He said non-functional K-P chief minister Sohail Afridi and provincial assembly speaker Babar Saleem Swati were missing and their whereabouts were unknown.
Justice Anwar asked whether the petition sought their production before the court or their recovery. “Yes, we have made that request in the petition,” Khosa replied.
Citing the Supreme Court’s judgment in the Pir Sabir Shah case, Khosa argued that even if an emergency was imposed, the chief minister and cabinet would continue to function. In the present case, however, the chief minister, cabinet and advocate had been prevented from performing their duties and rendered inactive, he said.
Khosa urged the court to restore the provincial assembly and secure the release of Afridi and Swati.
Petitioners’ counsel PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja argued that governor’s rule and emergency had been imposed without fulfilling the legal requirements., urging the court to declare the measures illegal and restore the provincial assembly.
Read: PHC takes up challenge to emergency today
Raja maintained that Afridi remained the chief minister and that the provincial cabinet was still in place. He said that imposing an emergency required a resolution to be passed by the provincial assembly, adding that governor’s rule could only be justified if the provincial government was unable to function.
Raja also alleged that the sanctity of homes and the privacy of their occupants were being violated in the province.
Another petitioner’s counsel, Advocate Muazzam Butt, challenged the legality of both measures, arguing that the constitutional provisions invoked to impose emergency and governor’s rule had not been followed. He said provincial assembly approval had not been obtained for the imposition of emergency.
“If they claim that terrorism has increased, there is an Apex Committee for that,” Butt said, adding that the committee included representatives of the provincial and federal governments, the governor and security forces’ officials.
Butt also questioned the whereabouts of the governor’s report, after the president reportedly said governor’s rule had been imposed on the basis of a report submitted by the governor. The counsel argued that the authorities should explain where the report was and what it contained.
After hearing the petitioners, Justice Ijaz Anwar said the court was issuing notices to the federal government, the attorney general, the advocate general and other relevant parties.
Raja then requested the court to also issue an order on the interim relief sought by the petitioners. “We will examine it and pass an order,” the court said.
The hearing was adjourned until November 10.
Speaking to reporters outside the high court, Gohar said the PTI had challenged both emergency and governor’s rule, alleging that the measures were undemocratic and unconstitutional.
He said the mistreatment of party workers was continuing, adding that the party had always described terrorism as a menace and consistently supported the federal government in the fight against it.
“We had our own government, and our mandate was snatched away,” Gohar said.
He alleged that 12 PTI members of the National Assembly and 14 members of the provincial assembly had been picked up, claiming that raids were being conducted at party members’ homes and that they were being harassed.
Gohar said the office of a District Development Advisory Committee chairman had been demolished and plaques marking development projects completed by the party had been removed. He added that deputy commissioners, district police officers and officials at the advocate general’s office had been transferred on October 11.
Read more: Achakzai seeks K-P CM whereabouts
Opposition leader in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai said decisions should be made through the courts. “We want decisions to be made in courts. If that does not happen, matters will move to the streets,” he said, calling for peaceful protests against the government.
Achakzai said the 1973 Constitution had been drafted with great difficulty and recalled that Article 58(2) had led to the dissolution of four assemblies. He said the opposition had no enmity with either Nawaz Sharif or Asif Ali Zardari.
The K-P chief minister represented 40 million people and had been ridiculed, he said.
Referring to protests against inflation in France, Achakzai said millions of people had taken to the streets and set things on fire, but the French police had not fired a single bullet. “We will also have to stage peaceful protests against this government,” he said, adding that the final phase of the struggle had begun.
The federal government imposed emergency and governor’s rule in K-P on October 11 amid heightened political tensions involving the PTI. The move prompted legal challenges from the party and other opposition figures, who questioned its constitutional basis.
Gohar subsequently sought to amend his pending petition to challenge parliamentary resolutions passed by the National Assembly and Senate on October 14 and by a joint sitting of parliament on October 15, endorsing the emergency.
The application argued that the presidential action under Article 234 of the Constitution was unconstitutional and that subsequent parliamentary approval could not remedy a failure to meet the initial constitutional requirements. It maintained that Article 232 required a resolution from the provincial assembly for an emergency imposed on the grounds of internal disturbance, but no such resolution had been passed by the K-P Assembly.
Separately, petitions were filed seeking the recovery of Afridi, Speaker Babar Saleem Swati and PTI provincial president Junaid Akbar. In the chief minister’s case, the court issued notices to the government, police and other relevant authorities, directing them to submit replies within two days. In the petitions concerning Swati and Akbar, the authorities were directed to respond within 10 days.

title: South Korea orders stern response to any North Korean provocations amid border tensions
description: Military chief issues directive after Pyongyang threatens weapons deployments  propaganda broadcasts along border
content:
Military chief issues directive after Pyongyang threatens weapons deployments, propaganda broadcasts along border
South Korea's top military officer on Tuesday ordered troops to respond decisively to any North Korean provocations a day after Pyongyang threatened additional weapons deployments and renewed propaganda broadcasts along their heavily fortified border.
Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) Chairman General Jin Yong-sung issued the directive during a visit to a central front-line military unit, according to Yonhap News Agency .
Jin rejected North Korea's accusation that Seoul was responsible for escalating tensions following a September 21 landmine explosion that injured three South Korean soldiers. He said Pyongyang's attempt to portray legitimate South Korean military operations as provocations was unacceptable.
Read: South Korea calls for resuming dialogue with North
He ordered troops to respond firmly to further provocations and violations of the armistice agreement, including incursions across the Military Demarcation Line.
A day earlier, Kim Yo Jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, warned that Pyongyang could resume loudspeaker propaganda broadcasts and deploy additional tactical strike weapons along the border.
She accused Seoul of using warning shots and broadcasts to obstruct North Korea's border fortification work.
Read More: South Korea shifts focus to ‘peaceful coexistence' with North Korea instead of 'confrontation'
Jin described the September explosion involving North Korean-planted antipersonnel mines as a clear provocation and armistice violation.
The incident has heightened tensions around the Demilitarised Zone, which separates the two Koreas, which are technically still at war, as the 1950–1953 Korean War ended with an armistice rather than a formal peace treaty.

title: Two bodies found in Pasni  man killed in Quetta
description: Two bodies found in Pasni  man killed in Quetta
content:
Police arrest prime suspect in businessman Hashim Noorzai's murder
Police recovered two unidentified bodies from the Chakli area of Pasni, while separate incidents of violence in Quetta and Panjgur left one person dead and three others injured, respectively. In a separate development, police arrested the prime suspect in the murder of businessman Hashim Noorzai and recovered weapons and the vehicle allegedly used in the crime.
According to police, two bodies were found lying in the Chakli area of Pasni. Police took the bodies into custody and shifted them to a hospital. After completing the necessary legal formalities, the bodies were placed in the hospital mortuary for identification.
In Quetta, a man was shot dead by unidentified assailants on Qambrani Road. Police said Abdul Zahir, son of Faiz Muhammad and a resident of the area, was buying groceries from a shop when armed men opened fire on him before fleeing the scene.
He sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot. Police reached the site after receiving information about the incident and shifted the body to a hospital. Following the completion of medico-legal formalities, the body was handed over to his family.
A case was registered at the Kachi Baig police station, and the investigation was subsequently handed over to the Serious Crime Investigation Wing.
Meanwhile, three people were injured when unidentified gunmen opened fire on a vehicle near Star Chowk in the Tassap area of Panjgur. According to police, the vehicle was carrying three people when the assailants targeted it and escaped. Police rushed to the scene and shifted the injured to a hospital for treatment. title: Lawyers boycott courtsover governor's rule | The Express Tribune
description:
Lawyers boycott courts
over governor's rule
content:
Bar Council terms emergency unconstitutional, demands withdrawal
Lawyers across Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa boycotted court proceedings on Monday on the call of the K-P Bar Council to protest the imposition of governor's rule and an emergency in the province.
The boycott kept lawyers away from courts in various districts, disrupting hearings and affecting routine judicial business. The Bar Council termed the imposition of governor's rule and the emergency unconstitutional and illegal, demanding that the federal government immediately withdraw its decision.
The province-wide strike was announced as a mark of protest against the federal government's move, which the legal body said raised serious questions regarding constitutional and legal requirements.
According to the Bar Council, the decision warranted a review by the federal government, which should reverse the measures to address the concerns surrounding their constitutional and legal validity.
Responding to the council's call, lawyers did not appear before courts in several districts, affecting the hearing of cases and other judicial proceedings.
The protest was aimed at formally registering the legal community's objections to the imposition of the emergency and governor's rule, while urging the authorities to resolve the situation in accordance with the Constitution and the law.
Meanwhile, the imposition of the emergency and governor's rule in K-P has also been challenged before the Peshawar High Court through multiple petitions.
The petitioners have questioned the constitutional validity of the measures and sought the annulment of the relevant government notifications and parliamentary resolutions.
The legal challenges have brought the legality of the federal government's decision before the high court, where the petitioners have called for judicial intervention.
The K-P Bar Council reiterated its demand that the federal government withdraw its decision, stressing the need to resolve the controversy surrounding the province's constitutional and legal status.

title: Assembly seeks recovery of Hindu girl
description: Assembly seeks recovery of Hindu girl
content:
Lawmakers demand action over alleged abduction, forced conversion and underage marriage in Sindh
Minority members of the Balochistan Assembly on Monday protested the alleged abduction of a 14-year-old Hindu girl from Sibi, her alleged forced religious conversion and marriage in Sindh, demanding her immediate recovery.
Taking notice of the matter, Speaker Captain (retd) Abdul Khaliq Achakzai directed Provincial Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langove to contact the Sindh government and take immediate steps to resolve the issue.
Raising the matter on a point of order during the assembly session, PML-N MPA Dr Ashok Kumar said Bindiya, a member of the Hindu community, had allegedly been abducted from Sibi and taken to Bakhshapur in Sindh, where she was reportedly converted to Islam and married.
Dr Ashok Kumar pointed out that the Balochistan Assembly had enacted legislation concerning underage marriages, under which a 14-year-old girl could not legally marry.
PPP parliamentary secretary Sanjay Kumar said he possessed evidence establishing the girl's age as 14. He added that her mother had been in a distressed condition since the girl was taken away, while her family had repeatedly approached community representatives for help in securing her recovery.
National Party chief Dr Abdul Malik Baloch termed the matter extremely serious and condemned the incident. He said people belonging to all religions and ethnic communities living in Balochistan were equal and called for immediate contact with the Sindh government to resolve the issue.
Provincial Minister Ali Madad Jattak also condemned the alleged abduction and religious conversion, saying the government stood against injustice and would oppose oppression wherever it occurred in Balochistan.
Speaker Achakzai observed that if the girl had entered into a court marriage, her age would need to be examined, while any marriage conducted through tribal arrangements would require appropriate action if unlawful.
Home Minister informed the assembly that the government had taken notice of the matter and was contacting the Sindh government.
In a separate development, Speaker Achakzai sought a report from the Nasirabad commissioner over the proposed leasing of land at the Cattle Farm area and directed police officials to investigate pending murder cases.
PML-N MPA Sardar Abdul Rahman Khetran said a landowner and his son had been abducted in Barkhan. Although the father was later released, his son was allegedly tortured and shot dead.
He urged the government to ensure registration of an FIR, even if the victim's family was too frightened to pursue the case. The speaker directed the relevant deputy inspector general of police to explain the delay and ensure registration of the case.
Jamaat-e-Islami parliamentary secretary Abdul Majeed Badini said around 2,300 acres had been allocated to the agriculture and livestock departments at Cattle Farm in Nasirabad about 50 years ago.

title: Four dead as floods sweep eastern Spain
description: Four dead as floods sweep eastern Spain
content:
Torrential rain battered eastern Spain, unleashing severe flooding that left at least four people dead in recent days, inundated streets and forced many residents to stay indoors, authorities said Monday.
The downpours, which pummelled parts of Spain's Mediterranean coast particularly hard, dumped as much as 700 litres of rain per square metre (155 US gallons per square yard) in just 24 hours in some areas of the Valencia region.
Floodwaters swept away parked cars, submerged roads and cut off residents, some of whom had to be airlifted to safety by emergency crews.
"We are talking about three deaths," Valencia regional president Juan Francisco Perez Llorca told reporters Monday, while urging caution as authorities assessed the damage.
Two of the victims were found in the coastal resort of Oliva, one of the areas worst hit by Sunday night's storms.
One was a 79-year-old woman found in her home, while another was a man who suffered a fatal heart attack at a local campsite.
The third victim was a man who drowned Sunday while swimming at a beach in Sagunto.
Firefighters in neighbouring Catalonia had on Sunday also reported the death of a woman who fell into a rain-swollen stream.
Security forces carried out more than 400 rescues in the Valencia region, both by air and land, according to government representative Pilar Bernabe.
The heavy downpour, which also lashed the Balearic Islands and Catalonia, prompted authorities to order around 100 municipalities to remain indoors for several hours.
Most restrictions were lifted by early afternoon as conditions improved, the regional government said.
Members of Spain's military emergency unit were helping rescue and evacuation efforts, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said on X, pledging the government's "full support" and whatever personnel and resources were needed.
Scientists say human-driven climate change is intensifying the Mediterranean storms that typically hit eastern Spain in autumn as the sea absorbs heat during the summer, leading to increased evaporation and heavier rainfall.
National weather agency AEMET announced Friday that last month was mainland Spain's hottest September on record, after the country registered its warmest summer between June and August. AFP

title: Four soldiers of UN backed force in Haiti missing after ambush
description: Four soldiers of UN backed force in Haiti missing after ambush
content:
Four Salvadoran soldiers serving with a UN-backed force in Haiti are missing after their armored vehicle was ambushed near the capital Port-au-Prince, officials said Monday.
The attack happened on Sunday and targeted members of the Gang Suppression Force (GFS), which is tasked with helping stabilize the Caribbean nation plagued by violence and political chaos.
US envoy Mike Waltz told the Security Council that the soldiers were ambushed as they were returning to base from a market outside Port-au-Prince.
"These thugs attacked their armored vehicle with hundreds of bullets and explosives. By God's grace, we believe four of the men survived, but they do remain unaccounted for," he said.
"To our four Salvadoran brothers in arms. You are not forgotten. The GSF is with you. The United States is with you, and we will bring you home," Waltz said.
Egriselda Lopez, the representative for El Salvador, said efforts were ongoing to establish contact with the four soldiers and determine their whereabouts.
"El Salvador strongly condemns this attack against our deployed personnel, and we express our deep concern regarding the situation of the four personnel, our compatriots," she said.
Stephane Dujarric, spokesman for Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, said: "We condemn such kidnapping and we call for their immediate and safe release."
Haiti, the poorest country in the Americas, has long been in crisis but the situation has deteriorated in recent years as gangs step up killings, kidnappings, rape and child recruitment.
The GSF is being slowly deployed to assist overwhelmed local police. The mission is intended to reach 5,500 personnel.
Currently, it has only 2,000 members from six contributing countries, according to Jack Christofides, special representative for the GSF.
He told the Security Council there were signs of reduced gang control in areas where the GSF is active, but urged caution.
"We should recognize this progress without overstating it. Gangs are testing the GSF. We recorded an increase in hostile incidents against our force from two to 15 in a single month," Christofides said.
Earlier this month, Haitian authorities indefinitely postponed elections that were due to be held in December.
The country has not held elections since 2016, and its last president, assassinated in 2021, has not been replaced. AFP

He said bilateral trade last year rose 21% and grew by more than 10% in the first eight months of this year. The free trade agreement between Iran and the Eurasian Economic Union – a group of post-Soviet states – which took effect in May 2025 is also helping strengthen economic ties, he added.
Lavrov said Russian specialists are gradually returning to Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant, noting "significant prospects in the field of hydrocarbon extraction and redistribution." He also said that Russian contractors continued engineering work on the planned Rasht-Astara railway.

title: Putin floats meeting with Trump  Xi on ending war in Ukraine

The Kremlin said on Monday that Russian President Vladimir Putin, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping could hold a three-way meeting on the sidelines of next month's APEC summit in China and that a potential meeting had come up in talks.

title: France places Paris  Nice under partial curfews
description: France places Paris  Nice under partial curfews
content:
PM blames 'ultra-left' for exploiting protests
French authorities set curfews in parts of several cities on Monday, including Paris, Lille and Nice, as they faced pressure over security failings after a weekend of riots and looting stemming from nationwide anti-government protests.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu had ruled out a blanket curfew in Paris but not a state of emergency, and had said it was more appropriate for now to apply partial and localised curfews.
"My determination to restore order is absolute," he told reporters.
Paris police said they had issued orders barring protests in certain areas of the French capital from 8pm (1800 GMT) and had issued a curfew around the Place de la Republique and Les Halles from 11:00 p.m. Both would remain in effect until 6 a.m. on Tuesday morning.
"A police deployment is in place to ensure strict compliance with these measures," the police said in a statement.
A source in Lecornu's office said a curfew for minors had been set between 8 p.m. and 6 a.m. for the next two days in Lille, Douai, Wattignies and Denain with the agreement of the local mayors.
In Nice, mayor Eric Ciotti said in a video posted online that he had signed an order installing a curfew for minors in central Nice overnight.
Marseille banned gatherings and demonstrations. French unions meanwhile called for a new round of strikes and rallies on November 5.
The weekend of looting and violence between some protesters and police followed weeks of student demonstrations, rocking France six months ahead of its next presidential election and highlighting pressures from a weak economy and surging debt.
Lecornu blamed far-left groups for some of France's worst unrest in years. "There is, after all, a far-left movement that wants to cause - we can't put it any more strongly - profound unrest in the country in the run-up to the presidential election," he said.
Hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon urged him to provide evidence. "Otherwise, he should apologise, keep quiet and stop fanning the flames of unrest," he said on X.
The Federation of Trade and Retail said almost 3,000 shops had been affected over the weekend.
"Behind every ransacked shop are business owners, employees and families who have seen years of work and effort wiped out in a matter of hours," it added, calling for social security and tax relief for affected businesses.
Lecornu said the government would provide furlough measures from Tuesday.
Standing before a boarded-up shopfront, Gerard Nouchi, manager of two clothing stores in Marseille, said there weren't enough police to stop the looters.
"They trashed everything, broke things, insulted us," Nouchi said. "It was like a real tornado."
The government ordered platforms selling looted goods to take down announcements and collaborate to prosecute resellers, Junior Digital Minister Anne Le Hénanff wrote on X.
Some 2,400 people were arrested and one protester died from a cardiac arrest on Saturday while nearly 1,000 officers were injured, according to the Interior Ministry.
French assets were underperforming broader European markets on Monday, though moves were more contained than at some other moments of recent political friction.
Tensions in President Emmanuel Macron's fragile government over apparent security shortcomings - coming as the government needs to pass a budget bill to rein in its finances - could further unsettle investors.

title: US SC snubs bid to revive plea deal for 9 11 mastermind
description: US SC snubs bid to revive plea deal for 9 11 mastermind
content:
Case involves three men detained at Guantanamo Bay
The US Supreme Court declined on Monday to hear a bid by Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, the accused mastermind of the September 11, 2001, attacks, to revive a 2024 agreement that would have spared him the death penalty in exchange for a guilty plea - a deal scrapped by former Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin.
The justices turned away appeals by Mohammed and two co-defendants who had also signed plea agreements of a lower court's ruling that upheld Austin's decision to void the deals. The US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit rejected an argument that Austin, who served under former President Joe Biden, had acted too late.
The Supreme Court's action marks the latest milestone in a military prosecution of the detainees held in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, that has been beset by two decades of legal gridlock.
In August, a US Air Force judge set the trial for Mohammed and his co-defendants for June 2028.
Mohammed remains the most well-known inmate at the Guantanamo detention facility, which was set up in 2002 by then-US President George W. Bush to house foreign terrorism suspects following the 9/11 attacks, which killed nearly 3,000 people. Mohammed is accused of orchestrating the plot to fly hijacked passenger jetliners into the World Trade Center in New York City and into the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia.
Monday's Supreme Court action "clears the path for holding those responsible for the September 11 attacks accountable.

title: Army major martyred in IED blast in Pasni
description: Army major martyred in IED blast in Pasni
content:
Army major martyred in IED blast in Pasni
Security forces carried out two separate operations in central and southern Balochistan and eliminated four terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan, a term used to refer to separatist outfits. During one of the operations, a major also embraced martyrdom in an explosion.
According to a statement issued by the military's media wing, security forces conducted an intelligence-based operation (IBO) on October 18 in the general area of Jattakabad in district Kalat.
During the operation, troops effectively engaged the terrorists' location and, after an intense exchange of fire, killed four terrorists. A large cache of arms and ammunition was also recovered during the operation, the news release issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said.
Security forces also conducted a series of clearance operations in the general area of Shadi Kaur of tehsil Pasni in district Gwadar. During one of the operations, the lead force component, led by Major Wajahat Waheed, was targeted by an improvised explosive device (IED).
The IED blast resulted in the martyrdom of Major Waheed. Major Wajahat Waheed was 34-year-old and was a resident of Lahore, the ISPR said.
According to the military's media wing, the IBOs were carried out based on intelligence reports regarding the presence of multiple terrorist hideouts in the general areas of Shadi Kaur and Jattakabad and were aimed at removing the threat posed by the terrorists to the local population.
"Sanitisation operations will continue to eliminate any other terrorists found in the area. The relentless counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of Azm-e-Istehkam will continue at full pace.
"Security forces and law enforcement agencies remain committed to eliminating the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country," it further said.
President Asif Ali Zardari on Monday paid tribute to the security forces for eliminating terrorists of Fitna al-Hindustan in different areas of Kalat and Gwadar districts of Balochistan.
The president, in a statement, expressed deep grief over the martyrdom of Major Wajahat Waheed. He commended Major Waheed's supreme sacrifice for the defense of the motherland and the eradication of terrorism, extending his heartfelt condolences and sympathies to the bereaved family.

title: Houthi attack kills 53 at Yemen training camp

content:
Three ballistic missiles launched at security forces during training exercise
Fifty-three people were killed and 200 were injured in an attack on Monday by the Iran-aligned Houthis on a government security forces training camp in Yemen's Shabwa province, according to the local authority, ?as fighting in the impoverished country intensifies.
Video verified by Reuters from Shabwa province showed injured people and bloodied bodies scattered across the ground.
The Houthis and the internationally recognised government, which is backed by a Saudi-led coalition, have been trading attacks since the group advanced in September towards territory near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a shipping chokepoint at the mouth of the Red Sea.
Local authority sources who spoke on condition of anonymity said the Houthis had launched three ballistic missiles at security forces during a training exercise.
Shabwa, an energy-rich province in south-central coastal Yemen overlooking the Gulf of Aden, is home to the Balhaf liquefied natural gas facility, Yemen's largest industrial investment.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said on X that the group had targeted the training camp, which he said was run by Saudi forces. The Saudi authorities did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Government forces this month began ?a campaign aimed at recapturing areas controlled by the Houthis, recovering ground near the strait, while the group besieges Taiz, the last major urban stronghold of anti-Houthi forces in the southern highland area of Yemen.
The conflict in Yemen has become another front line in the wider US-Israeli war on Iran as the Houthis have escalated their attacks on Saudi Arabia, the world's largest crude exporter, targeting Riyadh's international airport and the state oil company Saudi Aramco.
War broke out in Yemen in 2014 when the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa, driving the government south. A Saudi-led military intervention the following year led to a bloody stalemate until the sides agreed a 2022 truce that held until this year.
Yemen is already one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, with aid agencies warning of rapidly deteriorating conditions there.

title: PM asks FBR to plug tax gap amid pruning plans
description: PM asks FBR to plug tax gap amid pruning plans
content:
The federal government on Monday dropped the idea of setting up a new tax agency but decided to compulsorily retire non-performing officers by amending the Civil Servants Act, which would allow it to retrench bureaucrats as part of any restructuring.
Chairing a high-level review meeting, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed that the pace of reforms within the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) be accelerated, noting that the initial results of the ongoing reforms were encouraging.
The prime minister emphasised that the FBR must continuously enhance its institutional capacity to effectively bridge the tax gap. He stressed that technology, effective professional training, transparency and accountability must remain central to ensuring that the ongoing reforms yield concrete results.
"It is the responsibility of FBR officers to improve their performance in line with the expectations of the nation," a statement from the Prime Minister's Office quoted Shehbaz as saying. "The ongoing reforms were in the broader interest of the state, and the process would continue in any case," the prime minister added.
The prime minister called for zero-tolerance and indiscriminate action against corrupt elements within the department. Staff showing genuine improvement in conduct and performance should be given an opportunity to reform, while there should be no room for corruption or underperformance, he emphasised.
Officials briefed the meeting on the use of technology, procedural workflows and human resource management. They said the FBR reforms had narrowed the estimated tax gap from 6% to 5% of GDP, while the effective use of technology had substantially reduced the discretionary powers of FBR officials.
According to officials who attended the meeting, it was decided to overhaul the FBR's human resources to make the organisation more efficient, less top-heavy and more taxpayer-friendly by removing officers who were either underperforming or falling short of professional benchmarks.
The prime minister directed that action be taken against corrupt elements without discrimination. The FBR was instructed to submit a report on human resource restructuring and reorganisation to the prime minister within this week.
Earlier this month, debate was triggered after the idea of setting up an entirely new organisation was floated at a high-level meeting. Some participants were of the view that setting up a new organisation would take years and that, by the time it became fully operational, it could develop problems similar to those faced by the existing FBR.
After The Express Tribune published a story about the proposed new organisation, the Inland Revenue Service Officers Association (IRSOA) threatened to observe a pen-down strike. The IRSOA later withdrew the threat after seeking assurances from senior officials.
Officials told The Express Tribune that Shehbaz expressed displeasure over the officers' conduct, saying there was no room for an association that could blackmail the government. The FBR's senior management said action could be taken against officers for illegally establishing a collective bargaining body.
The government, however, decided to restructure the FBR's human resources both vertically and horizontally. Surplus and non-performing officers would be sent packing. The meeting was told that amendments to the Civil Servants Act had been pending before the National Assembly since 2024.
The government also decided to fast-track the parliamentary approval of these amendments to secure the legal authority to compulsorily retire tax officials, a senior government official confirmed to The Express Tribune.
According to a proposed new clause 22 A and 22 B, which will be applicable on all service groups, the government will have powers to declare any officer redundant as a result of any restructuring and reorganisation, give him or her a severance package and to compulsory retire the person.
The clause 22B states, the federal government may at any time decide full or partial abolition, restructuring or reorganisation of a division, department or office and in respect of civil servants liable to be affected thereby declare the posts, cadres, or nomenclatures of civil servants to be abolished and incumbent civil servants thereof rendered surplus or redundant.
The sub clause 2 of clause 22B states, on receipt of decision of the federal government, the appointing authority shall offer a severance package to the civil servant declared redundant who shall be obliged to accept it, but can file an appeal only against the monetary value.
According to sub-clause 3 of the clause 22B, the service of a civil servant who stands redundant shall be liable to termination by the appointing authority. It says that provided that nothing contained in the Civil Servants Act, the rules, or any other law for the time being in force, agreement, contract or the terms and conditions of service or any order or judgment of any court or tribunal shall limit or abridge the power of the federal government or the appointing authority to decide full or partial abolition, restructuring or reorganisation of a division, department or office to declare the posts, cadres or nomenclatures of civil servants to be abolished or to decide rendering surplus or redundant civil servants against whom departmental or criminal proceedings are pending finalisation, however, the payment of severance package to them shall be subject to final decision of department.
Meanwhile, an FBR statement later said that two Inland Revenue Service officers - one in BS-20 and the other in BS-19 - had been suspended, while two other IRS officers in BS-20 had been repatriated to FBR Headquarters for further investigation over an unauthorised press statement and a call to halt official work.

title: Naqvi says peace more important than war
description: Naqvi says peace more important than war
content:
Naqvi says peace more important than war
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday said Pakistan had made every possible effort to ease tensions between Iran and the United States and bring both sides to the negotiating table, stressing that winning peace was more important than winning a war.
Addressing the 8th Global Security Forum in Doha, Naqvi said the conflict had created serious risks for the Middle East and the wider world. He said Pakistan had chosen the path of peace at a critical time and continued its diplomatic efforts despite moments of extreme tension.
Highlighting the role of Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, the minister said his personal efforts, relations with world leaders and continued engagement with all sides had helped open channels for dialogue.
Naqvi said he had participated in the peace efforts alongside Field Marshal Asim during visits to Tehran and meetings with senior Iranian officials, where he witnessed the difficulties involved in the negotiations. Despite the challenges, he said, Pakistan continued talking, listening and working to build trust.
"Peace is not achieved in one meeting; it requires patience, trust and continuous efforts," he said, adding that Pakistan and Qatar had never sought credit for their mediation efforts but aimed to prevent further conflict and save innocent lives.
Recalling the diplomatic process, Naqvi said Pakistan hosted the Islamabad talks in April, followed by the signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding in June. Pakistan and Qatar subsequently held discussions at a summit in Switzerland, where, he said, Field Marshal Asim and Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani worked for more than 16 hours without a break.
"There were no cameras, no announcements, only two men who refused to let the talks fail," he said, describing the meeting as an example of the commitment shown by the two mediating countries.
Naqvi also praised Qatar for continuing to engage with different sides when others chose to take positions, saying Pakistan had worked closely with Doha to promote dialogue and regional stability.
He outlined three lessons from the mediation efforts: the doors to dialogue should never be closed, trust was essential for negotiations, and peace required sincere efforts from all sides. No single country, he said, could achieve regional peace alone.
Referring to the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, Naqvi described it as a pact for defence rather than war. He said lasting peace was impossible while neighbouring countries remained caught in conflict.
Turning to counterterrorism, the minister said Pakistan understood the cost of insecurity, having lost thousands of citizens, soldiers and police personnel. Describing terrorism as a common enemy, he called for stronger international cooperation, improved intelligence-sharing and joint efforts to defeat the threat.
He also highlighted Pakistan's contribution to United Nations peacekeeping missions, saying its soldiers and police personnel had helped protect civilians, support local police and restore peace in conflict-affected countries.
"We do not want credit for stopping wars. We want a future where wars do not start," Naqvi said, reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to dialogue, peace and cooperation.

title: Russia offers a diplomatic off ramp in Pak Afghan standoff
description: Russia offers a diplomatic off ramp in Pak Afghan standoff
content:
Moscow signals readiness to help ease friction
Russia on Monday offered to help defuse tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan, signaling a potentially greater diplomatic role for Moscow at a time when relations between Islamabad and Kabul have deteriorated sharply over the issue of cross-border terrorism.
Speaking at a roundtable discussion on Pakistan-Russia relations at the Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad (ISSI), Russian Ambassador to Pakistan Albert Khorev expressed concern over the growing tensions between the two neighbours and said Moscow was ready to contribute towards easing their differences.
Khorev said the continued closure of the Pakistan-Afghanistan border was also affecting Pakistan's trade connectivity with Central Asia and Russia. He hoped the border would reopen and tensions between Islamabad and Kabul would subside.
Significantly, the Russian envoy revealed that Pakistan-Afghanistan tensions figured prominently during Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev's visit to Islamabad last week. He also referred to recent visits by senior Russian security officials to Pakistan, Afghanistan and India, indicating that Moscow was stepping up its diplomatic engagement in the region.
Kolokoltsev last week became the first Russian interior minister to visit Pakistan, holding talks with the civilian and military leadership, including Field Marshal Asim Munir. His visit coincided with Russian Foreign Intelligence Service chief Sergei Naryshkin's trip to Kabul for talks with senior Taliban officials. Meanwhile, a senior Russian Security Council official was in New Delhi for consultations.
Moscow's willingness to play a role between Islamabad and Kabul is significant because Russia has developed perhaps the closest relationship with the Taliban among major global powers.
Russia last year became the first country to formally recognise the Taliban government in Afghanistan. Moscow has since expanded political and security engagement with Kabul. In May this year, the two sides also signed a military-technical cooperation arrangement, although its full scope has not been made public.
Russia's approach towards the Taliban has at times differed sharply from Pakistan's increasingly critical position. Those differences were evident at the Moscow Format consultations on Afghanistan earlier this month. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov praised the Taliban-led administration, while Pakistan continued to press Kabul for concrete action against the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
The meeting failed to produce a joint communique, with Pakistan later saying the Afghan side had not accepted the language concerning terrorist networks operating from Afghanistan.
Islamabad accuses the Taliban authorities of allowing the TTP to use Afghan territory to plan and launch attacks inside Pakistan, a charge Kabul denies. Pakistan has insisted that any meaningful dialogue must be accompanied by concrete and verifiable action against such groups.
Despite those differences, Islamabad has left the door open for a possible Russian role. At his weekly briefing on Thursday, Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said Pakistan valued its engagement with Russia on Afghanistan and regional security.
He said Islamabad would welcome sincere efforts by friendly countries that could address Pakistan's legitimate security concerns, although he stressed that the Foreign Office was not aware of any separate formal Russian mediation initiative.
"Such efforts should be meaningful and yield tangible progress," the spokesperson said, adding that progress ultimately depended on concrete and verifiable Taliban action against terrorist groups operating from Afghanistan.
Pakistan's Ambassador to Russia Faisal Niaz Tirmizi, who also addressed Monday's discussion, stressed the need for expanding bilateral relationship and efforts to remove practical hurdles in ties.
On trade and connectivity, Ambassador Tirmizi prioritised visa facilitation, direct flights, and arrangements to remove banking and payment barriers. He outlined preparations for a bilateral business forum, including advance meetings between companies, and discussed transport links through Iran, Afghanistan and China.
He called for stronger partnerships between universities, increased student mobility, and cooperation in science, engineering and agriculture. He also highlighted Russian-language education, cultural exchanges, and closer links between the media and creative sectors of the two countries.
Pakistan and Russia have stepped up engagement in recent years in trade, energy, connectivity, counterterrorism and security. The two sides agreed earlier this year to work towards an economic cooperation programme extending through 2030, while officials have also discussed rail connectivity linking Pakistan with Russia and Central Asia.
The latest Russian diplomatic activity comes as Moscow seeks a larger role in Afghanistan and the wider region while Islamabad attempts to persuade regional countries to use their influence with the Taliban to address Pakistan's security concerns.

title: Pakistan  KSA satisfied with alliance progress
description: Pakistan  KSA satisfied with alliance progress
content:
CDF Asim Munir, Saudi envoy discuss regional security Both sides stress stronger defence cooperation DG ISPR say
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia on Monday expressed satisfaction over the progress made under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and underscored the need to strengthen defence cooperation, institutional linkages and strategic coordination.
The understanding came during a meeting between Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir and newly-appointed Saudi Ambassador to Pakistan Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy at General Headquarters in Rawalpindi, according to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).
The two sides discussed matters of mutual interest and regional security dynamics, with particular emphasis on further strengthening defence collaboration. Field Marshal Asim congratulated the ambassador on his appointment and expressed confidence that his tenure would reinforce longstanding ties between the two countries, rooted in shared faith, mutual trust and strategic partnership.
"Both the dignitaries expressed satisfaction over the progress made under the framework of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and underscored the importance of strengthening defence collaboration, institutional linkages and strategic coordination," the ISPR statement said.
The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed on August 7 by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. It followed the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed by Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in September 2025.
In an interview with Independent Arabia, ISPR Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry described the Makkah alliance as a defensive arrangement aimed at deterring aggression and promoting regional stability. He stressed that the alliance had no offensive intent and was intended to send a clear message to elements seeking to destabilise the region.
However, he warned that any direct or indirect attack on Pakistan, Saudi Arabia or Turkiye would trigger a collective response under the agreement. "The response will be collective," he said, adding that the alliance was intended to protect its members against threats to their security and territorial integrity.
His remarks came amid heightened regional tensions following missile and drone attacks by Yemen's Houthi group on Saudi Arabia. Chaudhry said collective deterrence would come into play if diplomatic efforts failed to prevent further escalation.
He said Pakistan considered Saudi Arabia's sovereignty, territorial integrity and the security of Islam's holiest sites non-negotiable, adding that Islamabad would continue providing whatever support was needed to safeguard the kingdom.
"The Saudis' sovereignty and territorial integrity, security, and foremost, the security of the Haramain Sharifain is paramount. It's non-negotiable. It's absolute as far as Pakistan is concerned," the chief military spokesperson stated.
The spokesperson urged Muslim countries to unite and avoid actions that could intensify hostilities. Escalation served neither regional interests nor the wider Muslim world, he said, calling instead for restraint and negotiations.
"We need to stop attacking each other," he said, adding that Pakistan's political and military leadership had been working towards that objective. "We need to come to a negotiated outcome. If this failed this instrument of collective deterrence of the Makkah alliance will come into play, as it is coming into play."
Chaudhry said military cooperation between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had existed for decades, predating the Makkah alliance, and covered multiple areas. He declined to disclose operational details, citing the confidentiality of military arrangements and their tactical and strategic considerations.
He reiterated that the alliance was purely defensive and would remain so. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye shared an interest in peace, stability and prosperity, while their longstanding relations and mutual trust had helped the arrangement develop rapidly, he said.
The military spokesperson said the alliance was not necessarily restricted to its founding members and remained open to countries sharing its commitment to collective deterrence, regional security and stability. However, decisions on potential expansion rested with the leadership of the three countries.
Asked about reports that Egypt and Syria had expressed interest in joining, Chaudhry said the matter would be considered at the appropriate political, strategic and military levels. He did not provide a timeline for any expansion.
On the possibility of Pakistan providing direct military support to Yemen's government, the spokesperson said he did not know whether Islamabad had received an official request. He added that the government would assess and respond to any such request.
Chaudhry also highlighted Pakistan's diplomatic engagement with countries involved in the regional conflicts, including Iran, saying Islamabad had sought to reduce tensions and secure a negotiated, peaceful outcome. He said these efforts would continue to prevent further escalation in the region.

The body of a 21-year-old mill worker was found buried in a pit behind a local mill in Chak 97-RB, within the jurisdiction of Balochni police station, after human remains were spotted nearby, police said.
The victim, Kashif Nawaz, a resident of Dera Ismail Khan, was allegedly murdered by unidentified individuals, who buried his body after digging a pit behind the mill where he worked.
According to the police report, Kashif's mobile phone had been switched off, prompting his brother, Bilal Sakhi Nawaz, to visit the mill and inquire about him.
Bilal had previously worked at the same mill before leaving for his hometown.
He was told that Kashif had not been reporting for work, raising concerns about his whereabouts. Bilal subsequently contacted police to seek help in locating his brother.
Meanwhile, Balochni Station House Officer Mohsin Abbas Heral received information that human body parts had been found behind the mill.
Police officers, including Khurrianwala Deputy Superintendent of Police Rana Mazharul Haq, reached the site.
The officers took the remains into custody and recovered Kashif's body from a nearby pit.

Speaking at the Pakistan Textile Exporters Association (PTEA), she said German industry was actively seeking to diversify supply chains and establish new global partnerships, creating opportunities for Pakistani businesses to strengthen their presence in international markets.

These initiatives were aimed at improving productivity, working conditions and the competitiveness of Pakistani exports.
"GIZ is working across different sectors of the economy to improve productivity and working conditions, and to enhance the quality and volume of Pakistan's exportable surplus," she said.
The ambassador also highlighted the establishment of a dedicated Pakistan Desk at the German-Emirati Joint Council for Commerce and Industry.
The desk aims to connect German companies with trade, investment and market opportunities in Pakistan, helping businesses explore potential partnerships.
He said Germany remained Pakistan's largest trading partner in the European Union, with bilateral trade exceeding $4.23 billion last year.

content:
Provincial cabinet briefed on value enhancement plans
The Punjab cabinet on Monday approved key features of an industrial development and export promotion programme envisaging investments of Rs1.995 trillion and creation of more than 162,000 jobs.
The programme presented by Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb at a cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif envisages investment of Rs1.089 trillion from the provincial government and Rs906 billion from the private sector.
It was shared in a briefing that the programme focuses on industrial infrastructure, cluster development, export competitiveness, value-chain transformation, mechanisation in agriculture and livestock, and public-private partnerships.
It also includes support for existing industries, e-business, e-commerce, garments, plug-and-play facilities, and testing and certification services for leather, footwear and sports goods.
Material-testing laboratories for the cutlery, handmade tools, ceramics and fan industries, along with export financing for horticulture and floriculture, are also part of the initiative.
Agriculture processing parks will be established in Sargodha, Khanewal, Okara and Bhakkar.
The programme also covers wheat value enhancement, meat and milk value chains, skills development, citrus, potato and mango value addition, tourism and aquaculture.
The cabinet approved the establishment of horticulture authorities in 20 districts.
It approved subsidies for a new phase of the Chief Minister Punjab Green Tractor Programme, under which the provincial government will provide Rs9.5b for 10,000 high-powered tractors. More than 250,000 applications have been received for the programme. Around 25,000 tractors have so far been delivered to farmers. The cabinet also approved a waiver of late registration fees under the scheme.
The cabinet approved subsidies for Phase IV of the low-powered Green Tractor Programme.
Subsidies were also approved for an agricultural transformation project in Thal.
The government will provide Rs7.6b for drip irrigation, solar power, water storage and other facilities across 10,000 acres in Mankera and Layyah.
The cabinet approved an allocation of Rs60b for the Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar loan programme. The chief minister rejected a proposal to impose stamp duty for the scheme.
She ordered immediate payment of the amount required to make medical equipment functional in hospitals. The cabinet approved funds to clear essential liabilities of the specialised healthcare and medical education department.
It also approved the donation of six clinic-on wheels vehicles to Gilgit-Baltistan and 15 to Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
Revision of traffic fines under the Punjab Ring Road Authority were approved, with higher penalties proposed for speeding, overloading, pedestrian-crossing violations and other offences.
The cabinet also approved amendments to an air-quality management project to provide electric trucks and anti-smog guns, along with funding for the expansion of public services and development schemes.
Other decisions included approval of the establishment of the Maryam Nawaz Medical College and Teaching Hospital in Mianwali, recruitment of teaching interns in government schools, and operational arrangements for 1,500 electric buses at the tehsil level.
The cabinet also approved the hosting of the 14th South Asian Games.
It approved relaxation of the recruitment ban for several departments and agencies.

title: LHC acquits murder convict | The Express Tribune
description: LHC acquits murder convict
content:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has acquitted a man sentenced to life imprisonment for murder, ruling that similarities in physical appearance and height were insufficient to sustain a conviction when CCTV footage failed to clearly establish the assailant's identity.
Justice Amjad Rafiq, in a written judgment on an appeal filed by Raja Shahid, held that CCTV footage was important documentary evidence in criminal cases, but its evidentiary value depended on whether the person concerned could be reliably identified.
The court observed that the facial features of the person seen firing at the deceased were not clearly visible in the footage. It ruled that a murder conviction could not be upheld solely on the basis of similarities in physical build and height.
The judgment stated that an accused did not need to establish multiple doubts to secure an acquittal, as a single reasonable doubt was sufficient to extend the benefit of doubt.
It further observed that where a person's face was not clearly visible in video footage, expert analysis and other reliable evidence assumed particular importance.

Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Monday inaugurated the first phase of Karachi's first sanitary engineered landfill at Jam Chakro, launching a scientific waste disposal system aimed at reducing pollution, improving public health and potentially generating $20 million in carbon credits.
The World Bank-backed project carries a total cost of $105 million, including $100 million in World Bank assistance and a $5 million contribution from the Sindh government. Number of rabies-related deaths in Sindh this year rises to 40
One more patient died of rabies in the metropolis, bringing the number of rabies-related deaths in Sindh this year to 40.
The 38-year-old man, Javed, was from Hyderabad. He had been bitten on the face by a stray dog four months ago and died at Jinnah Hospital.
Hospital officials said he was brought to the emergency department with hydrophobia, fever and difficulty swallowing. After examining him, the neurology team diagnosed rabies encephalitis. His condition was critical. He was given a dose of rabies vaccine during treatment, but could not survive.
This is the 11th rabies case reported at JPMC so far this year.
Medical experts warn that rabies is a fatal disease and that saving a patient's life becomes extremely difficult once symptoms appear. Anyone bitten or scratched by a dog or another animal suspected of carrying rabies should immediately wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical attention. Rabies vaccination-and, when advised by a doctor, immunoglobulin-should be given promptly.
Bites to the face or head can be particularly dangerous, so treatment should not be delayed.

Nine-day Hindu festival to conclude today, with devotees praying for peace and prosperity
Prayers rise from temples, offerings of prasad are made to the goddess, and the rhythmic beats of Garba and Dandiya fill the air as the city's Hindu community celebrates Navratri with religious fervour and festive enthusiasm.
Across the metropolis, temples have become gathering points for devotees observing the nine-day festival, with families coming together to worship "Mata Durga", perform religious rituals and seek blessings for their loved ones. Amid the celebrations, special prayers are also being offered for Pakistan's peace, security and prosperity.
From traditional worship services to colourful cultural performances, Navratri is bringing together members of the Hindu community in a celebration that blends faith, tradition and fellowship.
According to Hindu beliefs, Navratri is one of the religion's major festivals and is celebrated twice a year. The festival honours the nine forms of Goddess Durga, who is revered as the embodiment of divine power and the triumph of good over evil.
Religious traditions hold that Goddess Durga manifested herself to defeat Mahishasura and other demons. The combined powers of various deities took the forms of Mahakali, Mahalakshmi and Mahasaraswati to vanquish the forces of evil.
Maharaj Ram Nath said devotees observe nine days and nights of worship and religious rituals, with many observing fasts during the festival. Special prayers are held on the eighth day, known as Ashtami, and the ninth day, while the celebrations culminate in Vijayadashami, or Dussehra, on the tenth day.
This year, Navratri will conclude on October 20.

title: SHC rejects state appeal against Mahrang s acquittal
description: SHC rejects state appeal against Mahrang s acquittal
content:
The Sindh High Court (SHC) on Monday dismissed a provincial government appeal challenging the acquittal of Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC) leader Mahrang Baloch in an incitement case, declaring the appeal not maintainable.
The case against Mahrang and others was registered in Karachi on Oct 11, 2024, on the complaint of a citizen, Asad Ali, under the country's terror law. The complainant stated that Mahrang was a facilitator of terrorist organisations that were enticing educated youth from Balochistan and arranging a movement of terrorists under the guise of processions and rallies. A year later, an anti-terrorism court (ATC) acquitted Mahrang, ruling that the prosecution had failed to present credible evidence. Subsequently, the acting prosecutor general Sindh challenged the acquittal before the SHC in December 2025.
During today's hearing, the high court questioned the prosecution's authority to challenge the acquittal, observing that the original complainant in the case was a private individual. The bench questioned how the prosecution could independently file an appeal against the acquittal when the case had been lodged by a private complainant.
The prosecution argued that the ATC had overlooked material facts while allowing Mahrang's application for acquittal. The state counsel maintained that clear evidence existed against her and argued that the prosecution should have been allowed to present its evidence during the trial.
The prosecutor further contended that acquitting her before the formal framing of charges was inappropriate, as the prosecution had not yet presented its case before the trial court. However, the high court declared the appeal not maintainable and dismissed it, leaving the ATC's acquittal decision undisturbed.

title: Factory fire brought to heel after eight hour battle
description: Factory fire brought to heel after eight hour battle
content:
Third-degree blaze guts upper floors of garment unit, weakens factory structure
An eight-hour battle against a raging inferno at a garment factory in the city's Site area ended late Monday night, with firefighters bringing the third-degree blaze under control after flames ravaged the building's upper floors, destroyed stored goods and left the structure precariously weakened. A massive emergency response involving more than a dozen fire tenders, water bowsers, snorkels and Pakistan Navy personnel was mounted to contain the fire, while authorities ordered an investigation into its cause and a review of fire safety arrangements in industrial areas.
Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) Chief Fire Officer Humayun Khan said the fire was brought under control around 9:15pm, although cooling operations were expected to continue for several hours.
"More than a dozen fire tenders, three snorkels and two water bowsers participated in the rescue operation. All goods located on the second and third floors were destroyed in the blaze," he said.
Khan said a fire tender from the Pakistan Navy also took part in the operation. Plastic rolls were stored across all three floors, while dense smoke inside the premises made firefighting difficult.
He warned that the intensity of the fire had weakened the building, leaving the structure in a precarious condition. Firefighters used foam and water to contain the flames.
The fire was classified as a third-degree blaze to mobilise all relevant departments and ensure the immediate provision of resources. Earlier, the corporation had deployed 11 fire tenders and two water bowsers as teams battled the flames from both inside and outside the building.
Fire brigade officials at the site told The Express Tribune that they faced difficulties due to a shortage of water. The fire had spread to the factory's second and third floors, where combustible materials, including cardboard, wood, thread, garments, foam and plastic, were stored.
The Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC) activated additional hydrants to maintain water supplies for the operation. Focal person to the chief executive officer for the Hydrants Cell Shahbaz Bashir said approximately 300,000 gallons had been supplied to firefighting teams.
Of this quantity, 210,000 gallons came from Crush Plant Hydrants I and II, 40,000 gallons from Nipa, 35,000 gallons from Sakhi Hassan and 12,000 gallons from Safoora. KWSC spokesperson Qadir Sheikh had earlier reported that around 150,000 gallons had been supplied, with another 40,000 gallons kept on standby. The corporation said emergency arrangements were made on the directives of CEO Ahmed Ali Siddiqui to ensure uninterrupted water supplies until the operation was completed.
Earlier, Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah had directed the administration and rescue authorities to mobilise additional resources, bring the fire under control and protect nearby buildings.
The chief minister also sought a detailed report from the Karachi commissioner and the Industries Department, ordering a prompt and thorough investigation into the cause of the fire. He further directed the authorities to conduct a comprehensive review of fire safety arrangements in industrial areas to help prevent similar incidents in the future.

title: Social media amplifies insecurity  self doubt
description: Social media amplifies insecurity  self doubt
content:
Social media is increasingly transforming everyday life into a silent competition, encouraging constant comparison and fostering insecurity, dissatisfaction and unrealistic expectations, according to communication and mental health experts.
Industry observers say the culture of endless scrolling has become deeply embedded in modern life, exposing users to carefully curated lifestyles that often bear little resemblance to reality while subtly reshaping perceptions of success, happiness and self-worth.
Industry observer Shazia Rehman said social media has fundamentally altered the way people measure achievement and contentment. She noted that continuous exposure to seemingly perfect online lives encourages unspoken comparisons, leaving many individuals feeling less satisfied with their own circumstances.
Echoing these concerns, Mrs Ali said users frequently overlook the fact that social media presents only a selective and edited version of reality rather than a complete picture of people's lives. As a result, many compare themselves with unrealistic standards, leading to unnecessary disappointment and self-doubt.
Communication expert Sidra Iqbal observed that likes, followers and online engagement are increasingly replacing genuine measures of personal fulfilment. She explained that constant exposure to polished posts creates the illusion of flawless lives, prompting users to compare their everyday experiences with the carefully crafted highlights of others.

title: Ice trade declines with tech s rise in Rawalpindi
description: Ice trade declines with tech s rise in Rawalpindi
content:
Once considered one of the most profitable summer businesses for centuries, the ice factory and ice-selling trade has declined due to scientific advancement.
Until the 1990s, long queues outside ice stalls during summer were common, and obtaining ice was a tiring process.
Today, ice is available in almost every household. During Ramazan in summer, buying ice before iftar while fasting was particularly difficult.
In the 1990s, Rawalpindi had 54 small and large ice factories operating day and night, yet demand often exceeded supply. Today, the number has shrunk to just four, with production reduced to 2030 per cent. The labour force associated with ice factories has also disappeared.
Ice prices have risen from a few annas to Rs1 per kilogram, which once sparked protests. Demonstrations at Liaquat Bagh Chowk over the Rs1 price led to shelling and baton charge, after which no one dared protest again.
Today, ice is being sold at Rs200 per kg in the open market.
The city's largest central ice factory at Marir Chowk closed in 1995 due to losses. Other major factories in Lal Kurti, Westridge, Pirwadhai, Dhamial, Dhoke Syedan, and Dhoke Hassu have also shut down, leaving only small units.
The decline began in the 1990s with the spread of refrigerators in households. By 2000, 80 per cent of the city's ice factories had closed. Previously, people would buy ice in advance during Ramazan and store it wrapped in flour sacks.
Ice sellers used to cut blocks by estimation rather than weighing them. Standard ice blocks measured three feet wide, five feet long, and eight inches thick, produced using chemicals and water in iron moulds.
Loading and unloading ice was a skilled job, with experts completing the task in minutes and earning daily wages. A 67-year-old worker, Abdul Qadoos, said he worked for 31 years at the Marir Chowk factory, where conditions were cool and workers received free ice for home use.
He started with a salary of Rs850, which later increased to Rs1,550. After purchasing a refrigerator on instalments in the 1990s, he left the job and joined the flower market in Raja Bazaar.
He said the industry enjoyed a 5060 year boom but is now in decline due to scientific progress. Rising electricity costs have further strained the remaining factories, two of which may shut down this year.
Ice currently sells at Rs200 per kg and is expected to rise to Rs250270 in the coming weeks due to increasing electricity, petrol, and diesel prices. Where ice stalls were once easily visible across the city, they are now hard to find.

title: FCC bars indefinite deferment of civil servants  promotions
description: FCC bars indefinite deferment of civil servants  promotions
content:
Citing Jinnah's guidelines, court sets safeguards for officers
The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has ruled that repeated deferments of a civil servant's promotion cannot be used to indefinitely postpone consideration of his case, while clarifying that even three successive deferments do not automatically entitle an officer to promotion.
In a 19-page judgment authored by Justice Ali Baqar Najafi, the court laid down safeguards for civil servants whose promotion cases are repeatedly deferred by the Central Selection Board (CSB).
The judgment, which dismissed a petition challenging the denial of promotion to a police officer from grade 19 to grade 20, drew on the guidelines for civil servants outlined by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah in his famous speech delivered in April 1948.
The judgment observed: "The reason why service structure of civil servants is so much protected and their career progression is made with reasonable objective criteria also lies in the referred speech of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah in which he had given guidelines".
A division bench led by FCC Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan, citing Jinnah's speech, rephrased the guidelines for civil servants as follows: "Never be influenced by any political pressure, do your duty as servants of people and the state honestly and fearlessly, governments, Prime Ministers, Ministers come and go but it is not your business to support or oppose them, serve the governments loyally and morally while maintaining your high reputation, prestige, honour and integrity of your service, understand your own sphere of duty and act with others harmoniously within your sphere and leaders and politicians, likewise, should not try to interfere into your work which is bound to bring horrible diseases like corruption, bribery and nepotism which will do nothing but disservice to Pakistan."
The judgment said an officer whose promotion was repeatedly deferred by the CSB had, at a minimum, the following legally protected interests: first, to have his case considered for promotion whenever it fell due under the applicable rules; second, to have the decision based on objective and prescribed criteria; third, to be informed of specific and intelligible reasons for an adverse decision where the governing policy so required; fourth, to have a genuine opportunity to remove or address the deficiency underlying the deferment; and fifth, not to face indefinite or repeated deferments unsupported by fresh, tangible and legally relevant material.
The court said repeated deferment could not be treated as an unrestricted administrative device through which consideration for promotion could be postponed indefinitely.
"Each deferment must have an identifiable legal basis and must be referable to the conditions prescribed by the applicable promotion rules or policy."
"Where the original deficiency has already been removed, the authority must identify a fresh and lawful basis for any further deferment; otherwise, repeated postponement may amount, in substance, to an indefinite denial of consideration for promotion under the guise of deferment."
The court said deferments could not lawfully become a perpetual or open-ended obstacle to an officer's consideration for promotion. It said this principle assumed particular significance when an officer had been deferred on three successive occasions.
"Three deferments do not, by themselves, confer upon the officer an automatic right to promotion, because promotion is not a vested right and the competent authority retains the lawful discretion to assess comparative merit and suitability in accordance with the applicable rules," the order said.
The court also said that the promotion of junior officers during the intervening period could not, by itself, turn a temporary deferment into permanent supersession, particularly if the original ground for deferment no longer existed.
"The distinction is therefore material: the pendency of the reference may justify deferment; the subsequent acquittal removes the basis of that deferment."
"The former may postpone consideration, but the latter obliges the competent authority to restore the officer to the stream of lawful consideration."
"To hold otherwise would mean that an officer, although ultimately exonerated from the very proceedings which had prevented his consideration, would continue to suffer the adverse consequences of an allegation which never culminated in his conviction or adverse finding."
"Such an approach would effectively transform a temporary deferment into a substantive penalty, although the rules themselves do not contemplate deferment as a punishment."

The Senate approved the Passport Amendment Bill 2026, moved by Senator Abdul Qadir, after an extended debate over the eligibility criteria for blue passports and the treatment of parliamentarians by government departments.
The Directorate General of Immigration & Passports issues the blue passport in Pakistan as an Official (Gratis) Passport to designated government functionaries, state representatives, and authorized individuals for official state travel.
During the debate on the passport legislation, Abdul Qadir said children of Grade-21 government officers were eligible for blue passports, while members of the National Assembly also received the facility after being elected.
"We want the same principle to apply to senators. Either the blue passports issued to government employees should also be discontinued or senators should be given the same facility," he said.
Senator Abid Sher Ali questioned the restrictions allegedly imposed on parliamentarians by officials of the Ministry of Interior and the Directorate General of Immigration and Passports.
He said the interior secretary had told a Senate committee that a no-objection certificate (NOC) was required, while also maintaining that he was answerable to the minister rather than parliamentarians.
Ali said he had personally approached the passport authorities but was told that the directorate had received instructions from the Interior Ministry not to entertain certain requests. He questioned whether a senator needed an NOC from a government department to exercise his official privileges.
Responding to the concerns, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said public representatives were in parliament to serve the people and that no one should be subjected to unnecessary restrictions.
Senator Dilawar Khan called for an inquiry into the issuance of approximately 30,000 blue passports, saying the authorities responsible for issuing them should be held accountable if any had been issued to ineligible individuals.
He urged the government to investigate the period during which the passports were issued and take action against those found responsible for irregularities.
Minister of State for Interior Senator Talal Chaudhry told the Senate that the issuance of blue passports could affect Pakistan's global passport ranking and its efforts to secure visa-free travel arrangements with other countries.
He said the government has reduced the number of blue passports by 30, 000from about 75,000 to 45,000and that none of the cancelled passports belonged to political representatives.
Chaudhry said Pakistan had been seeking visa-free travel and other travel facilities with European, Gulf and other countries over the past 18 to 24 months. The number of blue passport holders also came under discussion during talks with Canada and other countries and could create difficulties, he added.

The prime minister on Monday said the government would provide all possible resources and facilities to Daanish schools, reaffirming its commitment to ensuring quality education and creating new opportunities for students, teachers and the younger generation across the country through artificial intelligence (AI).

title: No link between K P emergency  minerals
