title: Kevin Bacon calls out FedEx over missing vintage clothes shipment
description: Kevin Bacon says FedEx has failed to deliver his vintage clothes after package travelled between several countries
content:
Kevin Bacon says FedEx has failed to deliver his vintage clothes after package travelled between several countries
Kevin Bacon has appealed for help finding a missing shipment of vintage clothes after a package he sent to himself in Ireland travelled between several countries without reaching its destination.
The Footloose actor, 68, explained the situation in an Instagram video posted on Friday, saying he had shipped some of his favourite clothes from upstate New York while working in Ireland. The package has yet to be delivered, despite beginning its journey on September 26.
“I wanted to pack light, so I decided to ship some old clothes over here to Ireland,” Bacon said. He added that he had owned many of the items since the 1990s and used a shipping service he jokingly referred to as one that “rhymes with Bread Ex”.
According to Bacon, the box travelled from New York to Memphis before reaching France and Germany. On September 29, it was sent to Israel rather than Ireland, subsequently moving between Israel, France and Germany over several days.
By October 11, the package had reached England before finally making its way to Ireland, where Bacon said it had been sitting for five days. Despite its arrival in the country, he said the shipping company had told him the package could not be delivered.
“I don't understand why,” he said. “It's just sitting there. I can't get a person on the phone. I have not been able to talk to anybody.”
Bacon dismissed suggestions that he should simply replace the missing items, explaining that the clothes held sentimental value.
“I could buy some clothes, but I want these clothes,” he said. “I've had them since the 90s. They have a certain sentimental value. Old boots, old jeans, old hats.”
The actor also noted that colder weather was approaching and asked followers whether he would ever see his belongings again.
FedEx apologised in a statement, saying it was in direct contact with Bacon's team to arrange delivery and reviewing what went wrong.

title: Hong Kong hosts underwater hockey tournament
description: The niche sport gains traction through social media and live broadcasts
content:
The niche sport gains traction through social media and live broadcasts
Swimmers brandishing short, curved sticks held their breath as they somersaulted and dove towards a weighted puck at the bottom of a Hong Kong swimming pool, vying for first place in a sport likened to voluntary drowning.
The annual underwater hockey tournament, ominously advertised as "physical hell", nevertheless drew a roster of hardcore enthusiasts from countries across Asia to the Chinese city over the weekend.
"You have to choose when to use your breath and when not to... Anyone that's got the puck, you know that they've got some level of suffering," Leo Lines, a Japanese-New Zealander competitor from Hokkaido, told AFP.
Suited up in snorkel masks and fins, players only resurface for air when they absolutely have to, and their heads remain constantly underwater so they can monitor the game.
There are six players on each team and no goalkeepers, while referees watch for fouls and send players to a penalty box for serious rule-breaching.
"You're so into trying to succeed, trying to score the goal, that you forget about breath hold and how tough it is," competitor Rita Frieske, a Hong Kong-based Polish academic, told AFP.
Games last 30 minutes and are split into two halves with a three-minute break in between.
The gruelling sport has created a tight-knit community.
"It's like that sadistic study that forces everybody to survive together and then you stick together for a long time," Malaysian player Hui Chin Teoh said.
Underwater hockey, previously known as "octopush", was invented in England in 1954 as a way to keep divers fit during the off-season winter months.
While not yet an Olympic sport, it is recognised by the International Olympic Committee, and made its debut at the Southeast Asian Games in 2019.
Competition organisers hope that as underwater camera technology improves, the spectator experience will too.
"The future of underwater hockey, thanks to social media, is more active now than before," said head coach and tournament director Nowie Ignacio.
"When I was playing, it was just word of mouth. Now there are a lot of avenues to see it... (competitions) are actually televised live now," he said.
Many players at the Hong Kong tournament have their sights set on the Elite world championship in France next April, which organisers expect will draw around 20 nations.
"People are starting to understand what underwater hockey is," Ignacio said.

title: Street Fighter  leads box office with  51m global opening
description: Street Fighter  opens with  51m worldwide  while  Whalefall  takes  17 5m amid positive reviews
content:
'Street Fighter' opens with $51m worldwide, while 'Whalefall' takes $17.5m amid positive reviews
Street Fighter has topped the global box office with a $51 million opening weekend, including $31 million domestically, while survival thriller Whalefall has earned $17.5 million worldwide, according to TheWrap .
The Paramount and Legendary video game adaptation, produced with publisher Capcom, had an $82 million budget.
Its opening performance raises questions about whether it can attract audiences beyond its core gaming fanbase. The film received a B- CinemaScore, alongside ratings of 40% from critics and 80% from audiences on Rotten Tomatoes.
Street Fighter now faces competition from Warner Bros. and DC’s Clayface , which is expected to target both comic book and horror audiences.
Meanwhile, 20th Century Studios’ Whalefall , starring Austin Abrams as a scuba diver swallowed by a whale, opened with $8 million in North America and $17.5 million globally against a reported net budget of $60 million. The film received a B CinemaScore and scores of 71% from critics and 81% from audiences on Rotten Tomatoes.
A24’s documentary You Can See Everything took second place with $15 million from 855 locations, marking the highest opening for a documentary in at least 13 years.
Directed by Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder, the film examines convicted fraudster Elizabeth Holmes and has recorded more than 2,000 sold-out screenings. Its combined production and marketing budget was reportedly below $10 million.
Universal and Blumhouse’s Other Mommy placed third with $8.3 million in its second weekend, bringing its domestic 10-day total to $44.8 million. Focus Features’ Sense and Sensibility opened in fifth place with $7.25 million and received an A- CinemaScore.
Elsewhere, Sony’s Resident Evil reached $361 million worldwide, including $5.5 million domestically in its fifth weekend. The Social Reckoning fell 73% in its second weekend to $1.5 million domestically, bringing its global total to $14.2 million against a $30 million budget.
Warner Bros.’ Digger continued to struggle, earning $920,000 domestically in its third weekend and reaching $17 million overall in North America.

title: Samar Jafri cancels Hyderabad show over crowd misbehaviour  safety concerns
description: Singer says cannot risk safety of women and children as concerns grew over potential harassment and overcrowding
content:
Singer says cannot risk safety of women and children as concerns grew over potential harassment and overcrowding
Actor and singer Samar Jafri cancelled his much-anticipated performance in Hyderabad after crowd misbehaviour and growing safety concerns forced him to make what he described as a difficult decision.
In an official statement , Jafri’s management said the performer had been looking forward to meeting his fans and delivering a memorable evening. However, concerns about the crowd’s behaviour and the potential risks to attendees ultimately led to the cancellation.
According to the statement, the situation raised concerns about potential harassment, particularly of women, as well as the risk of overcrowding or a stampede.
“Samar was genuinely excited to perform for his fans in Hyderabad. However, due to crowd misbehaviour and growing safety concerns at the venue, Samar made the difficult decision to call off the show to prevent potential harassment, particularly towards women, and to avoid the risk of overcrowding or a stampede,” the management said.
Emphasising the importance of prioritising public safety at live events, the team added, “The safety and well-being of everyone present must always come first.”
The statement also stressed that event organisers were responsible for ensuring that venues and arrangements met the necessary safety standards. “Organisers must make this their foremost priority and ensure that every arrangement at the venue is up to that standard,” the team said.
The management apologised to disappointed fans, saying, “We sincerely apologise to everyone who was looking forward to the performance and thank you for your understanding.”
The statement was signed by Team Samar Jafri.
Following the announcement, Jafri shared a video from the event, accompanied by a personal message to his Hyderabad fans. Expressing disappointment over how the evening had unfolded, he said he had arrived with genuine excitement and hoped to share a special experience with his audience.
“Hyderabad, I was genuinely excited to perform for you. I came here looking forward to sharing a special evening with you all, and it genuinely hurts that things unfolded the way they did,” he said.
Explaining his decision, Jafri reiterated that the crowd’s behaviour and the resulting safety concerns had left him with little choice but to call off the show.
“Unfortunately, due to the crowd’s behaviour and growing safety concerns, I made the difficult decision to call off the show. I couldn’t risk anyone’s safety, especially the girls and kids in the audience, or allow the situation to escalate into something more serious.”
He stressed that, despite his eagerness to perform, the audience’s well-being had to take precedence.
“As much as I wanted to get on that stage, the safety and well-being of everyone present had to come first,” he continued.
Jafri also apologised to those who had attended the event expecting an enjoyable evening, acknowledging their disappointment over the abrupt cancellation.
“To everyone who came with love, excitement, and the intention of having a good time, I’m truly sorry things didn’t go as we had hoped. This isn’t how I imagined my time in Hyderabad, and I hope you understand why this decision had to be made.”
Thanking those who had supported him and his team, the performer expressed hope that he would return to Hyderabad for a more positive experience in the future.
“Thank you to everyone who stood by us. I hope we get to share a better, safer, and more beautiful evening together someday,” he concluded.
Jafri is a Pakistani actor, singer and composer who has established a presence in the country’s entertainment industry through his work in television, film and music.
He gained wider recognition through the 2025 television drama Parwarish and the recent Express Entertainment thriller Raja London Ka .
His work across acting and music has helped him build a following beyond television, with live performances giving fans an opportunity to connect with him in person.
As Jafri expressed hope of sharing a better experience with his Hyderabad fans in the future, the cancellation highlighted the importance of safety at live events. While performances can be rescheduled and opportunities to connect with audiences created again, the well-being of everyone at a venue must remain the priority.

title: Karachi to remain hot and dry as temperatures near 39  C  Met Office
description: PMD says cooler mornings and nights are expected from mid November  with colder weather likely to set in by December
content:
PMD says cooler mornings and nights are expected from mid-November, with colder weather likely to set in by December
Karachi is expected to experience hot and dry weather over the coming days, with maximum temperatures likely to reach 39 degrees Celsius, the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) said on Monday. In a city-wise temperature forecast posted on X , the PMD forecast a minimum temperature of 26°C and a maximum of 39°C for the city.
According to the department’s daily weather forecast , the maximum temperature was expected to reach 39°C on Monday and Tuesday before easing slightly to 38°C on Wednesday. The department forecast sunny conditions throughout the three-day period, with hot weather likely to persist.
Deputy Director of the Met Department in Karachi Anjum Nazir Zaigham said hot and dry conditions were likely to continue over the next few days, with maritime winds and north-westerly winds from Balochistan expected to influence weather conditions.
He said the heat in October was a normal seasonal phenomenon and that the current conditions were part of the seasonal transition. Winter winds gradually began to establish themselves during October, he added.
Also Read: Karachi city sizzles past nine-year September heat record
Cooler mornings and nights were expected to begin from mid-November, while colder weather was likely to set in between early and mid-December, Zaigham said. He added that unusually cold weather was not expected this year, with temperatures likely to remain within the normal seasonal range during winter.
Karachi has experienced unusually high temperatures since September, with the mercury reaching 40.7°C on September 21, making it the city’s hottest September day in nine years . The temperature recorded at the PMD’s Pehlwan Goth weather station surpassed the previous September high of 40.5°C, recorded in 2017.
The PMD attributed the intense heat to a circulation over the Arabian Sea that altered wind patterns, along with weak south-westerly sea breezes.
The department had also warned on September 23 that October could be warmer than usual. The warning followed a spell of persistent heat during which Karachi recorded a maximum temperature of 39.1°C on September 22. The PMD partly attributed the prolonged heat to the early end of the monsoon season.
The city also experienced an intense heatwave in May , when temperatures rose above 44°C, marking Karachi’s hottest day since 2018. The PMD had warned that temperatures could exceed 41°C during the spell, while high humidity pushed the feels-like temperature towards 50°C.

title: The Simpsons  brings Apu back after nearly decade with new voice actor
description: Apu returns to  The Simpsons  after nearly nine years  with Sunil Malhotra replacing Hank Azaria
content:
Apu returns to 'The Simpsons' after nearly nine years, with Sunil Malhotra replacing Hank Azaria
The Simpsons has brought Apu Nahasapeemapetilon back as a speaking character for the first time in nearly a decade, with voice actor Sunil Malhotra taking over the role from Hank Azaria.
Apu returned in the October 18 episode, “The Revengening”, which also introduced Janina Gavankar as his wife, Manjula.
According to Variety , executive producer Matt Selman confirmed that Apu and the Nahasapeemapetilon family will appear and speak more frequently following the reopening of the Kwik-E-Mart.
“We love this character, and wanted to bring him back in a smart, 'Simpsons'-y way that allowed him to evolve,” Selman said.
Apu had remained visible in Springfield after Azaria stepped away from the role but had not spoken since the October 2017 episode “The Serfsons”.
The decision followed criticism of the character’s stereotypical portrayal of a South Asian convenience store owner, highlighted in the 2017 documentary The Problem With Apu.
Azaria announced in 2020 that he would no longer voice the character. In 2021, he said, “I apologize for my part in creating that and participating in that.”
Malhotra said he initially had reservations about accepting the role but spoke with the producers about how Apu’s return would be handled.
“My callback was the first of many times that no one at 'The Simpsons' let me down,” he said, describing the process as a collaborative experience.
In “The Revengening”, Apu appears to seek revenge on Springfield after being abandoned by the town and separated from his family. The story ultimately reveals itself as a nightmare, ending with Apu back at the Kwik-E-Mart alongside Manjula.
The return follows other casting changes made after The Simpsons announced in 2020 that characters of colour would be voiced by actors from appropriate cultural backgrounds. Malhotra’s credits include The Legend of Korra, The Legend of Vox Machina and Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi.
Early social media reactions to Apu’s return included messages welcoming the character back and praising the casting change.

title: Victoria Falls Stadium nears completion
description: Zimbabwe steps up preparations for 2027 Cricket World Cup as new venue targets mid year completion
content:
Zimbabwe steps up preparations for 2027 Cricket World Cup as new venue targets mid-year completion
Zimbabwe’s preparations for the 2027 ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup are progressing, with the new Mosi-oa-Tunya International Cricket Stadium in Victoria Falls nearing completion ahead of its planned debut at the global tournament.
The stadium’s first World Cup match will see hosts Zimbabwe face India in their final group-stage fixture on October 24, 2027. The venue is also scheduled to stage three Super 7 matches on October 28 and 30, and November 1.
Zimbabwe Cricket (ZC) said the main construction work was substantially complete, with efforts now focused on finishing touches before an initial trial match, which will be announced in due course.
The media and broadcast centres, changing rooms, medical facilities, grandstands and grass banks are largely complete. Roofing, the installation of bucket seats and other finishing work remain underway, while corporate gazebos are also planned.
“The main building works are as good as complete and we are now concentrating on the finishes that will bring the stadium together, with all the outstanding materials having been delivered,” ZC managing director Givemore Makoni said.
Full completion is targeted for mid-2027, with an international series planned to provide a more extensive test of the facilities before the World Cup.
“The initial trial match will give us an opportunity to assess the playing facilities and essential match-day operations,” Makoni added.
Zimbabwe will co-host the tournament with South Africa and Namibia, with Harare, Bulawayo and Victoria Falls among the destinations set to welcome teams and supporters.
The latest progress was reviewed during a recently concluded International Cricket Council (ICC) inspection of Zimbabwe’s host cities. The delegation visited Takashinga Cricket Club and Harare Sports Club in Harare, the Victoria Falls venue and Queens Sports Club in Bulawayo.
Sarah Edgar, ICC tournament director for the 2027 World Cup, and Zimbabwe tournament director Hamilton Masakadza led the inspection.
“We are pleased with the progress made in addressing the baseline requirements to bring the venues up to the standards necessary for the ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup 2027,” Edgar said.
She singled out Victoria Falls as an exciting addition, saying international supporters would have the opportunity to experience cricket at a renowned tourist destination.
In Harare and Bulawayo, work is focused on upgrading existing grounds to meet tournament requirements, which have evolved since Zimbabwe last hosted the men’s World Cup in 2003.
“We’ve identified areas where we will adjust a little bit and tailor-make to the ICC requirements for the 2027 event,” Masakadza said.
He added that progress at Victoria Falls was encouraging and that officials were comfortable with the construction timelines.
Selected stands at Harare Sports Club and Queens Sports Club will receive bucket seats, while floodlights are planned for Queens Sports Club and the Victoria Falls stadium ahead of the tournament.
Zimbabwe’s preparations also include a series of international fixtures in October 2027, with the hosts scheduled to face Australia and Pakistan in Harare and Afghanistan in Bulawayo, alongside matches against qualifying teams.

Netflix has confirmed that South Korean medical drama The Trauma Code: Heroes on Call will return for seasons 2 and 3, with leading actors Ju Ji-hoon and Choo Young-woo reprising their roles.

Ju Ji-hoon returns as Baek Kang-hyuk, a talented surgeon determined to save lives, while Choo Young-woo reprises his role as Yang Jae-won, Baek’s first protégé who has since joined the hospital’s trauma team.

New cast member Jeong Ye-in joins the drama as nurse Cheon Jang-mi, securing the role following an extensive audition process.
Lee Do-yun, who directed the first season, will return to direct the upcoming instalments and write their scripts.

Both new seasons will stream exclusively on Netflix. However, the platform has yet to reveal when viewers can expect the next instalment.

title: Wiegman signs England contract extension | The Express Tribune
description: The Dutch coach has guided England to two European titles and a World Cup final since taking charge in 2021
content:
The Dutch coach has guided England to two European titles and a World Cup final since taking charge in 2021
England women's head coach Sarina Wiegman has signed a two-year contract extension taking her through until the end of the 2029 women's European Championship, the Football Association announced Monday.
Wiegman has led England to tournament triumphs at both the 2022 and 2025 Euros, as well as a first World Cup final in 2023, since taking charge in September 2021.
The 56-year-old Dutchwoman has reached five successive major tournament finals, also winning Euro 2017 with her native Netherlands.
"I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football," Wiegman said Monday.
England, beaten by Spain in the 2023 World Cup final in Australia, will face Ukraine over a two-legged play-off in November and December for a place in next year's tournament in Brazil.
"Of course, anyone who knows me will understand that my main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come," Wiegman added.
"We have an important job to do to confirm our place in Brazil, and hopefully we can do that and give the country another special summer to remember next year."
Wiegman's new deal will also encompass the 2027 Nations League, which serves as a qualifying tournament for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
She first agreed a contract extension in January 2024.

title: Jason Sudeikis leaves  Ted Lasso  fans guessing about the show   s future
description: Sudeikis said he would be interested in making more episodes  acknowledging that several factors would need to align
content:
Sudeikis said he would be interested in making more episodes, acknowledging that several factors would need to align
Jason Sudeikis has offered an update on the possibility of Ted Lasso returning for a fifth and sixth season, revealing that discussions about continuing the Apple TV comedy have not yet progressed to a writers’ room.
Speaking on the Talk Easy with Sam Fragoso podcast, the actor and co-creator said he would be interested in making more episodes but acknowledged that several factors would need to align.
Asked whether he wanted to continue the series, Sudeikis replied that he “would like to”, adding that “it takes a village”.
He also suggested Apple could be receptive to another season, saying, “I would assume so.”
However, the actor stopped short of confirming any plans for the show’s future. When pressed about whether more episodes would be made, he admitted, “I just don’t know,” before clarifying, “We haven’t started a writers’ room or anything like that.”
Sudeikis also reflected on how the series continued beyond his original expectations.
He had previously believed the third season would mark the end of the story, before the show returned for a fourth instalment.
During the podcast conversation, host Sam Fragoso asked whether the creative process behind the fourth season could inspire two more instalments.
Sudeikis responded humorously, “Um, we’re going to need a bigger cup.”
The actor explained that, after taking a lengthy break following season 3, he began hearing the characters’ voices again, followed by new voices that helped shape the women’s team members.
“I think it’d be fun,” Sudeikis said, leaving the door open to a possible continuation.
For now, Ted Lasso Seasons 5 and 6 remain unconfirmed, with no writers’ room currently underway.

title: Firefighters snuff out inferno at garment factory in Karachi s SITE area
description: 12 fire tenders  two water bowsers  and two snorkels at the site as Pakistan Navy joins the firefighting operation
content:
12 fire tenders, two water bowsers, and two snorkels at the site as Pakistan Navy joins the firefighting operation
A massive fire engulfed and precariously damaged a garments factory near Metroville in Karachi’s SITE area on Monday, prompting the deployment of fire and rescue teams, according to the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) and Sindh Rescue 1122.
KMC Chief Fire Officer Humayun Khan said around 9:15pm that the fire was brought under control after eight hours of firefighting operations, adding that the cooling down process might take several more hours.
"More than a dozen fire tenders, three snorkels, and two water bowsers participated in the rescue operation. All goods located on the second and third floors were destroyed in the blaze," he said.
Khan said that one fire tender from the Pakistan Navy was also present at the site to assist in the operation.
According to the chief fire officer, plastic rolls were stored on all three floors of the factory, while the premises were filled with heavy smoke, making firefighting efforts extremely challenging.
He also said that the intensity of the blaze has weakened the factory building, "leaving the structure in a precarious condition". He told the media that firefighters used foam and water to help contain the fire.
The Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC) earlier declared an emergency at one more hydrant — Safoora — to ensure an uninterrupted water supply to firefighting teams in SITE area.
According to Shahbaz Bashir, focal person to the CEO for the Hydrants Cell, approximately 300,000 gallons of water were supplied to the fire brigades taking part in the operation so far.
"Of the total quantity, 210,000 gallons were provided through Crush Plant Hydrants I and II; 40,000 gallons through NIPA Hydrant; 35,000 gallons through Sakhi Hassan Hydrant; and 12,000 gallons through Safoora Hydrant."
Bashir said the emergency measures were implemented on the directives of KWSC CEO Ahmed Ali Siddiqui to ensure an uninterrupted water supply to the fire brigade and rescue agencies. He added that the water supply would continue without interruption until the fire was completely brought under control.
A collage demonstrating blaze at a garment factory in Karachi on October 19, 2026. Photos: Express
The chief fire officer said earlier in the day that the fire was intense when firefighting teams arrived at the scene, adding that firefighting operations were underway with the assistance of a snorkel, and the corporation had deployed 11 fire tenders and two water bowsers to tackle the blaze.
"The warehouse contains cardboard, wood, thread, garments, foam, plastic and other combustible materials in the upper floors, making firefighting operations challenging. Our efforts are focused on bringing the fire under control as soon as possible, after which cooling operations will begin,” Khan said.
The chief fire officer also underscored that the fire was declared a "third-degree blaze" to mobilise all relevant departments, ensure their immediate attention and secure the resources required to deal with the emergency.
Khan stressed that parts of the building, along with its boundary wall, had become structurally unsafe due to the fire.
Meanwhile, fire brigade officials at the site told The Express Tribune that they faced difficulties due to a "shortage of water".
They also revealed that firefighting operations were underway from both the exterior and interior of the building and so far the fire has engulfed the factory’s second and third floors.
KWSC Spokesperson Qadir Sheikh told The Express Tribune that the facility provided an uninterrupted water supply to fire brigade teams responding to the factory blaze.
The spokesperson said emergency was notified at three hydrants located at the Crush Plant, NIPA and Sakhi Hassan areas to ensure an uninterrupted supply of water for firefighting operations.
"Approximately 150,000 gallons of water have so far been supplied to the fire brigade, while an additional 40,000 gallons are available on standby to meet any further requirements," Sheikh noted.
Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah took notice of the fire and directed the administration and rescue authorities to immediately mobilise resources at the site.
The chief minister directed the authorities to immediately summon additional fire brigade vehicles and Rescue 1122 units to intensify firefighting and rescue operations.
“The fire should be brought under control as soon as possible, and nearby buildings must be protected,” the chief minister said.
CM Shah sought a detailed report on the incident from the Karachi commissioner and the Industries Department, directing them to investigate the cause of the fire promptly and thoroughly.
He also issued strict instructions for a comprehensive review of fire safety arrangements in industrial areas to help prevent similar incidents in the future.

title: Eric Dane s daughter saving him from drowning amid ALS battle revealed in new memoir
description: Winona Ryder recalled facing appearance based criticism during early audition in 1980s  speaking with David Harbour
content:
Eric Dane recounts how his daughter Georgia helped save him from drowning during family holiday in Antigua in 2024
Eric Dane recalled how his daughter Georgia helped save him from drowning during a family holiday in Antigua in 2024, following his diagnosis with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). The late Grey’s Anatomy actor shared the experience in his posthumous memoir, My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments.
In an excerpt published by People , Dane described how he realised he could no longer swim while in a pool during the trip. His 14-year-old daughter and a friend helped rescue him.
Dane, who also shared daughter Billie, 16, with his estranged wife Rebecca Gayheart, recounted calling Gayheart after the incident to tell her what had happened.
“'I can't swim, Rebecca, I say. I can't swim,'” he wrote.
He described Gayheart’s emotional response to the news, adding, “She explodes into tears and I weep with her. We cry together.”
Dane continued, “Finally, the tears slow, become reduced to gasps, and when we're both cried out, Rebecca says, 'I was afraid of this day. I knew it would come. I've been dreading it.'”
The actor publicly announced his ALS diagnosis in April 2025. He died in February at the age of 53.
In another passage from the memoir, Dane recalled experiencing the first signs of the condition in January 2024 while eating sushi with his daughters. He noticed that his right hand was tingling and his fingers felt numb, making it difficult to use chopsticks.
“I'm eating sushi with my kids and suddenly I can't work the chopsticks with my right hand. My hand tingles, and then my fingers feel numb,” he wrote.
Dane initially dismissed the symptoms, believing they might be related to excessive texting. However, he experienced the problem again three weeks later, when he could no longer grip the chopsticks.
The actor said it took nine months to receive an official diagnosis.
My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments is scheduled to be available from November 3, offering further reflections on Dane’s life and his experience with ALS.

Riot Games’ virtual girl group K/DA has returned with FIRESTARTER , marking its first new music in approximately six years. The group released the single and its official music video on October 19, ahead of an upcoming EP of the same name scheduled for October 21.

Choreographer Sean Bankhead, whose previous work includes projects with Beyoncé and BLACKPINK, directed the choreography for the new video.
K/DA comprises four League of Legends champions: Ahri, Akali, Evelynn and Kai’Sa. The virtual group debuted during the 2018 League of Legends World Championship Finals in Incheon, South Korea, performing POP/STARS.
In 2020, K/DA released the singles THE BADDEST and MORE before launching its five-track EP ALL OUT in November. The collection included both singles alongside VILLAIN, DRUM GO DUM and I’LL SHOW YOU.
The group subsequently went on an extended hiatus without releasing new music. FIRESTARTER marks its first musical release since ALL OUT and introduces a new chapter for the League of Legends characters’ music project.

Pakistan will also be represented by Abdullah Nawaz and Azan Ali Khan in the men’s draw, while Anam Aziz and Rushna Mehboob will compete in the women’s event as wildcard entries. The tournament offers prize money of $41,000 each for the men’s and women’s competitions, taking the combined purse to $82,000. The event is part of the PSA World Tour calendar. The men’s draw features 20 players, led by top seed Curtis Malik of England, followed by Egypt’s Karim El Hammamy, Malaysia’s Sanjay Jeeva and Egypt’s Yassin Shohdy. Perry Malik of England is seeded fifth, while Rowan Damming of the Netherlands occupies the sixth seed. Egypt’s Yassin Elshafei is seeded seventh, with Pakistan’s Asim Khan completing the top eight. The field also includes Hong Kong’s Matthew Lai and Chi Him Wong, Malaysia’s Mohammad Syafiq Kamal and Yee Xian Siow, and Pakistan’s Nasir Iqbal. Other entrants include Ziad Ibrahim of Egypt, Naoki Hayashi of Japan, Salah Eltorgman of Egypt and Ravindu Laksiri of Sri Lanka. Egypt’s Amina El Rihany is the second seed, followed by compatriots Nadine Shahin and Rowan Elaraby in third and fourth place. France’s Marie Stephan is seeded fifth, Malaysia’s Ainaa Amani sixth, Switzerland’s Cindy Merlo seventh and England’s Hayley Ward eighth. With players from Pakistan, Egypt, England, Malaysia, Hong Kong, Japan, Sri Lanka, the Netherlands, Germany, Switzerland, France, the Czech Republic and South Korea in the entry lists, the Venus ABC Open is set to bring a diverse international field to Karachi.

title: French PM calls for  partial curfews  in cities hit by riots and looting
description: French PM urges partial curfews in some parts of France after violent protests
content:
Students block access to Louvre Museum in support of high school protests
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has asked regional authorities to impose "partial curfews" in some cities on Monday evening as France reels from two days of unrest that saw town halls burned down and hundreds of businesses looted.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez earlier admitted that police had "lost control" of the protests in several cities, while the Yellow Vest movement called for a new round of protests on Saturday.
Meanwhile, French President Emmanuel Macron rejected the resignation of Interior Minister Nunez following widespread violence and looting across the country during last weekend's protests , according to broadcaster BFMTV .
Nunez submitted his resignation to Macron a day earlier amid mounting criticism over the authorities' handling of the unrest. "I am the minister of the interior, I am responsible for everything that happens on the ground," he told France Inter radio , explaining his decision to resign.
Nunez acknowledged a "loss of control" by police in some cities and admitted there had been a "lack of anticipation" in deploying available security forces.
Read More: Student protests spread across France, Belgium
However, the president decided to keep him in office, citing the need for continuity in the command of security forces during the current crisis, according to a statement from the Elysee Palace .
Macron also called for greater transparency over what he described as "failures in anticipation and intelligence" that contributed to the scale of the violence.
The unrest, which erupted during demonstrations on Saturday, left nearly 1,000 law enforcement officers injured and resulted in approximately 2,400 arrests, according to official figures.
The government's response has faced criticism from several local leaders, including the mayors of Paris, Marseille and Limoges.
Nunez is expected to visit Marseille, one of the cities hardest hit by the violence, where authorities reported that up to 30,000 people were involved in looting on Saturday.
Students block access to Louvre Museum in support of high school protests
Students blocked access to the Louvre Museum in Paris on Monday in support of ongoing high school protests and to denounce what they described as police repression, the French media reported.
The blockade prevented the museum from opening at its usual time of 9am, according to management and unions cited by the daily Le Parisien .
Students from the École du Louvre led the action, while the CFDT trade union said students from the National School of Fine Arts also participated.
Museum management said the protest had no direct connection to the Louvre itself, describing the museum as being used “as an echo chamber.”
Also Read: French police clash with protesters as tens of thousands rally over cost of living
The CGT trade union, which supported the action without participating, said the museum would remain closed at least until noon.
Protesters placed the blockade within a broader struggle for the right to study, work and live freely in decent conditions.
The action follows a high school protest movement that began in mid-September . It also comes two days after nationwide demonstrations against the high cost of living that were marred by unrest in several French cities.
The Ecole du Louvre, located within the museum grounds, offers higher education courses in subjects including art history, archaeology, anthropology and museology.

title: Police allegedly arrest PTI MNA Nasim Ali Shah from Bannu
description: Video circulating on social media purportedly shows police officers taking the lawmaker away
content:
Video circulating on social media purportedly shows police officers taking the lawmaker away
Police on Monday arrested Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Member of the National Assembly Maulana Nasim Ali Shah from his madrassa, Al-Markaz-ul-Islami, in Ghoriwala, Bannu.
A video circulating on social media purportedly showed police officers taking the lawmaker away. The circumstances surrounding his arrest, the cases, if any, registered against him, and his whereabouts following the operation had not been officially confirmed.
The video purportedly showing the arrest was also shared from the detained MNA’s X account.
The arrest came amid a wider crackdown on PTI leaders and workers in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) following the imposition of governor’s rule and a state of emergency in the province on October 11.
Non-functional chief minister Sohail Afridi, PTI provincial president Junaid Akbar and K-P Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati were among the senior party figures taken into protective custody following the federal government’s intervention. Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry also confirmed that Afridi and some members of his cabinet had been placed in preventive custody.
According to a petition filed by Sohail Afridi’s brother, Muhammad Aamir, in the Peshawar High Court (PHC), the former K-P chief minister was allegedly taken from the Chief Minister’s House in Peshawar on October 11 by armed, masked men in the presence of the city’s police chief. The petition sought his recovery, disclosure of his whereabouts, and a judicial inquiry into the alleged detention.
In a related incident, Afridi’s lawyer, advocate Muhammad Bashir, was also reportedly picked up outside the PHC after filing a petition challenging the former chief minister’s detention. He was later released, according to media reports.
Police also arrested PTI workers in several parts of the province amid the party’s planned long march towards Islamabad. In Swabi, police reported arrests of party workers, while six PTI supporters were detained in Khyber district during protests against governor’s rule.
Separately, PTI founder Imran Khan’s sisters Aleema Khan, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi were detained for 30 days under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance in September, ahead of the party’s planned Islamabad march. Imran’s nephews, Shahraiz Khan and Sher Shah, were also briefly detained and later released, according to their lawyer.
The federal government imposed governor’s rule and a state of emergency in K-P on October 11, citing security concerns and what it described as the provincial government’s disengagement from counterterrorism efforts. PTI rejected the measures as unconstitutional and challenged them in the Peshawar High Court.

title: Imaan  Hadi seek suspension of ATC trial over alleged procedural violations during indictment
description: Defence says violations occured in framing of charges  argue that accused were not physically present when indicted
content:
Says violations occurred in framing of charges, argues that accused were not physically present when indicted
The defence on Monday urged the Islamabad High Court (IHC) to halt trial proceedings against lawyer Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chatha, alleging procedural violations in the framing of charges and arguing that the accused had not been physically present when they were indicted.
The court was hearing appeals filed by Imaan and Hadi against the anti-terrorism court's (ATC) dismissal of their applications challenging their indictment and the terrorism charges in a case related to the removal of barriers.
A division bench comprising Justice Inam Amin Minhas and Justice Sharukh Arjumand heard the appeals. Lawyers, including State Ali Azad and Zainab Janjua, appeared before the court.
Justice Inam asked whether the lawyers had received copies of the relevant documents.
“Copies have not been provided,” State Ali Azad told the court, adding that he wanted to examine how the indictment had been framed.
Azad argued that the Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) had passed the order without jurisdiction. He said the case had remained before Judge Abul Hasanat Muhammad Zulqarnain from March 12, 2025, until a period shortly before the current proceedings.
Referring to the Zulfikar Ali Bhutto case, the lawyer argued that the court in which a challan had been submitted should hear the case. He also maintained that copies of the documents had not been provided to the accused.
Azad said the charges had to be read out to the accused, which he argued had not happened because they were not physically present in court at the time. He added that proceedings could not be advanced in their absence and that framing charges without their physical presence also violated a decision of the National Judicial Policy Making Committee.
Read: Imaan, Hadi boycott proceedings as ATC records witness statements
“The charge is the foundation of a trial. If that foundation is defective, the entire structure of the trial built on it would be unlawful,” Azad argued.
Justice Inam asked whether the trial was being conducted through video link. Azad replied that it had initially been held through video link but that, since the previous hearing, proceedings had begun inside the jail.
The judge then asked whose signatures appeared on the indictment.
“My signatures are there, but the accused did not sign, although their signatures should legally have been obtained,” Azad said.
Justice Inam questioned whether proceedings could continue through a video link, noting that the accused had been present through the link and that their attendance had been recorded when the indictment was framed.
Azad replied that the accused had not been present when he signed the document and asked the court to summon the video recording to verify his claim. He also said copies had not been delivered to the accused in jail and that the defence had submitted an affidavit to this effect.
“You should not have taken the copies, then,” Justice Inam remarked.
Read More: ATC summons Islamabad IGP in Imaan, Hadi bail case on November 3
Azad said all the applications filed by the defence before the ATC had been dismissed. He added that the lawyers had also sought the case record and the video recording.
The judge asked where it was written that the accused had to be physically present for the charges to be framed. Azad responded that the defence had also challenged the terrorism provisions in the case.
The lawyer repeatedly urged the High Court to suspend the trial proceedings while the appeals were being considered.
“We will see and let you know,” Justice Inam said.
Zainab informed the court that the case had been fixed for a jail trial at 2:30 pm next Monday.
“We will pass an order and inform you,” Justice Inam said, adding that notices had been issued and the court would consider the matter once the respondents appeared.
Imaan and her husband Hadi were rearrested on September 17 , shortly after the Supreme Court granted them bail and suspended their sentences in a separate social-media posts case. They were produced before an Islamabad ATC in connection with a case registered at Kohsar Police Station.
Police sought 30-day physical remand, but ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain rejected the request and sent the couple on judicial remand. The judge noted that although they had been nominated in the FIR as members of an unlawful assembly, no weapon had been attributed to either accused.
Read More: SC suspends trial court order, grants bail to Imaan Mazari, Hadi Ali Chattha
On September 27, the court issued a contempt notice to the Adiala jail superintendent after the authorities failed to facilitate the signing and transmission of the documents and also failed to produce the accused through video link. Two days later, the issue was resolved after Imaan and Hadi signed the required powers of attorney.
On September 29 , the ATC ended the contempt proceedings against the jail authorities and separately confirmed that notices had been issued on the couple’s bail applications, with arguments scheduled before Judge Abul Hasnat.
On October 7, the ATC had framed charges against Imaan and Hadi in the case related to the alleged violation of a designated route and incitement during the arrival of an international cricket team, despite defence objections that legal requirements had not been fulfilled.

title: Kremlin dismisses allegations of Russia s involvement in Europe unrest
description: Kremlin dismisses allegations of Russia s involvement in Europe unrest
content:
Kremlin spokesman says Putin approved Prime Minister Mishustin's proposals for government reshuffle
No one is taking seriously "absurd accusations" of Russia's involvement in unrest in Europe, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Monday.
"Nobody anywhere takes such absurd accusations seriously anymore. Not even in Europe itself," Peskov told Zvezda News media outlet.
Mass protests took place in Paris and other French cities on October, 17, with peaceful demonstrations escalating into riots in some locations.
Protesters set fire to municipal buildings, looted shops and attacked police stations, according to reports.
Also Read: Macron rejects interior minister's resignation after France-wide riots
Peskov also said that Russian President Vladimir Putin had backed proposals by Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin for a reshuffle in the government.
Mishustin presented the proposals during a working meeting with Putin on Monday morning, he said.
He did not specify which government officials would be affected by the changes. Under the Constitution, Mishustin will submit the relevant nominations to the State Duma for approval.
Asked whether Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was expected to visit Russia by the end of this year or in 2027, Peskov said the visit would most likely take place next year.
Under the 2000 declaration on strategic partnership between Russia and India, the two countries' leaders meet annually. Under the established rotation, Modi is due to make the next visit to Russia.
Peskov also announced that Russian President Vladimir Putin's combined call-in show and annual news conference is traditionally scheduled for December.

title: SHC sets aside most cuts ordered by Sindh censor board in  Ghost School
description: Court rules board failed to justify the cuts  directs it to reconsider the film s certification within 10 days
content:
Court rules board failed to justify the cuts, directs it to reconsider the film's certification within 10 days
The Sindh High Court (SHC) on Monday set aside most of the cuts ordered by the Sindh Board of Film Censors in the feature film Ghost School, ruling that the board had failed to justify its decision and observing that “the power to excise is not unbounded”. The court directed the board to reconsider the film’s certification within 10 days.
The case concerned Ghost School, a film about a 10-year-old girl who discovers that the only school in her village has closed amid rumours that it is haunted. The story explores the abandoned school and the fears and beliefs that have taken hold in the village.
The filmmakers challenged the censor board’s decision before the SHC under Article 199 of the Constitution, contesting its requirement to remove eight items before the film could receive a Universal (U) certificate.
A division bench comprising Justice Yousuf Ali Sayeed and Justice Adnan Iqbal Chaudhry held that the board’s decision could not stand because it had failed to explain how the disputed material violated the law or why its removal was necessary.
“The power to excise is not unbounded,” the court observed, adding that the necessity of any cut had to be assessed against the purpose it served and the constitutional protection of freedom of expression.
The court set aside the board’s decision, except for one cut to which the filmmakers had agreed. It directed the board either to issue a certificate allowing the film to be shown publicly without further cuts or, if it considered a higher age rating necessary, to give the filmmakers a personal hearing and issue a reasoned order explaining each objection.
The court also clarified that the board could reconsider only the objections it had already raised and directed it to adopt the least restrictive age rating that adequately addressed its concerns.
In a letter dated September 11, the Sindh board had ordered the removal of the expressions “biradri ka wadera”, “wadera” wherever it appeared, “kameene”, “haram khor”, “manhoos siyasatdan” and “Buraq” wherever it appeared. It had also ordered the removal of a child’s abusive remark in a school scene, as well as scenes depicting books being burnt and the school being set on fire at the end of the film.
The Central Board of Film Censors and the Punjab Board of Film Censors had already cleared the film for unrestricted public exhibition without any cuts. The Sindh board, however, had initially refused to certify it without explaining the reasons for its decision.
The filmmakers challenged that refusal in an earlier petition. In an order issued on August 21, the SHC directed the board to reconsider the matter, provide the filmmakers with a meaningful opportunity to be heard in person and record “cogent and intelligible reasons” for its decision.
Also Read: SHC orders Sindh censor board to reconsider ban on ‘Ghost School’
In its latest judgment, the court held that the board had failed to comply with those directions. Neither its decision nor its comments explained how the disputed words and scenes violated any of the grounds for censorship under Section 6(1) of the Sindh Motion Pictures Act, 2011, or any provision of a censorship code.
“Mere reference to a statutory provision, unconnected to the material said to offend it, is not a reason,” the judgment stated, adding that the board could not justify its decision retrospectively through comments or submissions.
“While we accept that such a concern as to rating may be a legitimate consideration under Section 4(2)(c), the power to excise is not unbounded,” the court observed.
It added that whether an excision was “necessary” had to be assessed against “the purpose it serves” and, where a citizen’s expression was “curtailed”, measured against Article 19 of the Constitution.
The court also questioned why the Sindh board had reached a different decision from the central and Punjab boards, which had approved the same version of the film without cuts.
“Nevertheless, where the Film, in identical form, has been found suitable for the same category elsewhere in the country, the Board was obliged, if it considered a different course necessary for Sindh, to at least say why,” the court observed.
The judgment added that any justification for a different decision, whether based on local circumstances or other considerations, had to be disclosed in a “reasoned order” with reference to Section 6(1) of the Act or a Censorship Code, allowing the decision to be scrutinised. The absence of such reasoning, it said, “reinforces the conclusion that the Impugned Decision was not the product of a considered exercise of discretion.”
The bench also questioned the board’s decision to treat the disputed words and scenes as though they were all of the same nature, without explaining why each needed to be removed.
“A term of social description such as ‘wadera’, a mild political epithet, mildly abusive words such as ‘kameene’ or ‘haram khor’, and the depiction of a school’s burning in a film condemning such acts, do not all stand on the same footing, and no single unexplained direction can justify them all,” the court observed.
“The Board was directed on 21.08.2026 to record cogent and intelligible reasons for whatever conclusion it reached,” the judgment stated. “Neither the Impugned Decision nor the Respondents’ comments do anything of the sort, and in the absence of any stated ground, we are of the view that the excisions, other than the one consented to, cannot stand.”
Read More: Seemab Gul’s award-winning film 'Ghost School' barred from cinemas in Sindh
The bench also considered whether the filmmakers could approach the High Court directly. The respondents objected that Rule 36(2) of the Sindh Censorship of Film Rules, 2014, provided for an appeal to an appellate committee.
The filmmakers argued that the committee had neither been constituted nor notified and that their inquiries to the relevant department about its status had gone unanswered. The court noted that the respondents had not addressed the issue in their comments and had raised the objection only during the hearing.
“Needless to say, a remedy that the Government has itself failed to bring into being cannot be pressed as an alternative,” the court said, holding that the petition was maintainable.
In examining the legal limits of censorship, the court referred to an earlier SHC judgment in Moulvi Iqbal Haider v Federation of Pakistan, which emphasised the need to protect freedom of expression when reviewing censorship decisions.
Quoting from that judgment, the bench said, “The default position of the Court under Article 199 ought to be that of fully safeguarding the fundamental right by giving as expansive an interpretation to Article 19 as possible, and in the event of a restriction being imposed by the Board or any other authority that may be competent in that regard, testing the reasonableness of that restriction stringently, so as to ensure that the same is ‘reasonable’ in the strictest conceivable sense”.
The court also referred to the Supreme Court’s ruling in Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority v ARY Communications, which held that a work of art should be assessed as a whole and that restrictions should go no further than necessary.
The bench noted that the Supreme Court had called for a more lenient approach when reviewing elements of an artistic work that were necessary to convey its message. Where only a particular part was objectionable, the court said, only that part should be modified, with restrictions kept to a minimum.
The petition was allowed, and the board’s decision was set aside except for the cut accepted by the filmmakers. The court directed the board to reconsider the film’s certification within 10 days of the filmmakers removing the agreed item.
Under the order, the board must either issue a certificate allowing unrestricted public exhibition without further cuts or, if it considers any of the remaining excisions necessary for a category higher than U, provide the filmmakers with a personal hearing and issue a reasoned order. The order must identify the specific concern in each instance, with reference to Rule 11 of the 2014 Rules.

title: Any direct or indirect attack on Makkah alliance member state will trigger  collective response   DG ISPR
description: Chaudhry says necessary support to achieve objectives already being provided  will continue to be provided
content:
Says holy sites' security 'non-negotiable', Pakistan to review any Yemeni request for military support
Director General of Inter-Services Public Relations (DG ISPR) Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said that the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA) was purely defensive in nature and "has no offensive intent", warning that any direct or indirect attack on any of its three member states would trigger a collective response.
"So once you have this collective deterrence, what it does is that it gives a very strong and clear message to those elements of instability, of chaos in the region, that if you directly or indirectly wage this war against any of these three countries, then the response will be collective," Chaudhry said during an interview with Independent Arabia on Sunday.
The statement came amid escalating tensions in the Middle East following a series of missile and drone attacks by Yemen's Houthi group on Saudi Arabia, which have killed at least 17 people and injured 333 others, according to the Saudi-led coalition. The attacks have targeted key civilian and energy infrastructure, including Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and oil facilities, disrupting air travel and raising concerns over regional security.
Pakistan has repeatedly condemned the attacks and reaffirmed its solidarity with Saudi Arabia, reiterating its commitment to safeguarding the kingdom's sovereignty, territorial integrity and security. Islamabad has also emphasised the importance of protecting holy sites and pledged continued support for Saudi Arabia's defence amid growing regional instability.
The military spokesperson reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to safeguarding Saudi Arabia's sovereignty, territorial integrity and the security of holy mosques, expressing hope that collective deterrence would prevent further aggression. However, he warned that if deterrence failed, it would have to be re-established through all means available to the three member states of the Makkah Defence Alliance.
"The Saudis' sovereignty and territorial integrity, security, and foremost, the security of the Haramain Sharifain is paramount. It's non-negotiable. It's absolute as far as Pakistan is concerned. So once we say that, whatever support is needed to do that is being provided and will be provided," he said.
Speaking about the Makkah Defence Alliance, Chaudhry said operational details of military alliances were not disclosed publicly for security reasons.
"If you want to go into the domains, specifics, quantification, no alliance does that. No military does that. Because there is operational confidentiality. There are tactical, sub-tactical details, which are never made public," he added.
Regarding Pakistan's coordination with Saudi Arabia amid the Houthis' military gains, Chaudhry was asked whether Islamabad's support would remain purely defensive.
"The coordination between Pakistan and the Saudis is in all domains, and if you're talking specifically of the military domain, it has been there for decades. We have coordinated with each other. The coordination dates back before the Makkah alliance, and it is there right now," he said.
The coordination, Chaudhry added, was in "multiple domains" and would continue.
Asked about his reaction to the Houthis targeting Saudi Arabia, specifically the holy sites, Chaudhry noted that Pakistan's reaction "from the streets, from a young boy or girl, up to our military leadership is one of anger." He added, "Our reaction is that why anyone in their right mind would attack or threaten Saudi Arabia and the holy places or even give an impression of threatening the holy places."
That is why, he said, "there can be no negotiations, there cannot be any ifs and buts."
Read: Pakistan committed to 'negotiated and peaceful outcome' between US, Iran: DG ISPR
Chaudhry noted that the message Pakistan would like to give regarding the Houthis' targeting of mosques and the King Khalid Airport was already presented by the political leadership and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff, Field Marshal Asim Munir.
"The communications have been very clear, and I would just like to reiterate: the message is that the Muslims need to unite; we don't need to fight." He noted that no advantage came to any country which "vertically or horizontally" escalated the conflict.
"We need to stop attacking each other," Chaudhry said, adding that this is what Pakistan's political and military leadership had been trying to do.
According to the spokesperson, "We need to come to a negotiated outcome." If this failed, he said, then "this collective deterrence, this instrument of collective deterrence of the Makkah alliance will come into play, as it is coming into play."
Referring to the defensive nature of the pact, Chaudhry noted that the leadership of all three countries was "absolutely clear" that the alliance had no offensive intent. "It is purely defensive, so that's how it is and that's how it will remain," he said.
The spokesperson said that the alliance had evolved in a very short period of time, which he said was "phenomenal." He explained that it was phenomenal "because a meeting of three minds, for collective deterrence, and the three minds, the three countries that have met and joined, they have decades, even centuries of relationship based on mutual trust and respect."
The alliance, he said, was "not out of the blue," as relations between the three countries went "way back."
DG ISPR stated that Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye "believe in peace, stability, and prosperity for their people, as well as in the region," adding that the "foundation is so strong, the logic is so powerful that that is why you have seen how quickly it has evolved."
He noted that the alliance now had a general secretariat and had announced a general secretary, along with formulating a Strategic Political and Defence Committee which comprises the foreign ministers, the defence ministers and the services chief.
"The communication is very transparent and clear about what the pact says, what the intentions are, and its manifestations on the ground are also already there," Chaudhry said, noting that the sceptics "also have a job so let them do their job."
Regarding plans to expand the alliance if any countries expressed interest in joining, Chaudhry stated that the political and military leadership of the alliance had "already made itself very clear that this alliance is not only restricted to these three countries." He added that the alliance "is defensive in nature. It does not displace, replace, or abrogate any existing military-to-military relations or agreements or arrangements with any other countries."
"The alliance remains open to all those countries that believe in collective deterrence, peace, stability and security of the region, who have a common belief of the aspirations of regional security and the way the alliance is manifesting itself on the ground," he said. However, he noted that the decision on the process and timing of potential expansion was for the leadership of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye.
Further, he clarified that the leaderships would also decide on any conditions, aspirations or commonalities for joining the pact.
Responding to reports of Egypt and Syria expressing interest in joining the alliance, Chaudhry noted, "It is in layers; we are at the operational level - we're at the operational arm of this alliance which is to be implemented when decided by the political, strategic, and military leadership." He added, "The decision of who to come, when to come, how to come and join in the alliance is at that level."
Noting that the alliance was "not country-specific," Chaudhry noted that it was based on principles of peace, stability and regional security. "Any actor which threatens that peace, stability and security, it automatically interacts with this collective deterrence mechanism that has been established," the military spokesperson said.
Asked whether Islamabad had given any warning to Iran over the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, Chaudhry emphasised that "for months, the politico-military leadership of Pakistan has been interacting with the players involved in this conflict, including Iran, with the singular intent of restraint and to reduce the temperature and bring the parties to a negotiated, peaceful outcome."
Read More: Pakistan condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, calls for immediate halt at UN
He added, "All our interactions and conversations with the parties are based on dialling down the escalation, and that is what we are doing and will continue to do."
Regarding the escalation of the Houthi-Saudi Arabia conflict, Chaudhry compared it to a "sinusoidal pattern", saying that the conflict "goes down and then the agents of chaos come into play and then they take the ante up, and then the pragmatic forces, they understand that this escalation is going nowhere."
He added that parties like Pakistan, "who strongly believe in peace and sustained peace, which is based on a conviction of peace," then "play their part to dial down the escalation, to talk to the forces that this escalation that you are trying to bring up, it is not getting you anywhere, it is not going to resolve this conflict."
"Whether you expand it to the Houthis, whether you expand it to other places, it doesn't serve anything; it only serves those who are interested in chaos in the region," he said. The military spokesperson also noted that it did not serve the interests of Muslims.
"At the same time, you have seen through our forces, through our statements, through our acts, and through our operational employment, that Pakistan has been giving very strong signals that this collective deterrence is at play, has already been actualised, and we will take all necessary steps for the security and territorial integrity of Saudi Arabia and the holy places," he said.
"That message is going to everyone," Chaudhry said. Asked whether the Houthis would listen to such a message, Chaudhry noted that Pakistan had already been dealing with the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), the Kharjis, saying that "these non-state actors, they don't behave like states." He added, "Their conception actually stems from a concept of acting as proxies for others. How they're going to behave, that's a difficult thing to fathom and to predict."
However, he stated that one thing was clear "that they behave and respond only to clear communication and where the intent is absolute and there is no hesitation," adding that on part of the Makkah alliance "there is no hesitation in our communication to them."
Regarding the possibility of providing direct military support to the Yemeni government, Chaudhry said that he didn't know whether Islamabad had received an official request, but noted that the government would evaluate and respond to any request.
On hostilities between the United States and Iran escalating after the US midterms, Chaudhry stated, "The concern of escalation is always there."
Concluding, Chaudhry noted that the developments in the region were "more or less showing that the countries in the region are coming closer together for regional security, collective security, and peace and stability, looking towards each other, holding each others hands for the peace and prosperity of the respective people in the region."

title: Trump holds off on new measures against Russia to avoid undermining Ukraine peace talks
description: Trump holds off on new measures against Russia to avoid undermining Ukraine peace talks
content:
US president says he does not want to take action that would drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table
US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he would not sign a document imposing additional measures on Russia for now, arguing that doing so could undermine negotiations to end the war in Ukraine.
“My decision on Russia is a very simple one,” he said in a post on his Truth Social platform , adding that he was negotiating peace between Russia and Ukraine and did not want to take an action that would “drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table.”
Read More: Russia is ready for new ideas on Ukraine peace, but with conditions, senior diplomat says
Trump said “great progress” was being made in the negotiations, including ongoing “hostage negotiations.”
He said he could sign the document at a later date or “any time” he wanted.
The president did not provide details about the negotiations or identify the hostages to whom he was referring.
Trump’s statement came amid controversy over his administration’s decision to delay the implementation of new sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia and countries purchasing Russian energy.
The measures, approved by Congress, include sanctions against Russian officials, banks and energy traders as well as the possibility of steep tariffs on countries that continue to import Russian oil and gas.
Also Read: EU plans most far-reaching sanctions against Russia
Trump also cited Russia’s limited support for Iran as a reason to avoid increasing pressure on Moscow.
“Russia is doing very little, if anything, to help the Islamic Republic of Iran, compared to what they could be doing, and I want to keep it that way,” he said.
He also sharply criticised Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy over Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil and diesel refineries.
Trump said Zelenskyy was targeting Russian diesel facilities despite knowing that the attacks were “seriously hurting the world diesel markets,” including in the US.
He argued that farmers, ranchers and businesses were suffering from higher fuel costs while Russia was continuing to supply “millions of barrels” of diesel to international markets at low prices.
“Zelenskyy doesn’t care,” he said, accusing the Ukrainian leader of lacking an interest in ending the war.
Trump claimed that Zelenskyy could have secured a better agreement two years earlier and said Ukraine was now in ruins, had lost a large amount of territory and had suffered heavy casualties.
Read: Russian diesel deal puts Trump at odds with allies
Trump has faced criticism from Kyiv and lawmakers in both major US parties over his approach to Russia, including the postponement of additional sanctions and Washington’s decision to authorise imports of Russian diesel.
Zelenskyy has argued that easing pressure on Moscow would encourage Russia to continue the war rather than bring it to an end.
Ukraine has defended its attacks on Russian energy infrastructure as a response to Moscow’s continuing strikes against Ukrainian power facilities and as an attempt to reduce revenue available for Russia’s military campaign.
Trump, however, has repeatedly called on Kyiv to stop targeting Russian refineries, arguing that the attacks are contributing to higher global energy prices.

title: Five young men killed as speeding car overturns  catches fire in Multan
description: The car went out of control near Sabzazar Metro Station  hit a road divider  overturned  and crashed into a wall
content:
The car went out of control near Sabzazar Metro Station, hit a road divider, overturned, and crashed into a wall
Five young men were killed when a speeding car overturned and caught fire on Bosan Road in Multan early on Monday, Rescue 1122 said.
The car went out of control near Sabzazar Metro Station, hit a road divider, overturned and crashed into a wall, according to rescue officials. Rescue 1122 teams responded to the incident, extinguished the fire and shifted the bodies to Nishtar Hospital, officials said.
The deceased were identified as Muhammad Yasir, 22; Muhammad Muzammil, 23; Ramazan, 28; Wahab; and Kasho Khakhi. All five were from Shujaabad tehsil in Multan district.
Multan City Police Officer (CPO) Akhtar Farooq also reached the scene with a heavy police contingent after receiving information about the accident and reviewed the situation.
The bodies were later handed over to the families and taken to their native areas in Shujaabad. The deceased belonged to Multani Gate, Railway Station, Khakhi Banjani and Basti Khoja areas.
Rescue officials said several similar accidents caused by overspeeding had previously occurred on major roads in Multan, including Bosan Road, Multan Avenue and Multan Public School Road, resulting in numerous injuries and deaths.
The accident came amid a series of fatal road crashes across the country. On October 16, eight people were killed and eight injured in two separate accidents in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P). Six people died when a passenger van overturned in Buner, while two children were killed after being run over by a truck near Tarnab Road in Charsadda.
The same day, three members of a family, including a 15-year-old boy, were killed when a 22-wheeler trailer loaded with cement crushed their car at a traffic signal in Lahore’s Garhi Shahu area. According to Rescue 1122, the car’s occupants became trapped inside the wreckage. The FIR alleged that the trailer driver had been driving recklessly.
Read: 2 children among 8 killed in separate road accidents in K-P
On October 13, four people, including a woman, were killed and five others injured when a van collided with a truck on the Quetta-Karachi National Highway near Badrang in Mastung district. The van was travelling from Quetta to Kalat when the collision occurred.
A school van carrying 12 children from two private schools fell into a ravine and caught fire on Sign Road in Masiari, Murree, on September 29, injuring 11 children. Police said the van’s brakes had failed, while four children with serious burns were shifted to hospitals in Rawalpindi. An 11-year-old girl later died at Holy Family Hospital, while two other children remained in critical condition. Following the incident, Murree traffic police made fire extinguishers in school vehicles mandatory and ordered regular inspections to enforce safety requirements and prevent overloading and speeding.
Earlier, on August 30, four people were killed and seven injured when a passenger van collided with a dumper near Tunnel No 3 on the Swat Motorway in Lower Dir district. A motorway police spokesperson attributed the crash to the negligence and carelessness of the van driver.
In July, at least 40 people were killed and eight injured when a passenger coach travelling from Quetta to Peshawar plunged into a ravine in the Danasar area of the Sherani-Zhob Highway, near the Balochistan-K-P border. The difficult mountainous terrain complicated rescue efforts.
Then, in June, at least 10 people, including five children, were killed and 13 injured when a passenger van carrying a family from Multan to Murree plunged into a drainage channel and caught fire near Khajut on the Rawalpindi–Murree Expressway. Motorway Police said the van had lost control while negotiating a bend, while a subsequent investigation suspected negligence and careless driving by the driver.

title: Agha fixes leg alignment to rediscover scoring touch
description: Pakistan   s premier batsman says a good pitch encourages him to target 300 after early collapse against Sri Lanka
content:
Pakistan’s premier batsman says a good pitch encourages him to target 300 after early collapse against Sri Lanka
Pakistan’s experienced batsman Salman Ali Agha said correcting his leg alignment during domestic cricket helped him rediscover his form, which culminated in a match-winning century against Sri Lanka in the opening game of the ODI tri-series. Agha scored 107, his fourth ODI century, to help Pakistan post 305 all out before the bowlers dismissed Sri Lanka for 268 in the 49th over, securing a 37-run victory at the Pindi Cricket Stadium on Sunday. Shaheen Shah Afridi led the bowling attack with three wickets, while Haris Rauf, Naseem Shah and Faheem Ashraf claimed two wickets apiece to give Pakistan a winning start to the tournament, which also features England. Agha said he had identified a technical flaw in his batting during a difficult period in international cricket and used domestic matches to address it. “When you struggle in international cricket, you face issues with your technique. I also had an issue because my leg used to go across. I went back to domestic cricket, worked on it and corrected my leg alignment, which benefited me,” he said. The right-hander had endured a difficult England series before returning to domestic cricket, where he struck a triple century in his first President's Trophy match. He continued to build on that performance before carrying his improved form into international cricket. “I'm feeling good, especially when your team wins and you contribute to the victory,” Agha said. “We have come here after playing domestic cricket, and I was performing well there. I'm very happy to have carried that form into international cricket,” he added. Pakistan were struggling at 118-4 when Agha came to the crease, but the batsman said he quickly assessed the conditions and decided that a total of 300 was within reach. “At one point, we were 118-4. After facing a few balls, I realised the pitch was good. I felt we needed to score 300; otherwise, we would struggle,” he said. “I tried to take it ball by ball and get the team to 300.” Agha's innings provided the foundation for Pakistan's total, which ultimately proved beyond Sri Lanka's reach as the hosts' bowlers maintained pressure throughout the chase. The century also carried a personal significance for Agha, who revealed that his celebration after reaching three figures was dedicated to his four-year-old son. “That signal was for my son, who watches television while putting his finger on his cheek. He is only four years old, but I had told my family that the next time I would score a hundred, I would celebrate like that,” he said. Agha's return to form offers Pakistan an encouraging boost as they continue their campaign in the tri-series against Sri Lanka and England.
