title: PSX slips 454 points as investors struggle to find direction
description: KSE 100 Index settles at 165 966 amid lack of positive cues  subdued sentiment
content:
KSE-100 Index settles at 165,966 amid lack of positive cues, subdued sentiment
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) closed lower on Monday as a subdued market mood and persistent selling in key sectors kept investors cautious, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index failing to sustain its recovery amid a lack of positive triggers. The index shed 453.63 points, or 0.27%, to settle at 165,966.09 points.
The session began on a weak note, with the index falling to 166,120.90 points, down 298.81 points, or 0.18%, at 9:38am, reflecting early selling pressure. The market attempted to recover during the day, with the index climbing to an intraday high of 166,698.46 points. However, the recovery proved short-lived, and the index later touched a low of 165,918.35 points before ending the session in negative territory.
Selling was observed in major sectors including automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration companies and oil marketing companies. The broad-based pressure limited the market’s ability to build on its intraday recovery and left the benchmark below the previous close.
Investor sentiment remained fragile as the market lacked fresh positive cues to encourage sustained buying. With selling pressure persisting across key sectors, investors remained cautious, keeping the overall tone subdued through the session.
According to KTrade Securities, the KSE-100 Index declined 454 points (-0.27%) to close at 165,966 on Monday amid cautious investor sentiment and subdued volume of 109 million shares. Trading activity was concentrated in Pakistan Refinery, Cnergyico PK, TPL Trakker, Worldcall Telecom and Saif Power, while selective buying in MCB Bank, Attock Refinery, Pakistan Oilfield, TRG Pakistan and Bank Al Falah provided partial support.
Sectoral weakness was broad-based, led by commercial banks, cements, investment banks and techs while UBL, Systems, Fauji Fertiliser and Hub Power led stock-specific declines. Meanwhile, Brent crude remained elevated above $100 per barrel, resulting in macroeconomic uncertainty.
KTraded added that it expected the market to remain cautious and range-bound next week, with near-term direction contingent on global oil prices, geopolitical developments and corporate earnings. A sustained recovery in trading volumes remains critical to underpin broader market participation and a durable rally, it said.
Overall, trading volume decreased to 370.9 million shares against Friday’s total of 396.9 million while the value of traded shares stood at Rs19.56 billion. Shares of 499 companies were traded in the ready market, of which 163 stocks closed higher, 302 fell and 34 remained unchanged.
Pak Refinery was the volume leader with trading in 53 million shares, gaining Rs1.86 to close at Rs108.81.

title: Miley Cyrus hits back at critics questioning her stage presence during Hollywood Bowl comeback
description: Cyrus defended her commitment to live music after videos online questioned her stage presence during her comeback show
content:
Cyrus defended her commitment to live music after videos online questioned her stage presence during her comeback show
Miley Cyrus has responded to criticism of her recent Hollywood Bowl performance, defending her commitment to live music after social media videos questioned her stage presence during her comeback show.
The singer addressed the backlash during her second performance at the Los Angeles venue on Sunday, October 18, after returning to the stage following a four-year absence from live performances.
Cyrus said online commentary had accused her of not fully engaging with the performance because she did not sing every word of her songs.
“I’ve never heard that I don’t put my heart into something,” she told the audience, adding that some people were making videos to generate “clickbait”.
The singer also reflected on how her relationship with performing had evolved over the years, acknowledging that returning to the stage was not as natural as it once had been.
“It is hard for me to stand up here and do this show,” she said. “It does not come as natural as it once did to be before. Because, like all of us, we change, we evolve, we grow, and we find what gets to come with us.”
Cyrus explained that the experience was personally meaningful and allowed her to challenge her own limits rather than simply meet audience expectations.
She then made her position clear, saying, “I can take a lot, but one thing I will not stand is any question about where my heart is when I'm on the stage. Not one. I am fully present.”
During her performance of “Bass Persuades”, she also appeared to address the criticism directly, joking, “Oh I forgot, I’m supposed to sing every f**king word.”
Cyrus released her latest album, Bass Persuades , in September. No further tour dates were listed in the report.

title: Macron rejects interior minister s resignation after France wide riots
description: Macron rejects interior minister s resignation after France wide riots
content:
Violence targeted around 1,500 businesses, with nearly 2,400 arrested, according to official figures
French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday rejected the resignation of Interior Minister Laurent Nunez following widespread violence and looting across the country during last weekend's protests , according to broadcaster BFMTV .
Nunez submitted his resignation to Macron a day earlier amid mounting criticism over the authorities' handling of the unrest.
"I am the minister of the interior, I am responsible for everything that happens on the ground," he told France Inter radio , explaining his decision to resign.
Nunez acknowledged a "loss of control" by police in some cities and admitted there had been a "lack of anticipation" in deploying available security forces.
However, the president decided to keep him in office, citing the need for continuity in the command of security forces during the current crisis, according to a statement from the Elysee Palace .
Macron also called for greater transparency over what he described as "failures in anticipation and intelligence" that contributed to the scale of the violence.
The unrest, which erupted during demonstrations on Saturday, left nearly 1,000 law enforcement officers injured and resulted in approximately 2,400 arrests, according to official figures.
Read More: Student protests spread across France, Belgium
The government's response has faced criticism from several local leaders, including the mayors of Paris, Marseille and Limoges.
Nunez is expected to visit Marseille, one of the cities hardest hit by the violence, where authorities reported that up to 30,000 people were involved in looting on Saturday.
In a televised address a day earlier, Macron vowed that those responsible for the destruction would be held accountable.
"Those who sought to bring down the republic will be held accountable," he said, adding that the country felt "anger and shame" over the violence.
Further clashes and looting were reported late Sunday in Paris, Lyon and Marseille.
In the French capital, police arrested 92 people by around midnight following renewed incidents near Place de la République.
Read more: Greta Thunberg joins French teens on new day of school protests
Meanwhile, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu is due to chair an interministerial crisis meeting at 10 am local time (0800GMT) to assess the economic impact of the unrest, damage to businesses, insurance issues and ongoing legal proceedings.
According to the Federation of Commerce and Distribution, around 1,500 businesses were targeted during Saturday's violence, with estimated losses amounting to several hundred million euros.

title: US  exhausted and worn out   lacks capability to launch new conflict  IRGC
description: Foreign Minister Araghchi meets Russian counterpart  discusses bilateral  regional developments
content:
Foreign Minister Araghchi meets Russian counterpart, discusses bilateral, regional developments
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) spokesperson Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi said that the United States forces were "exhausted and worn out," and that they lacked the capability to launch a new conflict, Tehran Times reported on Monday.
The spokesperson stated that the US "entered the war with all its might in the past and is certainly not in a position now to launch a new conflict that would yield any additional gains for it." He added that most US bases in the region "have been rendered inactive," and American forces had "withdrawn hundreds of kilometres away from Iran."
"From a technical and military standpoint, the United States lacks the capability to launch a new conflict," Mohebbi said, according to Tehran Times . The spokesperson noted however, that as US midterm elections approach, "it may seek to manufacture some achievements."
"We do not rule out any possibilities and are prepared to respond. This time, our response will be much more forceful," he said.
On the IRGC's military capabilities , Mohebbi stated, "Our capabilities have undoubtedly increased significantly, both quantitatively and qualitatively, and are now at least 1.5 times greater than in the past."
According to Tehran Times , the spokesperson added that the production of missiles, drones, and other equipment Tehran needed was never halted. "We have even expanded production, improving range, accuracy, and destructive power, while also developing new weapons," Mohebbi said, adding that if the war escalated, "the IRGC’s surprises will reveal themselves."
Separately, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met his Russian counterpart Sergey Lavrov, with both sides reviewing bilateral, regional and international developments, IRNA news agency said in a post on X .
Lavrov arrived in Tehran for his first visit since the outbreak of the Middle East war, Iran’s state broadcaster IRIB reported earlier in the day. The foreign minister is expected to meet Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during the visit, IRIB said, citing Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei.
The spokesperson said the visit is part of ongoing bilateral consultations and efforts to follow up on agreements between the two countries. Iran and Russia have strengthened political, economic and military cooperation in recent years amid Western sanctions imposed on both countries.
In January 2025, Pezeshkian and Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a 20-year Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty in Moscow, covering cooperation in defence, security, energy, trade and transportation. The agreement also provides for closer coordination on regional and international issues, although it does not establish a mutual defence obligation.​​​​​​​
Oil tanker catches fire in Hormuz, IRGC says
An oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz, the IRGC Navy said late Sunday.
The blast struck the vessel’s engine room as it attempted to leave the strategic waterway, Iran’s semi-official Fars News Agency reported, citing an IRGC Navy statement. The tanker had switched off all its positioning and navigation systems from the start of its voyage and attempted to use what Tehran considers an unauthorised southern route, according to the statement.
The IRGC Navy accused the vessel of violating maritime regulations governing passage through the strait. It warned that ships operating in the Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf with their navigation and identification systems switched off would face a firm response.
Read: Vance acknowledges ‘failures’ in US handling of Iran war
The statement did not identify the tanker or provide information on possible casualties or the extent of the damage.
The announcement follows a series of similar incidents in the strategic waterway. On Saturday, the IRGC Navy said a second supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude oil struck a naval mine and caught fire while attempting to cross the strait through an unauthorised route.
A day earlier, the Iranian force reported that another tanker had struck a mine, triggering an explosion and fire.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on February 28. Tehran responded with missile and drone attacks across the region and effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, while Washington later imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports.
The US and Iran subsequently signed a memorandum of understanding in June concerning freedom of navigation in the strait, but implementation stalled over disagreements related to security in the strategic waterway.
Araghchi accuses Netanyahu of seeking to drag US into another war with Tehran
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of seeking to drag the United States into another war with Iran to avoid imprisonment, while warning Washington against renewed military action.
“Netanyahu is driving America into another war to stay out of jail,” Araghchi wrote on the US social media platform X, accusing the Israeli leader of disregarding the consequences for Israel and US President Donald Trump.
“Last time you wanted to ‘finish the job,’ Iran emerged even stronger. Want to try your luck again? Be our guest. But be careful; we have unfinished jobs too,” he added.
His remarks came after Trump endorsed Netanyahu a day earlier ahead of Israel’s October 27 elections , praising their partnership in confronting Iran and warning that Washington might have to take on the task itself if Israelis elected another leader.
Read More: EU calls ICC arrest warrants for Netanyahu, Gallant 'binding', urges swift enforcement
“If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work itself, and I am not inclined to do so,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform , using Netanyahu’s nickname.
Netanyahu has headed the current government since late 2022, which has been described as the most right-wing in Israel’s history. He is also standing trial domestically on corruption charges that could carry prison sentences if convicted and has been wanted by the International Court of Justice since 2024 for war crimes in Gaza.
Opposition parties have intensified coordination in an effort to replace Netanyahu’s government through the ballot box.
The US and Israel launched military strikes against Iran on Feb. 28, prompting retaliatory attacks by Tehran.
Despite an April ceasefire and a framework agreement reached in June, fighting later resumed as negotiations between Washington and Tehran stalled.

title: Deaf Reach golf event concludes
description: More than 120 golfers compete at DHA Country and Golf Club as charity event raises Rs42m for deaf education
content:
More than 120 golfers compete at DHA Country and Golf Club as charity event raises Rs42m for deaf education
Jubilee Life 1 and Touchpoint won the gross and net team titles, respectively, at the Deaf Reach Schools Charity Golf Tournament held at the Defence Authority Country and Golf Club on Sunday.
Jubilee Life 1, comprising Ibrahim Khan, Jameel Khan, Nasir Khan and Hamza Zahid Khan, claimed the gross title with a score of 58.
Touchpoint, represented by Salman Ali, Tabish Sabah, Imran Haroon and Syed Saquib Zafar, lifted the net competition with a score of 54.
HMB 1 finished runner-up in the gross category with 59, while A Qadir and Company placed third with 61. King Apparel secured second place in the net category with 55.9, followed by Mediplas with 56.2.
In the subsidiary prizes, Hamza Shikoh Khan won nearest to the pin on hole seven, while Ayhan Azeem took the honour on hole 17. Jawad Amjad recorded the longest drive on hole 13 at 359 yards, while Bilal Nasim won the longest-drive prize on hole 15 with 346 yards.
The tournament, powered by Mavericks, attracted more than 120 golfers and raised Rs42 million for Deaf Reach's education and development programmes for deaf children and young people across Pakistan.
Played in the Texas Scramble format, the annual event brought together members of the golfing community to compete for honours while supporting access to education and vocational training for the country's deaf community.
A Suzuki Fronx was offered as the prize for a hole-in-one, adding another incentive for competitors on the course.
“It was truly a team effort, and I'm delighted that we were able to help raise Rs42 million for such a worthwhile cause,” said Abdullah Nasser, captain of Mavericks.
“The response from the golfing community, sponsors and everyone who contributed has been tremendous. The real achievement is knowing that these funds will help create more opportunities for deaf children and young people in Pakistan,” he added.
Deaf Reach, a programme of the Family Educational Services Foundation (FESF), has been working since 1989 to improve access to education for underserved deaf children and young people.
Its network of schools, colleges and training centres provides academic education, Pakistan Sign Language-based instruction, information technology education and vocational skills training. The organisation also supports teacher development, parent training, employment opportunities and the development of digital learning resources in Pakistan Sign Language.
Richard Geary, founder of Deaf Reach, said events such as the tournament demonstrated how collective support could help broaden educational opportunities for deaf children.
“Every contribution helps us extend access to education, skills and opportunities, enabling more young people to realise their potential,” he said.

title: Kaia Gerber pays emotional tribute to brother Presley after his death at 27
description: The eldest son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber  Presley died at a rehabilitation facility on September 20
content:
The eldest son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber, Presley died at a rehabilitation facility on September 20
Kaia Gerber has paid an emotional tribute to her late brother, Presley Gerber, one month after his death at the age of 27, sharing heartfelt reflections on grief and their lifelong bond.
The 25-year-old model shared a personal message on Instagram on October 18, shortly after her mother, supermodel Cindy Crawford, posted a statement on behalf of the family.
“Prez, i don’t have the words. and maybe the tiny mercy is that we don’t need them all along,” Kaia began, describing the difficulty of finding language to express the loss.
She reflected on their relationship, writing, “you know how much i loved being your sister. it has always been, and will forever be, my favorite thing about myself.”
Accompanying her tribute were childhood photographs of the siblings on a beach and a video of them dancing together.
Kaia described Presley as “my best buddy, my great protector” and “the one true love of my life”.
In one of the most poignant passages, she wrote, “i was born loving you. i will die loving you. there was never anything else.”
Crawford and her husband, businessman Rande Gerber, also shared a message remembering their son as a “sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever”.
Presley died at a rehabilitation facility on September 20, according to Los Angeles County Medical Examiner records. His official cause of death has been deferred while the investigation continues, the report stated.
The eldest child of Crawford and Rande, Presley began modelling at 15, following in his mother's footsteps. He later worked with IMG Models and appeared in campaigns and fashion shows.
Kaia concluded her tribute by expressing how difficult life felt without her brother, writing, “my darling brother, i do adore you. i love my brother. my brother is dead. and this party sucks so bad without you, prez.”

title: FM Dar arrives in Tajikistan to lead Pakistan   s delegation at SCO meeting
description: Council of heads of govt expected to adopt joint commnique  statements and important decisions
content:
Council of heads of govt expected to adopt joint commnique, statements and important decisions
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar arrived in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on Monday to lead Pakistan’s delegation to the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Council of Heads of Government (CHG) meeting being held on October 19-20, the Foreign Office (FO) said.
Upon arrival, FM Dar was received by Tajikistan’s Minister of Energy and Water Resources and Co-Chair of the Pakistan-Tajikistan Joint Commission, Daler Juma, Pakistan’s Ambassador to Tajikistan, Irfan Ahmed, and Pakistan’s National Coordinator for the SCO, Khalil Hashmi, along with senior Tajik government officials, according to the FO.
In an earlier statement issued ahead of the visit, the FO said FM Dar would attend the meeting at the invitation of Tajikistan’s Prime Minister Qohir Rasulzoda.
“The FM Dar will lead Pakistan’s delegation to the meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of Government (CHG), to be held in Dushanbe, Republic of Tajikistan on 19-20 October 2026,” it said.
The meeting will bring together the prime ministers of Belarus, China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan, while Iran will be represented by its vice-president and India by its external affairs minister, according to the statement.
The FO said the Council of Heads of Government was the SCO’s “second highest decision-making institution” and provided guidance on economic and financial affairs, trade, connectivity, commerce, socio-economic cooperation and the organisation’s budget.
Read: Pakistan, Iran FMs to meet in Baghdad
“The CHG will also adopt a Joint Communiqué, statements and important decisions,” it said.
During the visit, FM Dar was also scheduled to call on Tajikistan’s president and prime minister and hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from SCO member states on the sidelines of the meeting.
The SCO is a regional organisation whose areas of cooperation include economic development, trade, connectivity and security. Its Council of Heads of Government focuses primarily on economic and financial cooperation among member states.
Regional cooperation and Pakistan’s role
The meeting comes as Pakistan advances its priorities under its chairmanship of the SCO Council of Heads of State for 2026-27, with the country scheduled to host the organisation’s next summit in Islamabad in 2027.
In September, Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to advancing the bloc’s objectives and called for greater practical cooperation among member states in areas including economic development, transport and connectivity.
Pakistan’s chairmanship is being pursued under the theme “Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation, and Shared Prosperity” , with FM Dar stressing the need to translate the organisation’s shared objectives into practical outcomes.
Read more: FM Dar, Iranian counterpart reaffirm importance of continued engagement
At the SCO Council of Heads of State meeting in Bishkek in September, member states adopted the Bishkek Declaration, outlining plans to deepen cooperation on security, trade and technology. More than 20 additional documents were signed or adopted, covering areas including transport, energy, drug trafficking, digital infrastructure and environmental cooperation.
The summit also designated Lahore as the SCO’s tourism and cultural capital for 2026-27. Pakistan is due to host the next Council of Heads of State summit in 2027.
Pakistan previously hosted the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in Islamabad on October 15-16, 2024. The gathering focused on cooperation, connectivity and trade, with member states issuing a joint communiqué and reaffirming their commitment to implementing decisions taken at earlier SCO meetings.
Dar, Araghchi maintain diplomatic contact
The foreign minister’s visit also comes amid continued diplomatic engagement between Pakistan and Iran over regional developments.
On Sunday, Dar held a telephone conversation with Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi, during which the two discussed the evolving regional situation and the ongoing Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) Council of Foreign Ministers meeting in Baghdad.
According to the FO, Dar underscored the importance of continued dialogue and diplomacy in addressing regional challenges, and the two leaders agreed to maintain close contact.
The two ministers have also met on the sidelines of previous multilateral gatherings. In September, they held talks in Bishkek ahead of the SCO Council of Heads of State meeting, discussing bilateral relations and regional developments and reaffirming the importance of continued engagement.
During the Dushanbe meeting, FM Dar is expected to hold bilateral talks with counterparts from SCO member states, providing an opportunity to discuss regional developments and cooperation alongside the organisation’s economic agenda.

title: Why Kylie Jenner was chosen to wear  50m Victoria   s Secret Fantasy Bra
description: Kylie Jenner wore Victoria   s Secret   s  50m Fantasy Bra at 2026 fashion show  marking her runway debut
content:
Kylie Jenner wore Victoria’s Secret’s $50m Fantasy Bra at 2026 fashion show, marking her runway debut
Kylie Jenner made her Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show debut on October 18, becoming the first non-Angel to model the brand’s iconic Fantasy Bra . Valued at $50 million, the lingerie piece returned to the runway after an eight-year absence.
The 29-year-old wore the elaborate design, which features a yellow diamond worth $22 million and 4,410 additional natural diamonds.
Her appearance placed her among previous Fantasy Bra models, including Gisele Bündchen, Heidi Klum, Tyra Banks, Adriana Lima, Alessandra Ambrosio and Candice Swanepoel.
Victoria’s Secret chief creative officer Adam Selman explained that Jenner was selected because of her influence across entertainment, fashion and popular culture.
“Kylie really extends beyond fashion, beyond culture, beyond TV, beyond one singular thing,” Selman told Vogue . “That’s the exact same thing that we do. Like, the show is so big, it’s true entertainment, and I think that she is a great catalyst for that.”
Selman also described Jenner as someone who had developed her own cultural following. He said the show’s central concept was “fandomonium” and explained that the brand wanted to pair the Fantasy Bra with an unexpected personality who had significant cultural influence.
“I think it’s an interesting pairing that we’re giving the fans: we’re giving them what they want with this amazing Fantasy Bra, and we’re going to put it on an unexpected talent who has a massive following and massive cultural impact,” he said.
The bra was created by 15 craftspeople from Jacob & Co. over more than 1,000 hours. Weighing just under four pounds, the design is made entirely of gold and diamonds, without fabric.
Designer Jacob Arabo explained that achieving a comfortable fit while preserving the design was a significant challenge.
Jenner was supported by boyfriend Timothée Chalamet and her mother, Kris Jenner, during her runway appearance. Sharing a close-up of herself wearing the Fantasy Bra on October 18, she captioned it, “BEST DAY EVER.”

title: Leverkusen fight back to beat Freiburg
description: Maza and Schick score in a 2 1 victory
content:
Ibrahim Maza and Patrik Schick combined to score two goals as Bayer Leverkusen came from behind to beat in-form Freiburg 2-1 in the German Bundesliga on Sunday.
After a shock defeat to promoted Elversberg in the season opener, Leverkusen have now picked up 13 of a possible 18 points and sit fourth, level with third-placed Freiburg on points but behind on goal difference.
Replaced by Bayern Munich atop the Bundesliga table after Vincent Kompany's men thumped RB Leipzig on Saturday, Freiburg host the Bavarian giants next weekend.
Schick's goal 14 minutes from time made him the first Leverkusen player to score in each of the first six matches in a Bundesliga season.
"It was a lot of fun, especially against such a strong opponent. Huge respect to Freiburg but we showed what we can do," Algeria attacker Maza told DAZN.
"Schicky and I are building some pretty good chemistry. The more time we spend playing together, the better it's getting. It's going pretty well right now."
Freiburg coach Julian Schuster said his side would learn from the defeat ahead of Bayern's visit next Sunday.
"It was completely unnecessary that we lost and dropped points here today," he said.
"But despite that there's plenty of positives to take out of it that will make us stronger and definitely help us," he added.
The Bundesliga's form team, Freiburg, took the pitch in Leverkusen under the watchful eyes of Germany coach Jurgen Klopp.
In October, Klopp called four Freiburg players up to the Germany squad for the first time and two of those combined for the opener with 14 minutes gone.
Right-back Philipp Treu laid on a counter-attacking opener for Derry Scherhant with a clever flick.
Five minutes later, Schick played a smart one-two with former Aston Villa winger Moussa Diaby before flicking to Maza who slammed home.
Schick blasted over the bar on the hour but did not need to wait long for his next opportunity.
With 15 minutes remaining, Maza dribbled in from the right and evaded several Freiburg defenders before playing an inch-perfect pass for Schick to guide a controlled strike home.
Rock bottom Borussia Moenchengladbach are still searching for a first point of the season after losing 2-1 at home against fellow strugglers Hoffenheim.
Hoffenheim's Bambase Conte opened the scoring with his second goal in two games since a surprise call-up to Klopp's Germany squad in October.
Wael Mohya pulled one back for the hosts just after the break but Alexander Prass put Hoffenheim back in front shortly afterwards as the visitors, who host Lyon in the Europa League on Thursday, won just their second game of the season.

title: Selena Gomez faces backlash over vaping nicotine after kidney transplant
description: Gomez revealed on Instagram that vaping had affected her voice and that quitting nicotine had been difficult
content:
Gomez revealed on Instagram that vaping had affected her voice and that quitting nicotine had been difficult
Selena Gomez has faced criticism on social media after opening up about her struggle to quit nicotine vaping, with renewed attention on her kidney transplant and former friend Francia Raisa, who donated the organ in 2017.
The singer and actress, 34, revealed in an Instagram Stories post on October 18 that vaping had affected her voice and that quitting nicotine had been difficult.
“I’m not gonna be able to change my voice,” Gomez said. “I vaped nicotine a lot.”
She added, “Nicotine is so hard to quit, and I think I just wanted to say, if you’re going through it or if you’re even trying to vape, it’s just not worth it.”
Gomez also acknowledged the impact on her voice, saying, “It’s so stupid. It changed my voice.”
Her admission prompted criticism online, with some users questioning her continued nicotine use following her kidney transplant.
One social media post read, “francia really gave this girl her kidney and she continued to smoke… oh wow”.
Another user wrote, “You actually gotta be a different level of asshole to have your friend give you their kidney and still continue to smoke whilst disrespecting them publicly, tragic 😭”.
However, the criticism comes amid a complicated history between Gomez and Raisa.
Raisa donated a kidney to Gomez in 2017 after the singer's lupus diagnosis led to serious complications.
Gomez said she hoped to maintain her efforts to quit, adding, “If you are going through something, you can get through it too.”

title: Lazio thrash Juventus to join Inter on top
description: The visitors reach 19 points in seven games  surpassing their previous best start in 1999 2000
content:
The visitors reach 19 points in seven games, surpassing their previous best start in 1999-2000
Lazio scored a statement win on Sunday, brushing Juventus aside 3-0 in Turin to move level on points with Inter Milan at the top of Serie A.
Lazio trail the defending champions on goal difference, but 19 points is their highest total after seven league games, surpassing the 17 accumulated by Sven Goran Ericsson's team to open the 1999-2000 season.
That side went unbeaten for their first nine games and ended up winning their second, and most recent, Serie A title, by one point from Juventus.
On Sunday, Lazio took control with a Danish double.
Oliver Provstgaard, a 1.93m centre back, leapt high above the home defence after 37 minutes and guided a header inside the far post.
After 66 minutes, winger Gustav Isaksen, faced by a backpedalling fullback, drifted inside and placed a low shot inside the far post.
With three minutes left, substitute Fisayo Dele-Bashiru picked up the ball in his own half and cantered unhindered into the Juventus penalty area before sliding home his shot.
AC Milan and Como both won earlier on Sunday to end the week in the top five.
Milan held off visiting Atalanta 3-2 to end the weekend fourth, four points off the lead.
Young Slovenian Relja Obric made a nightmare debut for Atalanta.
The 20-year-old came on for injured Sead Kolasinac after 19 minutes but his first touch in Serie A five minutes later was a handball as he instinctively moved his arm into the path of a shot from Yunus Musah.
Milan's club-record signing Goncalo Ramos placed the penalty inside Marco Carnesecchi's left-hand post.
Then Obric allowed a shot from France midfielder Adrien Rabiot through his legs as Milan doubled their lead before half-time.
Danish central defender Thomas Kristensen gave away a carbon copy handball penalty after 65 minutes. Ramos went the other way but Carnesecchi saved it.
The reprieve was short-lived. Rabiot nodded on the corner and Mario Gila headed in from point-blank range at the far post.
Gianluca Gaetano and Nikola Krstovic pulled two back for the visitors in the second half but it was too little, too late for Atalanta as they succumbed to a fourth defeat of the campaign.
Milan survived a nervous final 10 minutes.
"Usually, we struggle at the start of the match and play better in the second half. It was the opposite today; we need to find the right balance, but these are three important points in our season," said Rabiot.
Booked shorty before he scored, an irrate Rabiot hadshouted at the referee, leading to France team-mate Mike Maignan trying to calm him down.
"He's a very important player for us," said coach Ruben Amorim. "At half-time, we told him to be careful and, as he's a very intelligent person, he handled the situation well."
Como won 3-1 at struggling Fiorentina to rise to fifth.
First-half goals by Mattia Liberali and Nico Paz put Como in charge, before Marin Pongracic halved the deficit shortly before the interval.
Anastasios Douvikas netted early in the second period to keep the hosts locked in the relegation zone on four points.
For Como, it was a first win in four matches, going back over the international break to mid-September.
"We played a very complete game," coach Cesc Fabregas said. "There are risks when you play the way we do. There's no such thing as perfect tactics."
Earlier, Lecce won 3-0 at Udinese, with Kialonda Gaspar, Konan N'Dri and Jamil Siebert all finding the net.

title: Mbappe hits two as Real Madrid rout Sevilla
description: Los Blancos climb to third in the standings but remain six points behind Barcelona
content:
Los Blancos climb to third in the standings but remain six points behind Barcelona
Kylian Mbappe scored twice including one brilliant individual goal as Real Madrid thrashed Sevilla 4-1 on Sunday to climb into third in La Liga.
Arda Guler, who was fortunate to avoid an early red card for an elbow, netted a spectacular opener before Mbappe's double and a rocket from Yan Diomande as Jose Mourinho side moved above Real Betis.
Mbappe's first was a sensational strike, involving a roulette on the edge of Sevilla's box, and his second a chipped Panenka penalty.
Champions Barca are six points ahead of Real Madrid before next weekend's Clasico at Camp Nou after thrashing Betis on Saturday, with Atletico Madrid second, sandwiched between Spain's giants.
"We played a great game... we are a team and we work to improve, we've only been together for a very short time," Mourinho told Real Madrid TV.
"It's hard to have the calm that other coaches enjoy at other clubs, given the scale of Real Madrid, but we're making the most of every minute we have."
Mourinho lined up with Diomande on the left in place of suspended Brazilian winger Vinicius Junior, and brought Guler in as part of the midfield pivot.
Vinicius's red card for hair-pulling last weekend provoked ire in the Spanish capital at officiating in Spain.
Madrid fans at their Santiago Bernabeu stadium chanted and held up banners against La Liga president Javier Tebas, after he said the club's strategy of trying to discredit referees was similar to the techniques of Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels.
Los Blancos and their new coach Mourinho have complained bitterly about Spanish refereeing in recent weeks, and more generally over the past two seasons, in which they have failed to win a major trophy.
On this occasion it was Sevilla who had more to complain about in terms of officiating as Madrid eased to victory.
A quiet start was disrupted when Madrid midfielder Guler appeared to elbow Sevilla's Peque, which went unpunished midway through the first half.
"There's a match that's 11 against 11 where they deserve to win, without any doubt, but we were denied the chance to play another match," said upset Sevilla coach Luis Garcia Plaza.
"We were denied the chance to play a match of 11 against 10. From there on I don't want to talk about the match anymore. We should have been playing 11 against 10 from the 25th minute."
The coach said "maybe" Guler was not dismissed so Madrid did "not arrive nine points behind" Barca at the Clasico next weekend.
Mourinho said he had seen no replays of the incident which proved Guler had elbowed Peque.
Sevilla had resisted the probing of Madrid's attacking stars early on, but were undone by a moment of magic from Guler himself after 30 minutes.
Jude Bellingham played the ball out to the flank where record signing Diomande received it and fed Guler on the edge of the box.
The Turkish playmaker lofted a superb strike across Sevilla goalkeeper Odysseas Vlachodimos and into the top corner.
Mbappe came close to adding a second with a lightning-quick burst down the pitch, but his low effort was saved.
The French superstar soon got his goal, one of the best of the season.
Bellingham backheeled the ball into Mbappe's path and the forward produced a dazzling roulette turn into the area, before showing more skill to rapidly sidestep the goalkeeper and roll home.
Sevilla complained that striker Robbie Ure was fouled in the build-up, to no avail.
Mbappe extended the lead from the penalty spot after he went down under a light touch from Andres Castrin in the area.
The forward, who hopes to be crowned the best player in the world at the Ballon d'Or ceremony later in October, dinked home his ninth league goal of the season.
Sevilla pulled one back with a neat strike from Manuel Bueno, but there was no fightback on the cards.
Ivorian winger Diomande thumped home from outside of the box for his second goal since joining this summer from RB Leipzig, Madrid's next opponents in the Champions League.
Earlier, Real Sociedad rose to fifth with a thumping 5-2 win at bottom side Malaga, Celta Vigo defeated Alaves 2-1 and Osasuna beat Racing Santander 2-0.

title: Boland strikes twice for Australia in South Africa Test
description: Australia reduce South Africa to 20 2 in a rain shortened opening day
content:
Australia reduce South Africa to 20-2 in a rain-shortened opening day
Australia's Scott Boland took two wickets in two balls on a severely rain-shortened first day of the second Test against South Africa at St George's Park on Sunday.
South Africa, sent in to bat, were 20 for two when play was called off after two short periods of play during which only 12.2 overs were bowled.
But it was enough for Boland to strike two crucial blows. He dismissed Aiden Markram and David Bedingham – South Africa's most successful batsmen in their defeat in the first Test in Durban.
Coming on as first change, Boland bowled Markram for 11 with his tenth delivery, a ball which nipped in off the pitch to crash into Markram's middle stump off an inside edge. Then he produced a ball which seamed away to have Bedingham caught behind first ball.
Boland was making only his 20th appearance in Australia's 50th Test since making a sensational debut when he took six for seven against England in Melbourne in December 2021.
He has had to wait his turn behind Australia's world-class pace trio of skipper Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood. He got his chance on Sunday, replacing off-spinner Nathan Lyon when Australia decided to field an all-seam attack on a green-tinged pitch in heavily overcast conditions.
"Scotty Boland has been incredible whenever he's played Test cricket," Cummins said after winning the toss. "When there's anything in the wicket, he gets a lot of seam movement, super accurate, and then even if it does flatten out, he brings control, experience. He's the whole package."
Rain started falling ten minutes after the toss and delayed the start by two hours. Markram hit two boundaries off Starc before play was halted with South Africa on 11 for no wicket after 5.3 overs.
Boland was brought into the attack after the players returned in the afternoon and immediately struck a challenging length.
New cap Marques Ackerman was unbeaten on five and captain Temba Bavuma was on four when rain brought what proved to be the final stoppage of the day.
Boland for Lyon was the only change from the Australian team that won the first Test by 214 runs.
South Africa made three changes, with fast bowler Kagiso Rabada returning after recovering from a hamstring injury. He replaced left-arm spin bowler Keshav Maharaj.
Ackerman and fellow batsman Matthew Breetzke replaced Tristan Stubbs and Kyle Verreynne with Ryan Rickelton taking over from Verreynne as wicketkeeper.

title: Arsenal snatch late win to keep pressure on Manchester City
description: Manchester United drop more points in a draw at Leeds
content:
Manchester United drop more points in a draw at Leeds
Arsenal struck late to beat Nottingham Forest and keep the pressure on Premier League leaders Manchester City on Sunday, while struggling Manchester United dropped more points in a draw at Leeds.
The Gunners faced Forest a day after pacesetters City celebrated a seventh win in seven games at home to Ipswich -- shrugging off the fallout from the club's guilty verdict for serious financial irregularities.
Defending champions Arsenal huffed and puffed against Oliver Glasner's struggling side but finally secured the breakthrough when substitute Noni Madueke's effort found the net in the 80th minute after a deflection off Jair Cunha.
The goal was Arsenal's only shot on target in a disjointed performance that lacked attacking quality, but they are showing an impressive ability to grind out results when not at their best.
The 1-0 victory moved Mikel Arteta's side back up to second in the table, three points behind leaders City, while Forest, who failed to capitalise on a clutch of late chances, are now in the relegation zone.
"We had to earn it until the last second," Arteta told the BBC. "They are a well-coached team and hard to break down.
"We had to take risks, they are a dangerous team. We had to manage the emotional part really well. We stayed focused and the finishers made a huge impact."
Earlier, Manchester United travelled to the home of bitter rivals Leeds desperate to find a spark but were forced to settle for a 1-1 draw after Dominic Calvert-Lewin cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo's first-half opener.
United have just one win in seven league games this season and are winless in their past six matches in all competitions.
Manager Michael Carrick -- in his first full season in charge -- is scrambling for answers, with his team looking short of quality and confidence.
The sense of a growing crisis at Old Trafford was exacerbated by a midweek outburst from defender Lisandro Martinez, who took aim at the United hierarchy after a 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.
Carrick chose to focus on the positives after Sunday's game at Elland Road, insisting that the draw was a step in the right direction.
"If there's any weakness, it gets found out today," he told Sky Sports.
"I could feel before the game that the players were ready for it. It wasn't perfect, our confidence isn't sky-high, but the players were trying to do the right things.
"In moments we looked really good. Defended really well as a team."
Argentina centre-back Martinez gave an explosive interview in Spain on Tuesday during which he criticised the lack of investment in the summer transfer window.
Carrick insisted on Friday that United had "moved on" from the incident and Martinez was named in the starting line-up.
Mbeumo, playing as United's target man, wasted a couple of chances but broke the deadlock in the 35th minute when he guided a Youri Tielemans cross into the bottom corner for his fourth goal of the season.
Leeds put the visitors under sustained pressure after the break and were level in the 51st minute when England forward Calvert-Lewin controlled the ball on his chest and finished at full stretch after Tarik Muharemovic's header from a corner.
United, 13th in the table, have their fewest wins at this stage of a top-flight campaign since 1986/87.
Elsewhere on Sunday, Brighton hammered Crystal Palace 5-0, including a sensational Diego Gomez effort from the halfway line.
Only three sides in Premier League history have scored more goals in their first seven games of a season than Brighton's haul of 23.
Bournemouth beat 10-man Sunderland 2-0 with goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson for their first league win of the season.

description: Kendall Jenner skipped 2026 Victoria   s Secret Fashion Show after busy fashion month and series of recent appearances
content:
Kendall Jenner skipped 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show after busy fashion month and series of recent appearances
Kendall Jenner was absent from the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show, despite her sister Kylie Jenner making her debut at the event. The supermodel was not included in the lingerie brand’s confirmed model line-up and did not appear on the runway.
Jenner has walked in the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show three times, making her debut in 2015 alongside Gigi Hadid.
She returned in 2016, when she earned her wings, and appeared again in 2018. However, she did not return when the show resumed in 2024 after a multi-year hiatus.

title: Army major martyred in IED attack  four terrorists killed in Balochistan IBO  ISPR
description: The 34 year old major was leading a security force component during cleareance operation when it was targeted by IED
content:
PM Shehbaz expresses grief over martyrdom, pays tribute to security forces
A Pakistan Army major was martyred in an improvised explosive device (IED) blast during a security operation in Balochistan's Gwadar district, while security forces killed four terrorists in a separate operation in Kalat district, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement on Monday.
According to the military’s media wing, 34-year-old Major Wajahat Waheed, a resident of Lahore, was leading a security force component during clearance operations in the Shadi Kaur area of Pasni tehsil in Gwadar district when it was targeted by an IED.
“Major Wajahat Waheed, a son of the soil, made the ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty and embraced shahadat,” the ISPR said.
The military’s media wing added that intelligence agencies had reported the presence of multiple hideouts of Fitna Al Hindustan in the Shadi Kaur area of Gwadar and Jattakabad in Kalat district, posing a threat to the local population. “To safeguard the local populace and clear the area of terrorists, security forces are conducting operations in these areas,” the statement said.
In a separate operation conducted a day earlier in Jattakabad, Kalat district, security forces engaged the terrorists’ location. “During the operation, own troops effectively engaged the terrorists' location and, after an intense exchange of fire, four terrorists were sent to hell,” the ISPR said, adding that a large cache of arms and ammunition were also recovered.
The statement added that clearance operations were continuing in the Shadi Kaur area to eliminate any remaining terrorists. “Sanitisation operations will continue to eliminate any other terrorists found in the area,” the ISPR said.
Read: Security forces kill eight terrorists in three operations across Balochistan: ISPR
“The relentless counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of Azm-e-Istehkam , as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, will continue at full pace,” the statement said. “Security forces and law enforcement agencies remain committed to eliminating the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” it added.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paid tribute to security forces for killing the four terrorists and expressed grief over the death of Major Wajahat Waheed.
The Prime Minister’s Office, in a statement, said PM Shehbaz had paid tribute to the 34-year-old officer who embraced martyrdom in the IED blast in Pasni. “Major Wajahat Waheed sacrificed his life for the protection of our beloved homeland; the nation is proud of its brave son,” the prime minister said.
He also extended heartfelt condolences to the family of the martyred officer and prayed for the elevation of his ranks.
PM Shehbaz reiterated his resolve to continue the fight against foreign-sponsored terrorism until its complete elimination under the vision of Azm-e-Istehkam approved by the Federal Apex Committee.
President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to security forces for killing four terrorists and expressed grief over the martyrdom of Major Wajahat Waheed.
He paid tribute to the major for his sacrifice in defending the country and combating terrorism, and extended his heartfelt condolences and sympathies to the bereaved family.
Zardari also commended security forces for their continued sacrifices and professional services to ensure peace and stability in the country and protect the public. “Every conspiracy by terrorists’ foreign sponsors and their local facilitators will be thwarted,” the president.

title: Information ministry rejects claim army officer died at Rawalpindi match
description: Says man was a PCB employee who died of electrocution  was not present at the stadium  no involvement in the match
content:
Fact-checker says man was PCB employee who died of electrocution, was not involved in match
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting’s fact-checker early Monday morning rejected claims that a Pakistan Army officer had died of a heart attack during the Pakistan-Sri Lanka cricket match at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium, saying the deceased was a Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) employee who died of electrocution.
In a post on X, the ministry said the individual was not present at the stadium during the match and had no involvement in the event.
The claim was shared by journalist Naveed Satti, who said 50-year-old Muhammad Farooq, son of Muhammad Azam, had fallen unconscious during the match and was taken to Benazir Bhutto Hospital through Rescue 1122, where he could not survive. The post further claimed that Farooq was affiliated with the Pakistan Army and was posted at a security agency in Islamabad.
However, according to the FIR attached to the ministry’s fact-check, Farooq, aged around 60, died after suffering an electric shock while checking an electrical plug at his home. The report stated that his body was at Benazir Bhutto Hospital in Rawalpindi.
“He suffered electric shock following which his family contacted Rescue 1122 and he was shifted to local hospital,” the ministry said in its post, adding that he was not affiliated with the Pakistan Army but was actually a PCB employee.
Read: Info ministry rejects social media claims of unrest in K-P as misleading
The fact-checker added that hospital records had identified the cause of death as “electrocution” and that further inquiry would proceed in accordance with the relevant procedure.
“Linking this medical emergency to the cricket match is misleading,” the ministry said, adding that the individual’s employment with the PCB did not establish any connection between the incident and the ongoing match.
The ministry urged the public to verify facts before sharing misleading claims.
The match in question was the opening fixture of a seven-match ODI tri-series featuring Pakistan, Sri Lanka and England, which began at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on October 18. Pakistan defeated Sri Lanka by 37 runs, with Salman Ali Agha scoring 107 off 90 balls as the hosts posted 305 before bowling out the visitors for 268. The series is being held in Rawalpindi and Lahore as part of preparations for the 2027 ICC Men’s Cricket World Cup

title: Board under scrutiny over marking disparity
description: Board under scrutiny over marking disparity
content:
Court-ordered recheck exposes flaws in board's marking system
A paper that was once worth zero marks is now worth 72 - and the student's answer sheet is at the centre of a controversy that has put the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE) Peshawar's examination system under scrutiny.
The "one paper, two results" controversy involves ninth-grade student Abdul Aziz, whose father, Arif Khan, an advocate, approached the Peshawar High Court through Advocate Amin Yousafzai after his son was awarded zero marks in Biology.
According to Amin Yousafzai, the student and his family initially approached the board for re-totalling, but officials maintained that the original result was correct.
"The student was given zero marks in Biology, and when the family approached the board for re-totalling, they were told that the result was correct and there would be no improvement in the marks," Amin Yousafzai said.
He said the family then approached the high court, which directed the board to produce and examine the answer sheet. Following the examination, the board awarded the student 72 marks instead of zero.
"The most alarming aspect of this case is that a student who was initially declared to have obtained zero marks was awarded 72 marks after his paper was examined on the court's direction," he said.
According to him, the discrepancy raises questions about the credibility of the examination system and how students' complaints are handled.
He questioned how many students might have faced similar problems but lacked the resources or awareness to approach the courts.
The lawyer said the family was reluctant to publicise the case due to fears that it could affect the student's academic future or lead to unfair treatment in his tenth-grade examination.
The case has also raised concern among parents who believe examination boards should provide an effective mechanism for resolving complaints without forcing students to seek judicial intervention.
Bakshish Khan, a parent, said his daughter had secured 450 marks out of 550 and had consistently achieved top positions in her class, but her recent marks were unexpectedly low. He said parents remained concerned about the reliability of examination and marking systems.
"Parents trust the examination system because the marks awarded by the board can determine a student's future academic opportunities," he said, adding that incidents such as the Abdul Aziz case could weaken that trust.
Educationist and lecturer Shah Nawaz Khan also criticised the Peshawar Board, saying examination boards carried a major responsibility because their decisions directly affected students' academic futures.
He believed there should be strong internal checks to ensure mistakes in marking, tabulation and compilation were detected before results were announced.
"If a student is initially given zero marks and the same answer sheet later results in 72 marks, this is not a minor discrepancy," Shah Nawaz Khan said, calling for a serious review of the board's examination and rechecking procedures.
Amin Yousafzai reiterated that the issue was not merely about the 72 marks awarded to one student but about the wider credibility of the examination system.
He said examination boards received billions of rupees every year from students and their families and were required to provide transparent and accountable services.
The lawyer said the case should serve as an opportunity for authorities to examine whether the existing rechecking and re-totalling system was sufficient to protect students from marking errors.
The Peshawar Board Chairman was repeatedly contacted for his version on the matter, but he did not respond to calls.
The matter remains pending before the Peshawar High Court and was recently adjourned until September 29, when further proceedings are expected.

title: Malakand Division tax relief hopes fade
description: Malakand Division tax relief hopes fade
content:
Federal govt rejects further exemptions amid mounting local opposition
Disputes over the implementation of federal taxes in Malakand Division, effective from July 1, remain unresolved between the federal government and local traders and the public. A senior official has claimed that the federal government has finalised its position and is not inclined to grant any further tax exemptions or relaxations for the division.
According to the official, the decision on the matter has been taken and there is little likelihood of additional exemptions or leniency regarding the enforcement of taxes in Malakand Division. Meanwhile, the continued collection of taxes, deductions from bank savings accounts, and indications of forthcoming action against non-custom-paid vehicles have triggered a fresh wave of concern in the region.
Traders, political and social leaders, and people from various walks of life have been protesting the imposition of taxes. Plans for shutter-down strikes, protest rallies and road blockades were announced, but these were postponed indefinitely after the imposition of emergency and Governor's rule in the province. Despite the suspension of formal protest schedules, local unease persists, and stakeholders continue to demand that the government review its decision.
The senior official further stated that action against non-custom-paid vehicles could be taken in the next phase on the basis of different categories. If such measures are implemented, vehicle owners, those associated with the transport sector and related business circles could face new difficulties. Independent confirmation of the details and formal schedule of any proposed action against non-custom-paid vehicles has not yet emerged.
Following the imposition of taxes, significant amounts have been collected under various heads. Media reports have mentioned the recovery of billions of rupees, while information from the banking sector indicates that tax is also being deducted from profits earned on savings accounts after the completion of a three-month period. Bank officials say clear instructions exist in this regard, and deductions of up to 20 per cent have already been made on profits in some accounts. Official confirmation of overall tax collections and deductions under different heads is still required.
Traders and public representatives argue that the economic conditions of Malakand Division differ from those of other developed commercial centres in the country. They maintain that the tax issue should be resolved in light of local circumstances and historical background. The region's economy, they say, is already under severe pressure due to prolonged insecurity, terrorism, military operations, natural disasters including earthquakes and floods, and a decline in business activity. Additional tax burdens, in their view, could further damage local businesses, employment and the purchasing power of ordinary citizens.
Local traders and other stakeholders note that commercial activity remains limited, business opportunities are scarce, and a large section of the population already faces economic hardship. They contend that the need of the hour is special measures to promote trade, encourage investment and generate employment rather than fiscal decisions that place further strain on an already fragile economy.

title: Court to rule on first climate lawsuit against Italian state
description: Court to rule on first climate lawsuit against Italian state
content:
An Italian court is to rule on the country's first climate lawsuit against the state, with claimants hoping Rome will be ordered to slash greenhouse-gas emissions sharply.
The case, known as "Giudizio Universale" (Last Judgment), was launched in June 2021 by environmental group A Sud and more than 200 other associations and individuals.
They accuse the state of violating fundamental rights by failing to take sufficient action to meet the goals laid out in the landmark 2015 Paris agreement to reduce carbon emissions.
"I joined the trial because I have a mission to inform society about the risks we face due to climate change," climatologist Luca Mercalli, one of the claimants, told AFP.
A win would put pressure on "institutions to be much faster and more concrete in addressing the climate crisis", said Mercalli, who moved to the mountains in northern Italy to escape increasingly frequent heatwaves on the plains.
Scientists have long warned that humanity's burning of fossil fuels is warming the world with disastrous consequences for the environment.
In what promised to be a historic case for Italy -- a Mediterranean country exposed to multiple climate calamities -- the claimants initially asked a court to find the state responsible for contributing to the crisis, and to order it to cut emissions by 92 percent compared with 1990 levels by 2030.

title: CM eyes Punjab as regional livestock hub
description: CM eyes Punjab as regional livestock hub
content:
Punjab's livestock sector has recorded a 43 per cent increase in exports, with 400,000 animals prepared for export in a year and farmers expected to earn Rs11 billion.
Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif said the government aimed to connect Punjab's livestock farmers with national exporters and international websites to expand their access to markets and establish the province as a regional livestock hub.
Under a Livestock Card scheme, farmers are receiving Rs27,000 per animal to meet feed and fodder expenses.
A total of 129,581 animals reared under the scheme have been exported.
According to a statement, the government plans to establish five meat-processing plants and as many slaughterhouses, alongside packing facilities and commercial and corporate feedlots. It will provide Rs19 billion in financing subsidies for integrated livestock value-chain investments, while private investment of Rs65b is expected in the meat value chain.
Punjab will also establish its first FMD vaccine production unit under a public-private partnership, with private investment of Rs28 billion.
The district-wise export figures include 20,000 animals from Lahore, 24,297 from Bahawalpur, 12,529 from Faisalabad, 21,000 from Gujranwala and Gujrat, 27,000 from Multan, 22,000 from Sargodha and 2,661 from Sahiwal.
Under the Livestock Connect system, the government has established direct links with 1,725 fattening farms, 20 export slaughterhouses, 88 meat exporters and 34 traders.
The number of rural women farmers registered under the Livestock Card scheme has also increased.

title: Businessman shot dead while chasing carjackers | The Express Tribune
description: Businessman shot dead while chasing carjackers
content:
Robbers open fire after victim spots his stolen vehicle on Jaranwala Road
A businessman was shot dead while pursuing men who had taken away his vehicle from outside Chenab Club before abandoning it near Chak 215-RB on Jaranwala Road, police said.
Police from Civil Lines and Sadar police stations reached the scene after receiving reports of the carjacking and murder. They took custody of the body and the vehicle and launched an investigation.
City Police Officer Tanveer Hussain took notice of the incident and sought a detailed report from Iqbal Town SP Saeed Ahmed.
According to the FIR registered at Civil Lines police station on the complaint of Muhammad Hassan Ashraf, his brother, businessman Muhammad Rehan Ashraf, had gone for a meal with companions Muhammad Ikram and Muhammad Amjad in an Islamabad-registered vehicle.
They handed the vehicle over to a valet parking attendant before entering the club.
Shortly afterwards, they began receiving notifications from the vehicle's tracking system indicating that it was being switched on and off.
When they went to the parking area to check, the vehicle and the attendant were missing.
Hassan said they immediately contacted the tracking company and informed Rescue 15. They then pursued the vehicle in a pickup, using its tracking location.
The vehicle was traced near a bank on Jaranwala Road, close to the power station in Chak 215-RB, where traffic had slowed because of the construction of an overhead bridge near a super store.

The health implications are especially important for children, older people and residents with respiratory or cardiovascular conditions.

WCLA seeks billions from Punjab govt to complete Phase-I projects by December
The plan to restore Lahore's Walled City to its original character is facing delays due to a shortage of funds, with the Walled City of Lahore Authority (WCLA) seeking billions of rupees from the Punjab government to complete ongoing Phase-I projects by December 2026.
The projects include an underground parking plaza at Neela Gumbad, estimated to cost Rs2.4 billion, for which an additional Rs500 million is required.

Around Rs500 million is required to improve the appearance of historic city gates and move electricity wires underground.
The sites include Yakki Gate, Taksali Gate, Mochi Gate and the Spice Market.
A further Rs13 billion is required for underground parking plazas and shops at Mochi Gate, Sheranwala Gate and Taksali Gate.
Work on these projects has slowed, while delays could increase their overall cost.
The WCLA has requested the provincial government to release the required funds to meet the December 2026 completion deadline.
Azeem Dad, director of the WCLA's department responsible for the conservation of historic buildings, said development work was progressing under the vision of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif and the directions of the authority's director general.

title: Zoo s adoption scheme raises questions
description: Zoo s adoption scheme raises questions
content:
Citizens, schools and companies sponsor wild animals
Lahore Zoo's new adoption scheme puts a price on wildlife sponsorship, but will it do enough to improve life behind the enclosures?
A private school recently adopted a male hippopotamus, named "Gabo" by its students. Under the new scheme, adopters can visit their animals, learn about their health and diet, and offer care suggestions, but cannot take them home. They receive certificates and educational material, while their names may appear on enclosures.
Deputy Director Shahzaib Khurshid said individuals and institutions could adopt animals for one, three or six months, or a year. Veterinary Officer Dr Muhammad Azhar said zoo staff remained responsible for their feeding, health and care.
According to the zoo administration, annual adoption fees vary by species. Sponsoring lions, tigers and other big cats costs Rs1 million, while the annual fee for a hippopotamus is Rs600,000. A giraffe costs Rs300,000, a fawn Rs100,000 and other antelopes Rs150,000. Interested individuals can contact the administration for details of fees for shorter periods.
The programme has attracted celebrities and educational institutions in the past. Actress Reema adopted two fawns after becoming a goodwill ambassador, while Babra Sharif sponsored a lion cub named "Shainko". Actress Meera, the University of the Punjab, Government College University and several private educational institutions have also participated in animal adoption initiatives.
Citizen Abdul Rehman said the programme offered an opportunity for people interested in wildlife but lacking space to keep animals at home. Through adoption at the zoo, he said, enthusiasts could support animals while allowing them to remain in an appropriate environment.
Student Nida Fatima suggested extending the initiative to birds, saying it would encourage students and citizens to contribute to the conservation of a wider range of species.
Similar programmes operate at zoos across the region. Mysore Zoo in India has reportedly generated crores of rupees in a single year through its adoption scheme. Its annual fees include approximately Rs300,000 for an elephant, Rs100,000 for a lion or tiger and Rs50,000 for a hippopotamus, while deer can be adopted at lower rates. Zoos in Delhi and Hyderabad also allow families, schools and companies to sponsor animals such as lions, tigers and elephants.
The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) distinguishes domestic animal sponsorship from commercial wildlife trade. The World Association of Zoos and Aquariums (WAZA) stresses that animal welfare includes suitable habitats, good health, social needs and natural behaviours, with adoption funds supporting these needs.
Animal rights activist and lawyer Altamash Saeed said keeping wild animals at home was wrong and illegal. He supported zoo-based adoption but called for better facilities, larger enclosures and stricter monitoring to ensure animal welfare. Animals, he said, should not be treated merely as a source of entertainment, and their welfare must remain a priority.
Wildlife laws restrict keeping large wild animals in urban homes. Experts say the adoption programme can support conservation, provided funds are used transparently to improve animal care and living conditions.
Additional Chief Wildlife Ranger for Central Punjab Mudassar Hassan said the initiative was not limited to Lahore Zoo. Citizens and institutions could adopt animals at any zoo or safari park in Punjab.
He warned that keeping large cats, including lions and tigers, in homes posed serious risks to public safety and animal welfare. Such animals require specialised enclosures, appropriate diets, veterinary facilities and trained handlers. Adoption at recognised facilities, he said, provides a safer alternative for people wishing to support wildlife.

title: Foreign experts to find K2 Airways  black box
description: Foreign experts to find K2 Airways  black box
content:
Nearly four months after a K2 Airways aircraft plunged into the sea off Ormara, the search for its black box, wreckage and cockpit crew is entering a new phase, with Pakistan stepping up efforts to enlist international expertise for a deep-sea recovery operation.
With the aircraft believed to lie around 3,000 metres below the surface, the search is expected to draw on advanced sonar systems, autonomous underwater vehicles and remotely operated robots equipped with high-definition cameras and specialised recovery tools.
The government has intensified contacts with foreign experts and several international companies to determine how best to locate and recover the aircraft's remains from the seabed, according to sources. The black box and wreckage are considered crucial to establishing what happened in the aircraft's final moments.
The aircraft belonging to the privately owned domestic cargo operator crashed into the sea on July 7 this year after encountering adverse conditions near Ormara. Sources said the transmitter beacon fitted to its black box stopped emitting signals around a month after the accident, making the search more difficult.
The Pakistan Navy had earlier used specialised equipment and side-scan sonar to identify a possible location of the black box on the seabed. Acoustic signals were used to scan the area at a depth of around 3,000 metres, but further progress now depends on more sophisticated underwater technology and specialised deep-sea salvage expertise.
As part of the proposed operation, a detailed three-dimensional map of the seabed will be prepared using a multibeam echo sounder. The technology can map underwater terrain, measure depths and identify potential obstructions, helping search teams narrow down the area where the aircraft's wreckage may be located.
Autonomous underwater vehicles may also be deployed to survey the seabed using sonar, cameras and other sensors. The data and images collected by these unmanned systems can help identify suspicious objects and pinpoint areas requiring closer inspection.
Remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), controlled from a support vessel, could play an equally important role. Equipped with high-definition cameras, powerful lights and robotic arms, the machines can examine wreckage at close range and, where feasible, retrieve smaller objects or position specialised equipment around the debris.

title: Cabinet to decide fate of Mir Raza commission report on Tuesday
description: Cabinet to decide fate of Mir Raza commission report on Tuesday
content:
CM Office confirms receipt of sealed report containing Judicial Commission's findings
Nearly three months after the death of young Karachi entrepreneur Mir Raza Ali was initially treated as a possible suicide, a sealed Judicial Commission report is set to reach the Sindh cabinet, which will decide on Tuesday what action should follow its findings.
The report, submitted to Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, comes after an investigation marred by conflicting post-mortem findings, questions over the handling of evidence and allegations of serious lapses in the police probe. The commission's findings remain confidential ahead of the cabinet meeting.
The provincial cabinet will open the sealed report and consider its implementation at a meeting at the Chief Minister's House on Tuesday, according to a spokesperson for the chief minister.
Mir Raza, a 25-year-old businessman and owner of the Wafflix dessert brand, went missing on July 28 after leaving his home in PECHS. His body, bearing a gunshot wound, was found in bushes near Shahi Qila Ground in Gulistan-e-Jauhar the following day.
Police initially pursued the possibility of suicide, relying on the first post-mortem report and citing reported business losses and borrowed money. His family, however, maintained that he had been kidnapped, tortured and murdered, rejecting the suicide theory and demanding a thorough investigation.
The case took a significant turn after the family obtained a court order for the exhumation of Mir Raza's body and a second post-mortem examination. The resulting report concluded that the findings were inconsistent with suicide. The medical board found that the fatal bullet had entered through his back and exited through his chest, while also documenting injuries to other parts of his body.
Following the findings, murder charges were added to the first information report, and the police investigation team was reconstituted. The family continued to raise questions about the investigation and sought a more credible mechanism to establish the facts.
The investigation subsequently became the subject of a wider controversy over alleged mishandling of evidence and possible negligence by police officials. Among the issues examined were the burning of the crime scene, the recording of witness statements and the handling of Mir Raza's mobile phone.
