title: Earthquake of magnitude 7 strikes China's Tibet
description: The epicentre was in ⁠a sparsely populated, high-altitude county in Nagqu, northern Tibet
content: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck China's southwestern region of Tibet at around 10:33pm (1433 GMT) on Thursday, ​the China Earthquake Networks Centre (CENC) said. Local authorities have ‌found at least two people injured in a village near the epicentre, with some houses in villages closest to the epicentre showing cracks, ​the state broadcaster said. The quake is the strongest ​to hit China since January 2024. The epicentre was in ⁠a sparsely populated, high-altitude county in Nagqu, northern Tibet, at ​a depth of 10km (6.2 miles). The average elevation within ​5km of the epicentre is about 4,864 metres (15,960 feet), CENC data showed. Read: Hundreds missing after devastating flood hits Nepal-Tibet border, 95 bodies recovered Videos released by local officially run media showed people leaving their homes ​and seeking shelter outside or in their cars parked on ​the street. One resident reported being awakened by the strong quake and ‌heard ⁠the house squeaking in the tremor. The quake was clearly felt in the local area, CENC said. The epicentre was around 400 km from the Tibetan capital of Lhasa. Local fire and rescue ​teams have mobilised ​and are ⁠heading to the affected region, state media said. A string of smaller tremors of around magnitude ​3 and 4 have been recorded in surrounding ​regions following ⁠the magnitude 7 quake, CENC data showed. In 2010, a magnitude 7.1 tremor struck Yushu in neighbouring Qinghai province, killing at least ⁠2,698 ​people and leaving nearly 300 people ​missing.

title: President Zardari to visit Germany from Oct 22-24: FO
description: Will meet German president, senior leadership and businessmen to discuss bilateral relations, economic cooperation
content: President Asif Ali Zardari is scheduled to visit Germany from October 22 to 24 to discuss bilateral relations, economic ties, and trade cooperation, the Foreign Office said on Thursday. “The President will hold meetings with the President of the Federal Republic of Germany as well as senior leadership and business leaders to discuss Pakistan-Germany bilateral relations, with a particular focus on economic and trade cooperation,” the FO said in a post on X. The FO said that the visit is part of high-level exchanges between Pakistan and Germany and holds "special significance" in the context of the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries. “It reflects the deep commitment of both countries to further strengthening the Partnership,” it added. Pakistan and Germany established diplomatic relations in 1951 and are marking the 75th anniversary of their ties this year. Germany is Pakistan’s largest trading partner in the European Union, with both countries seeking to expand trade, investment and business cooperation. Read: Maldives president arrives for three-day visit In August, German Consul General Thomas E Schultze highlighted the longstanding relationship and said economic cooperation between the two countries dated back to 1922, when Siemens opened its first office in Lahore. Economic cooperation has remained a key focus of bilateral engagement. In October, the German ambassador called for greater trade diversification, investment and business-to-business cooperation, saying German companies were seeking to diversify their supply chains and establish new partnerships. Pakistani textile, engineering, pharmaceutical and information technology businesses have been identified as potential areas for closer collaboration. The two countries have also continued development cooperation. In May, Pakistan and Germany signed a €40.5 million technical cooperation agreement covering nine new development projects, with support from Germany’s development bank, KfW. The projects formed part of wider cooperation on climate change, the energy transition and social vulnerability.

title: Pakistan, EU agree to boost counterterrorism cooperation, tackle online radicalisation: FO
description: The two sides also discuss terrorist financing, violent extremism and security threats linked to Afghanistan
content: Pakistan and the European Union (EU) agreed on Thursday to strengthen counterterrorism cooperation, including efforts to combat violent extremism, terrorist financing and the misuse of cyberspace, during the 10th round of their bilateral counterterrorism dialogue in Islamabad, the Foreign Office (FO) said. According to a statement on X, Director General Counterterrorism Dr Fareha Bugti led the Pakistani delegation, while Anna Strzaska, the European External Action Service’s Special Envoy for Counterterrorism, headed the EU delegation. The two sides reviewed recent regional and global developments affecting the terrorism threat landscape and strongly condemned terrorism in all its forms, reaffirming their commitment to combating the threat. The EU delegation condemned recent terrorist attacks in Pakistan, expressed solidarity with the victims and acknowledged Islamabad’s efforts to counter terrorism, the Foreign Office said. Both sides also expressed concern over the security implications of the situation in Afghanistan and recognised each other’s role in the global fight against terrorism. Read More: PM Shehbaz emphasises need for 'safe, orderly migration' in meeting with EU commissioner During the dialogue, Pakistan and the EU agreed to enhance cooperation at multilateral forums, including the United Nations, to develop a coordinated approach to counterterrorism. They underscored the importance of effective multilateralism in building lasting international consensus on combating terrorism. The discussions also focused on emerging terrorist threats, particularly the exploitation of cyberspace, information and energy resources by terrorist groups to advance their objectives. Both delegations exchanged best practices on preventing violent extremism, countering terrorist financing and addressing radicalisation, particularly the growing use of digital platforms by terrorist organisations. The two sides identified priority areas for future cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining regular, institutionalised engagement on counterterrorism. The next round of the bilateral counterterrorism dialogue will be held in Brussels next year on a mutually convenient date, the Foreign Office said.

title: Arooj Aftab calls for fair pay when artists' music is used to train AI
description: Grammy winner backs calls for clear labelling of AI-generated music and compensation when AI systems use artists' work
content: Grammy-winning Pakistani singer Arooj Aftab has called for musicians to receive fair compensation whenever their recordings are used to train artificial intelligence (AI) models or generate new music, arguing that artists should be paid for the use of their work. In two Instagram stories, Aftab shared campaign messages from United Musicians and Allied Workers (UMAW), a trade union representing music industry professionals, highlighting the need for transparency, proper labelling and fair remuneration as AI-generated music becomes increasingly prevalent. The first post called for AI-generated recordings to be clearly labelled across the music industry, including by software developers, record labels, studios, distributors and retailers. The campaign argues that listeners should be able to distinguish music created using AI from recordings made by human artists. Screengrab: aroojaftab/Instagram Sharing the message, Aftab highlighted how musicians’ work could be used to develop AI systems, writing: “Even if you don’t use AI to make music - it is going to use your music to make AI music!! So let’s get the rules right and get on with it.” The singer also endorsed calls for artists to be paid when their recordings are used to train AI systems and when the resulting technology is used to generate new music. In her second story, Aftab argued that compensation should cover both the initial use of music to train AI models and the subsequent use of what those systems have learnt. “The artist should be paid bec AI has already used my music to train itself, aka usage,” she wrote, adding that artists should also be paid whenever AI draws on that learning to produce new music, which she described as “derivative work”. Screengrab: aroojaftab/Instagram The accompanying UMAW campaign called on the US Congress to pass the Living Wage for Musicians Act, which seeks to address musicians’ earnings from streaming and support direct payments to human recording artists for the use of their music. Aftab’s intervention comes amid growing opposition from musicians to the unauthorised use of copyrighted creative work in AI development. In 2024, more than 13,000 artists signed a statement condemning the unlicensed use of human-made music to develop AI systems. The signatories included ABBA’s Björn Ulvaeus and Radiohead’s Thom Yorke. In February 2025, more than 1,000 musicians, including Kate Bush, released a silent album to protest proposed changes to UK copyright rules that could allow AI developers to use copyrighted material, including music and books, to train their systems under certain conditions. Streaming platforms have also begun responding to concerns about AI-generated content. Spotify has introduced measures intended to help listeners identify verified human creators and distinguish them from AI music creators, while addressing spam and low-quality tracks. The debate centres on how copyright, attribution and compensation should apply when AI systems are trained on existing creative works and subsequently generate new material. For musicians such as Aftab, the central question is whether artists whose work helps power these systems should have a say in how it is used and receive compensation for the value it creates.

title: Atif Aslam unveils first look at 'Safar Main Hu' music video
description: Singer announces video from his first album in 18 years is set to release soon
content: Singer Atif Aslam has given fans an exclusive first look at the official music video for Safar Main Hu, a track from his latest album, Subah Aye Na, sharing a mountain-themed poster on Instagram alongside poetic Urdu verses about love and longing. In an Instagram post, Aslam confirmed that the full music video would be released soon, although he did not announce a specific date. The caption opened with the lines: “سفر میں ہوں، تو عشق ہے جانے بھی دوں کیسے؟ تو اوس ہے، میں ہوں صبح، تیرے بن جیوں کیسے؟” Translated into English, the couplet reads: “I am on a journey, and you are love itself — how could I ever let you go? You are the dew, and I am the morning — how could I live without you?” The verses evoke a journey shaped by love, comparing the beloved to morning dew and the singer to the dawn. The imagery also echoes the title of the album, Subah Aye Na. Announcing the first look, Aslam wrote: “The long wait is over. Here is the exclusive first look at the official music video for #SafarMainHu from the album Subah Aye Na.” He added that every frame was a painting and every melody a piece of his heart, inviting listeners to leave a wave or heart emoji in the comments if they were ready to embark on the musical journey with him. “Full music video dropping very soon. Turn your notifications ON,” he wrote. The mountain-themed poster offers a glimpse into the visual world of the song, with the natural landscape complementing the romantic tone of the accompanying verses. Aslam has yet to share further details about the video's storyline or whether the full release will build on the imagery featured in the poster. Safar Main Hu is part of Subah Aye Na, Aslam's fourth studio album and his first full-length release in 18 years. The eight-track record marked his return to an album format that helped establish him as one of Pakistan's most recognisable pop-rock artists. The album features Subah Aye Na, Safar Main Hu, Ishq, Let's Have Some Fun, Sunn Sajna, Hun Ishq Main, Chaar Yaar and Sachey Wadey. Aslam's last full-length studio album, Meri Kahani, was released in 2008. His earlier albums, including Jal Pari and Doorie, helped build a catalogue that has remained popular with listeners across South Asia. Ahead of the release of Subah Aye Na, Aslam spoke about reconnecting with his artistic roots after years of touring and working on commercial projects. He described the process as a return to basics, explaining that he wanted to make music that reflected his own experiences and creative instincts. The singer has also expressed a desire to release albums more regularly, suggesting that the project could mark the beginning of a new phase in his musical career. With the first look at Safar Main Hu now revealed, fans are waiting to see how Aslam translates the song's romantic lyrics and scenic imagery into a full music video. For now, he has offered a poster, a couplet and a promise that the wait will soon be over.

title: Asma Abbas criticises obsession with branded fashion, says similar finds cost Rs500 at local bazaars
description: Actor urges shoppers to look beyond labels, sharing why she values affordable finds and shops at Sunday Bazaar
content: Veteran actor Asma Abbas has criticised the growing obsession with branded clothing and accessories, stressing that people should prioritise affordability and personal preference over labels. In a recent interview, she observed that people increasingly identify their belongings by brand names rather than simply referring to the items themselves, turning labels into a way of displaying status while overlooking more affordable alternatives. “I have seen that people in our generation don’t say, ‘This is my bag.’ They say, ‘This is from MK. It is from here or there.’ It is all about the brand,” she remarked. Abbas further pointed out that people had become overly conscious of brand names, particularly when it came to fashion and accessories. “People have started thinking about these things way too much. Showing off that something is from Nike or elsewhere,” she said. She suggested that while people should be mindful of where products come from, a brand name should not be the sole factor influencing their purchasing decisions. Sharing a glimpse into her own shopping habits, Abbas revealed that she still shopped at Sunday Bazaar, highlighting her appreciation for affordable finds and local markets. The actor also spoke about the values she had tried to instil in her children, explaining that she wanted them to understand that wearing clothes from less expensive or lesser-known sources was perfectly acceptable. “My kids do not have this scary quality yet. I have raised them to know that wearing clothes from anywhere is okay,” she shared. Acknowledging that people sometimes judge those who prefer shopping at smaller stores or local markets, Abbas said such opinions did not influence her choices. “People talk a lot on these kind of people but I do not care because if you like something from somewhere small, you should just buy it,” she stated. “When I went to America, I got a very beautiful necklace from the brand Forever 21. When I came here, I found a very similar one in the bazaar here,” she recalled. Highlighting the price difference between branded products and locally available alternatives, she added, “You can find the same thing for Rs500 here.” Her remarks challenged the notion that fashion must come with a hefty price tag, encouraging shoppers to look beyond labels, explore local markets and make purchases according to their preferences rather than social expectations. The actor's comments also touched on the wider culture of consumerism and the pressure to keep up with branded fashion. While some shoppers value designer labels, others prefer affordable alternatives that offer a similar look without stretching their budgets. Ultimately, her message was that people should feel comfortable buying what they like, regardless of the brand name or where an item comes from. For her, personal choice and practicality matter more than impressing others with expensive labels. Alongside her acting career, Abbas is currently managing her own fashion brand, Asma Abbas Designs. She has also continued to entertain audiences through acting projects, including the series Winter Love.

title: Zoya Nasir questions praise for Sacha Baron Cohen's Pakistan shoutout
description: The actor questioned praise for Cohen’s Pakistan shoutout, citing concerns over his comedy’s use of racial stereotypes
content: Actor Zoya Nasir questioned the excitement surrounding Hollywood comedian Sacha Baron Cohen’s recent shoutout to Pakistan, arguing that his history of comedy involving racial and religious stereotypes warranted a closer look at the interaction. The Bas Tera Saath Ho actor shared her views on Instagram Stories after a video of Cohen’s brief interaction with Pakistani actor Haris Waheed began circulating online. Waheed, who shared the clip earlier this week, can be seen meeting Cohen, expressing his admiration for the comedian and telling him that he is from Pakistan. Cohen, dressed as his character for the upcoming film Ali G: Who Iz I, responds, “Yo, big up the Pakistan, man,” prompting cheers from people nearby. The exchange received a warm response on social media, with users appreciating the British star’s acknowledgement of Pakistan. Nasir, however, questioned whether the moment deserved the positive reaction it received. “I’m sorry but the sheer lack of awareness is staggering. Sacha Baron Cohen has been openly hostile towards Muslims. Majority of his movies back that up,” she wrote. Criticising the comedian’s approach to comedy, Nasir described his demeanour as marked by “smug, dripping sarcasm” and a “theatrical sense of superiority”. She challenged the enthusiasm surrounding the exchange, asking: “This was not a positive interaction in anyway, shape or form. Why are we excited about that again?” Screengrab: zoyanasir/Instagram Cohen is known for creating characters that use exaggerated accents, cultural appropriation and provocative humour to explore prejudice and social attitudes. However, his work has also attracted criticism over whether it challenges stereotypes or risks reinforcing them. His Borat character, for instance, has sparked debate over the use of ethnic and cultural caricatures, while The Dictator has faced scrutiny over its portrayal of authoritarianism and people from the Middle East. His Ali G persona, meanwhile, has been criticised for appropriating elements of Black culture. Cohen has consistently defended his work as satire intended to expose ignorance and prejudice rather than endorse them. In an interview published by Time on October 20, the comedian addressed criticism of Ali G, explaining that the character was designed to expose cultural bias and reveal how readily people in positions of power took him seriously. “I’ve always designed my characters and comedy as vehicles to expose prejudice, bias and stupidity, though I realise not everyone sees them that way,” he said. He further described Ali G as a white character who imitates the fashion and lyrics of gangsta rap and dancehall artists, adding that the joke was directed at the character himself and the predominantly white, male establishment that believed him. Nasir’s comments highlight the divide in how Cohen’s comedy is received, particularly when an interaction involving one of his characters is interpreted as a gesture of goodwill towards a country or community.

title: Turkish foreign minister to host top diplomats in R4, R4+E3 meetings in Istanbul on Friday
description: FMs of Germany, the UK, France, Türkiye, Egypt, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia set to attend combined format meetings
content: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan will host meetings of top diplomats of the R4 mechanism (Türkiye, Egypt, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia) and the European E3 mechanism (United Kingdom, Germany, and France), including in an unprecedented combined format, in Istanbul on Friday. The meetings will be attended by Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, German Foreign Minister Johann David Wadephul, UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty, and Saudi Minister Faisal bin Farhan, according to Turkish Foreign Ministry sources. The meeting of the seven countries in the combined R4+E3 format for the first time comes at Türkiye’s own initiative. Also Read: Pakistan, Turkiye, Qatar, Indonesia sign defence cooperation accord The meetings are set to address regional issues, particularly the Palestinian question, the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, developments related to Yemen, and efforts to resolve the Russia-Ukraine war. Participants are also expected to discuss opportunities for cooperation and coordination between R4 and E3 countries that could be pursued in the coming days. Fidan to highlight regional responsibilities In his remarks at the meetings, Fidan is expected to stress that regional security requires regional countries to take primary responsibility, adding that Türkiye prioritises strengthening cooperation mechanisms based on regional ownership in line with this approach. Fidan is likely to stress that existing disputes must not be allowed to fuel one another, conflicts must not spread to new areas, and regional tensions must not escalate into broader instability. He is also expected to reiterate that Israel’s ongoing occupation of Palestinian territories, its uncompromising stance that undermines the international community’s peace efforts, and its aggression extending across the region are the main causes of tensions in the Middle East. Fidan will likely reiterate that the dispute between the US and Iran can only be resolved through diplomacy and dialogue, stressing that military methods offer no lasting solution, exacerbate regional vulnerabilities, and carry the risk of a wider conflict. Houthi attacks, Syria, and Ukraine war In response to recent Houthi attacks targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, Fidan is expected to reaffirm Türkiye’s support for safeguarding Saudi security and highlight the importance of the solidarity and collective security approach demonstrated by the new Makka Defence Alliance, formed in August between Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan. He is also likely to acknowledge the valuable contributions of R4 and E3 countries toward strengthening stability and prosperity in Syria, while drawing attention to Israel’s continued actions aimed at destabilising the country. Read More: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia ‘satisfied’ over progress under Makkah defence agreement He is expected to note that Türkiye, as a Black Sea littoral state, continues to convey warnings and proposals for a resolution to the parties involved in the Russia-Ukraine war to prevent the conflict from spreading to the Black Sea and put an end to civilian casualties there. The R4 mechanism was established by Türkiye, Egypt, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia on the basis of regional ownership, with the aim of supporting lasting stability and strengthening dialogue on regional issues. The E3 mechanism, made up of Germany, the UK and France, emerged from trilateral diplomatic cooperation on Iran’s nuclear program launched in 2003. It has gradually evolved into a framework for joint diplomatic initiatives on various regional and international issues.

title: Millions of hacking attempts as companies, governments rush to patch PHP flaws
description: 'I've not seen anything like this in a long, long time,' says Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella
content: Global firms and governments rushed on Thursday ​to patch critical flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet, as a cloud firm reported millions of hacking attempts after vulnerabilities were disclosed. The push came ‌after governments in Europe and elsewhere took websites offline as a precaution on Wednesday while website operators scrambled to secure systems running the software. The emergency shutdowns of banking, airline, rail, tax and government services from Tokyo to Helsinki mark one of the most dramatic tests of the decades-old programming tools that keep the web running, exposing how deeply governments and companies depend on code that few people understand. Read: Government websites in Europe, elsewhere go dark as software flaw sparks security scramble "I've not seen anything like this in a long, long time," Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella ​said at an event in Germany on Thursday, saying the incident showed the importance of building software that can be maintained securely as systems grow more complex. "It was a long day ​and a long night, I know, for all the IT and security folks." PHP key to internet's foundations like html, python The developers of PHP - a key ⁠computing language like HTML and Python - released fixes on Wednesday for vulnerabilities that had lurked in the software for years until they were uncovered using AI, urging users to "update immediately". Madeline Lawrence, co-founder of Belgian cybersecurity ​firm Aikido Security, said that details of the flaws had become public before fixes were ready, with attacks reported since. "Companies are racing to update against attackers who can use AI to exploit them. That's the ​whole race," she said. As companies and governments deployed patches and suspended websites as a precaution, hacking attempts surged into the millions, according to cloud services firm Cloudflare. "In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it," Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince said in a post on X late on Wednesday. "That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post-announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now." Impact from ​Japan to Finland Japanese companies including brokerage Nomura, lender Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, airline ANA and East Japan Railway said on Thursday they were temporarily suspending some internet services as part of emergency measures. Brewer Asahi ​Group Holdings temporarily suspended certain websites and systems and was conducting a security impact assessment. Insurer Tokio Marine Holdings said it had suspended its group website. Japan's Ministry of Finance and Meteorological Agency partially suspended online services to implement ‌safety measures, ⁠while Japan's National Tax Agency temporarily took down its service. The precautionary shutdowns show Japan's growing concerns over cybersecurity, as the country recorded more cyber incidents in the first nine months of the year than in all of last year, according to data from TrendAI. Read More: How one hacker used AI agents and a few thousand dollars to break into scores of sites French telecoms group Orange said it had temporarily suspended access to certain PHP-based websites and applications across several subsidiaries as a precaution. Tencent Cloud, one of China's largest cloud-computing providers, urged customers to install updated PHP versions but stopped short of calling for widespread website shutdowns. Finland's state IT services provider Valtori said it had continued installing PHP security patches overnight and was gradually lifting precautionary ​service blocks after shutting down government public web services ​a day earlier. "Restoring services can take days or ⁠even weeks, as in addition to updates, the systems need to be carefully tested," Valtori Director General Hannu Naumanen said in a statement. Valtori said the outages were not caused by exploitation of the vulnerabilities or by a cyber breach, and that it was not aware of any active exploitation of the flaws. Some ​fixes may take weeks to implement Several Asian governments ordered cybersecurity inspections related to the PHP vulnerabilities on Thursday. China's industry ministry urged organisations and users ​to inspect systems and upgrade ⁠to the latest secure version of PHP. It also recommended strengthening cybersecurity monitoring and changing accounts, passwords and keys where necessary. South Korea raised its private-sector cybersecurity alert level and activated emergency response measures, citing concerns over an increased risk of hacking attacks. Felix Kuhlenkamp, head of security at German digital industry association Bitkom, said that many larger operators had already carried out updates, but that for complex IT systems and smaller organisations it could take ⁠longer. "They may run ​a website using PHP but don't really keep a close eye on it," he said. "If a website is based on ​an old version of PHP for which there is no security update, the entire system must be updated."

title: Apple will have limited iPhone Duo units available in stores on Friday
description: ​Online order ⁠pickup and limited walk-in purchases will be available in the US, Australia, Canada, Mexico and the UK
content: Apple has said it will ​have 'limited' numbers of its folding iPhone Duo phone available ‌for walk-in customers when the device launches on Friday, after initial online orders sold out in minutes and pushed delivery times for some customers to January. Apple announced ​its first folding phone in September, with analysts expecting it ​to quickly come to dominate a niche segment where ⁠rivals such as Samsung Electronics and Huawei Technologies have sold premium ​offerings for years. But the iPhone Duo is also a more complex ​product than standard candy-bar iPhones, with a tight-fitting hinge that analysts believe may take time for Apple to learn to manufacture in high volumes. Read: India investigating Tata data leak that exposed Apple iPhone secrets “On Friday morning, our ​teams look forward to welcoming customers at Apple Stores to ​experience iPhone Duo and the incredible iPhone line-up for themselves," Apple said in a ‌statement. "Apple ⁠Stores will have limited iPhone Duo available for walk-in customers, and we’re working hard to get this revolutionary new product into customers' hands as quickly as possible.” The availability of walk-in units will vary by ​country, Apple said. ​Online order ⁠pickup and limited walk-in purchases will be available in the United States, Australia, Canada, Mexico and much ​of the UK and Europe. But other regions will only ​have ⁠iPhone Duo units available for customers who already bought them online. Those include mainland China, France, Hong Kong, India, Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Taiwan, ⁠Thailand ​and the UAE, Apple said. In the China-governed territory of ​Macau, the iPhone Duo will be available for walk-in customers only, with limited inventory, ​Apple said.

title: DeepSeek wrapping up $15b fundraising to fuel AI race, sources say
description: The ​total number of investors in the funding round exceeded 15, source reveals
content: Chinese ​AI startup DeepSeek has raised about 100 billion yuan ($14.98 billion) in its latest funding round from investors including chipmaker ‌GigaDevice, food delivery company Meituan and automaker Geely, according to four people with knowledge of the matter. Battery maker Contemporary Amperex Technology (CATL) and WeChat operator Tencent Holdings, both existing shareholders, were among the biggest investors in the round, said two of the people. Home appliances maker Midea and existing shareholder NetEase also participated, the people ​said. Other investors include Boyu Capital, CPE and Legend Capital, as well as existing shareholder IDG Capital, three of the people said. The ​total number of investors in the funding round exceeded 15, one of the people said. Read: Trump says companies should pay 'dividend' to communities to make data centres popular DeepSeek, which sources have ⁠said is valued at 500 billion yuan before new capital is injected, will have doubled its original fundraising target of 50 billion ​yuan. The rise underscores strong interest from investors - many backed by the state and big corporations - as China aims to stay competitive in ​the AI race against the US. "It's encouraging to see such a high valuation for DeepSeek, showing the confidence from investors on the future of its open-source strategies," said Lian Jye Su, chief analyst at research firm Omdia. "Given that they (the investors) are all Chinese and critical component supply chain vendors, I can see ​DeepSeek itself becoming a key part of these domestic tech supply chains," Su said. The fundraising is set to be complete in the coming ​days, but financial details and the investor lineup are not ironclad and could still change, a second person said. DeepSeek could not be immediately reached for comment. ‌Geely declined ⁠to comment. The other firms mentioned in this article did not immediately respond to requests for comment. On Thursday, Bloomberg first reported, citing sources, that DeepSeek had raised $15 billion in the latest funding round, with CATL and Tencent as its main backers. DeepSeek's fundraising outcome comes amid growing concerns over massive AI spending that triggered a new selloff in global tech stocks this month. Read More: China's DeepSeek developing its own AI chip, sources say The soured sentiment has led to delays or withdrawals ​of data centre IPOs and poor market ​debuts of AI-related companies in South ⁠Korea and Hong Kong, Reuters has reported. Shares of Z.AI and MiniMax, two large language model developers listed in Hong Kong since January, have fallen sharply from their peaks earlier this year. After the fundraising, DeepSeek ​is getting closer to tapping public markets. In September, Reuters reported that the company aimed to kick ​off its IPO ⁠process this year and had hired CITIC Securities to prepare for the potential STAR Market float. Last month, the company released its latest model, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, which it said was designed for greater capability, faster inference, higher throughput and scaling to larger models. The Hangzhou-based firm raised $7.4 billion from its inaugural external funding round ⁠in June, ​Reuters has reported. Filings by two Chinese investors in July suggested DeepSeek was valued at ​350.88 billion yuan, or around $52 billion, in the June fundraising.

title: Pakistan whip Bhutan in tennis event
description: Debutants Romaisa Malik and Hajra Sohail help Green-shirts complete clean sweep
content: Pakistan beat Bhutan 3-0 on Thursday to maintain their winning run in the Billie Jean King Cup Asia/Oceania Group III (B) tournament in Islamabad. Ushna Suhail and Mahin Aftab Qureshi secured straight-set victories in the singles before debutants Romaisa Malik and Hajra Sohail completed the clean sweep in doubles at the Pakistan Tennis Federation Tennis Complex. Ushna defeated Tandin Dorji 6-0, 6-0, while Mahin overcame Tenzin Wangsel Lhaden by the same scoreline to give Pakistan a commanding lead. Romaisa and Hajra then beat Bhutan's Kinley Yangden and Tandin Tsheyang Wangmo 6-1, 6-4 in their first appearance at the international team competition. Elsewhere, Maldives defeated Bahrain 3-0 in Group A, while Qatar and Iran recorded identical 3-0 victories over Kuwait and Jordan respectively in Group B. Pakistan will face Maldives on Friday as they continue their campaign in the women's international team tournament.

title: Verstappen bids to delay Antonelli's F1 coronation
description: Red Bull driver rediscovers winning formula in last two races
content: Max Verstappen is set to be a party-pooper this weekend as he seeks to delay Kimi Antonelli's title celebrations by notching a third consecutive win with another triumph at the United States Grand Prix. Red Bull's four-time world champion won both the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and then the Singapore Grand Prix to emerge as a leading contender for more success just when Mercedes' precocious 20-year-old Italian moved within reach of the title. The 29-year-old Dutchman, who has acknowledged Antonelli's generational talent, won from pole at the Circuit of the Americas last year and is chasing a fifth win at the Texan track where Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton was won five times. But Verstappen has been reluctant to claim that Red Bull's recovery in form and results will automatically translate to more success. "It's difficult to say – I don't want to say now that I will be in the fight in Austin," he said after his Singapore win. "But the last few weekends have been great. I just take it race by race and we'll see how it goes there. It's another very different kind of track." After a run of seven podium finishes in his last eight races, including two wins and three second places, Verstappen, 119 points adrift in fourth, may well scupper hopes that Antonelli can win and, with the stars aligning, become Italy's first champion since 1953 and the youngest in F1 history. - Title within reach - To seize the title in Texas, the Italian, who leads Mercedes team-mate George Russell by 102 points, needs to win the race and see Russell fail to finish in the top nine and Hamilton outside the top four. Antonelli was only four years old when Sebastian Vettel took the record as youngest champion, with Red Bull, in 2010, and he knows he must stay focused and race to win, as he always does. "I know it's very close and I know it's there, but I need to make sure I keep doing my best and go out and win and perform in my best way," he said. Italy's last champion was Alberto Ascari for Ferrari. McLaren's deputy team principal Bradley Lord drew upon tennis when he described Antonelli's position by saying: "We're in that uncomfortable phase where you have to navigate the media with everyone saying 'you can do it – you've got first match point." Russell's hopes of reining in Antonelli may be aided by Verstappen while Hamilton could also be a threat as he returns to one of his favourite circuits seeking a record sixth win and seventh in the United States GP. Both Mercedes drivers will run the team's latest updates package as they go into a decisive triple-header of races in Texas, Mexico and Brazil, but it may be that Ferrari and Red Bull can steal the initiative. These races may be run on bumpy tracks and in hot conditions that deliver unexpected results, a prospect that Verstappen has anticipated. "From what I saw in the world endurance championship race in Austin, the track is incredibly bumpy and I will probably need to order a new spine after the weekend – or become like Robocop. It's crazy.

title: Opposition leaders criticise govt over stalled talks, restrictions on parliamentarians
description: Salman Akram Raja says all-parties conference being planned within 10 days to discuss K-P political situation
content: Opposition leaders Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Thursday criticised the government over stalled political negotiations and restrictions on parliamentarians, calling for meaningful dialogue and the protection of elected representatives’ rights. Speaking at a press conference outside Parliament House alongside opposition leaders, Gohar said the opposition had repeatedly engaged in negotiations with the government in good faith and without preconditions, but the process had failed to produce the desired results. “Our government went away while we kept negotiating with the government,” he said, referring to the opposition’s attempts to pursue political dialogue. Gohar also questioned the criteria used to assess political leaders’ loyalty to the state, saying that despite nearly three years of the current parliament, he still did not understand the formula used to determine such allegiance. “We have always said that Pakistan comes first and the state comes first,” he said. “We are treated as though we are not loyal to the state. This perception must end,” he added, calling for an end to questions about opposition politicians’ commitment to Pakistan. He also called for parliamentarians to be protected so they could represent their constituents freely and without fear. Recalling an incident in September 2024, when opposition lawmakers were allegedly picked up, Gohar said the opposition leader had moved a resolution in the National Assembly in response. He added that a special committee had also been constituted to address the issue of parliamentarians’ protection. Achakzai calls for complete recording of parliamentary speeches Speaking at the same press conference, Opposition Leader in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai stressed that parliamentary speeches should be recorded in their entirety, arguing that the official record was essential to preserving the country’s political history and allowing the public to assess the statements of elected representatives. “The complete speech of a member speaking in the National Assembly being recorded is a constitutional requirement,” he said. Achakzai said parliamentarians had to struggle even for rights that should ordinarily be guaranteed under parliamentary rules. He maintained that the speaker’s authority should be exercised in accordance with the rules and regulations governing the assembly. Referring to his speech in the National Assembly a day earlier, he said he had made no inappropriate remarks. He alleged that his four-and-a-half-minute speech had been presented as a nine-minute address. He also rejected suggestions that his remarks had been directed against the country, saying not a single word in his speech had been against Pakistan. The opposition leader said the time allotted to opposition lawmakers to speak in parliament had been curtailed, describing the restriction as another obstacle to democratic debate. Achakzai questioned what he described as the inconsistent issuance of production orders for lawmakers, saying such orders had been issued for some members but not others. He argued that parliamentary proceedings and the rights of elected representatives should be protected without discrimination. He also criticised the government’s approach to political negotiations, questioning how the opposition could trust a process that, in his view, had been ridiculed by those in power. He said political dialogue required a meeting with PTI founder Imran Khan. He also recalled that Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman had met the prime minister in connection with the issue. The opposition had asked the government to ensure that the prime minister personally extended an invitation for negotiations, he said. “Negotiations cannot take place in an atmosphere where the process itself is being mocked,” he said. Achakzai called for a committee to investigate allegations of corruption against the incumbent government, proposing that Defence Minister Khawaja Asif head it. He maintained that the opposition would resist what it considered an undemocratic system through democratic means. “It is the duty of every citizen who wants to save Pakistan to stand up for democracy,” he said, adding that the country needed a strong parliament and state institutions operating within their respective constitutional jurisdictions. “We will not hand Pakistan over to an undemocratic system,” he said, warning that such an order could threaten the country’s unity. Raja Nasir Abbas calls for rule of law, constitutional supremacy Also speaking at the press conference, Majlis Wahdat-e-Muslimeen chief Allama Raja Nasir Abbas stressed that the rule of law, justice and respect for the Constitution were essential for Pakistan’s progress, saying the country’s political and economic crises could not be resolved without the supremacy of law. He said the rule of law and access to justice were fundamental to national development. Pakistan could not overcome its ongoing political crisis unless the Constitution was upheld and the rule of law firmly established, he added. Addressing the country’s economic challenges, Abbas said the economic crisis, too, could not be resolved without ensuring the supremacy of law. He added that justice was necessary to restore public confidence in state institutions and the wider system. He expressed concern that the trust deficit between the rulers and the people had reached its highest level in the country’s history. He also criticised the continued registration of fabricated cases and first information reports (FIRs), saying such practices further undermined public trust. Referring to the February 8, 2024, general elections, Abbas alleged that the people’s mandate had been stolen. He said depriving citizens of their right to vote and undermining their electoral choices constituted serious injustices. He further said tampering with votes amounted to an attack on the Constitution and the rule of law, stressing that protecting the sanctity of the vote was essential to upholding democratic principles and restoring public confidence in the political system. Abbas reiterated that Pakistan’s sustainable progress, political stability and economic recovery depended on constitutional supremacy, the rule of law and justice for all citizens. Gohar denies reports of differences within PTI Meanwhile, Gohar addressed reports concerning internal party affairs, PTI lawmakers in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) and the provincial organisation, urging party members to verify information before reacting to reports. He said the news that had prompted a social media post by the party’s secretary general was incorrect and that he had spoken to the relevant leaders and lawmakers. Describing PTI’s lawmakers from K-P as a valuable asset, Gohar praised their role in supporting Imran over the past two years. He said they had remained steadfast despite difficult circumstances and continued to play a leading role in rallies, public meetings and protest marches. “All these members are standing even more firmly with Imran Khan, his ideology and his struggle,” he said, adding that they enjoyed the PTI founder’s full confidence. Gohar said no party lawmaker would consider disregarding Imran’s instructions and assured the provincial leadership that it would be consulted on important party decisions. On the provincial party presidency, he clarified that Junaid Akbar had been appointed by Imran himself and that he had issued the notification in accordance with the PTI founder’s instructions. Junaid would continue to serve as provincial president, he said. In Junaid’s absence, senior vice-president Noorul Haq Qadri would chair meetings of the provincial organisation under the party constitution, while provincial secretary general Ali Asghar Khan would oversee other organisational matters. Gohar said discussions had taken place with the relevant office-bearers and that the provincial organisation had expressed the same preference during its meeting. A formal notification was expected to be issued on the matter. He added that no changes would be made to the provincial organisation or its existing cabinet until Junaid returned. Emphasising party unity, the PTI chairman said the party’s focus should remain on Imran’s position, political narrative and struggle rather than internal disagreements or unnecessary public statements. He reiterated that the party remained united under Imran’s leadership and that his decisions and instructions were final. Gohar also reaffirmed PTI’s position on the K-P chief minister, saying Sohail Afridi remained the party’s choice and that there was no question of considering anyone else for the position, as the decision rested with Imran. Salman Akram Raja rejects claims Sohail Afridi derailed talks with govt Separately, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja has rejected claims that non-functional K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi was responsible for the breakdown of negotiations with the federal government, saying the talks collapsed over the denial of access to PTI founder Imran Khan’s personal physicians and concerns over provincial autonomy. In an interview with a private television channel on Thursday, he said the refusal to allow Khan’s personal doctors to examine him was one of the two principal reasons behind the failure of the negotiations. He said PTI could not grant the federal government unrestricted authority to intervene in the affairs of K-P. “These were the two principal reasons why the talks collapsed,” Raja said, alleging that the government had deliberately undermined the negotiations. The PTI leader also described the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province as unconstitutional, alleging that the government had introduced the measures to take control of the provincial administration. “They just wanted to take over the province,” he said. Raja said an all-parties conference (APC) was being planned within the next 10 days, or earlier, to discuss the prevailing political situation. “This is a political issue and therefore all political parties must play their role,” he said. He disclosed that several political parties were in contact with him over the situation, including Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman. Asked about the role of Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party chairman Mehmood Khan Achakzai, Raja said the final decision rested with the PTI founder. He described Achakzai and Majlis Wahdat-e-Muslimeen chief Allama Nasir Abbas as a shield for the party, adding that PTI would continue to seek their political advice and support. Raja also maintained that PTI’s long march had not ended, signalling that the party’s political campaign would continue. Meanwhile, PTI leader and Senator Syed Ali Zafar denied that negotiations with the government were imminent, saying decisions concerning the party would be made by its parliamentary party. “We are yet to determine the terms of reference,” Zafar said while speaking to a journalist from the same television channel. He further alleged that the government had decided to impose governor’s rule around one-and-a-half months earlier. Yousafzai distances party from YouTubers campaigning against state institutions PTI's K-P information secretary Shaukat Ali Yousafzai on Thursday distanced the party from YouTubers campaigning against state institutions, saying they had no links with PTI and that such campaigns had negatively affected the party. Speaking in an interview with a private television channel, Yousafzai said PTI founder Imran Khan had always referred to the armed forces as his own institution, adding that no other viewpoint would be entertained on the matter. He said PTI had always condemned terrorism and described it as unjustified to label the party’s leaders or workers as facilitators of terrorists. He also alleged that the government had used concerns over peace and security as a pretext to impose emergency and governor’s rule in K-P, calling the move unjustified. He expressed confidence in Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and Salman Akram Raja, adding that he would not be “intimidated by a YouTuber” based overseas. Deadlock on emergency and governor’s rule in K-P The debate over emergency and governor’s rule in K-P intensified in late September amid worsening security concerns and growing political tensions between the federal government and the PTI-led provincial administration. Federal ministers accused the provincial government of failing to address terrorism and governance challenges, while PTI considered the possibility of an in-house change or dissolution of the provincial assembly. The federal government subsequently stepped up its warnings, with Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and other officials arguing that constitutional provisions allowed the Centre to intervene if circumstances warranted extraordinary measures. The government cited the deteriorating law and order situation and the provincial administration’s handling of security challenges as precursors for governor’s rule and emergency. Later, on October 11, President Asif Ali Zardari approved the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, following approval by the federal cabinet. The government cited escalating terrorist attacks, threats to lives and property, and what it described as a breakdown of the constitutional system in the province. The measures invoked Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, while the federal government also authorised the deployment of the army to assist the civil administration. Read More: PHC takes up challenge to emergency today The move transferred executive authority from the elected provincial government to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi and affected 12 districts under the emergency proclamation. PTI rejected the decision, arguing that it undermined provincial autonomy and the party’s electoral mandate. The intervention also marked the fourth spell of governor’s rule in the province, following earlier instances in 1975, 1994 and 1999. The issue subsequently moved to Parliament and the courts. On October 12, a petition challenging the imposition of emergency measures and governor’s rule in K-P was filed in the Peshawar High Court by PTI, a day after President Asif Ali Zardari approved the federal government’s decision on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. The opposition argued that the constitutional requirements had not been fulfilled and that the intervention violated provincial autonomy. Three days later, on October 15, a joint sitting of Parliament approved separate resolutions endorsing the emergency and governor’s rule for two months, despite severe protests from the opposition parties. So far, the government and the opposition remain at loggerheads regarding the governance of the province.

title: ATC replaces state counsel after Imaan, Hadi object to appointment
description: Judge tells accused that if their lawyers are not present tomorrow, state counsel will cross-examine
content: An Islamabad anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Thursday replaced state counsel Taimoor Janjua, who had been appointed to represent lawyers Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha in a case concerning the removal of barriers and alleged interference in official duties, after the two defendants objected to his appointment. Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra, who heard the case at Adiala Jail, accepted an application filed by Imaan and Hadi challenging Janjua’s appointment and appointed Atif Mahmood as the new state counsel. During the hearing, Imaan said Janjua had previously been appointed as state counsel in their case. Hadi alleged that Janjua had told people he had received Rs500,000 and completed the cross-examination in a single day. “Are you the accused’s lawyer or are you against them?” their lawyer asked Janjua. Janjua responded, “Come with me to any private case outside, and you will find out whether I work or not.” Judge Sipra expressed displeasure over Janjua’s conduct and asked, “Has no one ever taught you how to appear in court?” Read: ATC summons Islamabad IGP in Imaan, Hadi bail case on November 3 Imaan told the court that they did not need a state counsel because they had their own lawyers. Hadi added that their lawyers were occupied with other cases at the high court while the ATC was conducting daily hearings. The prosecution had initially submitted a list of nine witnesses but later dropped two, leaving seven witnesses in the case. Statements from all seven prosecution witnesses had been recorded, and the court had summoned them for cross-examination. However, none of the witnesses was cross-examined during Thursday’s hearing. Judge Sipra directed that they be summoned again on Friday. “Imaan and Hadi, if your lawyers do not cross-examine the witnesses tomorrow, the state counsel will do so,” the judge said. The court adjourned the hearing until 9am on Friday. The case so far The Islamabad ATC framed charges against Imaan and Hadi on October 7 in a case relating to the alleged removal of security barriers and disruption of a designated route during the visit of an international cricket team. The court subsequently recorded statements from all seven prosecution witnesses, and the case has reached the cross-examination stage. The trial was shifted to Adiala Jail amid disputes over the accused’s production in court and defence lawyers’ access to their clients. Separately, Imaan and Hadi approached the Islamabad High Court (IHC) seeking to suspend the trial, alleging procedural violations in the framing of charges, including that they had not been physically present when indicted and had not received copies of relevant documents. The IHC heard their appeals on October 19 and said it would issue an order after hearing the respondents. Background Imaan and her husband Hadi were rearrested on September 17, shortly after the Supreme Court granted them bail and suspended their sentences in a separate social-media posts case. They were produced before an Islamabad ATC in connection with a case registered at Kohsar Police Station. Police sought 30-day physical remand, but ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain rejected the request and sent the couple on judicial remand. The judge noted that although they had been nominated in the FIR as members of an unlawful assembly, no weapon had been attributed to either accused. Read More: SC suspends trial court order, grants bail to Imaan Mazari, Hadi Ali Chattha On September 27, the court issued a contempt notice to the Adiala jail superintendent after the authorities failed to facilitate the signing and transmission of the documents and also failed to produce the accused through video link. Two days later, the issue was resolved after Imaan and Hadi signed the required powers of attorney. On September 29, the ATC ended the contempt proceedings against the jail authorities and separately confirmed that notices had been issued on the couple’s bail applications, with arguments scheduled before Judge Abul Hasnat. On October 7, the ATC had framed charges against Imaan and Hadi in the case related to the alleged violation of a designated route and incitement during the arrival of an international cricket team, despite defence objections that legal requirements had not been fulfilled.

title: Govt directs ministries to compile civil servants' foreign nationality declarations
description: Failure to submit declarations or provide accurate information will constitute misconduct under civil service rules
content: The federal government has directed all ministries and divisions to submit consolidated details of civil servants’ declarations regarding foreign nationality, travel documents and dependants’ nationality status, according to an official notification issued by the Establishment Division dated October 21. The notification referred to the Civil Servants (Disclosure and Regulation of Foreign Nationality) Rules, 2026, under which all civil servants were required to submit declarations regarding their own and their dependants’ nationality status within 90 days of the rules’ publication in the official gazette. Under Rule 3(3), civil servants must declare whether they hold the nationality of any foreign country, possess foreign travel documents or are married to a foreign national. They must also disclose the relevant nationality and travel-document status of their dependants. The Establishment Division said failure to submit the required declaration or providing false information would constitute misconduct under the Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 2020, in accordance with Rule 3(4) of the 2026 rules. The notification directed all ministries and divisions to provide the information in a consolidated format for officers under their administrative control, excluding those belonging to the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), Police Service of Pakistan (PSP), Secretariat Group (SG) and Office Management Group (OMG). The prescribed format requires the name, designation and basic pay scale of each officer, confirmation of whether a declaration has been submitted under Rule 3(3), and details of the foreign nationality or travel-document status of both the officer and their dependants. Earlier this month, the government decided to enforce the Foreign Citizenship Rules 2026, directing civil servants to submit declarations detailing any foreign citizenship held by themselves or their dependants within one week. The Establishment Division, through an office memorandum, directed civil servants to provide details of foreign citizenship, foreign travel documents and marriages to foreign nationals. The directive applies to officers holding dual nationality and requires them to furnish the relevant information within the stipulated one-week deadline.

title: Karachi court rejects Iqrarul Hassan's bail plea in anti-state content case
description: Case filed under Sections 9, 10, 20, 24, and 26-A of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) 2016
content: A Karachi court on Thursday rejected Iqrarul Hassan’s bail application in a case involving allegations of harming the state and national integrity by disseminating anti-state content. The District and Sessions Court East dismissed a petition challenging Hassan's physical remand, with the defence counsel questioning the legality of the proceedings and arguing that the case concerned digital and cyber matters. The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) registered the case against Hassan, who is currently in jail on judicial remand. Last week, the NCCIA produced Hassan before the judicial magistrate, who granted a four-day physical remand. On October 17, the court extended the physical remand by two days, rejecting an application filed by his lawyers and directed the NCCIA to submit a report at the next hearing. The case against Hassan, filed under Sections 9, 10, 20, 24, and 26-A of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) 2016, stated that the journalist, "through his personal social media accounts on the platforms X, Instagram and Facebook, is intentionally disseminating false, fabricated, anti-state and defamatory content with the object of instigating the general public against the state, its institutions and its functionaries." The FIR stated that the content of Hassan's social media posts portrayed the state, its institutions and its functionaries "in a false and distorted manner." Also Read: Journalist arrested on 'attempted rape' charges It also noted that Hassan "represented lawful measures as controversial with the intent to instigate and incite the general public at large against the state and the lawfully constituted authorities." The FIR stated further, "The accused instigated a substantial following, including the general public, on the aforesaid platforms," adding that the content that he posted was published and broadcast "in an open, publicly accessible manner, without restriction, so as to reach and influence the public at large throughout Pakistan and abroad." Hassan's wife Farah Iqrar told The Express Tribune on October 12 that a group of unidentified individuals posing as officials of the NCCIA had allegedly taken him away from their residence in Lahore’s Defence C area. According to Farah, between five and seven people, including women, arrived at the house late on Sunday night, during the intervening hours of Sunday and Monday, and demanded that Hassan come outside. She alleged that the individuals threatened to break down the door if he was not handed over. They subsequently entered the house, forcibly took the journalist from a room, and took him away. Later, Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari said that Punjab Police had not arrested Hassan, adding that investigations into the matter were underway and his family would be informed as soon as verified information about his whereabouts became available. Hours before the reported incident, Hassan had posted a message on X criticising the Pakistan Peoples Party and referring to Nawaz Sharif and President Asif Ali Zardari.

title: Nvidia boss criticises 'cheap' AI doomsday warnings
description: 'When you say that it will be the end of the human civilisation, first of all, it's not true'
content: Artificial Intelligence (AI) chip giant Nvidia's boss Jensen Huang said on Thursday that warnings that artificial intelligence could wipe out humanity were "cheap" attempts to grab headlines. "When you say that it will be the end of the human civilisation, first of all, it's not true," he told a conference organised by his company in Berlin. While such statements generate "headlines", they were "made up" and "cheap", added Huang, whose visit to Berlin is the final stop of a European tour. After incidents of the technology getting around controls during tests, there has been a heated debate about whether AI presents an existential risk to humanity. In September, a researcher resigned from Anthropic with a stark warning that leading AI labs were "gambling with our lives", and the bosses of Anthropic and fellow industry giant OpenAI have called for a slowdown. Read: DeepSeek wrapping up $15b fundraising to fuel AI race, sources say Huang, however, is firmly in the opposing camp, and has advocated for development of the technology to move full steam ahead. Speaking in Berlin, he urged the world to approach AI with "responsible optimism". "If you care about the future, past our own lives, if we care about the future of sustainability, this is the perfect time -- build AI," he said. "Don't try to stifle AI." US regulators are seen as unlikely to intervene when it comes to AI development. President Donald Trump opposes strict regulation and said in September that the US government would rename the technology "super intelligence" in official communications. During Huang's European tour, Nvidia pledged nearly $10 billion in investments in the continent's technology sector and urged Europe, which is lagging behind in the AI race, to move faster.

title: International Criminal Court, its senior officials awarded 2026 EU Sakharov Prize
description: EP recognises court's work on international justice amid waves of US sanctions targeting the court, its judges, staff
content: The European Parliament on Thursday awarded its 2026 Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought jointly to the International Criminal Court (ICC) and its senior officials, recognising their work in upholding international law and justice. "The European Union is founded on respect for multilateralism and international institutions. By awarding the Sakharov Prize to the International Criminal Court and its officials, Parliament recognises the important work carried out by the Court to uphold international law and justice," said EP President Roberta Metsola, announcing the winners to the full assembly. The parliament highlighted the ICC investigations, prosecutions, trials, and issuance or authorisation of arrest warrants for serious international crimes, including genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity. "The Court plays an essential role in the global fight against impunity," said an official statement. Also Read: US imposes sanctions on ICC hours after former judge wins Nobel Peace Prize The statement also reiterated concerns over sanctions imposed on the court since 2025, particularly by the US, targeting its prosecutors, judges, staff, and partners. Lawmakers have repeatedly called on the European Commission to activate the EU's blocking statute to protect ICC officials from the extraterritorial effects of sanctions and safeguard the court's independence. The parliament also stressed that all EU member states are parties to the Rome Statute, which established the ICC, and are obligated to implement its decisions. Established in 1988, the Sakharov Prize recognises individuals and organisations defending human rights, democracy, and the rule of law. The award ceremony will take place in December in Strasbourg.

title: France reports first human case of livestock virus Shamonda after patient dies
description: It is suspected that the victim was bitten by ​a midge carrying the virus in eastern France
content: France on Thursday reported the first ‌human case of the Shamonda virus, usually found in livestock, in a patient who later died, with authorities adding there was no risk to the general population at this stage. It is suspected that the victim was bitten by ​a midge carrying the virus in eastern France, where it had circulated among animals ​this spring and summer, the government said in a statement. The UN's World Health ⁠Organisation said it was in contact with French authorities about the outbreak. The patient died in early ​October and had been receiving treatment for a serious illness that made them more susceptible to infection ​than the general population, the Stockholm-based European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control said in a statement. Read: Govt swings into action after new polio case in Karachi The victim was a man in his 60s living in the Lyon area, local newspaper Le Progres reported. "Based on current information and knowledge ​of the transmission of closely related viruses, this is an isolated human case, and it is ​unlikely to lead to wider spread at this time," said the Geneva-based WHO, which coordinates responses to international ‌public health ⁠issues and emergencies. The French government also said no health risk to the general population had been identified. Virus spreading in animals in Europe Shamonda is transmitted by biting midges and most commonly found in cattle, though it has also been found in horses, alpacas, sheep and goats, according to the World Organisation for ​Animal Health (WOAH). It is not classified ​as a disease ⁠under the EU Animal Health Law and is not subject to official surveillance or control measures. Read more: Australia confirms first H5N1 bird flu case on sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island Identified in Nigeria in the mid-1960s, Shamonda was first confirmed in ​Europe in late July after genomic tests on sick cattle in southern ​Germany, Switzerland and ⁠eastern France. France's weekly animal health surveillance bulletin said it had also been detected in Austria, Belgium, Ireland, Italy, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, and the UK's Jersey. The virus has several effects on ⁠animals, with affected cattle ​showing diarrhoea, weakness, loss of appetite and, less often, ​fever, French animal health authorities said. A study of nine French dairy farms found milk production fell by up to 75%.

title: Outlander  star Sam Heughan teams up with Viola Davis for  Ascent
description: Sam Heughan joins Viola Davis in Paramount  thriller Ascent  with production set to begin in Los Angeles in 2027
content:
Sam Heughan joins Viola Davis in Paramount+ thriller Ascent, with production set to begin in Los Angeles in 2027
Outlander star Sam Heughan has joined Viola Davis in Ascent , an upcoming thriller series for Paramount+ set in the world of corporate crisis management and damage control.
Heughan will play Conal, one of the top agents at Ascent Ventures. According to the character description, Conal is a charming and adaptable operative who uses social intelligence and ruthlessness to complete his missions.
Davis will star as Catriona, an elite corporate fixer whose professional skills are put to the test when her estranged daughter faces danger. The character must use the same ruthless tactics that have made her indispensable to powerful corporate clients to protect her family.
The series was created by John Logan, whose writing credits include Skyfall and Gladiator . Logan will serve as showrunner and executive producer, alongside Michael Aguilar and Davis, who will executive produce through her production company, JuVee Productions, with Julius Tennon.
Ascent is produced by Paramount Television Studios. Production is scheduled to begin in Los Angeles in 2027, although Paramount+ has not announced a release date.
Heughan is best known for playing Jamie Fraser in the historical drama Outlander , in which he starred opposite Caitríona Balfe for eight seasons and 101 episodes. His television credits also include The Couple Next Door and Men in Kilts: A Road Trip with Sam and Graham . He is also set to appear in the upcoming series Embassy , alongside J.K. Simmons and Anna Kendrick.
His film credits include Love Again , The Spy Who Dumped Me , Bloodshot and SAS: Red Notice . Heughan has also appeared on stage as Macbeth with the Royal Shakespeare Company and written three New York Times bestselling books.

title: Carrie  renewed for season 2 by Prime Video after strong debut
description: Prime Video renews Mike Flanagan   s  Carrie  for season 2 after strong reviews  with Summer H  Howell set to return
content:
Prime Video renews Mike Flanagan’s 'Carrie' for season 2 after strong reviews, with Summer H. Howell set to return
Prime Video has renewed Carrie , Mike Flanagan’s adaptation of Stephen King’s horror classic, for season 2 following the strong reception of its debut season.
The renewal was announced on October 22, just two weeks after the eight-episode first season premiered on October 7. The series stars Summer H. Howell as Carrie White and marks another collaboration between Flanagan and King, who both serve as executive producers.
Since its release, Carrie has topped Prime Video’s weekly global television rankings, reaching number one in more than 105 countries. According to Luminate, the series recorded 653,000 US views during its first two days of availability and 3.6 million views during its first full week.
Peter Friedlander, head of global television at Amazon MGM Studios, said the series had connected with longtime Stephen King fans as well as younger and international audiences. He also highlighted its appeal among female viewers.
The renewal comes after season 1 departed from the ending of King’s original novel, leaving the story open for further development. In the finale, Carrie survives the events of prom night and leaves town in a car with her friend Emaline, played by Thalia Dudek.
Flanagan said the creative team had envisioned a story extending beyond the events of the prom, expressing gratitude for King’s support in exploring Carrie’s future.
King also welcomed the renewal, saying he was excited for audiences to discover what lies ahead for the character.
Howell is expected to return for season 2, with Dudek also among the potential returning cast members. Other characters who survived the first season’s prom night massacre could feature in the next instalment.
Prime Video has teased further revelations, major character developments and unexpected twists in the upcoming season. However, an official release date and complete cast list have yet to be announced.

title: Andrew Scott   s    Elsinore    to receive Ian Charleson Legacy Tribute at Gotham Awards
description: The tribute will recognise Scott  screenwriter Stephen Beresford  director Simon Stone and the wider production team
content:
The tribute will recognise Scott, screenwriter Stephen Beresford, director Simon Stone and the wider production team
Andrew Scott’s biographical drama Elsinore will receive the Gotham Legacy Tribute in honour of Ian Charleson at the 36th annual Gotham Film Awards, recognising the film’s portrayal of the Scottish actor’s life, career and final stage performance.
The Gotham Film & Media Institute announced the honour on October 22, ahead of the ceremony scheduled for November 30 at Cipriani Wall Street in New York City. The tribute will recognise Scott, screenwriter Stephen Beresford, director Simon Stone and the wider production team for bringing Charleson’s story to a new generation of audiences.
Elsinore follows Charleson, best known for starring in the Oscar-winning film Chariots of Fire , as he pursues his passion for theatre while confronting a devastating AIDS diagnosis. The film centres on his determination to perform Hamlet at London’s National Theatre during the final months of his life, capturing the courage and commitment behind what became one of his most celebrated performances.
Scott leads the cast as Charleson, alongside Academy Award winner Olivia Colman, Billie Piper, Johnny Flynn and Joe Locke. Colman portrays Dr Margaret Johnson, a physician who treated Charleson and other gay men during the HIV epidemic and helped establish a dedicated HIV clinic.
The film is directed by Stone and written by Beresford, whose previous work includes Pride . The creative team has reportedly nicknamed themselves “The Charleson Chaps” following their collaboration on the project.
Jeffrey Sharp, executive director of the Gotham Film & Media Institute, praised the filmmakers for creating a moving portrait of an artist whose final months demonstrated his dedication to performance and the community around him. He said the tribute would celebrate both the film and the remarkable actor who inspired it.
Charleson died in January 1990, aged 40, after being diagnosed with AIDS. His decision to speak openly about the illness and have AIDS recorded as his cause of death helped challenge the stigma surrounding the disease at a time when public understanding and acceptance remained limited.
Elsinore premiered at the Telluride Film Festival in September and later screened at the Toronto International Film Festival, where it won the International People’s Choice Award. It has continued to screen at autumn festivals, receiving audience awards at events including the Mill Valley Film Festival and the Hamptons International Film Festival.
Focus Features will release the film in select North American cinemas on November 20, with a wider release planned over the Thanksgiving holiday and through December.
The Gotham Awards have also announced other tributes for this year’s ceremony. Michael will receive the Gotham Musical Tribute, La Bola Negra will be honoured with the Gotham Vanguard Tribute, Danny Boyle will receive the Gotham Director Tribute for Ink , and animation studio LAIKA will receive the Gotham Anniversary Tribute. The nominees for the 36th annual awards will be announced on October 27.
