title: Next James Bond casting heats up as Amazon prepares final screen tests
description: Amazon prepares final James Bond screen tests  with Jack Lowden  Callum Turner and Josh O   Connor among contenders
content:
Amazon prepares final James Bond screen tests, with Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O’Connor among contenders
The search for the next James Bond is nearing a crucial stage, with Amazon MGM Studios preparing to hold final screen tests for the iconic 007 role over the coming week.
According to Deadline, auditions could begin as early as Friday, October 23, and continue through the following week. At least four screen-test offers have reportedly been issued, although the studio has not officially confirmed the candidates.
Sources cited by Deadline identified Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O’Connor as three of the expected contenders. The fourth potential candidate has not been publicly identified.
The final auditions were initially planned for earlier in October but were postponed because of scheduling conflicts involving the shortlisted actors. The revised dates are intended to allow the finalists to attend around the same time.
Despite the upcoming tests, Amazon MGM Studios has not established a confirmed date for announcing the next James Bond. Industry sources reportedly expect a decision before the end of 2026.
The casting process began in the spring, when casting director Nina Gold joined the project. Following several months of meetings and auditions, the shortlist was narrowed down as the studio and producers worked towards the final testing stage.
Producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman are overseeing the project alongside director Denis Villeneuve, who was selected to lead the next instalment of the James Bond franchise. Steven Knight has also been brought on to write the screenplay.
Amazon MGM Studios assumed creative control of the franchise earlier this year, making the selection of the next 007 a key step in developing the upcoming film.
While the reported contenders have generated interest among fans, the identity of the next James Bond remains unconfirmed. The final screen tests are expected to bring the lengthy casting search closer to a conclusion.

title: Nobody Wants This  season 3 shocks fans as Joanne and Noah get married
description: Nobody Wants This season  3 sees Joanne and Noah get engaged and marry in a surprise beach ceremony on the beach
content:
'Nobody Wants This season' 3 sees Joanne and Noah get engaged and marry in a surprise beach ceremony on the beach
Nobody Wants This season 3 takes Joanne and Noah’s relationship to a new level, with the couple getting engaged and married in the latest instalment of the Netflix romantic comedy series.
Starring Kristen Bell as Joanne and Adam Brody as Noah, the third season premiered on Netflix on October 22, 2026. The new episodes follow the couple as they navigate their relationship, beginning with the decision to move in together before making two major commitments.
In episode four, Noah plans a surprise proposal for Joanne by arranging a fake friend’s wedding in Napa. Despite several mishaps during their trip, the plan eventually succeeds when Noah gets down on one knee and asks Joanne to marry him.
“You are not what I saw coming, because I never realized how good I could have it,” Noah tells her. He adds that meeting Joanne has changed him and that he wants to spend his life with her.
Joanne accepts the proposal, with the arrival of her sister Morgan, played by Justine Lupe, and Noah’s brother Sasha, played by Timothy Simons, adding to the moment.
The couple’s wedding takes place in episode 10, following Joanne’s conversion to Judaism. Noah is moved by the occasion and decides to marry her in an impromptu beach ceremony with Rabbi Eden, portrayed by Sarah Silverman, officiating.
Although Noah makes the decision without discussing it with Joanne beforehand, she agrees to go ahead with the ceremony. Noah also finds a stranger on the beach to serve as their witness.
Joanne reflects on how their past experiences and failed dates ultimately led them to one another, while Noah tells her he had been waiting for her.
The season finale ends as Rabbi Eden begins the marriage ceremony, with the couple’s families still unaware of what is happening at the beach house.
All episodes of Nobody Wants This season 3 are now streaming on Netflix.

title: Carrie Anne Moss says Marvel did not ask her to return for    Daredevil  Born Again    season 3
description: Moss played attorney Jeri Hogarth in  Jessica Jones   appearing across the series    three seasons between 2015 and 2019
content:
Moss played attorney Jeri Hogarth in 'Jessica Jones', appearing across the series’ three seasons between 2015 and 2019
Carrie-Anne Moss has revealed that Marvel Studios did not ask her to reprise her role as Jeri Hogarth in the third and final season of Daredevil: Born Again , despite several stars from Marvel’s former Netflix series returning for the Disney+ show.
In an exclusive interview with Entertainment Weekly , Moss confirmed that she would not appear in the upcoming season, which is scheduled to arrive in 2027. Asked whether Marvel had contacted her about returning, the actress gave a brief response: “No.”
Moss played attorney Jeri Hogarth in Jessica Jones , appearing across the series’ three seasons between 2015 and 2019. She later reprised the character in Daredevil season two and Iron Fist , before joining the superhero crossover miniseries The Defenders in 2017.
Her character was among the notable figures from Marvel’s Netflix era who did not return for Daredevil: Born Again . The Disney+ series has gradually reunited several familiar faces, with Charlie Cox returning as Matt Murdock, while Krysten Ritter, Mike Colter and Finn Jones are also reprising their respective roles as Jessica Jones, Luke Cage and Iron Fist.
Although Moss will not be part of the reunion, she is working towards another collaboration with Ritter, her close friend and former co-star. The pair are developing Claire , a creature horror-thriller in which Ritter plays a single mother battling addiction when a malevolent entity that feeds on despair begins terrorising her and her two sons.
“Krysten Ritter and I are like besties,” Moss told Entertainment Weekly . “So we're always trying to think of things to do together.”
The actress added that the two regularly discuss potential projects, saying they have “a million ideas” and describing Ritter as “such a dear friend of mine”.
Moss’s latest comments come as Daredevil: Born Again prepares to conclude with its third season. The announcement that the series would end in 2027 disappointed fans, particularly those hoping to see more of the interconnected characters introduced through Marvel’s earlier Netflix shows.
At a New York Comic Con panel, Cox acknowledged the possibility of renewed fan campaigning to save the series. The actor joked about the “Save Daredevil” campaign and the response it could generate following the cancellation announcement.
While Moss will not be returning to the Marvel series, she remains active in television and film. She stars in Yaga , a detective thriller inspired by the Slavic folklore figure Baba Yaga, playing university professor Katherine Hargrove in the mystery set in the fictional coastal town of Whittock.
With Daredevil: Born Again approaching its final season, Moss’s absence means Jeri Hogarth will not be part of the show's concluding chapter, even as other characters from the Netflix-era Marvel universe return to the screen.

title: WAPDA win six gold medals on opening day of National Athletics Championships
description: Shajar Abbas claims the men s 100 metre title in 10 20 seconds
content:
Shajar Abbas claims the men's 100-metre title in 10.20 seconds
Pakistan WAPDA dominated the opening day of the Lok Sahaaita 54th National Athletics Championships 2026, winning six of the seven gold medals on offer.
National record-holder Shajar Abbas claimed the men's 100-metre title in 10.20 seconds to be crowned Pakistan's fastest man. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Attaullah finished second, while HEC's Haseeb took bronze.
WAPDA's Faiqa Riaz won the women's 100 metres in 11.56 seconds to earn the fastest woman title. HEC's Hawla secured silver, while Sindh's Iqra Riaz claimed bronze.
Sindh's Mah Noor Fatima won the championship's first gold medal in the women's 5,000-metre race walk, clocking 32 minutes 32.40 seconds. WAPDA's Amara Munawar took silver, while Punjab's Saira finished third.
WAPDA's Muhammad Waqas claimed gold in the men's 20-kilometre race walk. Pakistan Navy's Muhammad Younis Khan won silver, while WAPDA's Muhammad Gulfam secured bronze.
HEC's Khadija Mehreen, representing Superior University Lahore, won the women's shot put with a throw of 10.85 metres. WAPDA's Samia Sahar and Amna Ashiq finished second and third, respectively.
WAPDA continued their dominance in the middle-distance events, with Nazia Ehsan winning the women's 1,500 metres in 5:09.78. HEC's Gonash Batool took silver, while teammate Javeria Bibi claimed bronze.
Sohail Amir secured WAPDA's gold in the men's 1,500 metres. HEC's Abdul Wahab finished second, while WAPDA's Muhammad Akram took third.
The opening day's results underlined WAPDA's strength across sprinting, race walking, throwing and middle-distance running.

title: Asim Khan reaches quarter finals of ABC Open squash championship
description: Pakistan   s eighth seed beats Malaysia   s Shafiq Kamal 3 1 as other local players exit
content:
Pakistan’s eighth seed beats Malaysia’s Shafiq Kamal 3-1 as other local players exit
Pakistan’s seasoned player Asim Khan on Thursday reached the quarter-finals of the Venice ABC Open International Squash Championship after defeating Malaysia’s Shafiq Kamal 3-1 in the second round.
The eighth-seeded Khan secured a 11-2, 10-12, 11-7, 11-6 victory in 48 minutes at the Asif Nawaz Squash Complex at the Defence Authority Creek Club in Karachi.
Khan’s progress offered a bright spot for the hosts after all nine Pakistani players competing on the opening day of the tournament were eliminated.
In other matches, Egypt’s Ziad Ibrahim beat compatriot Yassin El-Shafei, while top seed Curtis Malik of Egypt defeated Japan’s Naoki Hayashi.
Egypt’s fourth seed Yassin Shoedey overcame Hong Kong’s Matthew Lai, and fifth seed Perry Malik beat Canada’s Salah Eltorgman.
In the women’s competition, England’s top seed Lucy Turmel defeated Germany’s Maya Weishar, while Malaysia’s Ainaa Amani beat Egypt’s Habiba Rizk. Egypt’s Fathy defeated compatriot Rawan Elaraby.
The Netherlands’ Tessa ter Sluis also recorded a victory over Hong Kong’s Toby Tse.
The tournament, organised by the Sindh Squash Association, offers a total prize purse of $82,000, with the finals scheduled for Sunday.

title: Amanda Seyfried confirms she will return for  Jennifer   s Body  sequel
description: Amanda Seyfried has confirmed she will join  Jennifer   s Body  sequel next year  alongside returning creative team
content:
Amanda Seyfried has confirmed she will join 'Jennifer’s Body' sequel next year, alongside returning creative team
Amanda Seyfried has confirmed her involvement in the upcoming Jennifer’s Body sequel, revealing that the follow-up to the 2009 comedy horror film is on her schedule for next year.
In an interview with WWD published on Wednesday, the Mean Girls actress said she was looking forward to reuniting with the original film’s creative team.
Her confirmation follows recent comments from screenwriter Diablo Cody, who said the sequel was moving towards production.
“The Jennifer's Body sequel is definitely on my calendar for next year because I love that team,” Seyfried said. “It was such a special experience, and I think we have a good shot at making something just as special.”
The original film starred Megan Fox as Jennifer, a high school student possessed by a demon who begins killing her classmates, while Seyfried played her best friend, Needy.
Although the film was a commercial failure on its initial release, it has since developed a cult following.
Earlier this month, Cody revealed during an appearance on the Petticoat Revolution podcast that the sequel was happening imminently. She also discussed the opportunity to explore Jennifer’s character in greater depth.
“One fun thing - I can't talk about it too much - but you know we're doing a sequel to this movie, like imminently, and I felt like in the new movie, I was able to explore even more about why Jennifer is sympathetic and what she's been through,” Cody said.
She added, “And there is absolutely, to me, a loneliness and a poignancy to that character that people don't always recognise.”
Filming is reportedly set to take place in Vancouver, Canada, with Seyfried and Fox expected to star.
Original director Karyn Kusama was also named alongside Cody. However, those details were never officially confirmed, as Seyfried’s latest comments suggest production is now planned for next year.

title: Eric Dane opens up about ALS battle  addiction and family in posthumous memoir
description: Dane died on February 19  2026  at the age of 53  following his battle with ALS
content:
Dane died on February 19, 2026, at the age of 53, following his battle with ALS
Eric Dane is sharing deeply personal details about his battle with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), his struggles with addiction and his relationship with his family in a memoir written before his death at 53.
The late Grey’s Anatomy and Euphoria actor’s book, My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments , offers an intimate account of his life, including his rise to fame, his recovery struggles and the progressive illness that ultimately claimed his life. An exclusive excerpt published by PEOPLE reveals how Dane wanted to document his experiences for his daughters, Billie, 16, and Georgia, 14.
Dane first noticed something was wrong on January 7, 2024, while eating sushi with his children. He struggled to hold chopsticks with his right hand as his fingers became numb. Initially dismissing the symptoms, he later experienced the same problem more severely. After months of seeking medical answers, he received an ALS diagnosis in April 2025.
In the memoir, Dane recounts calling his estranged wife, actress Rebecca Gayheart, after learning the diagnosis. The couple had filed for divorce in 2018 following 14 years of marriage but remained close and continued raising their daughters together.
Dane recalled Gayheart breaking down in tears when he told her the news. Despite their separation, she immediately reassured him that she would stand by him throughout the illness. He described her as his closest friend and someone who remained available whenever he needed support.
The actor also revisited his long struggle with substance addiction, including a relapse during his time on Grey’s Anatomy . Dane joined the medical drama in 2005 and became widely recognised as Dr Mark Sloan, nicknamed McSteamy. However, his growing dependence on drugs, particularly painkillers, affected his personal life and work.
Dane revealed that he went to rehabilitation five times during his tenure on the series. He also recalled how creator Shonda Rhimes approached him on multiple occasions to offer support when his struggles became apparent to those around him.
His departure from Grey’s Anatomy in 2012 was another subject he addressed in the memoir. While acknowledging that his addiction had not helped his circumstances, Dane said he believed financial considerations ultimately led to his character's exit. He wrote that, despite Mark Sloan's popularity, he had become too expensive for the show.
Beyond his career and addiction, Dane's memoir reflects on the importance of fatherhood and the family he maintained with Gayheart. Although their marriage had ended, the pair continued to co-parent their daughters and remained closely connected. His ALS diagnosis brought them together during an especially difficult period, as his condition progressively affected his physical abilities.
Dane died on February 19, 2026, at the age of 53, following his battle with ALS. His family said he spent his final days surrounded by loved ones, including Gayheart and their daughters.
My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments is scheduled for publication on November 3, 2026. Through the book, Dane leaves behind a personal account of his life, his struggles and the relationships that mattered most to him, offering his daughters and readers a deeper understanding of the man beyond his celebrated television roles.

title: Mod Sun pays emotional tribute to late ex girlfriend Sahara Ray   She was a true love of mine
description: Ray died on October 18 and her family said she had passed away at a hospital surrounded by loved ones
content:
Ray died on October 18 and her family said she had passed away at a hospital surrounded by loved ones
Mod Sun has paid tribute to his late ex-girlfriend Sahara Ray following the model and swimwear designer’s death at the age of 34, remembering her as “pure magic” and “a true love of mine”.
The musician, whose real name is Derek Ryan Smith, shared an emotional Instagram Reel on Wednesday, October 21, featuring a video of Ray interacting with a monarch butterfly. In the clip, the butterfly lands on her hand as she gently moves it towards her nose and back to her fingers.
“This is who Sahara was in this world,” Mod Sun wrote alongside the video. “Pure magic. She could turn any moment into art. She walked into a room + all the sudden it was vibrant.”
The singer, known for songs including Flames , also reflected on the special connection he shared with Ray, revealing that they had the same birthday. He said the coincidence made him feel as though they were “sharing the same soul somehow”.
Mod Sun described Ray as “everyone’s muse” and said he had always called her the “ETERNAL IT GIRL”. Reflecting on their relationship, he added: “When I was with her it was the most free I ever felt. She was my inspiration before, during, + long after we dated. She was a true love of mine.”
He continued by describing Ray as someone who saw life differently, adding that he believed she was “just too special for this world”.
“Everyone knew she was a magical fairy,” he wrote, ending his tribute by saying he would always love her and asking her to “save a spot for me in the forest”.
Ray and Mod Sun dated in 2023, following his split from Avril Lavigne. Although their relationship ended, his tribute made clear that she continued to hold a special place in his life.
Ray died on October 18 in Los Angeles, her family confirmed. She was 34. In a statement shared with TMZ, her family said she had passed away at a hospital surrounded by loved ones. Her official cause of death has not been confirmed.
The model had welcomed her daughter, Snow, in January, sharing glimpses of her early months as a mother on social media. Her death came less than a year after the birth of her first child.
Ray was also known for her work as a model and for founding her swimwear brand, Sahara Ray Swim, in 2014. She previously attracted public attention through reported links to Justin Bieber and Cody Simpson.
In the days following her death, Ray’s family and friends have shared tributes celebrating her personality, creativity and the impact she had on those around her. title: Sylvester Stallone defends AI in filmmaking and says technology is    here to stay
description: The actor admits critics have a moral point but argues the technology cannot be stopped
content:
The actor admits critics have a moral point but argues the technology cannot be stopped
Sylvester Stallone has defended the growing use of artificial intelligence in filmmaking, arguing that the technology is advancing too quickly to be stopped despite concerns from creative professionals.
During an appearance on The Overlap , the Rocky and Rambo star described himself as a major risk taker when discussing the future of AI. Asked by former footballer Roy Keane whether he takes risks, Stallone replied that he does, although he does not consider himself a gambler.
He then raised the prospect of combining human performances with AI, saying, “AI is here to stay, and I wanted to do half-human, half-AI, and put it together.”
Stallone acknowledged that the idea had attracted strong criticism from the creative community. However, he argued that the technology was already developing in ways that would make it difficult to reverse.
“People are now selling their images, and eventually, there are 20 Elvis avatars,” he said, suggesting that digitally recreated versions of famous performers could become increasingly common.
Although Stallone recognised the moral concerns surrounding AI, he maintained that the industry would have to confront its growing influence. “We can’t stop this avalanche, it’s out of our control,” he said, adding that those who refused to engage with the technology risked being left behind.
His comments follow an earlier proposal involving the Rambo franchise. Stallone reportedly pitched a prequel concept that would have used AI de-ageing technology to portray a younger version of John Rambo, allowing him to revisit the character at 18.
The project ultimately moved forward with Noah Centineo cast as the younger Rambo, rather than Stallone returning as the lead.
AI use in film has continued to generate debate in Hollywood, particularly over creative ownership, performers’ likenesses and the potential impact on filmmaking jobs. Director Eli Roth also faced criticism after acknowledging that generative AI had been used in a small portion of scenes in Ice Cream Man , following earlier comments that had suggested otherwise.
Stallone’s remarks highlight the continuing divide between those who see AI as an inevitable industry tool and those concerned about its ethical and creative consequences.

title: J  K  Rowling adds to her divisive views on transgender identity

content:
J. K. Rowling has reaffirmed her views on transgender issues in update to her 2020 essay
J. K. Rowling has said her views on transgender issues have not changed in six years, reaffirming her position in an update to an essay she published in June 2020.
The Harry Potter author addressed criticism and death threats she says she has received over her opposition to what she describes as trans activism.
On Wednesday, October 21, Rowling published an update to her original essay on her personal website, defending her decision to speak publicly about what she believes are risks to women's rights.
"What to me represents no change at all in my political or ideological outlook has, in recent years, seen me and women like me subject not only to criticism but also to death threats," she wrote.
Rowling argued that the effects of trans activism differ depending on a woman's circumstances, claiming that more privileged women are less likely to experience its consequences.
She also criticised women in media, publishing and academia who support prevailing trans activism positions, arguing that working-class women may face different concerns about access to women's changing rooms.
The British author also addressed the rights and safety of transgender people, stating that she did not believe they should be "stripped of their human rights or denied personal safety".
She said she would continue supporting women who could not otherwise afford legal action and helping ensure access to support services for women who have experienced rape.
"I'll continue to speak out, continue to use my money to help women who otherwise couldn't afford to go to court, and continue to ensure that women in my area can still access female-delivered, female-centred support after rape," Rowling wrote.
Her comments have drawn criticism from people who consider her views transphobic. The stars of the original Harry Potter films, including Daniel Radcliffe and Emma Watson, have previously publicly disagreed with her position.

title: Jenna Ortega opens up about OCD  describing childhood routines  counting habits and experience with therapy

content:
The 'Wednesday' actress shared details of her routines and ongoing journey in an interview with Vogue
Jenna Ortega has opened up about her experience with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), revealing that she began showing signs of the condition at the age of seven.
The Wednesday actress shared details of her routines and ongoing journey in an interview with Vogue .
Ortega recalled waking up early as a child to complete a series of specific tasks before starting her day.
“I had to open the bedsheet a certain way, and open the drawer one way, and brush my hair in a slow-paced way,” she explained.
The actress said some of these behaviours can still return when she feels stressed or overwhelmed. “I just bite the bullet and do the routine,” she said.
Discussing her current habits, Ortega described repeating particular words and following specific patterns when she feels anxious, tired or jet-lagged.
These include “repeating the phrase ‘take care’ a specific number of times throughout the day; stepping onto set with her left foot first; holding her breath and counting to 71.”
Ortega also revealed that she has attended therapy, continues to work with a therapist and has tried medication as part of managing her OCD.
One approach that has helped ease some of the pressure, she explained, is viewing the experience as a game.
According to the Mayo Clinic, OCD involves unwanted, recurring thoughts known as obsessions and repetitive behaviours called compulsions, which can cause distress and interfere with daily activities.
Ortega’s candid account offers insight into her personal experience with the condition while highlighting the different ways people seek support and manage their symptoms.

title: Tom Cruise to be honoured at Dolby Theatre with prestigious AFI award

The actor’s films have earned nearly $13bn at the worldwide box office
Tom Cruise will receive the American Film Institute’s 52nd AFI Life Achievement Award, with the Hollywood star set to be honoured at a gala ceremony in Los Angeles on April 24, 2027.
The AFI Board of Trustees announced the decision on October 21, describing the distinction as the highest honour for a career in film. The tribute will take place at the Dolby Theatre, recognising Cruise’s decades of work as an actor and producer.
“Tom Cruise is a global icon,” said Kathleen Kennedy, chair of the AFI Board of Trustees. She praised his commitment to filmmaking and his belief in cinema’s ability to bring people together, adding that his work has made him an ambassador for American film around the world.
Cruise, a three time Oscar nominee, has built a career spanning several decades, with credits including Risky Business , Top Gun , Jerry Maguire , A Few Good Men and the Mission: Impossible franchise. His films have collectively earned nearly $13bn worldwide, according to the announcement reported by Deadline .
The actor currently stars in Digger , directed by Alejandro González Iñárritu. The film has attracted considerable attention and divided audience opinion.
Cruise has also received several major honours throughout his career. In 2025, he received an honorary Oscar at the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences’ Governors Awards. Other recognitions include honours from the Cannes Film Festival, the Producers Guild of America and France’s Legion of Honour.
The AFI Life Achievement Award has a long history of recognising influential figures in cinema. First presented in 1973 to director John Ford, it has subsequently honoured performers and filmmakers including Bette Davis, Gregory Peck, Meryl Streep and Francis Ford Coppola.
Recent recipients include Eddie Murphy, Nicole Kidman, Julie Andrews, Denzel Washington, George Clooney and Diane Keaton.
Cruise’s upcoming tribute will add his name to that distinguished list, celebrating his lasting contribution to the film industry as both a leading performer and a producer.

British actress Judi Dench said her eyesight had deteriorated to the point that she could no longer ​act on stage or in films.
Dench, 91, has had ‌macular degeneration for more than a decade

Reflecting on her career, Dench ​said she ⁠had taken risks in choosing roles, adding that performing was always a daunting experience.
"For me, always frightening, but that's part ⁠of it," ​she said. "It's part of what that ​fear generates, an energy that you can use up, use the energy." "It's always 'work ​in progress', always."

“We still cannot know in what capacity AI was used in the creation of It was either that or die , and undoubtedly we will never have a definitive answer,” Boreal said in a statement.
“After the allegations, we continued to trust Orelien, who assured us he had never used such tools. This assertion has now been proven false,” Boreal added.

title: Samson stars as India mark record T20 chase
description: Opener scores a 33 ball 67 against New Zealand
content:
Opener scores a 33-ball 67 against New Zealand
Belligerent batting by Sanju Samson saw India chase 226 for victory against New Zealand in Christchurch on Thursday in a rematch of the T20 World Cup final.
Opener Samson made 67 from 33 balls as India chased down their highest-ever T20 total and secured a four-wicket win with two balls remaining.
India take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.
Samson and opening partner Abhishek Sharma belted 93 runs between them in the powerplay, obliterating New Zealand's highly regarded seam attack.
Black Caps captain Mitchell Santner put the handbrake on India's runaway start, bowling three miserly overs through the middle stages in tandem with fellow spinner Michael Bracewell, the pair snaring four wickets in five overs.
But India captain Shreyas Iyer was a calming presence after Samson fell, chopping on from Santner, finding the boundary when needed to keep the chase manageable.
He departed for 42 from 28 balls in the second to last over.
Naman Dhir saw India home with 42 from just 15 balls.
India won the toss and chose to bowl, seeking to seize on late evening dew during the chase rather than any life in the Hagley Oval pitch.
Finn Allen and Tim Seifert made what then seemed to be a fast start, New Zealand reaching 65-1 at the end of the powerplay.
India would reach the same mark inside four overs during the chase.
Allen hit five fours and two sixes on his way to 45 from 24 balls, out to Axar Patel in the eighth over when trying to hoist the spinner over long-off.
That brought Glenn Phillips to the crease, initially dove-tailing well with Daryl Mitchell in forcing India's bowlers into different lengths.
Where Phillips was brilliant cutting and pulling the seamers, Mitchell was strong down the ground driving the fuller deliveries.
Mitchell was dropped by Abhishek on 16 but fell soon after for 28 top-edging Arshdeep Singh.
Bevon Jacobs hit a 96m six clean out of the Hagley Oval with his first ball faced as he raced to a 16-ball 31.
But it was Phillips (82 not out) who piled on the most pressure, his running between the wickets pressuring fielders to step in off the boundary, before powering his shots past them to the boundary.
The second match of the series is also in Christchurch, on Saturday.

Julia Stiles sought Michelle Williams’ approval before paying tribute to her late friend and co-star Heath Ledger during an emotional performance on Dancing With the Stars .
The actress honoured Ledger through a dance set to Frankie Valli’s “I Can’t Take My Eyes Off of You”, recreating a memorable moment from their 1999 romantic comedy 10 Things I Hate About You . Speaking to Extra after the performance, Stiles confirmed that she had contacted Williams, Ledger’s former partner, before going ahead with the tribute.
“I did ask Michelle if this was OK, and she said yes,” Stiles said.
Williams and Ledger were in a relationship from 2004 to 2007 and share a daughter, Matilda. Stiles declined to speculate about how Ledger’s family might feel about the performance, explaining that she did not want to speak on their behalf.
The tribute also brought together several members of the original film’s cast on the Dancing With the Stars stage. Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Larisa Oleynik, Gabrielle Union, Susan May Pratt and Andrew Keegan joined Stiles for the reunion, celebrating the enduring popularity of the teen comedy.
However, David Krumholtz, who played Michael in the film, was notably absent. He addressed his absence in a video posted on Instagram, explaining that he was in upstate New York filming a movie and could not travel to Los Angeles for the event.
Krumholtz said he would have loved to attend and praised the reunion, describing Stiles’ tribute to Ledger as “amazing and stunning”. He also expressed how much he continued to miss his late friend.
Stiles responded warmly in the comments, writing, “We love you Krumholtz!”
Speaking to Variety after the performance, Stiles said she had personally encouraged every cast member to take part. She also reflected on the unexpected experience of returning to a film that continues to resonate with audiences decades after its release.

title: Foden can be one of EPL s best again  says Maresca
description: Englishman ends his goal drought in City s 3 2 win over Ipswich
content:
Englishman ends his goal drought in City's 3-2 win over Ipswich
Enzo Maresca said it is his job as Manchester City boss to help Phil Foden rediscover his best form after the England international ended his long goal drought. Foden had not scored for 10 months before netting in City's 3-2 win over Ipswich last weekend and then scored a Champions League hat-trick in a 5-1 rout of AEK Athens on Tuesday. The 26-year-old swept the board of personal awards for the Premier League's best player in the 2023/24 season after a 27-goal campaign. But Foden, who has admitted struggling with mental health issues, has failed to hit top form for the past two seasons. "Since we started I sat down with Phil two or three times, especially at the beginning. Just to show him, I don't know if love is the right word to use, but just to show him how important he is," said Maresca, who took charge of City in June. "I said many times that I know Phil from years ago so I know how for different reasons, the last few years it was not good enough. "When you have more players like Phil available, you are a better team because again it's a matter of improving players. If you improve the players, you improve the team. "So for me, I think it's my duty to try to help Phil to be again one of the best players in England." Other than a 4-2 Champions League defeat to holders Paris Saint-Germain, Maresca has made a flawless start to the daunting task of succeeding Pep Guardiola at the Etihad Stadium. The Italian is the first manager ever to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club. However, City's fine form has been overshadowed by the threat of severe sanctions against the club for widespread flouting of Premier League financial rules. A large points deduction, which could lead to relegation, is likely unless City win an appeal against a guilty verdict on more than 100 charges of wrongdoing. Maresca said the mood in the dressing room remained buoyant despite the cloud hanging over the club. "In any club, when you lose important players, many important players, and you lose the manager after 10 years, it always takes time to compete again," he said on Thursday. "But this organisation last summer changed many important players, changed the manager after 10 years and we are competing at the moment." City travel to Aston Villa on Saturday, boosted by the return of Erling Haaland. The Norwegian, who has scored 12 times in nine appearances this season, missed the AEK Athens match after picking up a foot injury against Ipswich. Matheus Nunes, Mateo Kovacic and Nico O'Reilly remain injury doubts.

title: Clayface    earns 75  Rotten Tomatoes score as DC horror film divides critics
description: Tom Rhys Harries stars as Matt Hagen  whose experimental treatment triggers a terrifying transformation
content:
Tom Rhys Harries stars as Matt Hagen, whose experimental treatment triggers a terrifying transformation
DC Studios’ Clayface has received a mostly positive early response from critics, earning a 75% score on Rotten Tomatoes from 83 reviews following the lifting of its review embargo on October 21, 2026.
Directed by James Watkins, the horror thriller is the third feature film released under James Gunn and Peter Safran’s DC Universe, following Superman and Supergirl . Its early critical score places it between the two earlier releases, with Superman holding an 83% rating and Supergirl at 52%, according to the figures reported by Forbes .
The film follows Matt Hagen, played by Tom Rhys Harries, a young man from Gotham who rises to Hollywood stardom before a violent encounter with a crime boss leaves his face disfigured. Seeking a way to repair the damage, Hagen turns to scientist Caitlyn Corr, portrayed by Naomi Ackie, for an experimental treatment. However, the procedure brings disturbing side effects and sends him towards a violent path of revenge.
Several critics have praised the film for embracing horror and exploring a lesser known character from DC Comics. Variety critic Guy Lodge described the film as an enjoyable genre experiment, while reviews highlighted its gruesome imagery and willingness to pursue a darker direction.
Other critics have been less impressed. IndieWire critic Kate Erbland criticised the film’s uneven plotting, character motivations and overall execution. Barry Hertz of The Globe and Mail also raised concerns about its lack of self-awareness and apparent borrowing from other films.
Reviews have therefore offered contrasting assessments of whether Clayface successfully balances its horror elements with the demands of a superhero franchise.
The character first appeared in DC Comics in 1940 as Basil Karlo, while the Matt Hagen version debuted in 1961. The film brings a new interpretation of the villain to the big screen, with Harries leading a cast that also includes David Dencik, Max Minghella, Nancy Carroll, Joshua James and Eddie Marsan.
Clayface is scheduled for preview screenings on October 22 before its nationwide theatrical release on October 23. Its Rotten Tomatoes score may change as additional reviews are published.

title: Carrie Anne Moss reflects on    The Matrix     motherhood and AI concerns ahead of    Yaga    premiere
description: Moss said using AI in her own writing can make her feel as though part of her creativity switches off
content:
Moss said using AI in her own writing can make her feel as though part of her creativity switches off
Carrie-Anne Moss is reflecting on her journey from Vancouver to Hollywood, her experience raising her children and her concerns about artificial intelligence as she prepares to star in the new mystery-thriller series Yaga .
In an interview with CBC News, the Canadian actress discussed returning to British Columbia to film the series, which draws inspiration from the Slavic folklore figure Baba Yaga. Moss plays Katherine Hargrove, a university professor who becomes connected to a mysterious disappearance in the fictional coastal town of Whittock.
Moss said the opportunity came at a meaningful moment, as she had recently opened Women Who Run with the Wolves: Myths and Stories of the Wild Woman Archetype , a book that explores myths and stories about women. The timing helped draw her towards the project, alongside the script and conversations with creator Kat Sandler.
The actress, who grew up in Burnaby, British Columbia, recalled discovering her passion for performing at an early age. She attended school plays, watched television with an emotional investment in the stories and found opportunities to perform through singing and writing plays and musicals.
Her career reached a major turning point when she was cast as Trinity in The Matrix . The role made her internationally recognised and remains one of her most celebrated performances. Moss also reflected on how difficult it was to watch herself on screen initially, explaining that it took several viewings before she could appreciate the film beyond her own performance.
Despite her success in Hollywood, Moss said motherhood became a central priority. She stepped away from acting at different points to raise her children, describing the experience as something she valued deeply. She and her family eventually left Los Angeles for a quieter life in New Hampshire, where she could enjoy a different pace away from the entertainment industry's demands.
However, stepping back from Hollywood has not ended her creative ambitions. Moss also shared concerns about artificial intelligence and its potential impact on artists and storytelling. She said using AI in her own writing can make her feel as though part of her creativity switches off, expressing reservations about technology that could diminish the human element of creative work.
For Moss, storytelling remains important because of its ability to build empathy and connection. Her concerns reflect wider questions about how AI may reshape creative industries and what could be lost if technology begins to replace human imagination and expression.
With Yaga , Moss returns to a project rooted in folklore and mystery, starring alongside Noah Reid, Clark Backo and Hudson Williams, known for Heated Rivalry . The eight-episode series is scheduled to premiere on AMC+ and Crave on October 23, bringing Moss back to British Columbia for a story that combines a contemporary investigation with the unsettling mythology of Baba Yaga.

title: Jacob Elordi emerges as James Bond favourite amid fresh 007 casting rumours
description: Producer Amy Pascal says the next 007 should bring something different and exciting to the franchise
content:
Producer Amy Pascal says the next 007 should bring something different and exciting to the franchise
Jacob Elordi has re-emerged as a potential frontrunner to play James Bond, with fresh reports suggesting the Australian actor could be in contention to become the next 007.
Speculation surrounding the role has intensified in recent weeks, with British actors Jack Lowden and Jack Barton also linked to the coveted part. However, entertainment journalist Jeff Sneider has reportedly claimed that the screen testing process is complete and that Elordi is now expected to land the role.
According to HuffPost UK , Sneider shared the claims in his entertainment newsletter, The InSneider, and suggested an announcement could arrive soon. These reports remain unconfirmed, and neither Elordi nor Amazon MGM has publicly confirmed the casting.
Elordi first gained widespread attention through The Kissing Booth film series before earning recognition for his role as Nate Jacobs in Euphoria . His subsequent film work has included Saltburn and Frankenstein , while his growing profile has made him a recurring name in discussions about major Hollywood roles.
Earlier reports had also linked Callum Turner and Paul Mescal to the Bond casting process, alongside Harris Dickinson. The shifting list of potential candidates suggests that speculation about Daniel Craig’s successor remains unsettled.
The next instalment in the official James Bond film series will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, known for Dune and Blade Runner 2049 . Steven Knight, the creator of Peaky Blinders , is attached to write the screenplay.
Producer Amy Pascal has previously indicated that the creative team wants a fresh direction for the iconic spy, describing their ambition as finding someone “stirring and exciting and different”.
Until Amazon MGM or the filmmakers make an official announcement, the identity of the next James Bond remains unknown.

title: CDF Munir meets senior Iranian officials as Pakistan continues diplomatic push to end conflict
description: Iran warns any US attack will be met with retaliation  dismisses claims of no response deal
content:
US-Iran negotiations ongoing as regional tensions mount: Qatari official
Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir on Tuesday met senior Iranian officials as Pakistan continued its diplomatic push to end the US-Iran conflict.
Pakistan is a ​key mediator between the US and ⁠Iran. Its earlier mediation efforts with ​both parties resulted in an interim peace agreement ​signed in June. But the Islamabad Memorandum quickly faltered, amid new fighting between Iran and ​the US weeks after.
According to Tehran Times , Field Marshal Munir met Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian and Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council Mohsin Rezaei during his visit.
Field Marshal Munir and Iranian President Pezeshkian discussed mediation efforts and regional developments, Iran’s Nournews reported.
During a meeting with CDF Munir, Major General Rezaei said Iran would not transfer any of its enriched nuclear material abroad.
“Not even the slightest amount of enriched nuclear material will be taken out of Iran,” Rezaei said, describing the material as a major asset and a national treasure of the Iranian people, intended for use within the country.
He said the Iranian people and officials were united in their position that negotiations would not take place until the United States took steps to build trust.
“The first step towards building that trust is for the United States to fulfil Iran’s conditions,” he said, while emphasising the close ties between the peoples of Iran and Pakistan.
Field Marshal Munir also met Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf to discuss the conflict between Iran and the United States.
During the meeting in Tehran, Ghalibaf said Washington could not win Tehran’s trust unless it implemented the seven conditions Iran had presented in New York. He added that Iran had nothing new to say on the matter.
Earlier, Iranian media reported that CDF Munir arrived in Tehran on Tuesday with a delegation of officials to meet senior Iranian officials, according to Mehr News Agency.
According to Tasnim News Agency , he was scheduled to meet Iranian officials to discuss diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict between Iran and the US, as well as broader regional developments.
US-Iran negotiations ongoing as regional tensions mount: Qatari official
Negotiations between Iran and the US remain ongoing, with both sides continuing to engage as regional tensions deepen, Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari said on Tuesday.
“The negotiation is ongoing. We are seeing engagement from the parties,” Ansari, who also serves as an adviser to the Qatari prime minister, said at the Global Security Forum in Doha.
He said discussions were taking place with regional partners and expressed hope that the process would eventually produce an agreement, while warning that conditions on the ground were becoming increasingly difficult.
“Escalation left unchecked will mean that we are spiraling towards a regional war that will expand beyond the borders of our region,” he warned.
Ansari said the current process followed an earlier attempt to use a ceasefire as a pathway toward negotiations, but that effort ultimately failed and fighting resumed.
“Any ceasefire is basically a door that opens towards a destination rather than the destination itself,” he said, adding that the previous ceasefire “broke down again.”
On Yemen, Ansari said the conflict could be linked to tensions involving Iran but also had its own dynamics, describing the latest developments as part of an “escalatory ladder” that began in 2023.
“The only way to make sure that doesn't continue is to start defusing all of these conflicts at the same time,” he said.
The spokesman voiced concern over political statements coming from Israel, saying regional instability should not be used for domestic political purposes.
“We are concerned about a lot of the statements coming out, political statements that are coming out, especially from Israel,” he said, adding that exploiting regional instability for political infighting was “not something that any responsible statesman should do.”
Turning to Gaza and the broader Palestinian question, Ansari said prospects for a political settlement were being undermined by the absence of a viable peace process.
“Sadly, right now we do not have a partner for peace in Israel,” he said, questioning whether Israeli political parties and candidates were offering any path toward peace with Palestinians.
“The only thing that we hear coming out of Israel right now is about war and death and destruction,” he said, warning that “war begets war, conflict begets conflict.”
Since October 2023, Israel has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians and injured over 175,000 others during its war on Gaza, while around 90% of the enclave's civilian infrastructure has been damaged or destroyed.
Ansari said successful mediation did not require the parties to trust one another, but rather to have confidence in the process itself.
“It is trust in the process, not trust in each other, that allows for mediation to succeed,” he said.
Iran warns any US attack will be met with retaliation, dismisses claims of no-response deal
Iran warned on Tuesday that any US military attack would be met with retaliation, dismissing claims that Washington had conveyed a message expecting Tehran not to respond to a potential strike.
Speaking at his weekly press conference, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei described suggestions that the US could attack Iran without facing retaliation as an “illusion.”
Baghaei rejected claims that Washington had sent a message based on the premise that Iran should refrain from responding to a potential US attack.
He said Tehran had demonstrated that it would not leave any military strike unanswered. “If our response is not stronger, it will certainly be equal in force,” he said.
The spokesperson stressed that the era of the US carrying out attacks and withdrawing without consequences was over.
His remarks came in response to claims concerning a possible US attack on Pickaxe Mountain in Iran.
Baghaei said Tehran had not entered nuclear negotiations with Washington and therefore had no details of such talks to discuss with Russia or other countries. “We have not entered nuclear negotiations with the American side to discuss their details with other parties,” he said.
He rejected speculations that Iran had softened its positions on the nuclear issue, stressing that Tehran remained committed to its principles and national interests. The spokesperson said Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s visit to Tehran was part of regular consultations between the two countries.
He noted that the visit had been planned for months and was aimed at discussing bilateral relations and regional and international developments. According to Baghaei, discussions covered the Caucasus, Europe, the Ukraine conflict, the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, as well as Iran’s nuclear program.
He said Russia had played an important role in previous negotiations leading to the 2015 nuclear agreement and continued to express willingness to help reduce tensions.
Baghaei said Tehran would continue pursuing diplomatic opportunities despite its longstanding distrust of Washington. He accused the US of repeatedly violating its commitments, including since its withdrawal from the 2015 nuclear agreement in 2018.
However, he stressed that Iran’s diplomatic institutions could not abandon negotiations solely because of previous experiences. “If there is even the slightest possibility that diplomacy can prevent an escalation of tensions, we must pursue that path,” he said.
Baghaei added that Iran’s priority remained protecting its national interests and security, whether through diplomacy or military defence.
Baghaei also rejected a resolution adopted at an Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) foreign ministers’ meeting in Baghdad expressing solidarity with Saudi Arabia against attacks by Yemen’s Houthis. He said Iran had formally opposed the resolution and did not consider it a valid OIC decision, citing failure to follow the organisation’s procedural rules.
According to Baghaei, Tehran also prevented the inclusion of two paragraphs concerning Yemen in the meeting’s final declaration, arguing that their wording would deepen divisions among Muslim countries.
He said the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen should be resolved through dialogue and reconciliation rather than military force.
“The issue of Yemen cannot be resolved through force and military means,” he said.
Baghaei called on neighboring countries to prevent foreign powers from using their territory and military facilities to threaten or attack other states.
He said preventing such activities was essential to establishing lasting regional security and maintaining good-neighborly relations.
The spokesperson also accused Israel’s policies and territorial expansion of fueling regional instability. He said the war in Gaza had not ended the suffering of Palestinians and reiterated Tehran’s criticism of US and European support for Israel.
IRGC says two tankers hit mines, set ablaze south of Hormuz
Two tankers were set ablaze and brought to a halt south of the Strait of Hormuz after hitting Iranian mines, the Revolutionary Guards' Navy said in a statement shared by state media on Tuesday, without saying when the tankers were hit.
The statement also said a US drone was downed by Iran on Monday night.
Iran says it downed US drone over Strait of Hormuz
Iran's IRGC on Tuesday said that it intercepted and destroyed a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz, according to the Fars news agency.
The Revolutionary Guard said the drone was downed on early Tuesday while flying over the strategic waterway, the news agency reported.
It claimed that the aircraft was the 54th US MQ-9 drone it had destroyed, according to the agency.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guard cites 7 internet cables under Strait of Hormuz, warns of ‘new targets’
Iran’s IRGC warned on Monday that it would unveil new targets and weapons, drawing attention to major undersea internet cables crossing the Strait of Hormuz amid tensions with the United States.
“Seven major internet cables run beneath the Strait of Hormuz,” said IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi, claiming that all internet and commercial data traffic passed through them.
“We just want them to know that new targets will be unveiled. New weapons will be unveiled,” he added.
Mohebbi made the remarks during a ceremony at Tehran’s Sacred Defence Museum, the Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reported.
He also vowed to drive what he called the remnants of US power out of the region.
Earlier this month, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, told Iranian state broadcaster Press TV that Tehran could target undersea internet cables, data centers and artificial intelligence facilities linked to the US if another war broke out.
“We have not yet included these assets among our targets,” Rezaei said, warning that such infrastructure could be destroyed in a renewed conflict.
Hormuz could be 'redundant' in five years, replaced by new routes, HSBC CEO says
Investment in alternative logistics routes in the Gulf to mitigate the impact of ​the Iran war could make the Strait of Hormuz "redundant" in the ‌next five years, HSBC Group Chief Executive Georges Elhedery said on Tuesday.
The conflict has highlighted the world's heavy reliance on the strategic waterway, through which a fifth of global oil ​and liquefied natural gas trade previously passed.
It is forcing Gulf nations ​to channel resources towards the development of energy pipelines to ⁠ports, investments that Elhedery said will allow the region to weather the fallout ​from the conflict. "We do see this region being able to recover and then ​continue growing. It will mean a lot of investment," the bank CEO said during the HSBC Future Forum event in Dubai.
"Of course, we do wish and hope to see ​a resolution to the conflict ... But Hormuz, probably in five years' time, may ​become redundant," he added.
The Middle East, North Africa and Turkey are offering $872 billion in individual ‌project ⁠packages, part of a wider $1.4 trillion planned and unawarded infrastructure pipeline, HSBC said in a report on Monday citing data from MEED, a Dubai-based construction industry market intelligence platform.
A recent HSBC survey of over 1,600 business leaders and ​around 820 global institutional ​investors, meanwhile, found ⁠that they still considered the Gulf an attractive investment hub.
However, after growth of 3.3% in 2025, the World Bank ​last week forecast a deep economic contraction of 1.3% in the ​Middle East, ⁠North Africa and Pakistan region this year due to the war. That should be followed by a strong but uneven rebound in 2027.
Elhedery was among global ⁠financiers expected ​to attend Saudi Arabia's flagship investment conference, ​which was planned for next week but postponed to 2027 on Monday following deadly strikes in Riyadh by Yemen's Houthis.
Hegseth discusses Iran with Netanyahu in unannounced visit to Israel, officials say
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth discussed Iran with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during an unannounced visit to Israel on Monday, three Israeli officials said, as tensions flare between the US and Iran.
The officials did not provide further details about the meeting, first reported by Axios . The Pentagon declined to comment. The Israeli prime minister's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Hegseth said in a social media post that he had visited US service members in the Central Command area of responsibility, which covers the Middle East, northeast Africa and parts of Asia.
Read: US 'exhausted and worn out', lacks capability to launch new conflict: IRGC
Israel's Army Radio reported his meeting with Netanyahu took place at an air force base in Israel's southern desert.
Hegseth's visit comes amid rising tensions in the Middle East war as tensions flare between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz and as Yemen's Houthis intensify their attacks on Saudi Arabia.
It also came a day after US President Donald Trump endorsed Netanyahu in next week's parliamentary election in Israel, the country's first ballot since the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack on southern Israel.
Iran summons German ambassador over ‘repetition of baseless accusations’
Iranian officials summoned German Ambassador to Iran Axel Dittmann over the “repetition of baseless accusations by German authorities” against Tehran, Tasnim news agency reported on Monday.
Dittmann was summoned to the Iranian Foreign Ministry by Alireza Yousefi, an assistant foreign minister and director general for Western Europe, who conveyed Iran’s protest, the outlet said.
Yousefi “emphasised that making security accusations against Iran was a long-standing practice of the Zionist regime and some Western countries against Iran,” it added.
The Iranian move came after Germany summoned the Iranian ambassador earlier on Monday, accusing Tehran of planning assassination attempts against pro-Israel figures and condemning the alleged plots in the strongest possible terms.
“We do not tolerate attacks on Jewish life and on those who defend it -- anywhere, and certainly not in Germany,” the German Foreign Ministry said in a statement on social media.
US 'exhausted and worn out', lacks capability to launch new conflict: IRGC
The IRGC spokesperson Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi said that the United States forces were "exhausted and worn out," and that they lacked the capability to launch a new conflict, Tehran Times reported on Monday.
The spokesperson stated that the US "entered the war with all its might in the past and is certainly not in a position now to launch a new conflict that would yield any additional gains for it." He added that most US bases in the region "have been rendered inactive," and American forces had "withdrawn hundreds of kilometres away from Iran."
"From a technical and military standpoint, the United States lacks the capability to launch a new conflict," Mohebbi said, according to Tehran Times . The spokesperson noted, however, that as US midterm elections approach, "it may seek to manufacture some achievements."

"We do not rule out any possibilities and are prepared to respond. This time, our response will be much more forceful," he said.
On the IRGC's military capabilities , Mohebbi stated, "Our capabilities have undoubtedly increased significantly, both quantitatively and qualitatively, and are now at least 1.5 times greater than in the past."
According to Tehran Times , the spokesperson added that the production of missiles, drones, and other equipment Tehran needed was never halted. "We have even expanded production, improving range, accuracy, and destructive power, while also developing new weapons," Mohebbi said, adding that if the war escalated, "the IRGC’s surprises will reveal themselves."

title: Brent crude holds near five month high on Middle East tension
description: Brent crude futures climb 55 cents  or 0 50   to  110 10 a barrel
content:
Brent crude futures climb 55 cents, or 0.50%, to $110.10 a barrel
Oil prices advanced on Tuesday, with Brent hovering ​around a five-month high as traders priced in a geopolitical risk premium from Houthi attacks ‌on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf.
Brent crude futures climbed 55 cents, or 0.50%, to $110.10 a barrel, after rising as high as $110.70 a barrel in the previous session to their highest since May 20.
The US West ​Texas Intermediate crude (WTI) contract for November delivery, set to expire on Tuesday, was up 0.24% to $103.91. The ​more-active December contract rose 39 cents, or 0.40%, to $98.93.
"Oil prices remain well-supported ... This suggests ⁠the market is pricing in a significant risk premium, given the situation's volatility," ING analysts said in a ​note on Tuesday.
"However, if flows continue uninhibited despite the geopolitical environment, the risk premium would likely erode slowly. Clearly, ​there are no signs of this yet."
At least 18 vessels were reportedly attacked over two weeks, which keeps the risk premium intact, shiptracker Kpler said in a note on Monday.
Houthis claim attacks on Saudi facilities
Yemen's Houthis said on Monday they launched several attacks ​on Saudi energy, airport and military targets, such as an Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield, Riyadh's ​King Khalid International Airport and Abha airport.
Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the claims, and Reuters could not independently verify them.
Also ‌on Monday, ⁠a Houthi attack on a training camp for government security forces in Yemen's Shabwa province killed 58 people, with more than 200 injured.
The renewed attacks heightened fears about regional stability and underscored continuing risks to energy supply from the region, keeping oil prices above $100 a barrel.

In the US, crude oil stockpiles were expected to have fallen last ​week along with product inventories, ​a preliminary Reuters poll showed ⁠on Monday.
Friday's executive order by President Donald Trump waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs, including goods duties and penalties for purchases of its energy.
However, Trump said on Saturday ​he had yet to announce a final decision on the matter, while Secretary of State ​Marco Rubio ⁠said officials wanted more time to evaluate the situation.
Russia's crude oil production increased by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million bpd, but remained about 870,000 bpd below that of a year ago, the International Energy Agency said last ⁠week.
"While ​the prospect of additional Russian diesel supply offers some theoretical relief, traders ​appear far more focused on the ongoing risk of further damage to energy infrastructure across the Gulf region," said Tim Waterer, KCM Trade ​chief analyst.

title: Kundi vows crackdown on encroachments
description: Kundi vows crackdown on encroachments
content:
Governor pledges province-wide action without favouritism
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi has announced a zero-tolerance policy against illegal encroachments across the province, warning that action will be taken without discrimination, regardless of the influence or political affiliation of those involved.
"Even if someone is my relative or a representative of a political party, no recommendation will be accepted," the governor said while speaking to the media during an inspection of the ongoing anti-encroachment drive in Peshawar on Sunday.
During his visit to Kohat Road, Kundi received a briefing from officials of the Peshawar district administration and the Peshawar Development Authority (PDA) on measures being taken to remove illegal encroachments.
He appreciated the efforts of the district administration and relevant departments, saying effective measures would be taken to rid the province of illegal occupation of public spaces.
The governor made it clear that the campaign would not be limited to Peshawar but would be extended across the province. He warned that officials concerned would be held responsible if encroachments reappeared after being removed.
Appealing to those responsible to remove illegal structures voluntarily, he said the authorities would take action against those who failed to comply. No concessions would be granted to influential individuals, he added.
"The days when people established encroachments through political connections and recommendations are over," Kundi said, criticising the previous provincial government for allegedly turning a blind eye to the problem.

title: Traditional Ghughu Ghoray toy fades into history
description: Traditional Ghughu Ghoray toy fades into history
content:
Three-century-old clay toy culture loses ground to electronic and plastic toys
Punjab's 300-year-old traditional clay toy known as ghughu ghoray has virtually disappeared due to the absence of official patronage and rapid technological advancement. During the 19th century, women from nomadic communities would carry baskets of these clay toys on their heads, selling them in streets and neighbourhoods while calling out, "Ghughu Ghoray Lo, Bhughu Ghoray."
The craft began declining in the early 20th century and has now almost completely vanished. These toys are rarely seen today except in antique toy shops, cultural festivals, Sunday bazaars or occasionally with nomadic families selling them outside parks and during Punjab Culture Day events.
In Punjabi, the word "Ghughu" refers to a bird or a soft, repetitive sound.
Since the toy produces a similar low-pitched whistle, it came to be known as Ghughu Ghoray. In literary and political discourse, the term has also become a metaphor for a person or system lacking independent decision-making ability and being controlled by others.
One of the key reasons for the toy's decline is that skilled artisans, including potters and nomadic craftsmen, have abandoned the profession.
Today, the toys are displayed at exhibitions as part of Punjab's folk heritage to keep younger generations connected with their cultural roots.
Cheap plastic and electronic toys imported from China have further contributed to the decline. Ghughu Ghoray was once one of Punjab's most popular traditional toys. Usually shaped like a horse, it was a handmade clay whistle that children played by blowing into it.
For centuries, it remained a major attraction for children at fairs and festivals across rural Punjab. The hollow horse-shaped toy, made from clay, straw, cloth and kite paper, contains a hole through which air is blown to produce the distinctive "Ghughu" sound. After being baked in a kiln, it turns red and is decorated with colorful indigenous patterns.
Potters and nomadic tribes in Multan, Attock and other parts of Punjab traditionally produced these toys from generation to generation.
Though plastic toys have largely replaced it in the digital age, the Ghughu Ghoray survives as a symbol of folk heritage and craftsmanship at cultural festivals and in some villages. More than just a toy, it is also linked to the ancient Indus Valley Civilization of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.
The clay version is made from fine soil, often collected from the Ravi and Chenab rivers. Potters mold the horse by hand, leaving it hollow and creating a small opening that produces a whistle-like sound when blown. After drying in the sun, it is baked in a traditional kiln and decorated with bright local colors.
Another version, mostly made by nomadic tribes, uses old cloth, waste paper, reeds and straw. A frame is stitched from cloth and stuffed with straw, while bamboo or wooden sticks form the legs. Decorative paper, glue and lace are used to adorn the neck, saddle and face.
Kamil Shah, owner of a toy shop in Rawalpindi, said his family has been in the toy business for generations and he has personally run the shop for the last 24 years.
He said Ghughu Ghoray once sold in large numbers, with fresh supplies arriving every ten days and being purchased by retailers and hawkers. Today, however, children prefer electronic toys. He added that the toys are now purchased mainly during cultural events in Rawalpindi, Islamabad and Punjab, making them more of a cultural item than a commercial product.

title: Teachers slam enrolment targets
description: Teachers slam enrolment targets
content:
Punjab Teachers Union General Secretary Rana Liaquat Ali has called for enrolment targets to be set for each educational institution in consultation with its head and in accordance with the available resources.
He said it was not possible for every school to achieve a 10 per cent increase in enrolment because of a persistent shortage of teachers and Class IV employees, as well as inadequate basic facilities.
He said school heads and teachers were responsible for meeting admission targets in line with the number of students leaving after completing Grade 5 in primary schools, Grade 8 in middle schools and Grade 10 in high schools.
However, pressuring teachers to achieve the 10 per cent target, summoning school heads and teachers to offices after school hours and making them sit outside for hours as punishment, and threatening them with dismissal amounted to encouraging fictitious enrolments, he said.
Rana Liaquat Ali said authorities had earlier directed schools to eliminate fake enrolments immediately, but were now setting unrealistic targets that could mislead senior officials.
He identified staff shortages, inadequate facilities, a lack of funds, excessive paperwork, examination-related and non-teaching duties assigned to teachers, and the temporary deployment of teachers and other employees to government offices as major obstacles to achieving enrolment targets and improving the quality of education.
He urged the Punjab chief minister to commission an independent third-party audit of schools instead of relying solely on Education Department statistics, saying it would provide a more accurate picture of the challenges facing educational institutions.

title: Suspect s father alleges torture
description: Suspect s father alleges torture
content:
Zeeshan's family disputes allegations as investigators cite DNA and polygraph results
The family of Zeeshan Arshad, a domestic worker arrested in the Hina Javed murder case, came forward, with his father alleging that his son was forced at gunpoint to restrain the victim and was subsequently tortured in custody to make him confess to the crime.
Muhammad Arshad said he had met his son twice in jail. According to him, Zeeshan recounted that an argument broke out between Hina and her husband, Faisal Asghar, on the night of August 20, waking him from sleep.
The father alleged that Hina was running ahead while Faisal chased her. Faisal allegedly ordered Zeeshan to catch her and, when he refused to intervene in the couple's dispute, beat him and forced him at gunpoint to comply.
Muhammad Arshad further alleged, attributing the account to his son, that Faisal had murdered Hina and hanged her body in the bathroom. He claimed that the entire blame had been shifted onto Zeeshan in an attempt to portray him as the prime suspect.
He said his son had worked at the victim's house for about seven months and regarded her as a mother. The family learnt of the murder 11 days after the incident, he added. Four days after the incident, a man named Tasawwur, who had arranged Zeeshan's employment, asked for his identity card, according to the father.
He rejected claims that his son had a criminal record, saying no case had been registered against the 18- or 19-year-old in any police station, including Miana Gondal police station in Mandi Bahauddin. Zeeshan's maternal uncle said he had arranged the job to help him earn a livelihood.
Meanwhile, a Rawalpindi police spokesperson said the murder took place on August 20 and that technical and forensic evidence had been collected from the outset.
A district-level special team was formed under the supervision of the Senior Superintendent of Police (Investigation), while the Punjab Inspector General of Police constituted another special investigation team headed by an officer of Additional Inspector General rank. The spokesperson said senior officers and experienced investigators had examined the case from all angles. Evidence collected from the crime scene by specialist teams from the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) was submitted for analysis.
The case was investigated in the light of DNA reports, polygraph test results and other material evidence received from the PFSA, the spokesperson said, adding that legal experts had also been consulted during the investigation and preparation of the case file.
RAWALPINDI. The family of Hina Javed, who was murdered in Rawalpindi, has once again expressed a lack of confidence in the police investigation and demanded the formation of a judicial commission to uncover all facts surrounding the case.
In response, Rawalpindi police issued a formal statement claiming that the investigation had been conducted under the supervision of senior officers, taking into account all technical, forensic and scientific evidence and that proceedings were being pursued on merit without any pressure or external influence.
The victim's family expressed serious reservations about the investigation during a press conference at the National Press Club in Islamabad, demanding a judicial commission to establish the complete facts of the case.
Following the press conference, a Rawalpindi police spokesperson said all necessary technical and forensic evidence had been collected from the first day of the incident, which occurred on August 20.
According to the spokesperson, a special team headed by the SSP (Investigation) was formed at the district level to investigate the murder. The Punjab inspector general of police also constituted a special investigation team led by an officer of additional inspector general rank.
The case was investigated by experienced officers under the direct supervision of senior officials, who examined the facts and evidence from various angles, the spokesperson said.
Expert teams from the Punjab Forensic Science Agency collected all necessary evidence from the crime scene and sent it for analysis.

title: Vance acknowledges  failures  in US handling of Iran war
description: Vance acknowledges  failures  in US handling of Iran war
content:
US Vice President JD Vance acknowledged "a lot of mistakes and a lot of fundamental failures" in the handling of the Iran war, as he faced questions over the conflict's rising human and economic costs during a CBS News town hall on Sunday.
Vance made the remarks in response to Joey Amor, whose wife, Master Sgt Nicole Amor, was among six US Army Reserve soldiers killed in an Iranian strike on a military site in Kuwait in the opening hours of the war that began in late February. At least 21 US service members have been killed and hundreds wounded so far.
Amor questioned reports that the facility had not been adequately secured, demanding accountability from the Trump administration.
"Though the Iranian drone was the weapon that killed my wife, there were a lot of mistakes and a lot of fundamental failures that led up to that," Amor said.
Vance acknowledged that there were shortcomings. "Sometimes information doesn't filter up to me," he said, pledging to "take every single failure extremely seriously."
The vice president also admitted that the positioning of US troops exposed weaknesses in the military's approach. "I know that there are some issues with, for example where troops were located that we realised was a huge mistake and that we could do better on. And we have changed that," he said.
Vance pointed to the growing threat posed by inexpensive drones, saying the US military had altered its tactics to better protect troops and prevent further casualties.
Asked why Washington had still not secured a decisive victory despite President Donald Trump's initial expectations, Vance argued that the US had "in some ways won decisively," but acknowledged the outcome also depended on Iran's actions. "The enemy gets a vote here," he said.
Vance defended the administration's strategy, saying Washington was seeking a "final firm commitment from the Iranians that they're not going to rebuild their nuclear program."
Meanwhile, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Sunday that he hopes his US-sanctioned defence minister nominee can "survive," claiming that he is also on a US "assassination list."
Pezeshkian made the remarks in a virtual address to parliament during a session considering Mehrdad Akhlaqi Ketabchi's nomination as minister of defence, according to the semi-official ISNA news agency.
Pezeshkian said Akhlaqi is under US sanctions and claimed that he is also on a US "assassination list." He expressed hope that the nominee would "take care of himself" and, with support from the country's institutions, "remain alive" and continue working to strengthen Iran's defence capabilities.
Pezeshkian urged lawmakers to give Akhlaqi a strong vote of confidence, saying he enjoys support across Iran's armed forces, including the army, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), the defence ministry and security institutions.
