title: MQM P calls for new administrative units to address urban Sindh   s woes
description: Siddiqui says failure to devolve powers has fuelled public discontent in Karachi  Hyderabad and other urban districts
content:
Siddiqui says failure to devolve powers has fuelled public discontent in Karachi, Hyderabad and other urban districts
The Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) has renewed its call for new administrative units in Sindh, arguing that the devolution of powers and authority is essential to address longstanding civic problems in Karachi, Hyderabad and other urban areas.
“Establishing new and empowered administrative units is the biggest challenge and the solution to ensuring that people receive their rights at their doorstep,” MQM-P Chairman Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui said during a meeting with legal experts at the party’s Bahadurabad headquarters.
The meeting brought together members of the Muttahida Lawyers Forum, the party’s Legal Aid Committee and prominent legal experts to discuss urban Sindh’s civic challenges, constitutional and legal reforms, judicial performance and strategies for securing the release of party activists in detention.
Read : 'The country's system is about to be reset': Naqvi says move will bring improvement in affairs
Senior MQM-P leader Wasim Akhtar and other party leaders attended the meeting, while former judge Qazi Khalid was also present.
Addressing the gathering, Siddiqui said the lack of basic facilities and the failure to devolve powers had fuelled public discontent in Karachi, Hyderabad and other urban districts. He called for a new administrative arrangement to restore balance in governance and ensure that citizens could access their rights and essential services more effectively.
Legal experts briefed the party leadership on what they described as shortcomings in existing laws and regulations that could be exploited to deprive citizens of their rights. They presented legal proposals and draft amendments aimed at addressing procedural and constitutional gaps.
The participants also discussed the need for far-reaching judicial reforms to ensure timely, affordable and transparent justice, particularly for disadvantaged and marginalised communities.
Members of the Legal Aid Committee pledged to expand and strengthen legal assistance for citizens facing difficulties in accessing justice. The meeting also considered legal strategies concerning detained party workers and efforts to secure their release.
At the conclusion of the meeting, MQM-P leaders and legal experts reiterated their commitment to pursuing the party’s demands through political, constitutional and legal means, including advocating new administrative units and reforms to existing laws.
The current debate over new provinces began on July 30, when Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi called for additional administrative units or provinces as part of a broader overhaul of the country’s governance system. Naqvi argued that meaningful structural reforms were needed to improve governance, deliver justice and create opportunities for young people.
Also Read : Governance system has collapsed: Naqvi
A day later, his proposal appeared to receive support from Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, who said an administrative reset, if required, should be undertaken to ensure good governance
The proposal quickly became politically sensitive in Sindh, where the PPP strongly opposed any move to divide the province. Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah rejected Naqvi’s assessment that the governance system had collapsed and called the proposal outdated, warning that no bloodshed would be allowed over the creation of new provinces.
The debate widened in August when Muttahida Qaumi Movement–Pakistan (MQM-P) backed the creation of new provinces and called for a national dialogue with political parties. The party argued that Pakistan’s growing population, poor governance and concentration of political power made greater administrative devolution necessary. The move put the party, which is part of the federal coalition but sits in opposition in Sindh, at odds with the PPP’s position on the province.
The PPP, meanwhile, maintained that administrative reform and the division of Sindh were separate questions. Sindh minister Nasir Hussain Shah said the provincial government was willing to discuss measures to improve governance and devolve power, but rejected linking those reforms to the creation of a new province.
The dispute reached the Sindh Assembly at the beginning of September. On September 3, the house unanimously passed a resolution rejecting any proposal to divide Sindh or alter its territorial limits. The resolution described Sindh as a “historic, civilisational and constitutional entity” and declared that “Sindh is one and shall remain one”.
Read More : PTI's Barrister Gohar warns against dividing provinces without broad public consensus
Naqvi, however, showed no sign of backing away. On September 5, he said he would continue to support new provinces regardless of whether he remained in office, arguing that the ultimate decision should belong to the people rather than politicians or governments. He said the public should first be told the “pros and cons” of creating new administrative units before being allowed to decide.
That position has since raised another question over how public opinion could be formally established. A constitutional debate emerged over whether a referendum could be used to gauge support for new provinces. Article 48(6) allows a matter of national importance to be put to a referendum following approval by a joint sitting of Parliament, although a referendum itself would not create a new province; any change to provincial boundaries would still have to follow the constitutional process.
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan warned on September 7 that dividing Sindh or any other province without the consent of its people and representatives would weaken the federation. He called for a commission and extensive deliberations before the issue was taken to parliament.
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, while accepting that Sindh had the right to take its own position, also said a final decision would have to emerge through consensus. Asif separately suggested that Islamabad could be used as a starting point for any future administrative restructuring, while Prime Minister’s Adviser Rana Sanaullah said the question of new provinces should be taken up at the relevant forums and resolved through consensus among political parties.

title: Govt turns to foreign experts to find K2 Airways  black box
description: Pakistan explores advanced sonar systems and underwater vehicles to search for aircraft  believed to lie 3 000m deep
content:
Pakistan explores advanced sonar systems and underwater vehicles to search for aircraft, believed to lie 3,000m deep
Nearly four months after a K2 Airways aircraft plunged into the sea off Ormara, the search for its black box, wreckage and cockpit crew is entering a new phase, with Pakistan stepping up efforts to enlist international expertise for a deep-sea recovery operation.
With the aircraft believed to lie around 3,000 metres below the surface, the search is expected to rely on advanced sonar systems, autonomous underwater vehicles and remotely operated vehicles equipped with high-definition cameras and specialised recovery tools.
The government has intensified contacts with foreign experts and several international companies to determine the best way to locate and recover the aircraft’s remains from the seabed, according to sources. The black box and wreckage are considered crucial to establishing what happened in the aircraft’s final moments.
Read : K2: families demand deep-sea search
The aircraft, operated by the privately owned domestic cargo carrier, crashed into the sea on July 7 this year after encountering adverse conditions near Ormara. Sources said the transmitter beacon fitted to the black box stopped emitting signals about a month after the accident, making the search more difficult.
The Pakistan Navy had earlier used specialised equipment and side-scan sonar to identify a possible location of the black box on the seabed. Acoustic signals were used to scan the area at a depth of around 3,000 metres, but further progress now depends on more sophisticated underwater technology and specialised deep-sea salvage expertise.
As part of the proposed operation, a detailed three-dimensional map of the seabed will be prepared using a multibeam echo sounder. The technology can map underwater terrain, measure depths and identify potential obstructions, helping search teams narrow down the area where the aircraft’s wreckage may be located.
Autonomous underwater vehicles may also be deployed to survey the seabed using sonar, cameras and other sensors. Data and images collected by these unmanned systems could help identify suspicious objects and pinpoint areas requiring closer inspection.
Remotely operated vehicles (ROVs), controlled from a support vessel, could play an equally important role. Equipped with high-definition cameras, powerful lights and robotic arms, the machines can examine wreckage at close range and, where feasible, retrieve smaller objects or position specialised equipment around the debris.
Search teams may also use a towed pinger locator to detect acoustic signals from the black box beacon. However, with the transmitter reportedly no longer functioning, its usefulness could be limited, increasing reliance on other methods.
A magnetometer could provide another means of locating the wreckage by detecting variations in the magnetic field associated with large metallic objects. Combining sonar readings, magnetic measurements and underwater imagery could help investigators verify the suspected location of the aircraft.
Specialised deep-sea salvage vessels may be required to support the operation. Such ships can carry heavy-duty winches, cranes, remotely operated systems and other equipment needed to access and recover wreckage from extreme depths. Operating at around 3,000 metres requires specialised machinery, technical expertise and careful planning.
Also Read : Deep-sea hunt for K2 crash wreckage to begin next month
The recovery of the black box and wreckage is considered essential to the investigation, as flight data and cockpit voice recordings could help investigators reconstruct the aircraft’s final moments, examine cockpit activity and determine the possible causes of the crash.
Sources said the company that owns the cargo aircraft would bear 50 per cent of the search costs. Raja Tariq, who owns up to 60pc of the cargo aircraft company’s shares, has been informed of the decision, they added.
The next phase of the search is expected to depend on assessments by international specialists, the availability of suitable equipment and the identification of the most promising locations on the seabed.

title: Fourth Wing    TV show  Cast  plot and everything to know about the Prime Video adaptation
description: Yarros is attached as an executive producer  helping guide the adaptation of her popular fantasy franchise
content:
Yarros is attached as an executive producer, helping guide the adaptation of her popular fantasy franchise
Rebecca Yarros’ bestselling fantasy novel Fourth Wing is officially heading to television, with Prime Video assembling its creative team and lead cast for the highly anticipated adaptation. The series will bring the first instalment of Yarros’ Empyrean book series to the screen, introducing audiences to a dangerous world of dragon riders, military training and romance.
The adaptation received an official series order in May 2026, following the initial development deal between Amazon MGM Studios and Michael B. Jordan’s Outlier Society in 2023. Yarros is attached as an executive producer, helping guide the adaptation of her popular fantasy franchise.
Fourth Wing follows Violet Sorrengail, a 20-year-old who is forced by her mother to enter Basgiath War College, where candidates undergo brutal training to become dragon riders. Despite her physical vulnerabilities and original plans for a quieter life surrounded by books, Violet must navigate a dangerous environment where failure can be fatal.
As she struggles to survive the college’s demanding training, Violet encounters Xaden Riorson, a powerful squad leader whose complicated history with her family adds another layer to their relationship. The story combines fantasy, high-stakes action and an enemies-to-lovers romance. The television adaptation is expected to follow the novel, although the production team has indicated that the series may include surprises for viewers familiar with the books.
Esther McGregor, daughter of actor Ewan McGregor and known for her role in We Were Liars , has been cast as Violet Sorrengail. Emilio Sakraya will portray Xaden Riorson opposite her. The casting marks a major step forward for the adaptation, which has attracted considerable attention from fans of Yarros’ books. Further casting details have yet to be announced.
Meredith Averill, known for The Haunting of Hill House and Locke & Key , serves as showrunner and executive producer. Lisa Joy, co-creator of Westworld , is set to direct the first episode and executive produce through Kilter Films alongside Jonathan Nolan and Athena Wickham.
Michael B. Jordan and Elizabeth Raposo will executive produce through Outlier Society, while Yarros, Liz Pelletier and Sherryl Clark are also among the executive producers.
Yarros has been involved in the adaptation’s development for several years. In January 2025, she revealed that she had read versions of the script and was pleased with how they captured the spirit of her novel. She has also shared the overarching story of her planned five-book series with the creative team to help maintain continuity across potential future seasons.
The Empyrean series is planned to span five books, with Fourth Wing , Iron Flame and Onyx Storm already published. The adaptation is being developed with the intention of bringing the wider story to television across multiple seasons. However, the scope and structure of future seasons have not been fully detailed, and the fifth book has yet to be released.
Prime Video has not announced a release date for Fourth Wing . The series remains in development, and further details about production and additional cast members are expected as the project progresses. When it premieres, the adaptation will stream on Prime Video.
With Yarros involved behind the scenes and a creative team experienced in fantasy and genre television, the series is among the upcoming adaptations attracting attention from romantasy readers.

title: Cable theft leaves 33 traffic signals dysfunctional across Karachi
description: Repeated thefts have crippled traffic signals  while funding shortages and a lack of effective action hamper repairs
content:
Repeated thefts have crippled traffic signals, while funding shortages and lack of effective action hamper repairs
Theft of cables and other equipment has rendered 33 traffic signals dysfunctional across Karachi, worsening traffic congestion on major roads and adding to commuters’ daily difficulties. After targeting iron railings around parks, playgrounds and roadsides, suspected drug addicts have now turned their attention to traffic signals, damaging critical urban infrastructure.
According to the Karachi Development Authority’s (KDA) Traffic Engineering Bureau (TEB), 94 traffic signals are installed across the city. However, repeated thefts have left many of them out of service, while the relevant authorities have yet to take effective measures to prevent further incidents.
Cameras installed along major roads have largely been used to issue traffic challans and monitor traffic violations, rather than to identify those responsible for damaging public infrastructure.
Read: Hyd's crumbling power network puts lives at risk
An Express Tribune survey found that traffic police personnel often resort to manually controlling traffic at intersections where signals are not functioning. In some instances, however, traffic officials are also absent from these locations. The deteriorating condition of roads, with several stretches damaged and broken, further compounds the problem.
As a result, traffic congestion has become a daily occurrence on major thoroughfares as well as roads within residential and commercial areas.
Traffic Engineering Bureau (TEB) sources said repairs had been suspended for over a year due to funding shortages, with more than Rs10 million in contractor payments outstanding. The Sindh government allocated funds to the Karachi commissioner’s office for repairs, lane marking and road signs.
Using the funds and TEB’s technical support, 20 signals were repaired, including five automated ones. However, cables were subsequently stolen from seven signals, including those in Red Zone areas monitored by surveillance cameras, forcing them to shut down again.
These locations included Ziauddin Road near Lily Bridge, Boat Basin Chowrangi, Sir Syed Khalid bin Walid Road intersection, Akbar Road, Court Road and Singer Chowrangi. Cables on Ziauddin Road were reportedly stolen on three separate occasions.
At Boat Basin, a private security guard foiled an attempt to steal a newly installed road sign. TEB sources said police had repeatedly been informed about the thefts but had taken no effective action.
A police officer, speaking anonymously, said Safe City cameras were monitored through a centralised control room and used for traffic enforcement, tracing stolen vehicles and monitoring suspicious activity in Red Zone areas.
District police can obtain footage through formal requests, while community policing cameras installed with private donations are monitored at local stations. The officer said footage could help identify the culprits, blaming police negligence for the lack of action. The South district police spokesperson sought a day to comment but did not respond to subsequent calls.

TEB sources said signals at another 26 locations were dysfunctional due to cable and equipment thefts, including Makki Masjid, Yaseenabad, Atrium Mall, Karachi Grammar School, Shahrah-e-Iraq, Albela Chowrangi, Guru Mandir, Banuri Town Mosque, II Chundrigar Road near Denso Hall, Aram Bagh and Shalimar Chowk.
Ghaus Bakhsh Abbasi, project director at the Karachi commissioner’s office, confirmed an increase in traffic signal cable thefts, saying FIRs had been registered and the commissioner had taken up the matter with senior police officials.
He said repairs had been delayed due to a funding shortage at the Traffic Engineering Bureau. Following the chief minister’s directives, the Sindh government released Rs100 million to the Karachi commissioner’s office, enabling the repair of 20 signals, including five automated ones, along with lane marking and road sign installation.
However, some repaired signals were damaged again by cable theft. Abbasi said a request for additional funds to repair the remaining faulty signals had been submitted to the provincial government.

US Vice President Vance links immigration, problems of ‘assimilation’ for violence in France
US President Donald Trump on Sunday blamed immigration for the widespread rioting that erupted in cities across France, stating that France was "burning", further urging authorities to "take control" and close borders.
The protests in France began last ‌month at high schools in Paris' working-class northern suburbs, where anger over teacher shortages and shabby facilities evolved into a broader movement focused on inequality, public spending and living standards.
In a Truth Social post on Sunday, Trump wrote that "France is burning!", accusing immigrants of "shattering a once great country".
Read : Trump blames France unrest on 'mass migration', Islam
"The immigration of people from an entirely different world, people with hatred in their hearts, has shattered that once great country."
Trump further urged French authorities to "close your borders and take control, before it is too late!"
Meanwhile, US Vice President JD Vance also blamed immigration for violence during protests in France, while sharing a video showing the city hall in Limoges on fire.
In a post on X, Vance said that “Western liberals imported the third world into France and other countries in the name of diversity and compassion. They ignored fundamental questions of assimilation and compatibility. They were told it would lead to this and they didn’t listen.”
“I pray that France, a beautiful country of amazing people, will stop this madness before more of its landmarks burn,” he added.
Read More : Mass protests in France spiral into worst riots in years
Vance, who is seen as a potential presidential candidate in the 2028 election, also drew a connection to upcoming midterm races for congressional seats on November 3, where Republicans are not expected to perform well.
“And I hope Americans are paying attention. This is the future congressional Democrats seek for your country,” Vance said.
Vance, 42, represents the most nationalist and identitarian wing of the Republican Party, and often criticises Europe’s immigration policies, which he considers too lax.
Vance went so far as to lecture Europeans on the subject during a February 2025 speech in Munich.

title: Wasim Akram advises over 50s to limit WhatsApp  social media use
description: The former cricketer urged over 50  to use WhatsApp wisely  avoid excessive messages and respect others    time
content:
Former cricketer urges over 50+ to use WhatsApp wisely, avoid excessive messages and respect others' time
Former Pakistan cricket captain Wasim Akram has shared a humorous message for people aged over 50, offering advice on how to use mobile phones, WhatsApp and social media without overwhelming others with messages and calls.
Sharing the video on Instagram , Akram wrote, “Viewer discretion: THIS VIDEO IS AVAILABLE FOR PEOPLE OVER 50 ON HOW AND WHEN TO USE A MOBILE PHONE/ WHATSAPP. AND YOU ARE WELCOME...”
In the video, Akram said he could understand Gen Z and Gen Alpha because they were always on their phones. However, he suggested that older generations should learn to use their devices more thoughtfully, particularly when communicating with younger people.
“This is special for 50+ that they should use WhatsApp, social media and their phones the correct way,” he said, before advising viewers to stop sending random content to people every day.
“Firstly, most importantly, stop sending random stuff to people every day,” Akram said, explaining that such messages could become annoying, even when the sender had good intentions. He added that people should not feel obliged to send good morning messages to everyone daily.
Akram also highlighted the importance of considering people's attention spans before forwarding videos. He suggested that lengthy videos were less likely to be watched in full, with shorter clips of around two minutes being more suitable for many viewers.
“I get you mean well, but it annoys people. Also, you don't have to send good morning to everyone every day. The third thing is when you send videos, please know that attention spans are short these days. Nobody will watch a 30-minute-long video, only 2 minutes”, he added.
His next piece of advice concerned constant phone use. Akram urged people not to remain available on WhatsApp around the clock, pointing out that there was nothing wrong with replying to a message five minutes later. Constantly checking notifications and responding immediately, he suggested, could create unnecessary stress.
Reflecting on his own experiences, Akram said he had friends who never seemed to put their phones down, even when spending time together. He encouraged people to take things easy, enjoy life and manage their messages rather than feeling pressured to respond to everything immediately.
Akram explained that he still checked and forwarded messages but preferred to keep things under control instead of allowing his phone to dominate his time.
The video sparked a discussion among social media users, with some agreeing with Akram's advice while others felt his message needed a more compassionate approach.
One user wrote, “At some part, I agree with you but never make someone feel like a burden because they are trying to stay connected.”
Another commenter expressed complete agreement, particularly with his point about daily good morning messages and people forwarding disaster videos.
The differing reactions highlighted a familiar dilemma in the digital age: while excessive messages and unsolicited videos can overwhelm recipients, such gestures may also be a way for some people to maintain relationships and feel connected to family and friends.
Akram's light-hearted advice highlights the importance of digital etiquette in an age when smartphones and social media have become central to everyday communication. His message is not necessarily about discouraging older people from using technology, but about encouraging them to be mindful of other people's time, attention and boundaries.
At the same time, staying connected should not make anyone feel like a nuisance or a burden. Whether it is forwarding videos, sending daily greetings or making frequent calls, a little consideration can go a long way. Ultimately, the goal is to use technology to strengthen relationships, not strain them, while remembering that meaningful connections matter far more than the number of messages exchanged.

title: Quetta chamber urges traders to reject  negative propaganda  amid Iran border closure
description: Chamber says the closure is temporary  urges traders to suspend new purchases from Iran
content:
Chamber says the closure is temporary, urges traders to suspend new purchases from Iran
The Quetta Chamber of Commerce and Industry on Sunday urged traders and people affected by the closure of the Pakistan-Iran border not to believe any “negative propaganda”, expressing hope that the situation would improve soon.
The appeal came as cross-border commercial activities between Pakistan and Iran were suddenly halted at the Taftan border crossing on Saturday following the unexpected closure of the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) immigration gate and withdrawal of an important import waiver, leaving traders concerned over potential multi-million-rupee financial losses.
According to a statement issued by the president of the Quetta Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the president, while in contact with senior officials regarding the closure of the borders adjoining Iran, informed the Ministry of Commerce about the difficulties being faced by traders, importers and other businesses.
Read : Trade at Taftan comes to a grinding halt
The statement said the Ministry of Commerce assured the chamber that the border closure was on technical and temporary grounds, with the sole purpose of addressing incidents involving vehicles on the Pakistan-Iran highway in recent days and issues faced at customs.
The chamber urged all traders and people affected by the border closures to remain hopeful that the situation would improve soon and not to believe any “baseless negative propaganda” in this regard.
Sources said the immigration gate at Taftan — a vital commercial artery connecting the two neighbouring countries — was closed on the instructions of senior officials in Islamabad.
However, the exact reasons behind the decision remain undisclosed, and authorities have yet to issue an official notification explaining the suspension or providing a timeline for reopening.
The border closure coincided with regulatory developments from the Ministry of Commerce.
On Friday, the ministry issued an office memorandum, No. 9(3)/2017-IRAN, withdrawing its earlier order dated Oct 3, which had extended the Electronic Import Form (EIF) waiver for imports from Iran.
Also Read : FM Dar, Iranian FM discuss regional situation, OIC meeting in Baghdad
Responding to the evolving situation, the Chamber of Commerce and Industry Quetta, Balochistan, issued an urgent advisory to its members and the broader business community, recommending a temporary suspension of all new purchases, product bookings and trade commitments from Iran.
Meanwhile, Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei, commenting on reports about the closure of the land border with Pakistan, said: “Due to certain technical issues and the need to take precautionary measures, border crossings and exchanges have been temporarily suspended. However, the relevant authorities of the two countries are in close contact and are holding consultations to resolve the issue as soon as possible and restore normal operations at the border crossings.”

Says some officials planned to settle abroad while still serving the government
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Sunday questioned the commitment of senior bureaucrats to Pakistan, alleging that a significant number of government officers had planned to settle abroad while still serving the country.
In a statement on X, Asif said that while Pakistan’s bureaucracy had capable and honest officers, many officials had made Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom and other European countries their permanent homes over the past several years.
He alleged that some officers had prepared for their relocation under a deliberate plan while employed by the Government of Pakistan, raising questions about their commitment to the country and their official responsibilities during their tenure.
Asif said Portugal had emerged as a destination for what he described as a bureaucratic exodus in recent years. He added that he had raised the issue on social media a few months ago.
The defence minister said the officers whose names had surfaced in connection with the matter had held important positions and had remained close to successive governments.

He further alleged that an individual who facilitated permanent residency (PR) arrangements had fled after collecting substantial sums of money from several influential bureaucrats.
Asif said several troubling accounts were circulating in connection with the matter, although he did not provide details or identify the individuals allegedly involved.
Questioning the commitment of senior officials who had occupied high offices and enjoyed the privileges and respect associated with public service, Asif asked whether their loyalty to Pakistan remained beyond suspicion throughout their careers.
He also questioned the conduct of officials who, he said, had enjoyed opportunities to accumulate wealth through both legitimate and illegitimate means while remaining favoured by politicians.
“Does it rise above all doubt and suspicion, or are they merely in transit?” Asif asked, questioning whether such officials viewed Pakistan as their permanent home or merely a temporary stop before settling abroad.

His remarks have brought renewed attention to questions surrounding the overseas settlement plans of serving and retired civil servants, particularly those holding influential positions in the government.

title: Eric Dane reveals heartbreaking details of his ALS battle in posthumous memoir
description: Eric Dane reflects on his ALS battle  addiction recovery and family in My Book of Days  his memoir arriving November 3
content:
Eric Dane reflects on his ALS battle, addiction recovery and family in My Book of Days, his memoir arriving November 3
Eric Dane opens up about his career, addiction struggles, family life and battle with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) in his upcoming memoir, My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments . The book offers a personal account of the actor’s life before his death in February 2026, aged 53.
In an exclusive excerpt published by PEOPLE on October 18, Dane recounts the early symptoms of ALS, which he first noticed on January 7, 2024. While eating sushi with his daughters, he struggled to hold chopsticks with his right hand. After months of seeking answers, he was diagnosed with the progressive neurological disease in April 2025.
Dane describes calling his estranged wife, actress Rebecca Gayheart, after receiving the diagnosis. Although the couple had filed for divorce after 14 years of marriage, they remained close and continued raising their daughters together.
The memoir also revisits Dane’s struggles with substance addiction, including a relapse during his time on Grey’s Anatomy . He joined the medical drama in 2005 as Dr Mark Sloan, a role that brought him widespread recognition. However, his addiction affected his personal life and work, leading him to seek rehabilitation five times during his tenure on the show.
Dane also reflects on his departure from Grey’s Anatomy in 2012, explaining that financial considerations, rather than his addiction alone, led to the end of his character’s run. He later starred in The Last Ship and HBO’s Euphoria .
In the book, Dane shares emotional moments with his daughters, Billie and Georgia, as ALS progressively affected his mobility. He recalls being unable to hug Billie after her ballet performance, describing the experience as painful but deeply meaningful.
Despite his illness, Dane urged his daughters to remain resilient and never give up. My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments will be published on November 3, 2026, by The Open Field, an imprint of Penguin Publishing Group.

title: Pope Leo pledges gradual return to duties in first event since cancer surgery
description: Pope is planning to visit Uruguay  Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17
content:
Pope is planning to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17
Pope Leo pledged on Sunday ​to slowly resume his usual activities as the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics as he ‌greeted crowds in St Peter's Square during his first public event since undergoing surgery for lung cancer five days ago.
The 71-year-old pontiff had an operation on Tuesday to remove the lower lobe of his right lung, fuelling speculation about how his illness might change his 17-month papacy.
Smiling from ​a window of the Vatican's Apostolic Palace as he spoke to pilgrims below in a firm, clear ​voice on Sunday, the first US pope thanked people across the world for their prayers and ⁠said he would now begin to resume his normal schedule.
Read : Pope Leo returns to Vatican four days after lung cancer surgery
"Having overcome this delicate phase... I will now gradually resume ​my activities, always with the help of God and your prayers," Leo said.
The pope, who was discharged from Rome's Gemelli ​hospital on Saturday, came to the window in the palace unaided and held his weekly midday appointment as usual.
He also urged pilgrims waiting below under cloudy skies to set aside any selfish ambitions and serve God "without compromise".
Leo has been diagnosed with lung ​adenocarcinoma , the most common form of lung cancer. The diagnosis, for the youngest pope in decades, who was elected only ​in May 2025, caused shock.
Read More : Pope Leo diagnosed with cancer
His doctors discharged him on Saturday after blood tests and chest imaging that day showed him well enough ‌to return ⁠home. They said he was able to perform normal daily activities independently.
Crowds in St Peter's Square, numbering about 15,000 according to the Vatican, shouted and clapped loudly as Leo first appeared at the window on Sunday. One Catholic nun knelt and cried, holding her hand over her face.
A few steps away, a group of other nuns held aloft a sign ​reading, "Best wishes, Holy Father. We ​love you, and we are ⁠praying for you".
Leo usually keeps a busy schedule, but the Vatican has cancelled his other public events until at least Wednesday, when he is due to hold ​a weekly general audience in St Peter's Square. It has not said whether he ​will hold that ⁠audience.
The pope is also planning to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17, in one of the most intense trips arranged for a Catholic leader in decades .
Dr Stefano Margaritora, the pope's lead surgeon, said on Saturday that Leo could be ⁠fully recovered ​in time for that trip.
Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican's secretary of state, ​has however expressed scepticism. He told journalists on Friday the pope may need to adjust the pace of his schedule going forward "according to the condition ​of his health".

title: Stanley Tucci has    no idea    why he   s the internet   s favourite boyfriend
description: I don   t know  I   ve been around a long time  So maybe I just wore them down   Tucci said
content:
"I don’t know, I’ve been around a long time. So maybe I just wore them down," Tucci said
Stanley Tucci has admitted he has “no idea” why he has become the internet’s favourite boyfriend, joking that years in the public eye may have helped win over fans. The 65-year-old actor discussed his unexpected online popularity in an exclusive interview with PEOPLE, reflecting on the viral moment that helped turn him into an internet heartthrob.
“I have no idea — I really don’t,” Tucci said when asked about his popularity. “I’m glad they are.” He added, “I don’t know, I’ve been around a long time. So maybe I just wore them down.”
Tucci traced the surge in his online fandom to the 2020 lockdown, when his wife, literary agent Felicity Blunt, encouraged him to share a video of himself making a cocktail on Instagram. The clip quickly attracted attention, transforming the actor’s image among fans and helping establish his reputation as an internet boyfriend.
“It’s all my wife’s doing,” Tucci joked, adding that he sometimes wonders whether Blunt was “trying to get rid of me”. He recalled reading the comments with his older children during lockdown and laughing at their overtly sexual nature.
“It was very funny for an older man. It was very flattering,” he said.
The actor has since continued sharing glimpses of his life beyond acting, particularly through cooking videos featuring Italian dishes. Tucci said the ideas for his food tutorials sometimes come spontaneously, while others are planned with help from Blunt, whom he credited with knowing “what to film and when to film it”.
Tucci’s internet popularity has also drawn attention from his longtime The Devil Wears Prada co-star Meryl Streep. During his Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony in April, Streep praised his elegance and charm, describing him as “urbane, sly and funny”. She also expressed her affection for the actor, declaring, “I’m in love with you, just like everybody else.”
Despite his online heartthrob status, Tucci offered a more domestic glimpse into his life, revealing that his family calls him “Cinderella” because of his habit of constantly cleaning the kitchen. He explained that he struggles to focus when the space is untidy and often cleans it several times a day.
Tucci is currently starring in Masterplan , a Prime Video film in which he plays Roger, a master thief who recruits two strangers for a heist targeting the Mona Lisa before revealing their family connection. The actor said he was drawn to the project by its unusual humour, complex character and resemblance to classic heist films from the 1960s and 1970s.
As his popularity continues to reach audiences beyond his film roles, Tucci said he has become more comfortable being himself on camera. For the actor, that shift has come with age and experience, even if the internet’s enthusiasm for him remains something of a mystery.

title: Messi brace fires Miami to victory | The Express Tribune
description: The 39-year-old superstar tops the Major League Soccer scoring chart with 25 goals
content:
The 39-year-old superstar tops the Major League Soccer scoring chart with 25 goals
Lionel Messi scored twice in the space of four minutes to lift Inter Miami to a 3-1 victory at Atlanta United on Saturday as the Herons' MLS title defense continued to gain steam with the playoffs approaching.
The 39-year-old superstar tops the Major League Soccer scoring chart with 25 goals, six ahead of Croatian striker Petar Musa of FC Dallas and Philadelphia's Milan Iloski.
At the same Atlanta stadium where Messi helped Argentina beat England in the World Cup semi-finals in July, Messi delivered two scintillating goals to secure Miami's third straight victory.
German Berterame, who put Miami up 1-0 in the 45th minute, turned provider, finding Messi who weaved through the Atlanta defense to unleash a left footed shot from the center of the box and make it 2-0 in the 56th minute.
Four minutes later Messi struck again, breaking away on a pass from Luis Suarez and getting the better of hapless Junior Alonso to fire past Atlanta keeper Lucas Hoyos.
Messi had helped put Miami on top shortly before halftime, heading the ball to Suarez who shook off his defender in the box and lofted a pass that Berterame nodded home to make it 1-0.
Messi was credited with an assist, that saw him pull level with LAFC's Son Heung-min atop the assists table. Messi is the first player in MLS history to record at least 15 assists in three straight seasons.
Messi now has four goals in three matches since his emotional Argentina send-off. Miami, who clinched a playoff berth on Wednesday, won their third straight game under Cristian "Kily" Gonzalez, who took over as coach last month.
Fafa Picault converted a penalty in the 89th minute to pull a goal back for Atlanta, but at second-from-bottom in the Eastern Conference Gerardo Martino's team are running out of time to turn things around in time to reach the playoffs.
Elsewhere, St. Louis City's MLS record-tying 19-match unbeaten streak ended with a 3-2 loss at Minnesota as Philadelphia's undefeated run reached 15 matches with a 2-2 draw with Charlotte.
Canadian Marcus Caldeira scored the game winner for Minnesota in the 86th minute after United fell behind early on St. Louis goals by Brazilian forward Rafael Navarro and South Korean winger Jeong Sang-bin.
Aziel Jackson answered for Minnesota in the 49th minute and Kelvin Yeboah netted the equalizer in the 68th.
St. Louis City, already headed to the playoffs for the first time since 2023, missed the chance to break the MLS unbeaten streak mark it now shares with Columbus, Dallas and Inter Miami.
City also saw their MLS-record 21-match unbeaten streak across all competitions snapped.
City had not lost an MLS match since falling 2-0 at Austin on May 3, with 13 victories and six drawn in the run.
Philadelphia had won eight MLS matches in a row before the fightback home draw with Charlotte.
Philadelphia lost 6-4 at Miami on May 24 but since then the Union have won 12 times and drawn three, taking 39 of a possible 45 points since Ryan Richter took over as interim head coach during the league's World Cup break.

title: Bilawal slams PTI s Afridi over K P security  says PPP ready to fight terrorists
description: Says terrorism should not be used for  political point scoring   accuses Afridi of unwilling to  defend his own land
content:
Calls for 'united policy' against terrorism to end emergency in K-P
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Sunday lashed out at Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) “non-functional” chief minister Sohail Afridi over the province’s security situation, saying the PPP was ready to fight terrorists if the PTI-led provincial government was unwilling to do so.
"If the chief minister of K-P is not ready to fight terrorists, then PPP is ready to fight them, and that is why we supported the government's decision to impose governors' rule", Bilawal said while speaking to the media during a visit to the Karsaz Monument on the anniversary of the Karsaz bombing.
He also defended the imposition of governor’s rule, saying his party had backed the move in view of the security challenges.
Read : Bilawal offers to approach PM for ending K-P emergency if PTI agrees to political dialogue
Bilawal underscored that Pakistan was once again confronting “terrorism from Khyber to Khuzdar”, recalling that the PPP government in 2008 had launched operations in Swat and other parts of K-P to fulfil a commitment made by former prime minister Benazir Bhutto.
“When the PPP formed the government in 2008, we launched operations in Swat and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and defeated the terrorists,” he said, adding that Pakistan was now facing the consequences of decisions to release militants who had previously been held in the country’s prisons.
Bilawal recalled that Benazir, in her final public address, had warned that certain forces did not want Swat to remain part of Pakistan. He said the country was once again facing attempts to undermine its control in the region.
He also criticised the handling of terrorism-related incidents, saying such attacks were not taken seriously and alleging that evidence had been washed away even in the Karsaz attack.
The PPP chairman said his party had once been at the forefront of the fight against terrorism, but the struggle had since become a collective responsibility, with citizens across the country striving for peace.
Bilawal underscored that terrorism should not be used for political point-scoring and urged political leaders to speak out unequivocally against terrorists
Read More : Bilawal accuses K-P of facilitating terrorists
Bilawal further stressed the importance of political reconciliation and consensus, citing Benazir’s efforts to strengthen democracy despite political differences and compromises.
He stated that Benazir had worked with parties that had previously opposed her and former prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, including during the Movement for the Restoration of Democracy (MRD).
PPP chairman also cited the 18th Amendment as an example of consensus-building, saying it had been passed after political parties sat together to deliberate. Political negotiations required all sides to find common ground, he added.
Bilawal said the current political climate called for the implementation of the government’s manifesto and measures to provide relief to the public on key issues.
While responding to a question about the creation of new provinces, he reiterated that the PPP supported establishing provinces through constitutional and legal means. However, he said such a move could not proceed without President Asif Ali Zardari’s endorsement.
He questioned why new provinces were not being created in areas where consensus already existed, citing Gilgit-Baltistan as an example. He also said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi was aware of the PPP’s position on the matter.
Commenting on Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s criticism of the government, Bilawal said the opposition leader had the right to question government policies but should also have unequivocally condemned terrorism.
He said members of Fazl’s own party had been killed in terrorist attacks and argued that the issue should not be exploited for political gain.
Bilawal added that whenever the PPP had imposed an emergency, it had acted in accordance with the Constitution and the law. He said the party’s decisions demonstrated its commitment to democratic principles rather than political self-interest.

title: Quentin Tarantino confirms script for tenth film but wants to    live a little    first
description: I   ve written a script that I really like  but I want to do the play and see who I am   Tarantino said
content:
“I’ve written a script that I really like, but I want to do the play and see who I am," Tarantino said
Quentin Tarantino has confirmed that he has written a script for his tenth film, but the acclaimed filmmaker is not ready to move forward with the project just yet. Instead, Tarantino plans to focus on his upcoming stage production, spend time with his family and take a break before deciding what comes next.
The Pulp Fiction director shared the update during an appearance on The Graham Norton Show , where he explained that he is happy with the screenplay but does not want to rush into making another film.
“I’ve written a script that I really like, but I want to do the play and see who I am; then I’ll then go back and spend time with my family and live a little and then see what I want to do,” Tarantino said.
The filmmaker has long maintained that he intends to retire from directing after making ten feature films, making the new script a significant development for fans waiting to see his final directorial project. However, his latest comments suggest that production is not imminent, and he has not revealed the film’s title, storyline or potential cast.
Before returning to filmmaking, Tarantino will turn his attention to The Popinjay Cavalier , his upcoming West End play starring Sacha Baron Cohen. The production began as a screenplay before Tarantino decided that the story would work better on stage.
Described as a swashbuckling comedy, The Popinjay Cavalier is scheduled to open at London’s Phoenix Theatre in March 2027, following previews in late February. The production is expected to run for three months, with its closing date set for June 13.
Tarantino’s most recent feature film as a director was Once Upon a Time in Hollywood , released in 2019 and starring Leonardo DiCaprio, Brad Pitt and Margot Robbie. Pitt won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for his performance, while Tarantino received nominations for Best Director and Best Original Screenplay.
Although the script for his tenth film is now written, Tarantino has made clear that he wants to experience life beyond filmmaking before deciding whether to take the project into production. For now, his focus remains on bringing The Popinjay Cavalier to the London stage.

title: Davidovich Fokina beats Jodar to win Shanghai Masters
description: The Spaniard rallies from a set down to defeat Jodar 1 6  7 6  7 5   6 4
content:
The Spaniard rallies from a set down to defeat Jodar 1-6, 7-6 (7/5), 6-4
Alejandro Davidovich Fokina fought back to beat rising star Rafael Jodar in the final of the Shanghai Masters on Sunday to claim the biggest title of his career.
The gutsy world number 26 from Spain outlasted his tiring compatriot 1-6, 7-6 (7/5), 6-4.
"I don't know what to say. I don't know what I feel. Just like a huge relief," Davidovich Fokina said.
It is a first title at the prestigious 1000 level for the 27-year-old, who extended his winning streak in China to 10 matches after claiming victory at an ATP 250 tournament in Chengdu.
The 20-year-old Jodar, ranked 13 and rising fast, was ruthless to start with.
He reached over his shoulder to save a point before winning it with an overhead smash as he broke for a 2-0 lead.
Davidovich Fokina put pressure on his backhand, but Jodar kept calm as his opponent succumbed to a series of errors.
Jodar broke again to go up 5-1 before closing out the first set after just 27 minutes with an ace.
A fighting Davidovich Fokina refused to go away.
He dropped serve to hand Jodar a 3-2 lead in the second set but finally came up with some answers in the next game, falling on his back to save a point at the net and level at 3-3.
Both men battled to hold serve in a run of intense rallies, with the duo needing to restart a point during the ninth game when a ball rolled onto the court.
Davidovich Fokina was shouting in frustration but saved two break points to go up 6-5 when Jodar returned into the net.
But the younger Spaniard would not crumble, sending down a dangerous backhand to force a tie-break.
The duo were neck and neck but Davidovich Fokina held his nerve in the tie-break to force a decider.
He was suddenly in control, breaking Jodar's serve in the first game.
His celebration was cut short when Jodar grabbed back a break.
But it went his way again when Jodar fired long to hand the elder Spaniard a 3-2 lead.
Jodar needed a medical timeout for his right thigh as he trailed Davidovich Fokina 4-3.
He buckled in pain as he went for a point during a must-win ninth game, keeping the match alive for a bit longer but needing a trainer for his left thigh at 5-4.
Davidovich Fokina sensed victory and claimed the title on his second championship point.

content:
Green-shirts dominate their opponents to secure their second successive win in the event
Pakistan junior hockey team continued their impressive run in the Sultan of Johor Cup 2026, defeating Canada 6-2 in their second match to record back-to-back victories.
The win followed Pakistan's emphatic 8-3 win over China in their opening match on Saturday, giving the team an encouraging start to the competition.
Pakistan took control early against Canada, with Hamza Fayyaz opening the scoring in the ninth minute before Hamza Ali doubled the advantage five minutes later.
Rana Abdullah Sami extended Pakistan's lead in the 25th minute, putting the team firmly in command. Canada responded through Bhullar Gurnoor in the 30th minute to reduce the deficit to 3-1.
Pakistan restored their three-goal advantage in the 38th minute when Rana Waleed scored the team's fourth goal.
Canada attempted to fight back, with Abhiram Yogeshwaran finding the net in the 45th minute to make it 4-2. However, Pakistan maintained their attacking pressure in the final quarter and added two more goals to secure the victory.
Aasam Haider scored in the 51st minute before Adeel completed the scoring in the 54th, sealing Pakistan's 6-2 win.
The result further strengthened Pakistan's position after their commanding performance against China on Saturday.
Pakistan Hockey Federation’s (PHF) president Mohyuddin Ahmad Wani congratulated the junior team and its players on the victory, praising their performance and wishing them success in their upcoming matches.
Pakistan will look to maintain their winning momentum as the brigade will meet hosts Malaysia on October 21.
This is an Under-21 event in which defending champions Australia are not participating.
Canada, Pakistan, China, Malaysia and Japan compete in the competitions. Top two teams will qualify for the October 24 final.
The third and fourth sided will play for the third place game on the same day.
After facing Malaysia in their next show on October 21 Pakistan will then meet Japan in their final show on October 23.
The event is being held at the Taman Daya Hockey Stadium in Johar Bahru.

title: Nadia Afgan draws parallels between her family life  Dar e Nijaat
description: The actor   s own relations with her in laws offers a real life contrast to the emotional turmoil in Dar e Nijaat
content:
Says her relationship with in-laws offers real-life contrast to the emotional turmoil in Dar-e-Nijaat
Pakistani actor Nadia Afgan recently offered a glimpse into her own family life, sharing a heartfelt account of the kindness she has experienced from her husband Jodi’s family, a reality that reminded her of the fictional character Zaryab in the drama series Dar-e-Nijaat .
In a social media post, Nadia reflected on how her experience of marriage challenged her expectations of in-laws, particularly the relationship she has developed with her mother-in-law. Her words offered a refreshing reminder that, despite the negative family dynamics often portrayed in television dramas and encountered in real life, loving and supportive families do exist.
“Story time: People like Abu Bakar and his mother do exist,” Afgan wrote, referring to the compassionate family dynamic depicted in Dar-e-Nijaat .
She continued by describing her own experience after marrying Jodi, explaining that his family’s warmth had surprised her.
“When Jodi and I got married, I was as shocked as Zaryaab. His parents and his family were and still are the loveliest, most decent, and kindest people in the world.”
Nadia also spoke affectionately about her mother-in-law, describing the bond they share as one that has grown beyond the conventional expectations of a relationship between a woman and her husband’s family.
“I have come to love my mother-in-law like my own mother; she loves me so much,” she shared.
The actor even recalled asking her husband a question that captured just how unexpected this kindness had been for her: “Are you guys actually that nice? And you guys do not argue with each other? Are you aliens?".
Her humorous observation, which translates roughly to asking whether his family really was that nice and why they never fought among themselves, added a personal and relatable touch to her account.
Afgan concluded her message with a sentiment that resonated with the drama’s central themes: “So, I can relate to Zaryaab, and believe me, good humans do exist.”
Nadia’s remarks draw an interesting parallel with Dar-e-Nijaat , a Pakistani television drama that explores love, family relationships, trust, morality and the consequences of personal choices.
The story follows Zaryab, played by Durefishan Saleem, whose life takes a painful turn after her long-standing relationship with her childhood sweetheart, Zamil, ends in betrayal. Zamil, played by Nameer Khan, moves on with his life without giving Zaryab the honesty or consideration she expected from someone she had trusted for years.
In contrast, Abu Bakar, portrayed by Sheheryar Munawar, represents a different kind of male character — one whose compassion and family values become increasingly significant as Zaryab struggles to come to terms with her heartbreak.
The drama’s portrayal of Abu Bakar and his mother, Khushbakht, provides the context for Nadia’s comparison. Their relationship highlights the possibility of a family environment built on affection, loyalty and mutual respect, rather than conflict and hostility.
One of the most touching aspects of Nadia’s post is the affection she expresses for her mother-in-law. In a society where stories of strained relationships between daughters-in-law and their husbands’ families are common in popular entertainment, her experience offers a different perspective.
Television dramas frequently draw audiences in through misunderstandings, family rivalries, controlling relatives and difficult marriages. While these conflicts can reflect genuine social concerns, they do not represent every household.
Afgan’s account suggests that family relationships can also be sources of comfort, acceptance and belonging. The actor herself got married to Jawad Samar Khan, also known as Jodi Pai in June 2008. Recently, the actor starred in the drama serial Pas E Dewaar and Hey Fam . She is also expected to play a side role in Dar-e-Nijaat in the coming episodes.

title: Visa delay costs Waseem five fight deal
description: Boxer urges government to issue diplomatic passport after losing Mexican promotion opportunity
content:
Boxer urges government to issue diplomatic passport after losing Mexican promotion opportunity
Pakistan’s professional boxer Mohammad Waseem, the WBA bantamweight gold champion, on Sunday said a delay in obtaining a Schengen visa cost him a potential five-fight deal with a Mexican promotion company.
Waseem submitted his passport for a Schengen visa at the Spanish Embassy in Islamabad on July 29 but is still waiting for its issuance.
“Yes, I was going to sign a deal with a Mexican company, but due to the visa delay, I could not finalise the agreement. Under the proposed deal, I could have had five fights, and it is a huge loss for me,” Waseem told The Express Tribune on Sunday.
The former three-time WBC world flyweight silver champion said he did not know why his visa application had been delayed.
“I don’t know what the reason is,” he said.
Waseem said visa problems had repeatedly deprived him of important opportunities during his professional career.
“In the past, too, visa issues denied me several golden opportunities. I missed a WBO title fight in Dubai in 2022 because of a visa issue, and then I had to rush to Malta on the eve of my fight in 2024 because of a visa delay. Moreover, I was unable to obtain visas for international training on several occasions,” he said.
“This problem has dented my career,” Waseem added.
He appealed to the federal government to issue him a diplomatic passport, saying it could help him avoid similar difficulties when travelling abroad for fights and training.
“I need a diplomatic passport. I have requested the federal government several times in the past, but there has been no response. Had I received visas on time, I could have won several world titles by now,” he said.
Waseem has recently won back-to-back WBA bantamweight gold titles in Quetta and Lahore.
Since turning professional in 2015, he has fought 17 bouts, winning 15 and losing two.
Waseem has also played for Pakistan as an amateur fighter for over a decade, having also won Commonwealth Games silver and Asian Games bronze.
Meanwhile Waseem also requested the federal government to financially back him so that he could hold a world title fight in Pakistan.
“I aim to hold a world title fight here and I request the federal government for support,” Waseem said.
Waseem is a rare fighter who won the WBC World silver flyweight title in only his fourth professional bout. He successfully defended the title three months later before winning it again. He also remained the WBC's number-one-ranked boxer in his division for an extended period.
Waseem has lost only two fights in his professional career, both of them world title bouts against South Africa's Moruti Mthalane and England's Sunny Edwards, despite the Pakistani boxer putting up strong performances in both contests.

title: Yin wins in Shanghai for back to back LPGA titles
description: The Chinese golfer finishes on 11 under to seal a thrilling home victory
content:
The Chinese golfer finishes on 11-under to seal a thrilling home victory
Home hero Yin Ruoning celebrated back-to-back LPGA Tour titles with a thrilling one-stroke victory in Shanghai on Sunday.
China's Yin carded a final-round four-under-par 68 at an energised Sheshan Golf Club to emerge victorious from a showdown with overnight leader Choi Hye-jin.
The 24-year-old Yin, winner at the FM Championship in Boston in August on her previous start on tour, finished on 11-under, one shot clear of Choi.
It was Yin's seventh LPGA title and her second in Shanghai, having won the event in 2024.
"I think this tournament means everything to me because you have the chance to play in front of all your family and friends and in front of all the amazing fans," she said.
South Korea's Choi was left kicking herself, having been in the lead after all three previous rounds and seemingly on course for her maiden LPGA crown.
She started the final day with a two-shot advantage over Yin but successive bogeys at the seventh and eighth saw her lead evaporate.
Roared on by the home fans, Yin was on the charge, four of her five birdies coming in her last nine holes.
She sank a nerveless putt for birdie on the 17th that effectively sealed the deal, and marked victory with a low-key pump of the fists.
"I mean, I still have emotions, but this time very calm, more calm than FM," she said, comparing her understated celebration this time with her jubilant win two months ago.
"I think it's a dream come true to win at home, and I think I'm lucky to win it twice.
South Korea's Amy Yang was third on eight-under, with Japan's Rio Takeda another shot back.

The PCB officials also remained tight-lipped over the issue when this correspondent approached.
Rizwan, who has been facing an investigation by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), was initially not permitted to play first-class cricket, alongside fellow batsman Imam-ul-Haq. His possible return comes as the domestic first-class season approaches its final stages.
Despite the uncertainty surrounding his career in the wake of the NCCIA probe the wicket-keeper batsman has continued training regularly in Peshawar and is in excellent physical condition.
“He is in top shape. He never stopped training and regularly went to the ground twice a day for practice,” a source close to Rizwan told this correspondent.
“I think he has been allowed by the PCB to play domestic cricket, and he will be heading towards Rawalpindi to feature in the match,” the source added.
Rizwan was among seven players sent home following Pakistan’s heavy defeat against England at Lord’s.
And latter NCCIA initiated a probe against him for his alleged involvement in online betting.
Rizwan subsequently challenged the proceedings in the Lahore High Court (LHC), which dismissed his petition and advised him to cooperate with the NCCIA. The court also directed the NCCIA not to harass the cricketer.
Rizwan is expected to lead SNGPL against KRL if his availability is confirmed. SNGPL are at the bottom of the table and on the brink of relegation.

title: Smith says head blow left him anxious in first test concussion scare
description: The Australian returns to action after recovering from the blow in Durban
content:
The Australian returns to action after recovering from the blow in Durban
Australia batsman Steve Smith said he was anxious after being hit on the head and facing the prospect of another concussion after a blow playing against South Africa in the first test a week ago.
Former captain Smith has previously suffered multiple concussions in his career, and ‌he had to go through concussion protocols after a bouncer from Anrich Nortje hit him on the helmet last Monday during the second-last day of the clash at Kingsmead in Durban.
“I was a little bit anxious after the hit, to be honest,” Smith said on Sunday before the start of the second test at St George’s Park in a television interview.
“It was a decent knock, and the rest of that day, ⁠I wasn't travelling too well, and I think it was more to do with anxiety, of hoping not to feel what I felt in the past, waking up the next morning and things like that.
“So, yeah, fortunately, I woke up well. I passed all the tests, and things recovered pretty quickly,” Smith added as he prepared to take part in the rain-delayed second test.
The 37-year-old was assessed on the field by the physio and the doctor, and his helmet was changed as is mandatory for all such hits, but he continued his innings, scoring 27 runs as Australia built a large lead.
But then Smith did not take to the field at the start ‌of South ⁠Africa's second innings on Monday, instead being subjected to the concussion protocols, which he passed.
He returned from the start of the last day’s play on Tuesday to help his side to a 214-run victory and a 1-0 lead in the three-match series.
Smith, who is 28 short of 11,000 test runs, was the first player replaced in a test after the introduction of a ⁠concussion substitute. He was struck on the back of the head by a Jofra Archer bouncer in the 2019 Ashes test at Lord's in London.
He also suffered a concussion after being hit on the head in practice during Australia's One Day International series ⁠in England in 2020 and two months later, back home in Sydney, woke on the morning of the second ODI against India with vertigo and was sick.
There have also been incidents in Sri Lanka in 2022, at ⁠the last World Cup in India and last December in the Ashes at Adelaide where he was ruled out of the third test about 20 minutes before the toss with a vestibular issue, the sensory system located in the inner ear that controls balance and spatial orientation.

title: PM Shehbaz stresses equal opportunities in education to realize Quaid s vision
description: Says Daanish School graduates show what children could accomplish when given access to education
content:
Says Daanish School graduates show what children could accomplish when given access to education
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Sunday said every child in Pakistan deserved equal access to education, regardless of their family’s wealth or social status, stressing that the country could not fulfil Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah’s vision without providing equal opportunities to all.
“Whether she is the daughter of a poor person or he is the son of a labourer, whether it is an orphan girl or an orphan boy, whether he is the son of a rich person or she is the daughter of a rich person, everyone should have equal opportunities for education and treatment,” the prime minister said while addressing the inauguration of a Daanish School in Islamabad.
Reflecting on the sacrifices made during the creation of Pakistan in 1947, the prime minister said millions of people had left their homes and belongings behind in the hope of building a country founded on justice, merit and equal opportunities.
He emphasized that Pakistan could not fully realize its founding ideals unless every child, from Karachi to Peshawar and from Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa to Gilgit-Baltistan, had access to quality education and healthcare.
“After eighty years down the lane, we must pause and honestly introspect what we had dreamt of in 1947,” he remarked, questioning whether the prevailing disparities in the education system reflected the Pakistan envisioned by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
PM Shehbaz said the accounts of students from disadvantaged backgrounds had moved the audience, highlighting how access to quality education had transformed their lives and opened doors to opportunities that might otherwise have remained out of reach.
“Until we achieve this goal, Pakistan will not be the Pakistan envisioned by Quaid-e-Azam,” the prime minister added.
The prime minister referred to the story of a student from Balochistan who had attended a Daanish School in Dera Ghazi Khan and was now serving as an officer at Punjab Safe Cities.
“He said that when he came from Balochistan to the Daanish School in Dera Ghazi Khan, he was apprehensive about how he would be treated in Punjab,” the prime minister recalled.
“But this Daanish School treated the children from Balochistan and other provinces like a caring mother, and ultimately everyone said: this is the real Pakistan, where we are all equal and united,” he said.
PM Shehbaz also referred to students from Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) and Gilgit-Baltistan (G-B) who had shared accounts of their experiences. He praised the courage of the children who spoke about the difficulties they had overcome, saying their stories had moved the audience.
Read: Pakistan's progress linked to education, teachers, says Shehbaz
“If these great sons and daughters of the nation can stand tall and tell the entire nation their stories, despite being overcome with emotion, why should I not stand here and pay tribute to them and their parents?” he said.
He noted that Daanish School graduates had gone on to become doctors, engineers, police officers, bureaucrats, sales managers and teachers, adding that the initiative represented the realisation of Quaid-e-Azam’s vision.
Recalling the initiative’s origins during his tenure as Punjab chief minister, PM Shehbaz questioned why children from affluent families could attend elite institutions while millions of equally talented children from poor households could not access comparable education.
He said the disparity had prompted his team to establish Daanish Schools in Punjab in 2010, with the aim of providing quality education to children whose circumstances might otherwise limit their opportunities.
The prime minister highlighted the journeys of Daanish School students and graduates to demonstrate how access to education could change lives.
“Imagine the plight of children like this daughter from Bahawalpur, this daughter from K-P, and this boy sitting before you, who also became a doctor,” he said.
The prime minister said the achievements of Daanish School graduates showed what children could accomplish when given access to education. Graduates had gone on to become doctors, engineers, police officers, bureaucrats, sales managers and teachers, he added.
Read more: PM Shehbaz vows equal education opportunities to realise Quaid-e-Azam’s welfare-state vision
Recalling the origins of the Daanish Schools initiative during his tenure as Punjab chief minister, PM Shehbaz said, “How come the sons of rich people enter the iron steel gates of Aitchison College?” he said, referring to children of prime ministers, governors, bureaucrats, judges, civil servants, landlords and mill owners.
He contrasted their opportunities with those available to children from poorer households across the country, including AJK and G-B, saying many talented students could not even imagine attending such institutions, let alone receiving a comparable education.
PM Shehbaz said the disparity had prompted his team to introduce Daanish Schools in Punjab in 2010. “The concept was introduced in Punjab, not only to match the quality and level of Aitchison College and other grammar schools all over Punjab and other parts of Pakistan, but to excel,” he said.
He also called for information technology and artificial intelligence laboratories to be established in the schools, urging officials to ensure that students had access to modern knowledge and technology.
“Let these young sons and daughters of the nation have modern knowledge and modern technology in their hands, so that they can prove their mettle not only in Pakistan but across the world through honesty, hard work and integrity,” he said.
The Daanish Schools initiative was launched in Punjab in 2010 under then chief minister Shehbaz Sharif to provide quality education to talented children from underprivileged backgrounds. The programme was designed to give students from low-income families access to educational opportunities comparable to those available at elite institutions, with residential facilities and other support provided to help them continue their studies.
The initiative initially focused on rural and underserved areas of Punjab, with the schools offering boarding facilities alongside education. The programme was later extended beyond the province, with plans for new institutions in Balochistan and Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
