title: Vance acknowledges    failures    in US handling of Iran war
description: Tugboat struck by 2 unknown projectiles off UAE  1 injured  UK maritime agency
content:
Iran’s president hopes defence minister nominee can ‘survive,’ cites US ‘assassination list’
US Vice President JD Vance acknowledged “a lot of mistakes and a lot of fundamental failures” in the handling of the Iran war, as he faced questions over the conflict’s rising human and economic costs during a CBS News town hall on Sunday.
Vance made the remarks in response to Joey Amor, whose wife, Master Sgt Nicole Amor, was among six US Army Reserve soldiers killed in an Iranian strike on a military site in Kuwait in the opening hours of the war that began in late February. At least 21 US service members have been killed and hundreds wounded so far.
Amor questioned reports that the facility had not been adequately secured, demanding accountability from the Trump administration.
“Though the Iranian drone was the weapon that killed my wife, there were a lot of mistakes and a lot of fundamental failures that led up to that,” Amor said.
Vance acknowledged that there were shortcomings. “Sometimes information doesn't filter up to me,” he said, pledging to “take every single failure extremely seriously.”
The vice president also admitted that the positioning of US troops exposed weaknesses in the military’s approach. “I know that there are some issues with, for example … where troops were located that we realised was a huge mistake and that we could do better on. And we have changed that,” he said.
Vance pointed to the growing threat posed by inexpensive drones, saying the US military had altered its tactics to better protect troops and prevent further casualties.
Asked why Washington had still not secured a decisive victory despite President Donald Trump’s initial expectations, Vance argued that the US had “in some ways … won decisively,” but acknowledged the outcome also depended on Iran’s actions. “The enemy gets a vote here,” he said.
Vance defended the administration’s strategy, saying Washington was seeking a “final firm commitment from the Iranians that they're not going to rebuild their nuclear program.”
Iran’s president hopes defence minister nominee can ‘survive,’ cites US ‘assassination list’
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Sunday that he hopes his US-sanctioned defence minister nominee can “survive,” claiming that he is also on a US “assassination list.”
Pezeshkian made the remarks in a virtual address to parliament during a session considering Mehrdad Akhlaqi Ketabchi’s nomination as minister of defence, according to the semi-official ISNA news agency.
Pezeshkian said Akhlaqi is under US sanctions and claimed that he is also on a US “assassination list.” He expressed hope that the nominee would “take care of himself” and, with support from the country’s institutions, “remain alive” and continue working to strengthen Iran’s defence capabilities.
Pezeshkian urged lawmakers to give Akhlaqi a strong vote of confidence, saying he enjoys support across Iran’s armed forces, including the army, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), the defence ministry and security institutions.
Akhlaqi, a longtime senior defence ministry official, previously headed Iran’s Aerospace Industries Organisation and the Shahid Bagheri Industrial Group (SBIG), which has been linked to the country’s ballistic missile program.
He has been subject to US sanctions over his involvement in Iran’s missile-related activities.
Akhlaqi was nominated to replace former Defence Minister Aziz Nasirzadeh, who was killed during US-Israeli attacks on Iran earlier this year.
Pezeshkian said Iran does not seek to attack other countries but would respond strongly to any attack against its territory.
“Our defence is not only missiles; our defence is the people and the unity and cohesion we have in the country,” he said.
He added that Tehran would not back down in the face of what he described as pressure and “bullying” by countries that attack Iran.
Iranian parliament approves Mehrdad Akhlaqi as new defence minister
Iran’s parliament approved Mehrdad Akhlaqi Ketabchi as the country’s new defence minister on Sunday, the state broadcaster IRIB reported.
Akhlaqi received 237 votes in favor and 15 against, with no abstentions, out of 277 votes cast during a parliamentary session held via video conference.
Lawmakers voted after hearing arguments from supporters and opponents of Akhlaqi and reviewing his plans for the Defence Ministry.
In his first remarks after securing parliamentary approval, Akhlaqi said Iran had taken measures to counter the possible use by the US of the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast Bomb, known as the “Mother of All Bombs,” against the country.
“We have taken the necessary measures to counter such an action and are continuing our work with confidence,” he told reporters.
Akhlaqi also warned that US President Donald Trump should be concerned about getting American forces out of the region safely.
“If he drops one bomb, he should see how many of his forces he will have to take out of the region horizontally,” he said, apparently referring to potential US military casualties.
He claimed Iran’s preparations were among the reasons Washington had so far refrained from using the bomb, adding that the situation would be different if US threats were turned into action.
Addressing lawmakers before the vote, Akhlaqi warned that Iran would deliver a “surprising and extensive” response if the US and Israel launched another attack against the country.
“If the American-Zionist enemy once again makes a miscalculation, the response of the Iranian nation and the fighters of Islam will be surprising and extensive,” he said, adding that Washington and its allies would bear responsibility for any regional and international consequences.
Akhlaqi also said he had been on what he called his enemies’ “assassination list” for 35 years and pledged to further strengthen what Iran calls the “resistance front.”
He said his priorities would include expanding defence production across Iran’s industrial network, boosting research and adapting the Defence Ministry’s structure to current security threats.
Iran urges US to accept proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
Iran's offer to the United States to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days is still on the table, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Iranian media outlets on Sunday.
If Washington accepts Tehran's conditions, the strategic waterway would be open within six days, and US-Iran talks would resume on the seventh day, he added.
Iran accuses US of breaking agreements and derailing peace efforts
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi that the US had “repeatedly disrupted” diplomatic efforts to end the war by violating agreements and resorting to force, Al Jazeera reported.
JD Vance says petrol prices would be "three times as high" without US Navy
US Vice President JD Vance acknowledged that “gas prices are too high right now” but said prices would fall once the US-Israel war on Iran “is over”, Al Jazeera reported.
He blamed Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on tankers for driving up fuel costs, saying, “We’ve never had a situation like this” in which one country was “trying to completely choke off world energy supply”.
Vance claimed petrol prices would be “three times as high if it weren’t for the US Navy keeping oil and gas moving out of the Strait of Hormuz”.
He added that letting Iran control shipping through the strategic waterway would raise fuel costs for consumers. “If we just … left and we let the Iranians control shipping out of the Strait of Hormuz, what that would mean is you would pay a lot more for gasoline,” he said.
Tugboat struck by 2 unknown projectiles off UAE, 1 injured: UK maritime agency
A tugboat traveling southbound was struck by two unknown projectiles northeast of Khor Fakkan in the UAE on Sunday, leaving one person with minor injuries, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said.
The UKMTO said the vessel sustained damage but was able to continue on its route.
“One minor casualty has been reported,” it said, without providing further details about the injured person or the extent of the damage.
The exact time of the incident has yet to be confirmed.
Iran’s IRGC says two oil tankers caught fire after striking mines in Hormuz
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said two oil tankers, each carrying around two million barrels of crude oil, caught fire after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Al Jazeera reported.
It also reported that Iranian state television aired footage that purportedly showed an oil tanker exploding after hitting a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz.
The footage emerged as the US guided ships along a route off Oman’s coast, despite Iran’s warnings against unauthorised transit.
Trump says war on Iran will end “very quickly” at Kentucky rally
US President Donald Trump said the war on Iran would end “very quickly” while speaking at a rally in Kentucky ahead of the US midterm elections the following month, Al Jazeera reported.
He also claimed that Washington’s “excursion” in Iran had “knocked out their nuclear capacity.”

title: Rubio heads to Central Asia while other US officials hit foreign policy hot spots
description: US officials portray resource rich Central Asia worthy of more attention than it received from Trump s predecessors
content:
US officials portray resource-rich Central Asia worthy of more attention than it received from Trump's predecessors
While the Iran war smolders, Saudi Arabia fights the Houthis and a new rift opens in US-Ukraine relations, Secretary of State Marco Rubio travels on Sunday to ​Uzbekistan, a nation far removed from the biggest US foreign policy challenges.
The top US diplomat is scheduled to land in Samarkand on Sunday to meet with ‌leaders from the C5+1, a grouping that brings together the United States and the Muslim-majority post-Soviet states of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan.
US officials have portrayed resource-rich Central Asia — the region between China, Russia and Iran — as worthy of more attention than it received from US President Donald Trump's predecessors.
Trump hosted C5 leaders at the White House last November, when Kazakhstan agreed to join the Abraham Accords, a series of agreements under ​which Muslim-majority countries have normalized or deepened relations with Israel. Separately, Trump met with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev at the United Nations General Assembly last September.
Regional politics aside, ​the trip fits an emerging pattern in which Rubio often visits regions not at the center of the news cycle, while leaving some more ⁠fraught foreign-policy portfolios to other Trump aides, including special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and Vice President JD Vance.
Read: Leaders of Russia, China, Iran to attend summit in Kyrgyzstan
For instance, Rubio has not visited Kyiv or Moscow since becoming ​secretary of state. He was not present for talks between US and Ukrainian officials in Florida earlier this month, when US officials pressed Ukraine to stop hitting Russian refineries. Vance, not Rubio, ​represented the US in Pakistan during peace talks with Iran in April.
Rubio's previous foreign trip, in early October, took him to Greece, Portugal and Iceland.
Trump administration officials have typically rejected any suggestion that cabinet-level officials should focus their travels on geopolitical capitals and hot spots.
Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, for instance, said on X last week that the idea only certain destinations were worthy of visits from secretaries of state "perfectly encapsulates ​the decadence and degeneracy of the contemporary US foreign policy establishment."
One Central Asian diplomat, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said officials in the region are wondering to what ​extent the US will continue targeting Russian sanctions evasion. All C5 states, while drawing closer to the US, have deep historical ties with Moscow, and the region has facilitated Russian imports and exports that violate ‌US and ⁠European Union sanctions, Western officials say.
In the past, the US has pushed regional states to clamp down on those illicit flows.
But Trump struck a deal with Moscow this month to import Russian diesel, a move to lower domestic fuel prices before the congressional midterm elections. On Friday, Trump waived all provisions of legislation that would have allowed him to slap massive tariffs on some nations that buy significant amounts of Russian crude or otherwise help Moscow evade sanctions. Among the nations that could have been affected, experts have said, are India and Kazakhstan.
India, which Rubio will visit after ​Uzbekistan, remains the world's No. 2 Russian crude ​importer after China, despite Trump saying in ⁠February that India had agreed to stop buying oil from Russia.
Additional questions hang over a potential trade deal with India and an expansion of the Abraham Accords in Central Asia.
Read more: US, Azerbaijan sign strategic partnership
A US official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, described the trade deal on Friday as "pretty much done," ​raising the possibility that an agreement could be announced during the Rubio trip.
Separately, the US has talked to additional Central Asian nations about ​joining the Abraham Accords, Reuters ⁠reported last year, conversations that could in theory continue in Samarkand.
More than 200 business executives will accompany Rubio to Uzbekistan, the State Department said. The Central Asian diplomat said the Trump administration has focused its commercial efforts on expanding access to the area's rare earth mineral resources.
The trip to Uzbekistan was largely organized by Sergio Gor, the US ambassador to India, the Central Asian diplomat said. Gor, ⁠who was ​born in Uzbekistan and is a friend of Rubio, also serves as the US special envoy for South and ​Central Asian affairs.
After Uzbekistan, Rubio will visit the Indian cities of Mumbai and Jamnagar to meet with business leaders, including Reliance Industries. Chairman Mukesh Ambani, who earned the Trump administration's favor earlier in the year by backing a new ​refinery in Texas. Rubio most recently visited India five months ago.

title: India  West Indies draw T20 series
description: Kishan smashes 30 off 10 balls as India reach 118 5 before rain brings the decider to an end
content:
Kishan smashes 30 off 10 balls as India reach 118-5 before rain brings the decider to an end
India and West Indies had to settle for a 2-2 draw in their five-match T20 series ‌after the fifth and deciding game ended with no result due to rain on Saturday.
Persistent showers delayed the start and reduced the contest to nine overs per side ⁠before West Indies won the toss and elected to field.
India lost opener Abhishek Sharma for six off the bowling of Keemo Paul but Ishan Kishan then hammered 30 off 10 balls to provide the early impetus.
The hosts surged to 118-5 in 7.4 overs but rain ‌returned ⁠before the innings could be completed, forcing the players off the field. With conditions failing to improve, officials ended the match and both teams ⁠shared the series honours.
The match was the first international fixture at Chinnaswamy Stadium in two years. Veteran ⁠seamer Bhuvneshwar Kumar, recalled to India's T20 squad for the first time since November ⁠2022, was denied the chance to mark his return with the ball.
India will now go on to New Zealand for an all-format tour that begins on 22 October, while West Indies will visit Bangladesh for a two-game ICC World Test Championship 2025/27 series.

title: Rubio says Trump to take up to 60 days to weigh Russia sanctions
description: Trump under pressure over high energy prices as war with Iran disrupts global oil supplies
content:
Trump under pressure over high energy prices as war with Iran disrupts global oil supplies
The day after waiving sanctions and tariffs related to Russian exports, US President ‌Donald Trump said on Saturday he has yet to announce a final decision on the matter as Secretary of State Marco Rubio said officials want more time to evaluate the situation.
Rubio said on Saturday that the president will use up to 60 days to assess the economic impact of Russia-related sanctions and tariffs that he ​waived a day earlier.
"A lot of you don't know what my decision is yet, but we'll figure it out, and you'll ​figure it out," Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida.
The waiver comes just weeks ⁠before November's midterm elections, with Trump under pressure over high energy prices as war with Iran disrupts global oil supplies.
Trump signed an executive ​order on Friday waiving key sanctions and tariffs under the law known as the Graham Act, which he signed last month at the urging of ​lawmakers who want to pressure Moscow over its war in Ukraine.
The measures, including tariffs on Russian goods and penalties on countries buying Russian oil and gas, were due to take effect next week. Friday's order did not specify how long the waiver would last, but Rubio said Trump opted for a 60-day review.
Read: Trump waives Russia sanctions, tariffs
"I think the ​president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyze what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the ​global economy and even to the US economy," Rubio told reporters before boarding a plane for a trip to Uzbekistan.
Complicating matters is the Graham Act's call not ‌only for ⁠sanctions on Russia but also for tariffs on goods from countries that import Russian energy supplies. Rubio pointed to India, an important US partner that has diversified its energy supplies but remains heavily dependent on Russian oil.
Friday's executive order drew criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who warned it would embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin and prolong the war.
Senator Darline Graham, a South Carolina Republican whose late brother Lindsey Graham championed the legislation ​that bears his name, said she ​disagreed with Trump's decision and ⁠planned to discuss it with him when he campaigns for her next week.
"Personally, I would choose to keep the pressure on Russia," she told reporters on Saturday. "Because I don't trust Putin and I don't trust Russia."
Rubio also defended a separate US agreement with Russia to increase diesel supplies to global markets, aimed at ​easing fuel prices ⁠that have climbed amid the war with Iran and disruptions to energy supplies.
Under the agreement, Trump said Russia initially would supply more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel to the United States, followed by shipments in November and beyond.
"That diesel is going to be sold one way or the other," Rubio ⁠said. "The only ​difference is how much of it the United States was going to get."
Rubio said ​the diesel deal and sanctions waiver reflected the challenge of managing conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine that have disrupted global energy supplies.
"These conflicts around the world are starting ​to crash into each other," he said.

title: Dubois defeats Wardley to retain WBO heavyweight title
description: The 29 year old floors Wardley early before the referee stops the fight in the second round
content:
The 29-year-old floors Wardley early before the referee stops the fight in the second round
'Dynamite' Daniel Dubois retained his WBO heavyweight belt with a one-sided and devastating second-round stoppage of fellow Briton Fabio Wardley in their world title rematch on Saturday.
The 29-year-old champion made a storming start at London's O2 Arena and Wardley's legs went ‌from under him for a count within 17 seconds of the opening bell as Dubois floored him with a straight right.
Wardley, 31, beat the count and could have been stopped at the end of the first round when he took a further brutal pounding on the ropes but was saved by the bell.
There was no escape from the onslaught of blows in the second with Dubois picking up where he left off and Wardley taking punch after punch until the towel was thrown in and referee Steve Gray brought the fight to a close.
"Fabio ⁠is a great warrior, coming in for a second time, but it was my time and my era," said 'Triple D', never a man for long speeches. "I had my intentions, bad intentions, from the beginning.
"Our back was against the wall the first time, this time we just had to go out there and show that we mean business and that's what we did tonight."
HRGOVIC READY TO PUT HIS TITLE ON THE LINE
Dubois dealt Wardley his first defeat as a professional when he came back from two knockdowns, the first after 16 seconds, to take the title in the 11th round of a thunderous and bloody clash in Manchester last May.
Wardley, promoted to WBO champion last November after Ukraine's Oleksandr Usyk vacated the title, was acclaimed for his courage and refusal to give in first time around but on Saturday he looked ‌a ⁠shell of the man seen in Manchester.
He now has a 20-2-1 record with Dubois on 24 wins with three defeats.
"I've always thrown myself in with the best competitors out there, the toughest, the biggest, hardest, meanest guys around. There's no shame in testing yourself against the best," he said.
"Daniel's a testament to coming up short and coming again, I'll be looking to do the exact same thing.
"Boxing is a game of fine margins. It can be done ⁠and over in a round or two or it can go into a big old war like it was last time."
Dubois was previously the IBF champion, losing it to Usyk in London in July last year before coming back to take the WBO belt from Wardley.
Croatian Filip Hrgovic, the IBF champion after beating Britain's ⁠Moses Itauma in August, was ringside on Saturday and challenged Dubois to a fight with both belts on the line.
"It was an easy night for Daniel. He did a good job, quick win. So he's ready to fight me in March, right Daniel?," said Hrgovic, ⁠before promoter Frank Warren suggested he might have to deal with other candidates first.
Dubois beat the Croatian in June 2024 to take the interim IBF belt and was then upgraded to champion when Usyk vacated his title.
"I want to have a rematch with him, I want to get my old belt back and rule the division," said Dubois.

title: Pakistan women win handball bronze in IHF Nations Trophy
description: Green shirts finish third in Tashkent after returning to international competition following seven year absence
content:
Green-shirts finish third in Tashkent after returning to international competition following seven-year absence
Pakistan’s women’s handball team won the bronze medal at the International Handball Federation (IHF) Women’s Nations Trophy Asia Zone III in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, finishing third after returning to international competition following a seven-year absence.
Hosts Uzbekistan won the trophy, Turkmenistan claimed silver, Kyrgyzstan placed fourth and Tajikistan came fifth in the five-team tournament held from October 13 to 17.
Uzbekistan also blasted their way into the Continental Women Nations Trophy.
Pakistan began their campaign on October 13 with a 38-19 defeat by Turkmenistan before suffering a 46-8 loss to hosts Uzbekistan the following day.
The team bounced back on October 15 with a 36-14 victory over Tajikistan, with captain Sehrish named player of the match. Pakistan completed their campaign with another impressive performance, beating Kyrgyzstan 33-23 on October 17, with Misbah receiving the player-of-the-match award.
Pakistan finished the tournament with two wins and two defeats, securing third place in the final standings. Their victories over Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan proved decisive in earning the bronze medal.
Pakistan Handball Federation’s (PHF) president Mohammad Shafiq described the result as an encouraging achievement given the challenges facing the team.
“It is a good achievement because our senior women’s team has participated in an international tournament after seven years. The team had a short training period and faced a lack of facilities,” Shafiq told The Express Tribune.
Pakistan women had to wait for long for international exposure since featuring in the 2019 Nepal South Asian Games. Pakistan previously were in the South Asian zone but now have shifted to the Central Asian zone because of issues with India.
Meanwhile Uzbekistan dominated the competition, winning all four matches to secure the title. They defeated Tajikistan 49-9, Pakistan 46-8, Kyrgyzstan 43-17 and Turkmenistan 21-16.
Turkmenistan finished runners-up with three victories, including their 38-19 win over Pakistan. Pakistan’s two wins placed them ahead of Kyrgyzstan, who recorded one victory, while Tajikistan finished without a win.

title: PSG fight back to beat Strasbourg  | The Express Tribune
description: Enrique’s side secure a fourth consecutive league victory with a 3-1 comeback win over Strasbourg
content:
Enrique’s side secure a fourth consecutive league victory with a 3-1 comeback win over Strasbourg
Ousmane Dembele missed a penalty but later scored as Paris Saint-Germain produced a fightback to win 3-1 away at Strasbourg on Saturday and go to the top of the French Ligue 1 table.
PSG were trailing to an early goal by United States star Giovanni Reyna for Strasbourg at the Stade de la Meinau, and last year's Ballon d'Or winner Dembele came off the bench before he put a penalty wide in the 72nd minute.
But Dembele made amends in style, first by setting up Illia Zabarnyi to equalise in the 78th minute and then by putting the reigning French and European champions ahead with five minutes to go.
He then played a part in setting up Desire Doue for PSG's third in stoppage time, as Luis Enrique's men made it four straight Ligue 1 wins, and six on the bounce including the Champions League.
"I told him: 'If you play for 25 minutes and you give an assist and score a goal, you don't need to play any longer. That is enough'," Luis Enrique said of Dembele, one of a host of PSG players rested from the starting line-up in between key European games against Manchester City and Barcelona.
"Ousmane and the other players are not machines and they will not always be at their best. There are games over the course of a season where you are not at your best level because that is normal," added Luis Enrique.
After failing to win any of their first three domestic league matches this season, PSG are up to 14 points from seven games and are therefore top of the standings on goals scored from Lille as well as Monaco, before the principality club visit Lorient on Sunday.
Lille drew 1-1 with Brest, while Rennes, Paris FC and Lyon all have the opportunity to go back above PSG when they play on Sunday.
This game, one of PSG's toughest domestic tests of the season, fell awkwardly just three days after their 4-2 Champions League victory at City and three days before they host Barcelona.
True to form, Luis Enrique therefore made sweeping changes with eight in total from the City game. Dembele was one of those relegated to the bench here with an eye on the meeting with Barcelona, his former side.
Strasbourg sought to take advantage and went in front on 17 minutes when Reyna received a Gessime Yassine pass just inside the area, turned and beat Matvey Safonov low at the goalkeeper's near post.
The visitors were grateful to Safonov for a superb save to deny Conrad Harder just after half-time, before Luis Enrique sent on some of the cavalry, including Dembele and Doue.
They won a penalty after a VAR check confirmed that a Doue shot had hit the arm of Pape Demba Diop, but Dembele -- who scored a penalty in May's Champions League final win over Arsenal -- put his spot-kick wide. Three different PSG players have now missed penalties in their last three games.
"We have lots of players who can take them but it is true that we don't have one specialist," said Luis Enrique.
However, Dembele crossed from the right for Ukraine defender Zabarnyi to equalise with a cushioned close-range finish, and then controlled on the edge of the box before firing in to make it 2-1.
That was his first Ligue 1 goal this season to go with three in the Champions League, and Dembele -- who is nominated again for this year's Ballon d'Or -- then brought down a long Safonov kick before finding Ferran Torres who set up Doue to seal the win.
Lille were looking to bounce back from a 3-0 Champions League loss at Arsenal when they entertained Brest, but they needed a penalty from 40-year-old Olivier Giroud to get a 1-1 draw.
Lens, France's other Champions League representative, won 3-1 away at Troyes.

title: Inter pull clear as Napoli endure another setback
description: The champions move to 19 points with a 3 1 comeback win over Bologna
content:
The champions move to 19 points with a 3-1 comeback win over Bologna
Inter Milan pulled clear at the top of Serie A after coming from behind to beat Bologna 3-1 on Saturday, while Roma dispatched Genoa to jump into second and Napoli's torrid start continued with a shock defeat by Venezia.
The champions moved up to 19 points, although Lazio can go level with the leaders if they beat Juventus in Turin on Sunday.
A 2-0 win for Roma at the Stadio Olimpico moved them two points off top in second, while Napoli's loss left them a distant ninth, nine points off the title pace.
Inter came in for criticism after a disappointing midweek Champions League defeat against Club Brugge but bounced back with a comeback win ahead of the visit of Shakhtar Donetsk on Wednesday.
"Our strength is the group and the quality of the players," Inter assistant coach Aleksandar Kolarov told DAZN.
"We don't have anything to prove to anyone except ourselves. We want to be more intense with and without the ball."
Bologna started brightly as Tommaso Pobega fired them in front after 10 minutes before hitting the bar with a powerful shot.
But Inter, shorn of injured captain Lautaro Martinez after he was ruled out for a month, responded through a towering Marcus Thuram header.
Chivu's substitutions proved decisive as Carlos Augusto scored within a minute of coming on midway through the second half, before turning provider for fellow replacement Ange-Yoan Bonny late on.
Just three days after throwing away a 3-1 lead to lose 4-3 in the dying minutes of a Champions League clash with Real Madrid, Roma responded strongly with a 2-0 win over Genoa.
With top scorer Donyell Malen suspended and several key players injured, Roma's young guns seized their chance as Santiago Castro and Emanuele Lulli scored their first goals for the club.
Both sides were denied by the woodwork in the first half, but an audacious flicked finish in a crowded box from Castro broke the deadlock after 50 minutes, before teenage wing-back Lulli made sure of the points with a close-range effort.
Genoa coach Daniele De Rossi, a celebrated former Roma player and coach, received a warm ovation from the home support but was unable to prevent counterpart Gian Piero Gasperini from claiming the 300th Serie A win of his managerial career.
Venezia coach Davide Nicola masterminded a shock 1-0 win over struggling Napoli on debut as Kevin De Bruyne had a penalty saved.
Renowned survival specialist Nicola was appointed during the week to replace sacked coach Giovanni Stroppa after last season's Serie B champions failed to pick up a single point in their opening six games.
He made an instant impact as Akor Adams struck the winner early in the second half to seal Venezia's first Serie A win over Napoli since 1942.
Rested Napoli stars Rasmus Hojlund and De Bruyne came on as coach Massimiliano Allegri searched for an equaliser and Hojlund soon won a penalty, but the Belgian midfielder's spot-kick was saved by Filip Stankovic.
The Venezia goalkeeper proved decisive in the closing stages with a string of impressive saves as Napoli pushed forward in vain.
It marked a second defeat in a row for Allegri's side after their midweek Champions League loss at Villarreal, and the first time in 25 years that Napoli have lost five of their first nine games in all competitions.
Next up for Napoli is the visit of Bodo/Glimt in the Champions League on Tuesday.
"In football you get moments like this and there is only one way out: keep working seriously and professionally, be more focused and turn this disappointment into anger," Allegri told a press conference.
"It's up to us to turn this situation around, starting with the Champions League."
Napoli are ninth on 10 points, while Venezia remain bottom with three points.

title: Neto double gives Chelsea win
description: The Blues beat Everton 2 0 to move into the top four
content:
The Blues beat Everton 2-0 to move into the top four
Pedro Neto's double condemned Everton to a first defeat of the season as Chelsea won 2-0 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium despite the loss of goalkeeper Emi Martinez to a head injury.
Neto opened the scoring inside the first minute of the second half and secured the three points during the 11 added minutes following the lengthy treatment given to the stricken Martinez.
The Argentine international was involved in a sickening head clash with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite and was taken to hospital.
"As far as I know he left the stadium conscious. Right now he's in the hospital doing the precautionary tests, so let's see," said Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso.
A first away win of the season lifts Chelsea above the Toffees into the top four and the Blues also recorded a first clean sheet in 23 Premier League games.
"We needed one of these wins away. We have played very professional, very serious, looking solid. It is a very good win," added Alonso.
"We need to get many more clean sheets for the rest of the of the league games but for sure the first one of the season feels good and now we need to keep going this way."
After a slow start, a fiery-tempered encounter sparked into life when Everton midfielder Harrison Armstrong launched into a tackle on Josh Acheampong for the first of five first-half yellow cards.
That challenge also enlivened the home crowd and spurred Everton on to their best spell of the game.
Thierno Barry was guilty of another wasteful day in front of goal as the Frenchman planted a header from Jack Grealish's cross too close to Martinez.
Chelsea have made a habit of fast starts under Alonso, but it took until four minutes before half-time to threaten when Moises Caicedo blasted off the bar from a well-worked corner.
Everton were furious that Morgan Rogers escaped a second booking just before the break after a thunderous clash with England team-mate James Garner.
That proved to be a huge decision as the visitors this time flew out of the blocks at the start of the second period.
Jorrel Hato got to the byline and his low cross fell to Neto, who had time to control before firing low past Jordan Pickford.
Chelsea had not kept a Premier League clean sheet since January, but were rarely troubled by an Everton side short on forward options despite the loss of Martinez.
"I just felt that Chelsea had that little bit more flair and ability which we didn't possess at the right moments today," said Everton boss David Moyes.
The treatment for Martinez threatened to halt Chelsea's momentum as they controlled the second half.
Belgian Mike Penders replaced the Chelsea number one for his first Premier League appearance but had little to do bar dealing with a few desperate Everton crosses.
At the other end Pickford made a fine save to deny Joao Pedro.
But Chelsea did get their second goal when Neto coolly stroked into the bottom corner after Jordan Henderson's free-kick was blocked by the Everton wall.

title: Diaz hat trick powers Bayern to top spot
description: Dortmund are held by Union Berlin
content:
Luis Diaz hit a hat-trick as Bayern Munich pummelled a listless RB Leipzig 6-1 at home on Saturday to climb to the top of the Bundesliga table.
Borussia Dortmund had edged ahead of Freiburg into top spot after their earlier draw at Union Berlin, but Bayern responded in typically ruthless fashion to take the summit.
The dominant display was Bayern's best performance of the season and will boost their confidence days out from Wednesday's home Champions League clash with English champions Arsenal.
Diaz had faced criticism after four league games without a goal but the Colombian sparked to life to terrorise Leipzig defender Lukas Klostermann down the left.
"Lucho (Diaz) has had some criticism this season but he was excellent tonight. Definitely the man of the hour," Bayern captain Joshua Kimmich said.
In his 100th Bundesliga match, Harry Kane scored a goal and laid on two assists as he pulled the strings from deep while Aleksandar Pavlovic and Michael Olise also got on the scoresheet.
Confined to his chair with a hip complaint, Bayern coach Vincent Kompany produced a masterclass against opposite number Martin Demichelis, his former Manchester City teammate.
"You can come here and lose a match, but not like that," Demichelis said to Sky Germany. Leipzig travel to face Real Madrid in the Champions League on Wednesday.
Bayern have now won their past three games against Leipzig by a combined scoreline of 17-1.
Bayern had drawn their past two matches, a rare run of middling form for the German giants, but shook off the funk early, with Diaz, Pavlovic and Olise putting the hosts in control before half-time.
Diaz scored either side of a Kane tap-in after the break, with the England captain withdrawn before the hour mark ahead of old rivals Arsenal's visit.
Leipzig's Andrija Maksimovic got on the board with a late late consolation in stoppage time.
Dortmund missed a chance to stay ahead of Bayern after being held to a scoreless draw at Union Berlin.
After starting the season strongly with six wins in a row in all competitions, Dortmund have stalled of late, drawing two and losing one of their last three matches.
"We simply have to get better in attack. Right now, it's just not good enough," Dortmund's Waldemar Anton told Sky.
Serhou Guirassy had a golden chance to snatch all three points for his side at the end of a match of few opportunities, but headed just wide with 11 minutes remaining.
It was the first draw between the two sides in their history, with each of their previous 16 clashes in all competitions producing a winner.
Compounding Dortmund's woes was a serious-looking ankle injury to substitute midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas, who was helped from the pitch just eight minutes after coming on.
"Let's hope it's not too serious. He's not feeling great right now," Dortmund sporting director Ole Book told reporters.
Stuttgart suffered a blow ahead of Tuesday's home Champions League clash with Atletico Madrid, going down 1-0 at Hamburg after an 88th-minute Miro Muheim goal.
Elsewhere, promoted Elversberg continued their impressive debut season in the top flight, winning 4-3 at home to Augsburg.
Lukas Petkov, Lasse Guenther, Maximilian Rohr and Frederik Schmahl got on the scoresheet as Elversberg, from the smallest town to ever host a Bundesliga side, climbed to sixth in the table.
Niclas Fuellkrug scored for the fifth straight Bundesliga match as his brace helped Werder Bremen come from two goals down to draw 2-2 at home against Paderborn.
A first-half goal for Phillip Tietz was enough for Mainz to win 1-0 at Schalke and climb to fifth in the standings.

title: Yamal powers Barcelona to Betis rout
description: Alex Baena seals Atletico   s victory in the 89th minute
content:
Alex Baena seals Atletico’s victory in the 89th minute
Barcelona coach Hansi Flick hailed Lamine Yamal as the best player in the world as his dominant side routed 10-man Real Betis 5-2 on Saturday to return five points clear at the top of La Liga.
Atletico, second, snatched a late 1-0 win at Espanyol, while third-placed Betis are eight points adrift of the leaders and Real Madrid, fourth, host Sevilla on Sunday.
Teenage winger Yamal scored a brilliant goal for Spanish champions Barca, with Rodri, Gabriel Jesus, Eric Garcia and Dani Olmo also finding the net at La Cartuja stadium in Seville.
Betis had Facundo Bernal sent off for a headbutt on Yamal early in the second half of a pulsating clash.
Barca set a new club record for victories at the start of a league campaign and equalled the all-time record of nine, set by Real Madrid in the 1968/69 season. Flick's side boast 11 wins from 11 games across all competitions.
Yamal, who is hoping to be crowned the world's best player at the Ballon d'Or ceremony later in October, got the ball rolling with a spectacular opener.
"I think it was an amazing match for the fans, and all the people who love football, it was amazing," Flick told reporters.
"Lamine today, when you see the first goal he scored, unbelievable, this is for me, at the moment the best player in the world."
Yamal, 19, turned sharply on the edge of the box to escape Bernal and then exquisitely curled into the top corner in the 10th minute.
"(It was) an incredible goal, we've got used to him doing this lately, I have to say," Rodri told DAZN.
"In the end, players like that make the difference. But I try to focus on the other things he brings... (like) hard work, a lot of solidarity with the team, understanding the game and where he could find space."
Despite their irresistible attacking play, Barca's clear weakness under Flick has been their defence and Betis were level before the half-hour mark through a Valentin Gomez header.
Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri put Barca back in front with a header from a corner, before Giovani Lo Celso thought he had equalised in spectacular fashion for the hosts.
However, the Argentine midfielder's long-range goal was ruled out for a handball by Cucho Hernandez earlier in the move, much to Betis' chagrin.
Jesus extended Barca's lead six minutes into the second half from Yamal's cut-back, moments after having another goal ruled out for offside.
Ez Abde immediately pulled one back for Betis during a wild spell, and in the aftermath they were reduced to 10 men when Bernal was sent off for a headbutt on Yamal, who was booked for his part in a confrontation between several players from both sides.
Garcia finished from close range for Barca's fourth and Raphinha came off the bench after missing the previous two matches injured, with Flick taking off Yamal to prevent a potential suspension for the Clasico next weekend.
"With this result, we have to change him," said Flick. "I (told him) I'm very proud of him because he played a fantastic game."
Substitute Olmo finished the match off with a neat finish from the edge of the box as Betis backed off to allow Barca's attention to turn to Europe, where they face Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday.
Earlier, Alex Baena struck in the 89th minute to snatch Atletico Madrid their narrow win at Espanyol.
Spain international Baena smashed home from the edge of the box to claim the Rojiblancos an important late victory from a tight game in Cornella.
Atletico have won six consecutive games across all competitions.
Baena, who struggled last season but has been in fine fettle since winning the World Cup with Spain this summer, hugged coach Diego Simeone after finding the net.
"The World Cup took him to a different place, he sees football differently than others and (now) he's more confident and stronger, he's the player we went looking for," Simeone told reporters after Baena's fifth league goal of the campaign.

title: Haaland stars in Manchester City win
description: Liverpool beat Brentford 2 1
content:
Erling Haaland starred with a double as Premier League leaders Manchester City beat Ipswich 3-2, while Liverpool came from behind to seal a 2-1 win at Brentford on Saturday.
City are in turmoil off the pitch after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.
On the grass they have made a perfect start, with seven successive league victories marking their best opening to a Premier League season.
City, who are appealing against the guilty verdict after branding it a "Premier League conspiracy", sit six points clear of champions Arsenal.
Second-placed Arsenal can close the gap with a win at Nottingham Forest on Sunday.
With City potentially facing a massive points deduction or even expulsion from the top flight if their appeal fails, it remains to be seen whether their results will even matter by the end of the season.
For now, Enzo Maresca's side are in fine form after bouncing back from their midweek loss to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League.
There was a defiant mood at the Etihad Stadium, where City fans booed the Premier League anthem before kick-off, while thousands waved inflatable bananas to underline their commitment to the club regardless of its plight.
Phil Foden put Maresca's men ahead in the 19th minute with a sharp turn and finish after Jeremy Doku's incisive run prised open the Ipswich defence.
Foden's first goal this season was followed by an Ipswich equaliser in the 21st minute when Daizen Maeda evaded Marc Guehi to fire home.
Haaland restored City's lead in the 34th minute with a pin-point header from Mateo Kovacic's cross.
Haaland killed off Ipswich in the 69th minute, sprinting onto Iliman Ndiaye's pass and steering his shot past Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton.
Zian Flemming's 90th-minute penalty, awarded for a foul by Guehi, set up a tense finale but City held on.
"Very happy with today's game, we controlled it for 95 minutes. We create chances, we score. We finish a little bit suffering together but overall, it is good," Maresca said.
In west London, Liverpool were stunned when Brentford defender Keane Lewis-Potter looped a header past Alisson Becker from Igor Thiago's cross in the 44th minute.
But the Bees were reduced to 10 men in first half stoppage-time after Yehor Yarmolyuk's head made contact with Jeremy Jacquet's face while they waited for a corner.
Liverpool lost Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong to injuries, but still made their numerical advantage count in the 62nd minute.
Victor Munoz cut inside and slotted a composed equaliser past Brentford's former Liverpool 'keeper Caoimhin Kelleher.
Alexander Isak blasted Liverpool's winner in the 70th minute after Barcola teed up the Sweden striker for his fifth goal this term.
Brentford finished with nine men following Vitaly Janelt's second booking in stoppage-time.
Beaten by City in their previous league game, Liverpool are up to fifth place after inflicting Brentford's first league defeat of the season.
"You see the results of Brentford at home and you have to be ready for these kinds of battles. We had 45 minutes to do the comeback and I think we played really well," Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola said.
Pedro Neto's double condemned Everton to a first defeat of the season as fourth-placed Chelsea won 2-0 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium despite the loss of goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez to a head injury.
Neto opened the scoring inside the first minute of the second half and secured the points during stoppage-time.
The Argentine shot-stopper was involved in a sickening head clash with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite and was taken to hospital.
Fulham won for the first time in the league this season as Alex Iwobi's 33rd-minute goal clinched a 1-0 victory against Hull at Craven Cottage.
Aston Villa won 1-0 at Newcastle as Johan Manzambi tormented the club he rejected in the close-season.
Villa winger Manzambi headed home from Joao Gomes's cross in the 33rd minute.
It was a bitter blow to Newcastle, who agreed a deal with Freiburg for Manzambi in the summer before Villa hijacked the deal.
