content:
The University of Agriculture Faisalabad (UAF) organised an awareness walk and seminar to mark World Food Day, highlighting the need to address hunger, malnutrition, food security and food safety through sustainable food systems, public awareness and research-based interventions.
UAF Vice Chancellor Dr Zulfiqar Ali said food security should not be measured solely by food availability but also by its nutritional quality, safety, affordability and accessibility.

He called for reducing food waste at every stage, from production and storage to transportation and consumption, to make better use of available resources.
Dean of Food Sciences Dr Imran Pasha said public awareness of balanced diets and healthy lifestyles was essential to tackling malnutrition.
He stressed that food safety standards must be followed at every stage, including preparation, storage, transportation and consumption, to protect public health.

title: Pakpattan tops Punjab pollution ranking
description: Pakpattan tops Punjab pollution ranking
content:
Barki Road in Lahore falls in unhealthy category
Pakpattan recorded Punjab's highest city-level Air Quality Index (AQI) at 149 at 3:00pm on Saturday, as the Pakistan Meteorological Department forecast mainly dry weather across most of the province.
Nankana Sahib followed at 140, with Sahiwal at 137, Okara 135, Multan 133, Mandi Bahauddin and Talagang 130, Faisalabad 127 and Dera Ghazi Khan 121, according to the Punjab Environmental Protection Agency's dashboard.
Another monitoring website showed Lahore's reading of 118 at 5:00pm, in the moderate range, compared with 109 at the same hour on Friday.
Barki Road recorded the city's highest reading at 218, classified as unhealthy.
Readings from 101 to 150 fall in the moderate band on the portal's scale, while 151 to 200 is classed as unhealthy for sensitive groups.
The EPA advises children, senior citizens and those with pulmonary or heart conditions to consider reducing prolonged or strenuous outdoor activities when pollution readings are moderate.
Short-term exposure to fine particulate matter in the air can aggravate asthma and other respiratory symptoms and is associated with cardiovascular effects.
A PMD forecast showed that mainly dry weather was expected in most of Punjab on Sunday.
Lahore was expected to remain sunny, with a highest temperature of 30°C to 32°C. The forecast gave a range of 29°C to 31°C for Monday.
The department said light rain or thunderstorms were possible at isolated places in Gilgit-Baltistan and adjoining hilly areas.

title: LHC acquits man sentenced in 2021
description: LHC acquits man sentenced in 2021
content:
Prosecution fails to explain delay in registration of murder case
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has acquitted a man sentenced to life imprisonment for murder, ruling that the prosecution failed to satisfactorily explain a delay in registering the FIR and establish the presence of witnesses at the crime scene.
Justice Farooq Haider allowed an appeal filed by Muhammad Ashraf against his conviction, setting aside his life sentence and a fine of Rs500,000 imposed by the trial court in 2021.
Ashraf had been accused of shooting dead Sikandar Firdous. Mandi Bahauddin police had registered the murder case against him in 2019.
In its written judgment, the court noted that the prosecution had failed to provide a convincing explanation for the delay in registering the FIR.
The court observed that the post-mortem examination had been conducted late and the police had prepared relevant documents after a delay.
According to the complainant, she was travelling on a motorcycle with her son to visit her daughter when Ashraf signalled them to stop outside his house. After they stopped, the accused allegedly took her son inside the house and shot him dead.
The court observed that the complainant's account raised questions about the circumstances of the incident, as her daughter's home was situated before the accused's house along the route in the village.
Finding weaknesses in the prosecution's case, the high court set aside the conviction and sentence.

title: Punjab CM  unfazed by criticism
description: Punjab CM  unfazed by criticism
content:
Urges public servants to realise obligation to the country investing in them
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Saturday said public service required timely decisions, integrity and the courage to take risks, adding that she remained unfazed despite facing more criticism than praise.
"Every decision taken by the chief minister can bring a change in the lives of millions of people," she said while addressing participants of the Common Training Programme from the Sindh government.
She said the responsibilities of the chief minister's office were demanding, with new challenges emerging every day. She stressed that public officials could not afford to waste time, adding that punctuality and efficient decision-making were essential to governance.
"I proudly say that I am made in Pakistan, educated in Pakistan and live in Pakistan," she said, urging public servants to recognise their responsibility towards a country that had invested in their education, identity and professional development.
She said personal feelings should not influence professional decisions, particularly in positions of authority. Officials must know what decision was required and take it at the appropriate time, she added.
Referring to her political journey, the CM said she had never held an elected office before becoming chief minister and had worked hard to reach her current position. She said public interest took precedence over personal considerations and she did not entertain influence in the appointment of senior officials.
The chief minister cited the Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar programme as an example of the government's approach to public welfare, saying it had received the UN-Habitat Scroll of Honour in Muscat for its rapid implementation and sustainable low-cost housing model.
She said more than 200,000 housing loans had been disbursed in 18 months and 125,000 houses completed. The scheme, she added, had a recovery rate of 99.9 per cent, with no defaults. She said the government had introduced checks and safeguards because the money being spent belonged to the public.
CM Maryam Nawaz urged citizens to place their trust in the government, describing it as a "new social contract" between the state and the people.
She said merit was the guiding principle in the appointment of district police officers and deputy commissioners, adding that she interviewed candidates for key positions and resisted political pressure and favouritism.
Emphasising the need for a citizen-centred state, she said people in need should not have to stand in queues or repeatedly approach government offices for assistance. Instead, the state should reach out to them.
She cited mobile health services, field hospitals and home delivery of medicines for patients requiring cardiac care, hepatitis treatment and insulin as examples of efforts to bring public services closer to citizens.
The government, she said, was also monitoring essential commodity prices through daily dashboards.
The chief minister highlighted other initiatives, including mobile police stations for women, emergency assistance against harassment, the Dastak app for accessing government services and ambulance services for transportation of deceased patients from hospitals.
She said 700 buses were providing transport services, while women, students and senior citizens could travel free on the electric buses.
The government planned to distribute 100,000 electric scooters among female students next to facilitate their mobility, she added.
On law and order, the CM Punjab stated that the crime rate in Punjab had declined by 70% following the establishment of the Crime Control Department (CCD). She said Safe City Authority cameras were operational across the province and enabled authorities to detect criminal acts within seconds.

The Sahil police have solved the mystery of an alleged robbery involving gold worth Rs15 million in Defence Phase VIII within 24 hours, arresting two suspects, including a driver, police said.

title: CM offers seawater desalination project
description: CM offers seawater desalination project
content:
Says Shanghai Electric's investment in project will address Karachi's water challenges
Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah has called for a new phase of strategic cooperation with Shanghai Electric Group, inviting the Chinese energy and engineering company to invest in seawater desalination, renewable energy, energy storage, coal-based chemical industries and human resource development in Sindh.
The proposal was made during a meeting with Shanghai Electric Group Chairman Wu Lei and senior company executives at the group's headquarters in Shanghai. The two sides reviewed ongoing projects in Sindh and explored new areas of cooperation.
Highlighting Karachi's growing water challenges, the chief minister invited Shanghai Electric to explore the development of a large-scale seawater desalination project under Sindh's public-private partnership framework.
He said the company's experience in desalination and water infrastructure could help ensure a sustainable water supply for Karachi's rapidly growing population.
"Karachi urgently needs modern, long-term solutions to its water challenges. We believe Shanghai Electric's expertise in desalination technology can play a significant role in addressing this issue," he said.
The chief minister acknowledged Shanghai Electric's role in Tharparkar's development, saying the project had generated employment, enhanced technical skills and opened up new economic opportunities for local communities.
He appreciated the company's efforts to train and employ young people from Thar and urged it to expand opportunities for local residents, particularly women.
"The benefits of Thar's development must continue to reach the people of the region. We want local communities, including women, to have a greater share in the economic opportunities generated by these projects," he said.
The chief minister also highlighted Sindh's considerable potential for wind and solar power, inviting the company to participate in upcoming renewable energy projects, battery storage systems and related industrial ventures.
He also encouraged Shanghai Electric to consider establishing local manufacturing or assembly plants for renewable energy equipment in Sindh's special economic zones.
Emphasising the importance of knowledge transfer, Murad proposed a structured training and capacity-building programme for Sindh's engineers, technical professionals and energy-sector officials at Shanghai Electric's facilities in China. He said the initiative would strengthen local expertise and support the long-term sustainability of major infrastructure and energy projects in the province.

Five including son of notorious gang-war commander Baba Ladla taken into custody
Five suspects, including a son of notorious Lyari gang-war commander Baba Ladla, have been taken into custody over the alleged abduction and brutal torture of a teenager in Lyari, after a video showing the assault surfaced on social media and was aired by Express News.
The disturbing mobile phone footage shows the teenager stripped, tied up with ropes and repeatedly beaten with a leather belt and a stick. His neck, arms and legs can be seen bound in the video, while the assailants continue the assault and record it on a mobile phone.
The incident reportedly took place on October 11 in Phool Patti Lane, Lyari. The footage has raised concerns about the possible re-emergence of gang-related intimidation in the area, although police officials have said the incident stemmed from a dispute among young men and was not linked to a clash between gang-war groups.
According to police, a case was registered at Baghdadi police station on October 14 on the complaint of the victim's maternal uncle, Kabir Ahmed, under charges including attempted murder, abduction and assault.
In his complaint, Kabir Ahmed said he worked at a cardboard box manufacturing unit in Pakistan Chowk, Karachi. His nephew, Ghulam Nabi, aged 17 or 18 and a Class VIII student, returned home on October 11 in a frightened state, with visible marks of torture on his face.
The teenager reportedly told his uncle that he had been walking towards Lyari General Hospital for work that night when he reached Phool Patti Lane No. 20, near Dongi Chowk. There, he allegedly encountered seven men, including Sharif and Arshad, sons of notorious gang-war commander Baba Ladla, along with Uzair, son of Ishaq; Faraz, son of Qasim; Ali, son of Tahir; Ghazanfar Ali; and Shahzaib.
The complainant said the suspects had been involved in a dispute with his nephew about two months earlier.
According to the teenager's account in the FIR, the men, some of whom were armed, seized him and took him to a small room, where they tied his hands and feet, stripped him and subjected him to severe torture with sticks. He also alleged that a bridle was forced into his mouth while the assault was filmed.
The complaint further stated that Sharif threatened to kill the teenager and allegedly drew a pistol to shoot him. However, Arshad reportedly pushed his hand upwards, causing the shot to miss the victim.
The suspects subsequently untied the teenager after he pleaded for his life, but allegedly warned him not to return to the area. He then put on his clothes and fled home.

title: Mystery deaths raise water safety fears
description: Mystery deaths raise water safety fears
content:
Residents of Islamabad's outskirts seek probe and laboratory testing of drinking water
Reports of four young people dying within a month in Sarai Kharboza, Dhoke Abbasi and Mohalla Usmania, on the outskirts of Islamabad, have sparked concern among local residents, who have urged the Federal Health Minister to order an immediate investigation into the deaths and laboratory testing of drinking water samples.
Following reports that liver failure was involved in some of the deaths, residents have called for a transparent inquiry to establish the actual causes and for urgent measures to protect public health.
According to World Health Organisation (WHO) statistics, Pakistan recorded a mortality rate of 38.8 deaths per 100,000 people in 2019 attributable to unsafe water, poor sanitation and inadequate hygiene facilities.
The indicator covers several water, sanitation and hygiene-related risks and should not be interpreted as the mortality rate caused solely by contaminated drinking water. The figures nevertheless underline the importance of safe water supplies and effective sanitation systems.
Dr Gul Khan of Sangjani Hospital said waterborne diseases in Pakistan could be caused by sewage entering drinking water pipelines, contamination of groundwater, inadequate access to safe water, damage to water sources during floods and poor sanitation arrangements.
He stressed that regular water quality testing, protecting supply pipelines from sewage contamination and ensuring access to clean water in homes, schools and hospitals were essential to safeguarding public health.
Dr Gul Khan advised residents to have their drinking water tested by an accredited laboratory and to use boiled water or an effective filtration system. He also urged them to ensure that water supply lines remained protected from sewage contamination. Anyone experiencing diarrhoea or symptoms of dehydration should seek medical advice promptly, he added.
Speaking to The Express Tribune, the father of one of the deceased young men said his son had appeared to be in good health before suddenly falling ill and being taken to hospital.
His condition deteriorated further the following day, and he was placed on a ventilator. According to his father, the family was informed that his son's liver had been severely damaged. Despite receiving medical treatment, the young man died three days later.
Political and social figure Wasif Hayat Khan also expressed concern over reports of the deaths and called on the relevant authorities to conduct a transparent investigation, arrange laboratory testing of drinking water samples and establish the actual causes of the fatalities.
He said protecting the health and lives of citizens was a fundamental responsibility of the relevant authorities and urged them to treat the matter with the utmost seriousness and take immediate action.

title: Varsity students explore Gandhara heritage

content:
A delegation of students and faculty members from the University of the Punjab visited Khanpur, the Julian Stupa and other historical and archaeological sites in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa to explore the region's rich Gandhara civilisation and cultural heritage.
The visit took place under the guidance of Dr Luca Oliveira, Project Director of the KP-Path Project, and Dr Kiran Siddiqui, Professor in the Department of History and Pakistan Studies at Punjab University.
On their arrival at the Julian Stupa near Khanpur, the delegation was received by Aamir Sajjad, Field Officer of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Directorate of Archaeology.
The delegation was taken on a guided tour of the Julian Stupa, the Bhamala Stupa and other historical sites. The participants received detailed briefings on the history of the Gandhara civilisation, ancient architectural techniques, the archaeological significance of the sites and the sculptures preserved there.
The students, accompanied by their professor, closely examined the historical remains and expressed keen interest in the region's ancient civilisation, architectural heritage and historical significance.
The visit aimed to familiarise students with Pakistan's historical heritage and enhance their academic and research experience through first-hand observation of archaeological sites.
The delegation members appreciated the efforts of Dr Abdul Samad, Director of Archaeology, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, for the preservation, maintenance and promotion of the province's historical sites.
They also thanked Field Officer Aamir Sajjad and other officials, commending their services towards safeguarding the country's archaeological heritage.
The participants emphasised that preserving Pakistan's historical and cultural heritage and raising awareness among younger generations about its significance were essential.
They observed that such educational visits not only broaden students' academic understanding but also help highlight the country's rich historical legacy.

The court observed that submitting an irrelevant response in contempt proceedings demonstrated negligence, which could not be taken lightly. It said the authorities could not evade clear judicial directives by shifting responsibility to other departments.
The IHC directed the concerned officials to submit a written report detailing the steps taken to comply with the court's orders.

His artistic practice reflects a sustained engagement with painting, printmaking and visual expression, informed by his academic background and extensive experience. The interactive discussion provided a platform for cultural exchange, artistic dialogue and strengthening longstanding cultural ties between Pakistan and Bangladesh.
Through such initiatives, the PNCA continues to promote contemporary art, encourage engagement between artists and audiences, and foster international cultural collaboration.

title: Five convicts spared gallows for murder of nine  | The Express Tribune

Five convicts 
spared gallows for murder of nine
content:
LHC cites legal flaws in trial court judgment; victims' family to challenge ruling
The Lahore High Court (LHC)'s Rawalpindi Bench has converted the death sentences of five convicts in the 2020 murder of nine members of a family in the Chontra area of Rawalpindi into life imprisonment, partially allowing their appeals against the capital punishment.
A division bench headed by Justice Sadaqat Ali Khan set aside the five death sentences awarded to each of the five convicts and dismissed the victim party's petitions seeking to uphold the capital punishment. The High Court observed that there were legal flaws in the trial court's judgment which could not be overlooked.
The five convicts - Rab Nawaz, Danish, Ashraf, Aqib and Akram - had allegedly joined other accomplices in carrying out the massacre to avenge an old enmity.
On 24 July 2020, they entered the victims' house in Karral Mial, Chontra, and opened fire with Kalashnikovs, killing nine members of the same family before fleeing the scene. They were subsequently arrested.
The victims included five women - Azran Bibi, Nisar Bibi, Salim Akhtar, Sabiha Bibi and Sidra Bibi - three minor girls, Iman Fatima, Abida Shaheen and Anzala Bibi, and one man. The trial court had sentenced the five convicts to death five times each and imposed a fine of Rs500,000 on each of them. The LHC had earlier suspended the sentences and remanded the case to the sessions court, directing it to rehear the final arguments and decide the matter afresh. The sessions court subsequently upheld the same sentences for a second time. However, while hearing the appeals for the second time, the LHC partially accepted the convicts' appeals.

title: Cockfighting finds a ring under police watch
description: Cockfighting finds a ring under police watch
content:
Animal welfare concerns grow; police say action will follow complaints of cockfighting
Despite restrictions on cockfighting, a regular market for the sale and fighting of specially bred Aseel gamecocks has reportedly emerged near City Police Station in Rawalpindi, with contests and trading taking place every Friday at Dingi Khoi Chowk.
The market operates from 10am until sunset, where Aseel cocks of various fighting breeds are brought in vehicles, carefully handled and sometimes covered with face veils to conceal their identities. The coverings are removed when a bird is put up for sale or after a transaction has been completed.
Highly prized fighting cocks reportedly command prices ranging from Rs50,000 to Rs250,000, depending on their breed and fighting ability. The birds are also made to fight in organised contests, with spectators gathering to watch the matches.
Cockfighting, traditionally known as murgh baazi, has a long history in the Indian subcontinent and was once a common feature of rural gatherings and fairs. Aseel breeds, particularly those associated with Mianwali and Sindh, are widely used for the purpose.
Their owners, known as murgh baaz, pay particular attention to their diet and exercise, with some feeding them desi ghee, almonds and other energy-rich foods to improve their stamina.
Traditional cockfighting arenas are known as parr, around which spectators gather as two birds are released to fight. The contests can continue until one bird retreats, is severely injured or dies, raising serious concerns about animal welfare.
The practice is also associated with gambling, with substantial sums reportedly wagered by owners and spectators on the outcomes of fights.
From an animal welfare perspective, forcing animals to fight and exposing them to unnecessary pain and injury have drawn strong criticism. Islamic teachings also prohibit cruelty to animals and the practice of making them fight for entertainment.
The Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act provides a legal framework against animal cruelty, although the precise legal provisions applicable to such events depend on the circumstances and relevant legislation.
Despite enforcement measures against illegal animal fighting and associated gambling, the reported activity near Dingi Khoi Chowk has continued.
A poultry trader, Abdul Mateen, said he had brought Aseel cocks from Mianwali, describing them as belonging to a particularly aggressive fighting breed.
A police spokesperson said that setting up a market to sell domestic chickens was not prohibited in itself, but the police would take action if complaints concerning cockfighting were received.

title: France protests  demonstrators vow to shake government
description: France protests  demonstrators vow to shake government
content:
Police and protesters clashed in Paris and other French cities Saturday, sending smoke from fires and tear gas over several demonstrations nationwide against high prices in the run-up to elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron.
Masked youths set a tourism office in the city of Lyon ablaze, as riot squads resorted to tear gas and water cannon to disperse hundreds confronting them.
In the second-largest city of Marseille, protesters broke into the town hall, overturning a bust and smashing furniture before being forced out by police, AFP journalists saw. The mayor called for police reinforcements.
In the northern city of Lille, protesters smashed their way into the mayor's office and vandalised the premises before leaving.
In Paris, tens of thousands marched across the east and north of the city, some shouting "Everyone hates the police" and "Macron, resign".
"For years we've had climate, economy and equality problems but the government is not doing anything about it," said Agnes, a 50-year-old actor who did not give her second name, as she marched.
High school student Kamil Alahyan, 18, said he was protesting "for so many reasons -- the elections coming up in 2027, politicians who lie, the ultra-rich who've been taking more and more wealth over the past 10 years".
Many of the demonstrators complained about inflation sent soaring over three percent by the war in the Middle East.
Others slammed perceived police brutality in student protests that have gripped France over the past four weeks.
The combined unrest of both protest movements makes for a febrile climate as the country heads towards presidential elections in six months' time.
Opposition politicians vying to succeed Macron have seized upon the protests.
Far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, who has sided with the police, said on X: "Looting, pillaging, attacking police -- rioters have once again sullied the October 17 demonstrations over the cost of living."
She claimed that the protesters' demands had been "hijacked by the far left".

title: Albanian capital sees fifth straight day of violent clashes
description: Albanian capital sees fifth straight day of violent clashes
content:
Albania's capital Tirana saw clashes for a fifth straight day Saturday as protesters demanded the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama, who pledged to listen to their criticism.
Several hundred people, some masked, gathered around noon in front of the ministry of education, with protests later spreading across the city.
Protesters threw rocks at the police and set litter bins on fire, using them as barricades to prevent the police from advancing.
After police officers had used megaphones to call on those gathered to desist from violence, they used water cannons and tear gas to temporarily disperse the crowd.
Violent demonstrations have rocked Tirana since Tuesday, with thousands of protesters calling for Rama to step down over university conditions and high tuition fees.
At the beginning of the protest demonstrators set a suitcase on fire and threw it in the education ministry courtyard -- symbolically showing they do not want to leave Albania.
Journalism student Sinan Billa said the protest was "a reaction to express discontent at the silence of our government."
"Young people have awoken for our parents, too," Billa told AFP.
"We are not asking for privileges. We are demanding our rights, our future and a better country," he said.
While visiting local business damaged in the demonstrations, Rama said he respected the students and added that "their right to protest must and will be protected.
"Their voices, the voices of young people and of every citizen who has taken part in protests today, must and will be heard with respect," Rama said.
However, he added that he "will not allow anyone to jeopardise the future of this country".

title: Trump waives Russia sanctions  tariffs
description: Trump waives Russia sanctions  tariffs
content:
Says waiver in national interest of the US
US President Donald Trump waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs days before they were to take effect under a law he ?signed last month, including duties on the country's goods and penalties for buying its oil and gas.
In an executive order released by the White House on Friday, Trump said the waiver was in the national interest of the United States.
The law is meant to increase pressure on Russia for its invasion of Ukraine that began in 2022. Trump, however, has been warming toward Moscow while publicly criticising Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, including suggesting Kyiv needs a new leader.
Weeks before US midterm elections in which Trump's Republicans are battling to maintain their narrow grip on both chambers of Congress, the new measures could have risked further raising oil prices as Americans face increased costs largely attributed to the US-Israeli war on Iran, analysts have said.
The legislation, whose primary backer in Congress was the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a South Carolina Republican, would have imposed tariffs of up to 100% within 30 days on all goods brought into the US from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or gas, as well as any country that knowingly bought oil or gas 30 days after the law was enacted or was among the top five countries helping Russia evade sanctions.
The order said the waiver will remain in effect until Trump or his top officials determine that "further action is appropriate." Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 in mid-September.
"I have submitted to Congress a certification that the issuance ?of such a waiver at this time is in the national interests of the United States," Trump said in the order.
Countries such as China and India, which are among the biggest buyers of Russian oil, have raised concerns about the Russia sanctions bill.
Beijing has said it "consistently opposed long-arm jurisdiction that lacks a basis in international law" while India warned Washington that new tariffs could impact bilateral ties.
The law allows the president to waive sanctions simply by informing Congress that he has determined that they are not in the national interest.
Russia on Saturday launched another ballistic missile attack on Ukraine's Zaporizhstal steelworks, causing ?damage to its blast furnace facilities, the plant's owner, Metinvest ?Group, said.
It said six ballistic missiles struck the plant's ?internal energy and logistics infrastructure. "Russia continues to target a steel plant that has not beenable to resume normal operations following previous ?attacks.

title: 17 killed in Kolkata festival stampede
description: 17 killed in Kolkata festival stampede
content:
At least 17 people were killed and several others injured in a stampede at a religious festival in north Kolkata in India, NDTV reported on Saturday.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
Durga Puja, the biggest annual festival of Hindus in India's eastern state of West Bengal, draws thousands of devotees to temporary structures known as pandals, which house idols of the goddess Durga.
A police statement said the stampede occurred in the evening due to "heavy crowds of pandal hoppers amid rainfall." All injured persons were rescued and shifted to hospital.
Besides the dead, 25 people were injured, according to West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari.
The injured were taken to Kolkata Medical College. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and the state's chief secretary Manoj Agarwal arrived at the hospital to monitor the situation.
According to eyewitnesses, many festivalgoers lost consciousness, and some were taken to the hospital on motorcycles. One witness said that the entrance to and exit from the pavilion were very narrow and that there was no lighting there.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on US social media company X that the stampede was "saddening."
"Condolences to the bereaved families. Wishing the injured a speedy recovery. The West Bengal Government is providing all possible help to the affected families," Modi wrote on US social media company X.
Interior Minister Amit Shah said on X that the "administration is ensuring that all possible medical facilities are being provided to the injured."
Unlike home ceremonies, in the city's pavilions (called "sarbojanin," which means "for everyone") the festival turns into a large-scale public event. Organizers compete for years in the decoration of such pavilions, often dedicating them to social themes, history, or art.

title: Egypt's Sisi says his presidency will end in 2030 | The Express Tribune
description:
Egypt's Sisi says 
his presidency will end in 2030
content:
Outlines plan for the country's main military academy to train potential future leaders
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday that his term would end in 2030 and outlined a plan for the country's main military academy to train potential future leaders for 30 months before then.
The proposal gives the Egyptian Military Academy a central role in preparing future leaders, underscoring the armed forces' influence beyond national defence. Under Sisi, a former general, the military has expanded its presence in the economy and civilian affairs.
Speaking at a graduation ceremony at the academy, Sisi said a committee overseen by the speaker of parliament and including intellectuals, politicians and the ministers of higher education and justice, would develop criteria for selecting candidates and draft legislation for the training programme.
Reiterating that Egypt's constitution would not be amended, he said the end of his presidential term in 2030 was "a matter that has been completely settled and will not be discussed".
He said the programme would allow Egyptians to "elect and choose from among" its graduates, but gave no details on how they would be put forward for elected or appointed posts.
"I ?will not leave the Egyptian state except when it is replete with sons and daughters capable of assuming responsibility," Sisi said.
The programme would target PhD holders from reputable Egyptian and foreign universities, who would spend 30 months at the academy learning about the state, its resources and how to preserve them, Sisi said. He said graduates would be prepared for leadership roles ranging from the presidency to ministries, governorates and parliament.
Sisi, 71, is serving a six-year term after being reelected in December 2023. Constitutional amendments approved in a 2019 referendum extended presidential terms from four to six years and allowed him to seek a third term, clearing the way for him to remain in office until 2030.
The latest in a line of Egyptian rulers drawn from the military, he became president in 2014, a year after toppling Mohamed Morsi of the Muslim Brotherhood - Egypt's first democratically elected leader - following mass protests.
He proceeded to crush the Brotherhood, the Middle East's oldest Islamist organisation, and maintain a grip on power.

title: Scores of Taliban killed as army retaliates border fire

Forces respond to unprovoked firing along Kurram border
Pakistan Army responded to unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's Upper Kurram and Ghozgarhi, with several Taliban personnel reportedly killed in the retaliatory action, state media reported on Saturday.
The army targeted the Afghan Taliban's Topsar post and Shipola base camp in the Upper Kurram sector with artillery fire, according to security sources. The Shipola base camp was reportedly destroyed.
Several Afghan Taliban personnel were reported killed during the retaliatory action along the Ghozgarhi border. In contrast, Taliban personnel abandoned a border post following the Pakistani response, the sources said, adding that an exchange of fire was continuing in the area.

On Friday, the Foreign Office said talks with Afghanistan could not be unconditional, but rejected suggestions that Islamabad was unwilling to engage with its neighbour. It also said Pakistan would welcome sincere efforts by friendly countries to help resolve the dispute.

"At present, I am not aware of any separate, formal Russian mediation initiative being under discussion," Khan said.

Iran offers to help end Saudi-Houthi conflict
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that Tehran supports a "political process" to resolve the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthi rebels.
Speaking at the 52nd session of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation's Council of Foreign Ministers in Baghdad, Araghchi said Iran was ready to help end the conflict involving the Houthis, one of Tehran's main regional allies.
Araghchi had offered last week to help facilitate dialogue between the two sides during a phone call with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan.
He said a military solution was not an option for ending Yemen's years-long civil war.
Araghchi arrived in Baghdad early Saturday and held meetings on the sidelines of the OIC gathering with his Turkish and Egyptian counterparts, Hakan Fidan and Badr Abdelatty.

Saudi warplanes targeted "civilian homes" in Taiz governorate on Saturday, killing nine people and wounding 16, the Iran-backed group's news agency said, adding that people were still trapped under the rubble.
The agency had earlier reported overnight strikes in Dhamar province that killed three children and wounded 17 other people.
It said the strikes were carried out "using cluster bombs, which are banned internationally".
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis has launched daily raids in Yemen backing the internationally recognised government in the country's long-running civil war.
The conflict, dormant for years, erupted again in July and intensified after the Iran-backed group seized the Red Sea coast last month.
The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi targets in recent weeks, including vessels in the Red Sea, oil facilities and Riyadh's international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week.

title: It would ve been criminal to let K P burn  PM
description: It would ve been criminal to let K P burn  PM
content:
Defends imposition of emergency, governor's rule Says Centre left with 'no other option' Nawaz throws weight behind
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday defended imposition of emergency and governor's rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, saying the government had been left with no other option amid fears of bloodshed during Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) long march and a breakdown of law and order.
"We were left with no other option. We understood that we could not simply remain silent and watch bloodshed unfold," the prime minister said while explaining the circumstances that led to the decision during a media talk in Gujranwala.
Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) president Nawaz Sharif also backed the imposition of emergency in K-P, saying the measure should have been taken much earlier as the province's law and order situation deteriorated.
Speaking to reporters in London, Sharif described the move as necessary and said the situation in the province was getting out of control. "Which country allows a chief minister to use government resources to attack the federal capital?" he asked.
Meanwhile, the prime minister, invoking the familiar expression about Rome burning while Nero played his fiddle, said the government could not continue to watch the situation deteriorate and risk being held responsible by future generations.
"That would have amounted to criminal negligence," he said, adding that the decision had been taken in the best interests of Pakistan. He prayed that it would produce positive results.
The prime minister made the remarks during a visit to Gujranwala, where he was accompanied by Federal Ministers Azam Nazeer Tarar and Attaullah Tarar to offer condolences on the death of Barrister Mahmood Virk, a party worker.
Describing the deceased as a loyal party worker and a decent person, the premier acknowledged his contributions.
During the speech, he appreciated Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz's performance and hoped her efforts would bring prosperity.
Turning to the situation in K-P, the prime minister said he had held several meetings with the province's former chief minister and also with Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, making what he described as sincere efforts to address the issues facing the province.
He said K-P was an integral and beautiful part of Pakistan, whose people possessed courage and resilience, and that the federal government remained willing to extend all possible assistance for the province's development and prosperity. However, he noted that the province was suffering from a spate of violence.
The prime minister said the security situation, particularly the resurgence of terrorism and infiltration from Afghanistan since 2018, required collective efforts to defeat terror groups. The premier pledged to provide "all available resources and administrative facilities" to eliminate the menace.
He regretted that law-enforcement personnel and security forces, including Pakistan Army officers, continued to sacrifice their lives in the fight against terrorism. Innocent civilians, including women and children, had also been killed in attacks, he added.
The prime minister said the government had made repeated efforts to defuse political tensions in view of the poor security outlook but alleged that long marches and protests organised by the PTI had disrupted the country's functioning one after the other.
Recalling the political turmoil of 2013-14, he said the unrest had brought economic activity to a standstill and affected imports, exports, agriculture and employment, inflicting what he described as enormous and irreparable losses on the country.
He said similar disruption had occurred last year and alleged that PTI had planned widespread violence during the October long march.
According to the prime minister, the government had established a committee and held discussions with the relevant parties for around 48 hours in an effort to reach a negotiated settlement and stop the long march from happening.
"A comprehensive agreement had eventually been prepared, with the expectation that PTI would withdraw its call for a long march while Pakistan pursued economic recovery and development, but the talks fell out after consultations with the now-suspended K-P chief minister."
He also referred to disagreements over consultations with the K-P chief minister, saying the situation had subsequently deteriorated and the government could not ignore the risk of further violence.
Now that the march had stopped, the prime minister said Pakistan's international standing improved and the domestic economy had begun to stabilise. "Today, the economy has not only stabilised but is gradually moving towards recovery and growth."
Defending the interim governance decision for two months, the prime minister said the government had concluded that inaction was no longer an option for the sake of the people of the province.
He said an advisory council had been established to help address the situation, describing it as a neutral body whose members were overwhelmingly non-political and included highly respected individuals.
"God willing, this council will help fix the situation in K-P," he said, adding that he would remain involved and attend its meetings whenever required.
The prime minister expressed hope that the measures would improve the situation and help restore peace and stability in the province.
Referring to the impact of unrest in the Middle East and resulting inflationary pressures, he said the government had provided relief to the public through a fuel subsidy scheme.

The prime minister noted that given the average household size of 5-6 people per family, the scheme's indirect benefits could extend to nearly 65 million people.

title: Trade at Taftan comes to a grinding halt
description: Sources say the immigration gate at Taftan was closed on instructions from senior officials in Islamabad
content:
Sources say the immigration gate at Taftan was closed on instructions from senior officials in Islamabad
Cross-border commercial activities between Pakistan and Iran on Saturday halted suddenly at the Taftan border crossing. This followed the unexpected closure of the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) immigration gate and the withdrawal of an important import waiver, leaving traders concerned over potential multi-million rupee financial losses.
Sources said the immigration gate at Taftan- a vital commercial artery connecting the two neighbouring nations- was closed on instructions from senior officials in Islamabad.
However, the exact reasons behind the decision remain undisclosed, and authorities have yet to issue an official notification explaining the suspension or providing a timeline for reopening.
The border closure coincides with regulatory developments from the Ministry of Commerce.
On Friday, the ministry issued an office memorandum No. 9(3)/2017-IRANwithdrawing its earlier order dated October 3, which extended the Electronic Import Form (EIF) waiver for imports from Iran.
Responding to the evolving situation, the Chamber of Commerce and Industry Quetta Balochistan issued an urgent advisory to its members and the broader business community, recommending a temporary suspension of all new purchases, product bookings, and trade commitments from Iran.
The chamber cautioned that proceeding with trade activities without regulatory clarity could result in severe customs clearance delays and financial distress for importers.
It urged local merchants to verify the legal status of EIF requirements directly with the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), the Ministry of Commerce, and border authorities before initiating fresh orders.
While official government representatives have yet to issue a public statement clarifying the policy posture, local business leaders emphasized that a swift resolution and clear policy framework are essential to safeguard commercial interests and restore smooth cross-border operations at Taftan.
Meanwhile, Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei, commenting on reports about the closure of the land border with Pakistan, said:
"Due to certain technical issues and the need to take precautionary measures, border crossings and exchanges have been temporarily suspended. However, the relevant authorities of the two countries are in close contact and are holding consultations to resolve the issue as soon as possible and restore normal operations at the border crossings."

title: Grieving families seek solace
description: Grieving families seek solace
content:
When 7-year-old Rumaisa Khan set off for school on Thursday she was wearing a brand-new pair of shoes her father had just bought for her.
Within hours she was dead, one of 35 students killed when the roof of her school collapsed in Peshawar. "I had got her a pair of new shoes which she wore that day after gifting the old one to a cousin," her father, garment shopowner Ismail Khan, said on Friday as the community mourned the victims of the tragedy.
He and his brother had pulled Rumaisa from the rubble of the Al-Khair Education Center, located in narrow alleys on the city outskirts. They rushed her to a hospital where she was declared dead. "She left us too early," he said.
School bags, books and broken furniture were scattered across the site where the roof came down on nearly 110 students taking lessons in three classes. A total of 35 students, all below the age of 13, and two female teacher were killed.
"We never imagined that sending him to school would end in such a tragedy. We had trusted that the school was a place where he could learn, grow, and fulfil his ambitions," his brother Mohammad Haroon told Reuters at their home in a densely populated area close to the school.
They were seven siblings, Amir, 13, being the youngest and Haroon, 24, the eldest. Haroon had joined the residents and rescuers to pull the children from the rubble, which took hours.
Maulana Zakirullah, 38, a prayer leader at a mosque, lost his two sons, Mohammad, 10, and Abu Bakar, 8. "The scene that confronted us when we arrived was devastating. Children were buried beneath the rubble, and it was difficult to see anything clearly," Zakirullah said.
He said he was asleep when his children had left for school. "I did not see them off," he said, adding that he only saw both his sons in coffins at a hospital several hours later.

title: Pakistan extends airspace ban on Indian aircraft until Nov 24
description: Pakistan extends airspace ban on Indian aircraft until Nov 24
content:
Pakistan has extended its airspace ban on Indian aircraft for another month, until November 24, according to a Notice to Airmen (Notam) issued by the Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA).
The restriction, which covers Indian-registered aircraft as well as aircraft owned, operated or leased by Indian airlines and operators, including military flights, continues to force Indian carriers onto longer and more expensive routes.
The previous extension was due to expire on October 24. The latest notice took effect at 7:45pm on Saturday and will remain in force until 4:59am on November 24, 2026.
"Pakistan airspace not available for Indian registered aircraft and aircraft operated/owned or leased by Indian airlines/operators, including military flights," the Notam said.
Pakistan's airspace is divided into two flight information regions (FIRs), Karachi and Lahore, according to a 2022 Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority (PCAA) document. The latest Notam applies to both regions: Karachi (OPKR) and Lahore (OPLR).
India and Pakistan closed their airspaces to each other's airlines in late April 2025, after tensions escalated following a deadly attack in Pahalgam, in India-occupied Kashmir.
On April 24, Pakistan's top brass announced a series of measures, including immediately closing Pakistani airspace to all India-owned or Indian-operated airlines, in response to aggressive moves by New Delhi.
India had alleged, without providing evidence, that Islamabad backed the Pahalgam attack. Pakistan strongly denied involvement and offered to support a neutral investigation.
The two nuclear-armed countries fought their fiercest air battle in May, during which Pakistan said it had downed seven Indian fighter jets.
Pakistan has extended the airspace restriction several times since then, compelling Indian carriers to take longer routes and absorb additional operating costs.

title: Criticism not aimed at institutions  Fazl
description: Criticism not aimed at institutions  Fazl
content:
Terms ministers' allegations character assassination
Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Saturday called the government "powerless", questioned its counterterrorism policy and challenged the rationale for imposing governor's rule and an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).
Demanding an in-camera session of parliament to examine why the country had failed to curb terrorism, Fazl said his criticism was directed at government policies rather than state institutions and was intended to bring about corrective action.
He termed the allegations levelled against him by federal ministers character assassination, arguing that political leaders should be taken into confidence on security decisions instead of being ridiculed or accused of undermining the state.
Addressing a news conference in Lahore, Fazl said his party had paid a heavy price in the fight against terrorism, with around 250 religious scholars and workers losing their lives.
He questioned how a party whose members had made such sacrifices could be accused of supporting terrorists, insisting that its contribution to the country's security should neither be ridiculed nor overlooked.
"Our only question is why the country has failed to eliminate terrorism. Let us sit together and find out why. Parliament is the most appropriate forum to discuss the issue and make decisions. Instead of ridiculing politicians, the government should take them on board in this fight so that we can move forward together," he said.
Fazl questioned where key security decisions were being made, alleging that parliament was expected to endorse decisions taken elsewhere.
"If Parliament is supreme, why are decisions taken in Rawalpindi while Parliament is simply told to follow them?" he remarked. "The issue is that this government is powerless. Decisions are taken somewhere else, and it implements them obediently," he alleged.
He maintained that the country needed a shared national narrative and a counterterrorism strategy developed through consensus. The government, he said, should explain its decisions and take the public into confidence rather than impose "unilateral measures".
"We have no desire to start a debate in the country. The sacrifices should not be made controversial," he said, urging parliament to assess the country's security situation and determine why efforts against militancy were not producing the desired results.
He also cautioned institutions responsible for security against ridiculing politicians or making light of their sacrifices.
Fazl said the government had decided to join an international alliance against terrorism and urged it to accept his proposal for an in-camera parliamentary session.
He questioned why the authorities were unwilling to explain their approach to the public, arguing that parliament was the only appropriate platform for taking the nation into confidence.
"If the nation is expected to form lashkars against terrorism and sit in trenches, it must at least be taken into confidence," he said.
The JUI-F chief also questioned the government's decision to negotiate with the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), which had been in power in K-P, while accusing the party of supporting terrorists.

title: Railways logs over 55 accidents this year
description: Railways logs over 55 accidents this year
content:
Minister visits Steel and Carriage Shops in Mughalpura
Federal Minister for Railways Muhammad Hanif Abbasi on Saturday visited the Steel and Carriage Shops in Mughalpura, where he inspected production facilities and directed officials to ensure quality standards in the manufacturing of railway components.
During his visit to the Mughalpura Steel Shop, the minister inspected the electric arc furnace and reviewed the spectro laboratory responsible for testing parts manufactured in the furnace.
Pakistan Railways has recorded more than 55 accidents involving passenger and freight trains since January 1, raising concerns over railway safety, maintenance standards and the effectiveness of measures announced to prevent mishaps.
The accidents have reportedly left several people dead and dozens injured, while also causing millions of rupees in damage to railway infrastructure. Repeated incidents have fuelled fear among passengers, some of whom say travelling by train remains a necessity despite the risks.
Passengers have questioned how they can avoid railway travel when it remains an essential mode of transport for them. The frequency of accidents has also raised questions about the implementation of safety measures under the directions of Federal Minister for Railways Hanif Abbasi.
Despite the minister's strict instructions, accidents have continued to occur, while railway officials have reportedly continued to provide reassuring assessments of the situation. The recurring incidents have placed the department's safety and maintenance arrangements under scrutiny.
According to railway sources, passenger and freight trains have been involved in more than 55 accidents of varying severity since the beginning of the year. The Yusufwala coal train has reportedly been involved in several accidents. On August 27, 10 wagons of a freight train derailed near Khanpur. On the same day, the engine and two coaches of the Rawal Express went off the tracks near Kala Gujran.
On September 27, the Yusufwala coal train met with an accident near Khairpur. Earlier, on September 9, three wagons of a coal-laden freight train derailed at Kotri yard. On September 2, the power van of the Khyber Mail derailed near Sanjani.
Another coal train accident occurred on September 6, when seven wagons went off the tracks. These incidents add to a series of mishaps involving freight operations, with railway sources identifying the Sukkur, Karachi and Multan divisions among the areas where most train accidents have occurred.
On May 24, a shuttle train in Quetta was targeted in an act of sabotage, damaging three coaches. The Rahman Baba Express also suffered a major accident in the Multan division, further highlighting the range of incidents affecting railway operations.

During July alone, 398,400 passengers travelled through the airport. Of 1,020 scheduled flights, 96 were cancelled and 326 were delayed.
Domestic and international airlines failed to provide affected passengers with meals and hotel accommodation in a timely manner, prompting protests and angry slogans at the airport.
The protests became so intense that personnel of the Airport Security Force (ASF) had to be called in to bring the situation under control. Umrah pilgrims accounted for a large proportion of those protesting, with many unable to perform Umrah at their intended time. Some lost a day of their pilgrimage, while others lost two days.

Federal ministers on Saturday intensified their criticism of JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman over his opposition to the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), insisting that the move was aimed at addressing terrorism rather than pursuing political interests.
In a statement posted on X, Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry lambasted Fazl for linking the imposition of emergency in K-P to an alleged attempt to take control of the province's mineral resources.
Chaudhry said it was regrettable to politicise a serious national issue such as terrorism through allegations. He urged the JUI-F chief, whom he described as a senior politician familiar with the consequences of terrorism, to play a constructive role in efforts to eliminate the menace.
He said the federal government's priority was to protect the public and restore peace in K-P. He added that Pakistan's armed forces were sacrificing lives to secure peace and that the situation called for national unity and a coordinated strategy against terrorism rather than political point-scoring.
Chaudhry also called on PTI, which he said had governed K-P for 13 years, to answer questions about its performance and the deteriorating law and order situation.
He said the people of K-P needed peace, security and development rather than political disputes, and urged Fazl to support national efforts against terrorism.
Speaking to the media in Jaranwala, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry said the decision was an administrative measure taken after considering other options, with the sole objective of combating terrorism.
He rejected the suggestion that the federal government intended to remove the PTI government to strengthen the presence of the PML-N in the province.
Talal expressed disappointment over Fazl's criticism, saying the government had not expected the JUI-F chief to seek a share in K-P's political arrangements following the removal of the PTI government.
Talal also questioned Fazl's references to the 2024 general elections and the separation of East Pakistan in 1971. He said the JUI-F had lost the election in K-P to the PTI, while in Balochistan it had been defeated by Mahmood Khan Achakzai's Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party.
The minister said he did not understand why Fazl was linking the current situation to the 1971 separation, adding that the measures in K-P were not intended to distribute political shares, form alliances or establish governments.
He maintained that JUI-F deserved respect when it stood with Pakistan's interests. Talal also offered to work with all relevant stakeholders to implement the National Action Plan and jointly combat terrorism, stressing that political activity was possible only where peace prevailed.
He said only one member of the K-P advisory council had a political background, explaining that she represented families of security personnel who had died in the line of duty.

title: Pakistani celebs speak out on cancer awareness
description: Pakistani celebs speak out on cancer awareness
content:
Urge women to undergo testing to guard against breast cancer
Every October, pink ribbons appear across social media, hospitals and public spaces as Breast Cancer Awareness Month encourages women to recognise warning signs and seek timely medical advice. In Pakistan, actresses Angeline Malik and Nadia Jamil have used their experiences with cancer to raise awareness, while the death of veteran actor Naila Jaffri remains a reminder of the challenges patients face.
Diagnosed with cancer, Angeline Malik has shared aspects of her treatment journey, including chemotherapy, to encourage others to seek help and speak openly about the disease.
Speaking to The Express Tribune, Malik emphasised the importance of awareness and early medical intervention.
"Look, I love all my fans that I am standing in front of you right now. This battle against cancer never ends and we should talk about it. Because there were a lot of things that I did not know. I try to create awareness on my platform. Please get your tests done and do not ignore help. Because for me, I realised too late."
Malik's message reflects the uncertainty that accompanies a cancer diagnosis and the importance of seeking support. By discussing her experience publicly, she hopes to help women recognise the importance of their health and avoid delaying medical attention.
Nadia Jamil, who was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2020, has also spoken candidly about treatment, recovery and the emotional impact of the disease.
In an Instagram post marking Metastatic Breast Cancer Awareness Day on 13 October, Jamil recalled chemotherapy sessions, hospital waiting rooms and the loss of people who, she wrote, should still be alive.
"Cancer took so much from me. But it also gave me something I never expected. It showed me my own strength and resilience. It taught me that I can stand up for myself, fully and fiercely, and never again wait for anyone else to meet my needs," she wrote.
Reflecting on the faith and community she found during her illness, she added, "It gave me a community of extraordinary women. And it gave me Faith, with a capital F, in the Almighty. Unwavering. Unshakeable. Alhamdulillah."
Jamil extended her support to women living with metastatic breast cancer, in which the disease spreads beyond the breast to other parts of the body.
"You are not a statistic. You are not your diagnosis. You are mothers, daughters, sisters, friends, women with laughter and plans and dreams that still matter," she wrote.
She encouraged women who have completed treatment to attend follow-up appointments and remain attentive to changes in their bodies.
"And to every woman hearing those words for the first time this week: you are stronger than you know, and we are with you. Hum saath hain."
She concluded: "Cancer takes so much. But it does not get to take our voice, our dignity, our faith, or each other."
Veteran television and theatre actor Naila Jaffri died in Karachi on 17 July 2021, aged 56, after battling cancer for several years. She had appealed to television channels to pay royalties for repeat broadcasts, explaining that the payments could help actors meet medical expenses when illness prevented them from working.
The experiences of Malik and Jamil, alongside Jaffri's story, underline the importance of open conversations about cancer, access to medical care and emotional support.

A state court judge in New Mexico has dismissed charges of child sexual abuse against West Wing actor and director Timothy Busfield, saying the prosecution did not act in a fair and impartial manner during grand jury proceedings.

Prosecutors said on Friday that they had not yet decided whether to pursue another indictment.
The twins reported that ?the alleged contact had occurred over a two-year period, when they were aged seven and eight, during breaks in production, prosecutors said in a criminal complaint filed in January.
Busfield, a director and producer of The Cleaning Lady, was charged in February in a four-count grand jury indictment that accused the actor of groping one of the ?boys.
He steadfastly professed his innocence, calling the allegations against him "lies", and his attorneys asked for the charges against him to be dismissed.
In Friday's ruling, Montano said the prosecution did not properly instruct members of the grand jury on procedures for requesting testimony from additional witnesses.
"The prosecuting attorney failed to act in a fair and impartial manner," Montano wrote.
Busfield, 69, is best known for his prime-time television roles as a White House reporter on the NBC political drama The West Wing and as an advertising agency executive on ABC ensemble series Thirtysomething. He also appeared in the baseball film Field of Dreams starring Kevin Costner. Agencies

title: China AI firms eye Hong Kong listings
description: China AI firms eye Hong Kong listings
content:
Hardware companies expect global investment; face scrutiny
Listings of Chinese AI supply chain companies are expected to stand their ground, weathering rising valuation concerns and increasingly sharper scrutiny, a Citi banker working with Chinese companies said.
Despite recent valuation pullbacks on data centre companies, largely originating from the US market, future AI supply-chain listings would continue in Hong Kong, said Simon Yuan, Citi's head of China investment banking.
Chinese companies plan to list in Hong Kong are cushioned by a roughly even split between domestic Chinese and international demand, Yuan, who also heads Citi's financial institutions group in APAC, said on the sidelines of the IMF meetings in Bangkok. The market is supported by a pool of local liquidity, with rising southbound capital from the Chinese mainland emerging as a key buying force, Yuan said.
Still, "if the whole AI cycle turns in the US – and we have seen some volatility in the last few weeks – you will see an impact everywhere, Hong Kong included," he warned.
Many Chinese hardware players have proactively established manufacturing footprints outside mainland China, he said, which helps them better service global clients and mitigate geopolitical friction. Chinese hardware suppliers have benefited from the global AI infrastructure boom, gaining both sales volume growth and higher unit prices, Yuan said.
Next year, the focus in Hong Kong's equity capital markets is expected to shift away from pure hardware, toward Chinese artificial intelligence models and application developers, he said.

title: India food probe names Reliance  Blinkit
description: India food probe names Reliance  Blinkit
content:
Five establishments' licences suspended; FDA alleges contractor-to-broker chain reaching retailers
India's food safety authority has named officials of Reliance retail and consumer units and of Eternal's Blinkit and Hyperpure units, including Blinkit CEO Albinder Dhindsa, in a probe over expired food products that have allegedly re-entered the food supply chain, according to case documents reviewed by Reuters.
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) of Maharashtra state, home to Mumbai, has led a crackdown on food safety under its chief Tukaram Mundhe, 51, including shutting down some of Mumbai's most popular eateries as well as outlets of Domino's and Pizza Hut for poor hygiene. The state agency has also suspended the permit of a McDonald's outlet.
The latest case, which has led to a police complaint by the food safety authority, involves large retail and quick-commerce companies, which sell products to millions of households in the world's most populous country.
Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration, according to the documents reviewed by Reuters, said its officials visited some warehouses of Reliance Retail, Reliance Consumer and Zomato Hyperpure, and that company officials could not provide verifiable proof that disposal of expired food was actually carried out by their contractors.
"The disposal agencies... do not destroy the stock," the case document alleged.
In the case of a Zomato Hyperpure warehouse, a company representative named a contractor as its disposal agency which FDA officials could not trace, according to the documents.
Reliance and Blinkit did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
"Any attempt to divert expired, damaged or consumer-rejected food products meant for destruction back into the market is a serious matter that demands strict scrutiny and accountability," Maharashtra's FDA chief Tukaram Mundhe told Reuters.
"No company, brand, business or individual is above the law when it comes to food safety."
Reliance Retail and Reliance Consumer are part of billionaire Mukesh Ambani's business group. Zomato's Hyperpure is a unit of Eternal that also runs food delivery service Zomato and quick commerce business Blinkit.
The FDA probe said it found a pattern where large retail and quick commerce distribution warehouses handed over expired and customer-rejected packages of food to contractors who passed the food to unlicensed sorting yards. These sorting yards then separated out saleable-looking packets, which eventually reached other retailers and the consumer market, according to case documents from the probe.
"The chain thus runs from company warehouse to disposal agency, unlicensed yard, broker, retailer and consumer."
The Maharashtra FDA on Thursday suspended the licences of five establishments in the state – three Reliance and two Eternal entities, the case documents said.
Enforcement of food safety laws has traditionally been weak in India and the recent round of extensive crackdowns has garnered large-scale public support.
In August, Indian authorities raided an illegal operation in Mumbai that faked expiry dates and nutritional information on original food products manufactured by PepsiCo, Nestle, Coca-Cola and Unilever, so they could be exported to other countries.
Ban on added sugars in infant foods proposed
India's food safety regulator on Saturday proposed a ban on adding sucrose and fructose to food products for infants up to six months of age, tightening rules on added sugars in infant nutrition products.
Under existing rules, lactose and glucose polymers are the preferred carbohydrate sources in infant nutrition products, while sucrose and fructose can be added when required, subject to prescribed limits, the regulator said.
The move comes amid an intensifying food safety crackdown in India, where regulators have forced local eateries and branded restaurants to suspend operations, while a push for front-of-pack warning labels has rattled the country's more than $100 billion packaged food industry.
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said the proposed measure aims to reduce infants' exposure to added sugars and address health risks linked to childhood obesity.
The existing regulations set nutritional composition, quality and safety standards for infant nutrition products intended for children from birth to 24 months of age, it said.
Activists and officials have long raised concerns about rising obesity rates, particularly among children. India had 180 million overweight or obese adults in 2021, a figure projected to reach 450 million by 2050, according to a study published in the medical journal The Lancet.
The FSSAI and some state regulators have intensified checks on food safety in recent months, releasing regular public updates including photos and videos of raids that have drawn widespread attention online.
In August, the FSSAI proposed a red hexagonal stamp on labels of food products high in any two or more nutrients of concern such as sugar, salt or saturated fat, but tightened the proposal after a public outcry, saying a warning would now be required if even one nutrient exceeds the prescribed level.

title: AI led bid rigging alert system created
description: AI led bid rigging alert system created
content:
CCP develops system to uncover concealed patterns of cartelisation in procurement
The Competition Commission of Pakistan (CCP) has developed an artificial intelligence-powered system to uncover concealed patterns of cartelisation in Pakistan's public procurement market, where an estimated $60 billion is spent annually on goods, works and services.
The Bid-Rigging Detection System (BRDS) is designed to screen large volumes of procurement data and flag suspicious bidding patterns for investigation. Its development assumes particular significance as public procurement is estimated to account for approximately 15-20% of Pakistan's gross domestic product.
Historically, fragmented procurement data and the absence of automated links with corporate ownership records have constrained the systematic detection of sophisticated practices such as bid rotation, cover-bidding and participation by related companies across multiple tenders. BRDS seeks to shift detection from a largely complaint-driven and manual process towards proactive, systematic and data-led market surveillance, says a CCP statement issued on Saturday.
The initiative has also gained international recognition, with BRDS featuring in the Computational Antitrust Worldwide: Fifth Cross-Agency Report, published by Stanford Computational Antitrust. The report brings together first-hand accounts from 30 competition authorities and examines how computational tools are enabling regulators to undertake enforcement work that would otherwise be difficult – or impossible – through conventional methods.
BRDS has reached an advanced stage of development and pre-deployment preparation. Understandings have been reached with the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority, provincial procurement authorities and the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan to facilitate its implementation and the institutional coordination required for effective data integration.
CCP Chairman Farid Ahmad Tarar said procurement worth trillions of rupees could not be effectively monitored solely through complaints and the manual examination of individual tenders. He said BRDS would enable the commission to identify complex and concealed bidding patterns across large datasets and direct its investigative resources towards the highest-risk cases.
He emphasised that alerts generated by the system would serve as investigative leads rather than determinations of wrongdoing. Each alert will require independent verification, evidence gathering and legal assessment under the Competition Act, 2010.
"CCP's contribution to the Stanford report also sets out practical lessons for competition authorities in developing economies, emphasising machine-readable data, inter-agency cooperation, controlled testing and legal defensibility," the statement said.

title: Pakistan takes basmati to Budapest buyers
description: Pakistan takes basmati to Budapest buyers
content:
First Rice Festival held to court Hungarian importers, chefs; recipe book and samples distributed
The Embassy of Pakistan in Hungary hosted the first Pakistan Rice Festival in Budapest, introducing Pakistani basmati rice to Hungarian importers, chefs and food industry professionals, according to a statement issued on Saturday.
The event was organised in collaboration with the Ministry of Commerce and the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan (TDAP).
Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan welcomed the holding of the festival, saying that taking Pakistani produce directly to buyers in European capitals is among the most effective ways of winning new customers and showing the world what the country has to offer.
The minister acknowledged the work of Pakistan's Ambassador to Hungary Asif Hussain Memon, Trade and Investment Attaché Shehryar Amjad Qaisrani and TDAP in putting the event together. He said basmati rice is one of Pakistan's most recognised exports and that growing demand for it in international markets is encouraging for farmers and exporters. He noted that Pakistan's missions abroad are increasingly taking agricultural and food products directly to buyers in new markets.
The festival was attended by importers and business leaders from the food and agriculture sector, leading Hungarian master chefs, representatives of public sector bodies and members of the diplomatic community. Ambassador Asif Hussain Memon briefed participants on the heritage and significance of basmati rice and its export potential, adding that the category is not only an agricultural product but a renowned brand protected through Geographical Indication (GI), underscoring its heritage and proven quality.
A live cooking demonstration, "The Art of Biryani", was conducted by the trade and investment attaché, offering guests an interactive introduction to Pakistani rice and the dishes built around it. Complementary Pakistani products were also displayed, including Himalayan Pink Salt, which participants were invited to sample.
The embassy prepared a short rice recipe book in Hungarian featuring a range of rice-based dishes, and distributed samples of Pakistani rice to all participants, encouraging them to cook with it in their own kitchens. Guests were also invited to attend FoodAg 2026, Pakistan's international food and agriculture exhibition, to be held at the Expo Centre in Karachi from November 23 to 26, 2026.
The festival follows the creation of the post of trade and investment attaché at the embassy last year, reflecting the government's push to deepen trade and investment engagement in non-conventional markets.
