title: Several Afghan Taliban posts destroyed as Pakistan responds to Kurram border firing  state media
description: Sources say several Afghan Taliban personnel were killed after Pakistan Army responded to cross border firing
content:
Sources say several Afghan Taliban personnel were killed after Pakistan Army responded to cross-border firing
The Pakistan Army responded to unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's Upper Kurram and Ghozgarhi, with several Taliban personnel reportedly killed in the retaliatory action, state media reported on Saturday.
The army targeted the Afghan Taliban’s Topsar post and Shipola base camp in the Upper Kurram sector with artillery fire, according to security sources. The Shipola base camp was reportedly destroyed.
Several Afghan Taliban personnel were reported killed during the retaliatory action along the Ghozgarhi border. In contrast, Taliban personnel abandoned a border post following the Pakistani response, the sources said, adding that an exchange of fire was continuing in the area.
Read : Info ministry calls out Afghan Taliban for deflecting attention from terrorist sanctuaries
Later, following another incident of unprovoked firing by the Afghan Taliban in the Kurram sector along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, the Pakistan Army responded with heavy weapons.
The sources said that the Afghan Taliban regime was assisting militants. Several Taliban posts were destroyed in the subsequent retaliatory action, while personnel fled their positions, they added.
The Pakistan Army remained alert and committed to defending the country’s borders and safeguarding national security, the security sources said.
Pakistan has repeatedly accused terrorist groups based in Afghanistan of carrying out attacks inside the country and demanded that Kabul take action against them. The Afghan Taliban government has rejected accusations that it allows its territory to be used for attacks against Pakistan.
Islamabad maintains that the terrorist nexus extended beyond the movement of terrorists across the border to their training, arming and operational support.
In 2026 alone, terrorism emanating from Afghan soil claimed the lives of 1,327 Pakistanis and injured another 2,484, according to figures cited by Pakistani authorities.
Officials said that whenever Pakistani forces targeted terrorist hideouts, the Taliban regime instead moved to defend the militants and their sanctuaries rather than dismantling the infrastructure. The issue, Pakistan has argued, was not confined to TTP.
UN assessments have continued to document the presence of several other militant organisations in Afghanistan, including al Qaeda, the East Turkestan Islamic Movement (ETIM) and Islamic State-Khorasan, reinforcing concerns about the broader militant ecosystem operating from Afghan territory.
Also Read : One soldier martyred, 12 terrorists killed as security forces foil infiltration attempt in Kurram: ISPR
Pakistani officials say the continued presence of these groups, combined with training facilities, cross-border infiltration and access to sophisticated weapons, demonstrates that Afghanistan remains an important base for terrorist activity affecting Pakistan.
Pakistan's position, according to officials, remains that Kabul must take concrete steps to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries, eliminate training infrastructure, prevent cross-border infiltration and ensure that Afghan territory is not used for attacks against Pakistan.
The government has maintained that the issue was fundamentally one of Pakistan's national security and that continued attacks from Afghan soil cannot be addressed through denials alone.
Pakistan says it expected the Taliban regime to fulfil its commitments by taking verifiable action against terrorist groups operating from its territory rather than defending or denying their presence.

title: Law Roach says he is ready to pursue acting after years of styling Hollywood   s biggest stars
description: I want to try everything  If I   m terrible at it  at least I tried   he said
content:
“I want to try everything. If I’m terrible at it, at least I tried," he said
Law Roach is ready to step in front of the camera, with the celebrity stylist revealing that he is interested in pursuing acting if the right opportunity comes along.
Roach, best known for his work with Zendaya and other major Hollywood stars, shared his ambitions during an appearance at the InStyle Imagemaker Awards on Thursday, October 15. Speaking to Variety, he said he was open to exploring new creative opportunities beyond fashion.
“When a director sees something for me,” Roach said, explaining that he wants to be willing to try different things. “I want to try everything. If I’m terrible at it, at least I tried.”
The comments mark a potential new chapter for Roach, who has built an influential career transforming celebrity fashion into a form of storytelling. His work with Zendaya, in particular, has helped establish the actress as one of the most closely watched figures on the red carpet.
Roach has become a celebrity in his own right through his distinctive approach to styling, regularly generating attention for the looks he creates for award ceremonies, premieres and major fashion events. His collaborations with Zendaya have included memorable appearances at the Met Gala, the Academy Awards and international film premieres.
Beyond styling, Roach has expanded his television presence, including appearing as a judge on Project Runway. His willingness to offer candid criticism and his strong fashion opinions have helped make him a recognisable personality beyond the industry.
An acting career would represent another expansion of his work in entertainment, although Roach has not announced a specific project or confirmed that he has been cast in a film or television production.
For now, the stylist appears interested in keeping his options open and approaching acting with the same willingness to experiment that has defined his fashion career.
Roach's potential move into acting comes as he continues to influence celebrity culture through his work with some of the industry's biggest names. Whether his next appearance will be on a film set or another red carpet remains to be seen.

title: Govt notifies 48 member Area Representative and Development Council for 12 K P districts
description: ADS outlines that the nomination process was completed through extensive consultations with local jirgas
content:
ADS outlines that the nomination process was completed through extensive consultations with local jirgas
The federal government on Saturday formally notified the establishment of the 48-member Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC) across 12 districts of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) as the governor consolidated his rule in the province.
The federal government imposed emergency and governor's rule in K-P on October 11 under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, which suspended the PTI-led provincial administration and transferred executive authority to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi. On October 15, a joint session of the Parliament adopted two separate resolutions ratifying the presidential proclamations imposing a state of emergency and governor's rule for two months in K-P amid opposition uproar.
Through the first resolution, the joint sitting approved the proclamation of emergency issued by President Asif Ali Zardari under the second proviso to Article 232(1) of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan. The approval was granted in accordance with Article 232(7) of the Constitution.
The official notification named 48 members drawn from the tribal and adjacent districts, with Shaukatullah Khan of the Tarkani tribe from Bajaur district appointed as chairman and Malik Khan Marjan of the Wazir tribe from North Waziristan named vice chairman.
https://x.com/fkkundi/status/2111474785368858728?s=20
According to the government, the move was intended to give local communities a direct role in developmental decision-making as well as ensure closer oversight of regional development projects.
The Area Development Secretariat (ADS) outlined that the entire nomination process had been completed through extensive consultations with local jirgas (assemblies of tribal elders), held with the full cooperation of the respective district administrations.
Read: K-P is rich in minerals; we will 'extract and sell them', says Kundi
The secretariat said deputy commissioners across all 12 districts facilitated the jirgas, during which communities identified “preferred and influential tribal elders” through consensus.
Officials explained that the names emerging from the jirgas underwent careful initial scrutiny and processing by the additional chief secretary and administrator of the ADS. The refined list was then forwarded to the K-P chief secretary, who examined it and forwarded the names to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi.
The governor subsequently sent the final list to the federal government for formal approval.
Once the process had been completed, the federal government issued the official notification through the Cabinet Division.
The notified council members represent a broad cross-section of the region’s major tribes.
From Bajaur, the Tarkani tribe was represented by Shaukatullah Khan, Shahabuddin Khan, Malik Sultan Zeb and Haji Lali Shah. Mohmand district was represented by Malik Fayyaz Khan of the Khadikhel Khozi, Malik Nadir Manan of the Bazai and Malik Sahib Khan Amber of the Utman Khel. In Khyber, five Afridi elders — Malik Abdul Razzaq, Malik Izzatullah, Malik Salahuddin, Malik Zahir Shah and Sherin Khan — served on the council.
Kurram’s representation included Munir Hussain Bangash of the Bangash tribe, Malik Abdul Wali Khan of the Ali Sherzai, and Malik Zameen Hussain, Syed Wali Syed Mian and Ehsanullah Ehsan of the Turi tribe.
Furthermore, Orakzai nominated Lal Man Shah of the Ali Khel, Syed Fakhar Abbas of the Syed tribe and Faizullah of the Mashti. North Waziristan was represented by Malik Khan Marjan, Malik Nasrullah and Malik Haji Sher Muhammad of the Wazir tribe, along with Mufti Misbahullah Khan of the Dawar and Malik Habib Khan of the Dawar Darpa Khel. Malik Khan Marjan also discharged the duties of vice chairman.
Read more: Parliament's joint session endorses K-P emergency, governor's rule amid opposition uproar
For the ARDC, Upper South Waziristan nominated Saleh Shah of the Qureshi Mehsud, Malik Irfanuddin Ahmed Burki of the Burki tribe, and Malik Muhammad Roman Mehsud and Malik Ramtal Khan of the Mehsud tribe. South Waziristan Lower was represented by Malik Alauddin Wazir, Malik Jameel Toji Khel and Malik Moinuddin Wazir of the Wazir tribe, together with Malik Sardar Abbas of the Suleman Khel.
Bannu was represented by Baz Muhammad Khan and Maulana Abdul Ghaffar Qureshi of the Bannuchi tribe, and Malik Sherin and Malik Ehsan Khan of the Wazir tribe.
Dera Ismail Khan’s members were Abdul Haleem of the Qasuria, Sardar Aghaz Khan of the Gandapur, Sardar Ibad Khan of the Sherani and Qaiser Khan Advocate of the Mian Khel, who represented their respective areas.
From Tank, Nawabzada Abdul Wahab of the Kati Khel, Abdullah Nangial of the Mehsud and Irfanullah Kundi of the Kundi tribe were nominated. Finally, Lakki Marwat was represented by Maulana Umar Ashrafi of the Bettani tribe and Malik Idris Khan, Najeebullah Khan and Rehmatullah, alias Matti, of the Marwat tribe.
Following the federal cabinet’s approval and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s advice, President Asif Ali Zardari invoked Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, imposing emergency measures and governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P). The move transferred executive authority from the provincial government to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi. All these measures were then ratified during the individual as well as joint sessions of the parliament held in mid-October.
The federal government subsequently formed an 11-member advisory council to oversee administrative affairs and ordered the immediate establishment of the ADS in 12 designated districts: Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Lakki Marwat, Bannu, Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, North Waziristan, Upper South Waziristan and Lower South Waziristan. The ADS was set to operate under the supervision of the ARDC, in coordination with federal and provincial authorities, security forces and law enforcement agencies.
Also Read: Explainer: What are the ARDC and ADS, and what are their roles and objectives?
Council members were to be nominated based on population and tribal representation, with appointments to be officially notified by the federal government. The ARDC would elect its chairman and vice chairman, meet every 15 days, and convene whenever required. Its members would also serve on district coordination committees to strengthen cooperation between local representatives and administrative institutions.
The council would also identify development projects based on local needs, public demands and ground realities, submitting recommendations to the federal government.
It will also review law and order, recommend measures to counter terrorism and illegal activities, and propose improvements in governance, public safety and basic services. The arrangement aims to strengthen local representation, improve institutional coordination and ensure more effective delivery of development and security initiatives.

title: Julia Stiles teases deeply emotional    Dancing with the Stars    dedication night tribute to Heath Ledger
description: Stiles and Sosa will dance to Frankie Valli s timeless classic  Can   t Take My Eyes Off You
content:
Stiles and Sosa will dance to Frankie Valli's timeless classic 'Can’t Take My Eyes Off You'
Julia Stiles has been teasing what promises to be one of the most emotional moments of the current television season, preparing a heartfelt tribute dedicated to her late co-star, Heath Ledger, for the upcoming "Dedication Night" on Dancing with the Stars.
The acclaimed actress, who has been wowing judges and audiences alike throughout her run on the hit dance competition alongside professional partner Ezra Sosa, is set to perform a moving contemporary routine honouring the beloved Australian actor, who tragically passed away in January 2008 at the age of 28.
For the special routine, Stiles and Sosa will dance to Frankie Valli's timeless classic "Can’t Take My Eyes Off You." The song holds immense sentimental value for fans of late-90s cinema, serving as the soundtrack to one of the most iconic romantic gestures in modern pop culture history.
In the beloved 1999 teen comedy 10 Things I Hate About You, Ledger's character, Patrick Verona, famously serenaded Stiles' character, Kat Stratford, from the high school stadium bleachers, backed by the school marching band in his quest to win her over.
Speaking about the upcoming performance during an appearance on Hulu’s Get Real podcast, Stiles kept specific choreography details under wraps while acknowledging the profound significance of the moment.
She shared with listeners that they were still finalising the routine, but expressed absolute certainty that it would be a truly special experience. Fans across social media have already expressed overwhelming emotional reactions to the announcement, flooding platforms with nostalgic tributes and highlighting the enduring cultural footprint left by both Ledger and the iconic film.
The anticipated tribute follows closely on the heels of another standout week for Stiles on the programme, which featured a Save the Last Dance-inspired jazz routine complete with a surprise cameo from her former co-star Sean Patrick Thomas.
As the remaining couples prepare to step onto the floor to honour the people, places, and memories that have shaped their lives, Dedication Night is shaping up to be an unforgettable evening, with viewers and judges alike reaching for the tissues as Stiles honours her late friend and colleague.

title: Two police head constables martyred in attack in Balochistan   s Nasirabad
description: Unidentified gunmen open fire on a police patrol near Bedar Bridge  Families of martyrds stage sit in with bodies
content:
Unidentified gunmen open fire on a police patrol near Bedar Bridge; families of martyrs stage sit-in with bodies
Two police head constables were martyred when unidentified armed men opened fire on a police patrol in Balochistan’s Nasirabad district on Saturday.
The attackers also made off with the slain officers’ official weapons.
Police told The Express Tribune that the incident occurred near Bedar Bridge, where the motorcycle-riding officers were on routine patrol. Unidentified gunmen suddenly opened fire, killing both head constables on the spot. The martyred officers have been identified as Head Constable Malik Bugti and Head Constable Ahmad Lashari.

Deputy Superintendent of Police Ghulam Sarwar Mengal said the assailants fled with the official weapons of the martyred personnel after the attack. Upon receiving information, police and security forces immediately sealed off the area and launched a search operation to track down the culprits. Investigations into the incident have also begun.
Meanwhile, the families of the martyred officers staged a protest sit-in with the bodies at Pat Feeder Bridge, blocking the Sindh-Balochistan National Highway. The blockade disrupted traffic, causing inconvenience to travellers.
Security in the area has been further tightened following the incident, and preparations for operations to arrest the perpetrators are underway.

title: India s  cockroach  movement founder released a day after detention
description: CJP s legal affairs head Ratna Singh said Dipke was    released after he agreed to certain conditions
content:
CJP's legal affairs head Ratna Singh said Dipke was ​released after he agreed to certain conditions
India's "cockroach" youth movement leader was released by an Indian court on Saturday, a ‌day after he was detained for trying to lead another protest rally in New Delhi calling for the resignation of the country's election chief.
Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), rose to prominence this year when a weeks-long ​sit-in contributed to India's education minister resigning.
CJP's legal affairs head Ratna Singh said Dipke was ​released after he agreed to certain conditions. Singh gave no details of the ⁠terms.
Dipke's youth-led group, opposition parties and student organisations have held near-daily protests this month demanding Chief ​Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter lists that they say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya ​Janata Party (BJP).
Read: Indian police detain 'cockroach' movement founder Dipke ahead of protest
More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision . The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning ​legitimate electoral processes.
Student activist Neha Bora, a prominent face of the protests, who was also detained ​on Friday as she tried to reach central Delhi with dozens of supporters, was released on Saturday.
"Please, spare the people ‌of ⁠India. Impeach Gyanesh Kumar and halt SIR (special intensive revision), so that the ordinary citizens of this country can breathe a sigh of relief, feel at ease, and have their voting rights ensured," Bora told ANI news agency after she was released.
Student groups call for more protest action
Dipke was detained on Friday as ​he stepped out of a ​house in central ⁠Delhi, with police hauling him into a police car and driving away after a brief argument.
Read more: From theatre to streets, Gen Z protester Neha Bora a new face of India's youth unrest
Dipke had called Friday's protest in support of two CJP leaders ​detained and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating ​at a protest ⁠site in violation of a ban.
Earlier on Friday, police had met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest.
Student groups called for more protest action on Saturday.
The movement, which was mobilised by the ⁠youth and ​joined by many opposition parties, has emerged as one of ​the biggest political challenges faced by Modi and the BJP in the prime minister's 12 years in power.

title: Pope Leo returns to Vatican four days after lung cancer surgery
description: Pope to lead prayers with pilgrims in St  Peter s Square on Sunday  plans South American trip next    month
content:
Pope to lead prayers with pilgrims in St. Peter's Square on Sunday, plans South American trip next ​month
Pope Leo left the hospital in Rome on Saturday afternoon and returned to the Vatican four days after ‌surgery for lung cancer, an illness that has prompted speculation about how it might affect his 17-month papacy.
The 71-year-old walked unaided to his waiting car, waving to well-wishers outside Rome's Gemelli Hospital. He stopped to speak to a 13-year-old girl named Varvara from Ukraine who has been in Italy for cancer treatment.
​He was pictured smiling broadly and waving through an open window when his black SUV left the hospital. He waved ​again to crowds as he was driven back into the Vatican but did not speak to anyone ⁠there before re-entering the world's smallest country.
Read : Pope Leo back on his feet after shock cancer diagnosis
His doctors had said earlier on Saturday that he was well enough to return home ​after they carried out the latest blood tests and chest imaging, and that he was able to perform normal daily activities independently.
Leo, who had ​an operation on Tuesday to remove the lower lobe of his right lung, will hold his first public engagement since surgery when he will lead weekly prayers with pilgrims in St. Peter's Square at noon (1000 GMT) on Sunday.
He has been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma , the most common form of lung cancer. The diagnosis for a pope known to ​be relatively young and energetic, and who was elected only in May 2025, caused shock and raised questions about the future shape of ​his papacy as he deals with the illness.
The pope's doctors have said his surgery was completed successfully, without complications. They have not yet disclosed the ‌size of ⁠the tumour or whether the disease had spread to nearby lymph nodes, key factors in determining prognosis.
The Vatican signaled on Friday that Leo, known for following a busy schedule, intended to keep up his commitments, as some cardinals began to publicly express concern about the pope's health.
In a sign the pope was back to work, Leo held a phone call on Friday with Russian President ​Vladimir Putin, urging a ceasefire to help ​get vital supplies into the ⁠Russian-controlled Ukrainian town of Oleshky.
The Vatican said work on Leo's November 6 to 17 visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, one of the most intense arranged for a pope in decades , was also "going forward". ​It released a list of journalists accredited to travel with Leo and cover the trip.
Also Read : Pope Leo admitted to Rome hospital for lung surgery
Cardinal Pietro Parolin, ​the Vatican's secretary ⁠of state, said on Friday that Leo may need to adjust the pace of his schedule going forward "according to the condition of his health". It is unusual for a cardinal to say openly that a pope might need to modify his routine.
On Friday, the Vatican released the first images ⁠of the ​pope since his surgery, showing him celebrating Mass and standing unaided.
Lebanese pilgrim Abdul ​Halim Fatha was in St. Peter's Square as Leo arrived back at the Vatican and expressed sadness over the pope's cancer diagnosis. "But I know God will be with ​him and protect him," he said.

title: PM Shehbaz says govt had    no other option    but to impose emergency or witness bloodshed in K P
description: The government could not continue to watch the situation deteriorate and risk being held responsible
content:
Says govt could not continue to watch the situation deteriorate and risk being held responsible
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday defended the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), saying the government had been left with no other option amid fears of bloodshed during Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) long march and a breakdown of law and order.
The remarks came amid continuing political tensions following the federal government's imposition of emergency and governor's rule in K-P on October 11 under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, which suspended the PTI-led provincial administration and transferred executive authority to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi.
The federal government defended the decision by citing security concerns and a lack of cooperation from the provincial government.
“We were left with no other option. We understood that we could not simply remain silent and watch bloodshed unfold,” the prime minister said while explaining the circumstances that led to the decision during a media talk in Gujranwala.
Invoking the familiar expression about Rome burning while Nero played his fiddle, PM Shehbaz said the government could not continue to watch the situation deteriorate and risk being held responsible by future generations.
“That would have amounted to criminal negligence,” he said, adding that the decision had been taken in the best interests of Pakistan. He prayed that it would produce positive results.
The prime minister made the remarks during a visit to Gujranwala, where he was accompanied by Federal Ministers Azam Nazeer Tarar and Attaullah Tarar to offer condolences on the death of Barrister Mahmood Virk, a party worker.
Describing the deceased as a loyal party worker and a decent person, the premier acknowledged his contributions.
During the speech, he appreciated Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s performance and hoped her efforts would bring prosperity.
Turning to the situation in K-P, the prime minister said he had held several meetings with the province’s former chief minister and also with Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, making what he described as sincere efforts to address the issues facing the province.
Read: K-P is rich in minerals; we will 'extract and sell them', says Kundi
He said K-P was an integral and beautiful part of Pakistan, whose people possessed courage and resilience, and that the federal government remained willing to extend all possible assistance for the province’s development and prosperity. However, he noted that the province was suffering from a spate of violence.
PM Shehbaz said the security situation, particularly the resurgence of terrorism and infiltration from Afghanistan since 2018, required collective efforts to defeat terror groups. The premier pledged to provide “all available resources and administrative facilities” to eliminate the menace.
He regretted that law-enforcement personnel and security forces, including Pakistan Army officers, continued to sacrifice their lives in the fight against terrorism. Innocent civilians, including women and children, had also been killed in attacks, he added.
The prime minister said the government had made repeated efforts to defuse political tensions in view of the poor security outlook but alleged that long marches and protests organised by the PTI had disrupted the country’s functioning one after the other.
Recalling the political turmoil of 2013-14, he said the unrest had brought economic activity to a standstill and affected imports, exports, agriculture and employment, inflicting what he described as enormous and irreparable losses on the country.
He said similar disruption had occurred last year and alleged that PTI had planned widespread violence during the October long march.
According to PM Shehbaz, the government had established a committee and held discussions with the relevant parties for around 48 hours in an effort to reach a negotiated settlement and stop the long march from happening.
“A comprehensive agreement had eventually been prepared, with the expectation that PTI would withdraw its call for a long march while Pakistan pursued economic recovery and development, but the talks fell out after consultations with the now-suspended K-P chief minister.”
He also referred to disagreements over consultations with the K-P chief minister, saying the situation had subsequently deteriorated and the government could not ignore the risk of further violence.
Read more: Fazl seeks joint in-camera session as ministers reject 'spoils of war' charge
Now that the march had stopped, the prime minister said Pakistan’s international standing improved and the domestic economy had begun to stabilise.
“Today, the economy has not only stabilised but is gradually moving towards recovery and growth.”
Defending the interim governance decision for two months, the prime minister said the government had concluded that inaction was no longer an option for the sake of the people of the province.
He said an advisory council had been established to help address the situation, describing it as a neutral body whose members were overwhelmingly non-political and included highly respected individuals.
“God willing, this council will help fix the situation in K-P,” he said, adding that he would remain involved and attend its meetings whenever required.
The prime minister expressed hope that the measures would improve the situation and help restore peace and stability in the province.
War in the Gulf and its impact on Pakistan
Referring to the impact of unrest in the Middle East and resulting inflationary pressures, he said the government had provided relief to the public through a fuel subsidy scheme.
He said the initiative had benefited around 12 million people, including motorcyclists, rickshaw users and owners of vehicles up to 800cc. The provincial government had allocated Rs75 billion for the scheme, which was intended to be utilised by the end of the year, he added.
PM Shehbaz noted that given the average household size of 5-6 people per family, the scheme’s indirect benefits could extend to nearly 65 million people.
Separately, PTI leader Asad Qaiser has said that talks are not on the cards after what the federal government has done.
“There is no room for consultations after what the federal government has done [imposed governor’s rule and emergency],” Qaiser outlined.
He said that from now on, all decisions would be undertaken by the joint opposition after careful deliberations and in uniformity. He also said all the opposition parties will put forth their stance and reach a conclusion in the All Parties Conference.
“PTI will not engage in talks on its own as the government is guilty of mishandling the situation,” he added.
The PTI stalwart lamented that CM Afridi and Speaker Babar Saleem Swati were arrested.
“Is this a democratic move?” he questioned.

title: Egypt s Sisi says his presidency will end in 2030  outlines plan to prepare future leaders
description: Says constitution won t be amended after 2019 changes allowed third term
content:
Says constitution won't be amended after 2019 changes allowed third term
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday that his term would end in 2030 and outlined a plan for the country's main military academy to train potential future leaders for 30 months before then.
The proposal gives ​the Egyptian Military Academy a central role in preparing future leaders, underscoring the armed forces' ​influence beyond national defence. Under Sisi, a former general, the military has expanded ⁠its presence in the economy and civilian affairs.
Speaking at a graduation ceremony at the academy, Sisi ​said a committee overseen by the speaker of parliament and including intellectuals, politicians and the ministers of higher ​education and justice, would develop criteria for selecting candidates and draft legislation for the training programme.
Read : Egypt's Sisi and Saudi crown prince stress need for security of Red Sea navigation
Reiterating that Egypt's constitution would not be amended, he said the end of his presidential term in 2030 was "a matter that has been completely ​settled and will not be discussed".
He said the programme would allow Egyptians to "elect and choose ​from among" its graduates, but gave no details on how they would be put forward for elected or appointed posts.
"I ‌will ⁠not leave the Egyptian state except when it is replete with sons and daughters capable of assuming responsibility," Sisi said.
The programme would target PhD holders from reputable Egyptian and foreign universities, who would spend 30 months at the academy learning about the state, its resources and how to preserve them, ​Sisi said. He said graduates ​would be prepared ⁠for leadership roles ranging from the presidency to ministries, governorates and parliament.
Also Read : Egypt rules out 'popular normalisation' with Israel without just peace, Palestinian state
Sisi , 71, is serving a six-year term after being reelected in December 2023. Constitutional amendments ​approved in a 2019 referendum extended presidential terms from four to six ​years and allowed ⁠him to seek a third term, clearing the way for him to remain in office until 2030.
The latest in a line of Egyptian rulers drawn from the military, he became president in 2014, a year ⁠after toppling ​Mohamed Morsi of the Muslim Brotherhood — Egypt's first democratically elected ​leader — following mass protests.
He proceeded to crush the Brotherhood, the Middle East's oldest Islamist organisation, and maintain a grip on power.

title: Cirotte lifts tennis singles title
description: France   s player downs Thailand   s Yodpetch in the final
content:
France’s player downs Thailand’s Yodpetch in the final
France’s Astrid Cirotte fought back from a set down to defeat Thailand’s Kamonwan Yodpetch and win the women’s singles title at the W-15 Islamabad Junaid Family Foundation World Tennis Women’s Championships 2026.
Cirotte prevailed 3-6, 6-4, 6-2 in the final of the tournament’s second leg at the Pakistan Tennis Federation (PTF) Tennis Complex, recovering from a difficult start to secure the title.
Yodpetch, however, returned to the winners’ podium in the doubles competition, partnering China’s Ru Xi Wu to claim the crown.
The pair defeated Germany’s Anastasiya Kuparev and Uzbekistan’s Sevil Yuldasheva 6-3, 4-6, 10-2 in the final, winning the deciding match tie-break convincingly after the teams split the opening two sets.
The international tournament featured 31 players from 17 countries, including France, China, Russia, Denmark, Mexico, Uzbekistan, South Africa, the Netherlands, South Korea, Nepal, Japan, Hong Kong, Germany, Thailand, Türkiye, the Czech Republic and hosts Pakistan.
United States Chargé d’Affaires Natalie A. Baker attended the closing ceremony as chief guest, while Ansir Junaid, chairman of the Junaid Family Foundation, and his wife were guests of honour. They joined officials in distributing prizes to the champions and runners-up.
PTF president Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi and secretary general Colonel Zia-ud-Din Tufail were also present at the ceremony.
French tennis player Aravane Rezaï received a shield in recognition of her services and contributions to the sport.
The closing ceremony was attended by ambassadors, diplomats, tennis officials, players, coaches, parents and spectators, reflecting growing interest in women’s tennis and international sporting events in Pakistan.
Qureshi congratulated the champions and runners-up on their performances and thanked Baker, the Junaid family and other guests for attending. He also acknowledged the foundation’s support in staging the tournament.
The championship forms part of the PTF’s efforts to promote women’s tennis, provide Pakistani players with opportunities to compete alongside international opponents and strengthen the country’s capacity to host international tennis events.
The Junaid Family Foundation sponsored the tournament, supporting efforts to develop the sport and expand opportunities for women players in Pakistan.

title: Pakistan seek solid start against Sri Lanka
description: Shaheen says World Cup preparation remains a priority during ODI tri series
content:
Shaheen says World Cup preparation remains a priority during ODI tri-series
Pakistan will look to make a strong start when they face Sri Lanka in the opening match of the ODI tri-series at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Sunday, with the match scheduled to begin at 1pm.
England are the third team in the series and they also held their first training session at the venue on Saturday ahead of the tournament.
Pakistan’s captain Shaheen Shah Afridi said his team were focused on building a solid squad for the 2027 World Cup.
“Our focus is on the World Cup. We have been trying to build the team since the previous series, keeping the conditions in South Africa in mind,” Shaheen told reporters on Saturday.
He declined to comment on Test cricket but praised Pakistan’s recent performances in the T20I series against Sri Lanka, saying the team were united and determined to improve.
“We want to play cricket aggressively,” he said, adding that Pakistan would make every effort to win the World Cup.
Shaheen backed experienced batsman Babar Azam, describing him as the backbone of the team and insisting that he was under no pressure.
He added that Babar, who captained Pakistan for five years, remained an important figure for younger players to learn from.
“Babar is the backbone of the team,” Shaheen said, noting that the batsman had also been working on his form in first-class cricket.
Pakistan captain also praised Salman Ali Agha’s form, highlighting his recent triple century in first-class cricket. Shaheen said he wanted to contribute with the bat, ball and in the field.
He expressed confidence in Pakistan’s batting resources, saying their experienced middle order could chase a target of 400 runs. He added that younger players would be given opportunities gradually, while highlighting Saim Ayub’s bowling as a valuable asset in the ODI format.
Pakistan have won several recent series but have been unable to complete a clean sweep, Shaheen said, adding that the team continued to work towards greater consistency.
Meanwhile Sri Lanka’s captain Kusal Mendis was also positive ahead of the challenging series.
"We have plans in place towards the World Cup and I hope my charges will show some good progress," Mendis said.
Sri Lanka struggled against Pakistan in the first two T20I matches in Pindi before whipping the Green-shirts by eight wickets in the third.
And they will be looking to transfer that late spark into the tri-series.
England’s captain Harry Brook, meanwhile, expects a demanding contest against two strong opponents but said his charges were keen to develop into a team capable of winning in all conditions.
“The tri-series will be a contest between very good teams,” Brook said, adding that playing cricket in Pakistan could be challenging.
Brook is familiar with local conditions after representing Lahore Qalandars in the Pakistan Super League at the age of 22. He said the experience had helped his international career and made him more confident when playing in the country.
“I know the conditions in Pakistan and the players here,” Brook said. “Playing in the PSL helped me a lot in international cricket.”
Brook said England wanted to become a side capable of chasing any target, acknowledging that their ODI squad lacked experience with only a handful of players having played 50 matches in the format.
The 27-year-old also called for batting-friendly pitches, saying he enjoyed surfaces that allowed high scores and believed spectators wanted to see boundaries and sixes.
He added that playing as much cricket as possible before the World Cup would benefit England’s preparations.
The tri-series begins in Rawalpindi on Sunday before moving to Lahore, with the final scheduled for October 31 at the Gaddafi Stadium.

title: Zverev stunned by Davidovich Fokina
description: Spaniard will either face Medvedev or Jodar in Shanghai final
content:
Spaniard will either face Medvedev or Jodar in Shanghai final
Top seed Alexander Zverev fell to a relentless Alejandro Davidovich Fokina in the Shanghai Masters semi-finals on Saturday over three tense sets.
The 26th-ranked Davidovich Fokina fought back to win 5-7, 6-4, 6-3 and will play either Daniil Medvedev or fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar in the final on Sunday.
The 27-year-old Spaniard combined grit, lightning-fast returns and graceful drop shots to stun the German, who will end the year world number one.
"I was a little bit nervous," Davidovich Fokina said of his shaky start.
"But I keep going, I keep fighting, every ball," he said.
The Spaniard extended his winning streak in China to nine matches, after claiming an ATP 250 title in Chengdu.
Zverev, the French and US Open champion, said fatigue had caught up with him.
"I think a break is quite necessary now," the 29-year-old told reporters, saying he would monitor his fitness ahead of a tournament in Vienna that begins October 24.
"I carried a little bit of injury, I carried fatigue into the tournament, and I'm okay to lose to a player like this today," said Zverev, who had felt his ankle at times in Shanghai.
The duo fought over long rallies in the first set, earning Davidovich Fokina a high-five from the world number two after one particularly impressive lob.
Despite a series of misjudged shots Zverev managed to avoid facing any break points in the first set.
He sprinted to send a brilliant backhand down the line, converting a crucial break point to go up 6-5.
He took the first set with an ace and looked to be heading back to the final he last reached in 2019.
Trouble arrived in the second set though as Zverev looked to be moving with some difficulty.
Davidovich Fokina worked his first break point in the fourth game but Zverev held when the Spaniard returned into the net.
Davidovich Fokina's growing pressure paid off and he successfully ran for a backhand to take the match into a deciding set.
The emboldened Spaniard raced into a 3-0 lead.

title: Sean    Diddy    Combs moved to new federal facility after losing 41 days of good conduct time
description: His spokesperson says the rapper is focused on moving forward after the Federal Bureau of Prisons confirmed the transfer
content:
His spokesperson says rapper is focused on moving forward after the Federal Bureau of Prisons confirmed the transfer
Sean “Diddy” Combs has been transferred from FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey to FCI Allenwood Low in Pennsylvania, the Federal Bureau of Prisons confirmed on October 16, 2026.
The 56 year old music mogul is serving a 50 month federal sentence following his 2025 conviction on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution. He was acquitted of racketeering conspiracy and sex trafficking charges. Combs and his legal team are awaiting a decision on his appeal.
The transfer follows reports about alleged contraband and special treatment during his time at Fort Dix. According to reporting cited by The Hollywood Reporter , Combs allegedly used a jailbroken tablet with Instagram installed and arranged for fellow inmates to receive money in exchange for helping with chores and other personal tasks.
Fort Dix officials reportedly sanctioned Combs for “disruptive conduct” and removed 41 days of good conduct time he had accumulated during his first year at the facility. He had also been moved into a special housing unit before suffering a head injury that led to a brief hospital visit.
The prison bureau confirmed the transfer but declined to discuss the circumstances, citing privacy, safety and security concerns. FCI Allenwood Low is a low security federal facility in Pennsylvania, near Williamsport.
Combs’ spokesperson, Juda Engelmayer, told the Associated Press that decisions about inmate placement are made by the Bureau of Prisons and said he could not comment on the reasons for the move. He added that Combs remained focused on moving forward and expressed hope that his time at the new facility would be productive.
The transfer comes during a difficult period for the once influential hip hop executive, whose criminal trial attracted extensive public attention. His sentence was imposed in October 2025 after the jury delivered its split verdict. The latest move does not change the conviction or sentence, and the outcome of his appeal remains unresolved.
The Bureau of Prisons has not publicly confirmed whether the reported contraband allegations directly prompted the transfer.

title: RJ Mitte   s mother speaks out after actor   s death at 34
description: Dyna Mitte says she wants her son remembered for his acting  philanthropy and disability advocacy
content:
Dyna Mitte says she wants her son remembered for his acting, philanthropy and disability advocacy
RJ Mitte’s mother, Dyna Mitte, has spoken publicly about the devastating loss of her son, sharing details of the morning she discovered him dead at his home in Brownsville, Texas.
The actor, best known for playing Walter White Jr in Breaking Bad , died on October 12 at the age of 34. His representative confirmed that he died by suicide, although the Brownsville Police Department had previously stated that the manner of death remained under investigation.
Speaking to NBC News in an interview published on October 15, Dyna recalled calling her son at around 11am. She said he often slept until noon, so his failure to answer initially did not immediately alarm her. She later picked up lunch and went to his home, where she found him.
Dyna said she believed her son’s death was a spur of the moment decision and that he had not left a note. She also recalled that a close friend had told her Mitte had been deeply hurt by certain issues.
The actor’s mother said she had encouraged him to seek therapy during the previous three months, but he had reassured her that he was managing. Looking back, she expressed regret that she had not pushed harder for him to receive support.
Dyna explained that she had decided to speak publicly in the hope that sharing her experience might help another family facing a similar situation.
Mitte played Walter White Jr across all five seasons of Breaking Bad , which aired from 2008 to 2013. He was born with cerebral palsy and used his public profile to advocate for disability awareness and inclusion.
His family said he served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s, and led The Mitte Foundation as president.
Following his death, co stars including Bryan Cranston and Bob Odenkirk paid tribute to the actor, remembering his warmth and commitment to helping others. His family has asked for privacy while loved ones grieve.

content:
Paramount and Legendary co financed the video game adaptation for $82m, with Kitao Sakurai directing
Street Fighter has earned $4 million from Thursday previews, setting up a competitive opening weekend for Paramount and Legendary’s new adaptation of the popular fighting video game franchise.
According to Variety , the film is projected to collect between $25 million and $35 million during its opening weekend. The preview figure places the action film among the leading new releases competing for cinema audiences.
Directed by Kitao Sakurai, Street Fighter features Noah Centineo, Andrew Koji, Callina Liang, Jason Momoa and 50 Cent among its cast. The performers portray fighters who enter a high stakes tournament, drawing on the colourful characters and combat focused world of the long running video game series.
Legendary and video game developer Capcom co financed the production, which reportedly cost $82 million. The release also marks the first film distributed under Paramount’s global distribution agreement with Legendary.
The opening weekend will provide an early indication of how successfully the adaptation attracts both established fans of the games and moviegoers unfamiliar with the franchise. Its commercial performance will also help establish the film’s position among this weekend’s new releases.
Other films entering the box office race include Whalefall , which collected $900,000 in Thursday previews. The thriller, directed by Brian Duffield and starring Austin Abrams, follows a scuba diver who becomes trapped inside a giant sperm whale. Its opening weekend projection stands at $10 million to $12 million.
The documentary You Can See Everything , from A24, earned $1.75 million in previews and is projected to open with $7 million to $8 million. Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, the film centres on former Theranos chief executive Elizabeth Holmes and reportedly includes footage captured through unusually extensive access to her life.
Jane Austen adaptation Sense and Sensibility , starring Daisy Edgar Jones and Esmé Creed Miles, also enters cinemas this weekend.
For Street Fighter , the final opening weekend total will determine whether its preview performance translates into a strong theatrical debut.

title: Pakistan face SAFF preparation crisis
description: Late camp raises concerns over team   s readiness
content:
Late camp raises concerns over team’s readiness
Pakistan’s preparations for the SAFF Championship have come under scrutiny, with the national team set to begin its training camp on October 26, just nine days before the tournament kicks off in Dhaka, raising concerns over the players’ fitness and readiness.
Pakistan’s head coach Nolberto Solano confirmed to this correspondent that the training camp would begin on October 26, just nine days before the team’s opening match against India on November 5.
The delayed start means the players will have barely a few days to prepare before travelling to Bangladesh, raising questions about the team’s readiness for the competition.
Pakistan previously faced criticism over its preparations for the ASEAN Cup, when Solano was unable to obtain a visa in time and had to travel directly to Indonesia to join the squad. The team had been prepared in Islamabad under inexperienced coaches.
Unlike India and Bangladesh, where domestic leagues provide players with regular competition and help maintain their fitness, Pakistan currently has no active domestic league. The lack of regular competitive football makes an extended training camp particularly important for the national team.
“It is absolutely unacceptable,” former Pakistan international and senior coach Gohar Zaman told The Express Tribune.
“There are no Ronaldos or Messis here who are always in shape. Our players are usually out of action and need time to regain their fitness. They needed at least a 30-day camp for that purpose,” Gohar said.
“I do not think football development is a priority. If we want to develop the sport, we must take it seriously and manage it professionally,” he added.
Gohar also recommended that Pakistan’s senior goalkeeping coach Aslam Khan be included in the national team’s coaching staff for the tournament.
“Aslam is in Dhaka, working as goalkeeping coach for Abahani Limited. It would be a plus if he were brought in for the SAFF Championship,” said Gohar, a former striker who has also served as an assistant coach of Pakistan’s senior team under several foreign coaches.
PFF Chief Operating Officer Shahid Niaz Khokhar also confirmed the dates, saying camp will begin on October 26 while the team will depart for Dhaka on November 2.
There are reports that some key Pakistan players based abroad may miss the tournament because of commitments to their clubs.
The training camp is expected to be held in Islamabad. This correspondent understands that Karachi could be a more suitable venue as the weather in the city is currently similar to that in Dhaka.
“It is a matter of professional thinking, but these people do not think that way. They will barely hold a camp for a few days,” he said.
Pakistan have been drawn in Group B alongside arch-rivals India and the Maldives. Hosts Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Bhutan make up Group A.
Pakistan will open their campaign against India on November 5 before facing the Maldives on November 7. The top two teams from each group will qualify for the semi-finals, scheduled for November 14. The final will also be held at the National Stadium in Dhaka on November 17.
Pakistan have a modest record in the SAFF Championship, with their best finish being third place in the 1997 edition in Nepal.
India lead the tournament’s honours list with nine titles, followed by the Maldives with two. Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Afghanistan have won one title each.
India are reportedly planning to field their under-23 team in the tournament to give younger players international exposure.
Pakistan’s biggest footballing problem is the absence of a domestic league. Over the past 12 years, the league has been held only once, during the 2018-19 season, when it was organised by two rival federations.
After FIFA installed the Normalisation Committee in 2019, it failed to make the revival of the league or domestic football. As a result, Pakistan’s national teams have largely relied on overseas players.
The current Pakistan Football Federation (PFF) administration has also spent more than a year in office without making meaningful progress towards restoring the league, deepening the crisis for local players and leaving them without regular competitive football.

title: K P is rich in minerals  we will  extract and sell them   says Kundi
description: Says the government has formed despite his opposition and continues to run successfully
content:
Says the government has formed despite Fazl's opposition and continues to run successfully
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Saturday said the province’s mineral resources would be extracted and sold to promote economic prosperity, urging domestic and foreign companies to invest in the sector through joint ventures to generate employment and support local businesses.
“Our province is rich in minerals, and we will extract and sell these minerals. We will have many agreements signed so that people can prosper,” said Kundi while addressing the media during a convocation ceremony held in Peshawar.
The governor defended the proposed exploitation of the province’s mineral resources, arguing that investment in the sector could generate employment, support local businesses and improve economic conditions.
“If an international company comes and enters into a joint venture with Pakistani companies and the people of K-P, providing them with employment and economic support, why are you speaking against this?” he probed.
Kundi invited foreign and domestic companies to invest in the province.
“K-P is rich in mineral resources, and we look forward to pursuing joint ventures to develop them,” the governor highlighted. He further added that oil and gas reserves should also be extracted to support economic growth.
He argued that economic prosperity and access to education would make communities less vulnerable to extremist narratives. He also criticised clerics who, he alleged, encouraged poor families to send their children to fight while remaining comfortable themselves.
Kundi assailed Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman over his stance against the governor’s rule in the province, saying the government had been formed without his support and would continue to function successfully.
Kundi questions Fazl’s stance on K-P governor’s rule
Taking a jibe at the JUI-F chief, Governor Kundi said, “Maulana himself used to say — I have heard him say — that no government could be formed without him, and that if one were formed, it would not be able to function. By the grace of Allah Almighty, it has been formed without you; it will function and succeed.”
Expressing disappointment over the JUI-F chief’s recent speech, Kundi said Fazl had himself raised concerns about the deteriorating law and order situation in K-P and the provincial government’s failure to address it.
“He says that imposing governor’s rule in K-P is wrong, then why did he complain that he could no longer move around the province and that the provincial government had failed to maintain law and order?” he questioned Fazl.
Read: Fazl draws ire over K-P governor's rule remarks
In a pointed criticism of JUI-F’s chief, the governor questioned what he described as inconsistencies in Fazl’s political positions.
“If imposing governor’s rule is haram [forbidden], then was supporting the Legal Framework Order (LFO) of 1970 halal? Was taking land from the army halal?” he threw a number of questions at Fazl. Referring to Dera Ismail Khan, he alleged that land belonging to martyrs had been allocated to Fazl as well.
“Whatever comes to you is halal, while whatever goes to others is haram?”
The governor then asked the JUI-F chief to compare the situation in K-P with that in Balochistan, where, he said, the provincial government and its chief minister were working alongside state institutions in the fight against terrorism.
He said Balochistan was facing the threat posed by the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA), while K-P was confronting the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and other terror outfits.
Criticising the previous Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) led provincial government, Kundi alleged that it lacked effective authority and that its decisions were being made in Kabul, Jalalabad and Kandahar rather than Islamabad.
He even suggested that they were still receiving directions from fugitives based across the border.
Read more: Sanaullah links reversal of K-P governor's rule to PTI support for counterterrorism efforts
“How long will we continue fighting wars? How long will our people continue fighting terrorism? Our people need peace. They need prosperity. They need development,” he added.
Softening his approach towards the JUI-F chief, Kundi invited Fazl to work with the government to promote peace, development and prosperity in the province, saying political differences should not obstruct efforts to improve the lives of the people.
He said he supported democracy and acknowledged the JUI-F chief’s efforts in this regard, but criticised his political alliances, alleging that the party had joined hands with people responsible for damaging the province.
The governor concluded by saying that he would support those who worked to establish peace, advance development and ensure prosperity for the people of K-P.
Achakzai pledges resistance to appropriation of K-P's natural resources
Meanwhile, National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai has vowed to resist what he described as the forcible occupation of Pashtun lands and the appropriation of their natural resources, calling for a peaceful, consensual jirga to address the community’s grievances.
“We will not allow anyone to forcibly occupy our homeland and its resources, whether they are in Khyber, Mohmand, Bajaur, Balochistan, or Sindh. This homeland is ours; we are its owners,” Achakzai said while addressing the people of Bara in K-P.
He maintained that no authority or power should be allowed to take control of local resources through force, stressing that disputes over ownership and access must be resolved through negotiations with the communities concerned.

“No power can seize our resources — marble, water, stones and mountains — by force. If anyone wants our resources, they must negotiate with us properly,” he said.
Achakzai argued that land ownership in Pakhtunkhwa was rooted in longstanding tribal and family boundaries, which he said were widely recognised and understood by local communities.
“Every single stone of the land of Pakhtunkhwa is divided among tribes and families, and its ownership is recognised,” he said, adding that even elderly women knew the limits of their tribes’ ancestral lands.
The opposition leader said the people would unite to convene a peaceful and consensual jirga to discuss their concerns and seek a resolution to what he described as injustices against Pashtun communities.
“We will also tell the world that injustice is being done to us,” he warned.

He cautioned that if the grievances of the people were not heard by Pakistan’s courts, or if their voices continued to be suppressed, they would seek legal recourse at the international level.
In his public address, Achakzai also criticised Pakistan’s past policies relating to Afghanistan and militancy, arguing that Pashtun communities had borne the brunt of the resulting violence.
He alleged that militants had been recruited, trained and supported during the Soviet intervention in Afghanistan, and rejected attempts to hold Pashtuns collectively responsible for the consequences.
The opposition leader also invoked the historical experiences of foreign powers in the region, warning against the use of military force and urging the authorities to exercise restraint.

title: South Africa look to re establish Test credentials
description: Hosts suffer a crushing 214 run defeat in the opening Test
content:
Hosts suffer a crushing 214-run defeat in the opening Test
South Africa will seek ​to show their heady ascent to the top of the Test cricket pile was ‌no accident as they bid to level the series against Australia in the second Test, starting on Sunday in Gqeberha.
The hosts suffered a 214-run defeat to Australia in the first Test that ended in Durban on Tuesday, a setback that ​left their status as world Test champions looking increasingly fragile.
South Africa secured a dramatic five-wicket victory ​over Australia to win the World Test Championship last year at Lord’s in ⁠London, but their qualification for the final prompted debate.
They played fewer tests than the likes of ​England and India and faced what was widely regarded as an easier schedule in the qualifying period.
Their ​winning form leading up to the WTC final also masked some poor batting performances, which coach Shukri Conrad acknowledged finally caught up with them against Australia at Kingsmead, where they looked anything but world champions.
“We’ve been heavily reliant on (captain) Temba (Bavuma) ​and (opener) Aiden Markram and then the lower order runs,” he said after Australia exposed their batting fragility.
Several ​changes are expected for the second Test where Matthew Breetzke is set to be given a renewed chance to ‌open ⁠alongside Markram.
Ryan Rickelton is primed to take over as wicketkeeper from Kyle Verreynne but move down the order.
Tristan Stubbs, who batted at number five for the first test, has been omitted, which could open the door for Marques Ackerman to make his Test debut.
South Africa will welcome ​back paceman Kagiso Rabada for ​his first outing ⁠since the Indian Premier League in May, placing considerable expectation on his shoulders despite his lengthy absence. That means they will drop one spinner.
Australia’s selection is ​also keenly anticipated but with Cameron Green’s return from injury likely delayed, ​they might ⁠resist the temptation to make any changes after such an emphatic win.
One possibility, however, is that Scott Boland is brought into the attack as Australia monitor the workloads of Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc ⁠after ​all three bowled at least 29 overs in the first Test.
Persistent ​rain and damp conditions are forecast for Gqeberha, particularly on the opening two days, which raises the prospect of delays or ​a shortened match at St George’s Park.

title: Trump waives key Russia related sanctions  tariffs before they take effect under new law
description: Trump said the waiver was in the national interest of the United States in executive order released Friday
content:
Trump said the waiver was in the national interest of the United States in executive order released Friday
US President Donald ​Trump waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs days before they were to take effect under a law he ‌signed last month, including duties on the country's goods and penalties for buying its oil and gas.
In an executive order released by the White House on Friday, Trump said the waiver was in the national interest of the United States.
The law is meant to increase pressure on Russia for its invasion of Ukraine that ​began in 2022. Trump, however, has been warming toward Moscow while publicly criticising Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, including suggesting Kyiv ​needs a new leader.
Weeks before US midterm elections in which Trump's Republicans are battling to maintain their ⁠narrow grip on both chambers of Congress, the new measures could have risked further raising oil prices as Americans face increased costs largely attributed ​to the US-Israeli war on Iran, analysts have said.
The legislation, whose primary backer in Congress was the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a South Carolina Republican, ​would have imposed tariffs of up to 100% within 30 days on all goods brought into the US from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or gas, as well as any country that knowingly bought oil or gas 30 days after the law was enacted or was among the top five ​countries helping Russia evade sanctions.
The order said the waiver will remain in effect until Trump or his top officials determine that "further action ​is appropriate." Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 in mid-September.
Read: Russian diesel deal puts Trump at odds with allies
"I have submitted to Congress a certification that the issuance ‌of ⁠such a waiver at this time is in the national interests of the United States," Trump said in the order.
Countries such as China and India, which are among the biggest buyers of Russian oil, have raised concerns about the Russia sanctions bill.
Beijing has said it "consistently opposed long-arm jurisdiction that lacks a basis in international law" while India warned Washington that new tariffs could impact bilateral ties.
The law allows the president to ​waive sanctions simply by informing Congress ​that he has determined that ⁠they are not in the national interest.
US Representative Don Beyer, a Virginia Democrat, blasted Trump for the waiver, saying he was giving in to Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"Trump's latest surrender to Putin again betrays our ​Ukrainian partners and defies clear congressional intent of legislation designed to punish Russia for its illegal war ​of aggression," Beyer ⁠said in a statement.
Trump had also faced criticism from several US senators, including some Republicans, over a recent diesel deal with Russia in which Trump agreed to lift sanctions on Russian exports and Russia agreed to supply diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices. ⁠The lawmakers ​who criticised the deal said it would help fund Russia's war efforts.
Putin's investment envoy, ​Kirill Dmitriev, called Trump's waiver "a truly historic moment," posting on X that the legislation could have effectively brought all economic cooperation between Russia and the US to a halt.

title: Armed men abduct 20 trainee police personnel travelling from Kalat to Nushki  officials
description: Efforts to recover them underway  say officials to The Express Tribune on condition of anonymity
content:
Efforts to recover them underway, say officials to The Express Tribune on condition of anonymity
Twenty trainee police personnel on Saturday were abducted by unidentified armed men while travelling between Kalat and Mastung in Balochistan, provincial government and police officials told The Express Tribune on condition of anonymity.
"The personnel were former Levies members who joined the police following the merger of the police and Levies forces. They were receiving training at the Kalat Police Training Centre and were travelling from Kalat to Nushki in a private van for their weekly leave," the officials said.
According to officials, the personnel had taken the shorter Sarband route from Kalat to Nushki, which connects Kalat and Mastung with Nushki, when armed men intercepted and surrounded their vehicle, the source added.
They further added that the armed men abducted the personnel from within the limits of Kalat district and took them to the Gargina-Kardgap area of Mastung district before moving them to an undisclosed location.
"The armed men later released the van's driver and three other civilian passengers some distance away, taking the police personnel with them," they said.
The abducted personnel belonged to the districts of Kharan, Nushki, Chagai and Washuk in Rakhshan Division. They included eight personnel from Kharan, five from Nushki, four from Chagai and three from Washuk.
Efforts to recover the abducted personnel have been launched, according to the source.
Read: 3 govt employees kidnapped in Balochistan
On September 26 , one private security guard was killed, two people were wounded, and 12 workers were abducted when heavily armed assailants raided a construction company's base in the Palari area of Nana Sahib Ziarat in Duki district, Duki Superintendent of Police (SP) Mansoor Ahmed Buzdar said.
On July 30 , the bodies of six labourers abducted from the Kalatak area of Kech district were recovered from the Nasirabad area on the outskirts of Turbat, Balochistan, Home Department media adviser Babar Yousafzai said.
According to Turbat police, the labourers were abducted by unidentified armed men after their vehicle was intercepted near Kalatak in Turbat. The attackers shot dead Javed Khan, a resident of Swabi district in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, immediately after the abduction and took the remaining six labourers with them.
Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022, and over the same period, TTP attacks increased more than sevenfold to 838 from 118.
Although K-P has borne the brunt of terrorism, Balochistan has also remained a major target of Indian proxies, which often target civilians and military installations in the province.
In one such attack on the last day of 2025, terrorists targeted innocent civilians in Balochistan’s Gwadar and Kharan districts, where 18 people, including women, children, the elderly and labourers, embraced martyrdom.

The forces continued operations across the provinces against what the state describes as Indian-sponsored terrorists and their proxies. Still, despite these efforts, the groups have continued to target civilian and defence installations.
Last month, in another such attack, at least 30 people, including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. The attackers also abducted several civilians and police personnel after the assault.
In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation , which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

content:
Brazilian receives red card during Madrid's win over Villarreal last weekend
Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said Saturday if he were winger Vinicius Junior he would have left the club this summer.
The Brazilian was sent off during Madrid's win over Villarreal last weekend for hair pulling and was banned for four matches, meaning he will miss the Clasico clash against Barcelona on October 25.
Vinicius, 26, has also been targeted regularly by opposition fans and been racially abused on many occasions since joining Madrid in 2018.
"He's a spectacular kid who it's easy to have a good relationship with," Mourinho told reporters.
"He's a fantastic boy, tremendous credit to him for the fact that he keeps living and surviving and still having a smile...
"If it were me in his place, probably I wouldn't be here. In this last summer I would have forced an exit to a league, a country, to somewhere there are rival clubs and stadiums that respect him."
In the summer Vinicius signed a new contract with Real Madrid until 2032.
Question marks remain over whether Madrid can line up with attacking superstars Vinicius, Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham together, without losing balance.
"Because he loves Real Madrid, for loving the club and the city, for believing that things can always improve, he renewed and he keeps on smiling," continued Mourinho.
"No one or nobody can... well, influence him negatively yes, because he's human... but take away his joy of living and working and being with his team-mates, no, no one can do that."
Mourinho took Vinicius off during the 4-3 Champions League win at Roma on Wednesday, with the winger still struggling to return to the form that helped him win the competition twice under Carlo Ancelotti.
Mourinho said he was happy that Vinicius's ban was four matches, saying he thought some hidden figures at the Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee "would give him one or two more".
Madrid face Sevilla on Sunday aiming not to fall further behind league leaders Barcelona, who visit Real Betis later on Saturday.
Hansi Flick's Barcelona have won every single match this season and are six points ahead of fourth-placed Real Madrid.
Los Blancos and Mourinho have blamed referees for some of their results, including the 2-1 derby defeat by Atletico Madrid in September.
On Friday Real Madrid called for La Liga president Javier Tebas to resign after he compared the club's efforts to discredit referees to the techniques of Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels.
Tebas later attempted to clarify that he was drawing comparisons with "those propaganda techniques" and not with the ideology of the Nazis.
"I don't want to talk about this, there are limits and there are limits. You can only excuse it if it's a clinical case -- otherwise there's no excuse," said Mourinho.
"I don't want to go down that road. Madrid and its fans understands what it is up against.
"For the prestige that the league has abroad, for being the current world champions, it's better if we try to keep this here and not let it get out (to the world)."
