title: Fazl seeks joint in camera session as ministers reject  spoils of war  charge
description: Tallal Chaudhry alleges PTI TTP links  rebukes Fazlur Rehma over K P setup
content:
Talal defends governor’s rule in K-P, rebukes JUI-F chief over power-sharing demands
Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Saturday called for a joint in-camera session of parliament to discuss the security situation in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), as government ministers rejected criticism of the federal government’s administrative arrangements in the province and defended the move as part of efforts to combat terrorism.
Speaking to reporters in Lahore, Fazl urged the government to convene an in-camera session of parliament to brief lawmakers on the security situation and its counterterrorism strategy, questioning why the nation was not being taken into confidence.
He said the government should accept his offer to hold an in-camera session and explain its position.
“If the nation is to form a force against terrorism and sit in the trenches, then take the nation into confidence,” he said.
He said parliament was the only platform through which the government could take the nation into confidence, questioning where else the public could be engaged in the process.
“The only platform for taking the nation into confidence is parliament. Apart from that, where is the nation?” he asked.
Earlier, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry, addressing the media in Jaranwala, noted that the final round of negotiations between the government and opposition took place in Parliament, with representatives of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) also participating.
Read: No breakthrough after marathon PTI-govt talks
Discussing Fazl's criticism of the federal government's decision, Talal expressed disappointment over what he described as an attempt to seek a share in the province's administration following the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's (PTI's) removal from power.
“We did not expect Maulana to consider this as spoils of war and seek his share because PTI is no longer there,” Talal said. “This is not spoils of war,” he added.
The minister further rejected the suggestion that the federal government had imposed governor's rule in K-P to establish a political foothold in the province, form a coalition government or replace PTI with another political arrangement. “This was an administrative setup,” he said, adding that it had been formed with a “one-point agenda: combating terrorism.”
Talal maintained that the government had exhausted other options before making the decision to impose emergency and governor's rule, saying that authorities wanted to restore security so that children could attend school, businesses could operate, and people could travel without fear of militant attacks.
Talal also warned that the state would respond if any political party was found supporting armed groups fighting against Pakistan. He said the government's counterterrorism efforts would extend to wherever the attacks originated.
The minister further alleged that the PTI and the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) shared mutual interests, citing the militant group's statement opposing governor's rule in K-P. “We have been saying for a long time that there must be some relationship, some mutual interest or something common between the TTP and PTI,” he said.
He claimed that no PTI leader, party member or gathering had been subjected to a terrorist attack since 2015, while other political parties, security forces, government offices and public gatherings had repeatedly been targeted.
“Tell me, this is the press release issued by the TTP against governor's rule and in favour of PTI. They have never issued a press release for any other political party,” Talal said, referring to a statement by the banned outfit opposing the imposition of governor's rule in K-P.
He argued that the statement supported his allegations about a relationship between the two.
The minister added that the federal government had repeatedly urged political stakeholders to set aside their differences and work together against militancy, including by condemning the TTP, the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and other groups by name, and implementing the National Action Plan.
“We said that politics has its place, but let us sit together and fight terrorism,” he said, adding that the government wanted political parties to fulfil their responsibilities under the counterterrorism framework.
Referring to the history of negotiations with the TTP, Talal said the group had included PTI founder Imran Khan's name among its proposed interlocutors during efforts to initiate talks in 2013-2014.
He also recalled Imran's alleged proposal to reintegrate TTP fighters and their families into Pakistan following the Taliban takeover of Afghanistan. Talal alleged that the reintegration policy had contributed to the worsening security situation, claiming that attacks had subsequently affected security personnel, civilians, schools, religious seminaries, mosques, markets and public gatherings.
The minister said the federal government had spent the past two-and-a-half years attempting to secure cooperation from successive K-P chief ministers on counterterrorism, including the now non-functional CM Sohail Afridi.
According to Talal, federal ministers had attended meetings at locations suggested by the provincial leadership, including official residences and offices, in an effort to reach an agreement.
Read More: Failed talks forced K-P emergency, says PM
Separately, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry also criticised Fazl for linking the imposition of an emergency in K-P to an alleged attempt to seize the province’s mineral resources, saying serious national issues such as terrorism should not be politicised.
In a post on X , Chaudhry said the federal government’s priority was to protect the public and restore peace in the province, urging political leaders to play a serious role in eliminating terrorism rather than resorting to political allegations.
“Maulana is a senior politician and is himself aware of the damage caused by terrorism,” he said, adding that Fazlur Rehman was expected to support national efforts against terrorism.
Chaudhry also called on the PTI, which he said had governed K-P for 13 years, to account for its performance and the deteriorating law and order situation in the province.
He said officers and soldiers of the Pakistan Armed Forces were sacrificing their lives to maintain peace in the country, adding that political accusations should give way to national unity and a joint strategy against terrorism. “The people of K-P want peace, security and development, not political disputes,” Chaudhry said.
The remarks came amid continuing political tensions following the federal government's imposition of emergency and governor's rule in K-P on October 11 under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, which suspended the PTI-led provincial administration and transferred executive authority to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi.
The federal government defended the decision by citing security concerns and a lack of cooperation from the provincial government.

title: Harry Styles debuts unreleased song written for Liam Payne on second anniversary of his death
description: Styles and Payne rose to fame together after competing on The X Factor in 2010
content:
Styles and Payne rose to fame together after competing on The X Factor in 2010
Harry Styles paid an emotional tribute to his late One Direction bandmate Liam Payne by performing an unreleased song written for him during his Madison Square Garden concert on October 16, marking the second anniversary of Payne’s death.
The singer introduced the song, titled “What Is Enough?”, during his sold-out show in New York, telling the audience that he had written it for his friend around two years earlier. The performance marked the first time Styles had publicly performed the track, giving fans an unexpected tribute to the late singer.
“I feel incredibly lucky to get to play these shows here in New York, and this building means a lot to me,” Styles told the crowd, reflecting on the people who had helped shape his life and career.
“There are so many people in my life, friends and people that I’ve worked with that I wouldn’t have been able to do this without. And two years ago today, I lost one of those friends,” he continued, before asking the audience for permission to perform the song he had written for Payne.
Styles also offered a message about grief and supporting the people around you, telling concertgoers, “I’m sure a lot of you have been through similar things. I hope you haven’t. But really, it’s just about looking after each other.” The singer then performed the previously unheard track, accompanying himself on guitar.
During the performance, Styles sang the poignant lyric, “You dance until you’re tired,” in a moment that resonated with fans who had gathered to celebrate his music while remembering Payne. Footage of the tribute subsequently circulated on social media, with One Direction fans sharing their reactions to the emotional performance.
Payne died on October 16, 2024, aged 31, after falling from a hotel balcony in Buenos Aires, Argentina. His death shocked fans around the world and prompted tributes from his former One Direction bandmates, who had shared the stage with him during the group's rise to international fame.
Styles previously reflected on the loss during a March 2026 interview with Apple Music’s Zane Lowe, discussing the difficulty of grieving while feeling that the public had a stake in his personal loss.
“I think there was a period when he passed away where I really struggled with acknowledging how strange it is to have people kind of own part of your grief in a way,” Styles said. He also explained that he had come to believe that living life fully was one way to honour friends who had died.
Styles and Payne rose to fame together after competing on The X Factor in 2010, where they were grouped with Niall Horan, Louis Tomlinson and Zayn Malik to form One Direction. The band went on to become one of the most successful pop acts of its generation, releasing five studio albums before going on hiatus in 2016.
Although the members subsequently pursued solo careers, their shared history has remained an important part of their connection with fans. Payne’s death has also prompted renewed reflection on the group's legacy and the friendships formed during their years together.
The tribute took place during Styles’ 30-show residency at Madison Square Garden, part of his Together, Together global tour, which supports his fourth studio album, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally., released in March 2026. The New York residency is scheduled to conclude on October 31.
By choosing the anniversary of Payne’s death to perform a song he had written for his former bandmate, Styles offered fans a rare glimpse into his personal grief. The performance served as a reminder of the bond they shared and the lasting impact Payne continues to have on the people who knew him and the millions who grew up listening to One Direction.

title: Karachi court extends journalist Iqrarul Hassan s physical remand by two days
description: Judicial magistrate rejects lawyers    application  orders NCCIA to present report at next hearing
content:
Judicial magistrate rejects lawyers’ application, orders NCCIA to present report at next hearing
A Karachi court on Saturday extended journalist Iqrarul Hassan's physical remand by two days in a case of harming the state and national integrity by disseminating anti-state content.
The judicial magistrate (East) also rejected Hassan's lawyers' application and ordered the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) to present a report at the next hearing.
Last week, the NCCIA produced Hassan before the judicial magistrate, who handed the journalist over to the NCCIA on a four-day physical remand . On Thursday, the District and Sessions Court East dismissed a petition challenging Hassan's physical remand, with the defence counsel questioning the legality of the proceedings and arguing that the case concerned digital and cyber matters.
The case against Hassan, filed under Sections 9, 10, 20, 24, and 26-A of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) 2016, stated that the journalist, "through his personal social media accounts on the platforms X, Instagram and Facebook, is intentionally disseminating false, fabricated, anti-state and defamatory content with the object of instigating the general public against the state, its institutions and its functionaries."
Read: Journalist arrested on 'attempted rape' charges
The FIR stated that the content of Hassan's social media posts portrayed the state, its institutions and its functionaries "in a false and distorted manner."
It also noted that Hassan "represented lawful measures as controversial with the intent to instigate and incite the general public at large against the state and the lawfully constituted authorities."
The FIR stated further, "The accused instigated a substantial following, including the general public, on the aforesaid platforms," adding that the content that he posted was published and broadcast "in an open, publicly accessible manner, without restriction, so as to reach and influence the public at large throughout Pakistan and abroad."
Hassan's wife Farah Iqrar told The Express Tribune on October 12 that a group of unidentified individuals posing as officials of the NCCIA had allegedly taken him away from their residence in Lahore’s Defence C area.
According to Farah, between five and seven people, including women, arrived at the house late on Sunday night, during the intervening hours of Sunday and Monday, and demanded that Hassan come outside. She alleged that the individuals threatened to break down the door if he was not handed over. They subsequently entered the house, forcibly took the journalist from a room and took him away.
Later, Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari said that Punjab Police had not arrested Hassan , adding that investigations into the matter were underway and his family would be informed as soon as verified information about his whereabouts became available.
Hours before the reported incident, Hassan had posted a message on X criticising the Pakistan Peoples Party and referring to Nawaz Sharif and President Asif Ali Zardari.

title: Bangladesh resort fire kills at least 10  injures 9 others
description: Fire erupts at a resort in Cox   s Bazar  tourist hub in southeastern Bangladesh  fire service confirms
content:
Fire erupts at a resort in Cox’s Bazar, tourist hub in southeastern Bangladesh, fire service confirms
At least 10 people, believed to be tourists, were killed, and nine others were injured in a fire at a resort on the Cox’s Bazar coast, a tourist hub in southeastern Bangladesh, on Saturday morning, the country's fire service confirmed.
The fire broke out at a wooden resort and restaurant at Inani Sea Beach in Cox's Bazar, the fire service said in a statement, adding that the blaze was completely extinguished after two firefighting units responded alongside local authorities and police.
The Border Guard said in a statement that its personnel also joined the rescue operation.
Read: 'Gul Plaza management involved in fire tragedy'
At least nine people were injured when the fire broke out early in the morning while they were asleep, Jamuna TV reported. Their identities have not yet been confirmed.
All those affected are believed to be tourists, as the area is a popular tourist destination, the report said.
The fire may have originated from a stove in the resort's kitchen or an electrical short circuit, the report noted, while the cause has not yet been verified.
The district authorities have formed a committee to investigate the incident.

title: Attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure pose risks to Pakistan s economic outlook  FinMin Aurangzeb
description: Says Pakistan has procured enough energy supplies to last through November  and now planning for winter months
content:
Says Pakistan has procured enough energy supplies to last through November, and now planning for winter months
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on Saturday told AFP the country had so far withstood the shock from skyrocketing energy prices due to the Iran war, but that attacks on infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries were "worrying" for the country's longer-term economic outlook.
In an interview on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Aurangzeb said Pakistan had procured enough energy supplies to last through November, and was now planning for the winter months, when household needs typically spike.
"The first-order impact has been negotiated well by Pakistan," he said.
"We've had no shortage, no queues at the gas stations, and no law and order situation, which at times we have seen in some of the countries."
He added that unless the government saw "an absolute dire need", it would not be procuring spot cargoes on the LNG front, which tend to be far more expensive than previously contracted shipments.
Since the United States and ally Israel launched the war on Iran in February, global energy prices have surged as Tehran's retaliatory action has targeted Washington's Gulf allies and curtailed oil and gas supplies.
With Yemen's civil war flaring back to life as well, the Houthis there have repeatedly attacked Saudi infrastructure, including energy facilities and airports, in recent days.
Aurangzeb expressed alarm at the escalation, saying damage to such sites would delay a return to economic normalcy.
Read: FinMin seeks BB rating, $1.5b financing
"What is now (the) worrying part of it is when the energy infrastructure starts getting hit," he said.
"I, to be very honest, I don't know where that would go. But one thing is very clear: that if the infrastructure continues to get hit, the return to normalcy, even if things subside, will take longer."
"Fortunately for us, we have been on this fiscal consolidation path for a while," Aurangzeb said with a rueful smile.
The country's tax revenues have grown significantly in recent years, and the finance minister said the government was targeting the theft of taxes by private sector businesses that collected sales tax from consumers but never deposited it in government accounts.
Such theft accounted for billions of dollars, Aurangzeb said, adding that there remained "room for improvement" on increasing income tax collection as well.
He said the government's reform agenda had faced resistance from industry, lobbying groups and vested interests.
"Every reform, everything that you try to do when you try to change the status quo, there is pushback," he said.
The finance minister also met Jihad Azour, director of the IMF Middle East and Central Asia Department, to discuss Pakistan’s economic performance and reforms, the Ministry of Finance said on Saturday.
According to the post on X, both sides reviewed progress on revenue, inflation, growth and the current account, noting Pakistan’s resilience despite regional conflict.
He made the remarks during a meeting with the delegation of Ajman Bank in Bangkok, Thailand.
"They also outlined energy procurement and winter preparedness measures, alongside adequate fertiliser supplies to safeguard food security," the ministry added.
It further added that the discussions covered stronger reserves, reduced forward foreign exchange liabilities, longer debt maturities and lower external repayment requirements.
Aurangzeb reaffirmed the government’s commitment to sustaining primary surpluses, reducing public debt and advancing growth-friendly tax reforms while protecting social spending.
Both sides also discussed privatisation, greater private-sector participation and export-oriented growth to strengthen economic resilience and creditworthiness.
The ministry said the discussions underscored the importance of maintaining reform momentum, political commitment and effective communication, while highlighting the link between economic stability and national security.

title: Pakistan stars relish ODI cricket   s twists and turns
description: Top players highlight the format   s shifting demands and comeback opportunities
content:
Top players highlight the format’s shifting demands and comeback opportunities
Pakistan’s start batsman Babar Azam believes the ability to handle changing situations is what makes one-day international cricket special, with the 50-over format demanding composure, adaptability and the ability to pull a team out of trouble.
“You face different situations in a one-day game, and you have to handle them,” Babar said. “Sometimes these situations favour you, and sometimes they go against you. You have to tackle them, get your team out of trouble and do something special.”
Babar’s views reflect a broader appreciation among Pakistan’s leading cricketers of the unique demands of ODI cricket, which combines the patience required in Test matches with the attacking instincts of Twenty20 cricket.
All-rounder Shadab Khan said the middle overs were crucial for both batsmen and bowlers, offering opportunities to shape the course of a match.
“For a bowler, the middle overs are important because taking wickets at that stage can change the entire match,” Shadab said. “For a batsman, it is equally important to dominate during that period.”
Hasan Nawaz said the format offered players time to settle at the crease and build an innings, while the fielding restrictions provided opportunities to score boundaries.
“In ODI cricket, you get overs and time to settle in,” Hasan said. “The best thing is that you have four fielders outside the circle, which gives you more boundary options. That is why I like one-day cricket.”
Salman Ali Agha described the format as a blend of the two other forms of international cricket, requiring players to adjust their approach according to the conditions and match situation.
“ODI cricket is a mixture of Test and T20 cricket,” Agha said. “Sometimes you have to score at a rate of eight to 10 runs an over, while on a difficult pitch you may have to rely on your Test-match technique.”
Saim Ayub said the changing phases of a 50-over contest were among its biggest attractions, requiring both acceleration and temperament.
“The best thing about ODI cricket is that you experience every kind of phase,” Saim said. “You need to accelerate, but you also need temperament.”
He added that the format could change direction quickly, particularly when bowlers began to exploit conditions later in an innings.
“Sometimes you concede runs, but if even one ball changes the situation towards the end, the reverse-swing factor can come into play,” Saim said. “The best thing about ODI cricket is that the game keeps changing over 50 overs.”
Fakhar Zaman also praised the balance between patience and aggression, saying the format allowed batsmen to build an innings before switching to an attacking approach.
“What I like about ODI cricket is that it is a mixture of Test and T20 cricket,” Fakhar said. “You get time to settle in, and then you can go for the big shots.”
For Pakistan all-rounder Faheem Ashraf, the use of a new ball from each end adds to the bowlers’ appeal, particularly when conditions favour seam movement.
“The best thing for bowlers is that new balls are used from both ends,” Faheem said. “If the conditions are favourable, bowlers really enjoy it. They also enjoy it when the ball starts to reverse.”
Left-arm spinner Sufiyan Muqeem highlighted another feature of the format: the opportunity for bowlers to recover after an expensive spell.
“In one-day cricket, even if you bowl a couple of bad overs, you still have time to recover,” Muqeem said.
Fast bowler Naseem Shah said the format gave bowlers several opportunities to make an impact, with different spells presenting different challenges.
“ODI cricket is a mixture of everything, and you have opportunities to make a comeback,” Naseem said. “You bowl in the powerplay, the middle overs and at the death. All these phases are challenging, but you always have a chance to come back.”
The comments underline the tactical complexity of ODI cricket, where momentum can swing repeatedly and success depends on a team’s ability to balance aggression with patience across 50 overs.
For Pakistan’s players, that constant shift between attack, defence and opportunity remains central to the format’s enduring appeal.

title: Ambassador Sheikh urges Pakistani Americans to drive  mutually rewarding  economic engagement
description: Envoy emphasises Pakistan s opportunities for investment  trade  business partnerships across range of sectors
content:
Envoy emphasises Pakistan's opportunities for investment, trade, business partnerships across range of sectors
Pakistan's Ambassador to the United States Rizwan Saeed Sheikh on Friday emphasised that Pakistan offered significant opportunities for investment, trade and business partnerships across a range of sectors, urging Pakistani-Americans to translate the "opportunity offered by the current ascendant trajectory of Pak-US relations into mutually rewarding economic engagement."
According to a press release by the Embassy of Pakistan in Washington, DC, Ambassador Sheikh attended a community event in the Greater San Francisco Bay Area, urging the Pakistani-American community to "lead the way and profit from deepening economic engagement between Pakistan and the US."
Addressing members of the Pakistani-American community, the release noted that Sheikh "highlighted the community’s unique role as a bridge between Pakistan and the United States." He "underscored longstanding and consequential relations between Pakistan and the United States," citing "important contributions of the Pakistani-American community in strengthening these ties."

Sheikh "underscored the enduring connection of the community with its motherland Pakistan," the release noted, adding that the ambassador "urged Pakistani-Americans to use their professional and business networks to showcase Pakistan’s investment potential, promote futuristically enduring partnerships and expand bilateral trade and investments," highlighting the IT sector in particular.
The ambassador further reaffirmed the embassy's "readiness to facilitate greater interaction between Pakistani and American businesses," while encouraging the community "to work collectively to advance mutually beneficial economic ties between Pakistan and the United States."
The event was attended by representatives of major Pakistani-American organisations of the Greater San Francisco Bay Area, the release noted. It added that community representatives expressed their gratitude towards Sheikh for his participation, appreciating the embassy’s efforts to strengthen Pakistan-US relations.
The representatives also thanked the consulate general of Pakistan in Los Angeles for facilitating consular services for the Pakistani-American community in the area.

title: Australia confirms first H5N1 bird flu case on sub Antarctic Macquarie Island
description: Australia confirms first H5N1 bird flu case on sub Antarctic Macquarie Island
content:
Deadly virus found in the remote ‌territory's vulnerable elephant seal population
Australia on Saturday confirmed its first case of H5N1 bird flu on the sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island, ​with the deadly virus found in the remote ‌territory's vulnerable elephant seal population.
Australia's Chief Veterinary Officer Beth Cookson said official testing confirmed the highly pathogenic virus strain "in samples collected ​from an elephant seal and a kelp gull ​on Macquarie Island, marking the first H5 event ⁠on this island".
Australia in June became the last ​continent to report bird flu, although the virus was detected ​in late 2025 on another of its sub-Antarctic territories, Heard Island, where more than 13,000 baby seals were killed by the virus, ​according to local media.
Read More: Japan culls 50,000 chickens after bird flu outbreak
Like Heard Island, Macquarie Island, ​a UNESCO World Heritage-listed territory located in the Southern Ocean halfway between ‌Australia's ⁠Tasmania state and Antarctica, is a key breeding ground for southern elephant seals.
The mammals, which can weigh up to 3,600 kg (7,936 pounds), are particularly susceptible to H5 ​bird flu, with ​pup mortality ⁠rates in some cases of more than 90%, according to the federal government.
In August, ​Australia's environment department said it would withdraw personnel from ​a ⁠research station on Macquarie Island due to the "psycho-social risk to expeditioners of a potential H5 avian influenza outbreak".
Expert assessments ⁠predicted the ​virus would likely cause a ​significant elephant seal mortality event during the upcoming breeding season, the environment department ​said.

title: Real Madrid demand resignation of LaLiga chief
description: Tebas takes a dig at Los Blancos management by comparing them with Nazi Party
content:
Tebas takes a dig at Los Blancos management by comparing them with Nazi Party
Real Madrid demanded the resignation of LaLiga President Javier Tebas after he compared rhetoric from the club's management to the propaganda methods used by the Nazi Party ​in Germany.
Tebas wrote earlier on Friday on social media that "Real Madrid’s management directs ‌an orchestra of mouthpieces and Real Madrid TV leads the singing."
The LaLiga president was responding to articles by two journalists saying he and LaLiga were acting against Real's interests.
Tebas added that the authors in the ​El Debate newspaper were amplifying a message on behalf of Real's management.
Reuters has asked ​El Debate for comment.
Real Madrid's demand for Tebas to immediately resign deepens a ⁠feud between the club and La Liga's chief.
Real in September called for a new LaLiga ​president in response to Tebas calling their complaints about refereeing decisions 'a smokescreen' for their shortcomings on ​the pitch.
Tebas on Friday criticised Real Madrid TV's coverage of officiating at their matches.
"Their score is always the same: select the plays that suit them, repeat the grievance, feed the suspicion, and point fingers at the ​enemies," he wrote.
"That method recalls propaganda mechanisms used by Goebbels, Nazi Germany's Minister of Propaganda.
"The ​comparison is with those propaganda techniques, not with an ideology or, of course, with the Madridista fanbase," added ‌LaLiga's ⁠president.
Real Madrid released a statement later on Friday demanding that Tebas resign from his positions as LaLiga chief and vice-president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation.
The statement called it "intolerable and extraordinarily serious" that Tebas used "a comparison with the propaganda methods of the Nazi regime ​to discredit our club, ​its management and its ⁠television.
"Tebas' repeated conduct demonstrates a lack of neutrality, respect and impartiality incompatible with his institutional responsibilities," said Real.
"It is unacceptable that he even ​takes advantage of questions, information or opinions from journalists unrelated to the ​club to ⁠direct his accusations at us, attributing to us actions of third parties for which we bear no responsibility."
The 64-year-old Tebas, who is elected by the 42 professional clubs in Spain's top two tiers, ⁠has ​been LaLiga president since 2013. In 2023, he was ​reelected unopposed until 2027.
Real Madrid's statement came hours after LaLiga confirmed that they are one of the six clubs that ​will sit on the league's Executive Committee this season.

title: Selma Blair makes first public appearance since arrest after alleged flight incident
description: The actress was originally expected to attend a question and answer panel during the three day convention
content:
The actress was originally expected to attend a question and answer panel during the three day convention
Selma Blair made her first public appearance since her recent arrest when she attended 90s Con 2026 in Hartford, Connecticut, on Friday, October 16.
The 54 year old actress appeared at a signing booth during the three day convention, which runs from October 16 to 18 at the Hartford Convention Center. She was photographed meeting fans and posing for pictures, including one shared online by influencer Brad Deiter.
Another attendee posted a photograph with Blair, showing the actress smiling while seated in a chair. Her appearance followed an incident aboard a flight from Los Angeles to New York on October 11, which resulted in her arrest after the plane landed at John F. Kennedy International Airport.
Organisers had confirmed before the incident that Blair would attend the convention as planned. That’s4Entertainment announced her participation on October 13, maintaining the arrangement despite the arrest.
Blair had initially been listed for a question and answer panel, but her name was absent from the full schedule shared on October 11. The organisers subsequently told a commenter that she had chosen to spend additional time meeting fans at her table.
According to reports cited by PEOPLE , Blair was accused of assaulting flight crew members, a nurse and a Port Authority police officer during the incident. She appeared in court on October 12 and was arraigned on two counts of assault involving the officer and nurse, according to a criminal court affidavit.
A judge set bail at $20,000 cash, $60,000 bond or a $60,000 partially secured bond. Blair was released later that evening.
A representative for Blair said she had experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct. The representative added that she received medical attention after landing and was in stable condition.
Delta confirmed that the flight departed Los Angeles earlier that day and said the incident had no operational impact. The airline also emphasised its commitment to the safety of passengers and crew.
Blair’s appearance at the convention proceeded as previously arranged, while the allegations surrounding the flight incident remained a separate legal matter.

title: Pakistan to host Canada for hockey series in 2027
description: Federation confirms Green shirts    participation in Azlan Shah Cup
content:
Federation confirms Green-shirts’ participation in Azlan Shah Cup
Pakistan will host Canada for a bilateral hockey series in Islamabad from February 8 to 21, 2027, the Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) said, in a move aimed at reviving international hockey in the country.
The PHF said it would work with the Ministry of Inter-Provincial Coordination and relevant federal authorities to arrange accommodation, transport, sports facilities and security for the visiting Canadian delegation.
PHF president Mohyuddin Ahmad Wani, and federal secretary of the Ministry of Inter-Provincial Coordination, welcomed the proposed tour, describing it as an opportunity to promote international hockey in Pakistan and strengthen sporting ties between the two countries.
The series will allow players and officials from both sides to gain international experience, exchange knowledge and contribute to the development of the sport, the federation said.
The PHF said the planned visit formed part of broader efforts to restore Pakistan’s presence on the international hockey calendar, attract foreign teams to the country and encourage greater participation among young players.
Pakistan, a former powerhouse in international hockey, has been seeking to rebuild the sport through increased international competition and improved development opportunities.
The federation said it was committed to welcoming the Canadian team to Islamabad and ensuring the series was organised to professional standards.
Meanwhile PHF also accepted an invitation to compete in the Sultan Azlan Shah Cup in Malaysia in November 2026.
The PHF said in a statement on Saturday that participation in the tournament would give the senior national team valuable match experience against international opponents and help players improve their technical skills and competitive standards.
Pakistan’s Under-21 team is already in Malaysia to compete in the Sultan of Johor Cup, providing emerging players with an opportunity to test themselves against international opposition.
The federation said it was pursuing a comprehensive development strategy covering Under-18, Under-21, senior men’s and women’s teams, with a focus on expanding international exposure, improving coaching and strengthening training facilities.
The PHF also plans to improve financial incentives and support systems for players, aiming to encourage performance, promote merit and create a pathway for young talent to progress to the senior national team.
Regular participation in international competitions, professional coaching and structured player development are essential to restoring Pakistan’s position among the world’s leading hockey nations, the federation said.
Pakistan, once a dominant force in international hockey, have been working to rebuild their competitiveness through improved preparation and greater exposure to international competition.
The PHF said it remained committed to strengthening national teams at all levels and creating opportunities for Pakistani players to compete on the international stage.

title: 5 9 magnitude earthquake jolts Balochistan s Khuzdar  adjoining areas
description: Tremors also felt in Kalat  Surab as district administration reports no loss of life  property
content:
Tremors also felt in Kalat, Surab as district administration reports no loss of life, property
Tremors from an earthquake measuring 5.9 on the Richter scale were felt on Saturday morning in Balochistan's Khuzdar district and the surrounding areas of Kalat and Surab.
According to the Pakistan Meteorological Department , the earthquake's depth was recorded at 25 kilometres, and its epicentre was 48 kilometres northwest of Khuzdar.
The tremors were so strong that people came out of their homes, gathering in open spaces.
According to the district administration, no loss of life or property occurred. However, officials stated that all relevant institutions were put on alert and the situation was being monitored. The administration also appealed to the public to trust only information received from official sources.
In August, an earthquake of magnitude 4.0 jolted Balochistan's Dalbandin. The earthquake was recorded at a depth of 35 kilometres, with its epicentre located 100 kilometres southwest of Dalbandin.
In the same month, a 5.4-magnitude earthquake originating in Afghanistan’s Hindu Kush region jolted parts of Pakistan, with tremors felt in Islamabad, Peshawar and other areas of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P). The earthquake was recorded at a depth of 187 kilometres and its epicentre was located in the Hindu Kush region of Afghanistan.
Read: 7.7-magnitude earthquake rattles Panama, damages buildings and halts flights
In July, an earthquake measuring 5.3 magnitude on the Richter scale jolted Islamabad and parts of Punjab and K-P. Tremors were felt in several cities across K-P, including Peshawar, Mardan, and Buner. The quake was also felt in the twin cities of Islamabad and Rawalpindi, as well as adjoining areas.
Earlier in June, three people were injured after earthquake tremors were felt in Balochistan’s Barkhan district and adjoining areas, causing fear and panic among residents.
In May, a series of mild to moderate earthquakes jolted parts of the country, with tremors felt in Islamabad, Khuzdar district and Azad Jammu and Kashmir. No casualties or damage were reported.
Most of the seismic activity affecting Pakistan originates in the Hindu Kush region, lying near the boundary of the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates. As the Indian plate pushes northward under the Eurasian plate, the resulting friction and pressure often trigger moderate to strong earthquakes.
Seismic activity in this region is common, but the depth of the quake often determines how strongly it is felt on the surface.

title: PCB central contracts delayed
description: Poor results stall approvals as players await new deals
content:
Poor results stall approvals as players await new deals
KARACHI: Pakistan’s central contracts remain unannounced, leaving players facing an increasingly prolonged wait for confirmation of their deals. Following Pakistan’s disappointing performance on the tour of England, the process has stalled, with progress now expected only if the team delivers improved results during the upcoming home season.
According to sources, the new central contracts for Pakistan’s national cricketers will cover the period from July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2027. Players were briefed on the matter before the team departed for the West Indies and England in July, and a preliminary list of 30 players had also been prepared.
However, Pakistan’s below-par performances in England, followed by a whitewash, brought the process to a standstill. The contracts have yet to be officially announced.
Sources suggest that changes to the initial list are likely, with Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood facing an increased risk of being dropped.
The preliminary list was generated using an algorithm developed by an American company. The software assessed players’ past international and domestic performances across all formats. Selectors were provided with a 15-point assessment framework to evaluate each cricketer’s future prospects, current form and past performances.
Players scoring between 50 and 60 points are eligible for central contracts.
Test players will not be granted no-objection certificates (NOCs) to participate in overseas leagues. However, they will be allowed to play red-ball county cricket and other forms of the game. Players in other categories will be permitted to participate in a limited number of overseas leagues, while Category C players will face no such restrictions.
According to sources, several cricketers want to be placed in Category C. They have reportedly assured the authorities that, despite seeking greater freedom to play in overseas leagues, they will remain available to represent Pakistan in any format whenever required.
Players eligible for the senior categories A, AB, BC and C, must play at least four Test matches, six one-day internationals or six T20 internationals in a year. Category D, reserved for emerging cricketers, is exempted from this requirement. Players must also participate in domestic cricket in their respective formats.
Test specialists in the first tier of Category A will receive a monthly retainer of Rs4 million, while those in the second tier will earn Rs3.6 million.
Players in the first tier of Category AB will receive Rs4.8 million per month, while those in the second tier will be paid Rs3.8 million.
Monthly retainers for Category BC players will be Rs3.4 million and Rs2.6 million, respectively. T20 specialists will receive Rs2.6 million and Rs2 million, depending on their tier. Players in Category D will be paid Rs1 million per month.
The PCB has allocated Rs1.1 billion in its budget for players’ monthly retainers and match fees.
The highest monthly retainer under the proposed central contracts is Rs4.8 million, translating into annual earnings of Rs57.6 million for a top-category player. Including match fees and other payments, a leading player’s annual earnings could rise to Rs80–90 million.
Interestingly, Saim Ayub reportedly earned Rs126 million in a single season of the Pakistan Super League (PSL). Players participating in overseas leagues could earn more than Rs200–220 million annually.
Consequently, restricting or limiting participation in foreign leagues could result in substantial financial losses for players. This is one reason several cricketers are keen to move into Category C, where they would face fewer restrictions when seeking NOCs for overseas competitions.
However, the final decision rests with the PCB.

title: Any miscalculation by adversaries will draw  response beyond imagination   warns CNSC Gen Aamer Raza
description: He conveys warmest felicitations to the cadets hailing from our friendly nations
content:
Says no space for conflict or war in nuclearised environment, Pakistan will not tolerate any cross-border aggression
Commander National Strategic Command (CNSC) General Syed Aamer Raza on Saturday warned adversaries against miscalculation, saying any hostile move against Pakistan would invite a "response far beyond their imagination", while stressing that there was no room for conflict in a nuclearised environment.
“To those who harbour hostile designs across our borders, our stance remains resolute and unambiguous. There is no space for conflict or war in a nuclearised environment, and any miscalculation will be met with a response far beyond the imagination or calculation of the initiator,” said Gen Raza while addressing the passing-out parade of the 154th PMA Long Course and 39th Technical Graduate Course at Kakul.
He said the Armed Forces of Pakistan stand prepared to defend every inch of our sacred motherland at all costs. Referring to disinformation and narrative warfare, he said, “In this post-truth era, our adversaries seek to drive a wedge between the proud people of Pakistan and its armed forces through calculated disinformation and narrative warfare.”
“After failure in Operation Sindoor, our adversary seeks to fracture our social cohesion and state infrastructure through the escalation of proxy terrorism and sub-conventional warfare. Furthermore, hostile elements actively attempt to exploit internal vulnerabilities across Pakistan to cultivate proxy instruments against our national unity,” he said.
The statement came after Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said on Thursday that any “fresh terrorist activity from across the border” would prompt a strike “even bigger than the last time”. A day later, Pakistan rejected and condemned Singh’s “provocative remarks” threatening aggression against the country, warning that any military action would be met with a forceful response.
Gen Raza said the conflict directly threatened the security of the people and the freedom secured through the sacrifices of previous generations, urging the cadets to remain steadfast in their duties, unwavering in their resolve and immune to malicious propaganda and narrative warfare.
Also read: Pakistan Army cadet shines at Australian Royal Military College: ISPR
“Our valiant officers and brave soldiers have willingly laid down their lives in the line of duty, preserving our honour without a shred of compromise,” he said.
The strategic command commander said, “As guardians of this nation, we must remain acutely mindful that safeguarding our national unity, sovereign integrity, and territorial inviolability is an absolute imperative which we shall uphold at all costs and under every circumstance," adding further that go forth with the unyielding conviction, for on our shoulders rests the solemn honour of protecting the sovereignty and dignity of this great nation.
Reiterating Pakistan's commitment to peace, Gen Raza said, “Pakistan stands resolutely as a peace-loving nation, consistently prioritising restraint, dialogue, and regional stability. It is a pursuit for which our nation and its defenders have borne the heaviest burden of sacrifice.”
He added, “However, let no adversary mistake our commitment to peace as weakness nor misinterpret our restraint as a lack of resolve, " adding further that we would neither tolerate cross-border aggression nor any violation of our sovereign borders, as safeguarding the territorial integrity of our motherland is absolute and unyielding.
Speaking about global developments, he said, “The recent shifts in global geopolitics, particularly against the backdrop of heightened Middle Eastern conflicts, have once again underscored Pakistan's pivotal strategic importance on the international stage, and our decisive role in restoring regional stability, exemplified by the landmark Islamabad Accord, demonstrates our enduring commitment to peace and diplomatic de-escalation," he added.
“The Mecca Accord is a sequel to the same vision of durable peace,” he added.
Expressing concern over the situation in Palestine, Gen Raza said, “Our hearts remain heavily burdened by the ongoing tragedy in Palestine, where innocent men, women and children continue to endure unspeakable hardship and systemic oppression," he stated without ambiguity that the Pakistani nation stands resolute and unwavering in our diplomatic, moral and political support for our Palestinian brothers and sisters.

He added, “The persistent violence targeting of non-combatants and destruction of civilian infrastructure are profound violations of international law and a grave stain on the collective conscience of humanity.”
Referring to the situation in Kashmir, he said, “Today the world witnesses increased volatility, where grey zone warfare and hybrid threats attempt to destabilise sovereign states.”
“Closer to home, Kashmir remains the artisan, and the sacrifices of our Kashmiri brothers and sisters in Indian illegally occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK) shall never be forgotten,” he said.
Gen Raza added, “People and the government of Pakistan stand firm in extending their full support to the just struggle of our Kashmiri brothers and sisters until the rightful conclusion of their struggle in accordance with their aspirations and relevant UN resolutions.”
He said, “This occasion, with its enduring significance, will forever remain deeply etched in your memories and core values, and my sincere compliments to your parents, who not only remained unwavering throughout your training, but also served as your foremost source of inspiration, motivation and guidance.”
The strategic command commander also conveyed warmest felicitations to the cadets hailing from our friendly nations of Bangladesh, Iraq, Maldives, Palestine, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan and Yemen on their graduation.
“I am confident that you will cherish the memories of these formative days and the enduring bonds of comradeship that you formed during your stay for decades to come,” he said.
He further added that for those who have earned accolades for outstanding performance across various domains of training, he offers his highest commendations. May this spirit of excellence inspire each of you to continuously strive for distinction throughout your military careers.
Addressing the cadets, CNSC said, “Your commanding presence, military bearing and precise drill movements during today's march past speak volumes about the motivation, discipline and dedication that have characterised your journey at Pakistan Military Academy,” and further added that this flawless display stands as a clear testament to the rigorous stewardship of your instructors, who are seasoned professionals. They have imparted knowledge with exceptional diligence, mastery and allegiance to duty.
“As you transition into professional life, it now becomes your responsibility to emulate their virtues and uphold these high standards with unblemished integrity,” he said.
Gen Raza said, “You are about to step into your professional life, which is a journey replete with challenges, day in and day out. A military career tests one's mettle, professional skills, and leadership qualities by unfolding unprecedented situations.”
He said leadership was the decisive factor in determining the outcome of battles, adding that the cadets would be required to make critical decisions based on sound judgement and the full exercise of their intellect.
“Understand clearly that mastering the art of leadership enables you to win the hearts and minds of your soldiers, for it is only then that you can truly earn the right to lead such finest men any army has to offer,” he said.

The strategic command commander said that true leadership cannot exist without unwavering strength of character, dedication, indomitable courage, professional competence and comradeship.
"When you embody these attributes, your men will follow you through peace and war, prepared to make the ultimate sacrifice," he said.
Referring to technological developments, CNSC said, “Dear cadets, the rapid proliferation of disruptive technology in this era has fundamentally altered the character and dynamics of modern warfare, dismantling traditional operational doctrines and rendering them redundant.”
“Fully cognisant of these shifting paradigms, Pakistan Armed Forces has undertaken a swift multi-domain transformation to fortify our military posture. In this high-tech battlefield, you must not merely adapt to innovation. Instead, you must preempt and master it, remaining constantly ahead of the technological curve as you step into command,” he added.
At the conclusion of his address, Gen Raza said, “In the end, I once again congratulate you all on your well-deserved commission in Pakistan Army.”
He added, “My special felicitations to the Champion Company for winning the coveted Qaide-Azam banner and to those who have received the Sword of Honour, President's Gold Medal, Chief of Army Staff's Marksmanship Award, Chief of Army Staff's Cane, Chief of Defence Forces' Overseas Gold Medal, and Commandant's Cane, owing to their excellent performances during their training at Pakistan Military Academy.”
“As you embark on this noble path, remain steadfastly committed to your assigned missions, executing every duty with utmost diligence, precision, and moral courage,” he said. “May Allah Almighty grant you the wisdom and fortitude to serve your motherland with the highest sense of loyalty, unyielding devotion, and selfless sacrifice. May Allah be your guide and protector,” he added.
Later, a statement issued by the military's media wing, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), said that Gen Raza graced the occasion as the chief guest, reviewed the passing-out parade and presented awards to outstanding cadets.
"The coveted Sword of Honour was awarded to Academy Senior Under Officer Muhammad Junaid Jabbar of 154th PMA Long Course; the President's Gold Medal to Battalion Senior Under Officer Syed Hassan Abbas of 154th PMA Long Course; and the Chief of Defence Forces Overseas Gold Medal to Friendly Country Company Senior Under Officer Riyad Mahmood Khan from Bangladesh of 154th PMA Long Course. Marksman Medal was awarded to Company Sports Sergeant Muhammad Abdullah of the 154th PMA Long Course," it said.
According to the ISPR, the Chief of Army Staff Cane was awarded to Course Under Officer Ali Ahmed Mustafa of the 39th Technical Graduate Course. title: J K  Rowling   s condemns trans rights protest at    Harry Potter and the Cursed Child
description: The production has been shortened to a single performance lasting almost three hours
content:
The production has been shortened to a single performance lasting almost three hours
J.K. Rowling’s agent, Neil Blair, has criticised a protest by transgender rights activists outside London’s Palace Theatre, saying the demonstration put audience members, performers and theatre staff at risk.
The protest took place on October 15, 2026, before a gala performance of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child in the West End. According to Variety , demonstrators entered the red carpet area as celebrities arrived, with some wearing masks, hats and goggles to conceal their identities.
One protester wore a T shirt bearing the slogan “Rowling money kills”. Demonstrators reportedly lay on the red carpet before security staff removed them from the area.
In a statement provided to Variety , Blair said the team respected peaceful activism and the right to express differing views, but argued that protests should not endanger other people.
“We respect peaceful activism and the right to express different views,” Blair said, adding that those rights should be exercised without putting others at risk. He specifically referred to audience members, performers and theatre staff who were present ahead of the performance.
Blair also emphasised the production’s commitment to providing a welcoming environment for audiences. He said the team wanted to continue bringing the Harry Potter world to fans and believed everyone should be able to enjoy the show in an atmosphere of respect and security.
Several public figures attended the gala, including television presenters Vanessa Feltz, Angellica Bell and Richard Arnold, as well as The Chase star Anne Hegerty.
The event also marked a revised version of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child . Previously staged in two parts, the production has been reworked into a single performance lasting almost three hours.
Rowling has faced sustained criticism over her public comments about gender identity and transgender rights. She has rejected allegations that she is transphobic and has previously expressed support for transgender people’s right to live authentically.
The protest highlights continuing tensions surrounding Rowling’s views and the wider Harry Potter franchise, while raising questions about how demonstrations can take place without disrupting theatre audiences or compromising safety.

title: Wolves pile more misery on Burnley

content:
The Wanderers come from behind to secure three points
Wolverhampton Wanderers came from behind to snatch a 2-1 Championship win on Friday and pile more misery on Burnley whose winless run at home extended to a year.
Jamie Vardy gave the hosts the lead with his first Burnley goal after 20 minutes against injury-hit Wolves who travelled north having lost their previous two games.
The home side failed to turn their first-half dominance into more goals and paid for a mistake by captain Kyle Walker resulted in Fer Lopez side-footing an equaliser six minutes before the break.
Wolves substitute Tawanda Chirewa struck within seconds of coming off the bench after 72 minutes, again following a Burnley defensive error.
Mateus Mane pounced on Igor Julio's heavy touch and sent the 23-year-old Zimbabwean international through to strike an angled shot past Clarets goalkeeper Gregoire Coudert.
Burnley's last league win at home was against Leeds in the Premier League on October 18 last year, with their winless run at Turf Moor now 21 games.
The last time these two sides faced off was on the final day of the 2025-26 season, with both teams already relegated from the Premier League.
Burnley are just above the Championship relegation zone with Wolves sixth.
The Clarets' next home game is against Portsmouth, with bitter local rivals Blackburn then scheduled to visit Turf Moor on November 22.

title: Trump threatens California officials with imprisonment over stance on mail ballots
description: Justice Department sues    California to block state from counting ballots
content:
Justice Department sues ​California to block state from counting ballots
The United States Justice Department a day earlier warned ​Los Angeles County and California election officials they could be liable as abettors of a federal ‌crime if they count mail ballots returned by more than 20,000 people the Trump administration says are probably noncitizens. The warning to the Los Angeles County Assistant Counsel Peter Bollinger came less than three weeks before the November 3 midterm elections and days after the department gave California 48 ​hours to review a list of alleged noncitizen voters or face legal action. On Thursday, the Justice Department sued ​California to block the state from counting the ballots.
"Noncitizen voting in a federal election is ⁠a federal crime — and knowingly facilitating such conduct is equally unlawful," Trent McCotter, the acting US deputy attorney general, ​wrote in a letter released on Friday. McCotter called on the county and California's secretary of state to reconsider their refusal ​to take steps that the Trump administration argues are needed to deter voter fraud.
Read: Trump government ads draw scrutiny weeks before midterm elections
US President Donald Trump shared the letter on Truth Social with the comment: "They will all go to jail for a long period of time!!!" California Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Los Angeles County ​Registrar-Recorder Dean Logan were copied on McCotter's letter. The county's counsel office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Weber's ​office referred Reuters to an earlier statement in which she said the Justice Department's attempts to "unlawfully gain access to states' protected voter ‌data and ⁠purge voter rolls serve only to cause chaos and fuel public distrust in our elections."
An earlier letter that McCotter sent on Tuesday to Weber and Logan said the Justice Department provided officials in Los Angeles County with a "password-protected thumb drive" with the names of people the federal government "believes are likely noncitizens" that were sent mail-in ballots from California.
Los Angeles County Counsel ​Dawyn R Harrison said on ​Thursday the county cannot ⁠comply with the Justice Department's requests because the Trump administration did not explain how the list was made. Friday's letter from McCotter said the Justice Department used "internal immigration records" and ​data matching.
Read More: Trump’s new AI-powered website says president lost 2020 election
In July, Trump said his administration had uncovered evidence of more than 275,000 non-citizens registered ​to vote, ⁠but it was not clear how many had actually voted.
In some previous cases, systems intended to verify citizenship have mistakenly flagged some naturalised US citizens as noncitizens. Studies have found that noncitizens casting actual ballots is exceedingly uncommon.
Since July, the Justice Department ⁠has ramped up prosecutions of people accused of illegally voting while not holding US citizenship. ​The White House has also pushed federal agencies to accelerate their review of at least 47 state voter rolls obtained by the Department of Homeland Security, ​according to an internal email seen by Reuters .

title: Iran offers help to end Saudi Houthi conflict through dialogue
description: Coalition spokesman says ballistic missile launch platforms were destroyed in northwestern Saada province
content:
Three civilians killed in Houthi shelling in Yemen, Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed two launch platforms
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Saturday that Tehran supports a “political process” to resolve the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi rebels.
Speaking at the 52nd session of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation’s Council of Foreign Ministers in Baghdad, Araghchi said Iran was ready to help end the conflict involving the Houthis, one of Tehran’s main regional allies.
Araghchi had offered last week to help facilitate dialogue between the two sides during a phone call with Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan.
He said a military solution was not an option for ending Yemen’s years-long civil war.
Araghchi arrived in Baghdad early Saturday and held meetings on the sidelines of the OIC gathering with his Turkish and Egyptian counterparts, Hakan Fidan and Badr Abdelatty.
Foreign ministers from OIC member states attended the first day of the two-day meeting, which is being held in the Iraqi capital for the first time in 45 years.
3 civilians killed, 5 injured in Houthi shelling in Yemen
Three civilians, including two women, were killed and five others injured in shelling by Yemen’s Houthis in the southwestern province of Taiz, a government office said.
The government-run Office of Siege Affairs in Taiz said in a statement late Friday that three civilians were killed when the Houthis shelled the Sabir al-Mawadim district south of the province.
The office identified the victims as Safwan Saeed Obeid, 28, Asia Abdulsamad Saeed Ahmed, 55, and Safiya Hazza Saif al-Baadani.
It said the Houthis also carried out separate shelling attacks on the al-Shaqab area south of Taiz and Aqaqa in the west, injuring five civilians, including two women.
On Friday, the Yemeni army said it had repelled a large-scale Houthi attack on the al-Shaqab front south of Taiz following clashes that lasted around eight hours, killing 16 Houthi fighters and injuring others, according to the Taiz Military Axis.
The army also said it carried out airstrikes against Houthi positions at the al-Hangar checkpoint and the al-Maqbaba and al-Kamil hills in the al-Dabab area west of Taiz.
Read: Iran denies Saudi accusation of involvement in Houthi attacks, offers to mediate
It added that the strikes also targeted Houthi military reinforcements, weapons and equipment east of the al-Shaqab front.
The Houthis did not immediately comment on the army’s claims.
2nd tanker attack reported in same area off Saudi Arabia: UKMTO
A second tanker attack was reported in the same area off Saudi Arabia, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said Saturday.
The latest incident occurred at 1922GMT Friday around 78 nautical miles (144 kilometres) northeast of Al Jubayl, according to a UKMTO advisory.

The tanker’s master reported that the vessel was attacked with a rocket-propelled grenade fired from a small boat, damaging its aft port quarter.
All crew members were accounted for and reported safe, while a full assessment of the damage and any environmental impact was not immediately available.
Authorities are investigating the incident, while vessels in the area were advised to transit with caution and report any suspicious activity.
Tanker hit by unknown projectile off Saudi Arabia: UK maritime agency
A tanker was struck by an unknown projectile off the coast of Saudi Arabia, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said Saturday.
UKMTO said it received a delayed report of an incident that occurred at 0200PKT on Saturday, around 68 nautical miles northeast of Al Jubayl, Saudi Arabia.

Citing the vessel’s company security officer, UKMTO said all crew members were safe and had been evacuated.
No environmental impact was reported at the time of the report.
Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed 2 Houthi missile launch platforms in Yemen
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said late on Friday that it destroyed Houthi ballistic missile launch ramps.
Spokesman Turki al-Maliki said on US social media platform X that the coalition destroyed launch platforms in northwestern Saada province.
No additional details were provided about the operation.
Yemen has been engulfed in conflict since the Houthis seized the Yemeni capital, Sanaa, and several provinces in September 2014. That prompted the Saudi-led coalition to intervene in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.
Saudi Arabia backs UN Security Council statement urging cooperation to prevent Houthis from acquiring arms
Saudi Arabia welcomed a UN Security Council presidential statement condemning Houthi attacks against the kingdom and urging cooperation to prevent the group from obtaining weapons.
Read more: Pakistan condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, calls for immediate halt at UN
In a statement, the ministry welcomed the council's condemnation of continued and escalating attacks by the Houthis against Saudi Arabia, including attacks targeting airports and energy infrastructure.
It also highlighted the council's condemnation of "ongoing threats to navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb."
“The Kingdom affirmed the importance of the statement's provisions, including its emphasis on the importance of full implementation of Security Council resolution 2216 (2015) and subsequent resolutions, and its call for practical cooperation to prevent the terrorist Houthi group from acquiring weapons and other forms of support,” the statement said.
Resolution 2216 demands that the Houthis immediately and unconditionally end the use of violence, withdraw from areas they seized, including the Yemeni capital, Sanaa, hand over weapons taken from military and security institutions, cease exercising the powers of Yemen’s internationally recognised government and facilitate humanitarian and medical access to civilians.
The ministry said the kingdom reaffirmed its "inherent right under international law" to take all necessary measures to defend its security and protect its citizens and residents.
The UN Security Council presidential statement, adopted earlier this week, condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and “called for cooperation, including with the Government of Yemen, to prevent the Houthis from acquiring arms and related materiel.”

title: Two terrorists killed in Balochistan IBO  state media
description: Sources say terrorists were involved in harassing passengers along the Quetta   Taftan Highway
content:
Sources say terrorists were involved in harassing passengers along the Quetta–Taftan Highway
Security forces killed two terrorists during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in the Dalbandin area of Balochistan’s Chagai district, Radio Pakistan reported on Saturday, citing security sources.
According to the sources, security forces effectively targeted the terrorists’ hideouts during the operation.
The killed terrorists were involved in harassing passengers travelling along the Quetta–Taftan Highway and spreading fear and panic in the area, the sources added.
On October 15 , security forces killed five terrorists belonging to the Indian proxy, Fitna al-Hindustan, during an IBO in the Washuk district of Balochistan, the military’s media wing said.
“During the conduct of the operation, a terrorist hideout was busted by security forces through swift and decisive action,” ISPR said, adding that five Indian-sponsored terrorists were neutralised.
Read: 49 terrorists killed in Balochistan, K-P IBOs
On October 14 , security forces also killed five terrorists and injured four others during an IBO against Fitna al-Hindustan in the same district of Balochistan. During the operation, advanced weapons and ammunition were recovered.
Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terrorist activity over the past three months, with a series of attacks across the country resulting in the martyrdom of security personnel and civilians.
Last week, 12 people were killed and 35 others injured when a blast struck a joint checkpoint near Aman Mela in the Darazinda area of Dera Ismail Khan, with the TTP claiming responsibility for the attack.
On September 19, 23 people, including 15 police personnel, were martyred in a blast at a mosque in Kohat’s Police Lines during Friday prayers. Eight terrorists were also killed during a subsequent search and clearance operation. Later, the Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers.
In a separate incident, a captain and a lieutenant were among six security personnel martyred in an exchange of fire in Hangu district, while eight terrorists were killed.
On September 1, six personnel, including two officers, and a customs department official were martyred as security forces thwarted an attempt to breach the Customs House in Balochistan.
In July, at least 30 people , including 27 police personnel, were martyred when terrorists identified by the state as the Indian proxy Fitna al-Hindustan ambushed police personnel deployed in the Kach Mangi Phase III area of Ziarat, triggering hours-long gun battles. title: AI agents accessed Indian computer systems without authorisation  Cybersecurity agency
description: Autonomous agents exceed assigned tasks  access live systems as no affected organisation detected unauthorised access
content:
Autonomous agents exceed assigned tasks, access live systems as no affected organisation detected unauthorised access
Autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents accessed Indian computer systems without authorisation during research and testing, India's cybersecurity agency said on Thursday.
In an advisory issued October 15, the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said AI model developers had voluntarily disclosed multiple incidents in which autonomous agents exceeded their assigned tasks and accessed live systems belonging to Indian organisations.
According to CERT-In, none of the affected organisations independently detected the unauthorised access. The agency also identified financially motivated cyberattacks involving publicly available AI-powered offensive security tools.
Read: Bill Gates warns cyberattacks most imminent AI threat
Some organisations were attacked again within days after failing to fully address their security vulnerabilities, it added.
CERT-In urged AI developers to restrict autonomous agents' internet access and conduct testing in simulated environments rather than live systems. It also called on developers to immediately report unauthorised activity involving their AI tools.
The agency advised organisations to strengthen authentication, remove exposed credentials and improve monitoring for automated cyberattacks. It also recommended retaining security logs for at least 180 days to support the detection and investigation of security incidents .

title: Vance suggests disagreement with Trump over Iran war
description: US Iran war
content:
US says Iran barred from maritime trade as pressure campaign targets oil revenue, military funding
US Vice President JD Vance suggested in an interview aired Friday that he may have disagreed with President Donald Trump over the Iran war.
“Even if you disagree with him on that one issue, you can have that disagreement. And I think I have had that disagreement,” Vance said on a political talk show hosted by former White House spokesman Sean Spicer.
Vance was responding to a question about his relationship with political commentator and former Trump ally Tucker Carlson, who has sharply criticised the Iran war, arguing that it serves Israeli rather than American interests and contradicts Trump’s pledge to avoid costly foreign military interventions.
Vance said that Carlson, who has espoused conservative views, was “very, very angry” over the war. “He and I have had that conversation in private, in public. I know how he feels, and I understand,” he said.
“What I've said to Tucker is don't throw the baby out with the bathwater … Aren't closed borders and ending the ridiculous anti-white racial discrimination in our university admissions, aren't these things worth actually acknowledging that Donald Trump has done a lot of good?”
US says Iran barred from maritime trade as pressure campaign targets oil revenue, military funding
US Central Command (CENTCOM) Commander Admiral Brad Cooper claimed Friday that Iran has been cut off from maritime imports and exports as Washington intensified its campaign against Tehran's oil revenue and military funding.
In a video message, Cooper said US efforts focused on three areas: restricting Iranian oil exports, disrupting digital financing and weakening the ability of Iran's security forces to pay their personnel.
"As a point of emphasis, with the exception of the humanitarian assistance we've allowed in, Iran has no exports and no imports by sea," Cooper said.
He said US forces have prevented Iran from exporting at least $25 billion worth of crude oil in recent months.
"CENTCOM has also supported US interagency partners in freezing nearly $350 million in digital cryptocurrency assets, further constricting Iran's ability to fund terrorism or replace weapons and factories that we destroy," he said.
Cooper claimed that Iran-aligned groups operating across the region had begun withholding payments to their fighters to redirect funds to the IRGC, which he said was also struggling to pay its personnel.
Read: Iran president says conflict in Mideast amounts to 'ecocide'
According to Cooper, the IRGC was also struggling to pay its personnel.
"The Islamic regime is clearly feeling the economic pain, and the IRGC is increasingly showing signs of greater desperation as a result," he said.
Despite the restrictions on Iranian maritime trade, Cooper said commercial shipping continued through the Strait of Hormuz.
He accused Iran of attacking commercial vessels and said US forces were working with regional allies and shipping industry partners to strengthen maritime security.
"Let me be clear: the Strait of Hormuz is controlled by the United States and our regional partners, not Iran, and it remains open for business," Cooper said.
He said approximately 400 merchant ships had transited the strait over the previous seven days.
He added that US forces had assisted Gulf partners in transporting more than 100 million barrels of crude oil through the waterway during the same period, bringing the total volume shipped with US assistance in recent months to more than 1.3 billion barrels.
Strait of Hormuz transits remain 70% below pre-conflict levels: UK maritime agency
Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remained about 70% below pre-conflict levels as attacks on commercial vessels continued, a UK maritime agency said Friday.
In its weekly overview, the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) reported 125 outbound and 129 inbound transits over the past seven days.
The figures marked a decline from 129 outbound and 146 inbound transits recorded the previous week, according to the agency.
UKMTO reported 12 attacks on vessels during the week, including 10 in the Strait of Hormuz, one in the Gulf and one in the Gulf of Oman. Six vessels continued or reached port, one was lost, two were disabled or not under command, and three have unconfirmed outcomes.
Container ship sinks after projectile strike
UKMTO said a container ship was struck by an unidentified projectile near Ras Shaykh Masud on October 13.
The vessel caught fire and sank the following day, according to the agency.
All crew members were evacuated, UKMTO said.
The agency warned that it was struggling to establish the actual number of attacks because most targeted vessels declined to report incidents.
UKMTO said it had recorded 84 incidents in the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict began in late February.
The reported attacks came amid continued tensions between Iran and the US over navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.
The waterway is a major route for global energy and commodity shipments and remains a key issue in negotiations between Washington and Tehran.
Iran says oil tanker hit naval mine in Strait of Hormuz
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said Friday that an oil supertanker struck a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz, triggering a massive explosion and fire.
The vessel was carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude oil when it attempted to transit the strategic waterway, according to a statement carried by the semi-official Tasnim News Agency.
The IRGC Navy described the vessel as a "rogue" tanker that had switched off its navigation and radar systems.
It claimed the tanker had attempted to exploit US military support to transport goods through the strait.
The statement did not identify the vessel, its owner or flag.
It also provided no information about possible casualties or the extent of the damage.
The conflict began with US and Israeli attacks against Iran on February 28, followed by a ceasefire in April.
Clashes between Washington and Tehran later resumed as negotiations stalled, although the two sides signed a framework agreement in June.
