title: FIFA orders partial stadium closure for Spain over anti Muslim chants
description: 15  of seats to close during Spain s next home friendly following discriminatory chants at match against Egypt
content:
15% of seats to close during Spain's next home friendly following discriminatory chants at match against Egypt
FIFA has ordered Spain to partially close its stadium for its next home friendly after supporters directed anti-Muslim chants during a match against Egypt, the football governing body said.
FIFA said in its decision that at least 15% of the available seats must remain closed, primarily in the stands behind the goals.
The world football governing body also fined the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) $20,000.
Subject to FIFA's approval, the federation may allocate the affected seats to community or special-interest groups, including families, students and anti-discrimination organisations.
Any proposed plan must include visible anti-discrimination measures and be submitted to FIFA at least 15 days before the match.
Read: Infantino offers apology but 'no answers' at FIFA meeting
The sanction stems from Spain's goalless friendly against Egypt on March 31 at the RCDE Stadium in Barcelona. During the first half and shortly after the second half began, a group of Spanish supporters resorted to discriminatory chants targeting Muslims.
An anti-discrimination warning appeared on the stadium screen, while an announcement urged supporters to stop the chants. The warning was repeated early in the second half, prompting whistles from some sections of the crowd.
FIFA subsequently opened disciplinary proceedings over what it described as Islamophobic and xenophobic conduct.
The RFEF argued that the chant did not constitute discrimination and that the word "Muslim" was not inherently insulting. FIFA's Disciplinary Committee rejected the argument, finding that words not offensive in isolation could become discriminatory when used to ridicule or demean a religious identity.
The committee said the federation could not "persuasively maintain both that the chant was entirely harmless and that it warranted activation of anti-discrimination measures."
FIFA acknowledged that Spanish officials had introduced preventive measures, cooperated with match authorities, publicly condemned the incident and sought to identify those involved.
Read More: Norwegian FA files complaints with FIFA committees
Following the match, the RFEF denounced the chants.
Spain coach Luis de la Fuente described the incident as "intolerable," saying violent individuals were using football as a platform. Spanish winger Lamine Yamal, who is Muslim, also condemned the chants, saying that using religion as a taunt was disrespectful and racist.
The Egyptian Football Association called the chants a "repugnant act of racism," stressing that the conduct of a small group would not damage relations between the two national federations.
The sanction applies only to Spain's next home friendly, not a competitive fixture. Its implementation could be delayed depending on Spain's Nations League and Euro 2028 qualifying schedule.

title: Selma Blair breaks silence on plane arrest with new statement
description: Selma Blair addresses plane arrest as her representative cites a medical emergency and denies intent to harm anyone
content:
Selma Blair addresses plane arrest as her representative cites a medical emergency and denies intent to harm anyone
Actress Selma Blair has addressed her recent arrest following an alleged altercation aboard a Delta Air Lines flight, with her representative saying she experienced a medical emergency and did not intend to hurt anyone.
In a statement shared exclusively with PEOPLE on October 16, Blair’s spokesperson said public reports had largely relied on a police statement and an earlier headline. The representative argued that important details surrounding the incident had not been fully reported.
“Selma Blair experienced a medical emergency on the flight. There was no attempt to open the door of the aircraft. Selma did not intend to harm anyone,” the statement said.
Blair, 54, was arrested at New York’s John F. Kennedy International Airport on October 11 after the alleged incident. She appeared in court the following day and pleaded not guilty to two counts of second-degree assault. She was subsequently released on bail.
Her representative also addressed Blair’s multiple sclerosis diagnosis, which she publicly disclosed in 2018. The spokesperson said the actress continues to experience daily pain and also has pseudobulbar affect, a neurological condition associated with her MS that can affect emotional expression. The statement further noted that Blair travels with a service dog.
According to PEOPLE, a criminal court affidavit accused Blair of repeatedly kicking a police officer and striking a nurse in the chest. The FBI confirmed that it was investigating the incident, while Delta Air Lines reiterated its commitment to the safety of passengers and crew.
The representative urged the public to consider all available facts before reaching conclusions about the case, adding that there was more to the incident than had been reported.
Blair, known for films including Cruel Intentions , has previously spoken publicly about living with multiple sclerosis and advocating for disability rights. The legal proceedings surrounding the October 11 incident remain separate from her representative’s account of what happened aboard the flight.

title: Pakistan to chair IMF  WB boards in 2027
description: Pakistan to chair IMF  WB boards in 2027
content:
WBG Corporate Secretariat briefed Cheema on the responsibilities associated with the chairmanship
Pakistan will chair the Boards of Governors of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group (WBG) in 2027, marking the country's first return to the leadership of both institutions since 1953, the Ministry of Economic Affairs said on Friday.
Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Cheema, who also serves as Pakistan's governor to the World Bank, was formally announced as the incoming chairman during the plenary session of the 2026 WBG-IMF Annual Meetings in Bangkok.
The annual meetings, being held from October 12 to 18, brought together policymakers, central bank governors, business leaders and other participants from around the world to discuss the global economy.
The ministry described the appointment as a historic milestone, saying the chairmanship would provide Pakistan with an opportunity to contribute to international economic and development discussions and facilitate constructive dialogue among member countries.
Following the plenary session, the WBG Corporate Secretariat briefed Cheema on the responsibilities associated with the chairmanship. He also met WBG Vice President and Corporate Secretary Aradhana Kumar-Capoor to discuss institutional support and coordination during Pakistan's tenure.
Cheema separately met outgoing chairman Carlos Carvallo Spalding, governor of Paraguay's central bank, congratulating him on completing his tenure and commending his stewardship. The two discussed the responsibilities of the office and priorities for the coming year.
During the meetings, Cheema reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to strengthening the voice of developing countries, improving coordination among multilateral development institutions and promoting effective and predictable development financing.
He emphasised the importance of mobilising private investment to support sustainable and inclusive growth. He said Pakistan would work closely with the WBG, the IMF and member countries to encourage constructive dialogue and contribute to a more responsive multilateral development and financial system.
Separately, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb met World Bank Group President Ajay Banga at a dinner hosted by the Thai prime minister on the sidelines of the annual meetings in Bangkok, according to state-run Pakistan Television.
Pakistan remains engaged with the IMF under a $7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and a $1.4 billion Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF). Earlier this month, Pakistan and the Fund reached a staff-level agreement following the fourth review under the EFF and the third review under the RSF.

title: PHC to hear challenge to emergency on 20th
description: PHC to hear challenge to emergency on 20th
content:
PTI Chairman approached the PHC on October 14, challenging imposition of emergency and governor's rule in K-P
The Peshawar High Court (PHC) has listed for hearing the petitions challenging the federal government's October 11 decision to impose emergency and governor's rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P). The court will take up the pleas on October 20.
PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan approached the PHC on October 14, challenging the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in K-P and seeking the annulment of the presidential proclamation issued on October 11. National Democratic Movement (NDM) leaders Mohsin Dawar and Bushra Gohar also separately filed similar petition in the court.
In his petition, filed through Advocate Ali Zaman, Gohar termed the measures unconstitutional and discriminatory, arguing that terrorism cannot be used as a pretext to curtail the powers of an elected provincial government.
The PTI chairman contended that terrorism had affected different parts of the country in the past without elected provincial governments being removed on that basis.
He cited the security situation in Balochistan, where terrorist attacks and casualties had been continually reported, arguing that governor's rule had not been imposed there despite the serious law and order challenges.
He referred to the period between 2007 and 2015, when K-P and the former tribal areas experienced a severe wave of militancy, resulting in substantial casualties among civilians and security personnel.
The petitioner argued that the elected provincial government had not been removed through governor's rule during that period and urged the court to examine the constitutional justification and alleged motives behind the current measures.
Gohar maintained that the PTI opposed terrorism and supported action against militant elements and efforts to restore peace. He rejected allegations that the party's provincial government had failed to take effective action against terrorism or had shown leniency towards militants.
He stated that such accusations were being used to exert political pressure and weaken the mandate PTI secured in the 2024 general elections.
The petition argued that the party had won a two-thirds majority in the province and that the federal government could not curtail the powers of an elected government because of political differences.
It also questioned the use of the failure of negotiations as a justification for action against PTI, maintaining that the party had not planned any unlawful activity during its long march and that peaceful political protest could not, by itself, justify suspending an elected government.
Invoking Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, the petition asked the court to examine whether the requirements for imposing an emergency and invoking governor's rule had been met.
Article 232 deals with emergency powers in specified circumstances, while Article 234 provides a mechanism for a presidential proclamation where a provincial government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.
Separately, NDM President Mohsin Dawar and Bushra Gohar filed a constitutional petition through Advocate Yousaf Orakzai, challenging the October 11 presidential proclamation as unlawful, unconstitutional and beyond the president's authority.
The NDM leaders asked the high court to declare the proclamation unlawful and set it aside. They have also sought interim relief suspending its implementation until the petition is finally decided.

title: Fazl draws ire over K P governor s rule remarks
description: Fazl draws ire over K P governor s rule remarks
content:
Naqvi alleges JUI-F chief upset over not being offered governorship
Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Friday took a swipe at JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman without naming him, saying a political party chief was upset over being left out of the proposed imposition of governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) and not being offered the governorship.
In remarks circulated in the media as an informal interaction with journalists in Lahore, Naqvi was quoted as saying that the politician had relied on the establishment for decades and had even secured his party's tickets through it.
He said such politicians were in no position to point fingers at others, adding that political differences should be debated through arguments and facts rather than abusive language and allegations.
However, no formal media interaction took place.
Naqvi also questioned why some political leaders had only recently begun expressing concern over the rights and resources of the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA), asking why they had remained silent when the merged districts were allegedly denied their due share.
He said the rights of former FATA residents should be treated as a matter above political interests.
Saying that K-P was facing serious security challenges, the interior minister urged political leaders to help restore peace and eliminate terrorism rather than fuel confrontation and unrest. He said the province needed peace, stability and collective efforts instead of political confrontation.
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif and her information minister also joined the chorus against Fazl, accusing him of supporting those backing terrorism.
Fazl, one of the most vocal opponents of governor's rule in K-P, has rejected the move and blamed the government for the failure of talks, countering its claim that PTI's negotiating team repeatedly changed its position on the chief minister's cues.
In a statement on X, Maryam said she had not expected a senior politician who had himself been a victim of terrorism to support those allegedly backing terrorism.
She said it was regrettable that, instead of holding accountable those responsible for K-P's deterioration through incompetence, corruption and poor governance, he was speaking in their favour.
Maryam questioned whether the people Fazl was defending had attended the funerals of martyrs during their 13 years in power in the province. She accused them of providing terrorists with shelter, resources, safe havens and land from which to launch attacks against Pakistan.
She further criticised the use of provincial resources for sit-ins and protests, alleging that years of PTI rule had been squandered through corruption and incompetence.
Referring to Fazl's remarks about the military leadership, Maryam said his comments about the field commander who had led Pakistan to a historic victory had hurt patriotic Pakistanis.
Maryam argued that Fazl's position was particularly difficult to understand given that his own party had suffered losses to terrorism and that his associates had been killed in attacks.
She also pointed to the personal attacks and abusive language directed at him in the past by those whose cause he was now defending.

title: Opposition unites against governor s rule in K P
description: Opposition unites against governor s rule in K P
content:
Vows joint resistance, keeps resignations option open
Opposition parties on Friday vowed a joint struggle against the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), demanding constitutional supremacy, parliamentary sovereignty and free and fair elections, while keeping open the option of resigning from the assemblies.
Opposition Leader in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai said he would contact opposition parties and convene an all-parties conference (APC).
He said the option of resigning from the assemblies remained open, but stressed that the opposition favoured a peaceful, constitutional struggle and was ready for talks.
Speaking at a news conference at the Peshawar High Court, Achakzai said he had come to express solidarity with the people of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, alleging that the federal government had acted unconstitutionally by removing the elected provincial government.
He said the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) had won seats in the elections but the government had been handed to another party. He also cited the disqualification of lawmakers and alleged irregularities in the electoral process.
Achakzai said no one should be prevented from meeting a prisoner and alleged that PTI founder Imran Khan was being pressured into an agreement.
He said former prime ministers Nawaz Sharif and Benazir Bhutto had faced similar treatment in the past, adding that the same was happening under the current governments led by the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP).
He questioned the whereabouts of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and said information about him should be made public. He also expressed concern over reports that provincial ministers, lawmakers and party workers had gone missing.
"This is not the time to remain silent but to stand up for the people's rights and constitutional protection," Achakzai said. "We will neither throw stones at anyone nor resort to violence. We will pursue a peaceful struggle."
He said the opposition was willing to negotiate if the government was serious about dialogue. Policies should be made in parliament, he added, and all institutions should operate within their constitutional limits.
Achakzai said the opposition had set out its demands in response to the government's offer of talks. These included upholding the Constitution, withdrawing controversial amendments, restoring parliament's role as the principal centre of decision-making and establishing an independent commission to ensure free and fair elections.
The country's problems could not be resolved unless parliament became the primary forum for decision-making, he said, adding that contacts with opposition parties were under way and all would be invited to the proposed APC.
On provincial rights, Achakzai said the people of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa had the first claim to the province's mineral resources. He called for unity across political lines to protect the country and safeguard public rights.
He also cited the merger of the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (Fata) with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, saying decisions of national importance should be made through constitutional and democratic procedures.
Akhtar Mengal, head of the Balochistan National Party, criticised those who claimed to be the architects of the Constitution while, he said, violating its provisions.
He alleged that the imposition of governor's rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa amounted to blaming the entire province for terrorism. Counterterrorism operations had also been under way in Balochistan for years, he said, but insecurity continued to affect the province.
Mengal questioned whether such measures could resolve the country's problems. He also alleged that the elected chief minister of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa had been taken away and cited reports concerning the whereabouts of the provincial assembly speaker and ministers.
He said people elected through what he called "Form 47" were occupying the assemblies and argued that such a system could not endure.
Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, opposition leader in the Senate, said lawlessness had worsened and accused the government of taking control of a province because it could not manage the existing system. Government ministers had themselves acknowledged the system's failure, he said.
He alleged that those who had stolen the public mandate were seeking to silence dissent and protests. Citing rising poverty, he said remaining silent about the country's situation was inconsistent with patriotism. He pledged to continue his struggle regardless of the circumstances.

title: Pakistan walks a diplomatic tightrope
description: Pakistan walks a diplomatic tightrope
content:
FO skirts KSA-Iran row over Houthi attacks
Pakistan on Friday reaffirmed its commitment to Saudi Arabia's security but declined to be drawn into Riyadh's latest accusation that Iran continues to arm and train Yemen's Houthi militia, signalling Islamabad's effort to balance its close defence ties with Saudi Arabia with its engagement with Tehran.
Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said Pakistan could not comment on the Saudi allegation against Iran while reiterating Islamabad's broader position that regional conflicts should be resolved through diplomacy.
Asked about Saudi Foreign Ministry Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly's accusation that Iran continued to arm, train and support the Houthi militia in violation of UN Security Council resolutions, Sajjad told reporters that Pakistan could not comment on the allegation.
"I would not be able to comment on the alleged accusation against Iran that you mentioned," he said.
The spokesperson instead reiterated Pakistan's broader position that the regional conflict should be resolved through diplomacy.
"Pakistan is keen to see peace and stability return to the entire region, including the Middle East and West Asia, and will continue to engage with all relevant stakeholders in this regard," he said.
"There is no solution through war. Peace can only be restored through negotiations and the peaceful settlement of disputes."
Pakistan, however, reaffirmed its commitment to Saudi Arabia's security and condemned the latest Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.
Sajjad said one Pakistani was killed at Riyadh airport and six others were injured in the recent attacks. The injured, he added, were receiving treatment at different locations in Riyadh while the Pakistani mission was in contact with them and their families.
Pakistan has repeatedly condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including attacks targeting civilian and economic infrastructure, while also supporting dialogue for a political settlement of the Yemen conflict.
The spokesperson said Pakistan remained committed to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, unity and independence of Yemen and supported diplomatic efforts to end the conflict.
He also reiterated that Pakistan would fulfil its obligations under its defence arrangements with Saudi Arabia.
"Pakistan will fulfill its obligations under these agreements," Sajjad said when asked whether the Makkah defence agreement could be practically invoked following repeated attacks on Saudi territory.
However, he stopped short of giving any timeline for military action, saying operational matters, including deployment and action on the ground, fell within the domain of the armed forces, ISPR and the General Secretariat of the Makkah Joint Alliance.
Sajjad also said Pakistan supported Saudi Arabia's right to defend itself under Article 51 of the UN Charter.
Against this backdrop, Pakistan also played down recent remarks by an Iranian lawmaker questioning Islamabad's mediation efforts between Iran and the United States, making clear that the comments would not affect its broader engagement with Tehran.
Sajjad described Iran as a "brotherly country" and said Pakistan's role in facilitating the Islamabad understanding between Iran and the US had been appreciated by the Iranian leadership.
"Iran is a brotherly country, and its leadership has greatly appreciated Pakistan's role in mediation and in bringing the Islamabad MoU to fruition," Sajjad said at his weekly briefing.
He was responding to a question about Iranian lawmaker Mohsen Zanganeh's recent remarks during his visit to Kabul, in which he reportedly questioned Pakistan's mediation role and suggested that even a Pakistani tweet on the issue had been written by Americans.
Sajjad said he had seen the reported remarks but would not comment on their credibility.
"They may also have been taken out of context, as Iran's leadership and people are grateful for Pakistan's efforts," he said, adding that members of Iran's National Assembly had also applauded Pakistan's "constructive role" in the region.
The remarks indicate that Islamabad does not want the comments by an individual Iranian lawmaker to undermine its broader engagement with Tehran, particularly after Pakistan's efforts to facilitate the Islamabad MoU between Iran and the United States.
On Afghanistan, Sajjad said Pakistan remained open to dialogue but made clear that any talks with the Taliban would not be unconditional.
He said Islamabad wanted a "verifiable mechanism" ensuring a complete cessation of terrorist activities emanating from Afghan soil.
Responding to questions about a possible Russian mediation initiative following the recent Moscow Format meeting, he said Pakistan valued its engagement with Russia and would welcome "any sincere efforts by friendly countries" that could address its security concerns.
"At present, I am not aware of any separate, formal Russian mediation initiative being under discussion," Sajjad said.
He added that meaningful progress would ultimately depend on "concrete and verifiable action on the ground" by the Taliban authorities against terrorist groups operating from Afghanistan.
He also confirmed that Pakistan's participation in the Moscow Format meeting was at the special representative level and noted that the absence of a joint communiqué was significant.
"The fact that no joint communiqué was issued after the Moscow Format is self-evident that Afghanistan did not accept the formulation which had been acceptable until last year particularly about presence of terrorist network in Afghanistan," Sajjad said.
On India, the Foreign Office strongly rejected recent remarks by the Indian defence minister threatening aggression against Pakistan, warning that any military action would receive a "forceful response".
"Let there be no ambiguity: Pakistan remains fully prepared to safeguard its sovereignty and territorial integrity against any ill-advised aggression," Sajjad said.
"Our restraint and commitment to peace must never be mistaken for weakness. Any aggression will be met with a forceful response."

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday, appreciating the remarkable progress in Pakistan-Saudi Arabia relations in recent years, reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to further strengthening existing institutional mechanisms to deepen and broaden bilateral cooperation across various sectors.
The prime minister, in a meeting with newly appointed Saudi Ambassador Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy, who called on him, reaffirmed that Pakistan stood shoulder-to-shoulder with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its sovereignty, security and territorial integrity.
He strongly condemned the recent escalation in Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, which had resulted in the loss of precious lives and injuries to scores of innocent people, including Pakistani nationals.
He underlined that Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had always stood by each other and that the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement and the Makkah Joint Defence Alliance marked historic milestones in their longstanding fraternal relations and reflected their shared commitment to regional peace and security.
Welcoming the ambassador to Pakistan, the prime minister congratulated him on assuming his new responsibilities and wished him success in his diplomatic assignment.
He thanked the Saudi leadership for its longstanding economic and financial support to Pakistan.
The prime minister also wished the ambassador every success in his assignment and assured him of Pakistan's full support and cooperation in further strengthening the longstanding fraternal ties between the two countries.
Ambassador Albugamy also met Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, where the latter underscored longstanding fraternal and strategic ties between Islamabad and Riyadh, according to the Foreign Office (FO).
He also reaffirmed Pakistan and Saudi Arabia's "shared commitment to further strengthen bilateral cooperation for mutual progress and prosperity".
The FO added that the new Saudi envoy conveyed greetings from the kingdom's leadership to Pakistan, with Dar reciprocating and conveying his best wishes to Saudi King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and other Saudi leaders.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Friday that it intercepted missiles and drones over Riyadh and other areas, as the kingdom comes under sustained attack from its Iran-backed foes.
Since Yemen's civil war flared back to life in July, the Houthis have repeatedly struck Saudi targets including Red Sea tankers, oil facilities and Riyadh's international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week.
Saudi Arabia leads a military coalition that has supported Yemen's internationally recognised government against the Houthis for more than a decade.
"We intercepted and destroyed three drones in the southern area and Riyadh... and two cruise missiles over the Red Sea," coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki wrote on X.
He added that "in the past hours, we intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile over Yanbu", a city home to the terminus of a major oil pipeline on the Red Sea coast.
The pressure on Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil exporter, comes as global energy markets were already rattled by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz at the outset of the wider Middle East war in February.
The Houthi attacks have proliferated since the group launched a lightning offensive in Yemen in September, seizing strategic government-held territory along the Red Sea coast overlooking a major chokepoint for global shipping.
The UN Security Council on Thursday "condemned in the strongest terms continued and escalatory Houthi attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia", as well as their "attacks and threats against commercial shipping in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab" Strait, the southern gateway to the Suez Canal.
The Security Council also denounced the group's "reckless strikes" on Riyadh's airport, which the Saudi-led coalition said had been targeted at least 20 times so far this month.
A Saudi foreign ministry official accused Iran on Thursday of continuing "to arm, train and support the Houthi militia in violation of UN security council resolutions".
"We think that the escalation by the Houthis at this latest stage of the conflict is encouraged by Iran," added Dr. Rayed Krimly, deputy minister for public diplomacy.
Yemeni government forces have launched a counteroffensive with Saudi air support to retake areas seized by the Houthis, but have so far failed to reverse their gains.
On Thursday, the group launched a deadly missile attack on the presidential palace in the interim seat of the Yemeni government in Aden, killing five people and wounding 16 others, according to the health minister.
Yemeni Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani denounced the "cowardly" act on X, calling it a "continuation of (the Houthis') criminal pattern".
A government minister said on condition of anonymity that Zindani had been present at the time, but "was not harmed in any way".
The minister said the Houthis hit a command centre for Yemeni government forces at the complex with three missiles, and another for Saudi coalition forces with two missiles.
Media affiliated with the Houthis said they had targeted "the headquarters of military operations, led by Saudi officers, at the Al-Maashiq Palace in Aden, as well as weapons depots belonging to them".

title: UN chief says fuel subsidy means  subsidising suicide
description: UN chief says fuel subsidy means  subsidising suicide
content:
UN chief Antonio Guterres on Friday urged governments to stop subisiding the production of fossil fuels that are "boiling our planet and are the scourge of biodiversity", a day after launching a report that warned the world was off track to achieving the 2030 biodiversity targets enshrined in a landmark pact for nature.
Addressing leaders in Armenia ahead of next week's UN biodiversity summit, Guterres said governments were still "spending money on the wrong things" and singled out incentives for fossil fuels. "Subsidising fossil fuels is subsidising suicide," Guterres said at an event in Yerevan.
"They are boiling our planet and are the scourge of biodiversity. I urge governments everywhere to end these handouts once and for all, and to use the savings for people and planet instead." The UN says that for every dollar invested in protecting or restoring nature, about $30 still goes into activities that degrade it. Nations have made little headway since pledging in 2022 to reduce public spending on activities that harm nature such as mining, fossil fuel extraction and intensive farming. This includes an estimated $2.6 trillion a year in public subsidies that negatively impact nature and the climate.

title: Russian diesel deal puts Trump at odds with allies
description: Russian diesel deal puts Trump at odds with allies
content:
Macron warns Trump-Putin accord will deepen division and doubt
A US deal to buy Russian diesel has sparked fresh tensions between Washington, Kyiv and European allies, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy warning that the agreement would channel more money into Russia's war effort, while French President Emmanuel Macron said the move sent a negative signal.
Macron also criticised the agreement, saying it was "not good for anyone" and created division, doubt and defiance. And speaking at an EU summit in Brussels, Zelenskiy said the agreement would allow cash to flow back into Russia and help finance its invasion of Ukraine. "This diesel deal will never be enough to offset the impact of the Strait of Hormuz on global markets. But it will put more money straight into Putin's pocket to fund this war," Zelenskiy said, a day after the Kremlin said Russian diesel had begun reaching global markets following the deal with US President Donald Trump.
European Union leaders rallied behind Zelenskiy, as Ukraine faces continued Russian attacks and uncertainty over future US military and intelligence support. Russian drone strikes on Kharkiv killed three people, while attacks elsewhere left hundreds of thousands without electricity, according to the report.
Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal said the EU would probably need to provide Ukraine with a new loan to cover its budget shortfall next year, as European leaders debated how to sustain financial and military support for Kyiv.
The dispute comes as the war continues to strain relations between Trump and Zelenskiy. Trump has criticised Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries, calling the latest strike "a disgrace", and blamed such attacks for pushing up energy prices ahead of US midterm elections in November.
Zelenskiy also accused Russian President Vladimir Putin of having no genuine interest in peace negotiations, describing Moscow's approach as a "parody" of a desire to end the war.
Putin, meanwhile, said Russia was establishing a security zone inside Ukraine along the border, which he declared would not be open to negotiation. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the planned zone stretched 660 kilometres, with Russia controlling about 70% of it.

title: Carney campaigns against Alberta secession vote
description: Carney campaigns against Alberta secession vote
content:
Canadian PM warns independence push could bring years of uncertainty
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney campaigned for national unity in oil-rich Alberta on Thursday, warning that a vote against Canada could trigger years of uncertainty ahead of a referendum on whether the province should pursue independence.
Polling suggests fewer than a quarter of Alberta's roughly five million residents support separation. However, Carney, who grew up in the western province, cautioned against relying on surveys to predict the outcome.
"Polls don't vote," he told a rally in Calgary, Alberta's largest city, describing the referendum as coming at the worst possible time. He warned that a vote against Canada would be a "dangerous bluff" that could cost the province opportunities and create prolonged uncertainty.
Alberta's right-wing Premier Danielle Smith opposes independence but has backed Monday's non-binding vote as a way to settle the divisive issue. She has pledged to initiate a legally binding separation process if a majority votes in favour, while ruling out another referendum if voters choose to remain in Canada.
Mitch Sylvestre, head of the Alberta Prosperity Project, a prominent separatist organisation, told AFP he believed the movement could win, expressing surprise at the prospect of receiving less than 40% support.
Carney has placed Alberta's oil industry at the heart of his economic strategy, backing a new pipeline and other projects to boost crude production and reduce Canada's dependence on the United States. Carney warned that outside forces were seeking to divide Canada.
Ryan Griffiths, a Syracuse University professor specialising in secessionist movements, said Alberta was unusual because its separatist campaign was driven largely by economic grievances, rather than a distinct linguistic or nationalist identity.
The movement has also attracted scrutiny over alleged contacts with allies of US President Donald Trump. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has described Alberta as a "natural partner" for the United States, while separatist representatives have held meetings at the State Department.
Carney warned that outside forces were seeking to divide Canada. Asked about possible foreign interference, he said the United States and other governments should not involve themselves in Canadian elections, just as Canada did not interfere in theirs.

title: Police detain  Cockroach  founder before Delhi rally
description: Police detain  Cockroach  founder before Delhi rally
content:
Indian police detained the founder of the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), Abhijeet Dipke, student leaders and supporters on Friday as hundreds protested in New Delhi, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over disputed voter-list revisions.
The CJP, opposition groups and student organisations have staged near-daily demonstrations this month, alleging that changes to electoral rolls favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission denies political bias and says wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol.
Dipke was detained while leaving a house in central Delhi, while student activist Neha Bora was taken into preventive custody as she tried to reach the protest venue. Police said Dipke had been warned earlier against proceeding with the demonstration.
Authorities closed Central Park in the Connaught Place commercial district for two days, deploying hundreds of police officers in riot gear. Nevertheless, nearly 500 protesters gathered in groups at several locations, waving Indian flags and chanting slogans. Some were detained.
The demonstrations followed reports that more than 130 million names had been removed from voter lists since last year. The Election Commission said the deletions included 28 million deceased people, 63 million who had relocated and 30 million who could not be traced.
Opposition parties allege the changes disproportionately affect Muslims and other minorities. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh accused the opposition Congress party of using young people for political ends, saying they were being turned into "pawns in the politics of anarchy".
Protests also took place in Mumbai, Bengaluru and Patna. The latest demonstrations add to mounting pressure on the election chief, whose resignation protesters have demanded throughout the month. The commission and the BJP rejected the charges hurled by protesters.

title: AI unlocks secrets buried for centuries

Artificial intelligence is helping researchers and enthusiasts solve historical codes that have remained unbroken for centuries, with a message commissioned by Napoleon Bonaparte in 1809 decoded in just six hours using OpenAI's latest model.
Carter Church, a 27-year-old AI engineer at US cybersecurity firm SentinelOne, deciphered the coded letter detailing the positions of French and allied troops. The document had remained overlooked in an online academic archive for more than 200 years.
Japanese patent engineer Satoshi Tomokiyo, who maintains an online database of unsolved ciphers, expressed mixed feelings about the technology's rapid progress, saying it was exciting to see old mysteries resolved but unsettling that difficult challenges could be overcome so easily.
Beyond code-breaking, AI is transforming historical research by analysing vast collections of manuscripts and revealing writing concealed inside fragile ancient scrolls. Researchers have used the technology to virtually unroll carbonised papyri from the Roman-era eruption of Mount Vesuvius.

content:

hurl stones at Palestinians, who threw rocks back

Settler violence has surged during this year's olive harvest. Israeli monitoring group Yesh Din recorded at least 170 attacks since September 27. The Abu Falah incident followed another attack near Turmus Ayya, where settlers reportedly burned three cars after confronting farmers harvesting olives.

title: Pope shows steady improvement
description: Pope shows steady improvement
content:
Leo celebrates mass at Rome hospital as doctors await tests resultsQ
Pope Leo XIV's health showed "steady improvement" on Friday, three days after he underwent surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung, with the 71-year-old pontiff celebrating mass at the Rome hospital where he is recovering.
The Vatican said blood tests and a chest X-ray conducted on Friday confirmed progress in his general condition. The pope was also carrying out his normal daily activities completely independently, according to a statement citing his medical team.
Doctors have described his recovery as normal, with a chest X-ray on Thursday indicating a "good recovery of the operated lung". However, test results to establish whether the cancer has spread are still awaited. These findings will help determine the next course of treatment, the Vatican press office said.
The Vatican released the first photographs of Leo since the operation, showing him standing before a makeshift altar in a room on the 10th floor of Rome's Gemelli hospital, dressed in green vestments. He appeared relaxed, with his private secretary, Peruvian priest Edgard Rimaycuna, standing beside him.
He celebrated mass with medical and nursing staff, along with other people present at the hospital and members of the police who were off duty. He thanked doctors, nurses and other hospital workers for their service, their care for vulnerable people and the attention they had given him during his stay.
Leo is expected to lead the traditional Angelus prayer on Sunday, although it remains unclear whether he will recite it from the hospital or the Vatican. The prayer is normally delivered from a window of the Apostolic Palace overlooking St Peter's Square.
Previous popes have led the Angelus while hospitalised. John Paul II appeared at a hospital window in 2005 while recovering from respiratory problems, while Pope Francis recited the prayer from hospital in 2021 following colon surgery.

title: DISCOs seek Rs2 6 unit hike for Sept
description: DISCOs seek Rs2 6 unit hike for Sept
content:
NEPRA to hold public hearing on Oct 29 to consider request
Distribution companies (DISCOs) have sought regulatory approval to recover an additional Rs2.5624 per unit from consumers through electricity bills under the September 2026 fuel charges adjustment (FCA). The proposed increase is also expected to apply to K-Electric consumers under the government's uniform tariff policy.
The Central Power Purchasing Agency-Guarantee (CPPA-G), on behalf of DISCOS, has filed an application with the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA), seeking approval for the monthly adjustment. The regulator has scheduled a public hearing on October 29.
According to the application, the reference fuel cost was Rs7.4596 per unit, while the proposed adjustment of Rs2.5624 per unit reflects the difference between the reference cost and the actual fuel-related charges incurred during September.
The data submitted to NEPRA shows that total electricity generation stood at 13,217 gigawatt-hours (GWh) during the month, while net electricity supplied to DISCOs amounted to 12,760 GWh after accounting for transmission losses and electricity sold to independent power producers (IPPs).
Hydropower remained the largest source of electricity generation, contributing 4,834 GWh, or 36.58% of the total. Nuclear power plants generated 1,893 GWh, accounting for 14.32%, while imported coal-fired plants produced 2,155 GWh, or 16.31%.
Imported coal generation cost Rs37.142 billion, translating into Rs17.2329 per unit. Meanwhile, liquefied natural gas (RLNG)-based generation produced 804 GWh, or 6.08% of the total, at a reported cost of Rs39.37 billion, equivalent to Rs39.7372 per unit.
High-speed diesel was the most expensive major fuel source listed in the September data. It generated 213 GWh at a cost of Rs13.262 billion, translating into Rs62.1381 per unit.
Furnace-oil-based plants contributed 263 GWh at a cost of Rs11.812 billion, or Rs44.8613 per unit, while gas-fired generation accounted for 1,066 GWh at the reported rate of Rs13.0414 per unit.
Local coal-fired plants generated 1,327 GWh at Rs5.9946 per unit, while nuclear generation was reported at Rs2.9045 per unit. Wind power contributed 464 GWh, while bagasse-based plants generated 35 GWh.
The data also indicates a continuing rise in nuclear generation costs over recent months, although the figures provided in the application would need to be compared with previous monthly filings to establish the extent of the increase.

The slain terrorist, identified as Zahid Gul and affiliated with the Gul Bahadur group, was wanted in connection with several serious terrorist attacks. The CTD said he had personally guided the explosive-laden vehicle used in the suicide attack on the old Kohat Police Lines.
According to the department, Zahid Gul was also present at the scene of a bank robbery at Bili Tang, where Rs6 million was looted. The stolen money was subsequently distributed among terrorist cells operating in Bakkakhel and Janikhel in Bannu, the CTD said.
The slain terrorist commander maintained close links with the Gul Bahadur group and was involved in transporting several suicide bombers to Kohat, The CTD said that two months ago, Zahid Gul had brought a suicide bomber to carry out an attack on the new Kohat Police Lines, however, the attempt was foiled.
The terrorist's next intended targets were a Pakistan Air Force installation and the Police Training School in Kohat, the CTD said. Other members of the terrorist network have already been taken into custody by security agencies, according to the department.
The federal government on October 11 imposed emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) province, bringing an end to 13 -year rule of the PTI. The Centre alleged that PTI government had failed to take effective action against terrorists.

title: Bipartisan NA panel to mull electoral reforms
description: Bipartisan NA panel to mull electoral reforms
content:
House passes motion to form parliamentary committee
The National Assembly on Friday passed a motion to constitute a parliamentary committee comprising members of both the houses of parliament to recommend electoral reforms aimed at ensuring free, fair and transparent elections.
The motion was moved by Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhary under Rule 244B of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the National Assembly, 2007.
According to the motion, the speaker of the National Assembly, in consultation with the Senate chairman and leaders of parliamentary parties, will constitute the committee.
It will comprise members from all parliamentary parties in proportion to their representation in parliament.
The motion also authorised the speaker to replace any committee member at the request of the leader of the parliamentary party concerned.
The committee will recommend electoral reforms to ensure free, fair and transparent elections, including the adoption of the latest available technology for conducting elections and the preparation of draft legislation, including constitutional amendments, where necessary.
The quorum for a committee meeting will be one-fourth of its total membership.
The committee will submit its report to parliament within the timeframe specified by the Speaker after the issuance of the notification constituting the committee.
The motion also authorises the committee to constitute subcommittees, if required.
Members of the National Assembly and the Senate will be included in the committee on the basis of proportional representation, which will formulate recommendations for electoral reforms.

Visitors from the United Kingdom, Afghanistan, the United States, Iran, Canada and China featured prominently in the figures. The arrivals from Malaysia and Thailand depicted a decline, according to the documents.
Tourist arrivals from the United Kingdom increased from 503,409 in 2024 to 514,412 in 2025. Visitors from Afghanistan numbered 641,199 in 2024 and 575,674 in 2025, while arrivals from the United States declined from 261,282 to 248,665 over the same period.
The number of Iranian tourists rose from 106,835 in 2024 to 152,885 in 2025. Canadian visitors increased from 116,529 to 117,600, while arrivals from China climbed from 74,093 to 85,575. Pakistan also received 43,097 German tourists and 58,578 Australian visitors in 2025.

title: Minor offences cannot bar government jobs  says FCC
description: Minor offences cannot bar government jobs  says FCC
content:
Notes that Rs500 fine cannot permanently disqualify constable candidate
The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has ruled that a minor or less harmful offence should not have disproportionately severe consequences that permanently deprive an individual of the opportunity to enter government service.
"A trivial or less harmful offence cannot have a severe consequence so as to rule out the possibility of induction into a government service," the court observed in a four-page judgement authored by Justice Ali Baqar Najafi. Justice Najafi was part of a division bench led by Chief Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan.
Through the verdict, the FCC upheld a Peshawar High Court (PHC) decision directing the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government to consider a candidate for appointment as a police constable.
It observed that although a crime remained a crime, the nature of the offence, the offender's disposition towards criminal conduct and the likelihood of committing further offences had to be considered before imposing lasting consequences on the individual.
The case concerned a candidate who had been convicted in a criminal case registered under Sections 285 and 286 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), relating to negligent conduct involving fire, combustible matter or explosive substances. He had been fined Rs500 following a confessional statement.
The court noted that a confession was often made through an understanding intended to avoid unnecessary consumption of the court's time and could also reflect an element of remorse. Its consequences, however, should remain proportionate to the offence rather than result in a lifelong disqualification from public employment.
"Without educating such convict about the result of making a confessional statement, he cannot be bound for a life-long prohibition," the judgement stated.
It added that the available record did not indicate that the candidate had been adequately informed of the lasting consequences of his confession before reaching an understanding under Section 243 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
The court observed that no sufficient cause had been shown to justify treating the conviction as a permanent bar to the candidate's induction into government service.
"Obviously, the punishment must commensurate with the crime and it cannot damage the entire life of such criminal," the judgement stated, adding that the candidate was not shown by the available record to be a habitual offender.
The court further observed that an accused who admitted guilt became, in a sense, a friend of the court and could be entitled to reasonable leniency, depending on the circumstances.
The judgement also underscored that the respondent enjoyed constitutional protection of his civil rights, alongside corresponding obligations, and was entitled to due process and a fair trial under Article 10-A of the Constitution.
At the same time, the FCC acknowledged that police recruitment required particular scrutiny of candidates' character and suitability. Rule 12.14 of the Police Rules, 1934, requires recruits to possess good character, making careful assessment essential when selecting candidates for police service.
The court also referred to paragraph 23 of Standing Order 6/2015, issued by the Punjab government's Police Department, which bars candidates with criminal records or affiliations with proscribed organisations from appointment.
An amendment introduced on June 1, 2018, further required candidates to submit affidavits declaring that they were not involved in criminal cases when applying.
However, the amended provision also addressed situations in which a case was registered after the application deadline, providing that candidature should not be rejected where the candidate had neither been challaned nor declared innocent through a compromise between the parties.
The judgement noted that these provisions reflected the objective of keeping individuals with established criminal records out of the police service. However, an allegation contained in an FIR, without subsequent indictment or conviction, remained only an allegation.
The court observed that FIRs could sometimes be registered because of personal enmity or ulterior motives, making the investigation and the investigating officer's findings relevant when assessing a candidate's record.

title: PML N s Sana says K P direct rule can be reversed
description: PML N s Sana says K P direct rule can be reversed
content:
Links move to PTI support for counterterrorism efforts
Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah on Friday hinted that the federal government could consider foregoing interim governance in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) if the PTI agreed to support law enforcement agencies in their fight against terrorism.
Speaking to a private news channel, Sanaullah said the government wanted all political parties to reach a consensus on counterterrorism, arguing that growing security challenges required a unified response from the federal and provincial governments.
He said the government's primary demand from the opposition was that it stand with Pakistan, its law enforcement agencies and armed forces. The fight against terrorism had cost the country precious lives, including those of military personnel, he added.
Sanaullah maintained that political differences should not undermine ongoing counterterrorism efforts, stressing that the strategy adopted to combat terrorism should not be questioned or made conditional on political demands.
Responding to questions about why the government was pursuing negotiations despite parliament's ratification of the emergency measures and governor's rule, Sanaullah said the administration continued to seek consensus among political parties on matters of national security.
He argued that the evolving security situation demanded cooperation rather than confrontation, adding that the federal and provincial governments needed to adopt a common strategy to counter the threat. "Everyone should stand with Pakistan, its law enforcement agencies, and its armed forces," he added.

title: Defence minister hits back over Monroe AI riddle
description: Defence minister hits back over Monroe AI riddle
content:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Friday brushed aside online criticism after being mocked for responding to an AI-generated image of Hollywood icon Marilyn Monroe, saying he personally operated his social media account and saw nothing unusual about his response.
Speaking on private television channel programme Naya Pakistan, the PML-N stalwart was asked about the post and whether he managed his account on X himself.
"200% I operate it myself," Asif said, adding that he led an ordinary life despite holding a prominent government position. "I have a personal life and a normal life. I am a normal human being; there is nothing special about me," he said, stressing he had no airs about him.
The controversy began on Tuesday when Asif responded to an AI-generated image depicting Monroe, which challenged social media users to identify an object that would have been out of place in the 1950s.
Resharing the image on X, the defence minister identified the smartwatch worn by Monroe as the anachronism. The original post shared by Asif has since been deleted.
Addressing the criticism, Asif defended his response, arguing that he had simply answered the question posed in the post. "They presented a riddle asking about what was amiss with the photo [of Monroe], asking what should not have been present in 1956, and that was a smartwatch, so I wrote 'watch'. What is non-serious about this?" he said.
Asif maintained that being the defence minister did not mean he had to give up his personality or refrain from engaging with light-hearted content on social media. He said he operated his account himself and used it "for fun", questioning why his position should prevent him from expressing himself like any other individual.

title: No one is bigger than Pakistan  Vawda
description: No one is bigger than Pakistan  Vawda
content:
Says the PTI also had capable people who would be given opportunities
Senator Faisal Vawda has said Pakistan is heading towards neither dictatorship nor a presidential system, while criticising what he described as "sham democracy" and saying no prime minister or chief minister was greater than the country.
Speaking on Express News programme Centre Stage, Vawda said ordinary Pakistanis needed basic necessities and services, including flour, sugar, schools, colleges and affordable transport, but those who controlled such resources had become rulers.
He said the living standards of ordinary people had continued to deteriorate, adding that public patience had run out.
Education in Sindh and Punjab was in a worse state than in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), Vawda said, but stressed that the country did not belong to any individual or family.
He said terrorism could not be eliminated within two to four months, although efforts to tackle it would begin. Recalling his remarks in 2018, he said he had called for the military to be respected, arguing that its role had enabled Pakistan to establish itself internationally.
Vawda said the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) also had capable people who would be given opportunities, whether as parliamentarians or in other roles.
PTI leader Ali Muhammad Khan said there was now greater room for dialogue than before, following the removal of the party's provincial government in K-P.
He said securing the release of PTI founder Imran Khan was currently a greater priority than access to medication.
Ali Muhammad Khan said a government enjoying what he described as three-fourths public support had been removed, throwing the country into a volatile situation. He questioned whether the fight against terrorism could be won without the PTI, saying the party had been cooperating.
He described the imposition of governor's rule in K-P as an arbitrary decision.
